entries.zh: 而察罕兵勢甚盛，遣使至金陵招太祖，故兌書於三者籌之為詳。
entries.en: Meanwhile Chaghan Temür's armies were very strong and had sent envoys to Jinling to win the Founder over, so Ye's memorial weighed all three rivals in careful detail.
entries.literal: Yet Chaghan's military power was very strong, and he sent envoys to Jinling to recruit the Founder; therefore in his memorial Ye deliberated on the three in detail.

entries.zh: 其略曰：
entries.en: The gist of it read:
entries.literal: Its summary said:

entries.zh: 子恭，舉人，累官工部尚書，有能聲。
entries.en: His son Gong, a provincial graduate, rose through the ranks to minister of works and won a reputation for competence.
entries.literal: His son Gong was a provincial graduate; through successive offices he rose to Minister of Works, with a reputation for ability.

entries.zh: 遇弟遠，字中復，嘗隨遇侍帝。
entries.en: Chen's younger brother Yuan, courtesy name Zhongfu, had once accompanied Chen in attendance on the Emperor.
entries.literal: Chen's younger brother Yuan, style name Zhongfu, once followed Chen in attending the Emperor.

entries.zh: 永樂初，為翰林待詔，精繪事。
entries.en: Early in the Yongle reign he served as a Hanlin awaiting edict and excelled at painting.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongle he was a Hanlin awaiting edict, refined in painting.

entries.zh: 遠子孟顒，善書。
entries.en: Yuan's son Meng'ang was accomplished in calligraphy.
entries.literal: Yuan's son Meng'ang was skilled at calligraphy.

entries.zh: 愚聞：取天下者，必有一定之規模。
entries.en: I have heard that whoever would take the realm must follow a fixed strategic design.
entries.literal: This foolish one has heard: he who takes the realm must have a fixed plan and pattern.

entries.zh: 韓信初見高祖，畫楚、漢成敗；
entries.en: When Han Xin first met Emperor Gaozu of Han, he mapped out the contest between Chu and Han;
entries.literal: When Han Xin first met the High Ancestor, he mapped the rise and fall of Chu and Han;

entries.zh: 孔明臥草廬，與先主論三分形勢者是也。
entries.en: and Zhuge Liang, still in his thatched hut, discussed the three-way balance of power with the Former Lord—such were the models.
entries.literal: Kongming lying in a thatched hut and discussing with the Former Lord the tripartite situation—such was the case.

entries.zh: 今之規模，宜北絕李察罕，南並張九四。
entries.en: The design for today should be to break off relations with Chaghan Temür in the north and absorb Zhang Shicheng in the south.
entries.literal: Today's plan and pattern should cut off Li Chaghan to the north and merge Zhang Jiusi to the south.

entries.zh: 撫溫、台，取閩、越，定都建康，拓地江、廣。
entries.en: Pacify Wenzhou and Taizhou, seize Fujian and Zhejiang, make Jiankang the capital, and extend your territory along the Yangzi and the coast.
entries.literal: Pacify Wen and Tai, take Min and Yue, fix the capital at Jiankang, and extend territory through Jiang and Guang.

entries.zh: 進則越兩淮以北征，退則畫長江而自守。
entries.en: If you advance, cross the Huai and campaign north; if you hold back, take the long Yangzi as your line of defense.
entries.literal: Advancing, cross the two Huai and campaign north; retreating, take the long Yangzi as boundary and hold it yourself.

entries.zh: 夫金陵，古稱龍蟠虎踞帝王之都。
entries.en: Jinling has since antiquity been called a capital where dragon and tiger coil—a seat fit for an emperor.
entries.literal: As for Jinling, in antiquity it was called a capital where the dragon coils and the tiger crouches.

entries.zh: 藉其兵力資財，以攻則克，以守則固，百察罕能如吾何哉？
entries.en: With its armies and wealth behind you, you will conquer when you attack and stand firm when you defend—what can even a hundred Chaghans do against us?
entries.literal: Relying on its military strength and resources, in attack you conquer, in defense you are firm—how can Chaghan in a hundred ways do anything to us?

entries.zh: 江之所備，莫急上流。
entries.en: In defending the Yangzi, nothing is more urgent than securing the upper river.
entries.literal: Of what the Yangzi requires for defense, nothing is more urgent than the upper reaches.

entries.zh: 今義師已克江州，足蔽全吳。
entries.en: Your army has already taken Jiangzhou, which is enough to shield all of Wu.
entries.literal: Now the righteous army has already taken Jiangzhou, sufficient to screen all Wu.

entries.zh: 況自滁、和至廣陵，皆吾所有。
entries.en: Moreover, from Chuzhou and Hezhou down to Guangling, all is already yours.
entries.literal: Moreover from Chu, He, to Guangling—all are ours.

entries.zh: 非直守江，兼可守淮矣。
entries.en: You can defend not only the Yangzi but the Huai as well.
entries.literal: It is not only defending the Yangzi—you can also defend the Huai.

entries.zh: 張氏傾覆可坐而待，淮東諸郡亦將來歸。
entries.en: Zhang's fall can be awaited at leisure, and the commanderies east of the Huai will soon submit as well.
entries.literal: Zhang's collapse can be awaited seated; the various commanderies east of the Huai will also come to submit.

entries.zh: 北略中原，李氏可並也。
entries.en: When you campaign north into the Central Plain, Li's territory can be absorbed as well.
entries.literal: Campaigning north into the Central Plain, Li's [domain] can also be merged.

entries.zh: 今聞察罕妄自尊大，致書明公，如曹操之招孫權。
entries.en: I hear that Chaghan has grown arrogant and sent Your Excellency a letter like Cao Cao's invitation to Sun Quan.
entries.literal: Now I hear Chaghan presumptuously holds himself high and sends a letter to Your Excellency, like Cao Cao recruiting Sun Quan.

entries.zh: 竊以元運將終，人心不屬，而察罕欲效操所為，事勢不侔。
entries.en: I believe the Yuan mandate is near its end and the people's hearts are no longer with it, yet Chaghan wishes to play Cao Cao's part—the situation does not match.
entries.literal: I venture to think the Yuan mandate is nearing its end and men's hearts do not belong to it, yet Chaghan wishes to imitate what Cao did—the circumstances do not match.

entries.zh: 宜如魯肅計，鼎足江東，以觀天下之釁，此其大綱也。
entries.en: You should follow Lu Su's plan, hold a tripartite footing east of the Yangzi, and watch for openings in the realm—that is the overarching strategy.
entries.literal: You should follow Lu Su's plan, stand on three feet in Jiangdong, and watch for openings in the realm—this is the main outline.

entries.zh: 太祖奇其言，欲留用之，力辭去。
entries.en: The Founder was impressed by his counsel and wished to keep him in service, but Ye firmly declined and departed.
entries.literal: The Founder marveled at his words and wished to keep and employ him; he firmly declined and left.

entries.zh: 賜銀幣襲衣。
entries.en: The court rewarded him with silver, silk, and a ceremonial robe.
entries.literal: He was granted silver, silks, and a robe of investiture.

entries.zh: 後數歲，削平天下，規模次第，略如兌言。
entries.en: Within a few years the Founder had pacified the realm, and the course of conquest followed Ye's design in broad outline.
entries.literal: Several years later, having cut down and pacified the realm, the plan and pattern in sequence were largely as Ye had said.

entries.zh: 方國珍狼子野心，不可馴狎。
entries.en: Fang Guozhen has the heart of a wolf cub and cannot be tamed.
entries.literal: Fang Guozhen has the heart of a wolf cub and cannot be tamed and made tractable.

entries.zh: 往年大兵取婺州，彼即奉書納款。
entries.en: When your army took Wuzhou in earlier years, he promptly sent a letter of submission.
entries.literal: In former years when the great army took Wuzhou, he at once presented a letter submitting allegiance.

entries.zh: 後遣夏煜、陳顯道招諭，彼復狐疑不從。
entries.en: Later, when Xia Yu and Chen Xiandao were sent to win him over, he wavered again and refused.
entries.literal: Later Xia Yu and Chen Xiandao were sent to summon and instruct him; again he was suspicious and did not follow.

entries.zh: 顧遣使從海道報元，謂江東委之納款，誘令張昶齎詔而來。
entries.en: Yet he also sent envoys by sea to report to the Yuan that he had entrusted Jiangdong's surrender, and induced Zhang Chang to come bearing an imperial edict.
entries.literal: Yet he sent envoys by the sea route to report to the Yuan, saying he had entrusted Jiangdong's submission, and lured Zhang Chang to come bearing an imperial edict.

entries.zh: 且遣韓叔義為說客，欲說明公奉詔。
entries.en: He even sent Han Shuyi as an envoy to urge Your Excellency to accept the Yuan edict.
entries.literal: Moreover he sent Han Shuyi as a persuader, wishing to persuade Your Excellency to accept the edict.

entries.zh: 彼既降我，而反欲招我降元。
entries.en: Having already submitted to you, he then tried to recruit you to submit to the Yuan.
entries.literal: He had already submitted to us, yet in turn wished to recruit us to submit to the Yuan.

entries.zh: 其反覆狡獪如是，宜興師問罪。
entries.en: His duplicity is such that you ought to raise an army and call him to account.
entries.literal: His reversals and cunning trickery being thus, you should raise troops to inquire into his crimes.

entries.zh: 然彼以水為命，一聞兵至，挈家航海，中原步騎無如之何。
entries.en: Yet he lives by the sea; at the first rumor of troops he will put his family aboard ship, and your northern infantry and cavalry can do nothing against him.
entries.literal: Yet he takes water as his life; once he hears troops arrive, he takes his family and goes to sea by ship—the Central Plain's infantry and cavalry can do nothing to him.

entries.zh: 夫上兵攻心，彼言杭、趙一平，即當納土，不過欲款我師耳。
entries.en: The highest form of warfare strikes at the mind: his promise to surrender once Hangzhou and Zhao are pacified is only a ruse to stall your army.
entries.literal: The supreme army attacks the mind; he says once Hang and Zhao are pacified he will at once yield territory—it is only that he wishes to stall our army.

entries.zh: 攻之之術，宜限以日期，責其歸順。
entries.en: The way to attack him is to set a deadline and demand his submission.
entries.literal: The method of attacking him should set a limit by date and charge him to return to allegiance.

entries.zh: 彼自方國璋之沒，自知兵不可用。
entries.en: Since the death of Fang Guozhang, he knows himself that his forces are useless.
entries.literal: Since Fang Guozhang's death, he himself knows his troops cannot be used.

entries.zh: 又叔義還稱義師之盛，氣已先挫。
entries.en: Moreover, when Han Shuyi returned he spoke of how strong your army was, and their morale was already shaken.
entries.literal: Moreover when Shuyi returned he praised the righteous army's strength; their spirit was already first broken.

entries.zh: 今因陳顯道以自通，正可脅之而從也。
entries.en: Now that he has opened contact through Chen Xiandao, you can press him into submission.
entries.literal: Now because Chen Xiandao has opened communication on his own behalf, you can justly coerce him into following.

entries.zh: 事宜速不宜緩。
entries.en: The matter calls for speed, not delay.
entries.literal: The affair should be swift and not slow.

entries.zh: 宣諭之後，更置官吏，拘集舟艦，潛收其兵權，以消未然之變。
entries.en: After you announce your demands, replace his officials, assemble his ships, and quietly strip him of military power to forestall any future revolt.
entries.literal: After proclaiming and instructing him, replace the officials, gather ships, secretly take his military authority, to dispel changes not yet arisen.

entries.zh: 三郡可不勞而定。
entries.en: The three coastal commanderies can be secured without a fight.
entries.literal: The three commanderies can be settled without labor.

entries.zh: 至其目有三。
entries.en: The three subsidiary points are as follows.
entries.literal: As for its sub-points, there are three.

entries.zh: 張九四之地，南包杭、紹，北跨通、泰，而以平江為巢穴。
entries.en: Zhang Shicheng's territory runs south through Hangzhou and Shaoxing, north across Nantong and Taizhou, with Pingjiang as his stronghold.
entries.literal: Zhang Jiusi's territory south embraces Hang and Shao, north spans Tong and Tai, and takes Pingjiang as its nest.

entries.zh: 今欲攻之，莫若聲言掩取杭、紹、湖、秀，而大兵直搗平江。
entries.en: To attack him now, it would be best to announce a feint against Hangzhou, Shaoxing, Huzhou, and Jiaxing while the main force strikes directly at Pingjiang.
entries.literal: If you now wish to attack him, nothing is better than proclaiming you will seize Hang, Shao, Hu, and Xiu, while the main army strikes straight at Pingjiang.

entries.zh: 城固難以驟拔，則以鎖城法困之。
entries.en: If the city is too strong to take quickly, use the encirclement method to wear him down.
entries.literal: If the city is strong and hard to seize in a rush, then use the method of locking the city to wear him down.

entries.zh: 於城外矢石不到之地別築長圍，分命將卒四面立營，屯田固守，斷其出入之路。
entries.en: Beyond range of missiles, build an outer cordon; station troops in camps on all four sides, farm the fields, hold the line, and cut off every route in or out.
entries.literal: Outside the city, in a place where arrows and stones cannot reach, separately build a long encirclement; divide orders to generals and soldiers to set camps on four sides, garrison fields and hold firm, and cut off his roads of going out and coming in.

entries.zh: 分兵略定屬邑，收其稅糧以贍軍中。
entries.en: Send detachments to secure the surrounding districts and levy their grain to feed your army.
entries.literal: Divide troops to pacify subordinate districts, collect their tax grain to supply the army.

entries.zh: 彼坐守空城，安得不困？
entries.en: Trapped in an empty city, how can he fail to be worn down?
entries.literal: He sits guarding an empty city—how can he not be worn down?

entries.zh: 平江既下，巢穴已傾，杭、越必歸，余郡解體。
entries.en: Once Pingjiang falls, his stronghold is gone; Hangzhou and Shaoxing will submit, and the other districts will collapse.
entries.literal: Once Pingjiang is taken, the nest is already overturned; Hang and Yue will surely submit, and the remaining commanderies will dissolve.

entries.zh: 此上計也。
entries.en: This is the best plan.
entries.literal: This is the upper plan.

entries.zh: 張氏重鎮在紹興。
entries.en: Zhang's chief stronghold lies at Shaoxing.
entries.literal: Zhang's key stronghold is at Shaoxing.

entries.zh: 紹興懸隔江海，所以數攻而不克者，以彼糧道在三江斗門也。
entries.en: Shaoxing lies across river and sea; the reason repeated attacks have failed is that their supply line runs through the Sanjiang sluice.
entries.literal: Shaoxing hangs separated by river and sea; the reason for repeated attacks without success is that their grain route lies at the Sanjiang sluice gate.

entries.zh: 若一軍攻平江，斷其糧道；
entries.en: If one army attacks Pingjiang and cuts their supply line,
entries.literal: If one army attacks Pingjiang and cuts off their grain route;

entries.zh: 一軍攻杭州，絕其援兵，紹興必拔。
entries.en: and another attacks Hangzhou and blocks their reinforcements, Shaoxing will surely fall.
entries.literal: one army attacks Hangzhou and severs their relief troops—Shaoxing will surely be taken.

entries.zh: 所攻在蘇、杭，所取在紹興，所謂多方以誤之者也。
entries.en: You strike at Suzhou and Hangzhou but take Shaoxing—this is the tactic of confusing the enemy on many fronts.
entries.literal: What is attacked is Su and Hang; what is taken is Shaoxing—this is what is called using many directions to confuse the enemy.

entries.zh: 紹興既拔，杭城勢孤，湖、秀風靡，然後進攻平江，犁其心腹，江北餘孽隨而瓦解。
entries.en: Once Shaoxing is taken, Hangzhou stands alone, Huzhou and Jiaxing will follow, and then you can advance on Pingjiang and strike at his core; his remaining forces north of the river will collapse in turn.
entries.literal: Once Shaoxing is taken, Hangzhou city's position is isolated; Hu and Xiu bow to the wind; then advance to attack Pingjiang, plow its heart and belly, and the remaining spawn north of the river follow in dissolution.

entries.zh: 此次計也。
entries.en: This is the second-best plan.
entries.literal: This is the second plan.

entries.zh: 福建本浙江一道，兵脃城陋。
entries.en: Fujian was originally part of the Zhejiang circuit; its armies are weak and its cities poor.
entries.literal: Fujian was originally one circuit of Zhejiang; its troops are weak and its cities crude.

entries.zh: 兩浙既平，必圖歸附。
entries.en: Once the two Zhejiangs are pacified, it will surely seek to submit.
entries.literal: Once the two Zhejiangs are pacified, it will surely plan to return to allegiance.

entries.zh: 下之一辯士力耳。
entries.en: It would take no more than a single persuasive envoy.
entries.literal: To take it requires only the effort of one debater.

entries.zh: 如復稽遲，則大兵自溫、處入，奇兵自海道入，福州必不支。
entries.en: If you delay again, your main force can enter from Wenzhou and Chuzhou while a flanking force comes by sea, and Fuzhou will not hold.
entries.literal: If you again delay, then the great army will enter from Wen and Chu, and surprise troops will enter by the sea route—Fuzhou will surely not hold.

entries.zh: 福州下，旁郡迎刃解矣。
entries.en: Once Fuzhou falls, the neighboring districts will collapse like bamboo split by a knife.
entries.literal: Once Fuzhou falls, neighboring commanderies will split like bamboo against the blade.

entries.zh: 威聲已震，然後進取兩廣，猶反掌也。
entries.en: Once your prestige has shaken the south, taking the two Guang provinces will be as easy as turning your hand.
entries.literal: Once prestige and fame already shake the realm, then advance to take the two Guangs—it is still like turning the palm.

entries.zh: 范常，字子權，滁人。
entries.en: Fan Chang, courtesy name Ziquan, was a native of Chuzhou.
entries.literal: Fan Chang, style name Ziquan, was a man of Chuzhou.

entries.zh: 太祖軍滁，杖策謁軍門。
entries.en: When the Founder's army was at Chuzhou, he took his riding crop and presented himself at the camp.
entries.literal: When the Founder's army was at Chu, taking up his riding crop he visited the army gate.

entries.zh: 太祖夙知其名，與語意合，留置幕下。
entries.en: The Founder had long known his reputation; they spoke together and found their views in accord, and Fan was kept on the staff.
entries.literal: The Founder had long known his name; in conversation their ideas accorded, and he was kept below the curtain.

entries.zh: 有疑輒問，常悉以實對。
entries.en: Whenever the Founder had doubts he would ask Fan, who always answered frankly.
entries.literal: When there were doubts he would at once ask; Fan always answered fully with truth.

entries.zh: 諸將克和州，兵不戢。
entries.en: When the generals took Hezhou, the troops would not restrain themselves.
entries.literal: The generals took Hezhou, but the troops would not restrain themselves.

entries.zh: 常言於太祖曰：「得一城而使人肝腦塗地，何以成大事？」
entries.en: Fan said to the Founder, "If you win a city only to leave the people slaughtered, how can you accomplish anything great?"
entries.literal: Fan said to the Founder: "Gaining one city yet making men's livers and brains smear the ground—how can you accomplish a great undertaking?"

entries.zh: 太祖乃切責諸將。
entries.en: The Founder then sternly rebuked the generals.
entries.literal: The Founder thereupon sternly reproached the generals.

entries.zh: 搜軍中所掠婦女，還其家，民大悅。
entries.en: He searched out the women seized by the troops and sent them home, and the people were greatly relieved.
entries.literal: He searched out women seized in the army and returned them to their families; the people were greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 太祖以四方割據，戰爭無虛日，命常為文，禱於上帝。
entries.en: With the realm divided and war unceasing, the Founder ordered Fan to draft a prayer to Heaven.
entries.literal: Because the four quarters were carved up and warfare had no idle day, the Founder ordered Fan to compose a text and pray to the Supreme Lord.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：「今天下紛紜，生民塗炭，不有所屬，物類盡矣。
entries.en: It read: "The realm is in turmoil and the people are in misery; unless they find a ruler to whom they can belong, all living things will perish.
entries.literal: Its words said: "Now the realm is in turmoil, the living people are charred on the coals; if they have no one to belong to, the kinds of things will be exhausted.

entries.zh: 倘元祚未終，則群雄當早伏其辜。
entries.en: If the Yuan mandate is not yet exhausted, then let the rival warlords be punished first.
entries.literal: If the Yuan mandate is not yet ended, then the many heroes should early submit to their guilt.

entries.zh: 某亦在群雄中，請自某始。
entries.en: I too am among those warlords; let the punishment begin with me.
entries.literal: I too am among the many heroes—please begin with me.

entries.zh: 若已厭元德，有天命者宜歸之，無使斯民久阽危苦。
entries.en: If Heaven has already turned from the Yuan, let those with the mandate be followed, and do not let the people suffer in danger any longer.
entries.literal: If already weary of the Yuan's virtue, whoever has Heaven's mandate should be followed; do not let this people long stand in peril and suffering.

entries.zh: 存亡之機，驗於三月。」
entries.en: Whether we survive or perish will be known within three months."
entries.literal: The hinge of survival and destruction will be tested in three months."

entries.zh: 太祖嘉其能達己意，命典文牘，授元帥府都事。
entries.en: The Founder praised him for voicing his own thoughts and put him in charge of documents, appointing him chief clerk of the marshal's headquarters.
entries.literal: The Founder praised his ability to express the Founder's own intent and ordered him to oversee documents, appointing him Chief Clerk of the Marshal's Headquarters.

entries.zh: 取太平，命為知府，諭之曰：「太平，吾股肱郡，其民數困於兵，當令得所。」
entries.en: When Taiping was taken, Fan was made prefect. The Founder told him, "Taiping is one of my core districts; its people have suffered repeatedly from war—you must give them relief."
entries.literal: When Taiping was taken, he was appointed prefect and instructed: "Taiping is my arm-and-thigh commandery; its people have repeatedly suffered from soldiers—you should let them find their place."

entries.zh: 常以簡易為治，興學恤民。
entries.en: Fan governed with simplicity, promoted schools, and cared for the people.
entries.literal: Chang governed with simplicity and ease, raised schools, and comforted the people.

entries.zh: 官廩有谷數千石，請給民乏種者，秋稔輸官，公私皆足。
entries.en: The government granary held several thousand piculs of grain; he lent seed to farmers in need, to be repaid after the autumn harvest, and both public and private stores were filled.
entries.literal: The official granary had several thousand piculs of grain; he requested to give it to people lacking seed; in autumn when ripe they paid the government—public and private were both sufficient.

entries.zh: 居三年，民親愛之，召入為侍儀。
entries.en: After three years the people loved him, and he was recalled to serve as attendant of ceremonies.
entries.literal: After three years in office the people loved him dearly; he was summoned in as Attendant of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 洪武元年，擢翰林直學士兼太常卿。
entries.en: In Hongwu 1 he was promoted to direct Hanlin academician and concurrent director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: In the first year of Hongwu he was promoted to Direct Academician of the Hanlin and concurrent Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 帝銳意稽古禮文。
entries.en: The Emperor was intent on reviving ancient ritual and ceremony.
entries.literal: The Emperor was keen to examine antiquity's ritual texts.

entries.zh: 群臣集議，間有異同。
entries.en: When the ministers met to deliberate, their views sometimes differed.
entries.literal: The ministers gathered to deliberate; at times there were differences.

entries.zh: 常能參合眾言，委曲當上意。
entries.en: Fan could reconcile the various opinions and shape them to satisfy the Emperor.
entries.literal: Fan was able to combine the many opinions and tactfully match the Emperor's intent.

entries.zh: 尋以病免歸。
entries.en: Soon afterward he retired on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: Before long, on grounds of illness he was excused and returned home.

entries.zh: 歲餘，手詔征詣闕，仍故官。
entries.en: A year later the Emperor summoned him back by personal edict and restored his former post.
entries.literal: After more than a year, by handwritten edict he was summoned to the court and restored to his former office.

entries.zh: 帝宴閒，輒命儒臣列坐，賦詩為樂。
entries.en: At leisure banquets the Emperor would have the scholar-officials sit together and compose poetry for amusement.
entries.literal: At the Emperor's leisure banquets he would order Confucian ministers to sit in rows and compose poetry for pleasure.

entries.zh: 常每先成，語多率。
entries.en: Fan always finished first, and his verse was plain and direct.
entries.literal: Fan always finished first; his language was mostly unadorned.

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「老范詩質朴，殊似其為人也。」
entries.en: The Emperor laughed and said, "Old Fan's poems are as plain as the man himself."
entries.literal: The Emperor laughed and said: "Old Fan's poetry is plain and unadorned—very much like the man himself."

entries.zh: 遷起居注。
entries.en: He was promoted to diarist of attendance.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Diarist of Attendance.

entries.zh: 常有足疾，數在告，賜以安車。
entries.en: Fan suffered from a foot ailment and often took leave; the Emperor granted him a comfort carriage.
entries.literal: Fan had a foot ailment and repeatedly took leave; he was granted a comfort carriage.

entries.zh: 尋乞歸，帝賦詩四章送之。
entries.en: Soon he asked to retire, and the Emperor wrote four poems to see him off.
entries.literal: Before long he begged to return home; the Emperor composed four stanzas of poetry to send him off.

entries.zh: 賜宅於太平。
entries.en: He was granted a house in Taiping.
entries.literal: A residence in Taiping was granted.

entries.zh: 子祖，歷官雲南左參政，有修潔稱。
entries.en: His son Zu rose to left vice commissioner of Yunnan and was known for integrity.
entries.literal: His son Zu through successive offices rose to Left Vice Commissioner of Yunnan, with a reputation for cultivated purity.

entries.zh: 潘庭堅，字叔聞，當塗人。
entries.en: Pan Tingjian, courtesy name Shuwen, was a native of Dangtu.
entries.literal: Pan Tingjian, style name Shuwen, was a man of Dangtu.

entries.zh: 元末為富陽教諭，謝去。
entries.en: Near the end of the Yuan he served as an instructor in Fuyang, then resigned.
entries.literal: At the end of the Yuan he was instructor at Fuyang and resigned.

entries.zh: 太祖駐太平，以陶安薦，征庭堅為帥府教授。
entries.en: While the Founder was at Taiping, Tao An recommended him, and Pan was summoned as professor at the marshal's headquarters.
entries.literal: When the Founder was stationed at Taiping, on Tao An's recommendation he summoned Tingjian as professor at the marshal's headquarters.

entries.zh: 慎密謙約，為太祖所稱。
entries.en: Discreet, humble, and restrained, he won the Founder's praise.
entries.literal: Cautious, close, humble, and restrained—he was praised by the Founder.

entries.zh: 下集慶，擢中書省博士。
entries.en: After the capture of Jiqing he was promoted to erudite of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Jiqing was taken, he was promoted to Erudite of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 婺州下，改為金華府，以庭堅同知府事。
entries.en: When Wuzhou was taken and made Jinhua Prefecture, Pan was appointed to assist in governing it.
entries.literal: When Wuzhou fell it was changed to Jinhua Prefecture; Tingjian was made to share prefectural affairs.

entries.zh: 時上游諸郡次第平定，擇儒臣撫綏之。
entries.en: As the upstream districts were pacified one by one, the Founder chose scholar-officials to govern and reassure them.
entries.literal: At that time the various commanderies upriver were pacified in sequence; Confucian ministers were chosen to pacify and comfort them.

entries.zh: 先後用陶安、汪廣洋於江西，而庭堅與王愷守浙東。
entries.en: Tao An and Wang Guangyang were sent in turn to Jiangxi, while Pan and Wang Kai held eastern Zhejiang.
entries.literal: In succession Tao An and Wang Guangyang were used in Jiangxi, while Tingjian and Wang Kai guarded eastern Zhe.

entries.zh: 太祖為吳王，設翰林院，與安同召為學士。
entries.en: When the Founder became King of Wu he established the Hanlin Academy and summoned Pan and Tao An as academicians.
entries.literal: When the Founder was King of Wu he established the Hanlin Academy and summoned him together with An as Academician.

entries.zh: 而庭堅已老，遂告歸。
entries.en: Pan was already old by then and asked to retire.
entries.literal: But Tingjian was already old and thereupon requested leave to return home.

entries.zh: 洪武四年復召至，主會試。
entries.en: In Hongwu year 4 he was summoned again to preside over the metropolitan examination.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he was again summoned and presided over the metropolitan examination.

entries.zh: 宋思顏，不知何許人。
entries.en: Song Siyan's place of origin is unknown.
entries.literal: Song Siyan—it is not known from what place he came.

entries.zh: 太祖克太平，以思顏居幕府。
entries.en: After the Founder took Taiping, Song served in his headquarters.
entries.literal: When the Founder took Taiping, he had Siyan dwell in the headquarters.

entries.zh: 及定集慶，置江南行中書省，太祖總省事，以李善長及思顏為參議。
entries.en: When Jiqing was secured, the Jiangnan branch secretariat was established with the Founder as its chief; Li Shanchang and Song were made deliberators.
entries.literal: When Jiqing was secured, the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat was established; the Founder oversaw secretariat affairs, and Li Shanchang and Siyan were made Deliberators.

entries.zh: 同時所設省中官李夢庚、郭景祥、侯元善、楊元杲、陶安、阮弘道、孔克仁、王愷、欒鳳、夏煜等數十人。
entries.en: At the same time the secretariat included Li Menggeng, Guo Jingxiang, Hou Yuanshan, Yang Yuangao, Tao An, Ruan Hongdao, Kong Keren, Wang Kai, Luan Feng, Xia Yu, and dozens of others.
entries.literal: At the same time officials established in the secretariat included Li Menggeng, Guo Jingxiang, Hou Yuanshan, Yang Yuangao, Tao An, Ruan Hongdao, Kong Keren, Wang Kai, Luan Feng, Xia Yu, and several tens of others.

entries.zh: 而思顏獨與善長並授參議，其任較諸人為重。
entries.en: Song alone shared the rank of deliberator with Li Shanchang, and his responsibilities were heavier than those of the others.
entries.literal: Yet Siyan alone with Shanchang was jointly granted Deliberator; his charge was heavier than the others'.

entries.zh: 已，建大都督府，以思顏兼參軍事。
entries.en: Soon afterward, when the great military commission was established, Song was also made a staff officer.
entries.literal: Before long the Great Military Commission was established, and Siyan was made concurrent Staff Officer.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗視事東閣，天暑，汗沾衣。
entries.en: Once, while conducting business in the Eastern Pavilion on a hot day, sweat soaked the Founder's clothes.
entries.literal: The Founder once conducted affairs in the Eastern Pavilion; the day was hot and sweat soaked his clothes.

entries.zh: 左右更以衣進，皆數經浣濯者。
entries.en: His attendants brought fresh garments, all of them well-worn from repeated washing.
entries.literal: Those at his side changed and brought in clothes—all had been washed many times.

entries.zh: 思顏曰：「主公躬行節儉，真可示法子孫，惟願終始如一。」
entries.en: Song said, "My lord practices thrift in person—a true model for your descendants; I only hope you will remain so to the end."
entries.literal: Siyan said: "My lord personally practices thrift and restraint—this truly can be shown as a model to sons and grandsons; I only wish it may be the same from beginning to end."

entries.zh: 太祖嘉其直，賜之幣。
entries.en: The Founder praised his frankness and rewarded him with silk.
entries.literal: The Founder praised his forthrightness and bestowed silks on him.

entries.zh: 他日又進曰：「句容虎為害，既捕獲，宜除之，今豢養民間何益？」
entries.en: On another day he said, "The tiger at Jurong has been doing harm; now that it has been captured, it ought to be killed—what good is it to keep it among the people?"
entries.literal: Another day he again advanced and said: "The tiger at Jurong does harm; now that it has been captured, it should be eliminated—what use is it now to keep and raise it among the people?"

entries.zh: 太祖欣然，即命殺虎。
entries.en: The Founder agreed at once and ordered the tiger killed.
entries.literal: The Founder was pleased and at once ordered the tiger killed.

entries.zh: 其隨事納忠類如此。
entries.en: His loyal remonstrances on everyday matters were mostly of this sort.
entries.literal: His offering loyalty on each affair was mostly of this kind.

entries.zh: 後出為河南道按察僉事，坐事死。
entries.en: Later he was sent out as vice commissioner of the Henan surveillance circuit and was executed for an offense.
entries.literal: Later he went out as Vice Commissioner of the Henan Circuit Surveillance Commission and died on account of an offense.

entries.zh: 郭景祥，濠人。
entries.en: Guo Jingxiang was a native of Hao.
entries.literal: Guo Jingxiang was a man of Hao.

entries.zh: 與鳳陽李夢庚皆從渡江，典文書，佐謀議，分任行中書省左右司郎中。
entries.en: He and Li Menggeng of Fengyang both crossed the Yangzi with the Founder, managed documents, assisted in planning, and served as left and right bureau directors of the branch secretariat.
entries.literal: He and Li Menggeng of Fengyang both followed in crossing the river, managed documents, assisted in deliberation, and shared duties as Left and Right Bureau Directors of the Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 既同調浙東分省，尋復同入為大都督府參軍。
entries.en: They were later posted together to the eastern Zhe branch secretariat, then both returned as staff officers of the great military commission.
entries.literal: Having been transferred together to the eastern Zhe Branch Secretariat, before long they again entered together as staff officers of the Great Military Commission.

entries.zh: 景祥性諒直，博涉書史，遇事敢言，太祖親信之。
entries.en: Guo was sincere and upright, widely read in history, and bold in speaking his mind; the Founder trusted him personally.
entries.literal: Jingxiang's nature was sincere and upright; he broadly traversed books and histories; on affairs he dared speak— the Founder personally trusted him.

entries.zh: 嘗曰：「景祥文吏，而有折衝禦侮才，能盡忠於我，可大任也。」
entries.en: The Founder once said, "Guo is a civil official, yet he has the talent to confront enemies and defend the realm; he can be utterly loyal to me and is fit for great responsibility."
entries.literal: He once said: "Jingxiang is a civil clerk, yet has talent to repel foes and resist insult; he can exhaust loyalty to me—great charge can be given."

entries.zh: 先是，克滁州、太平、溧陽。
entries.en: Earlier the army had taken Chuzhou, Taiping, and Liyang.
entries.literal: Earlier, Chuzhou, Taiping, and Liyang had been taken.

entries.zh: 以城郭不完，輒命景祥董治之。
entries.en: Because the city defenses were incomplete, the Founder repeatedly put Guo in charge of repairing them.
entries.literal: Because the city walls and moats were incomplete, he would at once order Jingxiang to supervise and repair them.

entries.zh: 既而和州守臣言，州城久廢，命景祥相度，即故址城之，九旬而工畢。
entries.en: When the Hezhou garrison reported that the city walls had long lain in ruins, the Founder ordered Guo to survey the site and rebuild on the old foundations; the work was finished in ninety days.
entries.literal: Before long the defending official of Hezhou reported that the prefectural city had long been abandoned; he ordered Jingxiang to survey and measure, and on the old site walled it—ninety days and the work was finished.

entries.zh: 太祖以為能，授和州總制。
entries.en: The Founder judged him capable and appointed him overall controller of Hezhou.
entries.literal: The Founder considered him capable and appointed him Overall Controller of Hezhou.

entries.zh: 景祥益治城隍樓櫓，廣屯田，練士卒，威望肅然。
entries.en: Guo further strengthened the walls and towers, expanded garrison farming, drilled the troops, and his authority became formidable.
entries.literal: Jingxiang further repaired city walls, moats, towers, and watchtowers, expanded garrison fields, drilled soldiers and officers, and his prestige and authority were solemn.

entries.zh: 和遂為重鎮。
entries.en: Hezhou thus became a major stronghold.
entries.literal: Hezhou thereupon became a key stronghold.

entries.zh: 璽書褒勞。
entries.en: The Founder sent an imperial letter of commendation.
entries.literal: An imperial letter of commendation praised and comforted him.

entries.zh: 仕終浙江行省參政。
entries.en: He served to the end as vice commissioner of the Zhejiang branch secretariat.
entries.literal: In office he ended as Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 夏煜，字允中，江寧人。
entries.en: Xia Yu, courtesy name Yunzhong, was a native of Jiangning.
entries.literal: Xia Yu, style name Yunzhong, was a man of Jiangning.

entries.zh: 有俊才，工詩，辟為中書省博士。
entries.en: He had outstanding talent and skill in poetry, and was recruited as a doctorate fellow of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: He had outstanding talent, was skilled in poetry, and was recruited as Doctor of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 婺州平，調浙東分省，兩使方國珍，咸稱旨。
entries.en: When Wuzhou was pacified, he was posted to the eastern Zhe branch secretariat; sent twice as envoy to Fang Guozhen, on both occasions to the Founder's satisfaction.
entries.literal: When Wuzhou was pacified, he was transferred to the eastern Zhe Branch Secretariat; twice sent as envoy to Fang Guozhen, and on both occasions won approval.

entries.zh: 太祖征陳友諒，儒臣惟劉基與煜侍。
entries.en: When the Founder campaigned against Chen Youliang, of the Confucian ministers only Liu Ji and Yu attended him.
entries.literal: When the Founder campaigned against Chen Youliang, among Confucian ministers only Liu Ji and Yu attended him.

entries.zh: 鄱陽戰勝，太祖所與草檄賦詩者，煜其一也。
entries.en: After the victory at Lake Poyang, among those with whom the Founder drafted proclamations and composed poems, Yu was one.
entries.literal: At the victory at Poyang, among those with whom the Founder drafted proclamations and composed poems, Yu was one.

entries.zh: 洪武元年使總制浙東諸府，與高見賢、楊憲、凌說四人以伺察搏擊為事，後俱以不良死。
entries.en: In Hongwu 1 he was sent to oversee the prefectures of eastern Zhe; together with Gao Jianxian, Yang Xian, and Ling Shuo, the four devoted themselves to surveillance and persecution, and later all died for misconduct.
entries.literal: In Hongwu year 1 he was sent to oversee the various prefectures of eastern Zhe; together with Gao Jianxian, Yang Xian, and Ling Shuo, the four of them made surveillance and persecution their business, and later all died for misconduct.

entries.zh: 謝再興之守諸全也，部將私販易吳境。
entries.en: While Xie Zaixing was defending Zhuquan, one of his subordinates traded privately across the border into Wu territory.
entries.literal: When Xie Zaixing was defending Zhuquan, a subordinate general privately traded across the Wu border.

entries.zh: 太祖怒殺部將，召諭再興，命夢庚往諸全總制軍事。
entries.en: The Founder had the subordinate executed in anger, summoned Xie to admonish him, and sent Li Menggeng to Zhuquan to take overall command of the army.
entries.literal: The Founder in anger killed the subordinate general, summoned and instructed Zaixing, and ordered Menggeng to go to Zhuquan as overall controller of military affairs.

entries.zh: 再興還鎮，忿夢庚出己上，遂叛。
entries.en: When Xie returned to his post, resentful that Li had been placed over him, he rebelled.
entries.literal: Zaixing returned to his command, resenting that Menggeng was placed above him, and thereupon rebelled.

entries.zh: 執夢庚降於吳，夢庚死之。
entries.en: They seized Li Menggeng and surrendered him to Wu; Li was put to death.
entries.literal: They seized Menggeng and surrendered to Wu; Menggeng died for it.

entries.zh: 其時，參佐行省者，又有毛騏、王濂。
entries.en: At that time, among those assisting the branch secretariat were also Mao Qi and Wang Lian.
entries.literal: At that time, among those assisting the branch secretariat, there were also Mao Qi and Wang Lian.

entries.zh: 濂，字習古，定遠人，李善長婦兄也。
entries.en: Wang Lian, courtesy name Xigu, was a native of Dingyuan and the elder brother of Li Shanchang's wife.
entries.literal: Lian, style name Xigu, was a man of Dingyuan; he was Li Shanchang's wife's older brother.

entries.zh: 才嗜學，事親孝。
entries.en: He was gifted and devoted to study, and filial toward his parents.
entries.literal: He was talented, devoted to learning, and filial in serving his parents.

entries.zh: 初從汝、潁賊，太祖克集慶，乃渡江來歸。
entries.en: At first he followed the rebels of Ru and Ying; after the Founder took Jiqing, he crossed the Yangzi to submit.
entries.literal: At first he followed the Ru and Ying bandits; when the Founder took Jiqing, he crossed the river to submit.

entries.zh: 善長為言，得召見，除執法官，讞獄平允。
entries.en: Li Shanchang spoke on his behalf; he was summoned for an audience, appointed judge of the law, and his judgments were fair and even.
entries.literal: Shanchang spoke on his behalf; he received a summons and audience, was appointed Judge of the Law, and his trial decisions were fair and even.

entries.zh: 遷中書省員外郎，出為浙江按察僉事，治行著聞。
entries.en: He was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat, then sent out as vice commissioner of the Zhejiang surveillance commission, where his record in office won wide notice.
entries.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Secretariat, then sent out as vice commissioner of the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission; his conduct in office was renowned.

entries.zh: 大風晝晦，濂應詔言民瘼，請緩征。
entries.en: When a great wind darkened the sky at midday, Wang responded to an imperial summons to speak on the people's hardships and asked that levies be eased.
entries.literal: A great wind darkened the day at noon; Lian responded to the edict to speak on the people's sufferings and requested that levies be relaxed.

entries.zh: 太祖納之。
entries.en: The Founder accepted his advice.
entries.literal: The Founder accepted it.

entries.zh: 洪武三年卒。
entries.en: He died in Hongwu year 3.
entries.literal: He died in the third year of Hongwu.

entries.zh: 帝謂善長曰：「濂有王佐才，今死，朕失一臂。」
entries.en: The Emperor said to Li Shanchang, "Wang had the talent of a king's minister; now that he is dead, I have lost an arm."
entries.literal: The Emperor said to Shanchang: "Lian had the talent of a royal minister; now that he is dead, I have lost an arm."

entries.zh: 後善長坐事，帝嘆曰：「使王濂在，必不至是。」
entries.en: Later, when Li Shanchang was implicated in a case, the Emperor sighed and said, "If Wang Lian had still been alive, things would surely not have come to this."
entries.literal: Later Shanchang was implicated in a case; the Emperor sighed and said: "If Wang Lian had been alive, it would surely not have come to this."

entries.zh: 騏，字國祥，與濂同里。
entries.en: Mao Qi, courtesy name Guoxiang, was from the same district as Wang Lian.
entries.literal: Qi, style name Guoxiang, was from the same district as Lian.

entries.zh: 太祖自濠引兵趨定遠，騏扶縣令出降。
entries.en: When the Founder led troops from Hao toward Dingyuan, Mao helped the county magistrate come out to surrender.
entries.literal: When the Founder led troops from Hao toward Dingyuan, Qi helped the magistrate out to surrender.

entries.zh: 太祖喜，留與飲食，籌兵事，悉當意。
entries.en: The Founder was pleased, kept him to dine with him, and discussed military affairs; everything Mao said accorded with his wishes.
entries.literal: The Founder was pleased, kept him for food and drink, and discussed military affairs with him—all accorded with his intent.

entries.zh: 取滁州，擢總管府經歷。
entries.en: After Chuzhou was taken, he was promoted to manager of the general administration.
entries.literal: When Chuzhou was taken, he was promoted to manager of the General Administration.

entries.zh: 典倉廩，兼掌晨昏歷，稽將帥之失伍者。
entries.en: He managed the granaries, also kept the schedule of dawn and dusk watches, and inspected commanders who were absent from their posts.
entries.literal: He managed the granaries, also kept the calendar of dawn and dusk watches, and checked commanders absent from their posts.

entries.zh: 從渡江，擢兵省郎中。
entries.en: After crossing the Yangzi, he was promoted to director in the military secretariat.
entries.literal: Following the crossing of the river, he was promoted to director of the Military Secretariat.

entries.zh: 是時太祖左右惟善長及騏，文書機密，皆兩人協贊。
entries.en: At that time only Li Shanchang and Mao Qi stood at the Founder's side; confidential documents were all handled jointly by the two of them.
entries.literal: At that time at the Founder's side there were only Shanchang and Qi; confidential documents—all were jointly handled by the two of them.

entries.zh: 尋授參議官。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was appointed deliberator.
entries.literal: Soon he was appointed Deliberator.

entries.zh: 征婺州，命權理中書省事，委以心膂。
entries.en: During the campaign against Wuzhou, he was ordered to manage Secretariat affairs on a provisional basis and was entrusted as the Founder's right-hand man.
entries.literal: When campaigning for Wuzhou, he was ordered to provisionally manage Secretariat affairs and was entrusted as the Founder's heart and backbone.

entries.zh: 俄病卒，太祖親為文哭之，臨視其葬。
entries.en: Before long he died of illness; the Founder personally composed a funeral elegy and wept for him, and attended the burial in person.
entries.literal: Before long he died of illness; the Founder personally composed a eulogy and wept for him, and attended his burial in person.

entries.zh: 楊元杲、阮弘道，皆滁人，家世皆儒者。
entries.en: Yang Yuangao and Ruan Hongdao were both natives of Chuzhou, from families of Confucian scholars for generations.
entries.literal: Yang Yuangao and Ruan Hongdao were both men of Chuzhou; their families for generations were Confucians.

entries.zh: 從渡江，同為行省左右司員外郎，與陶安等更番掌行機宜文字。
entries.en: After crossing the Yangzi they both served as vice directors of the left and right sections of the branch secretariat, and with Tao An and others took turns handling urgent administrative documents.
entries.literal: Following the river crossing, they both served as vice directors of the left and right sections of the branch secretariat, and with Tao An and others took turns managing urgent administrative documents.

entries.zh: 元杲以郎中擢理軍儲於金華，而弘道亦於是歲以郎中從大都督文正守南昌，皆有功。
entries.en: Yuangao was promoted from director to manage military supplies at Jinhua, while Hongdao in the same year, also as director, followed Grand General Wen Zheng in defending Nanchang; both performed with merit.
entries.literal: Yuangao was promoted from director to manage military supplies at Jinhua, while Hongdao in the same year as director followed Grand General Wen Zheng in defending Nanchang—both had merit.

entries.zh: 二人皆於太祖最故，又皆儒雅，嗜文學，練達政體，而元杲知慮尤周密。
entries.en: Both were among the Founder's oldest associates; both were refined and literary, devoted to letters, and skilled in the ways of government, though Yuangao's forethought was especially thorough.
entries.literal: Both men were among the Founder's oldest associates, and both were refined and literary, devoted to letters, proficient in government—and Yuangao's forethought was especially thorough.

entries.zh: 帝嘗曰：「文臣從渡江，掌簿書文字，勤勞十餘年，無如楊元杲、阮弘道、李夢庚、侯元善、樊景昭者。」
entries.en: The Emperor once said, "Among the civil officials who crossed the Yangzi and managed ledgers and documents, laboring for more than ten years, none compare with Yang Yuangao, Ruan Hongdao, Li Menggeng, Hou Yuanshan, and Fan Jingzhao."
entries.literal: The Emperor once said: "Among civil officials who crossed the river and managed ledgers and documents, laboring over ten years, none compare to Yang Yuangao, Ruan Hongdao, Li Menggeng, Hou Yuanshan, and Fan Jingzhao."

entries.zh: 其後，元杲歷應天府尹，弘道歷福建、江西行省參政，皆卒官。
entries.en: Later, Yuangao served as prefect of Yingtian, and Hongdao served as branch secretariat commissioner in Fujian and Jiangxi; both died in office.
entries.literal: Afterward Yuangao served as prefect of Yingtian, and Hongdao served as branch secretariat commissioner in Fujian and Jiangxi—both died in office.

entries.zh: 又汪河者，舒城人。
entries.en: There was also Wang He, a native of Shucheng.
entries.literal: There was also Wang He, a man of Shucheng.

entries.zh: 嘗師余闕，以文章名。
entries.en: He had once studied under Yu Que and was famed for his literary writing.
entries.literal: He once studied under Yu Que and was famed for his literary writing.

entries.zh: 從渡江，為行中書省掾，數陳時務。
entries.en: He followed the Founder's crossing of the Yangzi and served as a clerk of the branch secretariat, repeatedly presenting policy advice.
entries.literal: He followed in crossing the river and served as clerk of the Branch Secretariat, repeatedly presenting affairs of the age.

entries.zh: 太祖高其才，進大都督府都事。
entries.en: The Founder valued his talent and promoted him to chief clerk of the great military commission.
entries.literal: The Founder valued his talent and advanced him to Chief Clerk of the Great Military Commission.

entries.zh: 使察罕，議論稱旨。
entries.en: Sent as envoy to Chahan, his discussions won the Founder's approval.
entries.literal: Sent as envoy to Chahan, his discussions won approval.

entries.zh: 後奉命偕錢楨至河南，報擴廓聘，為所留。
entries.en: Later, ordered to go with Qian Zhen to Henan to report on Köke Temür's marriage proposal, he was detained.
entries.literal: Later ordered together with Qian Zhen to go to Henan to report on Köke Temür's marriage proposal, he was detained by them.

entries.zh: 太祖前後七致擴廓書，終不報。
entries.en: The Founder sent seven letters to Köke Temür in succession, yet received no reply.
entries.literal: The Founder seven times in succession sent letters to Köke Temür, yet in the end received no reply.

entries.zh: 洪武元年，大軍下河、洛，擴廓走定西，河始得歸，被拘凡六年。
entries.en: In Hongwu 1 the main army descended on the He and Luo regions; Köke Temür fled to Dingxi; He was only then able to return, having been held for six years.
entries.literal: In Hongwu year 1 the great army descended on the He and Luo regions; Köke Temür fled to Dingxi; He was only then able to return, having been detained altogether six years.

entries.zh: 帝甚嘉之，進吏部侍郎，備陳西征方略。
entries.en: The Emperor greatly commended him and promoted him to vice minister of personnel, presenting in detail the strategy for the western campaign.
entries.literal: The Emperor greatly commended him and advanced him to Vice Minister of Personnel, presenting in full the strategy for the western campaign.

entries.zh: 二年改御史臺侍御史。
entries.en: In year 2 he was made an attendant censor of the Censorate.
entries.literal: In year 2 he was changed to Attendant Censor of the Censorate.

entries.zh: 九年，拜晉王左相，親御便殿諭遣之。
entries.en: In year 9 he was appointed left counselor to the Prince of Jin; the Emperor personally received him in the side hall to instruct and send him off.
entries.literal: In year 9 he was appointed Left Counselor of the Prince of Jin; the Emperor personally received him in the side hall to instruct and send him off.

entries.zh: 居數歲，卒於官。
entries.en: After several years in office, he died in his post.
entries.literal: After several years in office, he died in his post.

entries.zh: 子驤，管軍千戶，積功擢親軍指揮僉事。
entries.en: His son Ziang served as a commander of a thousand households and, by accumulated merit, was promoted to assistant commander of the personal guard.
entries.literal: His son Ziang was a commander of a thousand households; by accumulated merit he was promoted to assistant commander of the Personal Guard.

entries.zh: 從定中原，進指揮使。
entries.en: After the pacification of the Central Plains, he was promoted to commander.
entries.literal: Following the pacification of the Central Plains, he advanced to commander.

entries.zh: 滕州段士雄反，驤討平之。
entries.en: When Duan Shixiong of Tengzhou rebelled, Ziang campaigned against him and put down the revolt.
entries.literal: Duan Shixiong of Tengzhou rebelled; Ziang campaigned and pacified him.

entries.zh: 捕倭浙東，斬獲多，擢都督僉事，見親任，嘗掌錦衣衛事，典詔獄。
entries.en: In pursuing Japanese pirates in eastern Zhejiang he took many heads and captives; he was promoted to vice commissioner of the chief command, enjoyed the Founder's trust, once managed the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and oversaw the imperial prison.
entries.literal: Pursuing pirates in eastern Zhejiang, he beheaded and captured many; he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Chief Command, was seen as trusted, once managed the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and oversaw imperial prison cases.

entries.zh: 後坐胡惟庸黨死。
entries.en: Later he was executed as an associate of Hu Weiyong's faction.
entries.literal: Later he was executed as a member of Hu Weiyong's faction.

entries.zh: 孔克仁，句容人。
entries.en: Kong Keren was a native of Jurong.
entries.literal: Kong Keren was a man of Jurong.

entries.zh: 由行省都事進郎中。
entries.en: He rose from chief clerk of the branch secretariat to director.
entries.literal: He advanced from chief clerk of the branch secretariat to director.

entries.zh: 嘗偕宋濂侍太祖，太祖數與論天下形勢及前代興亡事。
entries.en: He once attended the Founder together with Song Lian, and the Founder often discussed with them the strategic situation of the realm and the rise and fall of earlier dynasties.
entries.literal: He once accompanied Song Lian in attending the Founder; the Founder repeatedly discussed with them the world's strategic situation and the rise and fall of former dynasties.

entries.zh: 陳友諒既滅，太祖志圖中原，謂克仁曰：「元運既隳，豪傑互爭，其釁可乘。
entries.en: After Chen Youliang was destroyed, the Founder turned his ambitions toward the Central Plains and said to Kong, "The Yuan mandate is already broken and rival lords contend with one another; the opening can be seized.
entries.literal: After Chen Youliang was destroyed, the Founder set his sights on the Central Plains and said to Keren: "The Yuan mandate is already broken; heroes contend with one another—the opening can be seized.

entries.zh: 吾欲督兩淮、江南諸郡之民，及時耕種，加以訓練。
entries.en: I wish to oversee the people of the Two Huai and the Jiangnan commanderies, have them sow and plow in season, and train them as well.
entries.literal: I wish to oversee the people of the Two Huai and Jiangnan commanderies, sow and plow in season, and also train them.

entries.zh: 兵農兼資，進取退守。
entries.en: With both military and agricultural resources in hand, we can advance or hold our ground.
entries.literal: With both military and agricultural resources, we can advance or retreat and hold firm.

entries.zh: 仍於兩淮間饋運可通之處，儲糧以俟。
entries.en: Moreover, at points between the Two Huai where supply lines can pass, we should store grain and wait.
entries.literal: Moreover at places in the Two Huai where supply transport can pass, store grain and wait.

entries.zh: 兵食既足，中原可圖。
entries.en: Once troops and provisions are sufficient, the Central Plains can be taken.
entries.literal: When troops and provisions are sufficient, the Central Plains can be targeted.

entries.zh: 卿以為何如？」
entries.en: What do you think of this?"
entries.literal: What do you think?"

entries.zh: 克仁對曰：「積糧訓兵，觀釁待時，此長策也。」
entries.en: Kong replied, "To accumulate grain and train troops, watch for openings and await the right moment—this is the long-term strategy."
entries.literal: Keren replied: "Accumulating grain and training troops, watching for openings and awaiting the time—this is the long-term strategy."

entries.zh: 當是時，江左兵勢日盛，太祖以漢高自期，嘗謂克仁曰：「秦政暴虐，漢高帝起布衣，以寬大馭群雄，遂為天下主。
entries.en: At that time military strength east of the Yangzi grew daily; the Founder measured himself against Emperor Gaozu of Han and once said to Kong, "Qin rule was cruel and tyrannical; Emperor Gaozu rose from common cloth, governed the rival lords with magnanimity, and thus became ruler of the realm.
entries.literal: At that time military strength east of the river grew daily; the Founder measured himself against Emperor Gaozu of Han and once said to Keren: "Qin rule was cruel and tyrannical; Emperor Gaozu rose from common cloth, used magnanimity to control the rival lords, and thus became ruler of the realm.

entries.zh: 今群雄蜂起，皆不知修法度以明軍政，此其所以無成也。」
entries.en: Now rival lords swarm forth, yet none know how to establish regulations and clarify military government—this is why they cannot succeed."
entries.literal: Now rival lords swarm forth, all failing to establish regulations and clarify military government—this is why they cannot succeed."

entries.zh: 因感嘆久之。
entries.en: He sighed at length.
entries.literal: Thereupon he sighed long.

entries.zh: 又曰：「天下用兵，河北有孛羅帖木兒，河南有擴廓帖木兒，關中有李思齊、張良弼。
entries.en: He also said, "Across the realm at war, Hebei has Boluo Temür, Henan has Köke Temür, and Guanzhong has Li Siqi and Zhang Liangbi.
entries.literal: He also said: "Under arms across the realm, in Hebei there is Boluo Temür, in Henan there is Köke Temür, and in Guanzhong there are Li Siqi and Zhang Liangbi.

entries.zh: 然有兵而無紀律者河北也；
entries.en: Yet Hebei has troops but no discipline;
entries.literal: Yet Hebei has troops but no discipline;

entries.zh: 稍有紀律而兵不振者河南也；
entries.en: Henan has some discipline but its armies lack vigor;
entries.literal: Henan has some discipline but its troops are not vigorous;

entries.zh: 道途不通、饋餉不繼者關中也。
entries.en: Guanzhong has blocked roads and broken supply lines.
entries.literal: Guanzhong has roads blocked and supply lines cut off.

entries.zh: 江南則惟我與張士誠耳。
entries.en: In Jiangnan there are only Zhang Shicheng and myself.
entries.literal: In Jiangnan it is only I and Zhang Shicheng.

entries.zh: 士誠多奸謀，尚間諜，御眾無紀律。
entries.en: Shicheng relies on treacherous schemes, favors spies, and commands his troops without discipline.
entries.literal: Shicheng uses many treacherous schemes, favors spies, and commands his troops without discipline.

entries.zh: 我以數十萬眾，修軍政，任將帥，相時而動，其勢有不足平者。」
entries.en: With several hundred thousand men under me, if we rectify military government, appoint generals, and move according to the times, their strength can surely not be enough to resist us."
entries.literal: I with several hundred thousand men, rectifying military government, appointing generals, moving according to the times—their power surely cannot be enough to stand against us."

entries.zh: 克仁頓首曰：「主上神武，當定天下於一矣。」
entries.en: Kong bowed and said, "My lord is divinely martial; you will surely unify the realm."
entries.literal: Keren bowed and said: "My lord is divinely martial; you will surely unify the realm as one."

entries.zh: 贊曰：太祖起布衣，經營天下。
entries.en: The commentator says: The Founder rose from common cloth and set about winning the realm.
entries.literal: The commentator says: The Founder rose from common cloth and managed the realm.

entries.zh: 渡江以來，規模宏遠，聲教風馳。
entries.en: Since crossing the Yangzi, his designs have been vast and far-reaching, and his civilizing influence has spread like the wind.
entries.literal: Since crossing the river, his scope was vast and far-reaching, and his civilizing influence spread like wind.

entries.zh: 雖曰天授，抑亦左右丞弼多國士之助歟。
entries.en: Although one may call it heaven's gift, was it not also because the ministers and assistants at his side included many men of national talent?
entries.literal: Although one may say it was heaven's gift, was it not also that the ministers and assistants at his left and right included many outstanding men of the state to help?

entries.zh: 陳遇見禮不下劉基，而超然利祿之外。
entries.en: Chen Yu received honor no less than Liu Ji, yet stood aloof from salary and rank.
entries.literal: Chen Yu received honor no less than Liu Ji, yet stood aloof beyond salary and rank.

entries.zh: 葉兌於天下大計，籌之審矣，亦能抗節肥遯，其高致均非人所易及。
entries.en: Ye Dui deliberated with thoroughness on the great designs for the realm, and could also uphold his integrity and withdraw into reclusion; his lofty character, too, is not easily matched.
entries.literal: Ye Dui on the great designs for the realm deliberated with thoroughness, and could also uphold integrity and withdraw into reclusion—his lofty character alike is not what ordinary men can easily reach.

entries.zh: 孔克仁無可稱述，以太祖之雄謀大略具其事中，故敘列於篇。
entries.en: Kong Keren has nothing especially worth recounting in his own right; because the Founder's heroic stratagems and great designs are fully preserved in the affairs in which he appears, he is therefore included in this chapter.
entries.literal: Kong Keren has nothing specially worth recounting; because the Founder's heroic stratagems and great designs are fully contained in the affairs involving him, he is therefore listed in this chapter.

entries.zh: 克仁侍帷幄最久，故獲聞太祖謀略居多。
entries.en: Kong Keren attended in the command tent longer than anyone else, and so heard more of the Founder's stratagems than the others.
entries.literal: Keren attended in the command tent longest, and so heard most of the Founder's stratagems.

entries.zh: 洪武二年四月，命克仁等授諸子經，功臣子弟亦令入學。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Hongwu year 2, Kong and others were ordered to teach the classics to the princes, and the sons of meritorious ministers were also ordered to enter school.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Hongwu, Keren and others were ordered to teach the classics to the princes; sons of meritorious ministers were also ordered to enter school.

entries.zh: 已，出知江州，入為參議，坐事死。
entries.en: Before long he went out as prefect of Jiangzhou, then returned as deliberator, and was executed for an offense.
entries.literal: Before long he went out as prefect of Jiangzhou, entered as deliberator, and was executed for an offense.

entries.zh: 嘗閱《漢書》，濂與克仁侍。
entries.en: Once, while reading the Book of Han, Song Lian and Kong Keren were in attendance.
entries.literal: Once when reading the Book of Han, Song and Keren attended.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「漢治道不純者何？」
entries.en: The Founder said, "Why was Han governance not pure?"
entries.literal: The Founder said: "Why was Han governance not pure?"

entries.zh: 克仁對曰：「王霸雜故也。」
entries.en: Kong replied, "Because kingship and hegemony were mixed."
entries.literal: Keren replied: "Because kingship and hegemony were mixed."

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「誰執其咎？」
entries.en: The Founder said, "Who bears the blame?"
entries.literal: The Founder said: "Who bears the blame?"

entries.zh: 克仁曰：「責在高祖。」
entries.en: Kong said, "The fault lies with Gaozu."
entries.literal: Keren said: "The fault lies with Gaozu."

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「高祖創業，遭秦滅學，民憔悴甫蘇，禮樂之事固所未講。
entries.en: The Founder said, "Gaozu founded the enterprise at a time when Qin had destroyed learning, the people were worn out and only just reviving, and matters of ritual and music had naturally not yet been addressed.
entries.literal: The Founder said: "Gaozu founded the enterprise, met with Qin's destruction of learning, the people worn and just recovering—matters of ritual and music were naturally not yet discussed.

entries.zh: 孝文為令主，正當制禮作樂，以復三代之舊。
entries.en: Emperor Wen was an excellent ruler; precisely then he should have made rites and music to restore the institutions of the Three Dynasties.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen was an excellent ruler; precisely then he should have made rites and music to restore the old of the Three Dynasties.

entries.zh: 乃逡巡未遑，使漢業終於如是。
entries.en: Yet he hesitated and had no leisure for it, and so Han's enterprise ended as it did.
entries.literal: Yet he hesitated and had no leisure, so Han's enterprise ended thus.

entries.zh: 帝王之道，貴不違時。
entries.en: The way of emperors and kings lies in not acting against the proper time.
entries.literal: The way of emperors and kings values not violating the right time.

entries.zh: 三代之王有其時而能為之，漢文有其時而不為，周世宗則無其時而為之者也。」
entries.en: The kings of the Three Dynasties had their time and were able to act; Emperor Wen of Han had his time but did not act; Emperor Shizong of Zhou had no proper time yet acted anyway."
entries.literal: Kings of the Three Dynasties had their time and could act; Han Wen had his time but did not act; Emperor Shizong of Zhou had no time yet acted."

entries.zh: 又嘗問克仁：「漢高起徒步為萬乘主，所操何道？」
entries.en: He also once asked Kong, "Gaozu of Han rose from a foot soldier to lord of ten thousand chariots—what Way did he follow?"
entries.literal: He also once asked Keren: "Gaozu of Han rose from footsoldier to lord of ten thousand chariots—what Way did he practice?"

entries.zh: 克仁對曰：「知人善任使。」
entries.en: Kong replied, "Knowing men and employing them well."
entries.literal: Keren replied: "Knowing men and appointing them well."

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「項羽南面稱孤，仁義不施，而自矜功伐。
entries.en: The Founder said, "Xiang Yu faced south and styled himself a lone ruler, showed no benevolence or righteousness, yet prided himself on merit and boasted of his victories.
entries.literal: The Founder said: "Xiang Yu faced south and called himself a lone ruler, showed no benevolence and righteousness, yet prided himself on merit and bragged of his victories.

entries.zh: 高祖知其然，承以柔遜，濟以寬仁，卒以勝之。
entries.en: Gaozu knew this; he met him with soft humility and aided his cause with generous benevolence, and in the end overcame him.
entries.literal: Gaozu knew this; he met it with soft humility and aided it with generous benevolence, and in the end overcame him.

entries.zh: 今豪傑非一，我守江左，任賢撫民，以觀天下之變。
entries.en: Now rival lords are many; I hold the left bank of the Yangzi, appoint the worthy and comfort the people, and watch the changes in the realm.
entries.literal: Now rival lords are not one; I hold the left bank of the river, appoint the worthy and comfort the people, to watch the changes in the realm.

entries.zh: 若徒與角力，則猝難定也。」
entries.en: If we merely contend in brute force, sudden settlement will be difficult."
entries.literal: If we merely contend in force, sudden settlement will be hard."

entries.zh: 及徐達等下淮東、西，又謂克仁曰：「壬辰之亂，生民塗炭。
entries.en: When Xu Da and others took eastern and western Huai, he again said to Kong, "In the disorder of the renchen year, the people were burned in fire and crushed on the anvil.
entries.literal: When Xu Da and others took east and west Huai, he again said to Keren: "In the disorder of renchen, the people were burned in fire and crushed on the anvil.

entries.zh: 中原諸將，孛羅擁兵犯闕，亂倫干紀，行已夷滅。
entries.en: Among the generals of the Central Plains, Boluo seized troops and violated the palace, transgressing ethics and order; his line has already been extinguished.
entries.literal: Generals of the Central Plains—Boluo seized troops and violated the palace, violating ethics and transgressing order; he has already been wiped out.

entries.zh: 擴廓挾太子以稱戈，急私仇，無敵愾之志。
entries.en: Köke held the crown prince hostage and took up arms, pressing private enmities and lacking any will to resist the common foe.
entries.literal: Köke held the crown prince hostage and raised arms, was urgent about private enmity, and had no will of righteous anger against the common foe.

entries.zh: 思齊輩碌碌，竊據一方，民受其害。
entries.en: Siqi and his ilk are mediocre men who have seized and hold one region, and the people suffer under them.
entries.literal: Siqi and his ilk were mediocre, stole and held one region—the people suffered their harm.

entries.zh: 士誠外假元名，反覆兩端。
entries.en: Shicheng outwardly borrowed the Yuan name yet wavered between two sides.
entries.literal: Shicheng outwardly borrowed the Yuan name but wavered between two sides.

entries.zh: 明玉珍父子據蜀僭號，喜於自用而無遠謀。
entries.en: Ming Yuzhen and his son hold Shu and have usurped a title; they delight in acting on their own judgment and lack long-range plans.
entries.literal: Ming Yuzhen and his son held Shu and usurped a title, delighted in acting on their own judgment without long-range plans.

entries.zh: 觀其所為，皆不能有成。
entries.en: Judging by their conduct, none of them can succeed.
entries.literal: Observing their conduct, none can succeed.

entries.zh: 予揆天時，審人事，有可定之機。
entries.en: I have measured heaven's timing and examined human affairs, and there is an opening for conquest.
entries.literal: I measure heaven's timing and examine human affairs; there is an opening for conquest.

entries.zh: 今師西出襄、樊，東逾淮、泗，首尾相應，擊之必勝。
entries.en: Now our armies advance west from Xiang and Fan and east beyond the Huai and Si, head and tail responding to one another; strike and we are sure to win.
entries.literal: Now our army west out from Xiang and Fan, east over Huai and Si, head and tail responding—strike and we surely win.

entries.zh: 大事可成，天下不難定。
entries.en: The great enterprise can be accomplished, and the realm will not be hard to settle.
entries.literal: The great enterprise can be accomplished; the realm is not hard to settle.

entries.zh: 既定之後，生息猶難，方勞思慮耳。」
entries.en: After it is settled, restoration and nurturing will still be difficult—that is what will truly tax our thought."
entries.literal: After it is settled, restoration and nurturing will still be difficult—that is what will truly tax our thought."

entries.zh: 安從克集慶，進郎中。
entries.en: An accompanied the campaign that took Jiqing and was promoted to Director in the Secretariat.
entries.literal: An followed in the conquest of Jiqing and was promoted to Director.

entries.zh: 及聘劉基、宋濂、章溢、葉琛至，太祖問安：「四人者何如？」
entries.en: When Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen were brought in, the emperor asked An, "What do you make of these four?"
entries.literal: When Liu Ji, Song Lian, Zhang Yi, and Ye Chen were invited and arrived, the Taizu emperor asked An: "How are these four men?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「臣謀略不如基，學問不如濂，治民之才不如溢、琛。」
entries.en: He answered, "Your servant is no match for Ji in strategy, for Lian in scholarship, or for Yi and Chen in governing the people."
entries.literal: He replied: "In strategy and planning your subject is not equal to Ji; in learning not equal to Lian; in talent to govern the people not equal to Yi and Chen."

entries.zh: 太祖多其能讓。
entries.en: The emperor admired his modesty.
entries.literal: The Taizu emperor greatly valued his ability to yield.

entries.zh: 黃州初下，思得重臣鎮之，無逾安者，遂命知黃州。
entries.en: When Huangzhou was newly pacified, the emperor sought a senior official to secure it and found no one better than An, so he appointed him Huangzhou magistrate.
entries.literal: When Huangzhou was first taken, he thought to obtain a weighty minister to guard it; none surpassed An, so he was ordered to govern Huangzhou.

entries.zh: 寬租省徭，民以樂業。
entries.en: He reduced rents and levies, and the people settled contentedly into their work.
entries.literal: He eased rents and reduced corvée labor; the people thereby took joy in their occupations.

entries.zh: 坐事謫知桐城，移知饒州。
entries.en: After a disciplinary offense he was demoted to Tongcheng and later transferred to Raozhou.
entries.literal: For an offense he was demoted to govern Tongcheng, then transferred to govern Raozhou.

entries.zh: 陳友定兵攻城，安召吏民諭以順逆，嬰城固守。
entries.en: When Chen Youding's army besieged the city, An rallied officials and commoners, explained the difference between loyalty and rebellion, and held the walls in a stubborn defense.
entries.literal: Chen Youding's troops attacked the city; An summoned officials and people and instructed them on obedience and rebellion; they closed the city and firmly defended.

entries.zh: 援兵至，敗去。
entries.en: When relief arrived, the besiegers were defeated and withdrew.
entries.literal: Relief troops arrived and Chen's forces were defeated and withdrew.

entries.zh: 諸將欲盡戮民之從寇者，安不可。
entries.en: The generals wanted to execute every civilian who had sided with the enemy, but An refused.
entries.literal: The various generals wished to slaughter all among the people who had followed the bandit; An would not permit it.

entries.zh: 太祖賜詩褒美，州民建生祠事之。
entries.en: The emperor granted him a poem of commendation, and the people of the prefecture raised a living shrine in his honor.
entries.literal: The Taizu emperor bestowed a poem in praise; the people of the prefecture built a living shrine to serve him.

entries.zh: 洪武元年，命知制誥兼修國史。
entries.en: In the first Hongwu year he was charged with drafting edicts and compiling the dynastic history.
entries.literal: In Hongwu year one he was ordered to draft imperial proclamations and concurrently edit the national history.

entries.zh: 帝嘗御東閣，與安及章溢等論前代興亡本末。
entries.en: The emperor once held court in the Eastern Lodge and debated with An, Zhang Yi, and others the causes of rise and fall in earlier dynasties.
entries.literal: The emperor once took the eastern pavilion and with An and Zhang Yi and others discussed the roots and ends of the rise and fall of former ages.

entries.zh: 安言喪亂之源，由於驕侈。
entries.en: An argued that the root of dynastic collapse was arrogance and lavish excess.
entries.literal: An said the source of ruin and disorder lies in arrogance and extravagance.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「居高位者易驕，處佚樂者易侈。
entries.en: The emperor said, "Those who hold high rank easily grow arrogant, and those who live in comfort easily grow extravagant.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Those who dwell in high position easily become arrogant; those who dwell in ease and pleasure easily become extravagant.

entries.zh: 驕則善言不入，而過不聞；
entries.en: Arrogance shuts out good counsel so that faults go unheard;
entries.literal: When arrogant, good words do not enter and faults are not heard;

entries.zh: 侈則善道不立，而行不顧。
entries.en: extravagance uproots the right path so that conduct is no longer restrained.
entries.literal: when extravagant, the good Way is not established and conduct is not looked back upon.

entries.zh: 如此者，未有不亡。
entries.en: Rulers who fall into this have never failed to fall.
entries.literal: Those like this—none have failed to perish.

entries.zh: 卿言甚當。」
entries.en: Your analysis is entirely apt."
entries.literal: Your words are very apposite."

entries.zh: 又論學術。
entries.en: The conversation turned to learning and doctrine.
entries.literal: They again discussed learning and doctrine.

entries.zh: 安曰：「道不明，邪說害之也。」
entries.en: An said, "When the Way is unclear, heretical teachings are to blame."
entries.literal: An said: "When the Way is not clear, heterodox doctrines harm it."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「邪說害道，猶美味之悅口，美色之眩目。
entries.en: The emperor replied, "Heresy harms the Way as dainties please the palate and bright colors dazzle the eye.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Heterodox doctrines harming the Way are like delicacies pleasing the mouth and beautiful colors dazing the eyes.

entries.zh: 邪說不去，則正道不興，天下何從治？」
entries.en: Until heresy is cleared away the right Way cannot flourish—how can the realm be governed?"
entries.literal: If heterodox doctrines are not removed, then the correct Way cannot rise—how would all under Heaven be governed from?"

entries.zh: 安頓首曰：「陛下所言，可謂深探其本矣。」
entries.en: An kowtowed and said, "Your Majesty has struck the very root of the matter."
entries.literal: An knocked his head and said: "What Your Majesty has spoken may be called deeply probing its root."

entries.zh: 安事帝十余歲，視諸儒最舊。
entries.en: An had served the emperor for more than a decade and was the senior-most of the scholarly counselors.
entries.literal: An had served the emperor more than ten years; among the various scholars he was the most senior.

entries.zh: 及官侍從，寵愈渥。
entries.en: Once he entered the inner circle of attendants, imperial favor only deepened.
entries.literal: When he reached the office of attendant and follower, favor grew ever richer.

entries.zh: 御制門帖子賜之曰：「國朝謀略無雙士，翰苑文章第一家。」
entries.en: The emperor personally composed a couplet for his gate: "Unrivaled strategist of the dynasty; foremost writer of the academy."
entries.literal: The emperor in his own hand composed a gate couplet and bestowed it on him, saying: "Of the dynasty's strategists, an unrivaled man; of the Hanlin garden's writings, the foremost family."

entries.zh: 時人榮之。
entries.en: Contemporaries regarded this as the highest honor.
entries.literal: Men of the time took it as glory.

entries.zh: 御史或言安隱過。
entries.en: A censor reported that An had concealed misconduct.
entries.literal: A censor at times spoke of An's hidden faults.

entries.zh: 帝詰曰：「安寧有此，且若何從知？」
entries.en: The emperor demanded, "Would An truly do such a thing—and how do you know?"
entries.literal: The emperor interrogated: "Could An truly have this? Moreover, how did you come to know?"

entries.zh: 曰：「聞之道路。」
entries.en: The censor answered, "I heard it on the streets."
entries.literal: He said: "I heard it on the road."

entries.zh: 帝大怒，立黜之。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage and had him dismissed on the spot.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and immediately dismissed him.

entries.zh: 洪武元年，與侍御史文原吉、起居注魏觀等循行天下，訪求賢才。
entries.en: In the first Hongwu year he traveled the realm with the attending censor Wen Yuanji, the recorder Wei Guan, and others to seek out men of talent.
entries.literal: In Hongwu year one, together with Attending Censor Wen Yuanji, Daily Records Wei Guan, and others, he made a circuit of all under Heaven seeking worthy talents.

entries.zh: 還，進翰林直學士，遷侍讀學士。
entries.en: On his return he was made a direct Hanlin academician and then promoted to reader-in-waiting.
entries.literal: On return he advanced to Hanlin Direct Academician and was transferred to Reader-in-Waiting.

entries.zh: 帝御下峻，御史中丞劉基曰：「古者公卿有罪，盤水加劍，詣請室自裁，所以勵廉恥，存國體也。」
entries.en: The emperor ruled harshly. Vice censor-in-chief Liu Ji said, "In antiquity, when high ministers offended, they were given a tray of water and a sword and went to the execution chamber to take their own lives—this was how integrity was enforced and the dignity of the state preserved."
entries.literal: The emperor was stern toward subordinates; Vice Censor-in-chief Liu Ji said: "In antiquity when dukes and ministers had offenses, tray of water and sword were added; they went to the execution chamber to cut themselves short—this was to encourage integrity and shame and preserve the state's stature."

entries.zh: 同時侍側，遂取《戴記》及賈誼疏以進，復剴切言之。
entries.en: Tong, who was attending nearby, cited the Record of Rites and Jia Yi's memorial and pressed the point with further earnest argument.
entries.literal: Tong was at the time attending at his side; he thereupon took the Record of Rites and Jia Yi's memorial and advanced them, again speaking with earnest incisiveness.

entries.zh: 帝嘗與侍臣言：聲色之害甚於鴆毒，創業之君，為子孫所承式，尤不可不謹。
entries.en: The emperor once told his attendants that the lure of pleasure was deadlier than poison and that a founding ruler, being the model for his heirs, must be doubly careful.
entries.literal: The emperor once spoke to attendant ministers: the harm of sound and color exceeds that of poison wine; a ruler who founds the enterprise is the model his descendants inherit—especially he must be cautious.

entries.zh: 同因舉成湯不邇聲色，垂裕後昆以對。
entries.en: Tong answered by citing how King Tang kept his distance from sensual delights to leave a legacy for his descendants.
entries.literal: Tong thereupon cited that King Tang did not approach sound and color, extending abundance to his posterity, in reply.

entries.zh: 其因事納忠如此。
entries.en: Thus he offered loyal remonstrance whenever occasion arose.
entries.literal: His offering loyal counsel on occasions was like this.

entries.zh: 張籌，字惟中，無錫人。
entries.en: Zhang Chou, styled Weizhong, was from Wuxi.
entries.literal: Zhang Chou, style name Weizhong, was a man of Wuxi.

entries.zh: 父翼，嘗勸張士誠將莫天佑降，復請於平章胡美勿僇降人，城中人得完。
entries.en: His father Zhang Yi had urged Zhang Shicheng to accept Mo Tianyou's surrender and persuaded Commissioner Hu Mei not to massacre the surrendered, sparing the city's population.
entries.literal: His father Yi had once urged Zhang Shicheng to have Mo Tianyou submit, and again requested of Pacification Commissioner Hu Mei not to slaughter those who surrendered, so the people in the city were preserved intact.

entries.zh: 以詹同薦，授翰林應奉，改禮部主事。
entries.en: Recommended by Zhan Tong, he was appointed to respond to imperial compositions in the Hanlin Academy and later made a section chief in the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: On Zhan Tong's recommendation he was appointed Hanlin Responding to Imperial Composition and changed to Ritual Department Section Chief.

entries.zh: 奉詔與尚書陶凱編集漢、唐以來籓王事跡，為《歸鑒錄》。
entries.en: By imperial order he and Minister Tao Kai compiled the deeds of feudal princes from Han and Tang onward into the Returning Mirror Record.
entries.literal: By imperial command together with Minister Tao Kai he compiled deeds of feudal princes from Han and Tang onward, making the Returning Mirror Record.

entries.zh: 洪武九年，由員外郎進尚書，與學士宋濂定諸王妃喪服之制。
entries.en: In the ninth Hongwu year he rose from vice director to minister and, with Song Lian, set mourning regulations for princely consorts.
entries.literal: In Hongwu year nine, from Vice Director he advanced to Minister and with Academician Song Lian fixed the mourning-garb system for various princely consorts.

entries.zh: 籌記誦淹博，在禮曹久，諳於歷代禮文沿革。
entries.en: Chou had a prodigious memory; after long service in the Ministry of Rites he knew the evolution of ritual texts through the ages.
entries.literal: Chou's memory and recitation were broad and deep; long in the Ritual Office, he was thoroughly versed in the evolution of ritual texts through the ages.

entries.zh: 然頗善附會。
entries.en: Yet he was inclined to force classical texts to fit present needs.
entries.literal: Yet he was rather good at forced interpretation.

entries.zh: 初，陶安等定圜丘、方澤、宗廟、社稷諸儀，行數年矣。
entries.en: Tao An and others had years earlier set rites for the Round Mound, Square Mound, ancestral temple, and state altars.
entries.literal: At the beginning Tao An and others had fixed the rites of the Round Mound, Square Mound, ancestral temple, and state altar, and they had been practiced several years.

entries.zh: 洪武九年，籌為尚書，乃更議合社稷為一壇，罷勾龍、棄配位，奉仁祖配饗，以明祖社尊而親之之道，遂以社稷與郊廟祀並列上祀。
