entries.en: As minister in the ninth year Chou merged the altars of soil and grain into one, removed Gou Long and Qi from associated worship, and enshrined the founding emperor's father there, elevating the state altars to the highest tier of sacrifice alongside suburban rites.
entries.literal: In Hongwu year nine Chou became Minister and then again deliberated merging the state altars into one altar, abolishing the associated positions of Gou Long and Qi, offering the benevolent ancestor as associated sacrifice, to clarify the Way of honoring the state altars while treating them as kin—and thus placed the state altars in upper sacrifice alongside suburban and temple sacrifice.

entries.zh: 識者竊非之。
entries.en: Knowledgeable observers quietly disapproved.
entries.literal: Men of insight privately disapproved.

entries.zh: 已，出為湖廣參政。
entries.en: He was soon posted as administrative commissioner of Huguang.
entries.literal: Before long he went out as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.

entries.zh: 十年坐事罰輸作。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was sentenced to corvée labor for an offense.
entries.literal: In year ten for an offense he was penalized to perform labor service.

entries.zh: 十二年仍起禮部員外郎。
entries.en: In the twelfth year he was restored as vice director in the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: In year twelve he was still raised as Ritual Department Vice Director.

entries.zh: 後復官，以事免。
entries.en: He was later reappointed but dismissed again after another incident.
entries.literal: Later his office was restored again; for an affair he was dismissed.

entries.zh: 贊曰：明初之議禮也，宋濂方家居，諸儀率多陶安裁定。
entries.en: The appraiser writes: When the Ming first debated ritual, Song Lian was still in retirement and Tao An settled most of the forms.
entries.literal: The eulogy says: In the early Ming deliberation on ritual, Song Lian was still at home; the various ceremonies were mostly drawn up and settled by Tao An.

entries.zh: 大祀禮專用安議，其餘參匯諸說，從其所長：祫禘用詹同，時享用硃升，釋奠、耕耤用錢用壬，五祀用崔亮，朝會用劉基，祝祭用魏觀，軍禮用陶凱。
entries.en: Great sacrifices followed An exclusively; other rites combined specialists—Zhan Tong for collective and seasonal rites, Zhu Sheng for seasonal offerings, Qian Yongren for Confucian sacrifice and plowing, Cui Liang for the five sacrifices, Liu Ji for court audiences, Wei Guan for prayer sacrifices, and Tao Kai for military ritual.
entries.literal: Great-sacrifice ritual exclusively used An's deliberations; the rest combined various opinions, following each man's strength: collective and seasonal sacrifice used Zhan Tong, seasonal offerings used Zhu Sheng, Confucian sacrifice and royal plowing used Qian Yongren, the five sacrifices used Cui Liang, court audiences used Liu Ji, prayer-sacrifice used Wei Guan, military ritual used Tao Kai.

entries.zh: 皆能援據經義，酌古準今，郁然成一代休明之治。
entries.en: All cited the classics, weighed antiquity against the present, and helped shape a brilliant age of governance.
entries.literal: All were able to cite classical meaning, weigh antiquity against the present, and richly form the brilliant governance of a generation.

entries.zh: 雖折中斷制，裁自上心，諸臣之功亦曷可少哉。
entries.en: Though final decisions rested with the emperor, the ministers' contributions can hardly be slighted.
entries.literal: Although the final compromise and judgment and cutting were from the ruler's own mind, how could the merit of the various ministers be slighted?

entries.zh: 陶安，字主敬，當塗人。
entries.en: Tao An, styled Zhujing, was from Dangtu.
entries.literal: Tao An, with the style name Zhujing, was a man of Dangtu.

entries.zh: 少敏悟，博涉經史，尤長於《易》。
entries.en: As a youth he was exceptionally quick-witted; he read widely in the classics and histories and was especially skilled in the Book of Changes.
entries.literal: In youth he was perceptive and quick; he ranged broadly through the classics and histories, and was especially accomplished in the Book of Changes.

entries.zh: 元至正初，舉江浙鄉試，授明道書院山長，避亂家居。
entries.en: Early in the Zhizheng reign, he passed the Jiang and Zhe regional examination and was appointed director of the Mingdao Academy; he then retired at home to escape the civil unrest.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan Zhizheng era, he passed the Jiang-Zhe provincial examination, was appointed headmaster of the Mingdao Academy, and stayed at home to avoid the turmoil.

entries.zh: 太祖取太平，安與耆儒李習率父老出迎。
entries.en: When the founding emperor captured Taiping, An and the elder scholar Li Xi led the local elders out to welcome him.
entries.literal: When the Taizu emperor took Taiping, An together with the venerable scholar Li Xi led the elders to go out and welcome him.

entries.zh: 太祖召與語。
entries.en: The emperor summoned him for an audience.
entries.literal: The Taizu emperor summoned him and conversed with him.

entries.zh: 安進曰：「海內鼎沸，豪傑並爭，然其意在子女玉帛，非有撥亂、救民、安天下心。
entries.en: An spoke up: "The empire is in uproar and rival strongmen fight one another, but their aim is spoil and luxury, not to restore order, relieve the people, or bring peace to the realm.
entries.literal: An advanced and said: "Within the seas the tripod boils; heroes struggle with one another, yet their intent lies in children, women, jade, and silks—they lack the mind to put chaos in order, save the people, and settle all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 明公渡江，神武不殺，人心悅服，應天順人。
entries.en: Your Grace has crossed the Yangzi with a martial spirit that shuns needless slaughter; the people gladly submit. You answer Heaven's mandate and win men over.
entries.literal: My lord has crossed the Yangzi: divine in martial prowess and sparing in killing; hearts rejoice and submit—he responds to Heaven and accords with men.

entries.zh: 以行吊伐，天下不足平也。」
entries.en: March forth as the champion of the wronged, and pacifying the realm will be a small matter."
entries.literal: By acting as one who comforts the wronged and punishes the guilty, all under Heaven is not enough to remain un pacified."

entries.zh: 太祖問曰：「吾欲取金陵，何如？」
entries.en: The emperor asked, "I mean to take Jinling. What do you think?"
entries.literal: The Taizu emperor asked: "I wish to take Jinling—how would that be?"

entries.zh: 安曰：「金陵，古帝王都。
entries.en: An replied, "Jinling was the seat of emperors in antiquity.
entries.literal: An said: "Jinling is the ancient capital of emperors and kings.

entries.zh: 取而有之，撫形勝以臨四方，何向不克？」
entries.en: Seize it and hold its strategic heights to command the four quarters—what enemy could withstand you?"
entries.literal: Take it and possess it; soothe its commanding terrain to look down on the four directions—what direction would not be overcome?"

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「善。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Well said."
entries.literal: The Taizu emperor said: "Good."

entries.zh: 留參幕府，授左司員外郎，以習為太平知府。
entries.en: He was retained on the military staff as Left Department Assistant Director, and Li Xi was appointed prefect of Taiping.
entries.literal: He was kept to participate in the staff headquarters and appointed Left Department Assistant Director; Li Xi was made Taiping prefect.

entries.zh: 習字伯羽，年八十余矣，卒於官。
entries.en: Li Xi, styled Boyu, was over eighty and died in his post.
entries.literal: Xi, style name Boyu, was more than eighty years old and died in office.

entries.zh: 明開國時即重師儒官。
entries.en: From the founding of the dynasty, Ming already placed great weight on posts for teachers and Confucian scholars.
entries.literal: At the founding of Ming, posts for masters and Confucian scholars were already highly valued.

entries.zh: 許存仁、魏觀為祭酒，老成端謹；
entries.en: Xu Cunren and Wei Guan served as Chancellor; they were mature, steady, and dignified;
entries.literal: Xu Cunren and Wei Guan served as Chancellor; they were mature, steady, and careful;

entries.zh: 訥稍晚進，最蒙遇。
entries.en: Ne entered somewhat later and enjoyed the greatest imperial favor.
entries.literal: Ne entered somewhat later and received the greatest favor.

entries.zh: 與訥定學規者，司業王嘉會、龔斅。
entries.en: Those who worked with Ne to establish the school regulations were Vice Chancellors Wang Jiahui and Gong Xiao.
entries.literal: Those who with Ne established the school regulations were Vice Chancellors Wang Jiahui and Gong Xiao.

entries.zh: 三人年俱高，鬚髮皓白，終日危坐，堂上肅然。
entries.en: All three were advanced in years, with snow-white beards and hair; they sat upright throughout the day, and the hall was solemn.
entries.literal: All three were advanced in years, their beards and hair snow-white; they sat upright all day, and the hall was solemn.

entries.zh: 而張美和、聶鉉、貝瓊等皆名儒，當洪武時，先後為博士、助教、學錄，以故諸生多所成就。
entries.en: Zhang Meihe, Nie Xuan, Bei Qiong, and others were all renowned Confucian scholars; during Hongwu they served in turn as Erudite, Assistant Instructor, and Recorder, and for this reason many students achieved distinction.
entries.literal: Moreover Zhang Meihe, Nie Xuan, Bei Qiong, and others were all famous Confucians; during Hongwu they served in succession as Erudite, Assistant Instructor, and Recorder, and for this reason many students achieved distinction.

entries.zh: 魏觀事別載。
entries.en: Wei Guan's biography is recorded separately.
entries.literal: Wei Guan's affairs are recorded separately.

entries.zh: 趙俶，字本初，山陰人。
entries.en: Zhao Chu, style name Benchu, was a native of Shanyin.
entries.literal: Zhao Chu, style name Benchu, was a native of Shanyin.

entries.zh: 元進士。
entries.en: He was a jinshi graduate of the Yuan dynasty.
entries.literal: A Yuan-dynasty jinshi graduate.

entries.zh: 洪武六年，征授國子博士。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Hongwu he was summoned and appointed erudite at the Directorate of the National University.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu, he was summoned and appointed Erudite at the Directorate of the National University.

entries.zh: 帝嘗禦奉天殿，召俶及錢宰、貝瓊等曰：「汝等一以孔子所定經書為教，慎勿雜蘇秦、張儀縱橫之言。」
entries.en: The Emperor once held court in the Hall of Upholding Heaven and summoned Chu, Qian Zai, Bei Qiong, and others, saying, "You must teach only the classics established by Confucius as your teaching. Be careful not to introduce the stratagem rhetoric of Su Qin and Zhang Yi."
entries.literal: The Emperor once held court in the Hall of Upholding Heaven, summoned Chu along with Qian Zai, Bei Qiong, and others, and said: "You shall take exclusively the classics established by Confucius as your teaching; be careful not to mix in the stratagem rhetoric of Su Qin and Zhang Yi."

entries.zh: 諸臣頓首受命。
entries.en: The officials all kowtowed and accepted the command.
entries.literal: The officials all kowtowed and accepted the command.

entries.zh: 俶因請頒正定《十三經》於天下，屏《戰國策》及陰陽讖卜諸書，勿列學宮。
entries.en: Chu then asked that the corrected 《Thirteen Classics》 be promulgated throughout the realm, and that the 《Strategies of the Warring States》 together with works on yin-yang lore, prophecy, and divination be barred from the academies.
entries.literal: Chu thereupon requested that the corrected 《Thirteen Classics》 be promulgated throughout the realm, and that the 《Strategies of the Warring States》 together with books on yin-yang lore, prophecy, and divination be excluded and not placed in the academies.

entries.zh: 明年擇諸生穎異者三十五人，命俶專領之，教以古文。
entries.en: The following year thirty-five exceptionally gifted students were chosen, and Chu was ordered to take charge of them and teach them ancient-style prose.
entries.literal: The next year thirty-five outstanding students were selected, and Chu was ordered to take charge of them exclusively and teach them ancient-style prose.

entries.zh: 尋擢李擴、黃義等入文華、武英二堂說書，皆見用。
entries.en: Soon Li Kuo, Huang Yi, and others were promoted to lecture in the Wenhua and Wuying halls, and all were put to use.
entries.literal: Soon Li Kuo, Huang Yi, and others were promoted to lecture in the Wenhua and Wuying halls, and all were employed.

entries.zh: 九年，御史臺言：「博士俶以《詩經》教成均四年，其弟子多為方嶽重臣及持節各部者。
entries.en: In the ninth year the Censorate reported, "Erudite Chu has taught the 《Classic of Poetry》 at the Imperial Academy for four years, and many of his disciples have become leading provincial ministers and imperial envoys in various departments.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Censorate reported: "Erudite Chu has taught the 《Classic of Poetry》 at the Imperial Academy for four years; many of his disciples have become great ministers of provincial governors and envoys holding imperial insignia in various departments.

entries.zh: 今年逾懸車，請賜骸骨。」
entries.en: This year he has passed the age of retirement and asks to be permitted to return home."
entries.literal: This year he has passed the age for retiring, and requests to be granted leave to return his bones."

entries.zh: 於是以翰林院待制致仕，賜內帑錢治裝。
entries.en: Thereupon he retired with the title of Hanlin attendant draftsman and was granted money from the inner treasury for his journey home.
entries.literal: Thereupon he retired with the title Hanlin Academy Attendant Draftsman and was granted money from the inner treasury for travel expenses.

entries.zh: 宋濂率同官暨諸生千余人送之。
entries.en: Song Lian led more than a thousand fellow officials and students to see him off.
entries.literal: Song Lian led more than a thousand fellow officials and students to see him off.

entries.zh: 卒年八十一。
entries.en: He died at the age of eighty-one.
entries.literal: He died at the age of eighty-one.

entries.zh: 子圭玉，兵部侍郎，出知萊州，有聲。
entries.en: His son Guiyu became vice minister of war and went out to serve as prefect of Laizhou, where he earned a fine reputation.
entries.literal: His son Guiyu became Vice Minister of War and went out to serve as Prefect of Laizhou, where he won renown.

entries.zh: 劉三吾
entries.en: Liu Sanwu
entries.literal: Liu Sanwu

entries.zh: 〈（汪睿朱善）〉
entries.en: (Wang Rui and Zhu Shan)〉
entries.literal: (Wang Rui, Zhu Shan)〉

entries.zh: 安然
entries.en: An Ran
entries.literal: An Ran

entries.zh: 〈（王本等）〉
entries.en: (Wang Ben and others)〉
entries.literal: (Wang Ben and others)〉

entries.zh: 吳伯宗
entries.en: Wu Bozong
entries.literal: Wu Bozong

entries.zh: 〈（鮑恂任亨泰）〉
entries.en: (Bao Xun and Ren Hengtai)〉
entries.literal: (Bao Xun, Ren Hengtai)〉

entries.zh: 吳沈桂彥良
entries.en: Wu Chen and Gui Yanliang
entries.literal: Wu Chen, Gui Yanliang

entries.zh: 〈（李希顏徐宗實陳南賓劉淳董子莊趙季通楊黼金實等）〉
entries.en: (Li Xiyan, Xu Zongshi, Chen Nanbin, Liu Chun, Dong Zizhuang, Zhao Jitong, Yang Fu, Jin Shi, and others)〉
entries.literal: (Li Xiyan, Xu Zongshi, Chen Nanbin, Liu Chun, Dong Zizhuang, Zhao Jitong, Yang Fu, Jin Shi, and others)〉

entries.zh: 宋訥
entries.en: Song Ne
entries.literal: Song Ne

entries.zh: 〈（許存仁張美和聶鉉貝瓊）〉

entries.literal: (Elder brother Xiong, Wang Shihong, Ni Mengxian, and Lang Min appended)

entries.zh: 青文勝
entries.en: Qing Wensheng
entries.literal: Qing Wensheng

entries.zh: 魏觀，字杞山，蒲圻人。
entries.en: Wei Guan, whose style was Qishan, came from Puqi.
entries.literal: Wei Guan, styled Qishan, was a native of Puqi.

entries.zh: 元季隱居蒲山。
entries.en: In the closing years of the Yuan dynasty he withdrew to live in seclusion on Pu Mountain.
entries.literal: At the end of the Yuan he lived in seclusion on Pu Mountain.

entries.zh: 太祖下武昌，聘授國子助教，再遷浙江按察司僉事。
entries.en: After the Founding Emperor captured Wuchang, Guan was summoned and made an assistant instructor at the Directorate of Education, then promoted to vice commissioner of the Zhejiang surveillance commission.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor took Wuchang, he was invited and appointed Assistant Instructor at the Directorate of Education, then was transferred again to Vice Commissioner of the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission.

entries.zh: 吳元年，遷兩淮都轉運使。
entries.en: In the first year of the Wu regime he was appointed director of transport for the Two Huai region.
entries.literal: In the first year of Wu he was transferred to Director of Transport for the Two Huai.

entries.zh: 入為起居註。
entries.en: He was brought into the capital as recorder of imperial actions.
entries.literal: He entered service as Recorder of Imperial Actions.

entries.zh: 奉命偕吳琳以幣帛求遺賢於四方。
entries.en: On imperial command he joined Wu Lin in traveling the realm with gifts of silk and cloth to seek out neglected men of talent.
entries.literal: By order he accompanied Wu Lin, bearing silks and gifts to seek out lost worthies in every quarter.

entries.zh: 洪武元年，建大本堂，命侍太子說書及授諸王經。
entries.en: In Hongwu 1 the Great Foundation Hall was established, and he was charged with attending the crown prince in classical instruction and teaching the imperial princes.
entries.literal: In the first year of Hongwu the Great Foundation Hall was built, and he was ordered to attend the crown prince in lecturing on the classics and to instruct the princes in the classics.

entries.zh: 未幾，又命偕文原吉、詹同、吳輔、趙壽等分行天下，訪求遺才，所舉多擢用。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was again sent out with Wen Yuanji, Zhan Tong, Wu Fu, Zhao Shou, and others to scour the empire for overlooked talent; most of their nominees were raised to office.
entries.literal: Before long he was again ordered, together with Wen Yuanji, Zhan Tong, Wu Fu, Zhao Shou, and others, to travel the realm in separate parties seeking out neglected talent; most of those they recommended were promoted and employed.

entries.zh: 三年，轉太常卿，考訂諸祀典。
entries.en: In the third year he became minister of ceremonies and undertook a systematic review of the state ritual codes.
entries.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies and examined and revised the various sacrificial regulations.

entries.zh: 稱旨，改侍讀學士，尋遷祭酒。
entries.en: The Emperor was pleased with his work and made him a reader-in-waiting, then shortly afterward promoted him to libationer of the Directorate of Education.
entries.literal: His work pleased the Emperor, and he was changed to Reader-in-Waiting, then soon promoted to Libationer.

entries.zh: 明年坐考祀孔子禮不以時奏，謫知龍南縣，旋召為禮部主事。
entries.en: The following year he was punished for failing to submit his review of Confucian temple rites on schedule and was demoted to magistrate of Longnan County, but was soon recalled as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
entries.literal: The next year, on a charge of reporting the examination of Confucian sacrificial rites not at the proper time, he was demoted to magistrate of Longnan county, then soon recalled as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

entries.zh: 五年，廷臣薦觀才，出知蘇州府。
entries.en: In the fifth year court officials recommended Guan's ability, and he was appointed prefect of Suzhou.
entries.literal: In the fifth year court ministers recommended Guan's talent, and he was sent out as prefect of Suzhou.

entries.zh: 前守陳寧苛刻，人呼「陳烙鐵」。
entries.en: His predecessor Chen Ning had ruled with harsh severity, and the people nicknamed him "Iron Brand Chen."
entries.literal: The previous prefect Chen Ning was harsh and exacting; people called him "Iron Brand Chen."

entries.zh: 觀盡改寧所為，以明教化、正風俗為治。
entries.en: Guan reversed everything Ning had put in place and made his administration a project of moral instruction and the reform of local custom.
entries.literal: Guan completely changed what Ning had done, taking clarification of teaching and transformation and correction of customs as his governing principle.

entries.zh: 建黌舍。
entries.en: He founded a school.
entries.literal: He built a school hall.

entries.zh: 聘周南老、王行、徐用誠，與教授貢潁之定學儀；
entries.en: He engaged Zhou Nanlao, Wang Xing, and Xu Yongcheng, and together with the instructor Gong Yingzhi drew up the school's ceremonial regulations;
entries.literal: He engaged Zhou Nanlao, Wang Xing, and Xu Yongcheng, and together with Instructor Gong Yingzhi fixed the school ceremonies;

entries.zh: 王彜、高啟、張羽訂經史；
entries.en: Wang Yi, Gao Qi, and Zhang Yu edited the classical and historical texts;
entries.literal: Wang Yi, Gao Qi, and Zhang Yu revised the classics and histories;

entries.zh: 耆民周壽誼、楊茂、林文友行鄉飲酒禮。
entries.en: and the village elders Zhou Shouyi, Yang Mao, and Lin Wenyou presided over the community drinking rites.
entries.literal: the elders Zhou Shouyi, Yang Mao, and Lin Wenyou conducted the village drinking ceremony.

entries.zh: 政化大行，課績為天下最。
entries.en: His policies took deep root, and his administrative rating ranked first in the empire.
entries.literal: Government and transformation were carried out on a grand scale, and his performance rating was the highest in the realm.

entries.zh: 明年擢四川行省參知政事。
entries.en: The following year he was promoted to vice administrator of the Sichuan branch secretariat.
entries.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Administrator of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.

entries.zh: 未行，以部民乞留，命還任。
entries.en: Before he could leave, the populace petitioned to keep him, and the throne ordered him to resume his post.
entries.literal: Before he departed, because the people of his department begged that he remain, he was ordered to return to his post.

entries.zh: 初，張士誠以蘇州舊治為宮，遷府治於都水行司。
entries.en: Earlier, Zhang Shicheng had turned Suzhou's old government compound into a palace and relocated the prefectural offices to the waterways directorate.
entries.literal: Earlier, Zhang Shicheng had taken the old seat of government in Suzhou as his palace and moved the prefectural seat to the Directorate of Waterways.

entries.zh: 觀以其地湫隘，還治舊基。
entries.en: Finding the new site damp and cramped, Guan moved the government back to its former location.
entries.literal: Guan, because that site was low-lying and cramped, returned administration to the old foundations.

entries.zh: 又浚錦帆涇，興水利。
entries.en: He also dredged the Brocade Sail Canal and undertook hydraulic works.
entries.literal: He also dredged the Brocade Sail Canal and promoted water conservancy.

entries.zh: 或譖觀興既滅之基。
entries.en: Someone accused him of rebuilding on ground associated with a defeated regime.
entries.literal: Someone slandered Guan for raising foundations already destroyed.

entries.zh: 帝使御史張度廉其事，遂被誅。
entries.en: The Emperor dispatched Censor Zhang Du to investigate on the spot, and Guan was put to death.
entries.literal: The Emperor sent Censor Zhang Du to investigate the matter on the spot, and Guan was thereupon executed.

entries.zh: 帝亦尋悔，命歸葬。
entries.en: The Emperor soon came to regret the decision and ordered Guan's remains sent home for burial.
entries.literal: The Emperor also soon regretted it and ordered that his body be returned for burial.

entries.zh: 王觀，字尚賓，祥符人。
entries.en: Wang Guan, whose style was Shangbin, came from Xiangfu.
entries.literal: Wang Guan, styled Shangbin, was a native of Xiangfu.

entries.zh: 性耿介，儀度英偉，善談論。
entries.en: Upright and unyielding by nature, he had a commanding presence and was an engaging speaker.
entries.literal: By nature he was upright and unyielding; his bearing was heroic and imposing, and he was skilled in discourse.

entries.zh: 由鄉薦入太學，擢知蘇州府。
entries.en: Recommended from his district, he entered the Directorate of Education and was appointed prefect of Suzhou.
entries.literal: Through provincial recommendation he entered the Directorate of Education and was selected as prefect of Suzhou.

entries.zh: 公廉有威。
entries.en: He was upright, incorruptible, and commanded respect.
entries.literal: He was public-spirited, incorrupt, and possessed authority.

entries.zh: 黠吏錢英屢陷長官，觀捶殺之。
entries.en: A crafty clerk named Qian Ying had repeatedly framed his superiors; Guan had him beaten to death.
entries.literal: The cunning clerk Qian Ying had repeatedly entrapped his superiors; Guan beat him to death.

entries.zh: 事聞，太祖遣行人賫敕褒之，勞以禦酒。
entries.en: When word reached the throne, the Founding Emperor sent an envoy with an edict of praise and rewarded him with imperial wine.
entries.literal: When the matter was reported, the Founding Emperor sent an envoy bearing an edict to praise him and rewarded him with imperial wine.

entries.zh: 歲大，民多逋賦，部使者督甚急。
entries.en: In a year of severe drought many taxpayers fell into arrears, and the ministry envoy pressed collection relentlessly.
entries.literal: In a year of great drought many people defaulted on taxes; the ministry envoy pressed collection with extreme urgency.

entries.zh: 觀置酒，延諸富人，勸貸貧民償，辭指誠懇，富人皆感動，逋賦以完。
entries.en: Guan held a feast for the wealthy and urged them to lend money so the poor could pay their taxes. His appeal was so sincere that the rich were moved to comply, and the arrears were cleared.
entries.literal: Guan set out wine, invited the wealthy, and urged them to lend so the poor could pay; his words were sincere and earnest, and the rich were all moved—arrears were thereby cleared.

entries.zh: 朝廷嘉其能，榜以勵天下。
entries.en: The court praised his resourcefulness and posted his example to encourage officials throughout the empire.
entries.literal: The court commended his ability and posted a notice to encourage the whole realm.

entries.zh: 守蘇者前有季亨、魏觀，後有姚善、況鐘，皆賢，稱「姑蘇五太守」，並祀學宮。
entries.en: The worthy prefects of Suzhou included Ji Heng and Wei Guan in the early years and Yao Shan and Kuang Zhong later; with Guan they were known as the "Five Prefects of Gusu" and all were enshrined in the school temple.
entries.literal: Among those who governed Suzhou, earlier there were Ji Heng and Wei Guan, later Yao Shan and Kuang Zhong—all were worthy—and they were called the "Five Prefects of Gusu," all enshrined in the school temple.

entries.zh: 贊曰：太祖起閭右，稔墨吏為民害，嘗以極刑處之。
entries.en: The eulogist writes: The Founding Emperor rose from humble origins and knew well how corrupt clerks preyed on the people; he sometimes punished them with the harshest penalties.
entries.literal: The eulogist says: The Founding Emperor rose from the common lanes and was well acquainted with how corrupt clerks harmed the people; he once punished them with extreme penalties.

entries.zh: 然每旌舉賢能，以示勸勉，不專任法也。
entries.en: Yet he also repeatedly honored worthy officials to encourage others and did not rely on punishment alone.
entries.literal: Yet he repeatedly commended and raised the worthy and able to display encouragement—he did not rely on law alone.

entries.zh: 嘗遣行人賫敕並鈔三十錠、內酒一尊，賜平陽知縣張礎。
entries.en: He once sent an envoy with an edict, thirty ingots of paper money, and a jar of imperial wine as gifts to Zhang Chu, magistrate of Pingyang.
entries.literal: Once he sent an envoy bearing an edict together with thirty ingots of paper money and one jar of imperial wine to bestow on Pingyang Magistrate Zhang Chu.

entries.zh: 又建陽知縣郭伯泰、丞陸鎰，為政不避權勢，遣使勞以酒醴，遷其官。
entries.en: When Jianyang magistrate Guo Botai and assistant magistrate Lu Yi governed without fear of the powerful, he sent envoys with wine to honor them and promoted them.
entries.literal: Also Jianyang Magistrate Guo Botai and Assistant Magistrate Lu Yi, in governing did not avoid the powerful; he sent envoys to comfort them with wine and spirits and transferred them to higher posts.

entries.zh: 丹徒知縣胡夢通、丞郭伯高，金壇丞李思進，坐事當逮，民詣闕，言多善政。
entries.en: When Dantu magistrate Hu Mengtong, assistant magistrate Guo Bogao, and Jintan assistant magistrate Li Sijin were to be arrested on charges, the people went to court to testify to their good governance.
entries.literal: Dantu Magistrate Hu Mengtong, Assistant Magistrate Guo Bogao, and Jintan Assistant Magistrate Li Sijin, implicated in cases and due for arrest, had the people go to court reporting their many good policies.

entries.zh: 帝並賜內尊，降敕褒勞。
entries.en: The Emperor rewarded them all with imperial wine and issued edicts of praise.
entries.literal: The Emperor bestowed imperial wine on them all and issued edicts of praise and consolation.

entries.zh: 永州守余彥誠、齊東令鄭敏等十人坐事下獄，部民列政績以請，皆復官。
entries.en: Yongzhou prefect Yu Yancheng, Qidong magistrate Zheng Min, and eight others were imprisoned on charges. Their constituents petitioned listing their achievements, and all were restored to office.
entries.literal: Yongzhou Prefect Yu Yancheng, Qidong Magistrate Zheng Min, and others—ten men in all—were imprisoned on charges; the people of their districts listed their administrative achievements in petition, and all were restored to office.

entries.zh: 宜春令沈昌等四人更擢郡守。
entries.en: Yichun magistrate Shen Chang and three others were further promoted to prefects.
entries.literal: Yichun Magistrate Shen Chang and three others were further promoted to prefects.

entries.zh: 其自下僚不次擢用者，寧遠尉王尚賢為廣西參政，祥符丞鄒俊為大理卿，靜寧州判元善為僉都御史，芝陽令李行素為刑部侍郎。
entries.en: Among those promoted out of turn from junior posts: Wang Shangxian, assistant magistrate of Ningyuan, became administrative commissioner of Guangxi; Zou Jun, assistant magistrate of Xiangfu, became minister of the Court of Judicial Review; Yuan Shan, judge of Jingning, became censor-in-chief; and Li Xingsu, magistrate of Zhiyang, became vice minister of justice.
entries.literal: Among those promoted out of turn from lower offices: Ningyuan Assistant Magistrate Wang Shangxian became Guangxi Administrative Commissioner; Xiangfu Assistant Magistrate Zou Jun became Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; Jingning Prefecture Judge Yuan Shan became Censor-in-Chief; Zhiyang Magistrate Li Xingsu became Vice Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 至如懷寧丞陳希文、宜興簿王復春，先以善政擢，已知其貪肆，旋置重典。
entries.en: Chen Xiwen, assistant magistrate of Huaining, and Wang Fuchun, clerk of Yixing, were first promoted for good governance but, once their greed became known, were soon punished severely.
entries.literal: As for Huaining Assistant Magistrate Chen Xiwen and Yixing Clerk Wang Fuchun, first promoted for good governance, once their greed and license were known they were soon subjected to severe punishment.

entries.zh: 所以風厲激勸者甚至，以故其時吏治多可紀述雲。
entries.en: His methods of warning, rewarding, and exhorting officials were carried to an extraordinary degree; for that reason the governance of the age left much worth recording.
entries.literal: The means by which he admonished, encouraged, and exhorted were carried to the utmost; for this reason the official governance of that time affords much that can be recorded—thus it runs.

entries.zh: 青文勝，字質夫，夔州人。
entries.en: Qing Wensheng, whose style was Zhifu, came from Kuizhou.
entries.literal: Qing Wensheng, styled Zhifu, was a native of Kuizhou.

entries.zh: 仕為龍陽典史。
entries.en: He served as the clerk of Longyang.
entries.literal: He served as clerk of Longyang.

entries.zh: 龍陽瀕洞庭，歲罹水患，逋賦數十萬，敲撲死者相踵。
entries.en: Longyang lay on Dongting Lake and suffered floods every year. Tax arrears ran into the hundreds of thousands, and people died under the tax collectors' beatings one after another.
entries.literal: Longyang bordered Dongting Lake; every year it suffered flood disasters, with several hundred thousand in tax arrears, and those who died under beating and flogging followed one upon another.

entries.zh: 文勝慨然詣闕上疏，為民請命。
entries.en: Wensheng went to the capital in indignation and submitted a memorial pleading for the people's lives.
entries.literal: Wensheng, stirred with indignation, went to court and submitted a memorial, pleading for the people's lives.

entries.zh: 再上，皆不報。
entries.en: He submitted again, but received no reply.
entries.literal: He submitted again, but received no response.

entries.zh: 嘆曰：「何面目歸見父老！」
entries.en: He sighed and said, "How can I face the elders of my district again?"
entries.literal: He sighed and said: "With what face can I return to see the elders of my district!"

entries.zh: 復具疏，擊登聞鼓以進，遂自經於鼓下。
entries.en: He drafted another memorial, struck the Petition Drum to present it, and hanged himself beneath it.
entries.literal: He again drew up a memorial, struck the Petition Drum to present it, and thereupon hanged himself beneath the drum.

entries.zh: 帝聞大驚，憫其為民殺身，詔寬龍陽租二萬四千余石，定為額。
entries.en: The Emperor was deeply shaken and pitied him for dying on the people's behalf. He ordered Longyang's grain levy reduced by more than twenty-four thousand shi and fixed that as the permanent quota.
entries.literal: When the Emperor heard he was greatly alarmed, pitied him for giving his life for the people, and ordered that Longyang's tax be reduced by more than twenty-four thousand shi, fixing this as the quota.

entries.zh: 邑人建祠祀之。
entries.en: The people of the district built a shrine in his honor.
entries.literal: The people of the district built a shrine to worship him.

entries.zh: 妻子貧不能歸，養以公田百畝。
entries.en: His wife and children were too poor to return home and were supported on one hundred mu of public land.
entries.literal: His wife and children were too poor to return home; they were supported with one hundred mu of public fields.

entries.zh: 萬歷十四年，詔有司春秋致祭，名其祠曰「惠烈」。
entries.en: In Wanli 14 the court ordered seasonal sacrifices at his shrine and named it "Benevolent and Ardent."
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year of Wanli an edict ordered the responsible offices to offer sacrifices in spring and autumn, naming the shrine "Benevolent and Ardent."

entries.zh: 燕兵之襲大寧也，守將都指揮卜萬與都督劉真、陳亨帥兵扼松亭關。
entries.en: During the Yan assault on Daling, garrison commander Bu Wan and commissioners Liu Zhen and Chen Heng held Songting Pass with their troops.
entries.literal: When Yan troops raided Daling, defending commander Bu Wan and Commissioners Liu Zhen and Chen Heng led troops to block Songting Pass.

entries.zh: 亨欲降燕，畏萬，不敢發。
entries.en: Chen Heng wanted to defect to the Prince of Yan but feared Bu Wan and held back.
entries.literal: Heng wished to surrender to Yan but feared Wan and did not dare act.

entries.zh: 燕行反間，貽萬書，盛稱萬；
entries.en: The Yan side ran a counter-intelligence scheme, sending Bu Wan a letter that lavishly praised him;
entries.literal: Yan carried out a counter-intelligence plot, sending Wan a letter lavishly praising Wan;

entries.zh: 極詆亨。
entries.en: while viciously denouncing Chen Heng.
entries.literal: and bitterly slandering Heng.

entries.zh: 厚賞所獲大寧卒，緘書衣中，俾密與萬。
entries.en: They richly rewarded captured soldiers from Daling, hid the letter in their clothes, and had them deliver it secretly to Bu Wan.
entries.literal: They richly rewarded captured Daling soldiers, sealed the letter in their clothing, and had them secretly give it to Wan.

entries.zh: 故使同獲卒見之，亦縱去而不與賞。
entries.en: They made sure other captives saw this favor, then released those men without paying them.
entries.literal: They deliberately let fellow-captured soldiers see this, and also released them without giving reward.

entries.zh: 不得賞者發其事。
entries.en: The men who went unrewarded reported what had happened.
entries.literal: Those who received no reward exposed the affair.

entries.zh: 真、亨搜卒衣，得書。
entries.en: Liu Zhen and Chen Heng searched the men's clothing and found the letter.
entries.literal: Zhen and Heng searched the soldiers' clothes and obtained the letter.

entries.zh: 遂執萬下獄死，籍其家。
entries.en: Bu Wan was arrested, died in prison, and his property was confiscated.
entries.literal: Thereupon they seized Wan, imprisoned him until he died, and confiscated his household.

entries.zh: 萬忠勇而死於間，論者惜之。
entries.en: Bu Wan was loyal and courageous yet died by treachery; observers mourned the waste of it.
entries.literal: Wan was loyal and brave yet died through intrigue; commentators regretted it.

entries.zh: 及大寧陷，指揮使朱鑒力戰，不屈死。
entries.en: When Daling fell, Commander Zhu Jian fought to the end and died rather than submit.
entries.literal: When Daling fell, Commander Zhu Jian fought fiercely, refused submission, and died.

entries.zh: 鐵鉉 暴昭
entries.en: Tie Xuan and Bao Zhao
entries.literal: Tie Xuan, Bao Zhao

entries.en: (Hou Tai)〉
entries.literal: (Hou Tai)〉

entries.zh: 陳性善
entries.en: Chen Xingshan
entries.literal: Chen Xingshan

entries.zh: 〈（陳植 王彬 崇剛）〉
entries.en: (Chen Zhi, Wang Bin, and Chong Gang)〉
entries.literal: (Chen Zhi, Wang Bin, Chong Gang)〉

entries.zh: 張昺
entries.en: Zhang Bing
entries.literal: Zhang Bing

entries.zh: 〈（謝貴 彭二 葛誠 余逢辰）〉
entries.en: (Xie Gui, Peng Er, Ge Cheng, and Yu Fengchen)〉
entries.literal: (Xie Gui, Peng Er, Ge Cheng, Yu Fengchen)〉

entries.zh: 宋忠
entries.en: Song Zhong
entries.literal: Song Zhong

entries.en: (Yu Zhen)〉
entries.literal: (Yu Zhen)〉

entries.zh: 馬宣
entries.en: Ma Xuan
entries.literal: Ma Xuan

entries.zh: 〈（曾浚 卜萬 朱鑒 石撰）〉
entries.en: (Zeng Jun, Bu Wan, Zhu Jian, and Shi Zhuan)〉
entries.literal: (Zeng Jun, Bu Wan, Zhu Jian, Shi Zhuan)〉

entries.zh: 瞿能
entries.en: Qu Neng
entries.literal: Qu Neng

entries.zh: 〈（莊得 楚智 皂旗張 王指揮 楊本）〉
entries.en: (Zhuang De, Chu Zhi, Soap-banner Zhang, Commander Wang, and Yang Ben)〉
entries.literal: (Zhuang De, Chu Zhi, Soap-banner Zhang, Commander Wang, Yang Ben)〉

entries.zh: 張倫
entries.en: Zhang Lun
entries.literal: Zhang Lun

entries.en: (Chen Zhi)〉
entries.literal: (Chen Zhi)〉

entries.zh: 顏伯瑋
entries.en: Yan Bowei
entries.literal: Yan Bowei

entries.zh: 〈（唐子清 黃謙 向樸 鄭恕 鄭華）〉
entries.en: (Tang Ziqing, Huang Qian, Xiang Pu, Zheng Shu, and Zheng Hua)〉
entries.literal: (Tang Ziqing, Huang Qian, Xiang Pu, Zheng Shu, Zheng Hua)〉

entries.zh: 王省 姚善
entries.en: Wang Sheng and Yao Shan
entries.literal: Wang Sheng, Yao Shan

entries.en: (Qian Qin)〉
entries.literal: (Qian Qin)〉

entries.zh: 陳彥回
entries.en: Chen Yanhui
entries.literal: Chen Yanhui

entries.zh: 〈（張彥方）〉
entries.en: (Zhang Yanfang)〉
entries.literal: (Zhang Yanfang)〉

entries.zh: 二十四年，拜平羌將軍，討越州叛蠻阿資，破降之。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year he was named General for the Pacification of the Qiang, defeated the rebel chieftain Azi of Yuezhou, and accepted his surrender.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed General for the Pacification of the Qiang and campaigned against the rebel tribesman Azi of Yuezhou, defeating and accepting his surrender.

entries.zh: 擇地立柵處其眾，置寧越堡。
entries.en: He chose a site, built stockades for the surrendered people, and established Ningyue Stockade.
entries.literal: He chose ground, set up stockades to settle their people, and established Ningyue Stockade.

entries.zh: 遂平九名、九姓諸蠻。
entries.en: He then pacified the Jiuming, Jiuxing, and other tribal groups.
entries.literal: He thereupon pacified the Jiuming and Jiuxing tribes and others.

entries.zh: 尋與都督茅鼎會兵，徇五開。
entries.en: Soon he joined Vice Commissioner Mao Ding and marched on Wukai.
entries.literal: Shortly thereafter he joined Vice Commissioner Mao Ding's forces to advance on Wukai.

entries.zh: 未行，而畢節諸蠻復叛，大掠屯堡，殺吏士。
entries.en: Before they could march, the Bijie tribes rebelled again, sacked garrison posts, and killed officials and troops.
entries.literal: Before they set out, the Bijie tribes rebelled again, raiding garrison posts on a great scale and killing officials and soldiers.

entries.zh: 福令畢節諸衛嚴備，而檄都督陶文等從鼎搗其巢。
entries.en: He Fu ordered the Bijie guards to stand ready and sent Vice Commissioner Tao Wen and others with Mao Ding to strike their stronghold.
entries.literal: Fu ordered the Bijie guards to stand on strict alert and dispatched orders to Vice Commissioner Tao Wen and others to follow Ding in striking their lair.

entries.zh: 擒叛酋，戮之。
entries.en: They captured the rebel leader and executed him.
entries.literal: They captured the rebel chieftain and executed him.

entries.zh: 分兵盡捕諸蠻，建堡設戍，乃趨五開。
entries.en: They split their forces to round up the tribes, built stockades and garrisons, and then advanced on Wukai.
entries.literal: They divided forces to capture all the tribes, built stockades and set garrisons, and then pressed on to Wukai.

entries.zh: 請因兵力討水西奢香，不許。
entries.en: He asked to use his troops against She Xiang of Shuixi, but the court refused.
entries.literal: He requested to use his army's strength to campaign against She Xiang of Shuixi; permission was not granted.

entries.zh: 三十年三月，水西蠻居宗必登等作亂，會顧成討平之。
entries.en: In the third month of the thirtieth year the Shuixi chieftain Juzong Bideng and others rose in revolt; Gu Cheng happened to be campaigning there and put them down.
entries.literal: In the third month of the thirtieth year the Shuixi tribesman Juzong Bideng and others rebelled; Gu Cheng happened to campaign and pacify them.

entries.zh: 其冬拜征虜左將軍，副西平侯沐春討麓川叛蠻刀幹孟。
entries.en: That winter he was named Left General for the Punishment of Barbarians and served under Marquis of Xiping Mu Chun against the Luchuan rebel Dao Ganmeng.
entries.literal: That winter he was appointed Left General for the Punishment of Barbarians and served as deputy to Marquis of Xiping Mu Chun in campaigning against the Luchuan rebel tribesman Dao Ganmeng.

entries.zh: 明年，福與都督瞿能逾高良公山，搗南甸，擒其酋刀名孟。
entries.en: The next year He Fu and Vice Commissioner Qu Neng crossed Gaolianggong Mountain, struck Nandian, and captured the chieftain Dao Mingmeng.
entries.literal: The next year Fu and Vice Commissioner Qu Neng crossed Gaolianggong Mountain, struck Nandian, and captured the chieftain Dao Mingmeng.

entries.zh: 回軍擊景罕寨，不下。
entries.en: On the return march they attacked Jinghan Stockade but could not take it.
entries.literal: On the return march they attacked Jinghan Stockade but could not take it.

entries.zh: 春以銳軍至，賊驚潰。
entries.en: Mu Chun arrived with elite troops and the rebels broke and fled.
entries.literal: Chun arrived with crack troops and the rebels fled in panic.

entries.zh: 幹孟懼，乞降。
entries.en: Dao Ganmeng was terrified and sued for peace.
entries.literal: Ganmeng was afraid and begged to surrender.

entries.zh: 已而春卒，賊復懷貳。
entries.en: Soon afterward Mu Chun died, and the rebels wavered in their submission again.
entries.literal: Before long Chun died, and the rebels again harbored double loyalty.

entries.zh: 是時太祖已崩，惠帝初即位，拜福征虜將軍。
entries.en: By then the founding emperor was dead and the Hui Emperor had just taken the throne; He Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
entries.literal: At that time the founding emperor had died and the Huidi had just taken the throne; Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.

entries.zh: 福遂破擒刀幹孟，降其眾七萬。
entries.en: He Fu then defeated and captured Dao Ganmeng and accepted the surrender of seventy thousand of his followers.
entries.literal: Fu thereupon defeated and captured Dao Ganmeng and received the surrender of seventy thousand of his followers.

entries.zh: 分兵徇下諸寨，麓川地悉定。
entries.en: He sent detachments to subdue the outlying stockades, and the whole Luchuan region was pacified.
entries.literal: He divided forces to subdue the stockades below, and the Luchuan region was entirely pacified.

entries.zh: 建文元年，還京師，論功進都督同知。
entries.en: In Jianwen 1 he returned to the capital and was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief for his service.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwen he returned to the capital; for merit he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief.

entries.zh: 練兵德州，進左都督。
entries.en: He drilled troops at Dezhou and was promoted to left commissioner-in-chief.
entries.literal: He trained troops at Dezhou and was advanced to Left Commissioner-in-chief.

entries.zh: 與盛庸、平安會兵伐燕，戰淮北不利，奔還。
entries.en: He joined Sheng Yong and Ping An against the Prince of Yan; beaten north of the Huai, he fled back.
entries.literal: He joined Sheng Yong and Ping An in campaigning against Yan; fighting north of the Huai without success, he fled back.

entries.zh: 八年，帝北征，召福從出塞。
entries.en: In the eighth year the emperor marched north and summoned He Fu to accompany him beyond the frontier.
entries.literal: In the eighth year the Emperor campaigned north and summoned Fu to follow beyond the frontier.

entries.zh: 初，帝以福有才略，寵任逾諸將。
entries.en: At first the emperor favored He Fu above other generals for his talent and strategic sense.
entries.literal: At first the Emperor, because Fu had talent and strategy, favored and entrusted him beyond other generals.

entries.zh: 福亦善引嫌，有事未嘗專決。
entries.en: He Fu also knew how to avoid arousing suspicion and never decided important matters on his own.
entries.literal: Fu also knew how to avoid suspicion; when there were matters he never decided alone.

entries.zh: 在鎮嘗請取西平侯家鞏昌蓄馬，以充孳牧。
entries.en: While in command he once asked to take horses kept at Gongchang by the Marquis of Xiping's household to replenish his breeding herds.
entries.literal: While at his post he once requested to take the horses kept at Gongchang by the Marquis of Xiping's household to replenish breeding herds.

entries.zh: 帝報曰：「皇考時貴近家多許養馬，以示共享富貴之意。
entries.en: The emperor replied, "In our late father's time the noble and close families were often allowed to keep horses, to show that wealth and honor were to be shared.
entries.literal: The Emperor replied, "In our late father's time the noble and close families were often allowed to keep horses, to show the meaning of sharing wealth and honor.

entries.zh: 爾所奏固為國矣，然非待勛戚之道。」
entries.en: Your proposal serves the state, but it is not how meritorious kin should be treated."
entries.literal: What you report is indeed for the state, yet it is not the way to treat meritorious kin."

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: The request was refused.
entries.literal: He did not consent.

entries.zh: 其余有請輒行，委寄甚重。
entries.en: Other requests he generally carried out at once; the trust placed in him was very great.
entries.literal: For other requests he generally acted at once; the trust placed in him was very great.

entries.zh: 及從征，數違節度。
entries.en: On campaign he repeatedly disobeyed orders.
entries.literal: When he followed on campaign he repeatedly violated command discipline.

entries.zh: 群臣有言其罪者，福益怏怏有怨言。
entries.en: When ministers spoke of his offenses, He Fu grew resentful and voiced complaints.
entries.literal: When ministers spoke of his offenses, Fu grew still more resentful and voiced complaints.

entries.zh: 師還，都御史陳瑛復劾之。
entries.en: When the army returned, Censor-in-chief Chen Ying impeached him again.
entries.literal: When the army returned, Censor-in-chief Chen Ying again impeached him.

entries.zh: 福懼，自縊死，爵除。
entries.en: He Fu, in fear, hanged himself, and his title was abolished.
entries.literal: Fu was afraid and hanged himself; his title was abolished.

entries.zh: 而趙王妃亦尋廢。
entries.en: The Princess of Zhao was soon deposed as well.
entries.literal: The Princess of Zhao was also soon deposed.

entries.zh: 盛庸平安何福顧成
entries.en: Sheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, and Gu Cheng
entries.literal: Sheng Yong, Ping An, He Fu, Gu Cheng

entries.zh: 仁宗即位，義、原吉皆以元老為中外所信。
entries.en: When the Renzong Emperor ascended the throne, Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji were both trusted throughout the court and empire as senior statesmen.
entries.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, Yi and Yuanji were both trusted within and without as senior veterans.

entries.zh: 帝又念義監國時舊勞，尤厚倚之。
entries.en: The Emperor also remembered Jian Yi's service when the Crown Prince had governed the realm, and relied on him all the more heavily.
entries.literal: The Emperor also recalled Yi's old labors when governing the realm and relied on him all the more.

entries.zh: 首進義少保，賜冠服、象笏、玉帶，兼食二祿。
entries.en: He first promoted Jian Yi to Junior Guardian, bestowed court dress, an ivory tablet, and a jade belt, and granted him double stipends.
entries.literal: He first advanced Yi to Junior Guardian, bestowed cap and robe, ivory tablet, and jade belt, and granted double stipends.

entries.zh: 歷進少師，賜銀章一，文曰「繩愆糾繆」。
entries.en: He was further promoted to Junior Preceptor and given a silver seal inscribed "Correcting faults and remedying errors."
entries.literal: He was advanced in turn to Junior Preceptor and given one silver seal inscribed "Correcting faults and remedying errors."

entries.zh: 已，復賜璽書曰：「曩朕監國，卿以先朝舊臣，日侍左右。
entries.en: Shortly afterward he bestowed another imperial letter, which read: "When I was governing the realm as heir, you, as a veteran of the previous reign, attended me day after day.
entries.literal: Soon after, he again bestowed an imperial letter saying: "Formerly when I governed the realm, you as an old minister of the previous reign attended me daily.

entries.zh: 兩京肇建，政務方殷，卿勞心焦思，不恤身家，二十余年，夷險一節。
entries.en: As the two capitals were being built and government affairs pressed hard upon us, you labored with anxious devotion, heedless of yourself and your family—for more than twenty years you held the same integrity through good times and bad.
entries.literal: As the two capitals were first established and state affairs were pressing, you toiled in mind and burned with thought, heedless of self and family—for more than twenty years one integrity through ease and peril.

entries.zh: 朕承大統，贊襄治理，不懈益恭。
entries.en: When I inherited the throne, you assisted in governing the realm, never slackening but growing ever more devoted.
entries.literal: When I received the great succession, you assisted in governance, never slackening but growing more respectful.

entries.zh: 朕篤念不忘，茲以已意，創制『蹇忠貞印』賜卿。
entries.en: I hold this in deep remembrance; of my own accord I have had made the "Seal of Jian the Loyal and Upright" and bestow it upon you.
entries.literal: I cherish this and do not forget; now of my own accord I have created the "Jian Loyal and Upright Seal" to bestow on you.

entries.zh: 俾藏於家，傳之後世，知朕君臣共濟艱難，相與有成也。」
entries.en: Keep it in your household and pass it down to posterity, so they may know how we, ruler and minister, weathered hardship together and achieved what we did."
entries.literal: Keep it in your house and pass it to later generations, so they may know how ruler and minister together crossed hardship and achieved success."

entries.zh: 時惟楊士奇亦得賜「貞一」印及敕。
entries.en: At that time only Yang Shiqi likewise received the "Upright and One" seal and an imperial edict.
entries.literal: At that time only Yang Shiqi also received the "Upright and One" seal and an edict.

entries.zh: 尋命與英國公輔及原吉同監修《太宗實錄》。
entries.en: He was soon ordered, together with the Duke of Ying, Zhang Fu, and Xia Yuanji, to supervise compilation of the Veritable Records of the Taizong Emperor.
entries.literal: Soon he was ordered, together with the Duke of Ying, Fu, and Yuanji, to supervise compilation of the Veritable Records of Taizong.

entries.zh: 義視原吉尤重厚，然過於周慎。
entries.en: Jian Yi regarded Xia Yuanji with especial respect and warmth, yet he himself was excessively thorough and cautious.
entries.literal: Yi regarded Yuanji as especially weighty and generous, yet he himself was overly thorough and cautious.

entries.zh: 士奇嘗於帝前謂義曰：「何過慮？」
entries.en: Shiqi once said to Jian Yi in the Emperor's presence, "Why such excessive worry?"
entries.literal: Shiqi once said to Yi before the Emperor, "Why worry so much?"

entries.zh: 義曰：「恐鹵莽為後憂耳。」
entries.en: Jian Yi replied, "I fear that acting rashly will bring trouble later."
entries.literal: Yi said, "I fear rashness will bring trouble later."

entries.zh: 帝兩是之。
entries.en: The Emperor approved of both views.
entries.literal: The Emperor approved both.

entries.zh: 楊榮嘗毀義。
entries.en: Yang Rong once spoke ill of Jian Yi.
entries.literal: Yang Rong once slandered Yi.

entries.zh: 帝不直榮。
entries.en: The Emperor did not take Rong's side.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not side with Rong.

entries.zh: 義頓首言：「榮無他。
entries.en: Jian Yi kowtowed and said, "Rong means no harm.
entries.literal: Yi kowtowed and said, "Rong has no other intent.

entries.zh: 即左右有讒榮者，願陛下慎察。」
entries.en: If anyone at your side speaks against him, I beg Your Majesty to look into it carefully."
entries.literal: If those at your side slander Rong, I beg Your Majesty to examine carefully."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：「吾固弗信也。」
entries.en: The Emperor smiled and said, "I never believed it in the first place."
entries.literal: The Emperor smiled and said, "I never believed it in the first place."

entries.zh: 宣宗即位，委寄益重。
entries.en: When the Xuanzong Emperor ascended the throne, his reliance on Jian Yi grew even greater.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, his trust in Yi grew heavier still.

entries.zh: 時方修獻陵，帝欲遵遺詔從儉約，以問義、原吉。
entries.en: The Xian Mausoleum was then under construction; the Emperor wished to follow his father's testament and keep the work frugal, and consulted Jian Yi and Xia Yuanji.
entries.literal: At that time the Xian Mausoleum was under construction; the Emperor wished to follow the testament and keep to frugality, and asked Yi and Yuanji.

entries.zh: 二人力贊曰：「聖見高遠，出於至孝，萬世之利也。」
entries.en: Both men strongly endorsed the plan, saying, "Your sage vision is far-reaching and springs from deepest filial piety; it will benefit generations to come."
entries.literal: The two men strongly praised, saying, "Your sage vision is far-reaching, springing from utmost filial piety—a benefit for ten thousand generations."

entries.zh: 帝親為規畫，三月而陵成，宏麗不及長陵，其後諸帝因以為制。
entries.en: The Emperor personally oversaw the design; the mausoleum was completed in three months. It was less grand than the Chang Mausoleum, and later emperors took this as their standard.
entries.literal: The Emperor personally planned it; in three months the mausoleum was complete—its grandeur did not match the Chang Mausoleum, and later emperors took this as the model.

entries.zh: 迨世宗營永陵，始益崇侈雲。
entries.en: Only when the Shizong Emperor built the Yong Mausoleum did imperial tombs grow more lavish.
entries.literal: Only when Emperor Shizong built the Yong Mausoleum did extravagance grow greater.

entries.zh: 已而仁宗崩，太子至自南京。
entries.en: Soon Emperor Renzong died, and the Crown Prince came up from Nanjing.
entries.literal: Before long Emperor Renzong died, and the Heir Apparent arrived from Nanjing.

entries.zh: 原吉奉遺詔迎於盧溝橋。
entries.en: Following the testamentary edict, Xia Yuanji welcomed him at the Lugou Bridge.
entries.literal: Yuanji, following the testamentary edict, welcomed him at the Lugou Bridge.

entries.zh: 宣宗即位，以舊輔益親重。
entries.en: When the Xuanzong Emperor came to the throne, he treated this veteran counselor with even greater intimacy and respect.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, as an old assistant he was all the more trusted and honored.

entries.zh: 明年，漢王高煦反，亦以「靖難」為辭，移檄罪狀諸大臣，以原吉為首。
entries.en: The following year the Prince of Han, Zhu Gaoxu, rebelled, likewise invoking the "Pacification of Difficulties"; he circulated a proclamation denouncing the senior ministers, with Xia Yuanji listed first.
entries.literal: The next year the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, rebelled, likewise taking "Pacifying Difficulties" as his plea; he circulated a proclamation listing the crimes of the great ministers, with Yuanji named first.

entries.zh: 帝夜召諸臣議。
entries.en: The Emperor summoned his ministers for a night council.
entries.literal: At night the Emperor summoned the ministers to deliberate.

entries.zh: 楊榮首勸帝親征。
entries.en: Yang Rong was the first to urge the Emperor to take the field in person.
entries.literal: Yang Rong was the first to urge the Emperor to campaign in person.

entries.zh: 帝難之。
entries.en: The Emperor hesitated.
entries.literal: The Emperor found it difficult.

entries.zh: 原吉曰：「獨不見李景隆已事耶？
entries.en: Xia Yuanji said, "Have you forgotten what became of Li Jinglong?
entries.literal: Yuanji said, "Have you alone not seen what became of Li Jinglong?

entries.zh: 臣昨見所遣將，命下即色變，臨事可知矣。
entries.en: Yesterday I saw the generals you dispatched; the moment they received orders their faces changed—you can guess how they will perform in battle.
entries.literal: Yesterday I saw the generals you sent out; the moment the order was given their faces changed—how they will act in battle can be known.

entries.zh: 且兵貴神速，卷甲趨之，所謂先人有奪人之心也。
entries.en: Moreover, war favors speed; march at once in full armor—that is how you seize the initiative.
entries.literal: Moreover, in warfare speed is prized; roll up armor and hurry there—this is what is called seizing the enemy's heart by acting first.

entries.zh: 榮策善。」
entries.en: Rong's plan is sound."
entries.literal: Rong's plan is good."

entries.zh: 帝意遂決。
entries.en: The Emperor's mind was made up.
entries.literal: The Emperor's mind was thereupon settled.

entries.zh: 師還，賚予加等，賜閽者三人。
entries.en: When the army returned, rewards were increased and he was given three gatekeepers.
entries.literal: When the army returned, rewards and gifts were increased by a grade, and three gatekeepers were bestowed.

entries.zh: 原吉以無功辭。
entries.en: Xia Yuanji declined on the grounds that he had done nothing to deserve them.
entries.literal: Yuanji declined on the grounds of having no merit.

entries.zh: 不聽。
entries.en: The Emperor would not hear of it.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not listen.

entries.zh: 帝征樂安，義、原吉及諸學士皆從，預軍中機務，賜鞍馬甲胄弓劍。
entries.en: When the Emperor campaigned against Le'an, Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji, and the Hanlin academicians all accompanied him, took part in military planning, and were given saddles, horses, armor, bows, and swords.
entries.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Le'an, Yi, Yuanji, and the academicians all followed, taking part in military counsels, and were given saddles, horses, armor, bows, and swords.

entries.zh: 及還，賚予甚厚。
entries.en: On their return, the rewards were very generous.
entries.literal: On return, rewards were very generous.

entries.zh: 三年從巡邊還。
entries.en: In the third year of the reign he returned from accompanying the border inspection tour.
entries.literal: In the third year he returned from accompanying the border tour.

entries.zh: 帝以義、原吉、士奇、榮四人者皆已老，賜璽書曰：「卿等皆祖宗遺老，畀輔朕躬。
entries.en: Seeing that Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji, Yang Shiqi, and Yang Rong were all advanced in years, the Emperor bestowed an imperial letter: "You are all surviving elders left by our ancestors, entrusted to assist me.
entries.literal: The Emperor, seeing that Yi, Yuanji, Shiqi, and Rong were all old, bestowed an imperial letter: "You are all surviving elders left by our ancestors, entrusted to assist my person.

entries.zh: 今黃髮危齒，不宜復典冗劇，傷朝廷優老待賢之禮。
entries.en: Now that your hair has turned white and your teeth are failing, you should no longer bear the burden of heavy routine duties, to the detriment of the court's policy of honoring the aged and treating the worthy with care.
entries.literal: Now with yellow hair and failing teeth, you should not again preside over tedious duties, harming the court's rite of honoring age and treating the worthy.

entries.zh: 可輟所務，朝夕在朕左右討論至理，共寧邦家。
entries.en: You may set aside your official duties and remain at my side day and night to discuss fundamental principles and together bring peace to the realm.
entries.literal: You may set aside your duties and morning and evening be at my side to discuss ultimate principles and together bring peace to the state and family.

entries.zh: 官祿悉如舊。」
entries.en: Your rank and stipends shall all remain unchanged."
entries.literal: Rank and stipend shall all remain as before."

entries.zh: 明年，郭琎代為尚書。
entries.en: The following year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister of Personnel.
entries.literal: The next year Guo Jin replaced him as Minister of Personnel.

entries.zh: 尋以胡濙言，命義等四人議天下官吏軍民建言章奏。
entries.en: Soon afterward, on Hu Ying's recommendation, the Emperor ordered Jian Yi and the other three to deliberate on memorials submitted by officials, soldiers, and civilians throughout the empire.
entries.literal: Soon, on Hu Ying's recommendation, the Emperor ordered Yi and the other four to deliberate on memorials from officials, soldiers, and civilians throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 復賜義銀章，文曰「忠厚寬宏」。
entries.en: He again bestowed on Jian Yi a silver seal inscribed "Loyal, generous, broad, and magnanimous."
entries.literal: He again bestowed on Yi a silver seal inscribed "Loyal, generous, broad, and magnanimous."

entries.zh: 七年詔有司為義營新第於文明門內。
entries.en: In the seventh year of the reign an edict ordered the authorities to build Jian Yi a new residence inside the Wenming Gate.
entries.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered the authorities to build Yi a new residence inside the Wenming Gate.

entries.zh: 原吉與義皆起家太祖時。
entries.en: Xia Yuanji and Jian Yi both began their careers under Taizu.
entries.literal: Xia Yuanji and Jian Yi both began their careers under Ming Taizu.

entries.zh: 義秉銓政，原吉筦度支，皆二十七年，名位先於三楊。
entries.en: Jian Yi held authority over appointments, Xia Yuanji managed state finances—each for twenty-seven years, and both ranked ahead of the Three Yangs in seniority.
entries.literal: Yi held the power of selection, Yuanji managed revenue—all for twenty-seven years, their fame and rank preceding the Three Yangs.

entries.zh: 仁、宣之世，外兼臺省，內參館閣，與三楊同心輔政。
entries.en: Under the Renzong and Xuanzong emperors they held censorial posts abroad and served in the Hanlin at court, working in concert with the Three Yangs to govern.
entries.literal: During the reigns of Renzong and Xuanzong, they held censorial and provincial posts outside the court and served in the Hanlin within it, working with the Three Yangs to assist the government.

entries.zh: 義善謀，榮善斷，而原吉與士奇尤持大體，有古大臣風烈。
entries.en: Jian Yi excelled at planning, Yang Rong at decision, while Xia Yuanji and Yang Shiqi especially upheld the larger pattern, with the bearing of great ministers of antiquity.
entries.literal: Jian Yi was skilled in planning and Yang Rong in deciding, while Xia Yuanji and Yang Shiqi especially upheld the larger principles, with the bearing of great ministers of old.

entries.zh: 義為人質直孝友，善處僚友間，未嘗一語傷物。
entries.en: Jian Yi was by nature plainspoken, upright, filial, and friendly; he handled relations among colleagues well and never spoke a word that wounded anyone.
entries.literal: Yi as a man was plain, upright, filial, and friendly; he was skilled among colleagues and never once spoke to wound others.

entries.zh: 士奇常言：「張詠之不飾玩好，傅堯俞之遇人以誠，範景仁之不設城府，義兼有之。」
entries.en: Shiqi often said, "Zhang Yong's disdain for ornamental luxuries, Fu Yaoyu's sincerity toward others, and Fan Jingren's freedom from hidden designs—Jian Yi combined them all."
entries.literal: Shiqi often said, "Zhang Yong's not adorning himself with curios, Fu Yaoyu's treating people with sincerity, Fan Jingren's setting up no hidden schemes—Yi combined them all."

entries.zh: 子英，有詩名，以蔭為尚寶司丞，歷官太常少卿。
entries.en: His son Ying was renowned as a poet; through hereditary privilege he became a director in the Imperial Seals Office and eventually rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: His son Ying was famed for poetry; by hereditary privilege he became Director of the Imperial Seals Office and rose to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 蹇義夏原吉
entries.en: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji
entries.literal: Jian Yi, Xia Yuanji

entries.zh: 〈（俞士吉李文郁鄒師顏）〉
entries.en: (Yu Shiji, Li Wenyu, Zou Shiyan)
entries.literal: (Yu Shiji, Li Wenyu, Zou Shiyan)

entries.zh: 蹇義，字宜之，巴人，初名容。洪武十八年進士。授中書舍人，奏事稱旨。帝問：「汝蹇叔後乎？」容頓首不敢對。帝嘉其誠篤，為更名義，手書賜之。滿三載當遷，特命滿九載，曰：「朕且用義。」由是朝夕侍左右，小心敬慎，未嘗忤色。惠帝既即位，推太祖意，超擢吏部右侍郎。是時齊泰、黃子澄當國，外興大師，內改制度，義無所建明。國子博士王紳遺書責之，義不能答。
entries.en: Jian Yi, style Yizhi, was from Ba and was originally named Rong. He became a jinshi in Hongwu 18 and was appointed Secretariat Drafter, where his memorials pleased the emperor. The emperor asked, "Are you a descendant of Jian Shu?" Rong kowtowed and did not dare reply. Admiring his sincerity, the emperor changed his name to Yi and bestowed the written name in his own hand. After Yi had completed three years and was due for promotion, the emperor specifically ordered him to serve the full nine years, saying, "I am about to make use of Yi." From then on Yi attended the emperor morning and evening, cautious and reverent, never offending him. When Emperor Hui came to the throne, he inferred Taizu's intention and exceptionally promoted Yi to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel. At that time Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng controlled the government, raising major armies outside and altering institutions within, but Yi offered no constructive proposals. Wang Shen, a doctor of the Directorate of Education, sent him a letter of reproach, and Yi could not answer.
entries.literal: Jian Yi, style Yizhi, was a man of Ba and was originally named Rong. In Hongwu year eighteen he became a jinshi. He was appointed Secretariat Drafter, and his memorials suited the emperor's intent. The emperor asked, "Are you a descendant of Jian Shu?" Rong kowtowed and did not dare answer. The emperor praised his sincerity and simplicity, changed his name to Yi, and bestowed it on him in his own handwriting. When Yi had completed three years and should have been promoted, the emperor specifically ordered him to complete nine years, saying, "I am about to use Yi." From then on Yi attended at the emperor's side morning and evening, careful and reverent, and never offended his expression. When Emperor Hui came to the throne, he inferred Taizu's intent and exceptionally promoted Yi to right vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel. At this time Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng controlled the government, raising great armies abroad and changing institutions at home, but Yi made no proposals or clarifications. Wang Shen, a doctor of the Directorate of Education, sent him a letter reproaching him, and Yi could not answer.

entries.zh: 任禮趙安趙輔劉聚宋晟，字景陽，定遠人。
entries.en: Ren Li, Zhao An, Zhao Fu, and Liu Ju. Song Cheng, styled Jingyang, was a native of Dingyuan.
entries.literal: Ren Li, Zhao An, Zhao Fu, Liu Ju. Song Cheng, styled Jingyang, was a man of Dingyuan.

entries.zh: 父朝用，兄國興，並從渡江，皆積功至元帥。
entries.en: His father Chaoyong and elder brother Guoxing both followed in the crossing of the Yangtze and, through accumulated merit, rose to the rank of commander.
entries.literal: His father Chaoyong and elder brother Guoxing both followed in crossing the Yangtze, both accumulating merit until reaching commander.

entries.zh: 攻集慶，國興戰歿，晟嗣其職。
entries.en: During the attack on Jiqing, Guoxing was killed in battle, and Cheng succeeded to his command.
entries.literal: Attacking Jiqing, Guoxing died in battle; Cheng succeeded to his post.

entries.zh: 既而朝用請老，晟方從鄧愈克徽州，召還，襲父官。
entries.en: When Chaoyong later requested retirement, Cheng was with Deng Yu capturing Huizhou. Recalled from the campaign, he inherited his father's post.
entries.literal: Thereafter Chaoyong requested retirement; Cheng was just following Deng Yu in capturing Huizhou—recalled, he inherited his father's office.

entries.zh: 累進都指揮同知，歷鎮江西、大同、陜西。
entries.en: He was promoted step by step to regional military commissioner of the third rank and successively served as regional commander in Jiangxi, Datong, and Shaanxi.
entries.literal: Repeatedly promoted to regional military commissioner of the third rank, successively commanding at Jiangxi, Datong, and Shaanxi.

entries.zh: 洪武十二年坐法降涼州衛指揮使。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Hongwu he was demoted for an offense to garrison commander of Liangzhou Guard.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Hongwu, through violation of law he was demoted to garrison commander of Liangzhou Guard.

entries.zh: 十七年五月討西番叛酋，至亦集乃路，擒元海道千戶也先帖木兒、國公吳把都剌赤等，俘獲萬八千人，送酋長京師，簡其精銳千人補卒伍，余悉放遣。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year he marched against rebel chieftains of the western tribes. Reaching Yijina'i Road, he captured the Yuan maritime-route chiliarch Esentemür, the state duke Wu Badur chi, and others—altogether eighteen thousand captives. He sent the chieftains to the capital, drafted one thousand of their best troops into the ranks, and released the remainder.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the seventeenth year he campaigned against the rebellious chieftains of the western barbarians; reaching Yijina'i Road, he captured the Yuan maritime-route chiliarch Esentemür, the state duke Wu Badur chi, and others, taking captive eighteen thousand persons; he sent the chieftains to the capital, selected one thousand elite men to fill the ranks, and released the rest entirely.

entries.zh: 召還，復為都指揮，進右軍都督僉事，仍鎮涼州。
entries.en: Recalled to court, he was restored as regional commander, promoted to assistant regional commander of the Rear Army, and continued to hold command at Liangzhou.
entries.literal: Recalled, he again became regional commander, advanced to assistant regional commander of the Rear Army, and still commanded at Liangzhou.

entries.zh: 二十四年充總兵官，與都督劉真討哈梅裏。
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year he served as overall commander and, with Commissioner-in-Chief Liu Zhen, campaigned against Hami.
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he served as overall commander, together with Commissioner-in-Chief Liu Zhen campaigning against Hami.

entries.zh: 其地去肅州千餘里。
entries.en: Hami lay more than a thousand li from Suzhou.
entries.literal: That place was more than a thousand li from Suzhou.

entries.zh: 晟令軍中多具糧糗，倍道疾馳，乘夜至城下。
entries.en: Cheng had the army carry abundant dry rations and forced a rapid march, reaching the city walls under cover of night.
entries.literal: Cheng ordered the army to prepare much dried provisions, doubled the march speed at forced pace, and by night reached below the walls.

entries.zh: 質明，金鼓聲震地，闔城股栗，遂克之。
entries.en: At daybreak, drums and gongs shook the earth; the entire city trembled with fear, and the place was taken.
entries.literal: At dawn, drums and gongs shook the earth; the whole city trembled in fear, and they then captured it.

entries.zh: 擒其王子別兒怯帖木兒，及偽國公以下三十餘人，收其部落輜重以歸。
entries.en: He captured Hami's prince Bie'erqietemür and more than thirty others down to the false state duke, then withdrew with the tribe's baggage train.
entries.literal: They captured its prince Bie'erqietemür and more than thirty persons including the false state duke downward; they gathered its tribal baggage and returned.

entries.zh: 自是番戎慴服，兵威極於西域。
entries.en: From then on the frontier peoples submitted in fear, and Ming military prestige reached its height in the Western Regions.
entries.literal: From this the frontier barbarians feared submission, and military awesomeness reached its peak in the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 明年五月從藍玉征罕東，徇阿真川，土酋哈昝等遁去。
entries.en: The following May he followed Lan Yu on the campaign against Handong, advancing along the Azhen River while native chieftains such as Haza fled.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the next year he followed Lan Yu in campaigning against Handong, marched along Azhen River, and the native chieftains Haza and others fled away.

entries.zh: 師還，調中軍都督僉事。
entries.en: When the army returned, he was reassigned as assistant regional commander of the Central Army.
entries.literal: The army returned; he was transferred to assistant regional commander of the Central Army.

entries.zh: 二十八年六月，從總兵官周興出開原，至忽剌江。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year he joined overall commander Zhou Xing in marching from Kaiyuan to the Hula River.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-eighth year, he followed overall commander Zhou Xing out from Kaiyuan to Hula River.

entries.zh: 部長西陽哈遁，追至甫答迷城，俘人畜而還。
entries.en: The tribal chief Xiyangha fled; Cheng pursued him to Pudami City, took captives and livestock, and withdrew.
entries.literal: The tribal chief Xiyangha fled; pursuing to Pudami City, they took captive people and livestock and returned.

entries.zh: 明年拜征南右副將軍，討廣西帡幪諸寨苗，擒斬七千餘人。
entries.en: The following year he was appointed Right Vice General for the Southern Expedition and campaigned against Miao stockades at Pingmeng in Guangxi, capturing or killing more than seven thousand.
entries.literal: The next year he was appointed Right Vice General for the Southern Expedition, campaigning against the Miao of the various stockades at Pingmeng in Guangxi; captured and beheaded more than seven thousand persons.

entries.zh: 又明年，總羽林八衛兵討平五開、龍裏苗。
entries.en: The year after that he led the eight Palace Guard garrisons and pacified the Miao of Wukai and Longli.
entries.literal: Again the next year, commanding the troops of the eight guards of the Palace Guard, he campaigned to pacify the Miao of Wukai and Longli.

entries.zh: 三十一年出鎮開平，從燕王出塞，還城萬全諸衛。
entries.en: In the thirty-first year he took command at Kaiping, accompanied the Prince of Yan on a campaign beyond the frontier, and on the return fortified the garrisons at Wanquan.
entries.literal: In the thirty-first year he went out to command at Kaiping, followed the Prince of Yan beyond the frontier, and on return walled the various guards at Wanquan.

entries.zh: 建文改元，仍鎮甘肅。
entries.en: When the Jianwen era began, he continued to hold command in Gansu.
entries.literal: When the Jianwen reign era began, he still commanded at Gansu.

entries.zh: 成祖即位，入朝，進後軍左都督，拜平羌將軍，遣還鎮。
entries.en: After Emperor Chengzu took the throne, he came to court, was promoted to Left Regional Commander of the Rear Army, appointed General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and sent back to his frontier command.
entries.literal: When Emperor Chengzu ascended the throne, he entered court, was advanced to Left Regional Commander of the Rear Army, appointed General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and sent back to command.

entries.zh: 永樂三年招降把都帖木兒、倫都兒灰等部落五千人，獲馬駝牛羊萬六千。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongle he induced five thousand tribesmen under Badutemür, Lundu'erhui, and others to submit, and seized sixteen thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongle he induced the surrender of the tribes of Badutemür, Lundu'erhui, and others—five thousand persons—and obtained sixteen thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

entries.zh: 封西寧侯，祿千一百石，世指揮使。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xining with an annual stipend of 1,100 shi and the hereditary rank of garrison commander.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xining, with an emolument of 1,100 shi, hereditary garrison commander.

entries.zh: 晟凡四鎮涼州，前後二十餘年，威信著絕域。
entries.en: In all Cheng held command at Liangzhou four times over more than twenty years, and his prestige reached the farthest frontiers.
entries.literal: Cheng altogether four times commanded at Liangzhou; front and back more than twenty years, prestige and authority were renowned in the remote regions.

entries.zh: 帝以晟舊臣，有大將材，專任以邊事，所奏請輒報可。
entries.en: The emperor, regarding Cheng as a veteran with true generalship, gave him exclusive charge of frontier affairs, and his proposals were invariably approved.
entries.literal: The Emperor, because Cheng was an old minister with great general's talent, specially entrusted him with frontier affairs; whatever he memorialized requesting was always approved.

entries.zh: 御史劾晟自專。
entries.en: A censor impeached Cheng for acting autocratically.
entries.literal: A censor impeached Cheng for acting on his own authority.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「任人不專則不能成功，況大將統制一邊，寧能盡拘文法。」
entries.en: The emperor replied: "If one does not give an appointee full authority, nothing can be accomplished—and when a major general controls an entire frontier, how can he be shackled by every rule in the code?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said: "If one does not entrust a man with full authority, success cannot be achieved; moreover, when a great general commands a frontier, how can he be fully bound by written regulations?"

entries.zh: 即敕晟以便宜從事。
entries.en: He immediately authorized Cheng to act at his discretion as circumstances required.
entries.literal: He at once ordered Cheng to act at his discretion as circumstances required.

entries.zh: 晟嘗請入朝。
entries.en: Cheng once requested leave to come to court.
entries.literal: Cheng once requested to enter court.

entries.zh: 報曰：「西北邊務，一以委卿，非召命，毋輒來。」
entries.en: The reply read: "Northwestern frontier affairs are entirely yours; unless you are summoned, do not come on your own."
entries.literal: The reply said: "Northwestern frontier affairs I entirely entrust to you; unless summoned, do not come on your own."

entries.zh: 尋命營河西牧地，及圖出塞方略。
entries.en: He was soon ordered to develop pasture lands west of the Yellow River and to draft plans for campaigns beyond the frontier.
entries.literal: Soon he was ordered to develop pasture lands west of the river and to map plans for campaigns beyond the frontier.

entries.zh: 會病卒，五年七月也。
entries.en: He then fell ill and died, in the seventh month of the fifth year.
entries.literal: He happened to die of illness—it was the seventh month of the fifth year.

entries.zh: 晟三子。
entries.en: Cheng had three sons.
entries.literal: Cheng had three sons.

entries.zh: 長瑄，建文中為府軍右衛指揮使，戰靈璧，先登，斬數級，力鬥死。
entries.en: The eldest, Xuan, was garrison commander of the Right Guard of the Palace Army during the Jianwen reign. At Lingbi he was first over the wall, killed several enemies, and died fighting.
entries.literal: The eldest Xuan, during Jianwen's reign served as garrison commander of the Right Guard of the Palace Army; at the battle of Lingbi he was first to ascend, beheaded several heads, and died fighting with full strength.

entries.zh: 瑄弟琥，尚成祖女安成公主，得嗣侯，予世券。
entries.en: Xuan's younger brother Hu married Emperor Chengzu's daughter, Princess Ancheng, succeeded to the marquisate, and received a patent of hereditary entitlement.
entries.literal: Xuan's younger brother Hu, married Emperor Chengzu's daughter Princess Ancheng, obtained succession to the marquisate, and was granted a patent of hereditary entitlement.

entries.zh: 八年佩前將軍印，鎮甘肅。
entries.en: In the eighth year he bore the former general's seal and held command in Gansu.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he wore the seal of the former general and commanded at Gansu.

entries.zh: 十年與李彬捕叛酋老的罕，俘斬甚眾。
entries.en: In the tenth year he and Li Bin captured the rebel chieftain Laodehan, taking many prisoners and heads.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, together with Li Bin, he captured the rebellious chieftain Laodehan; captives and beheadings were very numerous.

entries.zh: 召還。
entries.en: He was then recalled.
entries.literal: Recalled.

entries.zh: 洪熙元年坐不敬奪爵，並削駙馬都尉官。
entries.en: In the first year of Hongxi he was stripped of his title for disrespect and also lost his post as Commandant of Attendants-in-Ordinary.
entries.literal: In the first year of Hongxi, through disrespect he was stripped of the marquisate and also removed from the office of Commandant of Attendants-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 宣德中復都尉。
entries.en: During the Xuande reign his commandant rank was restored.
entries.literal: During Xuande the commandant post was restored.

entries.zh: 琥既廢，弟瑛嗣。
entries.en: After Hu's deposition, his younger brother Ying succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: Hu having been deposed, his younger brother Ying succeeded.

entries.zh: 瑛尚鹹寧公主。
entries.en: Ying married Princess Xianning.
entries.literal: Ying married Princess Xianning.

entries.zh: 正統中，歷掌左軍前府事。
entries.en: During the Zhengtong reign he successively directed affairs in the Front Office of the Left Army.
entries.literal: During Zhengtong, he successively managed the affairs of the Front Office of the Left Army.

entries.zh: 瓦剌也先入寇，瑛充總兵官，督大同守將朱冕、石亨等戰陽和，全軍敗沒，瑛及冕皆戰死。
entries.en: When Esen of the Oirats invaded, Ying served as overall commander, directing Datong garrison commanders Zhu Mian and Shi Heng in the battle at Yanghe. The entire force was destroyed, and both Ying and Mian were killed.
entries.literal: When the Oirat leader Esen invaded, Ying served as overall commander, supervising the Datong garrison commanders Zhu Mian, Shi Heng, and others in battle at Yanghe; the whole army was defeated and destroyed, and both Ying and Mian died in battle.

entries.zh: 贈鄆國公，謚忠順。
entries.en: He was posthumously ennobled as Duke of Yun with the posthumous title Loyal and Obedient.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted Duke of Yun, posthumous title Zhongshun.

entries.zh: 子傑嗣。
entries.en: His son Jie succeeded him.
entries.literal: His son Jie succeeded.

entries.zh: 景泰中典禁兵宿衛，以謹慎稱。
entries.en: During the Jingtai reign he commanded the palace guard, noted for his careful conduct.
entries.literal: During Jingtai he managed the forbidden troops on palace guard duty, renowned for prudence.

entries.zh: 卒，子誠嗣。
entries.en: On his death his son Cheng succeeded.
entries.literal: He died; his son Cheng succeeded.

entries.zh: 署右府事，復佩平羌將軍印，鎮甘肅。
entries.en: He acted in the Right Office, again bore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang, and held command in Gansu.
entries.literal: Acting in the affairs of the Right Office, he again wore the seal of General Who Pacifies the Qiang and commanded at Gansu.

entries.zh: 誠有材武，嘗出獵至涼州，遇寇掠牛馬北去。
entries.en: Cheng was skilled in arms; once while hunting near Liangzhou he encountered raiders driving stolen cattle and horses northward.
entries.literal: Cheng had talent and martial ability; once on a hunting outing he reached Liangzhou, encountered bandits plundering cattle and horses and going north.
