entries.zh: 誠三矢殪三人，寇驚散，盡驅所掠還。
entries.en: Cheng killed three raiders with three arrows; the rest fled in panic, and he recovered all the stolen livestock.
entries.literal: Cheng with three arrows killed three men; the bandits startled and scattered, and he drove back all that had been plundered.

entries.zh: 九傳至孫裕德，死流寇難。
entries.en: After nine generations the line reached his grandson Yude, who was killed in the roving-bandit upheavals.
entries.literal: Through nine transmissions to grandson Yude, he died in the calamity of roaming bandits.

entries.zh: ○宋晟薛祿
entries.en: Song Cheng and Xue Lu
entries.literal: ○ Song Cheng, Xue Lu

entries.zh: （郭義金玉）
entries.en: (Guo Yi, Jin Yu)
entries.literal: (Guo Yi, Jin Yu)

entries.zh: 劉榮朱榮費瓛譚廣陳懷
entries.en: Liu Rong, Zhu Rong, Fei Huan, Tan Guang, and Chen Huai
entries.literal: Liu Rong, Zhu Rong, Fei Huan, Tan Guang, Chen Huai

entries.zh: （馬亮）
entries.en: (Ma Liang)
entries.literal: (Ma Liang)

entries.zh: 蔣貴
entries.en: Jiang Gui
entries.literal: Jiang Gui

entries.zh: （孫琬）
entries.en: (Sun Wan)
entries.literal: (Sun Wan)

entries.zh: 贊曰：明太祖時，國學師儒，體貌優重。
entries.en: The historian comments: Under the founding emperor, Imperial University teachers enjoyed exceptional honor.
entries.literal: The comment says: In the time of Ming Taizu, teachers at the Imperial Academy received preferential treatment in bearing and status.

entries.zh: 魏觀、宋訥為祭酒，造就人才，克舉其職。
entries.en: As chancellors, Wei Guan and Song Na trained talent and fulfilled their roles.
entries.literal: Wei Guan and Song Na as chancellors molded talent and fully performed their duties.

entries.zh: 諸生銜命奉使，往往擢為大官，不專以科目進也。
entries.en: Students sent on missions often rose to high office without relying solely on examinations.
entries.literal: Students bearing orders on missions were often promoted to high office; advancement was not solely through the examination track.

entries.zh: 中葉以還，流品稍雜，撥歷亦為具文，成均師席，不過為儒臣序遷之地而已。
entries.en: By mid-dynasty ranks grew mixed and practical training became nominal; the chancellorship was merely another step for literati.
entries.literal: From the mid-dynasty onward the stream of ranks grew somewhat mixed; practical assignments also became empty form; the master's seat at the Imperial Academy was no more than a place in the orderly promotion of scholar-officials.

entries.zh: 李時勉、陳敬宗諸人，方廉清鯁，表範卓然，類而傳之，庶觀者有所法焉。
entries.en: Yet Li Shimian, Chen Jingzong, and their peers were upright exemplars; recorded together, they might still teach later ages.
entries.literal: Li Shimian, Chen Jingzong, and the others were upright, pure, and stern, with outstanding models; if grouped and transmitted, perhaps observers would have something to emulate.

entries.zh: 李時勉陳敬宗劉鉉
entries.en: Li Shimian, Chen Jingzong, and Liu Xuan
entries.literal: Li Shimian, Chen Jingzong, Liu Xuan

entries.en: (Sa Qi)〉
entries.literal: (Sa Qi)〉

entries.zh: 邢讓
entries.en: Xing Rang
entries.literal: Xing Rang

entries.en: (Li Shao)〉
entries.literal: (Li Shao)〉

entries.zh: 林瀚
entries.en: Lin Han
entries.literal: Lin Han

entries.zh: 〈（子庭㭿庭機孫燫烴）〉
entries.en: (sons Ting'ang and Tingji; grandsons Xun and Xuen)〉
entries.literal: (sons Ting'ang and Tingji; grandsons Xun and Xuen)〉

entries.zh: 謝鐸魯鐸
entries.en: Xie Duo and Lu Duo
entries.literal: Xie Duo, Lu Duo

entries.en: (Zhao Yong)〉
entries.literal: (Zhao Yong)〉

entries.zh: 曹鼐
entries.en: Cao Nai
entries.literal: Cao Nai

entries.zh: 〈（張益鄺埜）〉
entries.en: (Zhang Yi; Kuang Ye)〉
entries.literal: (Zhang Yi; Kuang Ye)〉

entries.zh: 王佐
entries.en: Wang Zuo
entries.literal: Wang Zuo

entries.zh: 〈（丁鉉等）〉
entries.en: (Ding Xian and others)〉
entries.literal: (Ding Xian and others)〉

entries.zh: 孫祥
entries.en: Sun Xiang
entries.literal: Sun Xiang

entries.en: (Xie Ze)〉
entries.literal: (Xie Ze)〉

entries.zh: 袁彬
entries.en: Yuan Bin
entries.literal: Yuan Bin

entries.zh: 〈（哈銘袁敏）〉
entries.en: (Ha Ming; Yuan Min)〉
entries.literal: (Ha Ming; Yuan Min)〉

entries.zh: 十四年七月，也先入寇，中官王振挾帝親征。
entries.en: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, Esen of the Oirats invaded; the eunuch Wang Zhen pressed the Emperor to take the field in person.
entries.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year, Esen of the Oirats invaded; the eunuch Wang Zhen induced the Emperor to lead a campaign in person.

entries.zh: 朝臣交章諫，不聽。
entries.en: Officials of the court submitted memorial after memorial in protest, but he would not heed them.
entries.literal: Court officials submitted memorial after memorial in remonstrance, but he would not listen.

entries.zh: 鼐與張益以閣臣扈從。
entries.en: Nai and Zhang Yi accompanied the campaign as Grand Secretariat ministers.
entries.literal: Nai and Zhang Yi accompanied the expedition as Grand Secretariat ministers.

entries.zh: 未至大同，士卒已乏糧。
entries.en: Before they reached Datong, the soldiers were already without adequate grain.
entries.literal: Before they reached Datong, the troops were already short of provisions.

entries.zh: 宋瑛、朱冕全軍沒。
entries.en: Song Ying and Zhu Mian were destroyed with their whole forces.
entries.literal: Song Ying and Zhu Mian were wiped out with their entire armies.

entries.zh: 諸臣請班師，振不許，趣諸軍進。
entries.en: The ministers asked to withdraw the army; Zhen refused and pressed the troops to advance.
entries.literal: The ministers asked to withdraw the army; Zhen would not permit it and urged the forces forward.

entries.zh: 大將朱勇膝行聽命，尚書鄺埜、王佐跪草中，至暮不得請。
entries.en: The commander Zhu Yong advanced on his knees to receive orders; the Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo knelt in the grass, yet until evening could not secure a hearing.
entries.literal: The commander Zhu Yong crawled on his knees to receive orders; the Ministers Kuang Ye and Wang Zuo knelt in the grass, but until evening could not obtain an audience.

entries.zh: 欽天監正彭德清言天象示警，若前，恐危乘輿。
entries.en: The Director of the Astronomy Bureau Peng Deqing said the heavens showed warnings: if they proceeded as before, the imperial carriage might be imperiled.
entries.literal: The Director of the Astronomy Bureau Peng Deqing said the heavens showed warnings: if they went on as before, the imperial carriage might be endangered.

entries.zh: 振詈曰：「爾何知！
entries.en: Zhen cursed him, saying: "What do you know!
entries.literal: Zhen reviled him, saying: "What do you know!

entries.zh: 若有此，亦天命也。」
entries.en: If that should come to pass, it is likewise Heaven's mandate."
entries.literal: If this should happen, it is also the mandate of Heaven."

entries.zh: 鼐曰：「臣子固不足惜，主上系天下安危，豈可輕進？」
entries.en: Nai said: "We subjects are not worth sparing, but Your Majesty holds the safety of the realm in your hands—how can you advance so lightly?"
entries.literal: Nai said: "We subjects are indeed not worth sparing, but Your Majesty bears the safety of the realm—how can you lightly advance?"

entries.zh: 振終不從。
entries.en: Zhen in the end would not agree.
entries.literal: Zhen in the end would not comply.

entries.zh: 前驅敗報踵至，始懼，欲還。
entries.en: Reports of defeat from the advance guard arrived in succession; he at last grew afraid and wished to turn back.
entries.literal: Reports of defeat from the van arrived one after another; he at last grew afraid and wished to turn back.

entries.zh: 定襄侯郭登言於鼐、益曰：「自此趨紫荊，裁四十餘里，駕宜從紫荊入。」
entries.en: Guo Deng, Marquis of Dingxiang, said to Nai and Yi: "From here it is only a little over forty li to Zijing—the imperial carriage ought to enter by Zijing."
entries.literal: Guo Deng, Marquis of Dingxiang, said to Nai and Yi: "From here it is only a little over forty li to Zijing—the carriage ought to enter by Zijing."

entries.zh: 振欲邀帝至蔚州幸其第，不聽，復折而東，趨居庸。
entries.en: Zhen wished to bring the Emperor to Yu Prefecture to visit his own house; the Emperor did not listen, and they turned east again toward Juyong.
entries.literal: Zhen wished to invite the Emperor to Yu Prefecture to visit his own residence; the Emperor did not listen, and they turned east again toward Juyong.

entries.zh: 張益，字士謙，江寧人。
entries.en: Zhang Yi, styled Shiqian, came from Jiangning.
entries.literal: Zhang Yi, styled Shiqian, was a native of Jiangning.

entries.zh: 永樂十三年進士。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he passed the metropolitan examination.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle he became a metropolitan graduate.

entries.zh: 由庶吉士授中書舍人，改大理評事。
entries.en: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, then moved to Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: From Student of the Hanlin he was appointed Secretariat Drafter, then transferred to be Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 與修《宣宗實錄》成，改修撰。
entries.en: When the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were finished, he was made Compiler.
entries.literal: When the Veritable Records of the Xuande Emperor were completed, he was made Compiler.

entries.zh: 博學強記，詩文操筆立就，三楊雅重之。
entries.en: He was learned and had a powerful memory; his verse and prose were finished the moment he set brush to paper, and the Three Yangs greatly valued him.
entries.literal: He was broadly learned and had a strong memory; his poetry and prose were completed as soon as he took up the brush, and the Three Yangs held him in high esteem.

entries.zh: 尋進侍讀學士，正統十四年入文淵閣。
entries.en: He was soon promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and in the fourteenth year of Zhengtong entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.
entries.literal: Soon he was promoted to Reader-in-Waiting and in the fourteenth year of Zhengtong entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.

entries.zh: 未三月，遽蒙難以歿。
entries.en: In less than three months he suddenly met disaster and died.
entries.literal: In less than three months he suddenly met disaster and died.

entries.zh: 景帝立，贈學士，謚文僖。
entries.en: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, he was posthumously granted the title of Academician, with the posthumous name Wenxi.
entries.literal: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, he was posthumously given the title of Academician, with the posthumous name Wenxi.

entries.zh: 曾孫琮進士。
entries.en: His great-grandson Cong passed the metropolitan examination.
entries.literal: His great-grandson Cong was a metropolitan graduate.

entries.zh: 嘉靖初歷官南京右都御史。
entries.en: Early in the Jiajing reign he rose to Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he served successively as Right Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing.

entries.zh: 八月辛酉次土木。
entries.en: On the xinyou day of the eighth month they encamped at Tumu.
entries.literal: On the xinyou day of the eighth month they halted at Tumu.

entries.zh: 地高，掘地二丈不及水。
entries.en: The ground was high; they dug two zhang deep but still did not reach water.
entries.literal: The ground was high; they dug two zhang deep but still did not reach water.

entries.zh: 瓦剌大至，據南河。
entries.en: The Oirats arrived in strength and occupied the south bank of the river.
entries.literal: The Oirats came in force and held the south bank of the river.

entries.zh: 明日佯卻，且遣使通和。
entries.en: The next day they feigned retreat and also sent envoys to discuss peace.
entries.literal: The next day they feigned withdrawal and moreover sent envoys to negotiate peace.

entries.zh: 帝召鼐草詔答之。
entries.en: The Emperor summoned Nai to draft an edict in response.
entries.literal: The Emperor summoned Nai to draft an edict in reply.

entries.zh: 振遽令移營就水，行亂。
entries.en: Zhen abruptly ordered the camp shifted toward the water, and the army fell into disorder.
entries.literal: Zhen abruptly ordered the camp moved toward the water, and the march fell into disorder.

entries.zh: 寇騎蹂陣入，帝突圍不得出，擁以去。
entries.en: Enemy horsemen overran the formation; the Emperor could not break out and was seized and borne away.
entries.literal: Enemy horsemen trampled through the formation; the Emperor could not break out and was seized and carried away.

entries.zh: 鼐、益等俱及於難。
entries.en: Nai, Yi, and the others all perished in the disaster.
entries.literal: Nai, Yi, and the others all met disaster.

entries.zh: 景帝立，贈鼐少傅、吏部尚書、文淵閣大學士，謚文襄，官其子恩大理評事。
entries.en: When the Jing Emperor took the throne, Nai was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, with the posthumous title Wenxiang; his son En was appointed Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.
entries.literal: When the Jing Emperor ascended the throne, Nai was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, with the posthumous title Wenxiang; his son En was given office as Evaluator of the Court of Judicial Review.

entries.zh: 英宗復位，加贈太傅，改謚文忠，復官其孫榮錦衣百戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Ying regained the throne, Nai was further posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and his posthumous title changed to Wenzhong; his grandson Rong was again appointed a commander of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ying restored the throne, he was further posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and his posthumous title changed to Wenzhong; his grandson Rong was again given office as commander of one hundred households in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

entries.zh: 鼐弟鼎進士，歷吏科都給事中。
entries.en: Nai's younger brother Ding was a metropolitan graduate and rose to Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.
entries.literal: Nai's younger brother Ding was a metropolitan graduate and served successively as Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Personnel.

entries.zh: 景帝即位，進太子太傅。
entries.en: When the Jingtai emperor succeeded, Hu Ying was made grand tutor to the heir apparent.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jingdai took the throne, Ying was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 楊善使也先，濙言上皇蒙塵久，宜附進服食，不報。
entries.en: When Yang Shan went on embassy to the Oirats, Hu Ying urged that supplies be sent to the captive emperor, who had long suffered in the north, but the court did not reply.
entries.literal: When Yang Shan was sent to the Oirats, Ying urged that because the retired emperor had long been in hardship, food and clothing should be sent along with the mission, but there was no response.

entries.zh: 上皇將還，命禮部具奉迎儀。
entries.en: As the retired emperor was about to return, the throne ordered the ministry of rites to draw up welcome rites.
entries.literal: When the retired emperor was about to return, the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to prepare the welcome ceremony.

entries.zh: 濙等議遣禮部署迎於龍虎臺，錦衣具法駕迎居庸關，百司迎土城外，諸將迎教場門；
entries.en: Hu Ying and his colleagues proposed that rites officials meet him at Longhu Terrace, the imperial guard deploy the state carriage at Juyong Pass, all ministries receive him outside the earthen city wall, and generals receive him at the drill ground;
entries.literal: Ying and the others proposed that the Ministry of Rites send officials to welcome him at Longhu Terrace, the Brocade-Imperial Guard provide the imperial carriage to welcome him at Juyong Pass, the hundred officials welcome him outside the earth wall of the city, and the generals welcome him at the drill-ground gate;

entries.zh: 上皇自安定門入，進東安門，於東上北門南面坐；
entries.en: the retired emperor would enter by the Anding Gate, go on to the Dong'an Gate, and take a seat facing south at the upper north gate on the east side;
entries.literal: the retired emperor would enter by the Anding Gate, proceed to the Dong'an Gate, and be seated facing south at the north gate on the eastern upper level;

entries.zh: 皇帝謁見畢，百官朝見，上皇入南城大內。
entries.en: after the reigning emperor had performed his visit, the officials would attend, and the retired emperor would enter the inner quarters of the Southern Palace.
entries.literal: after the emperor paid his respects, the hundred officials would have audience, and the retired emperor would enter the Great Inner Palace of the Southern City.

entries.zh: 議上，傳旨以一轎二馬迎於居庸關，至安定門易法駕，余如奏。
entries.en: The proposal went up; the response was that a single sedan and two horses should meet him at Juyong Pass, the full imperial carriage only at the Anding Gate, with the rest as proposed.
entries.literal: When the proposal went up, an order was transmitted that one sedan chair and two horses should welcome him at Juyong Pass, and at the Anding Gate the state carriage should be exchanged for — the rest as memorialized.

entries.zh: 給事中劉福等言禮太薄。
entries.en: Supervising secretary Liu Fu and others protested that the ceremony was too mean.
entries.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Fu and others said the rites were too meager.

entries.zh: 帝報曰：「朕尊大兄為太上皇帝，尊禮無加矣。
entries.en: The emperor answered, "I honor my elder brother as Retired Emperor; no welcome could exceed that.
entries.literal: The emperor replied: I honor my elder brother as Retired Emperor; no honor can be added.

entries.zh: 福等顧雲太薄，其意何居？
entries.en: Why do Liu Fu and his fellows call the rites too thin — what are they driving at?
entries.literal: Why do Fu and the others speak of the rites being too meager — what is their intent?

entries.zh: 禮部其會官詳察之。」
entries.en: Let the ministry of rites convene officials and review this carefully."
entries.literal: Let the Ministry of Rites assemble officials and examine this in detail.

entries.zh: 濙等言：「諸臣意無他，欲陛下篤親親耳。」
entries.en: Hu Ying and his colleagues replied, "Their only aim is that Your Majesty should show deep family feeling."
entries.literal: Ying and the others said: "The ministers have no other intent; they wish Your Majesty to deepen the bonds of kinship."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「昨得太上皇書，具言迎駕之禮宜從簡損，朕豈得違之。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Yesterday I received a letter from the Retired Emperor stating plainly that the welcome should be kept simple; how could I go against it?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Yesterday I received a letter from the Retired Emperor, stating in full that the welcome rites should be kept simple and reduced — how can I disobey?"

entries.zh: 群臣乃不敢言。
entries.en: The officials fell silent.
entries.literal: The ministers then dared not speak further.

entries.zh: 會千戶龔遂榮為書投大學士高谷，言奉迎宜厚，具言唐肅宗迎上皇故事。
entries.en: Meanwhile the qianhu Gong Suirong sent Grand Secretary Gao Gu a letter arguing that the welcome should be lavish and citing Tang Suzong's reception of his father.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Qianhu Gong Suirong wrote a letter and sent it to Grand Secretary Gao Gu, saying the welcome ought to be generous and citing in full the Tang precedent of Emperor Suzong welcoming the retired emperor.

entries.zh: 谷袖之以朝，與王直等共觀之。
entries.en: Gao Gu carried it to court and read it with Wang Zhi and the others.
entries.literal: Gu tucked it in his sleeve and took it to court, and with Wang Zhi and the others examined it together.

entries.zh: 直與濙欲聞之帝，為都御史王文所阻，而給事中葉盛竟以聞。
entries.en: Wang Zhi and Hu Ying wanted to report it to the throne but were stopped by Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen; supervising secretary Ye Sheng nevertheless brought it forward.
entries.literal: Zhi and Ying wished to inform the emperor, but were blocked by Censor-in-Chief Wang Wen; yet Supervising Secretary Ye Sheng in the end reported it.

entries.zh: 盛同官林聰復劾直、濙、谷等，皆股肱大臣，有聞必告，不宜偶語竊議。
entries.en: Ye's colleague Lin Cong impeached Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, Gao Gu, and the rest for talking in private instead of reporting what they knew, as pillar ministers should.
entries.literal: Ye's colleague Lin Cong again impeached Zhi, Ying, Gu, and the rest, saying that as pillar ministers, whatever they learned they ought to report, and ought not to whisper in private deliberation.

entries.zh: 有詔索書。
entries.en: An edict was issued demanding the letter.
entries.literal: An imperial order was issued to demand the letter.

entries.zh: 濙等因以書進，且言：「肅宗迎上皇典禮，今日正可仿行。
entries.en: Hu Ying and his colleagues then submitted the letter and added, "The rites with which Tang Suzong welcomed his father are just what should be followed now.
entries.literal: Ying and the others thereupon submitted the letter, and moreover said: "The ceremony by which Emperor Suzong welcomed the retired emperor is exactly what should be followed today.

entries.zh: 陛下宜躬迎安定門外，分遣大臣迎龍虎臺。」
entries.en: Your Majesty should meet him in person outside the Anding Gate and send senior ministers to Longhu Terrace."
entries.literal: Your Majesty ought personally to welcome him outside the Anding Gate and dispatch great ministers to welcome him at Longhu Terrace."

entries.zh: 帝不悅曰：「第從朕命，無事紛更。」
entries.en: The emperor, angered, said, "Do as I command; do not keep stirring this up."
entries.literal: The emperor, displeased, said: "Just follow my command; do not stir up trouble."

entries.zh: 上皇至，居南城宮。
entries.en: When the Retired Emperor returned, he lived in the palace of the Southern City.
entries.literal: When the Retired Emperor arrived, he dwelt in the Southern City palace.

entries.zh: 濙請帝明年正旦率群臣朝延安門，不許。
entries.en: Hu Ying asked that on the next New Year's Day the emperor lead the ministers in homage at the Yan'an Gate, but the request was denied.
entries.literal: Ying asked that on New Year's Day of the following year the emperor lead the ministers in audience at the Yan'an Gate, but permission was refused.

entries.zh: 上皇萬壽節，請令百官拜賀延安門，亦不許。
entries.en: On the Retired Emperor's birthday Hu Ying again asked that officials offer congratulations at the Yan'an Gate; again the request was denied.
entries.literal: On the Retired Emperor's longevity birthday, Ying again asked that the hundred officials offer congratulations at the Yan'an Gate; again permission was refused.

entries.zh: 三年正月與王直並進少傅。
entries.en: In the third year, first month, he and Wang Zhi were both promoted to junior grand tutor.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year he and Wang Zhi were both advanced to Junior Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 易太子，加兼太子太師。
entries.en: When the heir was changed he was also made grand preceptor to the crown prince.
entries.literal: When the crown prince was replaced, he was additionally made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 王文惡林聰，文致其罪，欲殺之。
entries.en: Wang Wen hated Lin Cong, fabricated charges against him, and sought his death.
entries.literal: Wang Wen hated Lin Cong; he forged charges against him and wished to kill him.

entries.zh: 濙不肯署，遂稱疾，數日不朝。
entries.en: Hu Ying refused to countersign, then pleaded illness and stayed away from court for days.
entries.literal: Ying refused to sign, then claimed illness and for several days did not attend court.

entries.zh: 帝使興安問疾。
entries.en: The emperor sent the eunuch Xing An to ask after his health.
entries.literal: The emperor sent Xing An to inquire after his illness.

entries.zh: 對曰：「老臣本無疾，聞欲殺林聰，殊驚悸耳。」
entries.en: He answered, "This old minister is not ill; hearing they meant to kill Lin Cong, I was only shaken with alarm."
entries.literal: He replied: "This old minister has no illness; hearing that they wished to kill Lin Cong, I was greatly startled and distressed."

entries.zh: 聰由是得釋。
entries.en: Lin Cong was released as a result.
entries.literal: Lin Cong was thereby released.

entries.zh: 帝將親征也先，直率廷臣力諫曰：「國家備邊最為謹嚴。
entries.en: When the emperor was about to take the field against Esen personally, Wang Zhi led the ministers in strong remonstrance: "The empire guards its frontiers with the utmost care.
entries.literal: When the emperor was about to campaign personally against Esen, Zhi led the court ministers in forceful remonstrance: "The state's frontier defense is maintained with greatest strictness.

entries.zh: 謀臣猛將，堅甲利兵，隨處充滿，且耕且守，是以久安。
entries.en: Counsellors and bold generals, stout armor and sharp weapons, fill every post; men farm and guard together, and so the realm has long been at peace.
entries.literal: Counsellors and fierce generals, strong armor and sharp weapons, are plentiful everywhere, farming and guarding together — thus long peace is secured.

entries.zh: 今敵肆猖獗，違天悖理，陛下但宜固封疆，申號令，堅壁清野，蓄銳以待之，可圖必勝。
entries.en: Now the enemy rampages in defiance of Heaven and right; Your Majesty need only hold the borders firm, issue orders, clear the countryside, and gather strength to wait — victory can be assured.
entries.literal: Now the enemy runs riot in defiance of Heaven and reason; Your Majesty need only secure the borders, issue commands, clear the countryside and hold fast, and store sharpness to await them — victory can be planned for.

entries.zh: 不必親禦六師，遠臨塞下。
entries.en: There is no need for Your Majesty to lead the Six Armies in person to the distant frontier.
entries.literal: There is no need for Your Majesty personally to lead the Six Armies far to the borderlands.

entries.zh: 況秋署未退，旱氣未回，青草不豐，水泉猶塞，士馬之用未充。
entries.en: Moreover autumn heat lingers, drought has not lifted, grass is thin, springs are low, and men and horses are not ready.
entries.literal: Moreover the autumn heat has not yet passed, drought has not yet broken, green pasture is not rich, springs are still blocked, and horses and men are not fully supplied.

entries.zh: 兵兇戰危，臣等以為不可。」
entries.en: War is perilous — we your ministers believe it must not be done."
entries.literal: War is perilous — we your subjects believe it cannot be done."

entries.zh: 帝不從，命直留守。
entries.en: The emperor would not listen and ordered Wang Zhi to remain and guard the capital.
entries.literal: The emperor did not assent and ordered Zhi to remain on guard.

entries.zh: 王師覆於土木。
entries.en: The imperial army was destroyed at Tumu.
entries.literal: The imperial army was destroyed at Tumu.

entries.zh: 大臣群請太后立皇子為皇太子，命郕王攝政。
entries.en: The great ministers asked the empress dowager to install the prince as heir apparent and have the Prince of Cheng act as regent.
entries.literal: The great ministers together asked the Empress Dowager to establish the prince as heir apparent and order the Prince of Cheng to govern as regent.

entries.zh: 已，勸王即位，以安反側。
entries.en: Soon they urged the prince to ascend the throne to steady the realm.
entries.literal: Before long they urged the prince to take the throne to secure the realm against unrest.

entries.zh: 時變起倉卒，朝臣議屢上，皆直為首。
entries.en: In the sudden crisis memorials poured in, and Wang Zhi led them all.
entries.literal: At that time sudden turmoil arose and court debates came up repeatedly — Zhi led them all.

entries.zh: 而直自以不如于謙，每事推下之，雍容鎮率而已。
entries.en: Yet Wang Zhi felt himself inferior to Yu Qian and always deferred to him, himself remaining calm and steady.
entries.literal: Yet Zhi himself felt he was not the equal of Yu Qian and always deferred to him in affairs, remaining calm and steady in command.

entries.zh: 加太子太保。
entries.en: He was made grand guardian of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: He was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 明年正月進少傅。
entries.en: In the first month of the following year he was made junior grand tutor.
entries.literal: In the first month of the following year he was advanced to Junior Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 帝欲易太子。
entries.en: The emperor meant to depose the crown prince.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to replace the crown prince.

entries.zh: 未發。
entries.en: He had not yet announced it.
entries.literal: The matter had not yet been announced.

entries.zh: 會思明土知府黃矰以為請。
entries.en: Then Huang Zeng, native-office prefect of Siming, memorialized asking for it.
entries.literal: It happened that Huang Ying, native-office prefect of Siming, requested this.

entries.zh: 帝喜，下禮部議。
entries.en: The emperor was pleased and referred the matter to the ministry of rites.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and sent the matter down to the Ministry of Rites for deliberation.

entries.zh: 胡濙唯唯，文武諸臣議者九十一人當署名，直有難色。
entries.en: Hu Ying gave vague assent; ninety-one civil and military officials who debated had to sign, and Wang Zhi looked troubled.
entries.literal: Hu Ying assented vaguely; ninety-one civil and military officials who deliberated had to sign, and Zhi showed reluctance.

entries.zh: 陳循濡筆強之，乃署，竟易皇太子。
entries.en: Chen Xun dipped the brush and pressed him until he signed; the heir was changed in the end.
entries.literal: Chen Xun dipped the brush and forced him — he signed, and in the end the crown prince was replaced.

entries.zh: 直進兼太子太師，賜金幣加等。
entries.en: Wang Zhi was made grand preceptor to the heir apparent as well, with extra gifts of gold and silk.
entries.literal: Zhi was promoted to concurrent Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent with enhanced gifts of gold and silks.

entries.zh: 頓足嘆曰：「此何等大事，乃為一蠻酋所壞，吾輩愧死矣。」
entries.en: He stamped his foot and sighed, "What a great matter, ruined by a tribal chief — we should die of shame."
entries.literal: He stamped his foot and sighed: "What a great affair, to be ruined by a barbarian chieftain — we ought to die of shame."

entries.zh: 景帝疾亟，直、濙等會諸大臣臺諫，請復立沂王為皇太子，推大學士商輅草疏。
entries.en: When the Jingtai emperor was critically ill, Wang Zhi and Hu Ying met ministers and censors to ask that the Prince of Yi be made heir again, asking Grand Secretary Shang Lu to draft the memorial.
entries.literal: When Emperor Jing was gravely ill, Zhi, Ying, and others met the great ministers and censorial officials and asked to restore the Prince of Yi as crown prince, entrusting Grand Secretary Shang Lu to draft the memorial.

entries.zh: 未上，而石亨、徐有貞等奪門迎上皇復位，殺王文等。
entries.en: Before it was submitted, Shi Heng and Xu Youzhen seized the gate to restore Yingzong and killed Wang Wen and others.
entries.literal: Before it was submitted, Shi Heng, Xu Youzhen, and others seized the gate to welcome the retired emperor back to the throne and killed Wang Wen and the rest.

entries.zh: 疏草留姚夔所，嘗出以示郎中陸昶，嘆曰：「是疏不及進，天也。」
entries.en: The draft stayed with Yao Kui; he once showed it to director Lu Chang and sighed, "That this memorial was not submitted in time was Heaven's doing."
entries.literal: The draft remained with Yao Kui; he once showed it to Director Lang Lu Chang and sighed: "This memorial was not submitted in time — Heaven's will."

entries.zh: 直遂乞休。
entries.en: Wang Zhi then asked to retire.
entries.literal: Zhi then asked to retire.

entries.zh: 賜璽書、金綺、楮幣，給驛歸。
entries.en: He received a sealed letter, gold brocade, and paper money, with an imperial courier home.
entries.literal: He was granted a sealed letter, gold brocade, and paper currency, and given an express post for his return.

entries.zh: 二年進少保、東閣大學士。
entries.en: In the second Jingtai year he was made junior guardian and grand secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
entries.literal: In the second year he was advanced to Junior Guardian and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

entries.zh: 易儲，加太子太傅，給二俸。
entries.en: When the crown prince was replaced, he was made grand tutor to the heir apparent and granted a double stipend.
entries.literal: When the heir was changed, he was given the additional title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and granted two salaries.

entries.zh: 應天、鳳陽災，命祀三陵，振貧民。
entries.en: After famine struck Yingtian and Fengyang, he was charged with rites at the three imperial tombs and relief for the destitute.
entries.literal: When disasters struck Yingtian and Fengyang, he was ordered to sacrifice at the three imperial tombs and relieve the poor.

entries.zh: 七年進謹身殿大學士，仍兼東閣。
entries.en: In the seventh year he became grand academician of the Hall of Cultivating Virtue while retaining his Eastern Pavilion post.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted Grand Academician of the Hall of Cultivating Virtue, still concurrently of the Eastern Pavilion.

entries.zh: 內閣七人，言論多齟齬。
entries.en: The seven grand secretaries often clashed in council.
entries.literal: The seven men of the Grand Secretariat were often at odds in debate.

entries.zh: 谷清直，持議正。
entries.en: Gao Gu was upright in character and steadfast in argument.
entries.literal: Gu was pure and upright and held to correct positions in debate.

entries.zh: 王文由谷薦，數擠谷。
entries.en: Wang Wen owed his rise to Gao Gu's recommendation yet repeatedly tried to undermine him.
entries.literal: Wang Wen had been recommended by Gu, yet repeatedly tried to squeeze him out.

entries.zh: 谷屢請解機務，不許。
entries.en: Gao Gu repeatedly asked to leave state affairs but was not allowed to resign.
entries.literal: Gu repeatedly asked to be relieved of administrative duties, but permission was refused.

entries.zh: 都給事中林聰忤權要論死，谷力救，得薄譴。
entries.en: Chief supervising secretary Lin Cong, who had offended the powerful, was condemned to death; Gao Gu fought hard for him, and Lin escaped with a mild punishment.
entries.literal: The Chief Palace Secretary Lin Cong, having offended powerful figures, was sentenced to death; Gu exerted himself to save him, and Lin received only a light reprimand.

entries.zh: 陳循及文構考官劉儼、黃諫，帝命禮部會谷復閱試卷。
entries.en: Chen Xun and Wang Wen framed the chief examiners Liu Yan and Huang Jian; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites, together with Gao Gu, to review the examination papers again.
entries.literal: Chen Xun and Wen fabricated charges against the examiners Liu Yan and Huang Jian; the emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to join with Gu in re-examining the papers.

entries.zh: 谷力言儼等無私，且曰：「貴胄與寒士競進，已不可。
entries.en: Gao Gu insisted that Liu Yan and his colleagues had shown no favoritism, adding, "It is bad enough when scions of great houses contend with poor scholars for advancement.
entries.literal: Gu strongly maintained that Liu and the others were unbiased, and said: "For nobles and poor scholars to compete in advancement is already hard enough.

entries.zh: 況不安義命，欲因此構考官乎？」
entries.en: Must they also refuse to accept their fate and use this affair to destroy the examiners?"
entries.literal: How much worse to be discontent with one's lot in life and try to use this to frame the examiners?"

entries.zh: 帝乃賜循、文子中式，惟黜林挺一人，事得已。
entries.en: The emperor then allowed the sons of Chen Xun and Wang Wen to pass the examinations, demoting only Lin Ting, and the matter was closed.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon granted Chen Xun's and Wen's sons passage in the examinations, dismissing only Lin Ting, and the affair was closed.

entries.zh: 高谷胡濙王直
entries.en: Gao Gu, Hu Ying, and Wang Zhi
entries.literal: Gao Gu, Hu Ying, Wang Zhi

entries.zh: 十三年以兵部左侍郎召。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was recalled as Left Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of War.

entries.zh: 明年秋，也先大入寇，王振挾帝親征。
entries.en: The following autumn Esen invaded in force, and Wang Zhen pressed the emperor to lead the campaign himself.
entries.literal: The next autumn Esen launched a major invasion, and Wang Zhen compelled the emperor to campaign in person.

entries.zh: 謙與尚書鄺埜極諫，不聽。
entries.en: Qian and Minister Kuang Ye remonstrated with all their strength, but were not heard.
entries.literal: Qian and Minister Kuang Ye remonstrated to the utmost, but were not heeded.

entries.zh: 埜從治兵，留謙理部事。
entries.en: Ye went with the army; Qian was left to manage the ministry's affairs.
entries.literal: Ye followed to manage the army; Qian was left to handle ministry affairs.

entries.zh: 及駕陷土木，京師大震，眾莫知所為。
entries.en: When the emperor was captured at Tumu, the capital was convulsed with panic and no one knew what to do.
entries.literal: When the imperial carriage was trapped at Tumu, the capital was greatly shaken and none knew what to do.

entries.zh: 郕王監國，命群臣議戰守。
entries.en: The Prince of Cheng took charge of the realm and ordered the ministers to debate whether to fight or to hold the capital.
entries.literal: The Prince of Cheng supervised the state and ordered the ministers to deliberate on fighting or holding.

entries.zh: 侍講徐珵言星象有變，當南遷。
entries.en: Court lecturer Xu Cheng said the heavens showed ominous signs and urged moving the capital south.
entries.literal: Court Lecturer Xu Cheng said the stars showed change and that they should move the capital south.

entries.zh: 謙厲聲曰：「言南遷者，可斬也。
entries.en: Qian said sharply: "Whoever speaks of moving south deserves death.
entries.literal: Qian said in a stern voice: "Whoever speaks of moving south may be executed.

entries.zh: 京師天下根本，一動則大事去矣，獨不見宋南渡事乎！」
entries.en: The capital is the foundation of the realm; move it and the cause is lost—have you forgotten how the Song fled south across the Yangzi!"
entries.literal: The capital is the root of all under Heaven; if it moves then the great affair is lost—have you alone not seen the affair of the Song moving south across the river!"

entries.zh: 王是其言，守議乃定。
entries.en: The prince agreed, and the decision to defend the capital was settled.
entries.literal: The prince approved his words, and the plan to hold was settled.

entries.zh: 時京師勁甲精騎皆陷沒，所餘疲卒不及十萬，人心震恐，上下無固志。
entries.en: The capital's best armor and cavalry had perished; fewer than a hundred thousand exhausted troops remained. Panic gripped every heart, and court and city alike lacked firm resolve.
entries.literal: At the time the capital's strong armor and elite cavalry had all been lost; the remaining weary soldiers did not reach one hundred thousand, hearts were shaken with terror, and above and below had no firm resolve.

entries.zh: 謙請王檄取兩京、河南備操軍，山東及南京沿海備倭軍，江北及北京諸府運糧軍，亟赴京師。
entries.en: Qian asked the prince to issue orders summoning training troops from the two capitals and Henan, coastal anti-pirate forces from Shandong and Nanjing, and grain-transport troops from Jiangbei and the Beijing prefectures—all to rush to the capital.
entries.literal: Qian requested the prince issue orders to summon the training armies of the Two Capitals and Henan, the coastal anti-Wokou armies of Shandong and Nanjing, and the grain-transport armies of Jiangbei and the various prefectures of Beijing, to hurry to the capital.

entries.zh: 以次經畫部署，人心稍安。
entries.en: He arranged deployments in orderly stages, and minds grew somewhat steadier.
entries.literal: He deployed them in sequence step by step, and hearts were somewhat calmed.

entries.zh: 即遷本部尚書。
entries.en: He was promptly promoted to Minister of War.
entries.literal: He was immediately transferred to Minister of the ministry.

entries.zh: 郕王方攝朝，廷臣請族誅王振。
entries.en: As the Prince of Cheng held court, ministers called for the extermination of Wang Zhen's entire clan.
entries.literal: The Prince of Cheng was just regent in court; court ministers requested extermination of Wang Zhen's entire clan.

entries.zh: 而振党馬順者，輒叱言官。
entries.en: Wang Zhen's follower Ma Shun shouted down the remonstrating officials.
entries.literal: But Wang Zhen's partisan Ma Shun shouted down the remonstrating officials.

entries.zh: 於是給事中王竑廷擊順，眾隨之。
entries.en: Supervising secretary Wang Hong then struck Shun in open court, and the crowd followed.
entries.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretary Wang Hong struck Shun in the court, and the multitude followed.

entries.zh: 朝班大亂，衛卒聲洶洶。
entries.en: The court ranks dissolved into chaos; the guards' shouts rose in a roar.
entries.literal: The court ranks fell into great disorder, and the guard soldiers' voices were turbulent.

entries.zh: 王懼欲起，謙排眾直前掖王止，且啟王宣諭曰：「順等罪當死，勿論。」
entries.en: The prince, frightened, tried to rise; Qian pushed through the throng, seized the prince's arm, and urged him to announce: "Shun and his like deserve death—let it pass."
entries.literal: The prince in fear wished to rise; Qian pushed through the crowd straight forward to support the prince and stop him, and also addressed the prince to proclaim saying: "Shun and the rest deserve death by law—do not discuss it."

entries.zh: 眾乃定。
entries.en: Only then did the crowd quiet.
entries.literal: The multitude then settled.

entries.zh: 謙袍袖為之盡裂。
entries.en: Qian's sleeves were torn to shreds in the crush.
entries.literal: Qian's robe sleeves were completely torn because of it.

entries.zh: 退出左掖門，吏部尚書王直執謙手歎曰「國家正賴公耳。
entries.en: Leaving by the Left Flank Gate, Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi took Qian's hand and sighed: "The realm now depends on you alone.
entries.literal: Exiting the Left Flank Gate, Minister of Personnel Wang Zhi grasped Qian's hand and sighed: "The state just now relies on you.

entries.zh: 今日雖百王直何能為！」
entries.en: Today a hundred men like me could do nothing!"
entries.literal: Today even a hundred Wang Zhis—what could they do!"

entries.zh: 當是時，上下皆倚重謙，謙亦毅然以社稷安危為己任。
entries.en: At that moment court and capital alike leaned on Qian, and Qian in turn took the fate of the realm upon himself without hesitation.
entries.literal: At that time above and below all relied on Qian, and Qian also resolutely took the security of state and altars as his own responsibility.

entries.zh: 初，大臣憂國無主，太子方幼，寇且至，請皇太后立郕王。
entries.en: Earlier, ministers feared the realm had no ruler: the heir was young, the enemy was near, and they asked the empress dowager to enthrone the Prince of Cheng.
entries.literal: Initially the grand ministers worried the state had no ruler, the heir apparent was still young, and the enemy was about to arrive; they requested the empress dowager install the Prince of Cheng.

entries.zh: 王驚謝至再。
entries.en: The prince, alarmed, declined again and again.
entries.literal: The prince in alarm declined repeatedly.

entries.zh: 謙揚言曰：「臣等誠憂國家，非為私計。」
entries.en: Qian declared aloud: "We act only from concern for the state, not from private ambition."
entries.literal: Qian proclaimed aloud: "We ministers truly worry for the state and altars, not for private calculation."

entries.zh: 王乃受命。
entries.en: The prince then accepted.
entries.literal: The prince then accepted the mandate.

entries.zh: 九月，景帝立，謙入對，慷慨泣奏曰：「寇得志，要留大駕，勢必輕中國，長驅而南。
entries.en: In the ninth month the Jing Emperor was enthroned. Qian came before him, weeping as he spoke: "The enemy has triumphed and will hold the emperor hostage; they will surely despise China and drive south in force.
entries.literal: In the ninth month the Jing Emperor was established; Qian entered audience and, moved with emotion, wept as he memorialized: "The enemy has gained its aim and will detain the great carriage; they are certain to slight China and drive south at length.

entries.zh: 請飭諸邊守臣協力防遏。
entries.en: Order every frontier commander to cooperate in defense.
entries.literal: I request that frontier guarding ministers on all sides be ordered to cooperate in defense and obstruction.

entries.zh: 京營兵械且盡，宜亟分道募民兵，令工部繕器甲。
entries.en: The capital garrison's arms are nearly gone—recruit militia at once along several routes, and have the Ministry of Works repair armor and weapons.
entries.literal: The capital garrison's weapons and armor are nearly exhausted; we should urgently recruit civilian soldiers by separate routes and order the Ministry of Works to repair weapons and armor.

entries.zh: 遣都督孫鏜、衛穎、張軏、張儀、雷通分兵守九門要地，列營郭外。
entries.en: Send the military commissioners Sun Tang, Wei Ying, Zhang Yuan, Zhang Yi, and Lei Tong to hold the nine gates' critical points with divided forces, and pitch camps outside the walls.
entries.literal: Dispatch Military Commissioners Sun Tang, Wei Ying, Zhang Yuan, Zhang Yi, and Lei Tong to divide troops and guard the nine gates' vital points, arraying camps outside the wall.

entries.zh: 都御史楊善、給事中王竑參之。
entries.en: Let Censor-in-chief Yang Shan and supervising secretary Wang Hong assist them.
entries.literal: Censor-in-chief Yang Shan and Supervising Secretary Wang Hong should assist them.

entries.zh: 徙附郭居民入城。
entries.en: Move residents from the suburbs inside the walls.
entries.literal: Move suburban residents into the city.

entries.zh: 通州積糧，令官軍自詣關支，以贏米為之直，毋棄以資敵。
entries.en: For grain stored at Tongzhou, let troops draw it themselves at the passes, paying with surplus rice so nothing is abandoned to the enemy.
entries.literal: For accumulated grain at Tongzhou, order officers and soldiers to go in person to the pass to draw it, taking surplus rice as payment in kind, and not abandoning it to supply the enemy.

entries.zh: 文臣如軒輗者，宜用為巡撫。
entries.en: Civil officials such as Xuan Ni should serve as grand coordinators.
entries.literal: Civil officials such as Xuan Ni should be employed as grand coordinators.

entries.zh: 武臣如石亨、楊洪、柳溥者，宜用為將帥。
entries.en: Military men such as Shi Heng, Yang Hong, and Liu Pu should serve as commanders.
entries.literal: Military officials such as Shi Heng, Yang Hong, and Liu Pu should be employed as generals.

entries.zh: 至軍旅之事，臣身當之，不效則治臣罪。」
entries.en: As for the conduct of war, I will answer for it myself—if I fail, punish me."
entries.literal: As for military affairs, I myself will undertake them; if ineffective then punish my crime."

entries.zh: 帝深納之。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his counsel wholeheartedly.
entries.literal: The emperor deeply accepted it.

entries.zh: 景泰元年三月，總兵硃謙奏敵二萬攻圍萬全，敕范廣充總兵官禦之。
entries.en: In the third month of Jingtai 1, Commander Zhu Qian reported twenty thousand enemies besieging Wanquan; Fan Guang was ordered to take command of the defense.
entries.literal: In the third month of the first year of Jingtai, Commander-in-chief Zhu Qian memorialized that twenty thousand enemies were attacking and besieging Wanquan; an edict ordered Fan Guang to serve as commander-in-chief to defend.

entries.zh: 已而寇退，謙請即駐兵居庸，寇來則出關剿殺，退則就糧京師。
entries.en: When the enemy withdrew, Qian proposed stationing troops at Juyong: sally out to fight when the enemy came, fall back on the capital's grain when they retreated.
entries.literal: Soon the invaders retreated; Qian requested troops be stationed immediately at Juyong—when invaders came they would exit the pass to pursue and kill, and when they retreated they would draw grain from the capital.

entries.zh: 大同參將許貴奏，迤北有三人至鎮，欲朝廷遣使講和。
entries.en: Xu Gui, vice general at Datong, reported that three men from the north had arrived seeking peace talks with the court.
entries.literal: Datong Vice General Xu Gui memorialized that three men had come to the garrison from the north, wishing the court to dispatch envoys to negotiate peace.

entries.zh: 謙曰：「前遣指揮季鐸、嶽謙往，而也先隨入寇。
entries.en: Qian said, "We once sent Commanders Ji Duo and Yue Qian—and Esen invaded right behind them.
entries.literal: Qian said: "Previously we dispatched Commanders Ji Duo and Yue Qian, and Esen followed with invasion.

entries.zh: 繼遣通政王復、少卿趙榮，不見上皇而還。
entries.en: We then sent Wang Fu and Zhao Rong—they returned without even seeing the captive emperor.
entries.literal: We then sent Chief of Transmission Wang Fu and Junior Director Zhao Rong, and they returned without seeing the former emperor.

entries.zh: 和不足恃，明矣。
entries.en: Peace cannot be trusted. That much is plain.
entries.literal: Peace cannot be relied upon—it is clear.

entries.zh: 況我與彼不共戴天，理固不可和。
entries.en: We and they cannot live under the same sky; by right there can be no peace.
entries.literal: Moreover we and they cannot live under the same sky; by principle harmony is impossible.

entries.zh: 萬一和而彼肆無厭之求，從之則坐敝，不從則生變，勢亦不得和。
entries.en: Even if we made peace, their demands would know no end; yield and we exhaust ourselves, refuse and war reignites—in either case peace is impossible.
entries.literal: If by chance there were peace and they indulged insatiable demands, to agree would leave us exhausted sitting, and not to agree would breed change—by circumstance peace also could not be achieved.

entries.zh: 貴為介胄臣，而恇怯如此，何以敵愾，法當誅。」
entries.en: Gui, a minister who wears armor, yet shows such cowardice—how can he fight the enemy? By law he deserves death."
entries.literal: Gui is a minister in armor and helmet, yet so timid and cowardly—how can he face the enemy with shared wrath? By law he should be executed."

entries.zh: 移檄切責。
entries.en: He sent a stern rebuke by dispatch.
entries.literal: He sent a dispatch sternly rebuking him.

entries.zh: 自是邊將人人主戰守，無敢言講和者。
entries.en: From then on every frontier commander argued for war and defense; none dared speak of peace.
entries.literal: From this time frontier generals all advocated fighting and holding, and none dared speak of negotiating peace.

entries.zh: 十月敕謙提督各營軍馬。
entries.en: In the tenth month an edict placed Qian in overall command of all camp forces.
entries.literal: In the tenth month an edict ordered Qian to supervise all camps' armies and horses.

entries.zh: 而也先挾上皇破紫荊關直入，窺京師。
entries.en: Esen, holding the captive emperor, broke through Zijing Pass and pressed toward the capital.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Esen, holding the former emperor, broke through Zijing Pass and entered directly, spying on the capital.

entries.zh: 石亨議斂兵堅壁老之。
entries.en: Shi Heng urged pulling troops inside the walls and waiting the enemy out.
entries.literal: Shi Heng proposed gathering troops, strengthening walls, and wearing the enemy down.

entries.zh: 謙不可，曰：「奈何示弱，使敵益輕我。」
entries.en: Qian refused: "How can we show weakness and invite the enemy to despise us further?"
entries.literal: Qian would not agree and said: "How can we show weakness and make the enemy further slight us."

entries.zh: 亟分遣諸將，率師二十二萬，列陣九門外：都督陶瑾安定門，廣寧伯劉安東直門，武進伯硃瑛朝陽門，都督劉聚西直門，鎮遠侯顧興祖阜成門，都指揮李端正陽門，都督劉得新崇文門，都指揮湯節宣武門，而謙自與石亨率副總兵范廣、武興陳德勝門外，當也先。
entries.en: He immediately sent out his generals with two hundred twenty thousand men, drawing up battle lines outside the nine gates: Tao Jin at Anding, Liu An at Dongzhi, Zhu Ying at Chaoyang, Liu Ju at Xizhi, Gu Xingzu at Fucheng, Li Duan at Zhengyang, Liu Dexin at Chongwen, Tang Jie at Xuanwu—while Qian himself, with Shi Heng, led Vice Commanders Fan Guang and Wu Xing, arrayed outside Desheng Gate to meet Esen head-on.
entries.literal: He urgently dispatched the various generals, leading an army of two hundred twenty thousand and arraying formations outside the nine gates: Military Commissioner Tao Jin at Anding Gate, Earl of Guangning Liu An at Dongzhi Gate, Baron of Wujin Zhu Ying at Chaoyang Gate, Military Commissioner Liu Ju at Xizhi Gate, Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Xingzu at Fucheng Gate, Regional Commander Li Duan at Zhengyang Gate, Military Commissioner Liu Dexin at Chongwen Gate, Regional Commander Tang Jie at Xuanwu Gate, while Qian himself with Shi Heng led Vice Commanders-in-chief Fan Guang and Wu Xing, arrayed outside Desheng Gate to face Esen.

entries.zh: 以部事付侍郎吳寧，悉閉諸城門，身自督戰。
entries.en: He left ministry affairs to Vice Minister Wu Ning, shut every gate, and supervised the fighting in person.
entries.literal: He entrusted ministry affairs to Vice Minister Wu Ning, closed all city gates completely, and personally supervised the battle.

entries.zh: 下令，臨陣將不顧軍先退者，斬其將。
entries.en: He issued orders: any general who retreats before his men will be executed.
entries.literal: He issued orders: in battle if a general does not care for the army and retreats first, execute the general.

entries.zh: 軍不顧將先退者，後隊斬前隊。
entries.en: Any soldier who retreats before his commander will be cut down by the rank behind.
entries.literal: If soldiers do not care for the general and retreat first, the rear rank executes the front rank.

entries.zh: 於是將士知必死，皆用命。
entries.en: Officers and men knew they faced certain death, and all fought as ordered.
entries.literal: Thereupon officers and soldiers knew they must die and all obeyed orders.

entries.zh: 副總兵高禮、毛福壽卻敵彰義門北，擒其長一人。
entries.en: Vice commanders Gao Li and Mao Fushou drove the enemy back north of Zhangyi Gate and captured one of their leaders.
entries.literal: Vice Commanders-in-chief Gao Li and Mao Fushou repelled the enemy north of Zhangyi Gate and captured one of their chiefs.

entries.zh: 帝喜，令謙選精兵屯教場以便調用，復命太監興安、李永昌同謙理軍務。
entries.en: The emperor was pleased and ordered Qian to select elite troops and hold them on the drill ground for rapid deployment; eunuchs Xing'an and Li Yongchang were again assigned to assist Qian in military affairs.
entries.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered Qian to select elite troops stationed on the drill ground for convenient deployment, and again ordered eunuchs Xing'an and Li Yongchang to handle military affairs together with Qian.

entries.zh: 初，也先深入，視京城可旦夕下。
entries.en: At first Esen had driven deep inland, expecting to take the capital within a day.
entries.literal: Initially Esen had penetrated deeply and regarded the capital as fallible within a morning or evening.

entries.zh: 及見官軍嚴陣待，意稍沮。
entries.en: When he saw government troops drawn up in tight formation awaiting him, his confidence faltered.
entries.literal: When he saw the government army in strict formation waiting, his intent was somewhat discouraged.

entries.zh: 叛閹喜寧嗾使邀大臣迎駕，索金帛以萬萬計，復邀謙及王直、胡濙等出議。
entries.en: The defecting eunuch Xi Ning urged them to summon ministers to welcome the captive emperor, demanding gold and silk by the myriad, and again invited Qian, Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, and others to come out and negotiate.
entries.literal: The rebel eunuch Xi Ning instigated them to invite grand ministers to welcome the imperial carriage, demanding gold and silk counted by the tens of thousands, and again invited Qian and Wang Zhi, Hu Ying, and others to come out to negotiate.

entries.zh: 帝不許，也先氣益沮。
entries.en: The emperor refused, and Esen's ardor cooled further.
entries.literal: The emperor would not permit it, and Esen's spirit was further discouraged.

entries.zh: 庚申，寇窺德勝門。
entries.en: On the gengshen day the enemy probed Desheng Gate.
entries.literal: On gengshen day the invaders spied on Desheng Gate.

entries.zh: 謙令亨設伏空舍，遣數騎誘敵。
entries.en: Qian had Heng lay ambush in empty buildings and sent a few horsemen to bait the enemy.
entries.literal: Qian ordered Heng to set ambush in empty houses and sent several horsemen to lure the enemy.

entries.zh: 敵以萬騎來薄，副總兵范廣發火器，伏起齊擊之。
entries.en: Ten thousand enemy horsemen pressed in; Vice Commander Fan Guang fired his guns, and the ambush rose as one to strike them down.
entries.literal: The enemy came with ten thousand horsemen to press close; Vice Commander-in-chief Fan Guang discharged firearms, and the ambush rose together to strike them.

entries.zh: 也先弟孛羅、平章卯那孩中砲死。
entries.en: Esen's brother Boluo and the pingzhang Onahai were killed by cannon fire.
entries.literal: Esen's younger brother Boluo and Pingzhang Onahai were struck by cannon and died.

entries.zh: 寇轉至西直門，都督孫堂禦之，亨亦分兵至，寇引退。
entries.en: The enemy shifted to Xizhi Gate; Sun Tang held them off, and Heng arrived with reinforcements, and the invaders withdrew.
entries.literal: The invaders turned to Xizhi Gate; Military Commissioner Sun Tang defended against them, and Heng also divided troops and arrived, whereupon the invaders withdrew.

entries.zh: 副總兵武興擊寇彰義門，與都督王敬挫其前鋒。
entries.en: Wu Xing attacked the enemy at Zhangyi Gate; Wang Jing joined him and blunted the vanguard.
entries.literal: Vice Commander-in-chief Wu Xing struck the invaders at Zhangyi Gate and with Military Commissioner Wang Jing checked their vanguard.

entries.zh: 寇且卻，而內官數百騎欲爭功，躍馬競前。
entries.en: The enemy was on the verge of retreat when several hundred eunuch horsemen, eager for glory, spurred ahead in a reckless charge.
entries.literal: The invaders were about to retreat, but several hundred horsemen of inner eunuchs wished to compete for merit and spurred their horses to race forward.

entries.zh: 陣亂，興被流矢死，寇逐至土城。
entries.en: The formation broke; Xing fell to a stray arrow, and the enemy chased the rout to the earthen wall.
entries.literal: The formation fell into disorder; Xing was killed by a stray arrow, and the invaders pursued to the earthen wall.

entries.zh: 居民升屋，號呼投磚石擊寇，嘩聲動天。
entries.en: Residents climbed to their rooftops, shouting and hurling bricks and stones at the invaders until the din shook the sky.
entries.literal: Residents climbed onto roofs, shouting and hurling bricks and stones at the invaders; the clamor shook heaven.

entries.zh: 王竑及福壽援至，寇乃卻。
entries.en: Wang Hong and Mao Fushou arrived with reinforcements, and the enemy finally withdrew.
entries.literal: Wang Hong and Fushou's reinforcements arrived, and the invaders then retreated.

entries.zh: 相持五日，也先邀請既不應，戰又不利，知終弗可得志，又聞勤王師且至，恐斷其歸路，遂擁上皇由良鄉西去。
entries.en: After five days of stalemate, Esen's invitations went unanswered and his battles went ill; seeing he could not prevail, and hearing relief armies were near—fearing his retreat would be cut—he led the captive emperor west from Liangxiang.
entries.literal: After five days of stalemate, Esen's invitations received no response and battle was again unfavorable; knowing he could never achieve his aim, and hearing that relief armies were about to arrive and fearing his retreat cut off, he then escorted the former emperor west from Liangxiang.

entries.zh: 謙調諸將追擊，至關而還。
entries.en: Qian sent the generals in pursuit, halting at the frontier passes.
entries.literal: Qian deployed the generals in pursuit, returning when they reached the pass.

entries.zh: 論功，加謙少保，總督軍務。
entries.en: For his merit Qian was made Junior Guardian with overall command of military affairs.
entries.literal: When merits were discussed, Qian was promoted to Junior Guardian and made overall supervisor of military affairs.

entries.zh: 謙曰：「四郊多壘，卿大夫之恥也，敢邀功賞哉！」
entries.en: Qian said, "When enemies camp at the capital's gates, it is the minister's shame—how dare I claim reward!"
entries.literal: Qian said: "When the four suburbs have many enemy ramparts, it is the shame of ministers and grandees—how dare I seek merit and reward!"

entries.zh: 固辭，不允。
entries.en: He refused firmly, but the court would not hear of it.
entries.literal: He firmly declined, but was not permitted.

entries.zh: 乃益兵守真、保、涿、易諸府州，請以大臣鎮山西，防寇南侵。
entries.en: He reinforced the garrisons at Zhending, Baoding, Zhuozhou, and Yizhou, and asked that a senior minister hold Shanxi against a southern thrust.
entries.literal: He then increased troops to guard the prefectures of Zhen, Bao, Zhuo, and Yi, and requested that a grand minister garrison Shanxi to guard against the invaders' southward aggression.

entries.zh: 帝知謙深，所論奏無不從者。
entries.en: The emperor knew Qian's depth and never refused his counsel.
entries.literal: The emperor knew Qian was profound; whatever he memorialized was never not followed.

entries.zh: 嘗遣使往真定、河間采野菜，直沽造幹魚，謙一言即止。
entries.en: Once the emperor sent men to gather wild vegetables in Zhending and Hejian and to make dried fish at Zhigu; a single word from Qian ended it.
entries.literal: He once dispatched envoys to Zhending and Hejian to gather wild vegetables and to Zhigu to make dried fish; at one word from Qian it stopped.

entries.zh: 用一人，必密訪謙。
entries.en: Before appointing anyone, the emperor always consulted Qian in secret.
entries.literal: To employ one man, he always secretly consulted Qian.

entries.zh: 謙具實對，無所隱，不避嫌怨。
entries.en: Qian answered truthfully, hiding nothing and sparing no one's feelings.
entries.literal: Qian answered with full truth, hiding nothing, not avoiding resentment from those disliked.

entries.zh: 由是諸不任職者皆怨，而用弗如謙者，亦往往嫉之。
entries.en: The incompetent resented him; those less capable than he often envied him.
entries.literal: Because of this all the incompetent resented him, and those employed who were not Qian's equal also often envied him.

entries.zh: 比寇初退，都御史羅通即劾謙上功簿不實。
entries.en: As soon as the enemy withdrew, Censor-in-chief Luo Tong impeached Qian for inflating the merit rolls.
entries.literal: When the invaders had just retreated, Censor-in-chief Luo Tong immediately impeached Qian for falsifying the merit register.

entries.zh: 御史顧躭言謙太專，請六部大事同內閣奏行。
entries.en: Censor Gu Dan said Qian held too much power and asked that major matters of the Six Ministries go through the Grand Secretariat.
entries.literal: Censor Gu Dan said Qian was too monopolistic and requested that great affairs of the Six Ministries be submitted together with the Grand Secretariat for execution.

entries.zh: 謙據祖制折之，戶部尚書金濂亦疏爭，而言者捃摭不已。
entries.en: Qian rebutted them on precedent; Minister of Revenue Jin Lian also protested, but the critics kept finding new grievances.
entries.literal: Qian refuted it according to ancestral institutions; Minister of Revenue Jin Lian also memorialized in dispute, yet the speakers kept gathering accusations without end.

entries.zh: 諸御史以深文彈劾者屢矣，賴景帝破眾議用之，得以盡所設施。
entries.en: Censors impeached him repeatedly on technicalities; only because the Jing Emperor overruled them could Qian carry out his plans.
entries.literal: The various censors impeached with harsh legal wording many times; relying on the Jing Emperor breaking collective opinion to employ him, he was able fully to carry out what he planned.

entries.zh: 謙自值也先之變，誓不與賊俱生。
entries.en: From the day of Esen's invasion Qian swore he would not live while the enemy survived.
entries.literal: From when Qian encountered Esen's crisis he swore not to live together with the bandits.

entries.zh: 嘗留宿直廬，不還私第。
entries.en: He often slept in his office and never went home.
entries.literal: He often lodged overnight in the duty hall and did not return to his private residence.

entries.zh: 素病痰，疾作，景帝遣興安、舒良更番往視。
entries.en: He suffered chronic phlegm disorder; when it flared the Jing Emperor sent Xing'an and Shu Liang in rotation to check on him.
entries.literal: He had long suffered from phlegm illness; when the illness flared the Jing Emperor sent Xing'an and Shu Liang in rotation to visit him.

entries.zh: 聞其服用過薄，詔令上方制賜，至醯菜畢備。
entries.en: Learning how spare his fare was, the emperor ordered the imperial workshops to supply him—even vinegar and vegetables in full measure.
entries.literal: Hearing his food and clothing were excessively spare, an edict ordered the imperial workshop to make gifts, down to vinegar and vegetables all complete.

entries.zh: 又親幸萬歲山，伐竹取瀝以賜。
entries.en: The emperor himself went to Longevity Hill, cut bamboo, and sent the sap as medicine.
entries.literal: He also personally visited Longevity Hill, cut bamboo and took the sap to bestow.

entries.zh: 或言寵謙太過，興安等曰：「彼日夜分國憂，不問家產，即彼去，令朝廷何處更得此人？」
entries.en: Some said the emperor favored Qian too much; Xing'an replied, "He shares the state's burdens day and night and never tends his own affairs—where will the court find another like him?"
entries.literal: Some said favoring Qian was excessive; Xing'an and others said: "He day and night shares the state's worry and does not inquire after household property—even if he left, where could the court find such a man again?"

entries.zh: 及籍沒，家無餘資，獨正室鐍鑰甚固。
entries.en: When his estate was seized, nothing remained but his main chamber, locked tight.
entries.literal: When his property was registered and confiscated, the household had no surplus funds; only the main chamber's lock and key were very secure.

entries.zh: 啟視，則上賜蟒衣、劍器也。
entries.en: Inside were only the python robes and swords the emperor had bestowed.
entries.literal: Opening to look, they were the imperial gifts of python robes and sword implements.

entries.zh: 死之日，陰霾四合，天下冤之。
entries.en: On the day he died dark clouds closed in from every side; the realm mourned a great injustice.
entries.literal: On the day of his death, dark clouds gathered from four sides; all under Heaven considered it wrongful.

entries.zh: 指揮朵兒者，本出曹吉祥部下，以酒酹謙死所，慟哭。
entries.en: Commander Duo'er, once under Cao Jixiang, poured wine at the place of Qian's death and wept.
entries.literal: Commander Duo'er, originally from Cao Jixiang's subordinates, poured wine at Qian's place of death and wept bitterly.

entries.zh: 吉祥怒，抶之。
entries.en: Jixiang had him beaten.
entries.literal: Jixiang was angry and flogged him.

entries.zh: 明日復酹奠如故。
entries.en: The next day he returned and poured wine again.
entries.literal: The next day he again poured libation as before.

entries.zh: 都督同知陳逵感謙忠義，收遺骸殯之。
entries.en: Chen Kui, vice military commissioner, moved by Qian's loyalty, gathered his remains and gave them burial.
entries.literal: Vice Military Commissioner Chen Kui, moved by Qian's loyalty and righteousness, collected the remains and encoffined them.

entries.zh: 踰年，歸葬杭州。
entries.en: A year later his body was brought home to Hangzhou for burial.
entries.literal: After more than a year, they were returned for burial in Hangzhou.

entries.zh: 逵，六合人。
entries.en: Chen Kui came from Liuhe.
entries.literal: Kui was a man of Liuhe.

entries.zh: 故舉將才，出李時勉門下者也。
entries.en: He had been recommended as a military talent and had studied under Li Shimian.
entries.literal: He was formerly recommended for general talent and came from Li Shimian's school.

entries.zh: 皇太后初不知謙死，比聞，嗟悼累日。
entries.en: The empress dowager had not known of Qian's death; when she learned of it she mourned for days.
entries.literal: The empress dowager at first did not know of Qian's death; when she heard, she sighed in grief for many days.

entries.zh: 英宗亦悔之。
entries.en: The Ying Emperor, too, came to regret it.
entries.literal: The Ying Emperor also regretted it.

entries.zh: 景泰八年正月壬午，亨與吉祥、有貞等既迎上皇復位，宣諭朝臣畢，即執謙與大學士王文下獄。
entries.en: On renwu day in the first month of Jingtai 8, after Heng, Jixiang, and Youzhen had restored the former emperor and addressed the court, they seized Qian and Grand Secretary Wang Wen and threw them into prison.
entries.literal: On renwu day in the first month of the eighth year of Jingtai, after Heng, Jixiang, Youzhen, and others had welcomed the former emperor's restoration, when the announcement to court ministers was finished they immediately seized Qian and Grand Secretary Wang Wen and sent them to prison.

entries.zh: 誣謙等與黃竑構邪議，更立東宮；
entries.en: They accused Qian and others of plotting with Huang Qiong to install a new heir;
entries.literal: They falsely charged Qian and others with Huang Qiong in plotting heterodox opinions to change and establish the Eastern Palace;

entries.zh: 又與太監王誠、舒良、張永、王勤等謀迎立襄王子。
entries.en: and of conspiring with eunuchs Wang Cheng, Shu Liang, Zhang Yong, and Wang Qin to enthrone the Prince of Xiang's son.
entries.literal: and further with eunuchs Wang Cheng, Shu Liang, Zhang Yong, Wang Qin, and others in plotting to welcome and establish the Prince of Xiang's son.

entries.zh: 亨等主其議，嗾言官上之。
entries.en: Heng and his faction drove the case and incited censors to submit the charges.
entries.literal: Heng and others directed this accusation and incited remonstrating officials to submit it.

entries.zh: 都御史蕭惟禎定讞。
entries.en: Censor-in-chief Xiao Weizhen pronounced sentence.
entries.literal: Censor-in-chief Xiao Weizhen fixed the verdict.

entries.zh: 坐以謀逆，處極刑。
entries.en: They were convicted of treason and sentenced to death.
entries.literal: Convicted of plotting rebellion, they received the extreme penalty.

entries.zh: 文不勝誣，辯之疾，謙笑曰：「亨等意耳，辯何益？」
entries.en: Wen could not bear the false charges and argued fiercely; Qian smiled and said, "This is Heng's doing—what good is argument?"
entries.literal: Wen could not bear the false charge and argued urgently; Qian smiled and said: "It is Heng and others' intent—what use is argument?"

entries.zh: 奏上，英宗尚猶豫曰：「于謙實有功。」
entries.en: When the memorial reached him, the Ying Emperor still hesitated: "Yu Qian truly served the realm well."
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Ying Emperor still hesitated, saying: "Yu Qian truly had merit."

entries.zh: 有貞進曰：「不殺于謙，此舉為無名。」
entries.en: Youzhen said, "If you do not kill Yu Qian, this restoration has no justification."
entries.literal: Youzhen advanced and said: "If Yu Qian is not killed, this undertaking has no name."

entries.zh: 帝意遂決。
entries.en: The emperor's mind was made up.
entries.literal: The emperor's intent was then settled.

entries.zh: 丙戌改元天順，丁亥棄謙市，籍其家，家戍邊。
entries.en: On bingxu the reign was renamed Tianshun; on dinghai Qian was executed in the marketplace, his property confiscated, and his family sent to frontier exile.
entries.literal: On bingxu the reign title was changed to Tianshun; on dinghai Qian was executed in the marketplace, his household registered and confiscated, and his family exiled to the frontier.

entries.zh: 遂溪教諭吾豫言謙罪當族，謙所薦舉諸文武大臣並應誅。
entries.en: Wu Yu, instructor at Suixi, said Qian's crime warranted extermination of his clan and that every civil and military official Qian had promoted should die as well.
entries.literal: Suixi Instructor Wu Yu said Qian's crime deserved clan extermination and all civil and military grand ministers Qian had recommended should also be executed.

entries.zh: 部議持之而止。
entries.en: The ministries debated the proposal and blocked it.
entries.literal: Ministry deliberation resisted the proposal and stopped it.

entries.zh: 千戶白琦又請榜其罪，鏤板示天下，一時希旨取寵者，率以謙為口實。
entries.en: Company commander Bai Qi asked that Qian's crimes be posted and carved on boards for all to see; for a time every sycophant found in Qian a convenient target.
entries.literal: Company Commander Bai Qi again requested posting his crimes, carving them on boards to show all under Heaven; for a time those currying favor by pleasing intent mostly took Qian as a pretext.

entries.zh: 謙既死，而亨党陳汝言代為兵部尚書。
entries.en: After Qian's death, Heng's follower Chen Ruyan became Minister of War.
entries.literal: After Qian died, Heng's partisan Chen Ruyan replaced him as Minister of War.

entries.zh: 未一年敗，贓累巨萬。
entries.en: Within a year he was exposed; his embezzlements ran to tens of thousands.
entries.literal: In less than a year he was ruined; embezzled goods accumulated to tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 帝召大臣入視，愀然曰：「于謙被遇景泰朝，死無餘資。
entries.en: The emperor summoned ministers to inspect the hoard and said bleakly, "Yu Qian served the Jingtai court honorably and died without a penny to his name.
entries.literal: The emperor summoned grand ministers to view them and said mournfully: "Yu Qian was favored in the Jingtai court and died without surplus funds.

entries.zh: 汝言抑何多也！」
entries.en: And you, Ruyan—how much you have amassed!"
entries.literal: Ruyan—how much you have!"

entries.zh: 亨俯首不能對。
entries.en: Heng bowed his head in silence.
entries.literal: Heng bowed his head and could not answer.

entries.zh: 俄有邊警，帝憂形於色。
entries.en: Soon a frontier alarm came, and worry showed on the emperor's face.
entries.literal: Soon there was a frontier alarm and worry showed on the emperor's face.

entries.zh: 恭順侯吳瑾侍，進曰：「使于謙在，當不令寇至此。」
entries.en: Marquis Wu Jin, attending him, said, "Had Yu Qian lived, the enemy would never have come this far."
entries.literal: Marquis of Gongshun Wu Jin attended and advanced, saying: "If Yu Qian were here, he would not have let the invaders reach this point."

entries.zh: 帝為默然。
entries.en: The emperor said nothing.
entries.literal: The emperor was silent.

entries.zh: 是年，有貞為亨所中，戍金齒。
entries.en: That year Youzhen was brought down by Heng and exiled to Jinchi.
entries.literal: That year Youzhen was struck by Heng and was exiled to garrison at Jinchi.

entries.zh: 又數年，亨亦下獄死，吉祥謀反族誅，謙事白。
entries.en: A few years later Heng died in prison; Jixiang rebelled and his clan was exterminated; Qian's case was cleared.
entries.literal: Several years later Heng also entered prison and died; Jixiang plotted rebellion and his clan was executed; Qian's case was cleared.

entries.zh: 吳寧，字永清，歙人。
entries.en: Wu Ning, styled Yongqing, came from She county.
entries.literal: Wu Ning, styled Yongqing, was a man of She.

entries.zh: 宣德五年進士，除兵部主事。
entries.en: He passed the jinshi in Xuande 5 and was made a director in the Ministry of War.
entries.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Xuande, appointed Director in the Ministry of War.

entries.zh: 正統中，再遷職方郎中。
entries.en: Under Zhengtong he rose twice to director in the Bureau of Operations.
entries.literal: In Zhengtong he was twice transferred to Bureau Director in the Bureau of Operations.

entries.zh: 郕王監國，謙薦擢本部右侍郎。
entries.en: When the Prince of Cheng took charge of the realm, Qian recommended him as Right Vice Minister of War.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Cheng supervised the state, Qian recommended him for promotion to Right Vice Minister of the ministry.

entries.zh: 謙禦寇城外，寧掌部事，命赴軍中議方略。
entries.en: While Qian fought outside the walls, Ning ran the ministry and was sent to the army to plan strategy.
entries.literal: Qian resisted invaders outside the walls; Ning managed ministry affairs and was ordered to go to the army to deliberate strategy.

entries.zh: 比還，城門弗啟，寇騎充斥，寧立雨中指揮兵士，移時乃入。
entries.en: On his return the gates were still shut and enemy horsemen filled the streets; Ning stood in the rain directing troops for a long while before he could enter.
entries.literal: When he returned, the gates were not opened and enemy horsemen filled the area; Ning stood in the rain directing soldiers, and only after some time entered.

entries.zh: 寇既退，畿民猶日數驚，相率南徙。
entries.en: Even after the enemy withdrew, people around the capital panicked daily and fled south in bands.
entries.literal: After the invaders retreated, capital-region commoners still were alarmed several times daily and led one another south in migration.

entries.zh: 或議仍召勤王兵。
entries.en: Some proposed summoning relief armies again.
entries.literal: Some deliberated again summoning relief armies.

entries.zh: 寧曰：「是益之使驚也，莫若告捷四方，人心自定。」
entries.en: Ning said, "That would only spread panic. Better to announce victory to the four quarters—then minds will steady themselves."
entries.literal: Ning said: "This would increase and make them alarmed; better to announce victory to the four quarters—hearts will settle themselves."

entries.zh: 因具奏行之。
entries.en: He memorialized accordingly and the court acted on it.
entries.literal: He then fully memorialized and it was carried out.

entries.zh: 景泰改元，以疾乞歸，後不復出。
entries.en: When the reign was renamed Jingtai he retired on grounds of illness and never served again.
entries.literal: When Jingtai changed the reign title, he begged return on account of illness and afterward did not emerge again.

entries.zh: 家居三十餘年卒。
entries.en: He lived at home more than thirty years and died.
entries.literal: He dwelt at home more than thirty years and died.

entries.zh: 贊曰：于謙為巡撫時，聲績表著，卓然負經世之才。
entries.en: The encomium reads: As grand coordinator Yu Qian's reputation and achievements were outstanding; he clearly possessed the talent to govern an age.
entries.literal: The encomium says: When Yu Qian was grand coordinator, his reputation and achievements were outstanding, and he outstandingly bore talent for ordering the age.

entries.zh: 及時遘艱虞，繕兵固圉。
entries.en: When crisis struck, he repaired the armies and secured the realm.
entries.literal: When the time encountered hardship and peril, he repaired arms and secured the frontier.

entries.zh: 景帝既推心置腹，謙亦憂國忘家，身系安危，志存宗社，厥功偉矣。
entries.en: The Jing Emperor trusted him utterly; Qian in turn forgot home for the state, tied his life to the realm's safety, and held the altars in his heart—his achievement was immense.
entries.literal: The Jing Emperor had already opened his heart and placed his belly in trust; Qian also worried for the state and forgot his household, his person tied to security and peril, his will set on the ancestral altars and state—his achievement was great.

entries.zh: 變起奪門，禍機猝發，徐、石之徒出力而擠之死，當時莫不稱冤。
entries.en: When the coup at the palace gate struck, disaster erupted in an instant; Xu, Shi, and their faction forced him to his death, and all who lived then called it injustice.
entries.literal: Crisis arose from seizing the gate; disaster's mechanism burst forth suddenly; Xu, Shi, and their kind exerted force and squeezed him to death—all at the time called it wrongful.

entries.zh: 然有貞與亨、吉祥相繼得禍，皆不旋踵。
entries.en: Yet Youzhen, Heng, and Jixiang each met ruin in turn, almost before they could turn around.
entries.literal: Yet Youzhen, Heng, and Jixiang in succession met calamity, all without turning the heel.

entries.zh: 而謙忠心義烈，與日月爭光，卒得復官賜恤。
entries.en: Qian's loyal heart and righteous fervor shine with the sun and moon; in the end his rank was restored and imperial consolation granted.
entries.literal: While Qian's loyal heart and righteous fervor vied in brilliance with sun and moon, and in the end he obtained restoration of office and bestowed consolation.

entries.zh: 公論久而後定，信夫。
entries.en: Public judgment takes time to settle—how true that is.
entries.literal: Public opinion after long time then was settled—truly so.

entries.zh: 偉喜任智數。
entries.en: Wei delighted in stratagem and cunning.
entries.literal: Wei delighted in employing stratagems and calculation.

entries.zh: 既為謙所引，恐嫉謙者目己為朋附，嘗密奏謙誤，冀自解。
entries.en: Having risen through Qian's patronage, he feared Qian's enemies would see him as a partisan; he once secretly reported Qian's faults, hoping to clear himself.
entries.literal: Having been brought in by Qian, he feared those who envied Qian would view him as a partisan and once secretly memorialized Qian's errors, hoping to extricate himself.

entries.zh: 帝以其奏授謙，謙叩頭謝。
entries.en: The emperor handed the memorial to Qian; Qian kowtowed in thanks.
entries.literal: The emperor gave his memorial to Qian; Qian knocked his head and thanked.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「吾自知卿，何謝為？」
entries.en: The emperor said, "I know you well—why thank me?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I myself know you—why thank?"

entries.zh: 謙出，偉問：「上與公何言？」
entries.en: Qian left; Wei asked, "What did His Majesty say to you?"
entries.literal: Qian exited; Wei asked: "What did His Majesty and Your Excellency say?"

entries.zh: 謙笑曰：「我有失，望君面規我，何至爾邪？」
entries.en: Qian smiled: "If I err, tell me to my face—why go behind my back?"
entries.literal: Qian smiled and said: "If I have faults, I hope you will face me and regulate me—how did it come to this?"

entries.zh: 出奏示之，偉大慚沮。
entries.en: He showed Wei the memorial; Wei was deeply ashamed.
entries.literal: He produced the memorial and showed it; Wei was greatly ashamed and dejected.

entries.zh: 然竟坐謙黨，罷歸。
entries.en: Yet when Qian fell he was dismissed as a partisan.
entries.literal: Yet in the end he was convicted as Qian's partisan and dismissed to return.

entries.zh: 成化三年復官，請毀白琦所鏤板。
entries.en: In Chenghua 3 he was restored to office and asked that Bai Qi's carved libel boards be destroyed.
entries.literal: In the third year of Chenghua his office was restored; he requested destroying the carved boards Bai Qi had made.

entries.zh: 踰年，告病歸卒。
entries.en: A year later he retired on grounds of illness and died at home.
entries.literal: After more than a year he reported illness, returned, and died.

entries.zh: 于謙子:冕 附:吳寧 王偉
entries.en: Yu Qian's son Mian; appended biographies: Wu Ning and Wang Wei
entries.literal: Yu Qian's son: Mian; appended: Wu Ning, Wang Wei

entries.zh: 昭居寧夏十二年，老成持重，兵政修舉，亦會敵勢衰弱，邊境得無事。
entries.en: Zhao held Ningxia for twelve years, steady and deliberate; military affairs were kept in good order, and as enemy strength waned the border remained quiet.
entries.literal: Zhao resided at Ningxia for twelve years, steady and deliberate in bearing; military administration was well maintained, and it happened also that the enemy's strength waned, so the border knew no disturbance.

entries.zh: 兵部尚書王驥、寧夏參將王榮嘗舉其過。
entries.en: Minister of War Wang Ji and Ningxia assistant commander Wang Rong once reported his faults.
entries.literal: Minister of War Wang Ji and Ningxia Assistant Commander Wang Rong once reported his faults.

entries.zh: 朝議，以昭守邊久，習兵事，不易也。
entries.en: At court it was held that Zhao had long guarded the frontier and knew military affairs too well to be replaced lightly.
entries.literal: At court it was argued that Zhao had long guarded the frontier and was versed in military affairs—he should not be replaced lightly.

entries.zh: 而與昭並為邊將最久、有勛績可稱者，都督同知劉昭鎮西寧二十年；
entries.en: Among frontier generals who, like Zhao, had served longest with merit worth noting were Assistant Commissioner Liu Zhao, who garrisoned Xining for twenty years,
entries.literal: Those who, like Zhao, had served longest as frontier generals with merit worth noting included Assistant Commissioner Liu Zhao, who garrisoned Xining for twenty years;

entries.zh: 都指揮李達鎮洮州至四十年。
entries.en: and Regional Commander Li Da, who held Taozhou for as long as forty years.
entries.literal: and Regional Commander Li Da, who garrisoned Taozhou for as long as forty years.

entries.zh: 並為蕃漢所畏服。
entries.en: Both were feared and obeyed by Tibetans and Chinese alike.
entries.literal: Both were feared and respected by Tibetans and Chinese alike.

entries.en: An Guo and Hang Xiong
