entries.zh: 八年，宣府送迤北降人脫脫太等至京，命充禦馬監勇士。
entries.en: That year Xuanfu presented the surrendered northerner Tuotuotai and his party at court, and the Emperor enrolled them as warriors of the Imperial Stud Office.
entries.literal: In the eighth year Xuanfu sent the surrendered northerner Tuotuotai and others to the capital; the Emperor ordered them enrolled as warriors of the Imperial Stud Office.

entries.zh: 鑒等上言：「漢、魏徙氐、羌於關中，郭欽、江統皆勸晉武早絕亂階。
entries.en: Jian and others memorialized: "Under Han and Wei the Di and Qiang were moved into Guanzhong; Guo Qin and Jiang Tong both urged Emperor Wu of Jin to cut off the source of disorder early.
entries.literal: Jian and others memorialized: "In Han and Wei the Di and Qiang were moved into the Guanzhong region; Guo Qin and Jiang Tong both urged Emperor Wu of Jin to cut off the source of disorder early.

entries.zh: 苻堅處鮮卑於漢南，苻融亦慮其窺測虛實。
entries.en: Fu Jian settled the Xianbei south of the Han, and Fu Rong too feared they would spy out weaknesses.
entries.literal: Fu Jian settled the Xianbei south of the Han, and Fu Rong also feared they would spy out weaknesses.

entries.zh: 今使降人出入禁中，假寵逾分，且生慢侮。
entries.en: To let surrendered men now enter and leave the forbidden precinct and grant them favor beyond their station will only breed contempt.
entries.literal: Now to let surrendered men enter and leave the forbidden precinct and grant them favor beyond their station will moreover breed contempt.

entries.zh: 萬一北寇聞之，潛使黠賊偽降，以為間諜，寧不為將來患哉？」
entries.en: Should northern enemies hear of this and secretly send cunning bandits to feign surrender as spies, would this not become a calamity in future?"
entries.literal: Should northern enemies hear of this and secretly send cunning bandits to feign surrender as spies, would this not become a future calamity?"

entries.zh: 帝不聽。
entries.en: The Emperor refused to listen.
entries.literal: The Emperor would not listen.

entries.zh: 嘉靖改元，用薦起故官，總督漕運。
entries.en: When Jiajing began he was recommended back to superintend grain transport.
entries.literal: At the change to Jiajing, on recommendation he was recalled to his former office to superintend grain transport.

entries.zh: 青州礦盜王堂等起顏神鎮，流劫東昌、兗州、濟南。
entries.en: Qingzhou mine rebels Wang Tang and others rose at Yanshen and raided Dongchang, Yanzhou, and Jinan.
entries.literal: Qingzhou mining bandits Wang Tang and others rose at Yanshen town and raided through Dongchang, Yanzhou, and Jinan.

entries.zh: 都指揮楊紀及指揮楊浩等擊之，浩死，紀僅免。
entries.en: Commander Yang Ji and Commander Yang Hao attacked; Hao was killed and Ji barely escaped.
entries.literal: Commander Yang Ji and Commander Yang Hao and others attacked them; Hao died and Ji barely escaped.

entries.zh: 詔責山東將吏，於是諸臣分道逐賊，賊不復屯聚，流劫金鄉、魚臺間。
entries.en: The throne rebuked Shandong commanders; ministers pursued on separate routes; the rebels stopped camping together and raided between Jinxiang and Yutai.
entries.literal: An edict rebuked Shandong officers; then the various ministers pursued the bandits on separate routes; the bandits no longer camped together but raided between Jinxiang and Yutai.

entries.zh: 突曹州，欲渡河不得，復掠考城並河西岸，至東明、長垣。
entries.en: They struck Caozhou, failed to cross the river, swept the west bank through Kaocheng, and reached Dongming and Changyuan.
entries.literal: They burst into Caozhou, could not cross the river, again raided the west bank of the examination route through Kaocheng, and reached Dongming and Changyuan.

entries.zh: 河南及保定守臣鹹告急。
entries.en: Henan and Baoding officials all cried for help.
entries.literal: Henan and Baoding defending officials all reported emergency.

entries.zh: 賊黨王友賢等轉掠祥符、封丘，南抵徐州。
entries.en: The rebel Wang Youxian and others raided Xiangfu and Fengqiu and pushed south to Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Bandit follower Wang Youxian and others turned to raid Xiangfu and Fengqiu, reaching south to Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 廷議以諸道巡撫權位相埒，乃命諫與都督魯綱並提督兩畿、山東、河南軍務，以便宜節制諸道兵討之。
entries.en: Because grand coordinators held equal rank, the court ordered Jian and Regional Commander Lu Gang jointly to direct the two capital regions, Shandong, and Henan, with full power to command all routes against the rebels.
entries.literal: Court debate held that the various grand coordinators' ranks were equal; Jian and Regional Commander Lu Gang were therefore ordered jointly to superintend military affairs in the two capital regions, Shandong, and Henan, with discretionary authority to command the various routes' troops in suppression.

entries.zh: 賊復流至考城。
entries.en: The rebels swept back toward Kaocheng.
entries.literal: The bandits again flowed to Kaocheng.

entries.zh: 官軍方欲擊，而河南降賊張進引三百騎馳至。
entries.en: As government forces prepared to attack, the Henan turncoat Zhang Jin arrived at a gallop with three hundred horsemen.
entries.literal: Government troops were about to strike when the Henan surrendered bandit Zhang Jin led three hundred horsemen galloping up.

entries.zh: 中都留守顏愷與俱前，方戰，進忽三麾其旗先卻。
entries.en: Central Capital commander Yan Kai marched with him; in the midst of battle Jin suddenly waved his standard three times and pulled back.
entries.literal: Central Capital garrison commander Yan Kai advanced with him; just as battle joined, Jin suddenly thrice waved his banner and withdrew first.

entries.zh: 賊乘之，官軍大潰，將士死者八百余人。
entries.en: The rebels pressed the advantage; government troops collapsed, and more than eight hundred officers and men were killed.
entries.literal: The bandits seized the moment; government troops were utterly routed and more than eight hundred officers and soldiers died.

entries.zh: 諫等連營進，賊始滅。
entries.en: Jian pressed forward in linked camps until the rebels were finally destroyed.
entries.literal: Jian and others advanced in linked camps, and only then were the bandits extinguished.

entries.zh: 其秋，召掌都察院事。
entries.en: That fall he was recalled to head the Censorate.
entries.literal: That autumn he was summoned to direct the Censorate.

entries.zh: 逾年卒官，贈太子太保，謚莊襄。
entries.en: A year later he died in post and was posthumously named Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the title Zhuangxiang.
entries.literal: The next year he died in office; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the title Zhuangxiang.

entries.zh: 何鑒馬中錫陸完洪鐘
entries.en: He Jian, Ma Zhongxi, Lu Wan, and Hong Zhong
entries.literal: He Jian, Ma Zhongxi, Lu Wan, Hong Zhong

entries.literal: (Sun Lu.)〉

entries.en: Ma Hao.
entries.literal: Ma Hao

entries.zh: 四十年，遷至戶部右侍郎。
entries.en: In the fortieth year he rose to vice minister of revenue on the right.
entries.literal: In the fortieth year he rose to vice minister of revenue on the right.

entries.zh: 廷議遣大臣赴薊州督餉練兵，嵩欲用貞吉，召飲示之意。
entries.en: The court debated sending a high minister to Jizhou to supervise grain transport and drill troops; Song wished to use Zhenji and summoned him to drink and show his intent.
entries.literal: The court debated sending a high minister to Jizhou to supervise grain transport and drill troops; Song wished to use Zhenji and summoned him to drink and show his intent.

entries.zh: 貞吉曰：「督餉者，督京運乎，民運乎？
entries.en: Zhenji said, "Does supervising grain mean capital transport or civilian transport?
entries.literal: Zhenji said: "Does supervising grain mean supervising capital transport, or civilian transport?

entries.zh: 若二運已有職掌，添官徒增擾耳。
entries.en: If both already have responsible offices, adding officials only increases disturbance.
entries.literal: If both already have responsible offices, adding officials only increases disturbance.

entries.zh: 況兵之不練，其過宜不在是，即十戶侍出，何益練兵？」
entries.en: Moreover, if troops are not drilled, the fault should not lie here. Even ten household stewards sent out would not help drill troops."
entries.literal: Moreover, if troops are not drilled, the fault should not lie here. Even ten household stewards sent out would not help drill troops."

entries.zh: 嵩怫然罷。
entries.en: Song left displeased.
entries.literal: Song left displeased.

entries.zh: 會嵩請告，吏部用倉場侍郎林應亮。
entries.en: When Song requested leave the Ministry of Personnel appointed the granary vice minister Lin Yingliang.
entries.literal: When Song requested leave the Ministry of Personnel appointed the granary vice minister Lin Yingliang.

entries.zh: 比嵩出，益怒。
entries.en: When Song came out he was still more angry.
entries.literal: When Song came out he was still more angry.

entries.zh: 令都給事中張益劾應亮，調之南京，而改用僉都御史霍冀。
entries.en: He had the supervising secretary Zhang Yi impeach Yingliang and transfer him to Nanjing, and instead used the vice censor-in-chief Huo Ji.
entries.literal: He had the supervising secretary Zhang Yi impeach Yingliang and transfer him to Nanjing, and instead used the vice censor-in-chief Huo Ji.

entries.zh: 益又言：「督餉戶部專職，今貞吉與左侍郎劉大賓廷推不及，是不職也，宜罷。」
entries.en: Yi also said: "Supervising grain is the special duty of the Ministry of Revenue. Now Zhenji and left vice minister Liu Dabin were not reached in court recommendation; this is dereliction and they ought to be dismissed."
entries.literal: Yi also said: "Supervising grain is the special duty of the Ministry of Revenue. Now Zhenji and left vice minister Liu Dabin were not reached in court recommendation; this is dereliction and they ought to be dismissed."

entries.zh: 於是二人皆奪官。
entries.en: Thereupon both men were stripped of office.
entries.literal: Thereupon both men were stripped of office.

entries.zh: 費宏
entries.en: Fei Hong
entries.literal: Fei Hong

entries.en: Gao Yi
entries.literal: Gao Yi

entries.zh: 未幾，河套議起。
entries.en: Before long, the debate over recovering the Ordos arose.
entries.literal: Before long, the debate over the Ordos arose.

entries.zh: 言故慷慨以經濟自許，思建立不世功。
entries.en: Xia Yan had always been ambitious and held himself out as a statesman, intending to win undying distinction.
entries.literal: Yan had always been bold and generous, promising himself in statecraft, thinking to establish unprecedented merit.

entries.zh: 因陜西總督曾銑請復河套，贊決之。
entries.en: When Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian of Shaanxi memorialized for recovering the Ordos, Xia Yan endorsed the proposal.
entries.literal: Because Shaanxi Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian requested recovery of the Ordos, he approved and decided it.

entries.zh: 嵩與元、炳媒孽其間，竟以此敗。
entries.en: Yan Song, together with Cui Yuan and Lu Bing, sowed trouble in the midst of it, and in the end Xia Yan was ruined because of it.
entries.literal: Song with Yuan and Bing planted mischief between them; in the end Yan failed because of this.

entries.zh: 江都人蘇綱者，言繼妻父也，雅與銑善。
entries.en: A man named Su Gang, from Jiangdu, was the father of Xia Yan's second wife and had long been on friendly terms with Zeng Xian.
entries.literal: One Su Gang of Jiangdu was Yan's father-in-law by a subsequent wife; he had always been on good terms with Xian.

entries.zh: 銑方請復河套，綱亟稱於言。
entries.en: While Zeng Xian was pressing his plan to recover the Ordos, Su Gang repeatedly spoke well of him to Xia Yan.
entries.literal: When Xian was just requesting recovery of the Ordos, Gang repeatedly praised him to Yan.

entries.zh: 言倚銑可辦，密疏薦之，謂群臣無如銑忠者。
entries.en: Xia Yan counted on Zeng Xian to see the campaign through and secretly memorialized in his favor, declaring that no minister was more loyal.
entries.literal: Yan relied on Xian to be able to accomplish it; secretly memorialized recommending him, saying among the officials none was as loyal as Xian.

entries.zh: 帝令言擬旨，優獎之者再。
entries.en: The Emperor had Xia Yan draft the rescripts and twice issued him warm commendation.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Yan to draft rescripts; he commended him with favor twice.

entries.zh: 銑喜，益銳意出師。
entries.en: Zeng Xian was elated and pressed all the harder to take the field.
entries.literal: Xian rejoiced and became even more determined to take the field.

entries.zh: 帝忽降旨詰責，語甚厲。
entries.en: The Emperor suddenly issued an edict of stern rebuke in the harshest terms.
entries.literal: The Emperor suddenly issued an edict of interrogation and rebuke; the language was very severe.

entries.zh: 嵩揣知帝意，遂力言河套不可復，語侵言。
entries.en: Yan Song read the Emperor's mind and forcefully argued that the Ordos could not be recovered, his words aimed openly at Xia Yan.
entries.literal: Song guessed the Emperor's intent and then forcefully argued the Ordos could not be recovered; his words encroached on Yan.

entries.zh: 言始大懼，謝罪，且言「嵩未嘗異議，今乃盡諉於臣」。
entries.en: Xia Yan was at last deeply alarmed. He apologized and added, "Yan Song never once objected—yet now he lays the entire blame on me."
entries.literal: Yan at first was greatly afraid; he apologized and moreover said, "Song never once differed in opinion; now he throws everything on me."

entries.zh: 帝責言「強君脅眾」，嵩復騰疏攻言，言亦力辨。
entries.en: The Emperor rebuked Xia Yan for "forcing the ruler's hand and browbeating the court." Yan Song followed with another memorial attacking him, and Xia Yan rebutted with equal force.
entries.literal: The Emperor rebuked Yan for "forcing the ruler and coercing the multitude"; Song again sent up a memorial attacking Yan, and Yan also vigorously defended himself.

entries.zh: 而帝已入嵩譖，怒不可解。
entries.en: But the Emperor had already taken Yan Song's accusations to heart, and his rage could not be softened.
entries.literal: But the Emperor had already accepted Song's slander; his anger could not be appeased.

entries.zh: 二十七年正月盡奪言官階，以尚書致仕，猶無意殺之也。
entries.en: In the first month of the twenty-seventh year of the reign, Xia Yan was stripped of all office and permitted to retire as Minister—yet the Emperor still had no wish to kill him.
entries.literal: In the first month of year twenty-seven all of Yan's official ranks were stripped; he retired as Minister—but still there was no intent to kill him.

entries.zh: 會有蜚語聞禁中，謂言去時怨謗。
entries.en: Rumors then reached the inner palace that Xia Yan, on leaving office, had spoken with resentment and slander.
entries.literal: There happened to be flying rumors heard within the forbidden precincts, saying Yan when leaving spoke with resentment and slander.

entries.zh: 嵩復代仇鸞草奏訐言納銑金，交關為奸利，事連蘇綱，遂下銑、綱詔獄。
entries.en: Yan Song then had Qiu Luan draft a memorial accusing Xia Yan of taking bribes from Zeng Xian and trading favors for profit. The case implicated Su Gang, and Zeng Xian and Su Gang were clapped into the imperial prison.
entries.literal: Song again had Qiu Luan draft a memorial denouncing Yan for receiving Xian's gold and colluding for corrupt profit; the matter implicated Su Gang; thus Xian and Gang were sent to the imperial prison by edict.

entries.zh: 嵩與元、炳謀，坐銑交結近侍律斬，綱戍邊，遣官校逮言。
entries.en: Yan Song plotted with Cui Yuan and Lu Bing. Zeng Xian was sentenced to decapitation under the statute on collusion with palace intimates; Su Gang was exiled to the frontier; and officers were sent to seize Xia Yan.
entries.literal: Song with Yuan and Bing plotted; Xian was sentenced under the law on collusion with close attendants to decapitation; Gang was exiled to the frontier; official runners were dispatched to arrest Yan.

entries.zh: 言抵通州，聞銑所坐，大驚墮車曰：「噫！
entries.en: When Xia Yan reached Tongzhou and learned what crime Zeng Xian had been charged with, he was so shaken that he fell from his carriage and cried, "Alas!
entries.literal: When Yan reached Tongzhou and heard what Xian was convicted of, he was greatly shocked, fell from his carriage, and said, "Alas!

entries.zh: 吾死矣。」
entries.en: I am a dead man."
entries.literal: I am dead.

entries.zh: 再疏訟冤，言：「鸞方就逮，上降諭不兩日，鸞何以知上語，又何知嵩疏而附麗若此？
entries.en: He memorialized again to clear his name: "Qiu Luan had only just been placed under arrest. The Emperor's edict is less than two days old—how could Luan already know the Emperor's words? How could he know of Yan Song's memorial and align himself with it in this way?
entries.literal: Again memorializing to plead his innocence, he said: "Luan had just been arrested; the Emperor's edict was less than two days ago—how could Luan know the Emperor's words? And how could he know Song's memorial and attach himself like this?

entries.zh: 蓋嵩與崔元輩詐為之以傾臣。
entries.en: Clearly Yan Song and men like Cui Yuan fabricated this to bring me down.
entries.literal: Surely Song with Cui Yuan and company fraudulently made this to overthrow me.

entries.zh: 嵩靜言庸違似共工，謙恭下士似王莽，奸巧弄權、父子專政似司馬懿。
entries.en: Yan Song's smooth words and treacherous deeds recall Gong Gong; his show of humility toward scholars recalls Wang Mang; his cunning grasp of power and the rule he and his son share recall Sima Yi.
entries.literal: Song's quiet speech and outward violation resemble Gong Gong; humble courtesy toward scholars resembles Wang Mang; cunning manipulation of power and father-son monopolizing government resemble Sima Yi.

entries.zh: 在內諸臣受其牢籠，知有嵩不知有陛下。
entries.en: The ministers within the palace are caught in his net—they know Yan Song, but not Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Officials within, subjected to his cage, know Song but do not know Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 在外諸臣受其箝制，亦知有嵩不知有陛下。
entries.en: The ministers beyond the palace are held under his thumb—they too know Yan Song, but not Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Officials without, subjected to his restraint, also know Song but do not know Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 臣生死系嵩掌握，惟歸命聖慈，曲賜保全。」
entries.en: My life and death rest in Yan Song's hands. I throw myself on Your Majesty's mercy and beg for gracious protection."
entries.literal: My life and death hang in Song's grasp; I only entrust myself to holy compassion, beseeching gracious preservation."

entries.zh: 帝不省。
entries.en: The Emperor paid no heed.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not heed.

entries.zh: 獄成，刑部尚書喻茂堅、左都御史屠僑等當言死，援議貴議能條以上。
entries.en: When the trial concluded, Minister of Justice Yu Maojian, Left Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao, and others recommended death for Xia Yan, citing the statutes granting leniency to men of rank and ability.
entries.literal: When the case was finalized, Minister of Justice Yu Maojian, Left Censor-in-Chief Tu Qiao and others sentenced Yan to death, citing the provisions on officials of merit and talent above.

entries.zh: 帝不從，切責茂堅等，奪其俸，猶及言前不戴香冠事。
entries.en: The Emperor refused. He sharply rebuked Yu Maojian and the others, docked their salaries, and even revived the old charge that Xia Yan had once failed to wear the incense crown.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not agree; he sharply rebuked Yu Maojian and the others and stripped their salaries, also bringing up Yan's earlier failure to wear the incense crown.

entries.zh: 其年十月竟棄言市。
entries.en: That October Xia Yan was at last executed in the public square.
entries.literal: That year in the tenth month Yan was finally executed at the market.

entries.zh: 妻蘇流廣西，從子主事克承、從孫尚寶丞朝慶，削籍為民。
entries.en: His wife, Lady Su, was banished to Guangxi. His nephew Ke Cheng, a department director, and his grand-nephew Chao Qing, an assistant in the Court of Imperial Studs, were struck from the rolls and reduced to common status.
entries.literal: His wife the Su was exiled to Guangxi; his nephew, Department Director Ke Cheng, and grand-nephew, Court of Imperial Studs Assistant Chao Qing, were struck from the registry and made commoners.

entries.zh: 言死時年六十有七。
entries.en: Xia Yan was sixty-seven when he died.
entries.literal: When Yan died he was sixty-seven years old.

entries.zh: 張璁
entries.en: Zhang Cong
entries.literal: Zhang Cong

entries.en: (also known as Hu Duo)〉
entries.literal: (Hu Duo)〉

entries.zh: 桂萼方獻夫夏言
entries.en: Gui E, Fang Xianfu, and Xia Yan
entries.literal: Gui E, Fang Xianfu, and Xia Yan

entries.zh: 五年出按山西，而妖賊李福達獄起。
entries.en: In his fifth year in office he was dispatched as touring censor to Shanxi, where the case of the heretic rebel Li Fuda broke out.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he went out as touring censor for Shanxi, and the case of the demonic rebel Li Fuda arose.

entries.zh: 福達者，崞人。
entries.en: Fuda was a native of Guo.
entries.literal: Fuda was a man of Guo.

entries.zh: 初坐妖賊王良、李鉞黨，戍山丹衛。
entries.en: He was first convicted as an accomplice of the heretics Wang Liang and Li Yue and sent to penal service at the Shandan Guard.
entries.literal: At first he was convicted as a follower of the demonic rebels Wang Liang and Li Yue and was banished to garrison service at the Shandan Guard.

entries.zh: 逃還，更名午，為清軍御史所勾，再戍山海衛。
entries.en: He escaped home, took the name Wu, was rounded up by a censor charged with clearing stragglers, and was banished again to the Shanhai Guard.
entries.literal: He fled back, changed his name to Wu, was seized by a Qing-army censor, and was banished again to the Shanhai Guard.

entries.zh: 復逃居洛川，以彌勒教誘愚民邵進祿等為亂。
entries.en: He fled once more and settled in Luochuan, where he used Maitreya sect teachings to stir up the commoner Shao Jinlu and others in revolt.
entries.literal: He fled again and lived in Luochuan, using the Maitreya teaching to entice the foolish commoner Shao Jinlu and others into rebellion.

entries.zh: 事覺，進祿伏誅，福達先還家，得免。
entries.en: When the plot was uncovered, Jinlu was put to death, but Fuda had already gone home and went unpunished.
entries.literal: When the affair was exposed, Jinlu was executed, but Fuda had already returned home and escaped punishment.

entries.zh: 更姓名曰張寅，往來徐溝間，輸粟得太原衛指揮使。
entries.en: He changed his name again to Zhang Yin, traveled between Xu and Gou, and bought his way into the post of commander of the Taiyuan Guard by delivering grain.
entries.literal: He changed his name again to Zhang Yin, traveled between Xu and Gou, and by delivering grain obtained the post of commander of the Taiyuan Guard.

entries.zh: 子大仁、大義、大禮皆冒京師匠籍。
entries.en: His sons Daren, Dayi, and Dali all fraudulently enrolled on the capital artisan rolls.
entries.literal: His sons Daren, Dayi, and Dali all fraudulently enrolled in the capital artisan registers.

entries.zh: 用黃白術幹武定侯郭勛，勛大信幸。
entries.en: He approached the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, with alchemical arts, and Xun came to trust and favor him deeply.
entries.literal: By means of alchemy he approached the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun, who greatly trusted and favored him.

entries.zh: 其仇薛良訟於錄，按問得實。
entries.en: His enemy Xue Liang brought the case before Ma Lu, and investigation confirmed the facts.
entries.literal: His enemy Xue Liang brought suit before Lu; on investigation the facts were established.

entries.zh: 檄洛川父老雜辨之，益信。
entries.en: He summoned Luochuan elders to identify the man in a group inquiry, which only strengthened the case.
entries.literal: He summoned the elders of Luochuan to identify him in a mixed inquiry, and confidence increased.

entries.zh: 勛為遺書錄祈免，錄不從，偕巡撫江潮具獄以聞，且劾勛庇奸亂法。
entries.en: Xun wrote to Lu asking that he be spared; Lu refused, and together with Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Chao submitted the completed case to the throne while also impeaching Xun for shielding a criminal and corrupting justice.
entries.literal: Xun sent a letter asking Lu to plead for exemption; Lu refused, and together with the surveillance commissioner Jiang Chao prepared the full case for report, also impeaching Xun for shielding a villain and subverting the law.

entries.zh: 章下都察院，都御史聶賢等覆如錄奏，力言勛黨逆罪。
entries.en: The memorial went to the Censorate, where Censor-in-chief Nie Xian and others endorsed Lu's findings and insisted that Xun was party to treason.
entries.literal: The memorial went to the Censorate; the Censor-in-chief Nie Xian and others replied as Lu had reported, strongly stating Xun's complicity in treason.

entries.zh: 詔福達父子論死，妻女為奴，沒其產，責勛對狀。
entries.en: An edict sentenced Fuda and his sons to death, enslaved their wives and daughters, confiscated their property, and ordered Xun to answer the charges in person.
entries.literal: An edict sentenced Fuda and his sons to death, made wife and daughters slaves, confiscated their property, and ordered Xun to answer the charges in person.

entries.zh: 勛懼，乞恩，因為福達代辨，帝置不問。
entries.en: Xun grew afraid and begged for mercy, pleading Fuda's case himself; the Emperor let the matter drop.
entries.literal: Xun was afraid and begged grace, pleading on Fuda's behalf; the Emperor set the matter aside.

entries.zh: 會給事中王科、鄭一鵬、程輅、常泰、劉琦、鄭自璧、趙廷瑞、沈漢、秦祐、張逵、陳臯謨，御史程啟充、盧瓊、邵豳、高世魁、任淳，南京御史姚鳴鳳、潘壯、戚雄、王獻，評事杜鸞，刑部郎中劉仕，主事唐樞，交章劾勛，謂罪當連坐。
entries.en: At this point a stream of memorials arrived impeaching Xun: from supervising secretaries Wang Ke, Zheng Yipeng, Cheng Lu, Chang Tai, Liu Qi, Zheng Zibi, Zhao Tingrui, Shen Han, Qin You, Zhang Kui, and Chen Gaomo; from censors Cheng Qichong, Lu Qiong, Shao Bin, Gao Shikui, and Ren Chun; from Nanjing censors Yao Mingfeng, Pan Zhuang, Qi Xiong, and Wang Xian; from reviewing official Du Luan; from Ministry of Punishments bureau director Liu Shi; and from section chief Tang Shu—all arguing that Xun's crimes warranted joint punishment.
entries.literal: Thereupon the supervising secretaries Wang Ke, Zheng Yipeng, Cheng Lu, Chang Tai, Liu Qi, Zheng Zibi, Zhao Tingrui, Shen Han, Qin You, Zhang Kui, and Chen Gaomo; the censors Cheng Qichong, Lu Qiong, Shao Bin, Gao Shikui, and Ren Chun; the Nanjing censors Yao Mingfeng, Pan Zhuang, Qi Xiong, and Wang Xian; the reviewing official Du Luan; the Ministry of Punishments bureau director Liu Shi; and the section chief Tang Shu all submitted memorials impeaching Xun, saying his crime warranted joint punishment.

entries.zh: 勛亦累自訴，且以議禮觸眾怒為言，帝心動。
entries.en: Xun pleaded his own case again and again, claiming he had only provoked the court's wrath through the Rites Controversy; the Emperor began to waver.
entries.literal: Xun also repeatedly pleaded his own case, saying moreover that he had provoked popular anger through the Rites Controversy; the Emperor's mind was moved.

entries.zh: 勛復乞張璁、桂萼為援。
entries.en: Xun again appealed to Zhang Cong and Gui E for help.
entries.literal: Xun again begged Zhang Cong and Gui E for support.

entries.zh: 璁、萼素惡廷臣攻己，亦欲借是舒宿憤，乃謂諸臣內外交結，借端陷勛，將漸及諸議禮者。
entries.en: Cong and E had long resented the court officials who attacked them and saw a chance to settle old scores; they claimed the officials were conspiring inside and outside the court, using the case as a pretext to trap Xun and would soon turn on everyone who had supported the new rites.
entries.literal: Cong and E had long hated court officials for attacking them and also wished to vent old resentments through this affair; they therefore said the officials were conspiring inside and outside the court, seizing a pretext to trap Xun, and would gradually extend the attack to all who had favored the new rites.

entries.zh: 帝深入其言，而外廷不知，攻勛益急。
entries.en: The Emperor was deeply persuaded, but the outer court knew nothing of this and pressed its attack on Xun ever harder.
entries.literal: The Emperor was deeply swayed by their words, but the outer court did not know this and pressed its attack on Xun ever harder.

entries.zh: 帝益疑，命取福達等至京下三法司訊，既又命會文武大臣更訊之，皆無異詞。
entries.en: Growing more suspicious, the Emperor ordered Fuda and the others brought to the capital for trial by the Three Judicial Offices, then ordered civil and military grandees to re-examine the case together; every account still matched.
entries.literal: The Emperor grew more suspicious and ordered Fuda and the others brought to the capital for interrogation by the Three Judicial Offices; he then ordered a joint re-examination by civil and military grandees, and in every case the testimony was unchanged.

entries.zh: 帝怒，將親訊，以楊一清之言而止，仍下廷鞫。
entries.en: The Emperor was furious and was about to interrogate them himself, but Yang Yiqing dissuaded him; the case was still sent down for court trial.
entries.literal: The Emperor was angry and was about to interrogate them in person, but stopped on Yang Yiqing's advice and still sent the case down for court trial.

entries.zh: 尚書顏頤壽等不敢自堅，改擬妖言律斬。
entries.en: Minister Yan Yishou and the others did not dare hold firm and revised the sentence to execution under the statute on demonic speech.
entries.literal: The ministers Yan Yishou and others did not dare stand firm and revised the sentence to execution under the demonic-speech statute.

entries.zh: 帝猶怒，命法司俱戴罪辦事，遣官往械錄、潮及前問官布政使李璋、按察使李玨、僉事章綸、都指揮馬豕等。
entries.en: Still furious, the Emperor ordered the judicial offices to continue their duties under suspended guilt, and sent officials to arrest Ma Lu, Jiang Chao, and the former investigators—Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Zhang, Surveillance Commissioner Li Jue, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Lun, and Regional Commander Ma Shi, among others.
entries.literal: The Emperor was still angry, ordered the judicial offices all to continue their duties while bearing guilt, and sent officials to arrest Lu, Chao, and the former investigating officials—the provincial administration commissioner Li Zhang, the surveillance commissioner Li Jue, the assistant surveillance commissioner Zhang Lun, and the regional commander Ma Shi, among others.

entries.zh: 時璋、玨已遷都御史，璋巡撫寧夏，玨巡撫甘肅，皆下獄廷訊。
entries.en: By then Zhang and Jue had already been promoted to censors-in-chief—Zhang as surveillance commissioner of Ningxia and Jue of Gansu—and both were thrown into prison for court interrogation.
entries.literal: At the time Zhang and Jue had already been promoted to censors-in-chief; Zhang was surveillance commissioner of Ningxia and Jue of Gansu, and both were imprisoned for court interrogation.

entries.zh: 乃反前獄，抵良誣告罪。
entries.en: The earlier verdict was overturned and Xue Liang was charged with false accusation instead.
entries.literal: The case was then reversed from the earlier verdict and Xue Liang was charged with false accusation.

entries.zh: 帝以罪不及錄，怒甚。
entries.en: Because the charges did not reach Ma Lu, the Emperor was furious.
entries.literal: Because the crime did not reach Lu, the Emperor was very angry.

entries.zh: 命璁、萼、方獻夫分署三法司事，盡下尚書頤壽，侍郎劉玉、王啟，左都御史賢，副都御史劉文莊，僉都御史張潤，大理卿湯沐，少卿徐文華、顧佖，寺丞汪淵獄，嚴刑推問遂搜錄篋，得大學士賈詠、都御史張仲賢、工部侍郎閔楷、御史張英及寺丞淵私書。
entries.en: He put Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu in charge of the Three Judicial Offices, imprisoned Minister Yan Yishou, Vice Ministers Liu Yu and Wang Qi, Left Censor-in-chief Nie Xian, Vice Censor-in-chief Liu Wenzhuang, Assistant Censor-in-chief Zhang Run, Court of Review President Tang Mu, Vice Presidents Xu Wenhua and Gu Yi, and Registrar Wang Yuan, and under severe torture pursued the inquiry; searching Ma Lu's papers they found private letters from Grand Secretary Jia Yong, Censor-in-chief Zhang Zhongxian, Works Vice Minister Min Kai, Censor Zhang Ying, and Registrar Yuan.
entries.literal: He ordered Zhang Cong, Gui E, and Fang Xianfu to divide supervision of the Three Judicial Offices, threw into prison the ministers Yan Yishou; the vice ministers Liu Yu and Wang Qi; the Left Censor-in-chief Xian; the Vice Censor-in-chief Liu Wenzhuang; the Assistant Censor-in-chief Zhang Run; the Court of Review president Tang Mu; the vice presidents Xu Wenhua and Gu Yi; and the Court registrar Wang Yuan, and under severe torture pursued the inquiry; they then searched Lu's box and obtained private letters from Grand Secretary Jia Yong, Censor-in-chief Zhang Zhongxian, Works Vice Minister Min Kai, Censor Zhang Ying, and Registrar Yuan.

entries.zh: 詠引罪致仕去，仲賢等亦下獄。
entries.en: Yong confessed guilt and retired; Zhongxian and the others were imprisoned as well.
entries.literal: Yong pleaded guilty and retired; Zhongxian and the others were also imprisoned.

entries.zh: 萼等上言：「給事中琦、泰，郎中仕，聲勢相倚，挾私彈事，佐錄殺人。
entries.en: Gui E and the others memorialized: "Supervising Secretaries Liu Qi and Chang Tai and Bureau Director Liu Shi rely on each other's influence, lodge partisan impeachments, and helped Ma Lu secure a man's death.
entries.literal: E and the others memorialized: "The supervising secretaries Qi and Tai, and the bureau director Shi, rely on each other's power, bring private charges in memorials, and helped Lu kill a man.

entries.zh: 給事中科、一鵬、祐、漢、輅，評事鸞，御史鳴鳳、壯、雄，扶同妄奏，助成奸惡。
entries.en: Supervising Secretaries Wang Ke, Zheng Yipeng, Qin You, Shen Han, and Cheng Lu; Reviewing Official Du Luan; and Censors Yao Mingfeng, Pan Zhuang, and Qi Xiong joined in reckless memorials and helped the crime along.
entries.literal: The supervising secretaries Ke, Yipeng, You, Han, and Lu; the reviewing official Luan; and the censors Mingfeng, Zhuang, and Xiong joined in false memorials and helped bring the villainy to completion.

entries.zh: 給事中逵，御史世魁，方幸寅就死，得誣勛謀逆，率同連名，同聲駕禍。
entries.en: Supervising Secretary Zhang Kui and Censor Gao Shikui, seeing their chance when Yin was about to die, framed Xun for plotting rebellion, led others in joint signatures, and raised a chorus of accusation to bring disaster down on him.
entries.literal: The supervising secretary Kui and the censor Shikui, just as Yin was about to die, were able to slander Xun with plotting rebellion; they led others in joint signatures and raised their voices together to bring disaster.

entries.zh: 郎中司馬相妄引事例，故意增減，誣上行私。
entries.en: Bureau Director Sima Xiang falsely cited precedents, deliberately twisting them to slander his superiors for private ends.
entries.literal: The bureau director Sima Xiang falsely cited precedents, deliberately adding and subtracting, and slandered his superiors for private ends.

entries.zh: 邇者言官締黨求勝，內則奴隸公卿，外則草芥司屬，任情恣橫，殆非一日，請大奮乾斷，彰國法。」
entries.en: Remonstrating officials of late have formed factions to win at any cost—treating grandees as servants within the court and subordinates as chaff without, indulging their will with impunity for far too long. We beg Your Majesty to act with decisive authority and make the law plain."
entries.literal: Of late remonstrating officials have formed factions to seek victory; within they treat grandees as slaves, without they treat subordinates as weeds; they indulge their will and act tyrannically—this has gone on for more than a day. We beg Your Majesty to exert great decisive authority and make the national law manifest."

entries.zh: 帝納其言，並下諸人獄，收系南京刑部。
entries.en: The Emperor accepted their argument, imprisoned all these men, and held them at the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.
entries.literal: The Emperor accepted their words, threw all these men into prison, and detained them at the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments.

entries.zh: 先是，廷臣會訊，太仆卿汪元錫、光祿少卿余才偶語曰：「此獄已得情，何再鞫？」
entries.en: Earlier, when court officials met for joint interrogation, Court of the Imperial Stud President Wang Yuanxi and Court of Imperial Entertainments Vice President Yu Cai happened to remark to each other, "This case already has its facts settled—why interrogate again?"
entries.literal: Earlier, when court officials met for joint interrogation, the Court of the Imperial Stud president Wang Yuanxi and the Court of Imperial Entertainments vice president Yu Cai happened to say to each other: "This case has already obtained the facts—why interrogate again?"

entries.zh: 偵者告萼，以聞，亦逮問。
entries.en: An informer reported this to Gui E, who passed it on; they too were arrested and questioned.
entries.literal: An informer reported this to E, who passed it on; they too were arrested and questioned.

entries.zh: 萼等遂肆搒掠。
entries.en: Gui E and his allies then freely applied beating and torture.
entries.literal: E and the others then freely applied beating and torture.

entries.zh: 錄不勝刑，自誣故入人罪。
entries.en: Ma Lu could not endure the torture and confessed to deliberately imposing guilt on others.
entries.literal: Lu could not endure the punishment and confessed to deliberately imposing guilt on others.

entries.zh: 萼等乃定爰書，言寅非福達，錄等恨勛，構成冤獄，因列諸臣罪名。
entries.en: Gui E and his allies then drew up the written verdict, declaring that Yin was not Fuda, that Ma Lu and the others bore a grudge against Xun and had fabricated a wrongful case, and they listed charges against every official involved.
entries.literal: E and the others then fixed the written verdict, saying Yin was not Fuda, that Lu and the others bore hatred for Xun and fabricated a wrongful case, and they listed the crimes of the various officials.

entries.zh: 帝悉從其言。
entries.en: The Emperor accepted everything they proposed.
entries.literal: The Emperor followed all their words.

entries.zh: 謫戍極邊，遇赦不宥者五人：璋、玨、綸、豕、前山西副使遷大理少卿文華。
entries.en: Five men were banished to garrison the farthest frontier with no amnesty on general pardon: Li Zhang, Li Jue, Zhang Lun, Ma Shi, and the former Shanxi vice commissioner who had been promoted to Court of Review Vice President Xu Wenhua.
entries.literal: Banished to garrison the farthest frontier with no amnesty on general pardon—five men: Zhang, Jue, Lun, Shi, and the former Shanxi vice commissioner promoted to Court of Review vice president Wenhua.

entries.zh: 謫戍邊衛者七人：琦、逵、泰、瓊、啟充、仕及知州胡偉。
entries.en: Seven were banished to border garrisons: Liu Qi, Zhang Kui, Chang Tai, Lu Qiong, Cheng Qichong, Liu Shi, and Prefect Hu Wei.
entries.literal: Banished to garrison border guards—seven men: Qi, Kui, Tai, Qiong, Qichong, Shi, and the prefect Hu Wei.

entries.zh: 為民者十一人：賢、科、一鵬、祐、漢、輅、世魁、淳、鳴鳳、相、鸞。
entries.en: Eleven were reduced to commoner status: Nie Xian, Wang Ke, Zheng Yipeng, Qin You, Shen Han, Cheng Lu, Gao Shikui, Ren Chun, Yao Mingfeng, Sima Xiang, and Du Luan.
entries.literal: Reduced to commoner status—eleven men: Xian, Ke, Yipeng, You, Han, Lu, Shikui, Chun, Mingfeng, Xiang, and Luan.

entries.zh: 革職閑住者十七人：頤壽、玉、啟、潮、文莊、沐、佖、淵、元錫、才、楷、仲賢、潤、英、壯、雄、前大理丞遷僉都御史毛伯溫。
entries.en: Seventeen were dismissed and left idle: Yan Yishou, Liu Yu, Wang Qi, Jiang Chao, Liu Wenzhuang, Tang Mu, Gu Yi, Wang Yuan, Wang Yuanxi, Yu Cai, Min Kai, Zhang Zhongxian, Zhang Run, Zhang Ying, Pan Zhuang, Qi Xiong, and the former Court of Review vice registrar who had been promoted to Assistant Censor-in-chief Mao Bowen.
entries.literal: Dismissed from office and left idle—seventeen men: Yishou, Yu, Qi, Chao, Wenzhuang, Mu, Yi, Yuan, Yuanxi, Cai, Kai, Zhongxian, Run, Ying, Zhuang, Xiong, and the former Court of Review vice registrar promoted to Assistant Censor-in-chief Mao Bowen.

entries.zh: 其他下巡按逮問革職者，副使周宣等復五人。
entries.en: Five more, including Vice Commissioner Zhou Xuan, were sent down to touring censors for arrest, questioning, and dismissal.
entries.literal: Others sent down to touring censors for arrest, questioning, and dismissal from office—five more, including the vice commissioner Zhou Xuan.

entries.zh: 良抵死，眾證皆戍，寅還職。
entries.en: Xue Liang was put to death; everyone who had testified against Yin was banished; Yin was restored to his post.
entries.literal: Liang was punished with death; all who had testified were banished to garrison; Yin was restored to office.

entries.zh: 錄以故入人死未決，當徒。
entries.en: Ma Lu, for deliberately imposing a capital charge before the case was settled, was sentenced to penal servitude.
entries.literal: Lu, for deliberately imposing death on others when the case was not yet decided, was sentenced to penal servitude.

entries.zh: 帝以為輕，欲坐以奸黨律斬。
entries.en: The Emperor thought this too lenient and wanted him executed under the statute on villainous factions.
entries.literal: The Emperor thought this too light and wished to punish him with execution under the statute on villainous factions.

entries.zh: 萼等謂張寅未死，而錄代之死，恐天下不服，宜永戍煙瘴地，令緣及子孫。
entries.en: Gui E and his allies argued that Zhang Yin was still alive while Ma Lu had been made to die in his place, which the realm would never accept; he should be banished forever to the miasmic south, with punishment extending to his descendants.
entries.literal: E and the others said Zhang Yin was not yet dead while Lu died in his place, and they feared the realm would not be satisfied; he should be banished forever to miasmic lands, with punishment extending to descendants.

entries.zh: 乃戍廣西南丹衛，遇赦不宥。
entries.en: He was banished to garrison the Nandan Guard in Guangxi, with no amnesty on general pardon.
entries.literal: He was then banished to garrison the Nandan Guard in Guangxi, with no amnesty on general pardon.

entries.zh: 帝意猶未慊，語楊一清等曰：「與其佼及後世，不若誅止其身，從《舜典》『罰弗及嗣』之意。」
entries.en: The Emperor was still not satisfied and told Yang Yiqing and others, "Rather than let his associates reach later generations, it would be better to execute only the man himself, following the 《Canon of Shun》: 'Punishment does not reach the heir.'"
entries.literal: The Emperor's mind was still not satisfied; he said to Yang Yiqing and others: "Rather than let companions reach later generations, better to execute only his person, following the meaning of the 《Canon of Shun》, 'Punishment does not reach the heir.'"

entries.zh: 一清曰：「祖宗制律具有成法，錄罪不中死律。
entries.en: Yiqing replied, "The ancestral code has fixed statutes; Ma Lu's crime does not warrant death under the law.
entries.literal: Yiqing said: "The ancestral code of laws has established statutes; Lu's crime does not fit the statutes for death.

entries.zh: 若法外用刑，吏將緣作奸，人無所措手足矣。」
entries.en: If you punish outside the law, officials will use that as a pretext for abuse and no one will know where he stands."
entries.literal: If punishment is applied outside the law, officials will use it as a pretext for villainy and people will have nowhere to place hand or foot."

entries.zh: 帝不得已，從之。
entries.en: The Emperor had no choice but to accept this.
entries.literal: The Emperor had no choice and followed this.

entries.zh: 以萼等平反有功，勞諭之文華殿，賜二品服俸、金帶、銀幣，給三代誥命。
entries.en: Because Gui E and his allies had merit in reversing the case, the Emperor addressed them at the Wenhua Hall, granted them second-rank salary and robes, a gold belt, and silver coins, and issued patent letters of appointment for three generations.
entries.literal: Because E and the others had merit in reversing the wrongful case, the Emperor rewarded them with an address at the Wenhua Hall, granted second-rank salary and robes, a gold belt, and silver coins, and issued patent letters of appointment for three generations.

entries.zh: 遂編《欽明大獄錄》頒示天下。
entries.en: He then compiled the 《Record of the Augustly Clarified Great Case》 and promulgated it throughout the realm.
entries.literal: He then compiled the 《Record of the Augustly Clarified Great Case》 and promulgated it throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 時嘉靖六年九月壬午也。
entries.en: This was on the renwu day of the ninth month of Jiajing 6.
entries.literal: This was on the renwu day of the ninth month of the sixth year of Jiajing.

entries.zh: 至十六年，皇子生，肆赦。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year, when a prince was born, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
entries.literal: By the sixteenth year a prince was born and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 諸謫戍者俱釋還，惟錄不赦，竟卒於戍所。
entries.en: All who had been banished were released and sent home, except Ma Lu, who was not pardoned and died in exile.
entries.literal: All who had been banished to garrison were released and returned, except Lu, who was not pardoned and in the end died at his place of exile.

entries.zh: 馬錄
entries.en: Ma Lu
entries.literal: Ma Lu

entries.zh: 〈（顏頤壽聶賢湯沐劉琦盧瓊沈漢王科）〉
entries.en: Yan Yishou, Nie Xian, Tang Mu, Liu Qi, Lu Qiong, Shen Han, and Wang Ke)〉
entries.literal: (Yan Yishou, Nie Xian, Tang Mu, Liu Qi, Lu Qiong, Shen Han, Wang Ke)〉

entries.zh: 程啟充張逵鄭一鵬唐樞杜鸞葉應聰
entries.en: Cheng Qichong, Zhang Kui, Zheng Yipeng, Tang Shu, Du Luan, and Ye Yingcong
entries.literal: Cheng Qichong, Zhang Kui, Zheng Yipeng, Tang Shu, Du Luan, Ye Yingcong

entries.zh: 〈（藍田黃綰）〉
entries.en: Lantian and Huang Guan)〉
entries.literal: (Lantian, Huang Guan)〉

entries.zh: 解一貫
entries.en: Jie Yiguan
entries.literal: Jie Yiguan

entries.zh: 〈（鄭洛書張錄）〉
entries.en: Zheng Luoshu and Zhang Lu)〉
entries.literal: (Zheng Luoshu, Zhang Lu)〉

entries.zh: 陸粲
entries.en: Lu Can
entries.literal: Lu Can

entries.zh: 〈（劉希簡王準）〉
entries.en: Liu Xijian and Wang Zhun)〉
entries.literal: (Liu Xijian, Wang Zhun)〉

entries.zh: 邵經邦劉世揚
entries.en: Shao Jingbang and Liu Shiyang
entries.literal: Shao Jingbang, Liu Shiyang

entries.en: Zhao Han)〉
entries.literal: (Zhao Han)〉

entries.zh: 魏良弼
entries.en: Wei Liangbi
entries.literal: Wei Liangbi

entries.zh: 〈（秦鰲張寅葉洪）〉
entries.en: Qin Ao, Zhang Yin, and Ye Hong)〉
entries.literal: (Qin Ao, Zhang Yin, Ye Hong)〉

entries.zh: 馬錄，字君卿，信陽人。正德三年進士。授固安知縣。居官廉明，征為御史，按江南諸府。世宗即位，疏言：「江南之民最苦糧長。白糧輸內府一石，率費四五石。他如酒醋局、供應庫以至軍器、胖襖、顏料之屬輸內府者，費皆然。戶部侍郎秦金等請從錄言，命石加耗一斗，毋得苛求。中官黃錦誣劾高唐判官金坡，詔逮之，連五百餘人。錄言：祖宗內設法司，外設撫、按，百餘年刑清政平。先帝時，劉瑾、錢寧輩蠱惑聖聰，動遣錦衣官校，致天下洶洶。陛下方勤新政，不虞復有高唐之命。」給事中許復禮等亦以為言，獄得少解。嘉靖二年大計天下庶官，被黜者多訐撫、按，以錄言禁止。
entries.en: Ma Lu, courtesy name Junqing, was a native of Xinyang. A jinshi of Zhengde 3, he was appointed magistrate of Gu'an. He governed with integrity and clarity, and was summoned as censor to inspect the prefectures of Jiangnan. When Shizong came to the throne, he memorialized: "The people of Jiangnan suffer most from grain-chief service. For every shi of white grain sent to the inner palace, the expense usually reaches four or five shi. Other deliveries to the inner palace, from the Wine and Vinegar Office and Supply Storehouse to military equipment, padded coats, and pigments, are all the same. Vice Minister of Revenue Qin Jin and others asked that Lu's proposal be adopted, so an order added one dou of allowance per shi and forbade harsh exactions. The eunuch Huang Jin falsely impeached Jin Po, Assistant Magistrate of Gaotang, and an edict ordered his arrest, implicating more than five hundred people. Lu said that the ancestors established judicial offices inside the capital and grand coordinators and inspectors outside it, so punishments had been clear and government peaceful for more than a century. Under the former emperor, Liu Jin, Qian Ning, and their sort deceived the imperial judgment and repeatedly sent out Embroidered Uniform Guard officers and constables, throwing the realm into alarm. Your Majesty is now diligently renewing government, so one would not expect another Gaotang order." Supervising Secretary Xu Fuli and others also spoke, and the case was somewhat eased. In Jiajing 2, during the grand evaluation of officials across the realm, many dismissed men accused the grand coordinators and inspectors. Because of Lu's statement, this was forbidden.
entries.literal: Ma Lu, courtesy name Junqing, was from Xinyang. He became a jinshi in the third year of Zhengde. He was appointed magistrate of Gu'an. In office he was honest and clear, and he was summoned to be censor, inspecting the prefectures of Jiangnan. When Shizong ascended the throne, he submitted a memorial, saying: "The people of Jiangnan suffer most from grain-chief service. For each shi of white grain transported to the inner palace, the cost commonly reaches four or five shi. Other deliveries to the inner palace, such as those for the Wine and Vinegar Office, the Supply Storehouse, and even military equipment, padded coats, and pigments, all cost the same. Vice Minister of Revenue Qin Jin and others requested that Lu's words be followed, and an order was issued adding one dou of wastage allowance per shi and forbidding harsh exactions. The eunuch Huang Jin falsely impeached Jin Po, Assistant Magistrate of Gaotang, and an edict ordered his arrest, implicating more than five hundred people. Lu said that the ancestors established judicial offices within and grand coordinators and regional inspectors without, and for more than a hundred years punishments had been clear and government peaceful. In the former emperor's time, Liu Jin, Qian Ning, and their kind misled the sacred intelligence and repeatedly dispatched Embroidered Uniform Guard officers and constables, causing turmoil throughout the realm. Your Majesty is now diligently pursuing new government, and one would not expect another Gaotang order." Supervising Secretary Xu Fuli and others also spoke on this, and the prison case was somewhat eased. In the second year of Jiajing, when officials throughout the realm underwent the grand evaluation, many of those dismissed attacked the grand coordinators and regional inspectors. Because of Lu's words this was prohibited.

entries.zh: 明年，哱拜反，遂煽諸部為亂。
entries.en: The following year Piba rebelled and stirred the tribes into general disorder.
entries.literal: The next year Piba rebelled and then incited the various tribes to revolt.

entries.zh: 拜，西部人也。
entries.en: Piba came from the western tribes.
entries.literal: Piba was a man of the western tribes.

entries.zh: 嘉靖中得罪其部長，父兄皆見殺，拜跳脫來降，驍勇屢立戰功。
entries.en: During the Jiajing reign he had fallen out with his tribal chief; his father and brothers were killed, but he escaped and surrendered to the Ming, proving himself a fierce fighter who won repeated battle honors.
entries.literal: In the Jiajing reign he offended his tribal chief; his father and elder brothers were all killed; Piba escaped by leaping away and came to surrender; brave and fierce, he repeatedly won battle merit.

entries.zh: 前督撫王崇古、石茂華先後奏加副總兵，遂多畜亡命。
entries.en: Earlier supreme commanders Wang Chonggu and Shi Maohua had successively recommended him for promotion to vice commander, and he thereafter gathered many outlaws about him.
entries.literal: Former supreme commanders Wang Chonggu and Shi Maohua in succession memorialized to add him as vice commander, and he then kept many fugitives.

entries.zh: 子承恩，拜夢妖物入妻施脅而生，狼形梟啼，性狠戾。
entries.en: His son Chengen was said to have been born after Piba dreamed that a demon entered his wife Shi; the child was wolflike in appearance, cried like an owl, and was savage by nature.
entries.literal: His son Chengen: Piba dreamed that a demonic thing entered his wife Shi and was born by compulsion; wolf-like in form with owl-like cries, by nature fierce and cruel.

entries.zh: 拜老，承恩襲父爵。
entries.en: As Piba aged, Chengen inherited his father's rank.
entries.literal: When Piba grew old, Chengen inherited his father's title.

entries.zh: 十九年，洮、河告警，御史周弘禴舉承恩及指揮土文秀、拜義子哱雲等。
entries.en: In year 19 (1591) alarms sounded on the Tao and Yellow River frontiers, and Censor Zhou Hongyi recommended Chengen along with Commanders Tu Wenxiu and Piba's adopted son Piba Yun.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, alarm was raised on the Tao and Yellow River frontiers; the censor Zhou Hongyi recommended Chengen and the commanders Tu Wenxiu, Piba's adopted son Piba Yun, and others.

entries.zh: 巡撫黨馨檄文秀西援，拜謁經略鄭洛，願與子承恩從出師。
entries.en: Grand Coordinator Dang Xin ordered Wenxiu west as reinforcement; Piba visited Commissioner Zheng Luo and offered to campaign with his son Chengen.
entries.literal: The grand coordinator Dang Xin ordered Wenxiu west as reinforcement; Piba called on the frontier commissioner Zheng Luo and wished to follow on campaign with his son Chengen.

entries.zh: 馨惡其自薦，抑損之，拜以故心怨。
entries.en: Xin disliked his self-recommendation and slighted him, and Piba came to resent him.
entries.literal: Xin disliked his volunteering himself and belittled him; Piba therefore bore resentment in heart.

entries.zh: 至金城，見諸鎮兵皆出其下。
entries.en: At Jincheng he saw that the garrison troops ranked below him.
entries.literal: When he reached Jincheng, he saw that the troops of the various garrisons were all beneath him.

entries.zh: 比賊退，取道塞外還，寇騎遇之皆辟易，遂有輕中外心。
entries.en: On the return march by an outer route after the enemy withdrew, raiding horsemen gave way before him, and he began to despise both Ming and tribal forces alike.
entries.literal: When the bandits had withdrawn, he returned by way outside the passes; enemy horsemen who met him all gave way, and he then had a mind to look lightly on Chinese and foreigners alike.

entries.zh: 馨數裁拜，且按承恩罪箠之二十，雲、文秀亦以他故怨馨。
entries.en: Xin repeatedly restrained Piba, prosecuted Chengen for an offense, and had him flogged twenty strokes; Yun and Wenxiu also bore grudges against Xin for other reasons.
entries.literal: Xin repeatedly curbed Piba, and moreover prosecuted Chengen for an offense and flogged him twenty strokes; Yun and Wenxiu also resented Xin for other reasons.

entries.zh: 會戍卒請衣糧久弗給，拜遂嗾軍鋒劉東旸、許朝作亂。
entries.en: When long-delayed requests for clothing and rations went unanswered, Piba incited the army vanguards Liu Dongyang and Xu Chao to mutiny.
entries.literal: It happened that garrison soldiers had long requested clothing and grain rations without receiving them; Piba then incited the army vanguard Liu Dongyang and Xu Chao to make rebellion.

entries.zh: 二十年三月，殺馨及副使石繼芳，逼總兵官張維忠縊死。
entries.en: In the third month of year 20 (1592) they killed Dang Xin and Vice Commissioner Shi Jifang and drove Commander Zhang Weizhong to hang himself.
entries.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year, they killed Xin and the vice commissioner Shi Jifang and forced the commander-in-chief Zhang Weizhong to hang himself.

entries.zh: 雲、文秀殺遊擊梁琦、守備馬承光，東旸稱總兵，奉拜為謀主，承恩、朝為左、右副總兵，雲、文秀為左、右參將。
entries.en: Yun and Wenxiu killed Mobile Corps Commander Liang Qi and Garrison Commander Ma Chengguang; Dongyang proclaimed himself commander-in-chief, made Piba chief strategist, appointed Chengen and Chao left and right vice commanders, and Yun and Wenxiu left and right assistant commanders.
entries.literal: Yun and Wenxiu killed the mobile corps commander Liang Qi and the garrison commander Ma Chengguang; Dongyang styled himself commander-in-chief, made Piba the chief strategist, made Chengen and Chao left and right vice commanders, and made Yun and Wenxiu left and right assistant commanders.

entries.zh: 承恩遂陷玉泉營、中衛、廣武，河西望風靡。
entries.en: Chengen then seized Yuchuan Camp, Zhongwei, and Guangwu, and the whole Hexi region collapsed before the rebels.
entries.literal: Chengen then captured Yuchuan Camp, Zhongwei, and Guangwu; west of the river all submitted at the wind.

entries.zh: 惟文秀徇平虜，參將蕭如薰堅守不下。
entries.en: Only Wenxiu besieged Pinglu, where Assistant Commander Xiao Ruxun held out and could not be dislodged.
entries.literal: Only Wenxiu attacked Pinglu; the assistant commander Xiao Ruxun held firm and could not be taken.

entries.zh: 賊既取河西四十七堡，且渡河，復誘河套著力兔、宰僧犯平虜、花馬池。
entries.en: After seizing forty-seven Hexi forts and crossing the river, the rebels induced the Ordos leaders Zhulitu and Zaiseng to attack Pinglu and Huamachi.
entries.literal: The bandits, having already taken forty-seven forts west of the river and moreover crossed the river, again enticed the Ordos leaders Zhulitu and Zaiseng to invade Pinglu and Huamachi.

entries.zh: 全陜皆震動。
entries.en: All Shaanxi was thrown into alarm.
entries.literal: The whole of Shaanxi was shaken.

entries.zh: 學曾檄副總兵李句率遊擊吳顯趨靈州，別遣遊擊趙武趨鳴沙州，沿河扼賊南渡，而自駐花馬池，當賊衛。
entries.en: Xueceng ordered Vice Commander Li Gou and Mobile Corps Commander Wu Xian to rush to Lingzhou, sent Zhao Wu to Mingsha to block a southern crossing along the river, and himself held Huamachi to face the rebel advance.
entries.literal: Xueceng ordered the vice commander Li Gou to lead the mobile corps commander Wu Xian in haste to Lingzhou, separately sent the mobile corps commander Zhao Wu in haste to Mingsha Prefecture, along the river to block the bandits' crossing south, and himself garrisoned Huamachi to meet the bandits' assault.

entries.zh: 句等渡河，賊將多遁去，四十七堡皆復，惟寧夏鎮城尚為賊據。
entries.en: Gou crossed the river, most rebel commanders fled, and all forty-seven forts were recovered, though the Ningxia garrison city remained in rebel hands.
entries.literal: Gou and others crossed the river; most of the bandit generals fled away; all forty-seven forts were recovered; only the Ningxia garrison town was still held by the bandits.

entries.zh: 著力兔等中外相呼應，拜、文秀攻趙武於玉泉。
entries.en: Zhulitu coordinated with the rebels inside and out while Piba and Wenxiu attacked Zhao Wu at Yuchuan.
entries.literal: Zhulitu and others coordinated inside and outside; Piba and Wenxiu attacked Zhao Wu at Yuchuan.

entries.zh: 雲引著力兔攻平虜，如薰設伏射殺雲。
entries.en: Yun led Zhulitu against Pinglu, but Ruxun ambushed and killed Yun.
entries.literal: Yun led Zhulitu to attack Pinglu; Ruxun set an ambush and shot Yun dead.

entries.zh: 句救武，圍亦解。
entries.en: Gou relieved Zhao Wu and broke the siege.
entries.literal: Gou rescued Wu and the siege was also lifted.

entries.zh: 四月，句引兵與故總兵牛秉忠抵鎮城下。
entries.en: In the fourth month Gou advanced with former Commander Niu Bingzhong to the walls of the garrison city.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, Gou led troops with the former commander Niu Bingzhong to reach below the garrison town.

entries.zh: 帝已擢董一奎為總兵，李蕡副之，已，復擢如薰代一奎，而以麻貴代蕡。
entries.en: The emperor had appointed Dong Yikui commander with Li Fen as deputy, then replaced Yikui with Ruxun and Fen with Ma Gui.
entries.literal: The emperor had already promoted Dong Yikui as commander-in-chief with Li Fen as his deputy; afterward he again promoted Ruxun to replace Yikui and made Ma Gui replace Fen.

entries.zh: 未至，句等攻城。
entries.en: Before the new commanders arrived, Gou and his forces attacked the city.
entries.literal: Before they arrived, Gou and others assaulted the city.

entries.zh: 賊於東西二門各出驍騎三千搏戰，步卒列火車為營。
entries.en: The rebels sent three thousand elite horsemen from each of the east and west gates while infantry formed camps behind gun carriages.
entries.literal: The bandits at the eastern and western gates each sent out three thousand picked horsemen to fight in close combat; foot soldiers arrayed gun carriages as a camp.

entries.zh: 官軍擊之，奪其車百輛，追奔入湖，賊溺死無算。
entries.en: Government troops routed them, captured a hundred gun carriages, pursued the fugitives into a lake, and drowned countless rebels.
entries.literal: The government army struck them, seized a hundred of their carriages, pursued the fleeing into a lake, and countless bandits drowned.

entries.zh: 副總兵王通戰尤力。
entries.en: Vice Commander Wang Tong fought with particular vigor.
entries.literal: The vice commander Wang Tong fought with especial force.

entries.zh: 家丁高益等乘勝入北門，後兵不繼被殺，通亦負傷，榆林遊擊俞尚德戰死。
entries.en: Household retainers led by Gao Yi broke into the north gate in the pursuit, but unsupported follow-up troops were cut down; Tong was wounded and Yulin Mobile Corps Commander Yu Shangde was killed.
entries.literal: The household retainers Gao Yi and others, riding the victory, entered the north gate; the following troops did not continue and were killed; Tong was also wounded; the Yulin mobile corps commander Yu Shangde died in battle.

entries.zh: 翼日，朝、文秀脅慶王上東城，乞暫罷兵，詭言願獻首惡。
entries.en: The next day Chao and Wenxiu forced the Prince of Qing onto the east wall to plead for a truce, falsely offering to hand over the ringleaders.
entries.literal: The next day, Chao and Wenxiu coerced the Prince of Qing to ascend the east wall, begged a temporary halt to fighting, and falsely claimed willingness to present the chief culprit.

entries.zh: 會官軍糧盡，乃引退，休近堡。
entries.en: When government provisions ran out, the army withdrew and encamped near the border forts.
entries.literal: It happened that the government army's grain was exhausted; they then withdrew and rested near the forts.

entries.zh: 魏學曾
entries.en: Wei Xueceng
entries.literal: Wei Xueceng

entries.zh: 〈（葉夢熊梅國楨）〉
entries.en: (see also: Ye Mengxiong, Mei Guozhen)]〉
entries.literal: (Ye Mengxiong, Mei Guozhen)]〉

entries.zh: 李化龍
entries.en: Li Hualong
entries.literal: Li Hualong

entries.en: (see also: Jiang Duo)]〉
entries.literal: (Jiang Duo)]〉

entries.zh: 一曰慎爵賞以肅軍情。
entries.en: Third, review ennoblements and rewards carefully to restore military discipline.
entries.literal: Third: be cautious with ranks and rewards to stern the military morale.

entries.zh: 請分別各帥封賞，孰當孰濫，輕則收侯爵，重則奪伯爵。
entries.en: Review every commander's titles and rewards: distinguish the deserved from the gratuitous. Strip lesser offenders of their marquisates; revoke earldoms from the worst.
entries.literal: I ask to distinguish the enfeoffments and rewards of each commander—who deserved them and who received them excessively; lightly, strip marquisates; heavily, revoke earldoms.

entries.zh: 夫以左帥之恢復而封，高、劉之敗逃亦封，又誰不當封者？
entries.en: If the Left Marshal was ennobled for recovering territory while Gao and Liu were rewarded for defeat and flight, who would not claim a title?
entries.literal: Now if the Left Marshal was enfeoffed for recovery, while Gao and Liu were also enfeoffed for defeat and flight—who then would not deserve enfeoffment?

entries.zh: 武臣既濫，文臣隨之，外臣既濫，中珰隨之，恐天下聞而解體也。
entries.en: Indiscriminate rewards to generals invite the same from civil officials, and from regional officials to palace eunuchs. The empire will lose heart when it sees this.
entries.literal: Once military ministers are excessive, civil ministers follow; once external ministers are excessive, palace eunuchs follow—I fear the empire will hear of it and disintegrate.

entries.zh: 士英大怒，即日具疏辭位，且揚言於朝曰：「劉公自稱草莽孤臣，不書新命，明示不臣天子也。」
entries.en: Ma Shi Ying was furious. That same day he submitted his resignation and declared at court: "Lord Liu calls himself a private subject of the wilderness and omitted the new imperial title from his memorial—a plain refusal to acknowledge the Son of Heaven."
entries.literal: Shi Ying was greatly enraged; that very day he prepared a memorial resigning his post, and proclaimed in court, saying: "Lord Liu styled himself a lone minister of the wilds and did not write the new appointment—openly showing he will not serve the Son of Heaven."

entries.zh: 其私人朱統𨰥遂劾宗周疏請移蹕鳳陽：「鳳陽，高墻所在，欲以罪宗處皇上，而與史可法擁立潞王。
entries.en: His client Zhu Tonglei then impeached Zongzhou for requesting that the court move to Fengyang: "Fengyang is a prison city. He means to confine the emperor there while he and Shi Kefa install the Prince of Lu.
entries.literal: His private man Zhu Tonglei then impeached Zongzhou's memorial requesting the transfer of the imperial residence to Fengyang: "Fengyang is where high walls stand; he wishes to place the emperor in the place of guilt, and with Shi Kefa to support and establish the Prince of Lu.

entries.zh: 其兵已伏丹陽，當急備。」
entries.en: His troops are already hidden at Danyang. Guard against them at once."
entries.literal: His troops are already lying in ambush at Danyang—urgent preparations should be made."

entries.zh: 而澤清、傑日夜謀所以殺宗周者不得，乃遣客十輩往刺宗周。
entries.en: Meanwhile Liu Zeqing and Gao Jie plotted day and night to kill Zongzhou. Failing in that, they sent ten groups of assassins after him.
entries.literal: Yet Zeqing and Jie day and night schemed how to kill Zongzhou without success; then they sent ten batches of assassins to stab Zongzhou.

entries.zh: 宗周時在丹陽，終日危坐，未嘗有惰容，客前後至者，不敢加害而去。
entries.en: Zongzhou was then at Danyang, sitting upright all day without a trace of fear. Assassins came and went but none dared strike.
entries.literal: Zongzhou was then at Danyang, sitting upright all day, never showing a lazy countenance; assassins who came before and after did not dare harm him and left.

entries.zh: 而黃鳴駿入覲，兵抵京口，與防江兵相擊鬥。
entries.en: Meanwhile Huang Mingjun came to court, and his troops reached Jingkou and fought with the river-defense forces.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Huang Mingjun entered audience; his troops reached Jingkou and clashed with the river-defense troops.

entries.zh: 士英以統𨰥言為信也，亦震恐。
entries.en: Ma Shi Ying, believing Zhu Tonglei's accusation, was terrified as well.
entries.literal: Shi Ying took Tonglei's words as true and was also shaken with terror.

entries.zh: 於是澤清疏劾：「宗周陰撓恢復，欲誅臣等，激變士心，召生靈之禍。」
entries.en: Then Liu Zeqing memorialized: "Zongzhou secretly sabotages the recovery effort, seeks to execute us, inflames the troops, and invites disaster upon the people."
entries.literal: Thus Zeqing memorialized in impeachment: "Zongzhou secretly obstructs recovery, wishes to execute us ministers, stirs mutiny in soldiers' hearts, and summons calamity upon the people."

entries.zh: 劉良佐亦具疏言宗周力持「三案」，為門戶主盟，倡議親征，圖晁錯之自為居守，司馬懿之閉城拒君。
entries.en: Liu Liangzuo also submitted a memorial accusing Zongzhou of championing the "Three Cases," leading the factional alliance, and urging a personal campaign—plotting, like Chao Cuo, to hold power while the emperor marched, and, like Sima Yi, to shut the gates against the throne.
entries.literal: Liu Liangzuo also prepared a memorial saying Zongzhou forcefully upheld the "Three Cases," acted as factional chief, advocated personal campaign, and schemed Chao Cuo's staying behind to hold the fort and Sima Yi's closing the gates to reject the sovereign.

entries.zh: 疏未下，澤清復草一疏，署傑、良佐及黃得功名上之，言：「宗周勸上親征，謀危君父，欲安置陛下於烽火兇危之地。
entries.en: Before that memorial was even issued, Liu Zeqing drafted another, signed by Gao Jie, Liu Liangzuo, and Huang Degong, declaring: "Zongzhou urged Your Majesty to lead the campaign personally, endangering the throne, and meant to place you in the midst of battle and peril.
entries.literal: Before the memorial was issued, Zeqing again drafted a memorial, signed by Jie, Liangzuo, and Huang Degong and submitted it, saying: "Zongzhou urged the sovereign to personally campaign, schemed peril to the sovereign and father, and wished to place Your Majesty in a place of beacon fires and fierce danger.

entries.zh: 蓋非宗周一人之謀，姜曰廣、吳甡合謀也。
entries.en: This was not Zongzhou's plot alone—Jiang Yueguang and Wu Shen were his co-conspirators.
entries.literal: This was not Zongzhou's plot alone—Jiang Yueguang and Wu Shen conspired together.

entries.zh: 曰廣心雄膽大，翊戴非其本懷，故陰結死黨，翦除諸忠，然後迫劫乘輿，遷之別郡。
entries.en: Yueguang is ambitious and bold; enthroning the emperor was never his true aim. He secretly formed a faction, purged the loyal, and then meant to seize the imperial carriage and relocate the court.
entries.literal: Yueguang's heart was bold and his courage great; supporting the enthronement was not his original intent—thus he secretly bound a diehard faction, cut down the loyal, and then coerced the imperial carriage and moved it to another commandery.

entries.zh: 如甡、宗周入都，臣等即渡江赴闕，面訐諸奸，正《春秋》討賊之義。」
entries.en: If Wu Shen and Zongzhou enter the capital, we shall cross the Yangtze, appear before the throne, denounce these traitors face to face, and uphold the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 principle of punishing rebels."
entries.literal: If Shen and Zongzhou enter the capital, we ministers will immediately cross the river and go to the palace, face-to-face denounce the traitors, and uphold the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》 righteousness of punishing rebels."

entries.zh: 疏入，舉朝大駭，傳諭和衷集事。
entries.en: When the memorial arrived, the court was horrified. An edict was issued calling for harmony and unity.
entries.literal: When the memorial entered, the whole court was greatly alarmed; an edict was transmitted urging harmony of heart and gathering of affairs.

entries.zh: 宗周不得已，以七月十八日入朝。
entries.en: Zongzhou had no choice but to enter court on the eighteenth day of the seventh month.
entries.literal: Zongzhou had no choice; on the eighteenth day of the seventh month he entered court.

entries.zh: 初，澤清疏出，遣人錄示傑。
entries.en: When Liu Zeqing's memorial was issued, he sent a copy to Gao Jie.
entries.literal: At first, when Zeqing's memorial was issued, he sent someone to copy and show it to Jie.

entries.zh: 傑曰：「我輩武人，乃預朝事耶？」
entries.en: Gao Jie said: "We are soldiers—since when do we meddle in court affairs?"
entries.literal: Jie said: "We military men—are we to participate in court affairs?"

entries.zh: 得功疏辨：「臣不預聞。」
entries.en: Huang Degong submitted a defense: "Your subject had no part in this."
entries.literal: Degong submitted a memorial in defense: "Your subject did not participate in hearing."

entries.zh: 士英寢不奏。
entries.en: Ma Shi Ying suppressed it and never forwarded it to the throne.
entries.literal: Shi Ying shelved it and did not memorialize.

entries.zh: 可法不平，遣使遍詰諸鎮，咸云不知，遂據以入告，澤清輩由是氣沮。
entries.en: Shi Kefa, indignant, sent envoys to question every garrison. All denied knowledge of the plot. He reported this to the throne, and Liu Zeqing and his allies lost heart.
entries.literal: Kefa was indignant; he sent envoys to question all the garrisons everywhere—they all said they did not know—then relied on this to enter and report, and Zeqing and company thereby lost their spirit.

entries.zh: 劉宗周
entries.en: Liu Zongzhou
entries.literal: Liu Zongzhou

entries.zh: 〈（祝淵王毓蓍）〉
entries.en: (Sub-biographies: Zhu Yuan and Wang Yushi)
entries.literal: (Zhu Yuan, Wang Yushi)

entries.zh: 黃道周
entries.en: Huang Daozhou
entries.literal: Huang Daozhou

entries.zh: 〈（葉廷秀）〉
entries.en: (Ye Tingxiu)
entries.literal: (Ye Tingxiu)

entries.zh: 召理京營戎政，改刑部尚書，預受兩朝顧命。
entries.en: Summoned to oversee the capital garrisons' military administration, he was transferred to Minister of Justice and received the deathbed trusts of two reigns.
entries.literal: He was summoned to take charge of military administration for the capital garrisons, transferred to Minister of Justice, and received the deathbed trusts of two reigns.

entries.zh: 李選侍將移宮，其內侍王永福、姚進忠等八人坐盜乾清宮珠寶下吏。
entries.en: As Lady Li was about to move out of the palace, eight of her eunuchs—Wang Yongfu, Yao Jinzhong, and others—were charged with stealing jewels from the Palace of Heavenly Purity and handed over to the judicial authorities.
entries.literal: When Lady Li was about to leave the palace, eight of her eunuchs—Wang Yongfu, Yao Jinzhong, and others—were charged with stealing jewels from the Palace of Heavenly Purity and handed over to the judicial authorities.

entries.zh: 克纘擬二人辟，余俱末減。
entries.en: Kezuan proposed the death penalty for two of them and reduced sentences for the rest.
entries.literal: Kezuan proposed execution for two of them and reduced sentences for the rest.

entries.zh: 帝不從，命辟六人，余遣戍。
entries.en: The emperor refused and ordered six executed; the rest were banished to frontier service.
entries.literal: The emperor did not agree and ordered six executed; the rest were sent into exile.

entries.zh: 克纘言：「姜升、鄭穩山、劉尚理不持一物，劉遜拾地上珠，還之選侍，而與永福、進忠同戮，輕重失倫。
entries.en: Kezuan said, "Jiang Sheng, Zheng Wenshan, and Liu Shangli took nothing at all; Liu Xun picked up a pearl from the floor and returned it to Lady Li, yet they are to die alongside Yongfu and Jinzhong—the gradation of punishment is out of balance.
entries.literal: Kezuan said: "Jiang Sheng, Zheng Wenshan, and Liu Shangli took not a single thing; Liu Xun picked up a pearl from the ground and returned it to Lady Li, yet they are to be executed together with Yongfu and Jinzhong—the gradation of punishment is out of balance.

entries.zh: 況選侍篋中物，安知非先朝所賜？」
entries.en: Besides, who can say the items in Lady Li's casket were not gifts from the previous reign?"
entries.literal: Moreover, who is to say the items in Lady Li's casket were not gifts from the previous reign?"

entries.zh: 當是時，諸珰罪重，謀脫無自，惟請帝厚待選侍，則獄情自緩。
entries.en: At that time the eunuchs' crimes were grave and they had no way to save themselves; they could only urge the emperor to treat Lady Li generously, in hopes the case would soften on its own.
entries.literal: At that time the eunuchs' crimes were grave and they had no way to escape on their own; they could only ask that the emperor treat Lady Li generously, and then the severity of the case would ease of itself.

entries.zh: 於是流言四布，謂帝薄待先朝妃嬪，而克纘首入其言。
entries.en: Rumors then spread that the emperor was treating the late emperor's consorts harshly, and that Kezuan had been the first to give voice to that view.
entries.literal: Rumors then spread everywhere that the emperor was treating the late emperor's consorts harshly, and that Kezuan was the first to give voice to this view.

entries.zh: 帝不悅，責克纘偏聽，命如前旨。
entries.en: The emperor was displeased, rebuked Kezuan for partiality, and ordered that the previous edict stand.
entries.literal: The emperor was displeased, rebuked Kezuan for partial listening, and ordered that the previous edict stand.

entries.zh: 崔景榮黃克纘畢自嚴李長庚
entries.en: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, and Li Zhanggeng
entries.literal: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, Li Zhanggeng

entries.zh: 〈（王誌道）〉
entries.en: (Sub-biography: Wang Zhidao)
entries.literal: (Wang Zhidao)

entries.zh: 劉之鳳
entries.en: Liu Zhifeng
entries.literal: Liu Zhifeng

entries.zh: 孟希文，字士煥，亞聖五十六代孫也。
entries.en: Meng Xiwen, styled Shihuan, was a fifty-sixth-generation descendant of Mencius, the Second Sage.
entries.literal: Meng Xiwen, courtesy name Shihuan, was a descendant of the Second Sage in the fifty-sixth generation.

entries.zh: 洪武元年詔以孟子五十四代孫思諒奉祀，世復其家。
entries.en: In Hongwu 1 an edict appointed Siliao, fifty-fourth in descent from Mencius, to perform sacrifices and restored his household by hereditary grant.
entries.literal: In the first year of Hongwu an edict ordered Siliao, fifty-fourth-generation descendant of Mencius, to perform sacrifices, and his household was restored by hereditary grant.

entries.zh: 思諒，字友道，子克仁，字信夫。
entries.en: Siliao, styled Youdao; his son Keren, styled Xinfu.
entries.literal: Siliao, courtesy name Youdao; his son Keren, courtesy name Xinfu.

entries.zh: 克仁子希文。
entries.en: Keren's son was Xiwen.
entries.literal: Keren's son was Xiwen.

entries.zh: 景泰三年授希文翰林院《五經》博士，子孫世襲。
entries.en: In Jingtai 3 Xiwen was made Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, a hereditary post for his line.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jingtai Xiwen was appointed Doctor of the Five Classics in the Hanlin Academy, hereditary for his descendants.

entries.zh: 卒，子元，字長伯，弘治二年襲。
entries.en: He died; his son Yuan, styled Changbo, succeeded in Hongzhi 2.
entries.literal: He died; his son Yuan, courtesy name Changbo, inherited in the second year of Hongzhi.

entries.zh: 卒，子公棨幼，嘉靖二年以元弟亨之子公肇襲。
entries.en: He died leaving a young son Gongqi; in Jiajing 2 Yuan's nephew Gongzhao, son of his brother Heng, succeeded.
entries.literal: He died; his son Gongqi was young; in the second year of Jiajing Yuan's younger brother Heng's son Gongzhao inherited.

entries.zh: 公肇，字先文，少好學，事繼母孔氏，以孝聞。
entries.en: Gongzhao, styled Xianwen, was studious from youth and famed for filial service to his Kong-clan stepmother.
entries.literal: Gongzhao, courtesy name Xianwen, loved study from youth and served his stepmother of the Kong clan with filial conduct, for which he was renowned.

entries.zh: 卒，十二年，仍以公棨襲。
entries.en: He died; in the twelfth year the title passed back to Gongqi.
entries.literal: He died; in the twelfth year Gongqi still inherited.

entries.zh: 公棨，字橐文。
entries.en: Gongqi, whose courtesy name was Tuowen.
entries.literal: Gongqi, courtesy name Tuowen.

entries.zh: 卒，子彥璞，字朝璽，隆慶元年襲。
entries.en: He died; his son Yanpu, styled Chaoxi, succeeded in Longqing 1.
entries.literal: He died; his son Yanpu, courtesy name Chaoxi, inherited in the first year of Longqing.

entries.zh: 卒，子承光，萬歷二十九年襲。
entries.en: He died; his son Chengguang succeeded in Wanli 29.
entries.literal: He died; his son Chengguang inherited in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.

entries.zh: 卒，子弘譽，天啟三年襲。
entries.en: He died; his son Hongyu succeeded in Tianqi 3.
entries.literal: He died; his son Hongyu inherited in the third year of Tianqi.

entries.zh: 卒，子聞玉，崇禎二年襲。
entries.en: He died; his son Wenyu succeeded in Chongzhen 2.
entries.literal: He died; his son Wenyu inherited in the second year of Chongzhen.

entries.zh: 孔希學
entries.en: Kong Xixue
entries.literal: Kong Xixue

entries.zh: 孔彥繩
entries.en: Kong Yanchang
entries.literal: Kong Yanchang

entries.zh: 顏希惠曾質粹孔聞禮孟希文仲於陛周冕程接道程克仁張文運邵繼祖朱梴朱墅
entries.en: Yan Xihui, Zeng Zhicui, Kong Wenli, Meng Xiwen, Zhong Yubi, Zhou Mian, Cheng Jiedao, Cheng Keren, Zhang Wenyun, Shao Jizu, Zhu Ting, and Zhu Shu
entries.literal: Yan Xihui, Zeng Zhicui, Kong Wenli, Meng Xiwen, Zhong Yubi, Zhou Mian, Cheng Jiedao, Cheng Keren, Zhang Wenyun, Shao Jizu, Zhu Ting, Zhu Shu

entries.zh: 韓愈言：「《蹇》之六二曰『王臣蹇蹇』，而《蠱》之上九曰『高尚其事』，由所居之時不一，而所蹈之德不同。」
entries.en: Han Yu wrote: "The second line of the Hexagram Jian reads, 'The king's ministers are in distress,' while the top line of Gu reads, 'Noble in his deeds'—for the age each man lived in was not the same, and the virtue each man embodied was not the same."
entries.literal: Han Yu said: "In the second line of Jian it says 'the king's ministers are in distress,' while in the top line of Gu it says 'noble in his conduct'—because the times in which they lived were not the same, the virtues they practiced were different."

entries.zh: 夫聖賢以用世為心，而逸民以肥遁為節 ，豈性分實然，亦各行其志而已。
entries.en: Sages and worthies set their hearts on serving the world, while men of retirement take luxuriant withdrawal as their standard of conduct. Was their nature utterly different? Each simply followed his own resolve.
entries.literal: Sages and worthies take serving the age as their heart, while recluses take prosperous withdrawal as their integrity—is it that their natures are utterly different? Each merely followed his own aspiration.

entries.zh: 明太祖興禮儒士，聘文學，搜求岩穴，側席幽人，後置不為君用之罰，然韜跡自遠者，亦不乏人。
entries.en: When the Hongwu Emperor revived ritual and honored Confucian scholars, he recruited men of letters, sought out hermits in mountain caves, and waited eagerly for recluses to appear. Later he imposed penalties on those who refused to serve the throne, yet men who hid their tracks and kept their distance were never in short supply.
entries.literal: Taizu of Ming promoted ritual and Confucian scholars, recruited men of letters, searched out those in mountain caves, and waited anxiously for recluses; later he imposed penalties on those who would not serve the ruler—yet those who hid their traces and kept far away were not lacking.

entries.zh: 迨中葉承平，聲教淪浹，巍科顯爵，頓天網以羅英俊，民之秀者，無不觀國光而賓王廷矣。
entries.en: By the mid-dynasty, in an age of peace, civilization had spread to every corner. Grand examinations and high offices cast the great net to gather the gifted, and none of the finest men among the people failed to behold the nation's splendor and present themselves at the royal court.
entries.literal: When the middle period enjoyed peace, culture penetrated everywhere; eminent degrees and lofty ranks cast the great net to gather the talented—none of the outstanding among the people failed to behold the nation's glory and present themselves at the royal court.

entries.zh: 其抱瑰材，蘊積學，槁形泉石，絕意當世者，靡得而稱焉。
entries.en: Those who held rare gifts, hoarded learning, wasted their bodies among springs and stones, and turned their backs on the world could scarcely be named at all.
entries.literal: Those who embraced rare talent, stored up learning, withered their forms among springs and rocks, and cut off all concern for the age—there was scarcely any way to name them.

entries.zh: 由是觀之，世道升降之端，系所遭逢，豈非其時為之哉。
entries.en: Seen in this light, whether the age rises or falls turns on what fortune brings—was it not the times that shaped it?
entries.literal: Viewed thus, the turning points in the rise and fall of the world depend on what one encounters—is it not the times that make it so?

entries.zh: 凡徵聘所及，文學行誼可稱者，已散見諸傳。
entries.en: All those reached by summons and appointment whose learning and conduct were worthy of note have already appeared in scattered biographies elsewhere.
entries.literal: All those reached by summons and recruitment whose literary accomplishment and conduct were praiseworthy have already been scattered through various biographies.

entries.zh: 茲取貞節超邁者數人，作《隱逸傳》。
entries.en: Here several men of steadfast integrity and extraordinary character are gathered to form the "Biographies of Recluses."
entries.literal: Here several persons of steadfast integrity and transcendent character are selected to compose the "Biographies of Recluses."

entries.zh: 楊恆，字本初，諸暨人。
entries.en: Yang Heng, courtesy name Benchu, was a native of Zhuji.
entries.literal: Yang Heng, styled Benchu, was a man of Zhuji.

entries.zh: 外族方氏建義塾，館四方游學士，恆幼往受諸經，輒領其旨要。
entries.en: His mother's clan, the Fang family, built a charity school and housed traveling scholars from every quarter. Heng went there as a boy to study the classics and always grasped their essentials at once.
entries.literal: His mother's clan, the Fang, built a charity school and housed traveling scholars from all quarters. Heng went there in youth to study the classics and always grasped their essentials.

entries.zh: 文峻潔，有聲郡邑間。
entries.en: His writing was austere and refined, and his reputation spread throughout the district.
entries.literal: His writing was severe and pure, and he had a reputation throughout the district.

entries.zh: 浦江鄭氏延為師，閱十年退居白鹿山，戴棕冠，披羊裘，帶經耕煙雨間，嘯歌自樂，因自號白鹿生。
