entries.en: The Zheng family of Pujiang invited him to serve as their teacher. After ten years he retired to Bailu Mountain, wore a palm-fiber cap and sheepskin cloak, carried the classics while farming amid mist and rain, and sang for his own delight. He styled himself the Man of White Deer.
entries.literal: The Zheng of Pujiang invited him as teacher. After ten years he retired to Bailu Mountain, wore a palm-fiber cap and sheepskin cloak, carried the classics while farming amid mist and rain, sang and rejoiced by himself, and styled himself the Man of White Deer.

entries.zh: 太祖既下浙東，命欒鳳知州事。
entries.en: After the Taizu had pacified eastern Zhejiang, he appointed Luan Feng to administer the prefecture.
entries.literal: After the Taizu had taken eastern Zhejiang, he appointed Luan Feng to administer the prefecture.

entries.zh: 鳳請為州學師，恆固讓不起。
entries.en: Feng asked him to serve as teacher of the prefectural school, but Heng firmly declined and would not accept.
entries.literal: Feng asked him to be teacher of the prefectural school, but Heng firmly declined and would not rise to serve.

entries.zh: 鳳乃命州中子弟即家問道。
entries.en: Feng then ordered the young men of the prefecture to come to Heng's home to study the Way.
entries.literal: Feng then ordered the young men of the prefecture to seek the Way at his home.

entries.zh: 政有缺失，輒貽書咨訪。
entries.en: Whenever governance fell short, Feng would send letters seeking his counsel.
entries.literal: When governance had shortcomings, he would send letters to consult him.

entries.zh: 後唐鐸知紹興，欲辟起之，復固辭。
entries.en: Later, when Tang Duo governed Shaoxing, he wished to summon Heng to office, but Heng again firmly declined.
entries.literal: Later Tang Duo governed Shaoxing and wished to summon him to office, but he again firmly declined.

entries.zh: 宋濂之為學士也，擬薦為國子師，聞不受州郡辟命，乃已。
entries.en: When Song Lian became a Hanlin academician, he planned to recommend Heng as teacher of the National University, but hearing that he would accept no appointment from prefecture or district, he let the matter drop.
entries.literal: When Song Lian became a Hanlin academician, he planned to recommend Heng as teacher of the National University, but hearing that he would not accept summons from prefectures and districts, he dropped the matter.

entries.zh: 恆性醇篤，與人語，出肺肝相示。
entries.en: Heng was by nature sincere and earnest; in conversation he laid bare his heart without reserve.
entries.literal: Heng's nature was sincere and earnest; in speaking with others he laid bare heart and liver.

entries.zh: 事稍乖名義，輒峻言指斥。
entries.en: Whenever a matter fell even slightly short of right principle, he would rebuke it in stern words.
entries.literal: When matters slightly violated right principle, he would sternly rebuke them in speech.

entries.zh: 家無儋石，而臨財甚介，鄉人奉為楷法焉。
entries.en: His household held scarcely a bushel of grain, yet he was scrupulous in the face of wealth, and the villagers took him as their standard of conduct.
entries.literal: His household had not a dan of grain, yet facing wealth he was very scrupulous; the villagers took him as their model.

entries.zh: 楊引，吉水人。
entries.en: Yang Yin was a native of Jishui.
entries.literal: Yang Yin, a man of Jishui.

entries.zh: 好學能詩文，為宋濂、陶安所稱。
entries.en: He loved learning and was accomplished in poetry and prose, and was praised by Song Lian and Tao An.
entries.literal: Fond of learning and skilled in poetry and prose, he was praised by Song Lian and Tao An.

entries.zh: 駙馬都尉陸賢從受學，入朝，舉止端雅。
entries.en: The imperial son-in-law Lu Xian studied under him, and when Xian entered court his bearing was dignified and refined.
entries.literal: The imperial son-in-law Lu Xian studied under him; when he entered court his bearing was dignified and refined.

entries.zh: 太祖喜，問誰教者，賢以引對，立召見，賜食。
entries.en: The Taizu was pleased and asked who had taught him. Xian named Yin, and Yin was immediately summoned to audience and given a meal.
entries.literal: The Taizu was pleased and asked who had taught him. Xian named Yin in reply, and Yin was immediately summoned and given food.

entries.zh: 他日，賢以褻服見，引太息曰：「是其心易我，不可久居此矣。」
entries.en: Another day Xian came to see him in informal dress. Yin sighed deeply and said: "His heart has turned away from me—I cannot remain here much longer."
entries.literal: Another day Xian came to see him in informal dress. Yin sighed deeply and said: "His heart has changed toward me—I cannot remain here long."

entries.zh: 復以纂修征，亦不就。
entries.en: When he was summoned again to join the compilation project, he again refused.
entries.literal: He was again summoned for compilation work, but again would not go.

entries.zh: 其教學者，先操履而後文藝。
entries.en: In teaching his students, he put conduct before literary accomplishment.
entries.literal: In teaching his students, he put conduct first and literary accomplishment after.

entries.zh: 嘗揭《論語鄉黨》篇示人曰：「吾教自有養生術，安事偃仰吐納為。」
entries.en: He once displayed the Xiangdang chapter of the Analects to others and said: "My teaching has its own way of nurturing life—why bother with breathing exercises and postures?"
entries.literal: He once displayed the Xiangdang chapter of the Analects to others and said: "My teaching has its own method of nurturing life—why bother with lying down and breathing exercises?"

entries.zh: 乃節飲食，時動息，迄老視聽不衰。
entries.en: He regulated his food and drink and kept regular movement and rest, and to the end of his life his sight and hearing never failed.
entries.literal: He then regulated food and drink and kept regular movement and rest; to old age his sight and hearing did not decline.

entries.zh: 既歿，安福劉球稱其學探道原，文范後世，去就出處，卓然有陶潛、徐穉之風。
entries.en: After his death, Liu Qiu of Anfu praised his learning for probing the origin of the Way, his writing as a model for later ages, and his conduct in withdrawal and emergence as bearing the unmistakable spirit of Tao Qian and Xu Zhi.
entries.literal: After his death Liu Qiu of Anfu praised his learning as probing the origin of the Way, his writing as a model for later ages, and his withdrawal and emergence as markedly bearing the spirit of Tao Qian and Xu Zhi.

entries.zh: 倪瓚，字元鎮，無錫人也。
entries.en: Ni Zan, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was a native of Wuxi.
entries.literal: Ni Zan, styled Yuanzhen, was a man of Wuxi.

entries.zh: 家雄於貲，工詩，善書畫。
entries.en: His family was immensely wealthy. He was accomplished in poetry and excelled at calligraphy and painting.
entries.literal: His family was wealthy; he was skilled in poetry and excelled at calligraphy and painting.

entries.zh: 四方名士日至其門。
entries.en: Renowned men of letters from every quarter came to his door each day.
entries.literal: Famous scholars from all quarters came daily to his door.

entries.zh: 所居有閣曰清閟，幽迥絕塵。
entries.en: His residence held a pavilion called Qingbi, secluded and utterly removed from the dust of the world.
entries.literal: In his residence was a pavilion called Qingbi, secluded and far removed from the dust of the world.

entries.zh: 藏書數千卷，皆手自勘定。
entries.en: He kept several thousand volumes in his library, every one collated by his own hand.
entries.literal: He kept several thousand volumes of books, all collated by his own hand.

entries.zh: 古鼎法書，名琴奇畫，陳列左右。
entries.en: Ancient bronzes, masterworks of calligraphy, famous zithers, and extraordinary paintings were arrayed all around him.
entries.literal: Ancient tripods, model calligraphy, famous zithers, and rare paintings were displayed on either side.

entries.zh: 四時卉木，縈繞其外，高木修篁，蔚然深秀，故自號雲林居士。
entries.en: Flowers and trees of every season encircled the pavilion outside, and tall timber and slender bamboo rose in lush, deep beauty. He therefore styled himself the Recluse of Cloud Forest.
entries.literal: Flowers and trees of the four seasons encircled it outside; tall trees and tall bamboo stood lush and deep in beauty, and so he styled himself the Recluse of Cloud Forest.

entries.zh: 時與客觴詠其中。
entries.en: He would often drink and compose poetry there with his guests.
entries.literal: From time to time he drank and composed poetry there with guests.

entries.zh: 為人有潔癖，盥濯不離手。
entries.en: By nature he was fastidiously clean and never stopped washing his hands.
entries.literal: By nature he had an obsession with cleanliness and never left off washing his hands.

entries.zh: 俗客造廬，比去，必洗滌其處。
entries.en: When common visitors came to his lodge, he would wash wherever they had sat as soon as they left.
entries.literal: When vulgar guests visited his lodge, as soon as they left he would wash the place where they had been.

entries.zh: 求縑素者踵至，瓚亦時應之。
entries.en: Those seeking silk scrolls for his paintings came in an endless stream, and Zan would sometimes oblige them.
entries.literal: Those seeking silk for painting came one after another, and Zan would sometimes oblige them.

entries.zh: 至正初，海內無事，忽散其貲給親故，人咸怪之。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Zhizheng era, when the realm was at peace, he suddenly gave away his wealth to relatives and friends, and everyone thought it strange.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Zhizheng era, when the realm was at peace, he suddenly distributed his wealth to relatives and friends, and all thought it strange.

entries.zh: 未幾兵興，富家悉被禍，而瓚扁舟箬笠，往來震澤、三泖間，獨不罹患。
entries.en: Before long warfare broke out, and wealthy families were ruined one after another. Zan alone, in a small boat and bamboo hat, moved between Lake Zhen and the Three Marshes and suffered no harm.
entries.literal: Before long warfare arose; wealthy families all suffered disaster, while Zan in a small boat and bamboo hat traveled between Lake Zhen and the Three Marshes alone untouched by calamity.

entries.zh: 張士誠累欲鉤致之，逃漁舟以免。
entries.en: Zhang Shicheng repeatedly tried to lure him into service, but he escaped aboard fishing boats to avoid capture.
entries.literal: Zhang Shicheng repeatedly wished to lure him in, but he escaped aboard fishing boats to avoid capture.

entries.zh: 其弟士信以幣乞畫，瓚又斥去。
entries.en: His younger brother Shixin sent gifts begging for a painting, and Zan drove him away once more.
entries.literal: His younger brother Shixin sent gifts begging for a painting, and Zan drove him away again.

entries.zh: 士信恚，他日從賓客游湖上，聞異香出葭葦間，疑為瓚也，物色漁舟中，果得之。
entries.en: Shixin was furious. One day, while touring the lake with his guests, he caught a strange fragrance rising from the reeds, suspected it was Zan, searched the fishing boats, and found him.
entries.literal: Shixin was resentful. Another day, while touring the lake with guests, he caught a strange fragrance from among the reeds, suspected it was Zan, searched the fishing boats, and indeed found him.

entries.zh: 抶幾斃，終無一言。
entries.en: They beat him nearly to death, yet he never uttered a word.
entries.literal: He was beaten nearly to death, yet in the end spoke not a word.

entries.zh: 及吳平，瓚年老矣，黃冠野服，混跡編氓。
entries.en: When Wu was pacified, Zan was already old. In a Daoist cap and rustic dress he mingled among the common people.
entries.literal: When Wu was pacified, Zan was already old. In Daoist cap and rustic dress he mingled among the common people.

entries.zh: 洪武七年卒，年七十四。
entries.en: He died in the seventh year of Hongwu, at the age of seventy-four.
entries.literal: He died in the seventh year of Hongwu, aged seventy-four.

entries.zh: 徐舫，字方舟，桐廬人。
entries.en: Xu Fang, courtesy name Fangzhou, was a native of Tonglu.
entries.literal: Xu Fang, styled Fangzhou, was a man of Tonglu.

entries.zh: 幼輕俠，好擊劍、走馬、蹴踘。
entries.en: In youth he was rakish, fond of swordplay, horse-racing, and cuju.
entries.literal: In youth he was rakish, fond of swordplay, horse-racing, and cuju.

entries.zh: 既而悔之，習科舉業。
entries.en: Later he repented of this and took up examination studies.
entries.literal: Later he regretted this and studied for the civil examinations.

entries.zh: 已，復棄去，學為歌詩。
entries.en: Then he abandoned that as well and turned to writing songs and poetry.
entries.literal: Then he abandoned that again and learned to write songs and poetry.

entries.zh: 睦故多詩人，唐有方干、徐凝、李頻、施肩吾，宋有高師魯、滕元秀，號睦州詩派，舫悉取步聚之。
entries.en: Mu had long produced many poets. In the Tang there were Fang Gan, Xu Ning, Li Pin, and Shi Jianwu; in the Song, Gao Shilu and Teng Yuanxiu—the so-called Muzhou school of poetry—and Fang took them all as models.
entries.literal: Mu had long had many poets: in Tang, Fang Gan, Xu Ning, Li Pin, and Shi Jianwu; in Song, Gao Shilu and Teng Yuanxiu—the so-called Muzhou school of poetry—and Fang took them all as models to follow.

entries.zh: 既乃游四方，交其名士，詩益工。
entries.en: He then traveled widely, befriended celebrated men, and his poetry grew ever more accomplished.
entries.literal: Then he traveled the four quarters, befriended famous men, and his poetry grew more accomplished.

entries.zh: 行省參政蘇天爵將薦之，舫笑曰：「吾詩人耳，可羈以章紱哉。」
entries.en: Su Tianjue, provincial administration commissioner, was about to recommend him. Fang laughed and said: "I am only a poet—how can you bind me with official robes and regalia?"
entries.literal: Su Tianjue, provincial administration commissioner, was about to recommend him. Fang laughed and said: "I am but a poet—how can I be bound with official regalia?"

entries.zh: 竟避去。
entries.en: In the end he slipped away and avoided appointment.
entries.literal: In the end he avoided it and left.

entries.zh: 築室江皋，日苦吟於雲煙出沒間，翛然若與世隔，因自號滄江散人。
entries.en: He built a house on the riverbank and spent his days composing poetry amid drifting mist and cloud, detached as if cut off from the world. He therefore styled himself the Wanderer of the Cang River.
entries.literal: He built a house on the riverbank and daily labored at poetry amid clouds appearing and vanishing, detached as if cut off from the world, and so styled himself the Wanderer of the Cang River.

entries.zh: 宋濂、劉基、葉琛、章溢之赴召也，舟溯桐江，忽有人黃冠鹿裘立江上，招基而笑，且語侵之。
entries.en: When Song Lian, Liu Ji, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi were traveling to answer the imperial summons, their boat went up the Tong River. Suddenly a man in a yellow cap and deerskin cloak stood on the bank, beckoned to Ji with a laugh, and spoke to him in mocking tones.
entries.literal: When Song Lian, Liu Ji, Ye Chen, and Zhang Yi were going to answer the summons, their boat went up the Tong River. Suddenly a man in yellow cap and deerskin cloak stood on the riverbank, beckoned to Ji and laughed, and his words were cutting.

entries.zh: 基望見，急延入舟中。
entries.en: Ji saw him from afar and hastily invited him aboard.
entries.literal: Ji saw him from afar and hastily invited him into the boat.

entries.zh: 琛、溢競歡謔，各取冠服服之，欲載上黟川，其人不可乃止。
entries.en: Chen and Yi joined in merry banter, each took cap and robe and dressed him in them, and wanted to carry him upriver to Yichuan, but the man refused and they desisted.
entries.literal: Chen and Yi vied in merry banter, each took cap and robe and dressed him in them, and wished to carry him up to Yichuan, but the man would not agree and they stopped.

entries.zh: 濂初未相識，以問。
entries.en: Lian did not know him at first and asked who he was.
entries.literal: Lian did not know him at first and asked who he was.

entries.zh: 基曰：「此徐方舟也。」
entries.en: Ji said: "This is Xu Fangzhou."
entries.literal: Ji said: "This is Xu Fangzhou."

entries.zh: 濂因起共歡笑，酌酒而別。
entries.en: Lian then rose and joined in laughter, poured wine, and they parted.
entries.literal: Lian then rose and joined in laughter, poured wine, and they parted.

entries.zh: 舫詩有《瑤林》、《滄江》二集。
entries.en: Fang's poetry survives in two collections, Yaolin and Cangjiang.
entries.literal: Fang's poetry was collected in two works, Yaolin and Cangjiang.

entries.zh: 年六十八，丙午春，卒於家。
entries.en: He was sixty-eight years old when he died at home in the spring of the bingwu year.
entries.literal: Aged sixty-eight, in the spring of the bingwu year, he died at home.

entries.zh: 吳海，字朝宗，閩縣人。
entries.en: Wu Hai, courtesy name Chaozong, was a native of Min County.
entries.literal: Wu Hai, styled Chaozong, was a man of Min County.

entries.zh: 元季以學行稱。
entries.en: In the late Yuan he was famed for learning and conduct.
entries.literal: In the late Yuan he was famed for learning and conduct.

entries.zh: 值四方盜起，絕意仕進。
entries.en: When bandits rose throughout the realm, he abandoned all thought of an official career.
entries.literal: When bandits rose in all quarters, he utterly abandoned any wish to advance in office.

entries.zh: 洪武初，守臣欲薦諸朝，力辭免。
entries.en: In the early Hongwu period the local officials wished to recommend him to court, but he firmly declined.
entries.literal: In the early Hongwu period the local officials wished to recommend him to court, but he firmly declined and was excused.

entries.zh: 既而徵詣史局，復力辭。
entries.en: Later he was summoned to the historiography bureau and again firmly declined.
entries.literal: Later he was summoned to the historiography bureau and again firmly declined.

entries.zh: 嘗言：「楊、墨、釋、老，聖道之賊，管、商、申、韓，治道之賊，稗官野乘，正史之賊，支詞艷說，文章之賊。
entries.en: He once said: "Yang Zhu, Mozi, Buddhism, and Daoism are enemies of the sage's Way; Guan Zhong, Shang Yang, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei are enemies of good governance; unofficial histories and wild records are enemies of orthodox history; florid and seductive writings are enemies of true literature.
entries.literal: He once said: "Yang Zhu, Mozi, Buddhism, and Daoism are thieves of the sage's Way; Guan Zhong, Shang Yang, Shen Buhai, and Han Fei are thieves of the way of governance; unofficial histories and wild records are thieves of the orthodox histories; florid words and seductive writings are thieves of literature.

entries.zh: 上之人，宜敕通經大臣，會諸儒定其品目，頒之天下，民間非此不得輒藏，坊市不得輒粥。
entries.en: Those in authority should order great ministers versed in the classics to assemble the Confucian scholars, fix the approved categories of books, and promulgate them throughout the realm, so that the people may not keep what is not on the list and markets may not sell what is forbidden.
entries.literal: Those above should order great ministers versed in the classics to assemble the Confucians, fix categories of books, promulgate them throughout the realm, forbid the people to keep what is not on the list, and forbid markets to sell them.

entries.zh: 如是數年，學者生長不涉異聞，其於養德育才，豈曰小補。」
entries.en: If this were done for several years, scholars would grow up untouched by heterodox learning. In nurturing virtue and forming talent, would this not be a great benefit?"
entries.literal: If this were done for several years, scholars would grow up untouched by heterodox learning—in nurturing virtue and forming talent, would this not be a great benefit?"

entries.zh: 因著書一編曰《書禍》，以發明之。
entries.en: He therefore wrote a book in one fascicle called Writings as Calamity to expound this view.
entries.literal: He therefore wrote a book in one fascicle called Writings as Calamity to expound this.

entries.zh: 與永福王翰善。
entries.en: He was on good terms with Wang Han of Yongfu.
entries.literal: He was on good terms with Wang Han of Yongfu.

entries.zh: 翰嘗仕元，海數勸之死，翰果自裁。
entries.en: Han had once served the Yuan. Hai repeatedly urged him to take his own life, and Han did so.
entries.literal: Han had once served the Yuan; Hai repeatedly urged him to die, and Han indeed took his own life.

entries.zh: 海教養其子偁，卒底成立。
entries.en: Hai raised and educated Han's son Cheng, who in the end grew into a fully accomplished man.
entries.literal: Hai taught and raised his son Cheng, who in the end was fully established.

entries.zh: 平居虛懷樂善，有規過者，欣然立改，因顏其齋曰聞過。
entries.en: In daily life he was open-minded and delighted in doing good. When someone pointed out a fault, he gladly corrected it at once, and named his study Hearing Fault.
entries.literal: In ordinary life he was open-minded and delighted in goodness; when someone corrected his faults he gladly changed at once, and so he named his studio Hearing Fault.

entries.zh: 為文嚴整典雅，一歸諸理，後學咸宗仰之。
entries.en: His writing was austere, orderly, and elegant, always grounded in principle, and later students all looked up to him as a model.
entries.literal: His writing was severe, orderly, and elegant, all returning to principle; later students all looked up to him as a model.

entries.zh: 有《聞過齋集》行世。
entries.en: His collected works, the Hearing Fault Studio Collection, circulated in his day.
entries.literal: His collected works from the Hearing Fault Studio circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 孫一元，字太初，不知何許人，問其邑里，曰：「我秦人也。」
entries.en: Sun Yiyuan, courtesy name Taichu, was of unknown origin. When asked where he came from, he said: "I am a man of Qin."
entries.literal: Sun Yiyuan, styled Taichu, was of unknown origin; asked about his native place, he said: "I am a man of Qin."

entries.zh: 嘗棲太白之巔，故號太白山人。
entries.en: He once lived on the summit of Mount Taibai and therefore styled himself the Man of Taibai Mountain.
entries.literal: He once dwelt on the summit of Taibai and therefore styled himself the Man of Taibai Mountain.

entries.zh: 或曰安化王宗人，王坐不軌誅，故變姓名避難也。
entries.en: Some say he was a clansman of the Prince of Anhua. When the prince was executed for sedition, he changed his name to escape persecution.
entries.literal: Some say he was a clansman of the Prince of Anhua; the prince was executed for sedition, and so he changed his name to avoid disaster.

entries.zh: 一元姿性絕人，善為詩，風儀秀朗，蹤跡奇譎，烏巾白帢，攜鐵笛鶴瓢，遍游中原，東逾齊、魯，南涉江、淮，歷荊抵吳越，所至賦詩，談神仙，論當世事，往往傾其座人。
entries.en: Yiyuan's gifts were extraordinary. He was skilled in poetry, his bearing elegant and bright, his tracks strange and uncanny. In a black cap and white headcloth, carrying an iron flute and a wine gourd, he traveled throughout the central plains, east beyond Qi and Lu, south across the Yangtze and Huai, through Jing to Wu and Yue. Wherever he went he composed poetry, spoke of immortals, and discussed affairs of the age, often overwhelming everyone seated with him.
entries.literal: Yiyuan's natural gifts were extraordinary; he was skilled in poetry, his bearing elegant and bright, his tracks strange and uncanny. In black cap and white headcloth, carrying an iron flute and a gourd, he traveled throughout the central plains, east beyond Qi and Lu, south across the Yangtze and Huai, through Jing to Wu and Yue. Wherever he went he composed poetry, spoke of immortals, and discussed affairs of the age, often overwhelming those seated with him.

entries.zh: 鉛山費宏罷相，訪之杭州南屏山，值其晝寢，就臥內與語。
entries.en: Fei Hong of Qianshan, having left the chancellorship, visited him at Nanping Mountain in Hangzhou. Finding him asleep in broad daylight, Hong spoke with him there in his bed.
entries.literal: Fei Hong of Qianshan, having left the chancellorship, visited him at Nanping Mountain in Hangzhou, found him asleep by day, and spoke with him inside his bed.

entries.zh: 送之及門，了不酬答。
entries.en: When Yiyuan escorted him to the door, he made no reply at all.
entries.literal: When Hong saw him to the door, he made no reply at all.

entries.zh: 宏出語人曰：「吾一生未嘗見此人。」
entries.en: Hong went out and told others: "In all my life I have never met a man like this."
entries.literal: Hong went out and told others: "In all my life I have never met a man like this."

entries.zh: 時劉麟以知府罷歸，龍霓以僉事謝政，並客湖州，與郡人故御史陵昆善，而長興吳珫隱居好客，三人者並主於其家。
entries.en: At the time Liu Lin had returned home after leaving office as prefect, and Long Ni had retired from his post as commissioner. Both were staying in Huzhou and were friendly with the former censor Ling Kun of the prefecture, while Wu Qiong of Changxing lived in seclusion and loved to entertain guests. The three all lodged as guests in Qiong's home.
entries.literal: At the time Liu Lin had returned home after leaving office as prefect, and Long Ni had retired from his post as commissioner; both were guests in Huzhou. They were friendly with the former censor Ling Kun of the prefecture, while Wu Qiong of Changxing lived in seclusion and loved guests. The three all presided as hosts in his home.

entries.zh: 珫因招一元入社，稱「苕溪五隱」。
entries.en: Qiong therefore invited Yiyuan into their circle and called them the "Five Recluses of Tiaoxi."
entries.literal: Qiong therefore invited Yiyuan into their society and called them the "Five Recluses of Tiaoxi."

entries.zh: 一元買田溪上，將老焉。
entries.en: Yiyuan bought fields beside the stream and planned to grow old there.
entries.literal: Yiyuan bought fields by the stream and planned to grow old there.

entries.zh: 舉人施侃雅善一元，妻以妻妹張氏，生一女而卒，年止三十七。
entries.en: The juren Shi Kan was on excellent terms with Yiyuan and gave him his wife's younger sister, née Zhang, in marriage. She bore a daughter and then died. Yiyuan was only thirty-seven.
entries.literal: The juren Shi Kan was on excellent terms with Yiyuan and gave him his wife's younger sister, née Zhang, in marriage. She bore a daughter and then died; Yiyuan was only thirty-seven.

entries.zh: 珫等葬之道場山。
entries.en: Qiong and the others buried him on Mount Daochang.
entries.literal: Qiong and the others buried him on Mount Daochang.

entries.zh: 張介福 倪瓚 徐舫 楊恆 陳洄 楊引 吳海 劉閔 楊黼 孫一元 沈周 陳繼儒
entries.en: Zhang Jiefu, Ni Zan, Xu Fang, Yang Heng, Chen Hui, Yang Yin, Wu Hai, Liu Min, Yang Fu, Sun Yiyuan, Shen Zhou, and Chen Jiru
entries.literal: Zhang Jiefu, Ni Zan, Xu Fang, Yang Heng, Chen Hui, Yang Yin, Wu Hai, Liu Min, Yang Fu, Sun Yiyuan, Shen Zhou, Chen Jiru

entries.zh: 瑾，初名陳蕪。
entries.en: Jin's original name was Chen Wu.
entries.literal: Jin's original name was Chen Wu.

entries.zh: 宣宗為皇太孫時，朝夕給事。
entries.en: When the future Xuanzong was still heir apparent as imperial grandson, Jin attended him from morning till night.
entries.literal: When the future Xuanzong was crown prince grandson, he served him morning and evening.

entries.zh: 及即位，賜姓名。
entries.en: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, he bestowed on him the name Wang Jin.
entries.literal: When he came to the throne, he gave him a new name.

entries.zh: 從征漢王高煦還，參預四方兵事，賞賚累巨萬，數賜銀記曰「忠肝義膽」，曰「金貂貴客」，曰「忠誠自勵」，曰「心跡雙清」。
entries.en: After the campaign against the Prince of Han he took part in military affairs throughout the realm, amassed rewards in the tens of thousands, and received silver tallies again and again bearing such inscriptions as "Loyal Liver and Righteous Gall," "Golden Marten and Noble Guest," "Loyal Self-Encouragement," and "Heart and Conduct Both Pure."
entries.literal: After returning from the campaign against the Prince of Han, Gao Xu, he took part in military affairs in every quarter, received rewards amounting to many tens of thousands, and was repeatedly given silver tallies inscribed "Loyal Liver and Righteous Gall," "Golden Marten and Noble Guest," "Loyal Self-Encouragement," and "Heart and Conduct Both Pure."

entries.zh: 又賜以兩宮人，官其養子王椿。
entries.en: He was also given two palace women, and his adopted son Wang Chun was granted an official post.
entries.literal: He was also given two palace women, and his adopted son Wang Chun was made an official.

entries.zh: 其受寵眷，英、弘莫逮也。
entries.en: In imperial favor neither Ying nor Hong could rival him.
entries.literal: In the favor he received, neither Ying nor Hong could match him.

entries.zh: 當是時，瑾權擅天下，威福任情。
entries.en: In those days Jin wielded sole power over the empire, dispensing favor and punishment entirely as he pleased.
entries.literal: At that time Jin held power over the whole realm and dispensed favor and punishment as he wished.

entries.zh: 有罪人溺水死，乃坐御史匡翼之罪。
entries.en: When a criminal drowned, the censor Kuang Yizhi was punished for it.
entries.literal: When a criminal drowned and died, the blame was placed on the censor Kuang Yizhi.

entries.zh: 嘗求學士吳儼賄，不得，又聽都御史劉宇讒，怒御史楊南金，乃以大計外吏奏中，落二人職。
entries.en: He once demanded a bribe from academician Wu Yan and did not get it; then, heeding the slander of Grand Censor Liu Yu, he turned on censor Yang Nanjin and, in the annual evaluation of outside officials, had both men removed from office.
entries.literal: He once sought a bribe from the scholar Wu Yan and got none; then, listening to the slander of Grand Censor Liu Yu, he became angry with the censor Yang Nanjin and used the annual evaluation of outside officials to have the two of them removed from office.

entries.zh: 授播州土司楊斌為四川按察使。
entries.en: He appointed Yang Bin, a native chieftain of Bozhou, surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.
entries.literal: He appointed Yang Bin, a native chief of Bozhou, as Sichuan surveillance commissioner.

entries.zh: 令奴婿閭潔督山東學政。
entries.en: He put his son-in-law Lü Jie in charge of the school administration of Shandong.
entries.literal: He ordered his son-in-law Lü Jie to supervise the school administration of Shandong.

entries.zh: 公侯勛戚以下，莫敢鈞禮，每私謁，相率跪拜。
entries.en: From dukes, marquises, meritorious nobles, and imperial in-laws downward, none dared insist on equal courtesy; whenever they paid a private visit, they knelt and bowed in succession.
entries.literal: Dukes, marquises, meritorious officers, and relatives by marriage all dared not insist on equal courtesy; whenever they paid a private visit, they all knelt and bowed in turn.

entries.zh: 章奏先具紅揭投瑾，號紅本，然後上通政司，號白本，皆稱劉太監而不名。
entries.en: Memorials had first to be prepared on red paper and submitted to Jin—the "red memorials"—and only afterward sent on to the Directorate of Communications as "white memorials"; everywhere he was addressed as Eunuch Liu, never by name.
entries.literal: Memorials had first to be prepared as red slips and submitted to Jin, known as the red memorials; only then were they sent on to the Court of State Affairs as white memorials. In all cases he was called Eunuch Liu and not by name.

entries.zh: 都察院奏讞誤名瑾，瑾怒詈之，都御史屠滽率屬跪謝乃已。
entries.en: When the Censorate named Jin in a judgment report by mistake, he flew into a rage and cursed them; Grand Censor Tu Yong and his subordinates had to kneel and apologize before he would let the matter drop.
entries.literal: When the Censorate referred to Jin by name in a judgment report, Jin cursed them in anger, and Grand Censor Tu Yong and his subordinates had to kneel and apologize before he stopped.

entries.zh: 遣使察核邊倉，都御史周南、張鼐、馬中錫、湯全、劉憲，布政以下官孫祿、冒政、方矩、華福、金獻民、劉遜、郭緒、張翼，郎中劉繹、王藎等，並以赦前罪，下獄追補邊粟，憲至瘐死。
entries.en: He sent envoys to audit the border granaries, and Grand Censors Zhou Nan, Zhang Nai, Ma Zhongxi, Tang Quan, and Liu Xian, along with provincial administrators Sun Lu, Mao Zheng, Fang Ju, Hua Fu, Jin Xianmin, Liu Xun, Guo Xu, Zhang Yi, and secretaries Liu Yi and Wang Jin, were all imprisoned on pre-amnesty offenses and forced to make restitution in border grain; Liu Xian died of illness in prison.
entries.literal: He sent envoys to inspect the border granaries, and Grand Censors Zhou Nan, Zhang Nai, Ma Zhongxi, Tang Quan, and Liu Xian, along with the provincial officials Sun Lu, Mao Zheng, Fang Ju, Hua Fu, Jin Xianmin, Liu Xun, Guo Xu, Zhang Yi, and the ministry officials Liu Yi, Wang Jin, and others, were all imprisoned for crimes supposedly covered by amnesty and made to repay border grain; Xian died in prison of illness.

entries.zh: 又察鹽課，杖巡鹽御史王潤，逮前運使寧舉、楊奇等。
entries.en: He also inspected the salt revenues, flogged salt censor Wang Run, and arrested former transport commissioners Ning Ju, Yang Qi, and others.
entries.literal: He also inspected the salt revenues, flogged the salt-surveillance censor Wang Run, and arrested the former transport commissioners Ning Ju and Yang Qi and others.

entries.zh: 察內甲字庫，謫尚書王佐以下百七十三人。
entries.en: He inspected the Inner Armor and Character Treasury and demoted one hundred seventy-three officials, including Minister Wang Zuo.
entries.literal: He inspected the Inner Armor Character Treasury and demoted 173 people, including Minister Wang Zuo.

entries.zh: 復創罰米法，嘗忤瑾者，皆擿發輸邊。
entries.en: He revived the penalty of grain fines as well; anyone who had ever offended Jin was hunted out and made to deliver grain to the border.
entries.literal: He also invented the penalty of grain fines again; anyone who had offended Jin was all exposed and sent to the frontier.

entries.zh: 故尚書雍泰、馬文升、劉大夏、韓文、許進，都御史楊一清、李進、王忠，侍郎張縉，給事中趙士賢，任良弼，御史張津，陳順、喬恕、聶賢、曹來旬等數十人悉破家，死者繫其妻孥。
entries.en: Thus former ministers Yun Tai, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, and Xu Jin; Grand Censors Yang Yiqing, Li Jin, and Wang Zhong; Vice Minister Zhang Jin; assistant secretaries Zhao Shixian and Ren Liangbi; censors Zhang Jin, Chen Shun, Qiao Shou, Nie Xian, Cao Laixun, and dozens more were ruined; where the accused died, their wives and children were held liable as well.
entries.literal: Thus ministers such as Yun Tai, Ma Wensheng, Liu Daxia, Han Wen, and Xu Jin; Grand Censors Yang Yiqing, Li Jin, and Wang Zhong; Vice Ministers Zhang Jin; Assistant Secretaries Zhao Shixian and Ren Liangbi; censors Zhang Jin, Chen Shun, Qiao Shou, Nie Xian, Cao Laixun, and dozens of others all lost their homes, and those who died left their wives and children bound up with them.

entries.zh: 明太祖既定江左，鑒前代之失，置宦者不及百人。
entries.en: Once the Ming founder had consolidated his hold on the lower Yangzi, he studied the mistakes of earlier dynasties and kept the number of eunuchs to under a hundred.
entries.literal: After the Ming founder had secured the lower Yangzi, he took warning from the failings of earlier dynasties and kept fewer than a hundred eunuchs.

entries.zh: 迨末年頒《祖訓》，乃定為十有二監及各司局，稍稱備員矣。
entries.en: By the end of his reign, when he promulgated the Ancestral Injunctions, the establishment was fixed at twelve directorates and the various bureaus—barely enough to count as a full complement.
entries.literal: By the end of his reign, when he issued the Ancestral Injunctions, they were fixed at twelve directorates and various offices, and could only just be said to be fully staffed.

entries.zh: 然定制，不得兼外臣文武銜，不得御外臣冠服，官無過四品，月米一石，衣食於內庭。
entries.en: Yet the standing regulations barred them from holding concurrent civil or military titles in the outer administration, from wearing the headgear and robes of outer ministers, and from rising above the fourth rank; they received one picul of rice a month and were clothed and fed within the inner palace.
entries.literal: But the established regulations forbade them from holding civilian or military titles outside the inner court, from wearing the hats and robes of outer ministers, and limited their rank to no higher than the fourth; they received one dan of rice a month and were housed and fed in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 嘗鐫鐵牌置宮門曰：「內臣不得干預政事，預者斬。」
entries.en: He once had an iron plaque engraved and placed at the palace gate, saying: "Inner servants must not interfere in government affairs; anyone who does so shall be executed."
entries.literal: He once had an iron plaque engraved and placed at the palace gate, saying: "Inner servants must not interfere in government affairs; anyone who does so shall be executed."

entries.zh: 敕諸司不得與文移往來。
entries.en: He also ordered the various ministries not to exchange official correspondence with them.
entries.literal: He also ordered the various offices not to exchange written documents with them.

entries.zh: 有老閹供事久，一日從容語及政事，帝大怒，即日斥還鄉。
entries.en: An old eunuch who had long served at court once spoke casually about state affairs; the emperor flew into a rage and sent him home that very day.
entries.literal: There was an old eunuch who had long served the court; one day he spoke casually about government affairs, and the emperor was furious and expelled him back to his hometown that same day.

entries.zh: 嘗用杜安道為御用監。
entries.en: He once appointed Du Andao director of the Directorate of Imperial Manufactories.
entries.literal: He once employed Du Andao as Director of Imperial Services.

entries.zh: 安道，外臣也，以鑷工侍帝數十年，帷幄計議皆與知，性縝密不泄，過諸大臣前一揖不啟口而退。
entries.en: Andao was an outer subject who had served the emperor for decades as a metalworker; he was privy to every plan and deliberation in the field camp, was meticulous and tight-lipped by nature, and whenever he passed the senior ministers he would bow once and withdraw without a word.
entries.literal: Andao was a commoner who served the emperor for several decades as a maker of tweezers; he was privy to all the plans and deliberations in the tented camp, was by nature meticulous and secretive, and whenever he passed the great ministers he would bow once and leave without saying a word.

entries.zh: 太祖愛之，然亡他寵異，後遷出為光祿寺卿。
entries.en: The founder held him in esteem but granted him no further extraordinary favor; later he was transferred out to serve as minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
entries.literal: The Ming founder favored him, but did not grant him any other special favor; later he was transferred out as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

entries.zh: 有趙成者，洪武八年以內侍使河州市馬。
entries.en: There was also Zhao Cheng, whom in the eighth year of Hongwu the court sent as an inner attendant to purchase horses in Hezhou.
entries.literal: There was one Zhao Cheng; in the eighth year of Hongwu he was sent as an inner attendant to buy horses in Hezhou.

entries.zh: 其後以市馬出者，又有司禮監慶童等，然皆不敢有所干竊。
entries.en: Later others were sent out on horse-buying missions as well, including Qingtong of the Directorate of Ceremonial—but none of them dared to meddle in affairs or steal.
entries.literal: Later there were also those sent out to buy horses, such as Qingtong of the Directorate of Ceremonial Service, but none of them dared to meddle or pilfer anything.

entries.zh: 建文帝嗣位，御內臣益嚴，詔出外稍不法，許有司械聞。
entries.en: When the Jianwen Emperor came to the throne, he tightened control over the inner servants still further, decreeing that if any of them went outside and committed even minor offenses, local officials might arrest them and report the matter.
entries.literal: When the Jianwen Emperor succeeded to the throne, he tightened control over the inner servants even more severely; he issued an edict that if any of them went outside and committed even minor offenses, the local authorities were permitted to arrest and report them.

entries.zh: 及燕師逼江北，內臣多逃入其軍，漏朝廷虛實。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yan's army pressed to the north bank of the Yangzi, many inner servants deserted into his ranks and betrayed the court's strengths and weaknesses.
entries.literal: When the Yan army pressed against the north bank of the Yangzi, many inner servants fled into its ranks and leaked the court's weaknesses.

entries.zh: 文皇以為忠於己，而狗兒輩復以軍功得幸，即位後遂多所委任。
entries.en: The Yongle Emperor regarded them as loyal to his cause, and men such as Dog'er won further favor through military service; once he took the throne, he entrusted them with ever wider responsibilities.
entries.literal: The Yongle Emperor considered them loyal to him, and Gou'er and the others were further favored because of military merit; once he came to the throne, he entrusted them with many responsibilities.

entries.zh: 永樂元年，內官監李興奉敕往勞暹羅國王。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongle, Li Xing of the Directorate of Palace Eunuchs was ordered to travel to Siam and convey the emperor's condolences to its king.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongle, the inner-court official Li Xing was ordered to go and present condolences to the king of Siam.

entries.zh: 三年，遣太監鄭和帥舟師下西洋。
entries.en: In the third year the court dispatched the eunuch Zheng He to lead a fleet on the voyage to the Western Ocean.
entries.literal: In the third year, Zheng He was sent with a fleet as envoy to the Western Ocean.

entries.zh: 八年，都督譚青營有內官王安等。
entries.en: In the eighth year inner officials such as Wang An were attached to the camp of the regional commander Tan Qing.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, at General Tan Qing's camp there were inner officials such as Wang An.

entries.zh: 又命馬靖鎮甘肅，馬騏鎮交阯。
entries.en: He also ordered Ma Jing to take command in Gansu and Ma Qi to take command in Jiaozhi.
entries.literal: He also ordered Ma Jing to garrison Gansu and Ma Qi to garrison Jiaozhi.

entries.zh: 十八年置東廠，令刺事。
entries.en: In the eighteenth year the Eastern Depot was set up and charged with intelligence gathering.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year the Eastern Depot was established and ordered to investigate matters.

entries.zh: 蓋明世宦官出使、專征、監軍、分鎮、刺臣民隱事諸大權，皆自永樂間始。
entries.en: Thus the great powers later wielded by eunuchs—diplomatic missions abroad, independent military campaigns, supervision of armies, regional commands, and surveillance of ministers and commoners—all had their beginning in the Yongle reign.
entries.literal: The great powers exercised by eunuchs in foreign missions, independent campaigns, military supervision, regional garrisons, and spying on the hidden affairs of ministers and commoners all began in the Yongle years.

entries.zh: 茂州，古冉駹國地。
entries.en: Maozhou was ancient Ranrang territory.
entries.literal: Maozhou was the land of the ancient Ranrang state.

entries.zh: 漢武帝置汶山郡，宣帝為北部都尉。
entries.en: Han Emperor Wu made Wenshan Commandery; Emperor Xuan a northern frontier command.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu of Han established Wenshan Commandery; Emperor Xuan made it the northern frontier commandant's district.

entries.zh: 隋為蜀州，尋改會州。
entries.en: Sui: Shu Prefecture, soon Hui Prefecture.
entries.literal: Under the Sui it was Shu Prefecture, soon changed to Hui Prefecture.

entries.zh: 唐貞觀改茂州。
entries.en: Tang Zhenguan: Maozhou.
entries.literal: In the Zhenguan era of Tang it was changed to Maozhou.

entries.zh: 宋、元仍舊，治汶山縣。
entries.en: Song and Yuan kept the name and ruled from Wenshan County.
entries.literal: Song and Yuan kept the old name, administering Wenshan County.

entries.zh: 洪武六年，茂州權知州楊者七及隴木頭、靜州、嶽希蓬諸土官來朝貢。
entries.en: Hongwu year 6: acting prefect Yang Zheqi and chiefs of Longmutou, Jingzhou, and Yuexipeng presented tribute.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu the acting prefect Yang Zheqi and the native officials of Longmutou, Jingzhou, and Yuexipeng came to court with tribute.

entries.zh: 十一年置茂州衛指揮使司。
entries.en: Year 11: Maozhou Guard was founded.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year the Maozhou Guard command was established.

entries.zh: 時四川都司遣兵修灌縣橋梁至陶關，汶川土酋孟道貴疑之，集部落阻陶關道。
entries.en: Sichuan troops repairing the Guanxian bridge to Taoguan alarmed Wenchuan chief Meng Daogui, who blocked the road.
entries.literal: At that time the Sichuan Regional Command sent troops to repair the bridge at Guanxian as far as Taoguan; the Wenchuan tribal chief Meng Daogui grew suspicious, gathered his tribes, and blocked the road at Taoguan.

entries.zh: 都司遣指揮胡淵、童勝等統兵分二道擊之，一由石泉，一由灌口。
entries.en: Commanders Hu Yuan and Tong Sheng attacked by Shiquan and Guankou.
entries.literal: The Regional Command sent Commanders Hu Yuan and Tong Sheng with troops on two routes to attack—one by Shiquan, one by Guankou.

entries.zh: 由灌口者進次陶關，蠻眾伏兩山間，投石崖下，兵不能進。
entries.en: The Guankou force reached Taoguan; tribes ambushed from both hills and rolled stones down the cliffs.
entries.literal: The Guankou column advanced to Taoguan; the tribes lay in ambush between the two mountains and rolled stones down the cliffs so the army could not advance.

entries.zh: 適汶川土官來降，得其間道。
entries.en: A Wenchuan chief then surrendered and showed a secret path.
entries.literal: Just then a Wenchuan native official came to surrender and revealed a hidden path.

entries.zh: 乃選勇士卷旗甲，乘夜潛出兩山後，遲明從山頂張旗幟，發火炮，蠻驚潰。
entries.en: Elite troops crept behind the hills by night, raised banners and fired cannon at dawn, and the tribes fled.
entries.literal: They therefore chose stalwarts, rolled up banners and armor, stole out by night behind the two mountains, and at dawn unfurled banners from the summits, fired cannon, and the tribes fled in alarm.

entries.zh: 師進雁門關，道險，蠻復據之。
entries.en: At perilous Yanmen Pass the tribes held the road again.
entries.literal: The army advanced to Yanmen Pass; the road was perilous and the tribes again held it.

entries.zh: 乃駐平野，得小舟渡，至龍止鐵冶寨，擊破之。
entries.en: They crossed by boat, reached Longzhi Tieye Stockade, and stormed it.
entries.literal: They camped on the open plain, obtained small boats to cross, reached Longzhi Tieye Stockade, and broke it.

entries.zh: 其由石泉者次泥池，蠻悉眾拒。
entries.en: The Shiquan column met full tribal resistance at Nichi.
entries.literal: The Shiquan column halted at Nichi; the tribes mustered all their strength to resist.

entries.zh: 千戶薛文突陣射卻之，士卒奮擊，大敗其眾。
entries.en: Commander Xue Wen charged shooting and routed them.
entries.literal: Company commander Xue Wen charged the line shooting and drove them back; the soldiers pressed the attack and routed their host.

entries.zh: 兩軍遂會於茂州，楊者七迎降，以者七仍領其州。
entries.en: Both columns met at Maozhou; Yang Zheqi surrendered and kept his prefecture.
entries.literal: The two armies met at Maozhou; Yang Zheqi came out to surrender and Zheqi was left to govern his prefecture.

entries.zh: 乃詔立茂州衛，留指揮楚華將兵三千守之。
entries.en: Maozhou Guard was founded with Commander Chu Hua and 3,000 troops.
entries.literal: An edict then established Maozhou Guard and left Commander Chu Hua with three thousand troops to garrison it.

entries.zh: 十五年，者七陰結生番，約日伏兵陷城。
entries.en: Year 15: Zheqi secretly allied with raw tribes to ambush the city.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year Zheqi secretly joined the raw tribes and agreed on a day to ambush troops and seize the city.

entries.zh: 有小校密告於官，遂發兵捕斬者七。
entries.en: A junior officer informed the garrison; Zheqi was captured and beheaded.
entries.literal: A junior officer secretly reported to the officials; troops were therefore sent to capture and behead Zheqi.

entries.zh: 生番不之覺，如期入寇，官軍掩擊敗之，於是盡徙羌民於城外。
entries.en: The raw tribes attacked on schedule and were ambushed; the Qiang were then moved outside the walls.
entries.literal: The raw tribes were unaware; they entered on schedule to raid, and government troops ambushed and defeated them, whereupon all Qiang people were moved outside the walls.

entries.zh: 四川土司諸境，多有去蜀遠，去滇、黔近者。
entries.en: Many of the Sichuan tribal domains lay far from the Sichuan heartland but close to Yunnan and Guizhou.
entries.literal: Of the various territories of the Sichuan tribal headmen, many are far from Shu yet close to Yunnan and Guizhou.

entries.zh: 如烏蒙、東川近於滇，烏撒、鎮雄、播州近於黔。
entries.en: Wumeng and Dongchuan lay near Yunnan, while Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Bozhou lay near Guizhou.
entries.literal: For example, Wumeng and Dongchuan were close to Yunnan; Wusa, Zhenxiong, and Bozhou were close to Guizhou.

entries.zh: 明太祖略定邊方，首平蜀夏，置四川布政司，使招諭諸蠻，次第歸附。
entries.en: After the Hongwu Emperor had broadly secured the borderlands, he first conquered the Xia regime in Shu, set up the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission, and sent envoys to summon the various tribes to submit one after another.
entries.literal: When the Hongwu Emperor had broadly pacified the frontier, he first subdued the Xia regime in Shu, established the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission, and sent envoys to summon and instruct the various barbarian peoples to submit in turn.

entries.zh: 故烏蒙、烏撒、東川、芒部舊屬雲南者，皆隸於四川，不過歲輸貢賦，示以羈縻。
entries.en: Thus Wumeng, Wusa, Dongchuan, and Mangbu, formerly part of Yunnan, were all placed under Sichuan jurisdiction, paying only annual tribute as a token of loose imperial control.
entries.literal: Therefore Wumeng, Wusa, Dongchuan, and Mangbu, which had formerly belonged to Yunnan, were all placed under Sichuan—nothing more than annual tribute payments to display loose reins.

entries.zh: 然夷性獷悍，嗜利好殺，爭相競尚，焚燒劫掠，習以為恒。
entries.en: Yet the tribes were fierce by nature, greedy for profit and quick to kill; they competed in prestige, and burning, looting, and raiding had become their habitual way of life.
entries.literal: Yet the barbarians were by nature fierce and violent, greedy for gain and fond of killing; they vied with one another in emulation, burning, plundering, and raiding as a constant practice.

entries.zh: 去省窎遠，莫能控制，附近邊民，鹹被其毒。
entries.en: So remote from the provincial seat that the government could not restrain them, they poisoned the lives of nearby border populations.
entries.literal: Being far from the provincial capital, they could not be controlled, and neighboring border people all suffered their harm.

entries.zh: 皆由規模草創，未嘗設立文武為之鈐轄，聽其自相雄長。
entries.en: This arose because the system was still rudimentary: no civil or military officials had been stationed to keep them in check, and they were left to vie among themselves for dominance.
entries.literal: All this was because the framework was newly established and no civil or military officials had been set up to exercise control, leaving them to contend among themselves for supremacy.

entries.zh: 雖受天朝爵號，實自王其地。
entries.en: Though they bore titles granted by the dynasty, in practice they ruled their own territories like kings.
entries.literal: Although they received titles from the Celestial Court, in truth they were kings of their own lands.

entries.zh: 以故終明之世，常煩撻伐。
entries.en: Hence throughout the Ming period the court was repeatedly obliged to launch punitive expeditions against them.
entries.literal: For this reason, throughout the Ming dynasty campaigns of suppression were constantly required.

entries.zh: 唯建昌、松、茂等處設立衛所，播州改遵義、平越二府以後，稍安戢雲。
entries.en: Only after guard posts were set up at Jianchang, Songpan, Maozhou, and elsewhere, and Bozhou was reorganized into the prefectures of Zunyi and Pingyue, did the region grow somewhat calmer.
entries.literal: Only after guard posts were established at Jianchang, Songpan, Maozhou, and elsewhere, and after Bozhou was reorganized into the two prefectures of Zunyi and Pingyue, did the region grow somewhat more tranquil.

entries.zh: 永昌，古哀牢固。
entries.en: Yongchang had been the land of the ancient Ailao people.
entries.literal: Yongchang was the territory of ancient Ailao.

entries.zh: 漢武帝時，置不韋縣。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Han, Buwei County was founded there.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Han, Buwei County was established.

entries.zh: 東漢置瀾滄郡，尋改永昌郡。
entries.en: Under the Eastern Han a Lancang Commandery was set up, which was soon renamed Yongchang Commandery.
entries.literal: In Eastern Han Lancang Commandery was established, soon renamed Yongchang Commandery.

entries.zh: 唐屬姚州，後為南詔蒙氏所據，歷段氏、高氏皆為永昌府。
entries.en: In Tang times it fell under Yaozhou; later the Nanzhao kingdom of the Meng clan seized it, and under the Duan and Gao dynasties in turn it was known as Yongchang Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the Tang it belonged to Yaozhou; later it was seized by the Nanzhao Meng clan, and successively under the Duan and Gao clans it became Yongchang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 元初，於永昌立三千戶所，隸大理萬戶府。
entries.en: Early in the Yuan dynasty a Three Thousand Households Office was established at Yongchang, under the Dali Ten Thousand Households Office.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, a Three Thousand Households Office was established at Yongchang, subordinate to the Dali Ten Thousand Households Office.

entries.zh: 至元間置永昌州，尋為府，隸大理路，置金齒等處宣撫司治。
entries.en: In the Zhiyuan period Yongchang was first made a prefecture and soon raised to a fu, subordinate to Dali Circuit and administered by the Jinchi Pacification Commission and related offices.
entries.literal: During the Zhiyuan era Yongchang Prefecture was established, soon elevated to a fu; it was subordinate to Dali Circuit, with the Jinchi Pacification Commission and other offices administering it.

entries.zh: 洪武十五年定雲南，立金齒衛。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu, after Yunnan was brought under control, the Jinchi Guard was established.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year of Hongwu Yunnan was pacified and the Jinchi Guard was established.

entries.zh: 以元雲南右丞觀音保為金齒指揮使，賜姓名李觀。
entries.en: The former Yuan Right Grand Councilor of Yunnan, Guanyin Bao, was appointed commander of the Jinchi Guard and given the Chinese name Li Guan.
entries.literal: The Yuan Yunnan Right Grand Councilor Guanyin Bao was appointed Jinchi Commander and granted the surname and personal name Li Guan.

entries.zh: 十六年，永昌州土官申保來朝，詔賜錦二匹、織金文綺二匹、衣一襲及钑花銀帶、鞾襪。
entries.en: In the sixteenth year the Yongchang native official Shen Bao came to court, and the emperor bestowed on him two lengths of brocade, two lengths of gold-threaded silk, a full set of robes, an engraved silver belt, and boots and socks.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year Yongchang Prefecture native official Shen Bao came to court; an edict granted him two bolts of brocade, two bolts of gold-woven patterned silk, one set of robes, and a silver belt with chased floral patterns, plus boots and socks.

entries.zh: 十七年以申保為永昌府同知。
entries.en: In the seventeenth year Shen Bao was made vice prefect of Yongchang.
entries.literal: In the seventeenth year Shen Bao was appointed Vice Prefect of Yongchang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 四月，金齒土官段惠遣把事及其子弟來貢，賜綺帛鈔有差。
entries.en: In the fourth month the Jinchi native official Duan Hui sent his steward together with sons and younger brothers to present tribute, and they received graded gifts of silk and paper money.
entries.literal: In the fourth month Jinchi native official Duan Hui sent a steward and his sons and younger brothers to present tribute; gifts of silk and paper money were granted in varying amounts.

entries.zh: 置施甸長官司，以土酋阿幹為副長官，賜冠帶。
entries.en: The Shidian Native Office was created, the chieftain A'gan was made its deputy headman, and he was invested with official cap and belt.
entries.literal: The Shidian Native Office was established, with tribal chieftain A'gan appointed deputy native official and granted cap and belt.

entries.zh: 洪武六年遣使田儼、程鬥南、張祎、錢允恭賫詔往諭。
entries.en: In Hongwu 6 the envoys Tian Yan, Cheng Dou'nan, Zhang Yi, and Qian Yonggong were sent with an imperial edict to announce the court's will.
entries.literal: In Hongwu 6 envoys Tian Yan, Cheng Dou'nan, Zhang Yi, and Qian Yonggong were dispatched bearing an imperial edict to announce the imperial will.

entries.zh: 至安南，留二年，以道阻不通。
entries.en: They reached Annam and stayed there two years, the road ahead blocked and impassable.
entries.literal: They reached Annam and remained two years, as the route was blocked and impassable.

entries.zh: 有詔召之，惟儼還，余皆道卒。
entries.en: An edict recalled them; only Tian Yan made it back—the others all died on the journey.
entries.literal: An edict summoned them back; only Tian Yan returned—the rest all died on the road.

entries.zh: 十五年，大兵下雲南，進以大理，下金齒。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year the main army swept into Yunnan, pushed through Dali, and captured Jinchi.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year the grand army descended on Yunnan, advanced through Dali, and took Jinchi.

entries.zh: 平緬與金齒壤地相接，土蠻思倫發聞之懼，遂降。
entries.en: Ping Mian bordered Jinchi directly; when the native chieftain Si Lunfa heard the news he was terrified and submitted.
entries.literal: Ping Mian shared a border with Jinchi; the tribal chieftain Si Lunfa heard of this and, fearing attack, submitted.

entries.zh: 因置平緬宣慰使司，以倫發為宣慰使。
entries.en: A Ping Mian Pacification Commission was accordingly established, and Lunfa was appointed its pacification commissioner.
entries.literal: A Ping Mian Pacification Commission was therefore established, with Lunfa appointed pacification commissioner.

entries.zh: 十七年八月，倫發遣刀令孟獻方物，並上元所授宣慰使司印。
entries.en: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year Lunfa sent Dao Lingmeng with local tribute and the Yuan-granted seal of the pacification commission.
entries.literal: In the eighth month of the seventeenth year, Lunfa sent Dao Lingmeng to present local products and surrender the seal of the pacification commission granted by the Yuan.

entries.zh: 詔改平緬宣慰使為平緬軍民宣慰使司，並賜倫發朝服、冠帶及織金文綺、鈔錠。
entries.en: An edict reorganized the commission as the Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission and granted Lunfa court robes, cap and belt, brocaded gold-thread silk, and banknotes.
entries.literal: An edict changed the Ping Mian Pacification Commission to the Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission, and Lunfa was granted court robes, cap and belt, brocaded gold-thread silk, and ingots of paper money.

entries.zh: 尋改平緬軍民宣慰使司為麓川平緬軍民宣慰使司。
entries.en: It was soon renamed the Luchuan-Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: Soon the Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission was renamed the Luchuan-Ping Mian Military-Civilian Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 麓川與平緬連境，元時分置兩路以統其所部，至是以倫發遣使貢，命兼統麓川之地。
entries.en: Luchuan and Ping Mian were adjacent; the Yuan had divided them into two circuits to govern their peoples separately. Now, because Lunfa had sent tribute envoys, he was ordered to govern Luchuan as well.
entries.literal: Luchuan and Ping Mian shared a border; under the Yuan two circuits had been separately established to govern their respective territories. Now, because Lunfa had dispatched envoys with tribute, he was ordered to govern Luchuan as well.

entries.zh: 萬歷初，緬甸莽瑞體叛，來招隴川宣撫多士寧，士寧不從。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Wanli reign Mang Ruiti of Burma rebelled and tried to recruit the Longchuan Pacification Superintendent Duoshining, but Shining refused.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, Mang Ruiti of Burma rebelled and came to recruit the Longchuan Pacification Superintendent Duoshining; Shining refused.

entries.zh: 其記室嶽鳳者，江西撫州人，黠而多智，商於隴川，士寧信任之，妻以妹。
entries.en: His secretary Yue Feng was a man from Fuzhou in Jiangxi, cunning and resourceful. He had traded in Longchuan; Shining trusted him and gave him his younger sister in marriage.
entries.literal: His secretary Yue Feng was a man from Fuzhou in Jiangxi—cunning and sharp-witted. He traded in Longchuan; Shining trusted him and gave him his younger sister in marriage.

entries.zh: 鳳曲媚士寧，陰奪其權，與三宣六慰各土舍罕拔等歃血盟，誘士寧往擺古，歸附緬酋。
entries.en: Feng flattered Shining to his face while secretly usurping his authority. With the native garrison officers of the Three Pacifications and Six Pacifications, Han Ba and others, he swore a blood oath, lured Shining to Baigu, and brought him to submit to the Burmese chief.
entries.literal: Feng flattered Shining outwardly while secretly usurping his authority; with the native garrison officers of the Three Pacifications and Six Pacifications, Han Ba and others, he swore a blood oath, lured Shining to Baigu, and brought him to submit to the Burmese chief.

entries.zh: 陰使其子曩烏鴆士寧並殺其妻女，奪印投緬，受緬偽命，代士寧為宣撫。
entries.en: Secretly he had his son Nangwu poison Shining and murder his wife and daughters; he seized the seal, defected to Burma, received a false commission from the Burmese, and replaced Shining as pacification superintendent.
entries.literal: Secretly he had his son Nangwu poison Shining and also kill his wife and daughters; he seized the seal and went over to Burma, received a false commission from the Burmese, and replaced Shining as pacification superintendent.

entries.zh: 及瑞體死，子應裏嗣，鳳父子臣服之。
entries.en: When Ruiti died his son Yingli succeeded, and Feng and his son submitted to him.
entries.literal: When Ruiti died, his son Yingli succeeded, and Feng and his son submitted to him.

entries.zh: 誘敗官軍，獻士寧母胡氏及親族六百余人於應裏，盡殺之，多氏之宗幾盡。
entries.en: He lured and defeated government troops, then presented Shining's mother Lady Hu and more than six hundred clansmen to Yingli, who killed them all; the Duo clan was nearly wiped out.
entries.literal: He lured and defeated government troops, and presented Shining's mother Lady Hu and more than six hundred clansmen to Yingli, who killed them all; the Duo clan was nearly exterminated.

entries.zh: 初，鳳之附於緬也，為瑞體招諸部，拒中國，傷官軍，逆勢浸成，緬深倚之。
entries.en: At first, when Feng joined Burma, he rallied the tribes for Ruiti, resisted the court, and harried government troops; the rebellion gathered strength, and Burma came to rely on him deeply.
entries.literal: At first, when Feng attached himself to Burma, he recruited the various tribes for Ruiti, resisted China, harmed government troops, and the rebellious momentum gradually grew; Burma came to rely deeply on him.

entries.zh: 久之，以緬不足恃。
entries.en: In time he came to see that Burma was not to be relied on.
entries.literal: After a long time, he came to see that Burma was not to be relied on.

entries.zh: 而鄧川土知州何鈺，鳳友婿也，初使人招鳳，鳳執使獻緬。
entries.en: The native prefect of Dengchuan, He Yu, was Feng's friend by marriage. At first He Yu sent men to recruit Feng, but Feng seized the envoys and handed them over to the Burmese.
entries.literal: The native prefect of Dengchuan, He Yu, was Feng's friend by marriage; at first he sent men to recruit Feng, but Feng seized the envoys and handed them over to the Burmese.

entries.zh: 及是，鈺復開示百方，與之盟誓。
entries.en: Now He Yu tried every means to win him over and made sworn alliance with him.
entries.literal: Now He Yu again tried every means to win him over and made sworn alliance with him.

entries.zh: 時官軍亦大集，諸將劉綎、鄧子龍各率勁師至，環壁四面。
entries.en: By then government troops had massed in strength; the generals Liu Ting and Deng Zilong each led crack forces to the scene and encircled the rebels on every side.
entries.literal: At that time government troops had also massed in strength; the generals Liu Ting and Deng Zilong each led crack forces to arrive and encircled them with walls on all four sides.

entries.zh: 鳳懼，乃令妻子及部曲來降。
entries.en: Frightened, Feng sent his wife, children, and followers to surrender.
entries.literal: Feng was afraid, and then sent his wife, children, and followers to surrender.

entries.zh: 綎責令獻金牌、符印及蠻莫、猛密地。
entries.en: Liu Ting ordered him to surrender his gold plaques, tally seals, and the territories of Manmo and Mengmi.
entries.literal: Liu Ting ordered him to surrender his gold plaques, tally seals, and the territories of Manmo and Mengmi.

entries.zh: 乃以送鳳妻子還隴川為名，分兵趨沙木籠山，先據其險，而自領大兵馳入隴川。
entries.en: Under the pretense of escorting Feng's wife and children back to Longchuan, he sent detachments to seize the heights of Shamuolong Mountain while he himself led the main force in a dash into Longchuan.
entries.literal: Under the pretense of escorting Feng's wife and children back to Longchuan, he divided troops to hurry to Shamuolong Mountain and seize its strategic heights first, while he himself led the main force in a dash into Longchuan.

entries.zh: 鳳度無可脫，遂詣軍門降。
entries.en: Seeing no escape, Feng came to the army gate and surrendered.
entries.literal: Feng saw that there was no escape and then came to the army gate to surrender.

entries.zh: 綎復率兵進緬，緬將先遁，留少兵隴川，綎攻之，鳳子曩烏亦降，綎乃攜鳳父子往攻蠻莫，蠻莫賊知鳳降，馳報應裏，發兵圖隴川。
entries.en: Liu Ting marched against Burma; the Burmese generals fled first, leaving a small force in Longchuan that Liu Ting attacked. Feng's son Nangwu also surrendered. Liu Ting then took Feng and his son to attack Manmo; when the Manmo rebels learned of Feng's surrender, they hurried word to Yingli, who sent troops to seize Longchuan.
entries.literal: Liu Ting again led troops against Burma; the Burmese generals fled first, leaving a small force in Longchuan, which Liu Ting attacked. Feng's son Nangwu also surrendered. Liu Ting then took Feng and his son to attack Manmo; when the Manmo bandits learned that Feng had surrendered, they hurried to inform Yingli, who dispatched troops to seize Longchuan.

entries.zh: 綎乘機掩殺，賊窘，乞降，縛緬人及象馬來獻。
entries.en: Liu Ting seized the moment and struck by surprise; hard pressed, the rebels begged to surrender and bound the Burmese men they held, presenting elephants and horses.
entries.literal: Liu Ting seized the opportunity to strike by surprise; the bandits were hard pressed, begged to surrender, and bound the Burmese men and presented elephants and horses.

entries.zh: 遂招撫孟養賊，賊將乘象走，追獲之。
entries.en: He then offered terms to the Mengyang rebels; a rebel general fled on an elephant and was pursued and captured.
entries.literal: He then offered pacification to the Mengyang bandits; a bandit general fled riding an elephant and was pursued and captured.

entries.zh: 復移師圍孟璉，生擒其魁，隴川平。
entries.en: The army shifted to besiege Menglian, captured the ringleader alive, and Longchuan was pacified.
entries.literal: The army was shifted to besiege Menglian, the ringleader was captured alive, and Longchuan was pacified.

entries.zh: 獻俘於朝，帝為告謝郊廟，時萬歷十二年九月也。
entries.en: Captives were presented at court, and the emperor offered thanksgiving at the suburban altars and ancestral temples—it was the ninth month of Wanli 12.
entries.literal: Captives were presented at court; the emperor offered thanksgiving at the suburban altars and ancestral temples—it was the ninth month of the twelfth year of Wanli.

entries.zh: 逾年復鑄隴川宣撫司及孟定府印，升孟密安撫為宣撫司。
entries.en: The following year new seals were cast for the Longchuan Pacification Superintendency and Mengding Prefecture, and the Mengmi Pacification Superintendency was promoted to a pacification commission.
entries.literal: The following year new seals were cast for the Longchuan Pacification Superintendency and the Mengding Prefecture, and the Mengmi Pacification Superintendency was promoted to a pacification commission.

entries.zh: 添設安撫司二，曰蠻莫，曰耿馬；
entries.en: Two pacification superintendencies were added: Manmo and Gengma;
entries.literal: Two pacification superintendencies were added, named Manmo and Gengma;

entries.zh: 長官司二，曰孟璉，曰孟養；
entries.en: Two native chief offices were added: Menglian and Mengyang;
entries.literal: Two native offices of chief were added, named Menglian and Mengyang;

entries.zh: 千戶所二，一居姚關，一居孟淋砦，皆名之曰鎮安；
entries.en: Two chiliarchies were added, one at Yaoguan and one at Menglin Stockade, both named Zhen'an;
entries.literal: Two chiliarchies were added, one at Yaoguan and one at Menglin Stockade, both named Zhen'an;

entries.zh: 並鑄印記，建大將行署於蠻莫。
entries.en: Seals were cast for all, and a field headquarters of the commanding general was established at Manmo.
entries.literal: Seals were cast for all, and a field headquarters of the great general was established at Manmo.

entries.zh: 從雲南巡撫劉世曾之議也。
entries.en: This followed the proposal of Liu Shiceng, Grand Coordinator of Yunnan.
entries.literal: This followed the proposal of Liu Shiceng, Grand Coordinator of Yunnan.

entries.zh: 於是，多士寧之子思順襲隴川宣撫使。
entries.en: Thereupon Duoshining's son Sisun inherited the post of Longchuan Pacification Superintendent.
entries.literal: Thereupon Duoshining's son Sisun inherited the post of Longchuan Pacification Superintendent.

entries.zh: 姚安鶴慶武定尋甸麗江元江永昌新化威遠北勝灣甸鎮康大侯瀾滄衛麓川
entries.en: Yao'an, Heqing, Wuding, Xundian, Lijiang, Yuanjiang, Yongchang, Xinhua, Weiyuan, Beisheng, Wandian, Zhenkang, Dahou, Lancang Guard, and Luchuan
entries.literal: Yao'an, Heqing, Wuding, Xundian, Lijiang, Yuanjiang, Yongchang, Xinhua, Weiyuan, Beisheng, Wandian, Zhenkang, Dahou, Lancang Guard, Luchuan

entries.zh: 明年，北部亦卜剌與小王子仇殺。
entries.en: The following year Yibulai of the north and the Little Prince turned on each other.
entries.literal: The next year Yibulai of the northern tribes and the Little Prince feuded and fought each other.

entries.zh: 亦卜剌竄西海，阿爾禿廝與合，逼脅洮西屬番，屢入寇。
entries.en: Yibulai fled to the Western Sea, allied with Aertusi, bullied the dependent tribes west of the Tao, and raided again and again.
entries.literal: Yibulai fled to the Western Sea, joined with Aertusi, coerced the dependent tribes west of the Tao River, and repeatedly entered in raids.

entries.zh: 巡撫張翼、總兵王勳不能制，漸深入，邊人苦之。
entries.en: Grand Coordinator Zhang Yi and Commander Wang Xun could not check them; the raids pushed ever deeper, and the border people suffered.
entries.literal: Grand Coordinator Zhang Yi and Commander-in-Chief Wang Xun could not control them; they gradually penetrated deeper, and frontier people suffered bitterly.

entries.zh: 八年夏，擁眾來川，遣使詣翼所，乞邊地駐牧修貢。
entries.en: In the eighth year, that summer, he brought a large force into the frontier valleys and sent envoys to Zhang Yi asking for pasturelands and permission to resume tribute.
entries.literal: In the summer of the eighth year he gathered a host and came to the frontier riverlands, sent envoys to Yi's headquarters, and begged for border land to pasture and restore tribute.

entries.zh: 翼啖以金帛，令遠徙，亦卜剌遂西掠烏斯藏，據之。
entries.en: Zhang Yi placated him with gold and silk and told him to move on; Yibulai then swept west into Tibet and seized the region.
entries.literal: Yi enticed him with gold and silks and ordered him to move far away; Yibulai then raided west into U-Tsang and occupied it.

entries.zh: 自是洮、岷、松潘無寧歲。
entries.en: After that Tao, Min, and Songpan knew no quiet year.
entries.literal: From this time Tao, Min, and Songpan had no peaceful year.

entries.zh: 韃靼，即蒙古，故元後也。
entries.en: The Tartars are the Mongols—the remnant house of the Yuan.
entries.literal: The Tartars are the Mongols, the successors of the former Yuan.

entries.zh: 太祖洪武元年，大將軍徐達率師取元，元主自北平遁出塞，居開平，數遣其將也速等擾北邊。
entries.en: In the founding emperor’s first Hongwu year, Grand General Xu Da marched to seize the Yuan capital; the Yuan emperor slipped from Beiping north of the passes and made Kaiping his seat, while repeatedly dispatching generals such as Yisu to raid the northern border.
entries.literal: In the first year of Hongwu under the founding emperor, Grand General Xu Da led troops to take the Yuan; the Yuan ruler fled from Beiping out beyond the passes, dwelt at Kaiping, and repeatedly sent his generals Yisu and others to harass the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 明年，常遇春擊敗之，師進開平，俘宗王慶孫、平章鼎住。
entries.en: The following year Chang Yuchun routed them; the army pushed on to Kaiping and took the imperial prince Qing Sun and Chancellor Dingzhu prisoner.
entries.literal: The next year Chang Yuchun defeated them; the army advanced to Kaiping and captured the imperial prince Qing Sun and the chancellor Dingzhu.

entries.zh: 高帝下
entries.en: Emperor Gao (continued)
entries.literal: Emperor Gao, Part Two

entries.zh: 建元元年夏四月甲午，上卽皇帝位於南郊，設壇柴燎告天曰：「皇帝臣道成敢用玄牡，昭告皇皇后帝。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, summer, fourth month, day jiawu, he took the throne at the Southern Altar. The altar was raised, firewood was burned, and he addressed Heaven: "Your subject Daocheng, now Emperor, dares offer the black bull and declare to Heaven and Earth:
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, fourth month, summer, day jiawu, the Emperor assumed the imperial throne at the Southern Altar, set up the altar, burned firewood offerings, and announced to Heaven: "The Emperor, your subject Daocheng, dares to use the black bull and announces to the August Sovereign above and the Empress below.

entries.zh: 宋帝陟鑒乾序，欽若明命，以命于道成。
entries.en: The Song emperor has read Heaven's order, bowed to the bright command, and entrusted the charge to Daocheng.
entries.literal: The Song Emperor has ascended to examine the sequence of Heaven, reverently followed the bright mandate, and bestowed the command upon Daocheng.

entries.zh: 夫肇自生民，樹以司牧，所以闡極則天，開元創物，肆茲大道。
entries.en: Since mankind began, rulers have been appointed to tend the folk, to touch the pole and mirror Heaven, to open an age and shape the world—to walk this great road.
entries.literal: From the beginning of mankind rulers have been set up as shepherds, in order to reach the utmost and accord with Heaven, open the origin and create things, and spread this great Way.

entries.zh: 天下惟公，命不于常。
entries.en: The realm belongs to the worthy; the mandate does not stay with one house forever.
entries.literal: Under Heaven only the public [virtue] [rules]; the mandate is not fixed.

entries.zh: 昔在虞、夏，受終上代，粵自漢、魏，揖讓中葉，咸炳諸典謨，載在方冊。
entries.en: In Yu and Xia, the throne passed from the old line; from Han and Wei, rulers yielded in mid-dynasty—all of it glows in the classics and lives in the annals.
entries.literal: Formerly in Yu and Xia they received the end from the prior age; from Han and Wei onward, abdication in the middle ages—all shine in the canonical records and are written in the registers.

entries.zh: 水德旣微，仍世多故，實賴道成匡拯之功，以弘濟于厥艱。
entries.en: The Water reign had faded and age after age brought disaster; only Daocheng's work of rescue bore the realm through its peril.
entries.literal: The Water phase has grown weak; generation after generation many troubles—truly relying on Daocheng's merit in righting and rescuing, to greatly cross through its hardships.

entries.zh: 大造顛墜，再構區宇，宣禮明刑，締仁緝義。
entries.en: He raised what had collapsed, built the realm anew, set rites in the open and law in the light, and wove humanity and duty into the state.
entries.literal: Greatly repairing the fallen, reconstructing the realm, proclaiming rites and clarifying punishments, binding benevolence and gathering righteousness.

entries.zh: 晷緯凝象，川岳表靈，誕惟天人，罔弗和會。
entries.en: The sun's shadow and the stars stood firm, rivers and peaks showed their numen; Heaven and humanity met, and all things fell into accord.
entries.literal: The gnomon's lines fixed the images, rivers and mountains displayed their spirits; Heaven and man were born together—none failed to harmonize.

entries.zh: 乃仰協歸運，景屬與能，用集大命于茲。
entries.en: He bowed to the turning of fate, the bright sign settled on worth, and the great charge was gathered here.
entries.literal: Thus bowing to accord with the returning fortune, the bright attribute attached to the able, thereby gathering the great mandate here.

entries.zh: 辭德匪嗣，至于累仍，而羣公卿士，庶尹御事，爰及黎獻，至于百戎，僉曰『皇天眷命，不可以固違，人神無托，不可以曠主』。
entries.en: He refused the throne again and again, but ministers high and low, officers of every rank, the people, and the hundred border tribes cried as one: "Heaven has chosen—you cannot stand against it; gods and men need a lord—you cannot leave the throne empty."
entries.literal: He declined virtue and would not succeed, even to repeated refusals; yet the host of ministers and grandees, the multitude of officials charged with affairs, down to the black-haired folk and the tribute-bearing border peoples, all said: "Imperial Heaven favors the mandate—it cannot be stubbornly disobeyed; men and spirits have nowhere to rest—it cannot be left without a lord."

entries.zh: 畏天之威，敢不祗順鴻曆？
entries.en: Who, fearing Heaven's wrath, would not bow to the great succession?
entries.literal: In awe of Heaven's majesty, how dare one not reverently follow the great calendar?

entries.zh: 敬簡元辰，虔奉皇符，升壇受禪，告類上帝，以永答民衷，式敷萬國。
entries.en: He chose the auspicious day, received the imperial tally in reverence, climbed the altar for the abdication rite, and reported to Heaven—to answer the people forever and bless the ten thousand realms.
entries.literal: Reverently choosing the first day, devoutly receiving the imperial tally, mounting the altar to receive abdication, announcing by category to the Supreme Lord, forever to answer the people's hearts and spread over the myriad states.

entries.zh: 惟明靈是饗！」
entries.en: May the bright powers accept this offering!"
entries.literal: May the bright spirits partake!"

entries.zh: 四月庚寅，上諡曰太祖高皇帝。
entries.en: Fourth month, day gengyin: he was given the temple title Grand Progenitor, High Emperor.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, day gengyin, the posthumous title was announced: Grand Progenitor, High Emperor.

entries.zh: 奉梓宮於東府前渚升龍舟。
entries.en: The coffin was carried to the dragon boat at the ford before the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: The coffin was borne to the dragon boat at the ford before the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 丙午，窆武進泰安陵。
entries.en: On day bingwu he was buried at Tai'an Mausoleum in Wujin.
entries.literal: On day bingwu he was buried at Tai'an Mausoleum in Wujin.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：孫卿有言：「聖人之有天下，受之也，非取之也。」
entries.en: The court historian writes: Xunzi said, "When a sage holds the realm, he receives it—he does not take it by force."
entries.literal: The court historian says: Master Sun has a saying: "When the sage possesses All-under-Heaven, he receives it—he does not seize it."

entries.zh: 漢高神武駿聖，觀秦氏東游，蓋是雅多大言，非始自知天命；
entries.en: Han Gaozu was fierce and far-seeing; when he saw the First Emperor of Qin parade east, it was mostly swaggering talk—he did not yet know his mandate for himself;
entries.literal: Han Gaozu was divinely martial and sagely bright; when he watched the Qin emperor tour east, it was largely grand words in excess—he did not from the first know Heaven's mandate by himself;

entries.zh: 光武聞少公之論讖，亦特一時之笑語；
entries.en: Guangwu, hearing Shaogong's prophecy, likewise laughed it off at first;
entries.literal: Guangwu, when he heard Shaogong's prophetic talk, likewise took it at first only as a jest for the moment;

entries.zh: 魏武初起義兵，所期「征西」之墓；
entries.en: Cao Cao, when he first took up arms, aimed no higher than the grave that read "Campaign West";
entries.literal: Cao Cao, when he first raised the army of righteousness, looked only to the tomb marked "Campaign West";

entries.zh: 晉宣不內迫曹爽，豈有定霸浮橋？
entries.en: Sima Yi would never have seized power at the Floating Bridge had Cao Shuang not driven him to it.
entries.literal: Jin Xuandi, had he not been pressed within by Cao Shuang, would he have fixed hegemony at the Floating Bridge?

entries.zh: 宋氏崛起匹夫，兵由義立：咸皆一世推雄，卒開鼎祚。
entries.en: The Liu Song rose from the ranks; their armies were born of righteous cause: each age made its champion, and each at last won the throne.
entries.literal: The Song house rose from a common man; its armies were raised by righteousness: each in its time was pushed forward as the hero, and each in the end opened the cauldron.

entries.zh: 宋氏正位八君，卜年五紀，四絕長嫡，三稱中興，內難邊虞，兵革世動。
entries.en: Song emperors reigned through eight rulers and five generations of omens; four times the main line failed, three times they hailed a "restoration"; at home rebellion, on the border raids, war without rest.
entries.literal: The Song occupied the throne through eight rulers, divined for five reign-periods; four times the direct line died out, three times they called it a restoration; within, trouble; on the borders, alarm; war never rested.

entries.zh: 太祖基命之初，武功潛用，泰始開運，大拯時艱，龍德在田，見猜雲雨之迹。
entries.en: When the Grand Progenitor first took the mandate, he kept his sword sheathed; in the Taishi years he dragged the age back from ruin; "dragon virtue in the fields"—yet already men read storm in his sky.
entries.literal: At the beginning when the Grand Progenitor founded the mandate, military achievement was kept in reserve; when Taishi opened fortune, he greatly rescued the age's distress; dragon virtue in the fields—traces of suspicion like clouds and rain appeared.

entries.zh: 及蒼梧暴虐，釁結朝野，百姓懍懍，命懸朝夕。
entries.en: When Emperor Cangwu turned cruel, wrath filled court and field; common folk trembled, their lives measured from dawn to dusk.
entries.literal: When Cangwu grew tyrannical, grievance bound court and countryside; the people were fearful; lives hung by dawn and dusk.

entries.zh: 權道旣行，兼濟天下。
entries.en: When the time for hard measures came, he steadied the realm as well as his own house.
entries.literal: Once the expedient way was deployed, he aided All-under-Heaven together.

entries.zh: 元功振主，利器難以假人，羣才戮力，實懷尺寸之望。
entries.en: His merit outshone the throne; power is not lent lightly; the great men strained together, yet each nursed only a handbreadth of hope.
entries.literal: The supreme achievement shook the ruler; the sharp tool is hard to lend to others; the host of talents joined their strength, yet in truth they cherished hope only an inch wide.

entries.zh: 豈其天厭水行，固已人希木德。
entries.en: Had not Heaven wearied of Song's "water" mandate, and men already hungered for Qi's "wood"?
entries.literal: Was it not that Heaven tired of the Water phase, and men already yearned for the Wood virtue?

entries.zh: 歸功與能，事極乎此。
entries.en: To give the merit to the man who could bear it and let the moment finish its course—that was the limit.
entries.literal: To return achievement to the able and let affairs reach their limit—this was the furthest point.

entries.zh: 雖至公于四海，而運卽時來；
entries.en: Though he was just to the four seas, the hour itself pressed forward;
entries.literal: Though utmost fairness was shown to the four seas, the turn came with the time;

entries.zh: 無心於黃屋，而道隨物變。
entries.en: he had no lust for the throne, yet the Way moved when things moved.
entries.literal: With no heart for the yellow house, yet the Way shifted as things changed.

entries.zh: 應而不爲，此皇齊所以集大命也。
entries.en: He answered and did not grasp—and so Great Qi received the mandate.
entries.literal: He responded yet did not act—therefore Great Qi gathered the great mandate here.

entries.zh: 贊曰：於皇太祖，有命自天，同度宇宙，合量山淵。
