entries.en: In praise: O august Grand Progenitor, Heaven-sent; vast as heaven and earth, deep as mountain and gorge.
entries.literal: In praise: O august Grand Progenitor, mandate from Heaven; you matched the cosmos in measure, mountains and abyss in depth.

entries.zh: 宋德不紹，神器虛傳。
entries.en: Song's virtue failed; the sacred vessel passed empty-handed.
entries.literal: Song virtue did not continue; the sacred vessel was passed in vain.

entries.zh: 寧亂以武，黜暴資賢。
entries.en: He stilled chaos with arms, cast down the cruel, and leaned on the worthy.
entries.literal: He stilled disorder by arms and deposed violence, relying on the worthy.

entries.zh: 庸發西疆，功興北翰，偏師獨克，孤旅霆斷。
entries.en: He stirred the west and built glory on the northern wall; one wing won alone; a single army struck like lightning.
entries.literal: From the western marches he raised merit; on the northern frontier achievement rose; a detached column took the victory alone; a lone host cut like thunder.

entries.zh: 援旆東夏，職司靜亂；
entries.en: He raised his standard in the eastern lands and by his post quelled revolt;
entries.literal: He raised his banner in eastern Xia and by office stilled rebellion;

entries.zh: 指斧徐方，時惟伐叛；
entries.en: he turned his axe to Xu and the east—the hour to punish rebels;
entries.literal: He pointed his axe at Xu and the lands of the east—then was the time to punish traitors;

entries.zh: 抗威京輦，坐清江漢。
entries.en: he showed force at the capital and, seated in silence, cleared the Yangtze and Han.
entries.literal: He showed might at the capital and sat still while the Yangtze and Han were cleared.

entries.zh: 文藝在躬，芳塵淵塞。
entries.en: Learning lived in his person; his fame filled even the far marches.
entries.literal: Letters and arts were in his person; fragrant dust filled the deep frontier.

entries.zh: 用下以才，鎮民以德。
entries.en: He used men for ability and ruled the folk by virtue.
entries.literal: He employed men by talent and settled the people by virtue.

entries.zh: 端己雄睟，君臨尊默。
entries.en: He straightened himself with a hero's eye and governed the realm in honored stillness.
entries.literal: He rectified himself with heroic gaze and faced the realm in honored silence.

entries.zh: 苞括四海，大造家國。
entries.en: He held the four seas and remade house and state.
entries.literal: He embraced the four seas and greatly made the house and state.

entries.en: [1] Endnote marker.
entries.literal: [1] Endnote marker.

entries.zh: 三月庚申，召司徒褚淵、左僕射王儉詔曰：「吾本布衣素族，念不到此，因藉時來，遂隆大業。
entries.en: Third month, day gengshen: Chu Yuan, minister over the masses, and Wang Jian, left vice director of the master of writing, were called in. The edict said: "I began as a man of plain cloth and never dreamed of this height; the age lifted me, and so I came to the throne.
entries.literal: In the third month, day gengshen, Minister over the Masses Chu Yuan and Left Vice Director of the Master of Writing Wang Jian were summoned; the edict said: "I was originally of a plain cloth clan and never thought to reach this; relying on the times, I have at last ascended the great enterprise.

entries.zh: 風道沾被，升平可期。
entries.en: The Way has begun to soak the realm; peace may yet be hoped for.
entries.literal: The wind of the Way has soaked through; peace and order may be expected.

entries.zh: 遘疾彌留，至于大漸。
entries.en: Sickness holds me fast, and the great passing is near.
entries.literal: I have met illness that lingers and now approach the great passing.

entries.zh: 公等奉太子如事吾，柔遠能邇，緝和內外，當令太子敦穆親戚，委任賢才，崇尚節儉，弘宣簡惠，則天下之理盡矣。
entries.en: Serve the crown prince as you have served me: be gentle to the far and firm with the near, knit court and country together. Let him cherish his kin, employ the worthy, love thrift, and show a simple kindness—and the realm will be well ordered.
entries.literal: You are to serve the crown prince as you served me: gentle with the distant, able with the near, harmonizing within and without. See that the crown prince treats his kin with generous courtesy, entrusts the worthy, honors frugality, and spreads simplicity and grace—then the principle of All-under-Heaven will be complete.

entries.zh: 死生有命，夫復何言！」
entries.en: Life and death are Heaven's order—what more can I say!"
entries.literal: Life and death have their mandate—what more is there to say!"

entries.zh: 壬戌，上崩于臨光殿，年五十六。
entries.en: On day renxu the emperor died in the Hall of Facing the Light, at fifty-six.
entries.literal: On day renxu the emperor died in the Hall of Facing the Light, aged fifty-six.

entries.zh: 二年春正月戊戌朔，大赦天下。
entries.en: Year 2, spring, first month, new year's day: general amnesty for the realm.
entries.literal: Second year, spring, first month, day wuxu, first day of the month: a general amnesty for All-under-Heaven.

entries.zh: 以司空、尚書令褚淵爲司徒，中軍將軍張敬兒爲車騎將軍，中領軍李安民爲領軍將軍，中護軍陳顯達爲護軍將軍。
entries.en: Chu Yuan, minister of works and director of the master of writing, became grand minister; Zhang Jing'er, central army commander, general of chariots and cavalry; Li Anmin, central army commander, director of the central army; Chen Xianda, director of the central guard, director of the guard.
entries.literal: Minister of Works and Director of the Master of Writing Chu Yuan was made Grand Minister; Central Army Commander Zhang Jing'er was made General of Chariots and Cavalry; Central Army Commander Li Anmin was made Director of the Central Army; Director of the Central Guard Chen Xianda was made Director of the Guard.

entries.zh: 辛丑，車駕親祠南郊。
entries.en: Day xinchou: the emperor offered sacrifice at the Southern Altar in person.
entries.literal: On day xinchou the imperial carriage in person sacrificed at the Southern Altar.

entries.zh: 癸卯，詔索虜寇淮、泗，遣衆軍北伐，內外纂嚴。
entries.en: Day guimao: an edict—northern raiders struck Huai and Si; armies marched north and the court and camps alike went on war footing.
entries.literal: On day guimao an edict: the northern enemy raided Huai and Si; hosts were sent on a northern campaign, and within and without the court martial law was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 三年春正月壬戌朔，詔王公卿士薦讜言。
entries.en: Spring, third year, first month, day renxu, new moon: the court asked lords and ministers to submit candid counsel.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring of the third year, day renxu, first day of the month, an edict called on princes, dukes, ministers, and scholars to recommend forthright words.

entries.zh: 丙子，以平北將軍陳顯達爲益州刺史，貞陽公柳世隆爲南兖州刺史，皇子鋒爲江夏王。
entries.en: On day bingzi, Chen Xianda, pacifying north, took Yi; Liu Shilong, duke of Zhenyang, took South Yanzhou; the prince Feng was enfeoffed as prince of Jiangxia.
entries.literal: On day bingzi, Pacifying North General Chen Xianda was made Inspector of Yi; Duke of Zhenyang Liu Shilong was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; the imperial son Feng was made Prince of Jiangxia.

entries.zh: 領軍將軍李安民等破虜于淮陽。
entries.en: Li Anmin, colonel director of the army, and his colleagues routed the barbarians at Huaiyang.
entries.literal: Colonel Director of the Army Li Anmin and others defeated the barbarians at Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 四年春正月壬戌，詔曰：「夫膠庠之典，彝倫攸先，所以招振才端，啓發性緒，弘字黎氓，納之軌義，是故五禮之迹可傳，六樂之容不泯。
entries.en: Spring, fourth year, first month, day renxu: an edict said, "The academy is the first pillar of human order—the place to gather talent, wake inclination, settle the people, and set them on the path of ritual, so that the five rites may endure and the six joys not fade.
entries.literal: In the first month of spring of the fourth year, day renxu, an edict said: "The institution of the school and academy is the constant that human relations hold first, the means to summon and shake out talent, to open one's nature and bent, to enlarge and settle the black-haired people, and to take them into the track of right—thus the traces of the five rites can be handed down and the countenance of the six joys does not perish.

entries.zh: 朕自膺曆受圖，志闡經訓，且有司羣僚，奏議咸集，蓋以戎車時警，文教未宣，思樂泮宮，永言多慨。
entries.en: Since taking the throne I have meant to revive the canon, and the ministries have piled up proposals—yet with armies always under arms, learning has gone unproclaimed, and I long for the schools with mounting regret.
entries.literal: Since I received the chart and mandate, my aim has been to clarify the classics and instructions, and the responsible offices and assembled ministers have all submitted plans together—yet with war-chariots ever on alert, culture and teaching have not been spread abroad; I think longingly of the Pan pool and sigh again and again.

entries.zh: 今關燧無虞，時和歲稔，遠邇同風，華夷慕義。
entries.en: Now the frontier is still, the year is kind, and near and far, Han and barbarian, turn toward the court.
entries.literal: Now the beacon-fires are quiet, the seasons harmonious and the harvest rich; far and near share one wind, and Chinese and barbarian alike incline to righteousness.

entries.zh: 便可式遵前准，修建敩學，精選儒官，廣延國胄。」
entries.en: Let the old model be followed: rebuild the imperial school, choose true scholars for its offices, and enroll the sons of the realm."
entries.literal: Let us at once follow the former standard, repair and build the school of instruction, carefully select Confucian officers, and broadly enroll the sons of the state."

entries.zh: 以江州刺史王延之爲右光祿大夫。
entries.en: Wang Yanzhi, inspector of Jiangzhou, was made senior master of the bright hall.
entries.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Wang Yanzhi was made Senior Master of the Bright Hall.

entries.zh: 癸亥，詔曰：「比歲申威西北，義勇爭先，殞氣寇場，命盡王事。
entries.en: On day guihai an edict said: "These last years in the northwest our soldiers strove to outdo one another; many fell in battle for the throne.
entries.literal: On day guihai, an edict said: "In recent years we showed might in the northwest; volunteers vied to be first, and men gave their breath on the battlefield and their lives for the throne.

entries.zh: 戰亡蠲復，雖有恆典，主者遵用，每傷簡薄。
entries.en: The usual exemptions for the war dead exist, but officials have applied them grudgingly.
entries.literal: Exemption for the fallen in war has a standing rule, but those in charge, in applying it, have often made it too spare.

entries.zh: 建元以來戰亡，賞蠲租布二十年，雜役十年。
entries.en: All who have died in battle since Jianyuan shall have twenty years' remission of rent and cloth and ten years' remission of labor.
entries.literal: For those who died in battle since Jianyuan, reward and exemption from rent and cloth for twenty years, and from miscellaneous corvée for ten years.

entries.zh: 其不得收屍，主軍保押，亦同此例。」
entries.en: Where no body could be brought home, the field commander shall stand guarantor under the same terms."
entries.literal: Where the body could not be recovered, the commanding officer shall stand surety—the same rule applies."

entries.zh: 以後將軍長沙王晃爲護軍將軍，中軍將軍南郡王長懋爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍安成王暠爲江州刺史。
entries.en: Prince of Changsha Xiao Huang, rear general, became protector of the army; Prince of Nan Commandery Xiao Zhangmao, general of the center, took South Xuzhou; Prince of Ancheng Xiao Gao, champion general, took Jiang.
entries.literal: Rear General, Prince of Changsha Xiao Huang was made Protector of the Army; General of the Center, Prince of Nan Commandery Xiao Changmao was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; Champion General, Prince of Ancheng Xiao Hao was made Inspector of Jiang.

entries.zh: 六月辛未，詔「相國驃騎中軍三府職，可依資勞度二官，若職限已盈，所餘可賜滿。」
entries.en: Sixth month, day xinwei: "Offices of the chancellery, the general who spreads might, and the central army may each take two men by merit and tenure; any posts beyond quota may be paid at full rate."
entries.literal: Sixth month, day xinwei: an edict—"Posts in the Three Offices of the Chancellor, the General Who Spreads Might, and the Central Army may be filled according to merit and seniority with two officers each; if the quota is full, the remainder may be granted to full salary."

entries.zh: 壬申，以遊擊將軍周山圖爲兖州刺史。
entries.en: Day renshen: Zhou Shantu, mobile corps general, became inspector of Yan.
entries.literal: On day renshen Mobile Corps General Zhou Shantu was made Inspector of Yan Province.

entries.zh: 乙亥，詔曰：「宋末頻年戎寇，兼災疾凋損，或枯骸不收，毀櫬莫掩，宜速宣下埋藏營䘏。
entries.en: Day yihai: "Song's last years saw war and pestilence. Bones lay in the open; broken coffins went uncovered. Let burial and mourning be ordered at once.
entries.literal: On day yihai an edict said: "In the last years of Song, year after year brought raids and plague; some dead were left unburied, some coffins destroyed and never covered—burial and mourning arrangements should be quickly announced.

entries.zh: 若標題猶存，姓字可識，可卽運載，致還本鄉。」
entries.en: Where tags survive and names can be read, the dead are to be carried home."
entries.literal: If markers still remain and surnames can be read, they should at once be transported and returned to their native districts."

entries.zh: 有司奏遣外監典事四人，周行離門外三十五里爲限。
entries.en: The ministries sent four overseers from the outer bureau, each to work within thirty-five li of the outer gate.
entries.literal: The relevant offices memorialized dispatch of four overseers from the outer office, ranging thirty-five li beyond the outer gates as their limit.

entries.zh: 其餘班下州郡。
entries.en: Other regions were handled by the provinces and commanderies.
entries.literal: The rest were ordered down to the provinces and commanderies.

entries.zh: 無棺器標題者，屬所以臺錢供市。
entries.en: Where there was no coffin or name marker, local officials were to buy them with funds from the capital.
entries.literal: Where there were no coffins or markers, the local office was to supply them from central funds.

entries.zh: 庚辰，七廟主備法駕卽于太廟。
entries.en: Day gengchen: the seven temple tablets, with full imperial escort, entered the ancestral shrine.
entries.literal: On day gengchen the seven ancestral tablets, with the full imperial equipage, were escorted to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

entries.zh: 詔「諸將及客，戮力艱難，盡勤直衛，其從還宮者，普賜位一階。」
entries.en: "Every officer and client who fought through the hard years and kept faithful guard—those who came home with me receive one step of rank."
entries.literal: An edict: "All generals and retainers who strove through hardship and gave loyal service in the guard—those who returned to the palace with Us are generally granted one step of rank."

entries.zh: 辛巳，罷荊州刺史。
entries.en: Day xinsi: the post of inspector of Jing was abolished.
entries.literal: On day xinsi the office of Inspector of Jing Province was abolished.

entries.zh: 甲申，立皇太子賾。
entries.en: Day jiashen: the heir apparent Ze was formally named.
entries.literal: On day jiashen the Heir Apparent Ze was installed.

entries.zh: 斷諸州郡禮慶。
entries.en: Celebrations from the provinces were stopped.
entries.literal: Congratulatory rites from all provinces and commanderies were cut off.

entries.zh: 見刑入重者，降一等，幷申前赦恩百日。
entries.en: Convicts under heavy sentence were lowered one degree, and the earlier pardon was extended by a hundred days.
entries.literal: Those who entered with serious punishment had their sentence reduced one grade, and the prior amnesty grace was extended by one hundred days.

entries.zh: 立皇子嶷爲豫章王，映爲臨川王，晃爲長沙王，曅爲武陵王，暠爲安成王，鏘爲鄱陽王，鑠爲桂陽王，鑒爲廣陵王，皇孫長懋爲南郡王。
entries.en: Princes were named: Yi of Yuzhang, Ying of Linchuan, Huang of Changsha, Ye of Wuling, Gao of Ancheng, Qiang of Poyang, Shuo of Guiyang, Jian of Guangling; the imperial grandson Zhangmao became prince of Nan commandery.
entries.literal: The princes Luan was made Prince of Yuzhang; Ying Prince of Linchuan; Huang Prince of Changsha; Ye Prince of Wuling; Gao Prince of Ancheng; Qiang Prince of Poyang; Shuo Prince of Guiyang; Jian Prince of Guangling; the imperial grandson Zhangmao Prince of Nan.

entries.zh: 乙酉，葬宋順帝于遂寧陵。
entries.en: Day yiyou: Emperor Shun of Song was laid in Suining tomb.
entries.literal: On day yiyou Emperor Shun of Song was buried at Suining Tomb.

entries.zh: 上少沈深有大量，寬嚴清儉，喜怒無色。
entries.en: In youth he was deep and still, with a large soul: stern when needed, open-handed, pure and spare; neither joy nor anger showed on his face.
entries.literal: In youth the emperor was deep and reserved, with great capacity; strict yet generous, pure and frugal; joy and anger never showed on his face.

entries.zh: 博涉經史，善屬文，工草隸書，弈棊第二品。
entries.en: He read widely in the classics and histories, wrote well, practiced clerical and cursive script, and at go held second rank.
entries.literal: He ranged widely through the classics and histories, was skilled at literary composition, practiced clerical and cursive script, and at go ranked second class.

entries.zh: 雖經綸夷險，不廢素業。
entries.en: Even through the perils of founding the state, he kept to his plain habits.
entries.literal: Though he passed through danger and ease in statecraft, he did not abandon his plain pursuits.

entries.zh: 從諫察謀，以威重得衆。
entries.en: He heard remonstrance and weighed advice, and held the host by sober gravity.
entries.literal: He accepted remonstrance and examined counsel, and by stern weight won the multitude.

entries.zh: 卽位後，身不御精細之物，敕中書舍人桓景真曰：「主衣中似有玉介導，此制始自大明末，後泰始尤增其麗。
entries.en: Once enthroned he would not touch fine things himself. He told Palace Attendant Huan Jingzhen: "The wardrobe still holds a jade sword-fitting—fashion began late in Daming and grew worse under Taishi.
entries.literal: After he took the throne he would not himself use fine and delicate things. He charged Palace Attendant Huan Jingzhen: "In the wardrobe there seems to be a jade sword-girdle ornament; this fashion began late in the Daming era, and after Taishi it grew all the more lavish.

entries.zh: 留此置主衣，政是興長疾源，可卽時打碎。
entries.en: Leave it there and you nurse the court's sickness—break it now.
entries.literal: Keep this in the wardrobe and it will only breed long sickness at court—smash it at once.

entries.zh: 凡復有可異物，皆宜隨例也。」
entries.en: Whatever else is extravagant should be treated the same."
entries.literal: Whatever else is similarly out of the way should be handled by the same rule."

entries.zh: 后宮器物欄檻以銅爲飾者，皆改用鐵，內殿施黃紗帳，宮人著紫皮履，華蓋除金花瓜，用鐵廻釘。
entries.en: In the inner quarters copper fittings on rails and screens were switched to iron; yellow gauze curtains hung in the private halls; palace women wore purple leather shoes; golden melon ornaments were stripped from the imperial canopy and iron nails used instead.
entries.literal: In the rear palace, utensils, rails, and balustrades ornamented with copper were all changed to iron; in the inner halls yellow gauze curtains were hung; palace women wore purple leather shoes; on the imperial canopy the golden melon flowers were removed and iron turning nails used instead.

entries.zh: 每曰：「使我治天下十年，當使黃金與土同價。」
entries.en: He would say, "Ten years on the throne and I would make gold worth no more than dirt."
entries.literal: He often said, "Give me ten years to rule All-under-Heaven and I would make gold the same price as earth."

entries.zh: 欲以身率天下，移變風俗。
entries.en: He meant to move the realm by example and change its habits.
entries.literal: He wished to lead All-under-Heaven by his person and shift custom.

entries.zh: 禮畢，大駕還宮，臨太極前殿。
entries.en: When the ceremony ended, the imperial procession returned to the palace and took seat before the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
entries.literal: When the rites were complete, the imperial carriage returned to the palace and attended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「五德更紹，帝迹所以代昌；
entries.en: An edict ran: "As the Five Phases turn, one throne gives way to the next.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The Five Phases succeed one another; thus imperial traces pass from house to house.

entries.zh: 三正迭隆，王度所以改耀。
entries.en: As the Three Calendars shift, the royal pattern takes a new light.
entries.literal: The Three First Months rise in turn; thus royal measure changes its splendor.

entries.zh: 世有質文，時或因革，其資元膺曆，經道振民，固以異術同揆，殊流共貫者矣。
entries.en: Each age has its plain speech and its polish, and custom bends with the times; yet those who hold Heaven's first seal, keep the Way, and rouse the people—different tools, one measure; different currents, one channel.
entries.literal: Ages have plainness and ornament, times now follow and now reform; those who bear the primal mandate, uphold the Way, and stir the people—surely they differ in method yet share one rule, diverge in stream yet run one course.

entries.zh: 朕以寡昧，屬值艱季，推肆勤之誠，藉樂治之數，賢能悉心，士民致力，用獲拯溺龕暴，一匡天下。
entries.en: I am dull and small, and came to power in bitter years; by honest toil and the arts of good government, with the worthy giving all they had and the people lending their strength, we pulled the drowned from the flood, caged the cruel, and set the realm right in a single stroke.
entries.literal: We, being shallow and dim, met a season of hardship; pushing forth the sincerity of diligence, relying on the reckoning of joyful rule, with worthies giving their hearts and gentry and people exerting their strength—we obtained rescue of the drowning and caging of the violent, and one correction of All-under-Heaven.

entries.zh: 業未參古，功殆侔昔。
entries.en: My work does not yet equal the ancients, yet my deed stands near theirs.
entries.literal: Our enterprise has not yet matched antiquity; our merit is nearly equal to the past.

entries.zh: 宋氏以陵夷有徵，歷數攸及，思弘樂推，永鑒崇替，爰集天祿于朕躬。
entries.en: Song was failing by every sign; its span had run its course. I wished only to honor the people's wish to yield, to read rise and fall in the mirror of history—and Heaven's blessing settled on me.
entries.literal: The Song house showed signs of decline; its term of years had arrived; thinking to extend the joy of yielding, forever to mirror elevation and fall, the celestial blessing was gathered upon Our person.

entries.zh: 惟志菲薄，辭弗獲昭，遂欽從天人，式繇景命，祗月正于文祖，升禋鬯于上帝。
entries.en: My heart is humble; refusal brought no peace—so I bowed to Heaven and the people, followed the bright command, set the calendar month at the shrine of Wen, and offered the sacred ale to the Lord on High.
entries.literal: Our will is slight and thin; in declining we could not win clarity—thus we reverently followed Heaven and man, took the bright mandate as our path, reverently set the month at the Wen Ancestor, and ascended to offer fragrant spirits to the Supreme Lord.

entries.zh: 猥以寡德，光宅四海，纂革代之蹤，托王公之上，若涉淵水，罔知所濟。
entries.en: With little merit I now light the four seas, take up the trail of a new dynasty, and sit above kings and lords—as a man fording deep water who cannot see the far bank.
entries.literal: Unworthily, with slight virtue, we illuminate the four seas, continue the traces of the changing age, and rest above kings and dukes—like crossing deep water, not knowing what shore to reach.

entries.zh: 寶祚初啓，洪慶惟新，思俾利澤，宣被億兆，可大赦天下。
entries.en: The throne is new and blessing is renewed. I would let favor reach every corner of the realm: let there be a general amnesty throughout the land.
entries.literal: The precious throne is newly opened; great felicity is fresh—We think to extend benefit and grace, spread it over the hundred millions: a general amnesty is proclaimed for All-under-Heaven.

entries.zh: 改昇明三年爲建元元年。
entries.en: Shengming 3 becomes the first year of Jianyuan.
entries.literal: The third year of Shengming is changed to the first year of Jianyuan.

entries.zh: 賜民爵二級，文武進位二等，鰥寡孤獨不能自存者穀人五斛。
entries.en: Commoners receive two steps of rank; civil and military officers rise two grades; widowers, widows, orphans, and the destitute alone receive five hu of grain apiece.
entries.literal: The people are granted two ranks of nobility; civil and military officers are advanced two grades; widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves are given five hu of grain each.

entries.zh: 逋租宿債勿復收。
entries.en: Back rent and old debts are forgiven.
entries.literal: Overdue rents and old debts are not to be collected again.

entries.zh: 有犯鄉論清議，贓汙淫盜，一皆蕩滌，洗除先注，與之更始。
entries.en: Offenses under village reputation law, graft, debauchery, and theft—all records are struck and names cleared for a fresh start.
entries.literal: Those guilty of village pure-criticism, corruption, lewdness, or theft—all are washed clean; prior notations are erased, and they are given a new beginning.

entries.zh: 長徒敕繫之囚，特皆原遣。
entries.en: Long-term convicts and those held by special order are pardoned and sent home.
entries.literal: Long-term exiles and prisoners under edict are specially all pardoned and released.

entries.zh: 亡官失爵，禁錮奪勞，一依舊典。」
entries.en: Men who lost posts or titles, or who were barred or stripped of corvée—each case follows the former code."
entries.literal: Those who lost office or rank, were confined or stripped of labor service—all according to the old statutes."

entries.zh: 秋七月丁未，詔曰：「交阯比景，獨隔書朔，斯乃前運方季，負海不朝，因迷遂往，歸款莫由。
entries.en: Autumn, seventh month, day dingwei: an edict said: "Jiaozhi and Biying lie beyond our maps and calendars—remnants of a failing age, facing the sea yet never bowing; they wandered in error with no way home.
entries.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day dingwei: an edict said: "Jiaozhi and Biying stand alone beyond our written calendar—this is the late fortune of a former age, facing the sea yet not coming to court; lost in error they went on, and there was no road back to allegiance.

entries.zh: 曲赦交州部內李叔獻一人卽撫南士，文武詳才選用。
entries.en: Jiao province receives a special pardon for Li Shuxian alone, that he may settle the south; worthy civil and military men are to be chosen carefully.
entries.literal: A special pardon is granted within Jiao Province to Li Shuxian alone, that he may pacify the southern lands; civil and military talent is to be chosen with care.

entries.zh: 幷遣大使宣揚朝恩。」
entries.en: Great envoys will carry the throne's mercy abroad."
entries.literal: Great envoys are also sent to proclaim the court's grace."

entries.zh: 以試守武平太守行交州府事李叔獻爲交州刺史。
entries.en: Li Shuxian, acting administrator of Wuping and acting for Jiao province, became inspector of Jiao.
entries.literal: Acting Administrator of Wuping, holding the office of Jiao Province, Li Shuxian was made Inspector of Jiao Province.

entries.zh: 丙辰，以虜偽茄蘆鎮主陰平公楊廣香爲沙州刺史。
entries.en: Day bingchen: Yang Guangxiang of Yinping, lord of the barbarian fort Qielu, became inspector of Sha.
entries.literal: On day bingchen Yang Guangxiang, Duke of Yinping, lord of the enemy fort Qielu, was made Inspector of Sha Province.

entries.zh: 丁巳，詔「南蘭陵桑梓本鄉，長蠲租布；
entries.en: Day dingsi: "Southern Lanling, the clan's home, is forever free of grain rent and cloth tax;
entries.literal: On day dingsi an edict: "Southern Lanling, native district of the imperial clan, is permanently exempt from land tax and cloth levy;

entries.zh: 武進王業所基，復十年。」
entries.en: Wujin, where the house first rose, is exempt for ten years."
entries.literal: Wujin, base of the royal house's enterprise, is exempt for ten years."

entries.zh: 以司空褚淵爲司徒，吳郡太守柳世隆爲南豫州刺史。
entries.en: Chu Yuan, minister of works, became grand minister; Liu Shilong, administrator of Wu, became inspector of South Yuzhou.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Chu Yuan was made Grand Minister; Administrator of Wu Commandery Liu Shilong was made Inspector of South Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「宸運肇創，實命惟新，宜弘慶宥，廣敷蠲汰。
entries.en: An edict said: "The throne is new and the charge is new—let mercy run wide and burdens be lifted.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The imperial fortune is newly founded; the mandate is fresh—felicity and pardon should be broadly spread, and exemptions widely granted.

entries.zh: 劫賊餘口沒在臺府者，悉原放。
entries.en: Captives left from rebel raids and held in central offices are all freed.
entries.literal: Surviving captives of bandit raids held in the palace offices are all pardoned and released.

entries.zh: 諸負釁流徙，普聽還本土。」
entries.en: Exiles and banished men may return home."
entries.literal: All who bear guilt and were exiled or banished may generally hear that they may return to their native lands."

entries.zh: 以齊國左衛將軍陳顯達爲中護軍，中領軍王敬則爲南兖州刺史，左衛將軍李安民爲中領軍。
entries.en: Chen Xianda, left guards general of Qi, became director of the central guard; Wang Jingze, central army commander, inspector of South Yanzhou; Li Anmin, left guards general, central army commander.
entries.literal: Left Guards General of Qi State Chen Xianda was made Director of the Central Guard; Central Army Commander Wang Jingze was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; Left Guards General Li Anmin was made Central Army Commander.

entries.zh: 戊戌，以荊州刺史嶷爲尚書令、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史，冠軍將軍映爲荊州刺史，西中郎將晃爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍垣崇祖爲豫州刺史，驃騎司馬崔文仲爲徐州刺史。
entries.en: Day wuxu: Yi, inspector of Jing, became director of the master of writing, general-in-chief who spreads might, with secretariat equal to the three excellencies, and inspector of Yang; Ying, champion general, inspector of Jing; Huang, west general of the gentlemen, inspector of South Xuzhou; Yuan Chongzu, champion general, inspector of Yu; Cui Wenzong, chief commandant under the general who spreads might, inspector of Xu.
entries.literal: On day wuxu, Inspector of Jing Province Luan was made Director of the Master of Writing, General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might, with Grand Secretariat and staff equal to the Three Excellencies, and Inspector of Yang Province; General Who Vanquishes the Foe Ying was made Inspector of Jing Province; West General of the Gentlemen Huang was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; General Who Vanquishes the Foe Yuan Chongzu was made Inspector of Yu Province; Chief Commandant of the General Who Spreads Might Cui Wenzong was made Inspector of Xu Province.

entries.zh: 九月辛丑，詔「二吳、義興三郡遭水，減今年田租。」
entries.en: Ninth month, day xinchou: "The two Wu districts and Yixing, all three struck by flood, pay reduced field tax this year."
entries.literal: Ninth month, day xinchou: an edict—"The two Wu commanderies and Yixing—three circuits—suffered flood; this year's field tax is reduced."

entries.zh: 乙巳，以新除尚書令、驃騎將軍豫章王嶷爲荊、湘二州刺史，平西將軍臨川王映爲揚州刺史。
entries.en: Day yisi: Yi, new director of the master of writing and general who spreads might, prince of Yuzhang, took Jing and Xiang; Ying, prince of Linchuan and general who pacifies the west, took Yang.
entries.literal: On day yisi the newly appointed Director of the Master of Writing, General-in-Chief Who Spreads Might, Prince of Yuzhang Luan was made Inspector of Jing and Xiang; General Who Pacifies the West, Prince of Linchuan Ying was made Inspector of Yang.

entries.zh: 丙午，司空褚淵領尚書令。
entries.en: Day bingwu: Chu Yuan, minister of works, also directed the master of writing.
entries.literal: On day bingwu Minister of Works Chu Yuan also held the office of Director of the Master of Writing.

entries.zh: 戊申，車駕幸宣武堂宴會，詔諸王公以下賦詩。
entries.en: Day wushen: the emperor feasted at Xuanwu Hall and ordered every prince and noble down the line to write a poem.
entries.literal: On day wushen the imperial carriage visited the Xuanwu Hall for a banquet; an edict ordered all princes and dukes downward to compose poems.

entries.zh: 十二月戊戌，以司空褚淵爲司徒。
entries.en: Twelfth month, day wuxu: Chu Yuan moved from minister of works to minister over the masses.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month, day wuxu, Minister of Works Chu Yuan was made Minister over the Masses.

entries.zh: 乙巳，車駕幸中堂聽訟。
entries.en: On day yisi the emperor heard cases in the Central Hall.
entries.literal: On day yisi the imperial carriage visited the Central Hall to hear lawsuits.

entries.zh: 壬子，以驃騎大將軍豫章王嶷爲司空，揚州刺史、前將軍臨川王映爲荊州刺史。
entries.en: On day renzi, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Yi, general of agile cavalry, became minister of works; Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying, forward general and inspector of Yangzhou, took Jing.
entries.literal: On day renzi, General of Agile Cavalry, Prince of Yuzhang Xiao Luan was made Minister of Works; Inspector of Yangzhou, Forward General, Prince of Linchuan Xiao Ying was made Inspector of Jing.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第二 本紀第二
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 2, Annals 2
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 2, Annals 2

entries.zh: 二月丙子，以左衛將軍、巴東王子響爲中護軍。
entries.en: Second month, day bingzi: Xiao Zixiang, prince of Badong and general of the left guard, became central protector of the army.
entries.literal: Second month, day bingzi: General of the Left Guard, Prince of Badong Xiao Zixiang, was made Central Protector of the Army.

entries.zh: 己丑，詔曰：「宣尼誕敷文德，峻極自天，發輝七代，陶鈞萬品，英風獨舉，素王誰匹！
entries.en: Day jichou: an edict said, "Confucius was born to spread the civil Way, lofty as heaven; seven generations felt his light, ten thousand things felt his mold; his wind stood alone—what king without a crown could equal him?
entries.literal: On day jichou, an edict said: "Confucius spread civil virtue from birth, lofty to the heavens; his radiance shone through seven generations and shaped ten thousand kinds of things; his noble wind stood alone—what uncrowned king could match him!

entries.zh: 功隱於當年，道深於日月。
entries.en: His merit lay hidden in his lifetime; his Way runs deeper than sun and moon.
entries.literal: His achievement was hidden in his own age, his Way deeper than sun and moon.

entries.zh: 感麟厭世，緬邈千祀，川竭谷虛，丘夷淵塞，非但洙泗湮淪，至乃饗嘗乏主。
entries.en: When the qilin came he wearied of the age and left it; a thousand years stand between us; rivers fail, valleys hollow, hills sink and depths close—not only did Zhu and Si fall silent, but even the sacrifices had no keeper.
entries.literal: Sensing the qilin, he loathed the world and passed away; a thousand years stretch remote; rivers dry and valleys empty, mounds level and abysses filled—not only were the Zhu and Si lost, but even the sacrificial offerings lacked a master.

entries.zh: 前王敬仰，崇脩寢廟，歲月亟流，鞠爲茂草。
entries.en: Earlier kings honored him and raised his shrine; the years raced by, and it turned to wild grass.
entries.literal: Former kings revered him and grandly repaired the temple; years flowed swiftly, and it became rank grass.

entries.zh: 今學敩興立，實稟洪規，撫事懷人，彌增欽屬。
entries.en: Now schools rise again on his great pattern; handling state, I cherish the man and my awe only grows.
entries.literal: Now learning and instruction are established—truly inheriting his great rule; as I handle affairs I cherish the man all the more and my reverence deepens.

entries.zh: 可改築宗祊，務在爽塏。
entries.en: Rebuild the ancestral shrine on high, open ground.
entries.literal: The ancestral temple may be rebuilt, striving for bright and open ground.

entries.zh: 量給祭秩，禮同諸侯。
entries.en: Grant sacrificial income by measure, with rites equal to a feudal lord.
entries.literal: Measure out sacrificial stipends; the rites are the same as for feudal lords.

entries.zh: 奉聖之爵，以時紹繼。」
entries.en: Let the Fengsheng marquisate pass in due time."
entries.literal: The fief of Fengsheng is to be continued in its season."

entries.zh: 壬寅，以丹陽尹王晏爲江州刺史。
entries.en: Day renyin: Wang Yan, intendant of Danyang, was made inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: On day renyin, Palace Attendant Wang Yan was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以巴陵王子倫爲豫州刺史。
entries.en: Day guimao: Xiao Zilun, prince of Baling, took Yu.
entries.literal: On day guimao, Prince of Baling Xiao Zilun was made Inspector of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 九年春正月甲午，以侍中江夏王鋒爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍劉悛爲益州刺史。
entries.en: Year 9, spring, first month, day jiawu: Xiao Feng, prince of Jiangxia and palace attendant, took South Xu; Liu Min, champion general, took Yi.
entries.literal: Year 9, spring, first month, day jiawu: Palace Attendant, Prince of Jiangxia Xiao Feng, was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; Champion General Liu Min was made Inspector of Yizhou.

entries.zh: 辛丑，車駕祠南郊，詔「京師見囚繫，詳量原遣。」
entries.en: Day xinchou: the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and ordered, "Review the prisoners in the capital and release them where mercy allows."
entries.literal: Day xinchou: the imperial carriage worshipped at the southern suburb; an edict said: "Prisoners now held in the capital—consider carefully and release as appropriate."

entries.zh: 秋九月戊辰，車駕幸琅邪城講武，觀者傾都，普頒酒肉。
entries.en: Autumn, ninth month, day wuchen: the emperor reviewed arms at Langya; the city poured out to watch, and wine and meat were given to all.
entries.literal: Autumn, ninth month, day wuchen: the imperial carriage visited Langya city for martial drill; the whole capital turned out to watch, and wine and meat were given broadly.

entries.zh: 冬十月乙丑，車駕幸玄武湖講武。
entries.en: Winter, tenth month, day yichou: the emperor drilled troops at Black Tortoise Lake.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, day yichou: the imperial carriage visited the Black Tortoise Lake for martial drill.

entries.zh: 甲午，車駕殷祠太廟。
entries.en: Day jiawu: the emperor performed the close rite at the Imperial Temple.
entries.literal: Day jiawu: the imperial carriage performed the close ancestral rite at the Imperial Temple.

entries.zh: 十二月乙丑，以振威將軍陳僧授爲越州刺史。
entries.en: Twelfth month, day yichou: Chen Sengshou, quelling-might general, took Yue.
entries.literal: Twelfth month, day yichou: Quelling Might General Chen Sengshou was made Inspector of Yuezhou.

entries.zh: 戊寅，詔「尚書丞郎職事繁劇，䘏俸未優，可量增賜祿。」
entries.en: Day wuyin: an edict said, "The Masters of Writing and their aides bear heavy work for thin pay—raise their stipends as fits."
entries.literal: Day wuyin, an edict said: "The directors and gentlemen of the Masters of Writing—their duties are dense and taxing, their stipends not generous—may receive measured increases in salary."

entries.zh: 己卯，皇子子建爲湘東王。
entries.en: Day jimao: the imperial prince Zijian was made king of Xiangdong.
entries.literal: Day jimao: Imperial prince Zijian was made King of Xiangdong.

entries.zh: 癸巳，以監青冀二州軍、行刺史事張沖爲青、冀二州刺史。
entries.en: Day guisi: Zhang Chong, overseer of Qing and Ji and acting inspector, took Qing and Ji.
entries.literal: Day guisi: Zhang Chong, overseer of Qing and Ji military affairs acting inspector, was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.

entries.zh: 夏四月乙亥，有司奏：「舊格一年兩過行陵，三月十五日曹郎以下小行，九月十五日司空以下大行。
entries.en: Summer, fourth month, day yihai: the offices reported, "The old rule called for two tomb visits a year—the fifteenth of the third month, a minor visit for Masters of Writing gentlemen and below; the fifteenth of the ninth, a major visit for the Minister of Works and below.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month, day yihai: the relevant offices memorialized: "By the old rule there were two tomb visits a year—on the fifteenth of the third month a minor visit for gentlemen of the Masters of Writing and below, and on the fifteenth of the ninth month a major visit for the Minister of Works and below.

entries.zh: 今長停小行，唯二州一大行。」
entries.en: Suspend the minor visit for good; hold one major visit every two years."
entries.literal: Now the minor visit is permanently suspended; only one major visit for the two provinces."

entries.zh: 詔曰：「可。」
entries.en: The edict said, "So be it."
entries.literal: An edict said: "Approved."

entries.zh: 十年春正月戊午，詔「諸責負衆逋七年以前，悉原除。
entries.en: Year 10, spring, first month, day wuwu: an edict said, "Every public and private debt seven years old or more is wiped clean.
entries.literal: Year 10, spring, first month, day wuwu, an edict said: "All public and private debts seven years old or more are entirely remitted.

entries.zh: 高貲不在例。
entries.en: Usurious loans are excepted.
entries.literal: High-interest loans are not included.

entries.zh: 孤老六疾，人穀五斛。
entries.en: Orphans, the aged, and the six classes of the sick receive five piculs of grain each.
entries.literal: Orphans, the elderly, and the six kinds of affliction—five piculs of grain per person.

entries.zh: 內外有務衆官增祿俸。」
entries.en: Officials with heavy duties inside and outside the court get higher pay."
entries.literal: All officials inside and outside with pressing duties receive increased stipends."

entries.zh: 以左民尚書南平王銳爲湘州刺史，司徒竟陵王子良領尚書令，右衛將軍王玄邈爲北徐州刺史，中軍將軍廬陵王子卿進號車騎將軍，北中郎將南海王子罕爲兖州刺史，輔國將軍臨汝公昭文爲南豫州刺史，冠軍將軍王文和爲北兖州刺史。
entries.en: Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and minister for the people, took Xiang; Xiao Ziliang, prince of Jingling and minister over the masses, concurrently headed the Masters of Writing; Wang Xuanmiao, right guard general, took North Xu; Xiao Ziqing, prince of Luling and central army general, became general of chariots and cavalry; Xiao Zihan, prince of Nanhai and north bureau general, took Yan; Zhaowen, duke of Linru and supporter of the state, took South Yu; Wang Wenhe, champion general, took North Yan.
entries.literal: Prince of Nanping Xiao Rui, Minister for the People, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou; Minister over the Masses, Prince of Jingling Xiao Ziliang, concurrently held Director of the Masters of Writing; Right Guard General Wang Xuanmiao was made Inspector of North Xuzhou; Central Army General, Prince of Luling Xiao Ziqing, was advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry; North Bureau General, Prince of Nanhai Xiao Zihan, was made Inspector of Yanzhou; Supporter of the State, Duke of Linru Zhaowen, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou; Champion General Wang Wenhe was made Inspector of North Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 十一月戊午，詔曰：「頃者霖雨，樵糧稍貴，京邑居民，多離其弊。
entries.en: Eleventh month, day wuwu: an edict said, "These rains have driven up the price of fuel and grain; the capital's people are hard hit.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, day wuwu, an edict said: "Lately the rains have made firewood and grain dear; residents of the capital suffer greatly.

entries.zh: 遣中書舍人、二縣官長賑賜。」
entries.en: Send palace secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties to give relief."
entries.literal: Send Palace Secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties for relief grants."

entries.zh: 十一年春正月癸丑，詔「京師見繫囚，詳所原遣」。
entries.en: Year 11, spring, first month, day guichou: an edict said, "Every prisoner held in the capital is to be reviewed in detail for pardon and release."
entries.literal: Year 11, spring, first month, day guichou: an edict said, "Prisoners held in the capital—examine them in detail for pardon and release."

entries.zh: 以驃騎大將軍王敬則為司空，江州刺史鄱陽王鏘為領軍將軍，鎮軍大將軍陳顯達為江州刺史，右衞將軍崔慧景為豫州刺史。
entries.en: Wang Jingze, grand general of agile cavalry, became minister of works; Xiao Qiang, king of Poyang and inspector of Jiangzhou, became leader of the army; Chen Xianda, pacifying-army grand general, took Jiangzhou; Cui Huijing, general of the right guard, took Yu.
entries.literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry Wang Jingze was made Minister of Works; Inspector of Jiangzhou Xiao Qiang, King of Poyang, was made Leader of the Army; Pacifying Army Grand General Chen Xianda was made Inspector of Jiangzhou; General of the Right Guard Cui Huijing was made Inspector of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 丙子，皇太子長懋薨。
entries.en: Day bingzi: Crown Prince Changmao died.
entries.literal: Day bingzi: Crown Prince Changmao died.

entries.zh: 是月，上不豫，徙御延昌殿，乘輿始登階，而殿屋鳴吒，上惡之。
entries.en: That month the emperor fell ill and moved to Yan-chang Hall. As he mounted the steps, the timbers groaned—the omen sickened him.
entries.literal: That month the emperor was unwell; he moved his residence to the Yan-chang Hall. When the imperial carriage had just mounted the steps, the hall beams roared and creaked—the emperor hated this.

entries.zh: 虜侵邊，戊辰，遣江州刺史陳顯達鎮雍州樊城。
entries.en: Barbarians struck the frontier; day wuchen: Chen Xianda, inspector of Jiang, was sent to hold Fancheng in Yong.
entries.literal: The barbarians raided the border; day wuchen: Inspector of Jiangzhou Chen Xianda was sent to garrison Fancheng in Yongzhou.

entries.zh: 上慮朝野憂惶，乃力疾召樂府奏正聲伎。
entries.en: Lest court and country panic, he roused himself in his sickness and had the Music Office play the orthodox repertoire.
entries.literal: The emperor, fearing anxiety in court and country, forced himself despite illness to summon the Music Office to perform orthodox pieces.

entries.zh: 戊寅，大漸。
entries.en: Day wuyin: the end drew near.
entries.literal: Day wuyin: he approached the final hour.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「始終大期，賢聖不免，吾行年六十，亦復何恨。
entries.en: An edict said, "Beginnings and endings come to every man, sage or simpleton; I am sixty—what is there to regret?
entries.literal: An edict said: "From first to last, the great term—even sages cannot escape it. I have lived sixty years; what is there to regret?

entries.zh: 但皇業艱難，萬機事重，不能無遺慮耳。
entries.en: Yet the throne was hard-won and the realm is heavy—I leave cares behind.
entries.literal: But the imperial enterprise is hard, and the myriad affairs weighty—I cannot be without lingering cares.

entries.zh: 太孫進德日茂，社稷有寄。
entries.en: The Grand Heir grows worthier by the day; the altars have their heir.
entries.literal: The Grand Heir grows in virtue day by day; the altars have one to rely on.

entries.zh: 子良善相毗輔，思弘治道；
entries.en: Ziliang knows how to assist—carry the policy of good government forward;
entries.literal: Ziliang is good at aiding and supporting—think to expand the way of rule;

entries.zh: 內外衆事，無大小悉與鸞參懷，共下意。
entries.en: within and without, great affairs and small—take counsel with Luan and speak with one mind.
entries.literal: inside and outside, matters great and small—all consult with Luan and share your intent.

entries.zh: 尚書中是職務根本，悉委王晏、徐孝嗣。
entries.en: The Masters of Writing are the root of government—leave them to Wang Yan and Xu Xiaosi.
entries.literal: Within the Masters of Writing lies the root of office—entrust it wholly to Wang Yan and Xu Xiaosi.

entries.zh: 軍旅捍邊之略，委王敬則、陳顯達、王廣之、王玄邈、沈文季、張瑰、薛淵等。
entries.en: Border defense goes to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanmiao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest.
entries.literal: The strategy of armies defending the border—entrust it to Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, Wang Xuanmiao, Shen Wenji, Zhang Gui, Xue Yuan, and the rest.

entries.zh: 百辟庶僚，各奉爾職，謹事太孫，勿有懈怠。
entries.en: Every minister and clerk—keep your charge, serve the Grand Heir, and do not grow slack.
entries.literal: All the hundred offices and the host of clerks—each keep your post, serve the Grand Heir faithfully, and do not slacken.

entries.zh: 知復何言。」
entries.en: I have said enough."
entries.literal: What more is there to say?"

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「我識滅之後，身上著夏衣，畫天衣，純烏犀導，應諸器悉不得用寶物及織成等，唯裝復裌衣各一通。
entries.en: Another edict said, "When I am gone, dress me in summer robes and painted heaven-garments, with a plain rhinoceros-horn belt; no precious ware or brocade in the rites—only one set of lined robes and one of padded robes for the coffin.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "After my consciousness is extinguished, on my body wear summer clothes and painted heaven garments, a pure rhinoceros-horn belt; all utensils must not use precious things or woven brocades—only one set each of lined and padded burial garments.

entries.zh: 常所服身刀長短二口鐵環者，隨我入梓宮。
entries.en: The two iron-ringed knives I wore at my side, long and short—bury them with me.
entries.literal: The personal knives I usually wear, long and short, two with iron rings—let them enter the inner coffin with me.

entries.zh: 祭敬之典，本在因心，東鄰殺牛，不如西家禴祭。
entries.en: Sacrifice is a matter of the heart; the neighbor who kills an ox is outdone by the neighbor who offers a simple spring prayer.
entries.literal: Sacrificial reverence lies in the heart; the eastern neighbor slaughters an ox, yet it is not as good as the western family's simple spring rite.

entries.zh: 我靈上慎勿以牲爲祭，唯設餅、茶飲、干飯、酒脯而已。
entries.en: At my spirit seat use no sacrificial beasts—only cakes, tea, dried grain, wine, and dried meats.
entries.literal: At my spirit altar be careful not to use victims; set out only cakes, tea, dried grain, wine, and dried meats.

entries.zh: 天下貴賤，咸同此制。
entries.en: High and low alike—let the realm follow this rule.
entries.literal: High and low throughout the realm—all follow this rule.

entries.zh: 未山陵前，朔望設菜食。
entries.en: Until the tomb is finished, on the new and full moon offer vegetarian food.
entries.literal: Before the hill tomb is complete, on the first and fifteenth of the month offer vegetable food.

entries.zh: 陵墓萬世所宅，意嘗恨休安陵未稱，今可用東三處地最東邊以葬我，名爲景安陵。
entries.en: A tomb is a home for ages; I always thought Xiuan Tomb unworthy—bury me on the easternmost of the three eastern plots and call it Jing'an Tomb.
entries.literal: The tomb is the dwelling for ten thousand ages; I have long regretted that Xiuan Tomb was not fitting—now the easternmost of the three eastern sites may be used to bury me; name it Jing'an Tomb.

entries.zh: 喪禮每存省約，不須煩民。
entries.en: Keep the funeral spare—do not burden the people.
entries.literal: Funeral rites should always be kept spare—do not trouble the people.

entries.zh: 百官停六時入臨，朔望祖日可依舊。
entries.en: Let the ministers end the six watches at the tomb; new moon, full moon, and ancestral days follow custom.
entries.literal: The hundred offices stop the six sessions of attendance at the tomb; on the new and full moon and the ancestral day follow the old practice.

entries.zh: 諸主六宮，並不須從山陵。
entries.en: Princesses and the palace women need not go to the tomb.
entries.literal: All princesses and the six palaces—none need follow the hill tomb.

entries.zh: 內殿鳳華、壽昌、耀靈三處，是吾所治制。
entries.en: Inside the palace, Fenghua, Shouchang, and Yaoling—the three halls I had made my own.
entries.literal: Within the inner palace, the three halls Fenghua, Shouchang, and Yaoling are quarters I had built.

entries.zh: 夫貴有天下，富兼四海，宴處寢息，不容乃陋，謂此爲奢儉之中，慎勿壞去。
entries.en: A man who owns the realm need not sleep rough; I aimed at the mean between show and spare—do not tear those halls down.
entries.literal: To hold the realm and the wealth of the four seas—yet where one dwells and rests cannot be crude; I call this the mean between luxury and austerity; do not demolish them.

entries.zh: 顯陽殿玉像諸佛及供養，具如別牒，可盡心禮拜供養之。
entries.en: The jade Buddhas in Xianyang Hall and their offerings—follow the separate memorial and tend them faithfully.
entries.literal: The jade Buddhas of Xianyang Hall and their offerings—as in the separate memorial, worship and supply them with full devotion.

entries.zh: 應有功德事，可專在中。
entries.en: Works of merit may be kept within the inner palace.
entries.literal: Merit works that should be done may be concentrated in the inner palace.

entries.zh: 自今公私皆不得出家爲道，及起立塔寺，以宅爲精舍，竝嚴斷之。
entries.en: Hereafter neither court nor household may ordain monks, raise pagodas, or turn a house into a chapel—the ban is absolute.
entries.literal: From now on, public and private alike may not leave home for the Way, erect pagodas and temples, or turn a residence into a cloister—all are strictly forbidden.

entries.zh: 唯年六十，必有道心，聽朝賢選序，已有別詔。
entries.en: Only at sixty, with a settled will for the Way, may worthies of the court be chosen in turn—as the other edict already provides.
entries.literal: Only at age sixty, when the mind for the Way is sure, may court worthies be selected in order, as already provided in a separate edict.

entries.zh: 諸小小賜乞，及閤內處分，亦有別牒。
entries.en: Small gifts and favors, and orders for the inner quarters—see the separate memorial.
entries.literal: Petty grants and requests, and dispositions within the inner quarters—as in the separate memorial.

entries.zh: 內外禁衛勞舊主帥左右，悉付蕭諶優量驅使之，勿負吾遺意也。」
entries.en: The inner and outer guards who have long served at my side—give them all to Xiao Chen, treat them well and set them to useful work, and do not betray what I mean you to do."
entries.literal: The long-serving commanders and attendants of the inner and outer palace guards—entrust them all to Xiao Chen, treat them generously and employ them as fits, and do not betray my dying wish.

entries.zh: 是日上崩，年五十四。
entries.en: That same day the emperor died. He was fifty-four.
entries.literal: That day the emperor died, aged fifty-four.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第三 本紀第三
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3

entries.zh: 鬱林王昭業，字元尚，文惠太子長子也。
entries.en: The Prince of Yulin, Zhaoye, bore the style Yuanshang and was the eldest son of Crown Prince Wenhui.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yulin, Zhaoye, styled Yuanshang, was the eldest son of Crown Prince Wenhui.

entries.zh: 小名法身。
entries.en: In childhood he was called Fashen.
entries.literal: His childhood name was Fashen.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，封南郡王，二千戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended, he was made prince of Nan commandery with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Nan commandery with two thousand households.

entries.zh: 永明五年十一月戊子，冠於東宮崇政殿。
entries.en: Yongming 5, eleventh month, day wuzi: he received the cap in the Eastern Palace's Chongzheng Hall.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, eleventh month, day wuzi, he was capped in the Chongzheng Hall of the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 其日小會，賜王公以下帛各有差，給昭業扶二人。
entries.en: That day the court held a minor feast and gave graded gifts of silk to princes and dukes and below; Zhaoye was given two attendants to steady him at the rite.
entries.literal: That day a small gathering was held; princes and dukes down were granted silk in graded amounts, and two arm-support attendants were given to Zhaoye.

entries.zh: 七年，有司奏給班劔二十人，鼓吹一部，高選友、學。
entries.en: In the seventh year the authorities asked to grant him twenty ceremonial halberd-bearers, a full pipe-and-drum band, and a high-grade pick of companions and tutors.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, the relevant office memorialized granting twenty halberd-bearers of the guard, one set of pipes and drums, and a careful selection of companions and tutors.

entries.zh: 十一年，給皁輪三望車。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he was given a black-wheeled carriage with a triple awning.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, a black-wheeled triple-canopy carriage was granted.

entries.zh: 詔高選國官。
entries.en: An edict called for a careful selection of officials for his household.
entries.literal: An edict ordered a careful selection of state officials.

entries.zh: 文惠太子薨，立昭業爲皇太孫，居東宮。
entries.en: After Crown Prince Wenhui died, Zhaoye was made imperial grandson-heir and moved into the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhui died, Zhaoye was established as imperial grandson-heir and dwelt in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，太孫卽位。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu died, the imperial grandson-heir ascended.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu died, the imperial grandson-heir took the throne.

entries.zh: 昭業少美容止，好隸書，世祖勑皇孫手書不得妄出，以貴重之。
entries.en: Zhaoye was handsome in youth and loved clerical script; Emperor Wu commanded that the great-grandson's hand must not circulate casually, holding it precious.
entries.literal: Zhaoye in youth had a fine countenance and bearing and loved clerical script; Emperor Wu ordered that the imperial grandson's own writing must not be sent out rashly, treating it as precious.

entries.zh: 進對音吐，甚有令譽。
entries.en: When he answered in audience, his voice and manner won high praise.
entries.literal: In audience his speech and tone were most praised.

entries.zh: 王侯五日一問訊，世祖常獨呼昭業至幄座，別加撫問，呼爲法身，鍾愛甚重。
entries.en: Princes and dukes attended court every five days, but Emperor Wu often summoned Zhaoye alone to the curtained seat for extra questioning, called him Fashen, and doted on him exceedingly.
entries.literal: Princes and dukes paid court every five days; Emperor Wu would often call Zhaoye alone to the curtained seat and question him with special favor, calling him Fashen, and cherished him deeply.

entries.zh: 文惠皇太子薨，昭業每臨哭，輒號咷不自勝，俄爾還內，歡笑極樂。
entries.en: After Crown Prince Wenhui died, whenever Zhaoye came to the mourning hall he would howl until he lost control; in a breath he would go back inside and laugh and revel to the full.
entries.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhui died, whenever Zhaoye came to mourn he would wail until he could not master himself; a moment later he would return inside and laugh and rejoice to the utmost.

entries.zh: 在世祖喪，哭泣竟，入後宮，嘗列胡妓二部夾閤迎奏。
entries.en: During Emperor Wu's mourning, as soon as the wailing ended he went to the inner palace and once lined two troupes of Hu performers on either side of the gate to greet him with music.
entries.literal: During Emperor Wu's mourning, when the weeping was finished he entered the rear palace and once had two companies of Hu entertainers set on either side of the gate to welcome him with music.

entries.zh: 爲南郡王時，文惠太子禁其起居，節其用度，昭業謂豫章王妃庾氏曰：「阿婆，佛法言，有福德生帝王家。
entries.en: As prince of Nan commandery, Crown Prince Wenhui controlled his movements and cut his allowance; Zhaoye told the princess of Yuzhang, Lady Yu: "Granny, the Buddha says those with merit and fortune are born into a royal house.
entries.literal: When he was Prince of Nan commandery, Crown Prince Wenhui restricted his comings and goings and curbed his expenses; Zhaoye said to the Princess of Yuzhang, Lady Yu of the household: "Grandmother, Buddhist teaching says that those with merit and fortune are born into an imperial house.

entries.zh: 今日見作天王，便是大罪，左右主帥，動見拘執，不如作市邊屠酤富兒百倍矣。」
entries.en: Now they have made me a king—that is the great sin; the stewards on every side bind me; I would rather be a rich butcher or tavern-keeper by the market a hundred times over."
entries.literal: Today I am made a king—that is a great crime; the stewards left and right seize me at every turn; better to be a rich butcher or wine-seller by the market a hundred times over."

entries.zh: 及卽位，極意賞賜，動百數十萬。
entries.en: Once enthroned he gave with abandon, each gift running to hundreds of thousands.
entries.literal: Once he took the throne, he rewarded with extreme liberality, each time in sums of hundreds of thousands.

entries.zh: 每見錢，輒曰：「我昔時思汝一文不得，今得用汝未？」
entries.en: Whenever he saw cash he would say: "Once I longed for you and could not get a single coin—may I spend you now?"
entries.literal: Whenever he saw money he would say: "In old days I longed for you and could not get a single cash—may I use you now?"

entries.zh: 朞年之間，世祖齋庫儲錢數億垂盡。
entries.en: Within a year the several hundred million in Emperor Wu's fasting treasury and stored coin was nearly spent.
entries.literal: Within a year Emperor Wu's fasting treasury and stored coin, several hundred million, was nearly exhausted.

entries.zh: 開主衣庫與皇后寵姬觀之，給閹人豎子各數人，隨其所欲，恣意輦取；
entries.en: He opened the imperial wardrobe for the empress and her favorites to see, gave several eunuch boys to each to take what they pleased and cart away at will;
entries.literal: He opened the lord's wardrobe and viewed it with the empress and her favored ladies, giving eunuch lads several men apiece to take what they wished and cart away at will;

entries.zh: 取諸寶器以相剖擊破碎之，以爲笑樂。
entries.en: they seized jewels and vessels and smashed them against each other for sport.
entries.literal: they took various treasures and smashed them against one another for laughter.

entries.zh: 居嘗裸袒，著紅穀褌雜采衵服。
entries.en: At leisure he often went bare-chested in red silk drawers and parti-colored inner robes.
entries.literal: At home he often went bare-chested, wearing red silk drawers and motley under-robes.

entries.zh: 好鬥雞，密買雞至數千價。
entries.en: He loved cockfighting and secretly bought cocks for several thousand cash apiece.
entries.literal: He loved cockfighting and secretly bought birds worth several thousand cash each.

entries.zh: 世祖御物甘草杖，宮人寸斷用之。
entries.en: Emperor Wu's sweet-reed walking staff was chopped inch by inch by palace women for their own use.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu's personal cane of sweet-reed was cut inch by inch by palace women for use.

entries.zh: 毀世祖招婉殿，乞閹人徐龍駒爲齋。
entries.en: He tore down Emperor Wu's Zhaowan Hall and asked the eunuch Xu Longju to keep a fast for him.
entries.literal: He destroyed Emperor Wu's Zhaowan Hall and begged the eunuch Xu Longju for a fast.

entries.zh: 龍駒尤親幸，爲後閤舍人，日夜在六宮房內。
entries.en: Longju was especially intimate, made householder of the rear pavilion, and day and night stayed in the six palaces' rooms.
entries.literal: Longju was especially favored and made rear-pavilion householder, staying day and night in the six palaces' chambers.

entries.zh: 昭業與文帝幸姬霍氏淫通，龍駒勸長留宮內，聲云度霍氏爲尼，以餘人代之。
entries.en: Zhaoye lay with Emperor Wen's favored lady, Lady Huo; Longju urged him to linger in the palace, saying he would have Lady Huo take the tonsure and put another in her place.
entries.literal: Zhaoye had illicit relations with Emperor Wen's favored lady, Lady Huo; Longju urged him to stay long in the palace, claiming he would have Lady Huo tonsured as a nun and replace her with another.

entries.zh: 嘗以邪諂自進，每謂人曰：「古時亦有監作三公者。」
entries.en: He once rose by sycophancy and often told people: "In antiquity there were supervisors who became one of the three dukes too."
entries.literal: He once advanced by flattery and often said to people: "In old times there were also overseers who became one of the Three Dukes."

entries.zh: 皇后亦淫亂，齋閤通夜洞開，內外淆雜，無復分別。
entries.en: The empress was debauched as well; the fasting pavilion stayed open through the night, court and camp mingled without distinction.
entries.literal: The empress also was dissolute; the fasting pavilion stood open all night, inside and outside tangled together without distinction.

entries.zh: 九月癸丑，詔「東西二省府國，長老所積，財單祿寡，良以矜懷。
entries.en: Ninth month, day guichou: an edict ran: "In the eastern and western secretariats, palace offices, and princely households, men who have served long yet are poor in goods and thin in salary stir our pity.
entries.literal: Ninth month, day guichou: An edict: "In the eastern and western two provinces, palace bureaus, and princely establishments, those who have labored long but whose wealth is thin and stipends few move us deeply to compassion.

entries.zh: 選部可甄才品能，推校年月，邦守邑丞，隨宜量處，以貧爲先。」
entries.en: Let the selection bureau weigh talent and rank, check years of service, and let prefects and magistrates place men as fits—always putting the needy first."
entries.literal: The Selection Bureau may sift talent and capacity, weigh years of service, and district heads and magistrates may dispose as fit, with poverty foremost."

entries.zh: 辛酉，追尊文惠皇太子爲世宗文皇帝。
entries.en: Day xinyou: Crown Prince Wenhui was raised posthumously to Emperor Wen, canonically titled Shizong.
entries.literal: Day xinyou: Crown Prince Wenhui was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, canonically titled Shizong.

entries.zh: 癸巳，皇太后令曰：「鎮軍、車騎、左僕射、前將軍、領軍、左衛、衛尉、八座：自我皇歷啓基，受終于宋，睿聖繼軌，三葉重光。
entries.en: Day guisi: the empress dowager ordered: "To the suppressing-army general, the general of chariots and cavalry, the left vice director, the former general, the defender-of-the-army, the left guards general, the commandant of the guards, and the eight seats: from the day our house founded its rule and took the mandate from Song, wise sovereigns have followed in succession and for three generations the light has redoubled.
entries.literal: Day guisi: The empress dowager's order said: "Suppressing-Army, Chariots-and-Cavalry, Left Vice Director, Former General, Defender-of-the-Army, Left Guards, Commandant of the Guards, and the Eight Seats: since our imperial line opened its foundation and received the mandate from Song, sage after sage has continued the track, and for three generations glory has doubled.

entries.zh: 太祖以神武創業，草昧區夏，武皇以英明提極，經緯天人。
entries.en: The Grand Progenitor, by divine martial worth, raised the cause in a realm still unformed; Emperor Wu, by luminous wisdom, set the axis and bound Heaven and man.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor by divine martial prowess founded the enterprise in the wilderness of the realm; Emperor Wu by brilliant sagacity reached the pole and wove Heaven and man together.

entries.zh: 文帝以上哲之資，體元良之重，雖功未被物，而德已在民。
entries.en: Emperor Wen, gifted with the highest wisdom, carried the heir's heavy charge; though his achievements had not yet covered the world, his virtue was already with the people.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen, with the endowment of supreme wisdom, bore the weight of the heir's station; though his merit had not yet spread over things, his virtue was already among the people.

entries.zh: 三靈之眷方永，七百之基已固。
entries.en: The three spirits' regard was still enduring, and the base of seven hundred years was already secure.
entries.literal: The favor of the three spirits was still long, and the foundation of seven hundred years was already firm.

entries.zh: 嗣主特鐘沴氣，爰表弱齡，險戾著于綠車，愚固彰於崇正。
entries.en: The reigning lord was singled out by ill omens; from early youth perversity showed; cruelty and violence appeared while he rode the green carriage, folly and stubbornness in the Chongzheng Hall.
entries.literal: The successor lord was specially marked by baleful vapors; from tender years he showed perversity; danger and harshness appeared in the green carriage, stupidity and obstinacy shone forth in the Chongzheng Hall.

entries.zh: 狗馬是好，酒色方湎。
entries.en: Dogs and horses were his delight; wine and women his constant intoxication.
entries.literal: He loved dogs and horses; wine and women were his deep delight.

entries.zh: 所務唯鄙事，所疾唯善人。
entries.en: He cared only for vulgar pursuits and loathed none but the worthy.
entries.literal: What he pursued was only base affairs; what he hated was only good men.

entries.zh: 世祖慈愛曲深，每加容掩，冀年志稍改，立守神器。
entries.en: Emperor Wu loved him deeply and repeatedly hid his faults, hoping that in time his heart might turn and he would keep watch over the throne.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu's loving kindness bent deep; again and again he covered faults, hoping that with years his will might change and he might stand guard over the sacred vessel.

entries.zh: 自入纂鴻業，長惡滋甚。
entries.en: Once he took up the great charge, the evil he had long fed only grew worse.
entries.literal: Once he entered upon the great enterprise, his long-nurtured evil grew worse.

entries.zh: 居喪無一日之哀，縗絰爲歡宴之服。
entries.en: In mourning he felt not a day's sorrow; sackcloth and mourning bands became clothes for revelry.
entries.literal: In mourning he showed not a day's grief; hemp and sackcloth became dress for feasting.

entries.zh: 昏酣長夜，萬機斯壅，發號施令，莫知所從。
entries.en: He drowned in wine through long nights and the myriad affairs stalled; edicts went out and no one knew whose will they were.
entries.literal: Drunken through the long night, the myriad tasks were blocked; when orders were issued, none knew whence they came.

entries.zh: 閹豎徐龍駒專總樞密，奉叔、珍之互執權柄，自以爲任得其人，表裏緝穆，邁蕭、曹而愈信、布，倚太山而坐平原。
entries.en: The eunuch Xu Longju held the keys of state; Fengshu and Zhenzhi traded the levers of power, each sure the right men were in place—court and camp "smooth as silk," outdoing Xiao He and Cao Shen, more trusted than Xin and Bo, resting on Mount Tai as if the plain were enough.
entries.literal: The eunuch Xu Longju monopolized the pivot of secrets; Fengshu and Zhenzhi by turns grasped the handles of power, each thinking the right men had been chosen—inside and outside were "silken and still," surpassing Xiao He and Cao Shen, more than Xin and Bo, leaning on Mount Tai while seated on the plain.

entries.zh: 於是恣情肆意，罔顧天顯，二帝姬嬪，竝充寵禦，二宮遺服，皆納玩府。
entries.en: Then he indulged every whim without regard for Heaven's dignity; consorts of the two late emperors all entered his bed, and leftover robes of the two palaces were carried into his toy vaults.
entries.literal: Thereupon he gave free rein to passion and will, heedless of Heaven's majesty; the two emperors' consorts and concubines were all taken into his private favor, and leftover garments of the two palaces were all swept into his pleasure store.

entries.zh: 內外混漫，男女無別。
entries.en: Palace and camp dissolved in disorder; men and women were no longer kept apart.
entries.literal: Inside and outside were chaotic; men and women were undistinguished.

entries.zh: 丹屏之北，爲酤鬻之所，青蒲之上，開桑中之肆。
entries.en: North of the crimson screen he set up taverns; on the ceremonial rush mats he opened tryst-houses of the mulberry lane.
entries.literal: North of the crimson screen became a place for selling wine; upon the green rush mats opened a "mulberry mid-path" shop.

entries.zh: 又微服潛行，信次忘反，端委以朝虛位，交戟而守空宮積旬矣。
entries.en: He slipped out in plain dress and wandered for nights without return; in full court robes he held a hollow throne while crossed halberds guarded an empty palace for weeks on end.
entries.literal: He also went in disguise by night, lodging abroad and forgetting return; robed for court he sat on an empty throne, and with crossed halberds they guarded a vacant palace for whole weeks.

entries.zh: 宰輔忠賢，盡誠奉主，誅鋤羣小，冀能悛革，曾無克己，更深怨憾。
entries.en: Loyal men among the chief counselors served with all their heart, rooting out petty villains in hope he might turn back—yet he never checked himself and only nursed deeper spite.
entries.literal: Loyal ministers among the chief counselors gave their utmost in service, executing the petty, hoping he might repent and reform—yet he never restrained himself and only deepened his resentment.

entries.zh: 公卿股肱，以異己寘戮，文武昭穆，以德譽見猜。
entries.en: The court's right hands were slaughtered for not being of his kind; kinsmen civil and martial were distrusted for goodness and fame.
entries.literal: The arms and legs of the court were put to death for being unlike him; civil and martial kin of the clan were suspected for reputation and virtue.

entries.zh: 放肆醜言，將行屠膾，社稷危殆，有過綴旒。
entries.en: With wild and ugly threats he was ready to slaughter; the state tottered worse than a crown with loose tassels.
entries.literal: With reckless ugly words he was about to carry out butchery; the altars were in peril worse than a swaying tassel on the royal cap.

entries.zh: 昔太宗克光於漢世，簡文代興于晉氏，前事之不忘，後人之師也。
entries.en: Long ago Emperor Wen of Han lit the dynasty; Emperor Jianwen of Jin raised a new house—the past remembered is the teacher of those who follow.
entries.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han made the Han shine; Emperor Jianwen of Jin raised a new line—the past not forgotten is a teacher for those who come after.

entries.zh: 鎮軍居正體道，家國是賴，伊霍之舉，實寄淵謨，便可詳依舊典，以禮廢黜。
entries.en: The suppressing-army general holds to the upright Way; state and house depend on him; the act of Yi and Huo rests on grave design—follow the ancient precedents in full and remove him by ritual.
entries.literal: The Suppressing-Army General stands upright in the Way; the state and clan rely on him; the deed of Yi and Huo rests truly on deep counsel—you may now follow the old statutes in detail and depose him by rite.

entries.zh: 中軍將軍新安王，體自文皇，睿哲天秀，宜入嗣鴻業，永寧四海。
entries.en: The central-army general, prince of Xin'an, is of Emperor Wen's blood, wise and bright by Heaven's endowment; let him succeed to the great charge and long pacify the realm.
entries.literal: Central-Army General, Prince of Xin'an, sprang from Emperor Wen's line, wise and luminous by Heaven's gift; he should enter to succeed the great enterprise and forever settle the four seas.

entries.zh: 外卽以禮奉迎。
entries.en: Receive him at once from outside with full ceremony.
entries.literal: At once receive him according to rite from without.

entries.zh: 未亡人屬此多難，投筆增慨。」
entries.en: I, who am not yet gone to my death, meet these many trials and set down the brush with a heavier sigh."
entries.literal: She who is not yet dead faces these many hardships and lays down the brush with added sighs."

entries.zh: 史臣曰：鬱林王風華外美，衆所同惑。
entries.en: The historian writes: The Prince of Yulin wore grace on the outside, and everyone was taken in alike.
entries.literal: The historian writes: The Prince of Yulin was outwardly fair in bearing, and all were deceived alike.

entries.zh: 伏情隱詐，難以貌求。
entries.en: He buried feeling and hid fraud; the face told you nothing.
entries.literal: He hid feeling and concealed deceit—one could not seek him by appearance.

entries.zh: 立嫡以長，未知瑕釁，世祖之心，不變周道。
entries.en: The heir was set by senior right of birth, and no stain was yet seen; the Grand Ancestor's mind held to the Zhou pattern still.
entries.literal: Establishing the eldest legitimate son, no flaw was yet known; the Grand Ancestor's heart did not depart from the Zhou way.

entries.zh: 旣而愆鄙內作，兆自宮闈，雖爲害未遠，足傾社稷。
entries.en: Then baseness rose within; the sign came from the women's quarters. Though ruin had not yet arrived, it was enough to topple the realm.
entries.literal: Then faults and vulgarity arose within; the omen came from the inner palace—though the harm was not yet far off, it was enough to overturn the altars of state.

entries.zh: 《春秋》書梁伯之過，言其自取亡也。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn records the fault of the lord of Liang—he chose his own fall.
entries.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records the Marquis of Liang's fault, saying he brought ruin on himself.

entries.zh: 八月壬午，詔稱先帝遺詔，以護軍將軍武陵王曄爲衛將軍，征南大將軍陳顯達卽本號，竝開府儀同三司，尚書左僕射西昌侯鸞爲尚書令。
entries.en: Eighth month, day renwu: by the late emperor's will, Protected-Army General Xiao Ye, prince of Wuling, became defender general; Chen Xianda, general who conquers the south, kept his rank, and both were given secretariat parity with the three excellencies; Xiao Luan, marquis of Xichang and left vice director of the masters of writing, became director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: Eighth month, day renwu: citing the late emperor's testament, Protected-Army General Prince Ye of Wuling was made Defender General; General Who Conquers the South Chen Xianda kept his original title—both with ceremonial parity equal to the Three Excellencies; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis Luan of Xichang, was made Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 太孫詹事沈文季爲護軍將軍。
entries.en: Shen Wenji, steward of the great-grandson's household, was made protected-army general.
entries.literal: Grandson's Household Steward Shen Wenji was made Protected-Army General.

entries.zh: 癸未，以司徒竟陵王子良爲太傅。
entries.en: Day guiwei: Xiao Ziliang, prince of Jingling and minister of works, was made grand tutor.
entries.literal: Day guiwei: Minister of Works Prince Ziliang of Jingling was made Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「朕以寡薄，嗣膺寶政，對越靈命，欽若前圖，思所以敬守成規，拱揖羣后。
entries.en: An edict said: "I am slight in virtue yet have taken up the throne, facing Heaven's mandate and following the models of old, seeking to keep the inherited order and yield the floor to you, my lords.
entries.literal: An edict said: "I, of little worth, have succeeded to the imperial charge, facing the mandate of Heaven and revering the precedents of old, thinking how to reverently hold to established rules and bow to the assembled lords.

entries.zh: 哀荒在日，有懵大猷，宜育德振民，光昭睿範。
entries.en: I am still in the days of grief and the great plan is unclear to me; I must cultivate virtue and lift the people, and let a wise example shine.
entries.literal: Days of mourning still lie before me, and the great design is dim; I should nurture virtue and steady the people, making bright the sage's model.

entries.zh: 凡逋三調及衆責，在今年七月三十日前，悉同蠲除。
entries.en: Every unpaid third impost and miscellaneous levy due before the thirtieth day of the seventh month of this year is forgiven in full.
entries.literal: All overdue third imposts and assorted levies—everything before the thirtieth day of the seventh month of this year—is wholly remitted.

entries.zh: 其備償封籍貨鬻未售，亦皆還主。
entries.en: Property sealed for forced sale or pawned but not yet sold shall be returned to its owners.
entries.literal: Goods registered for compulsory repayment and pawned but unsold shall all be returned to the owners.

entries.zh: 禦府諸署池田邸冶，興廢沿事，本施一時，於今無用者，詳所罷省。
entries.en: Ponds, fields, lodges, and smelters in the palace offices, begun or abandoned as times changed and meant only for the moment—whatever serves no purpose now should be examined and cut back.
entries.literal: Ponds, fields, lodges, and foundries in the various offices of the imperial household—started or dropped as occasion required and meant for a time—whatever is useless today shall be reviewed for abolition or reduction.

entries.zh: 公宜權禁，一以還民，關市征賦，務從優減。」
entries.en: What ought to be barred to the state should be wholly returned to the people; tolls at the passes and market taxes should be eased as far as possible."
entries.literal: What the state ought to forbid, let all be returned to the people; market tolls and taxes shall be kept as light as may be."

entries.zh: 丙戌，詔曰：「近北掠餘口，悉充軍實。
entries.en: Day bingxu: an edict said: "Lately northerners seized in raids have all been pressed into the army rolls.
entries.literal: Day bingxu: An edict said: "Recently captives taken in the north were all filled into military rolls.

entries.zh: 刑故無小，罔或攸赦，撫辜興仁，事深睿範。
entries.en: The law says that in punishment no guilt is too small to escape—but to comfort the injured and stir benevolence is the deeper pattern of sage rule.
entries.literal: In punishing guilt no offender is too small to be spared—or so the statutes say; to comfort the wronged and raise humanity runs to the heart of sage governance.

entries.zh: 宜從蕩宥，許以自新，可一同放遣，還復民籍。
entries.en: Let a broad amnesty allow them to begin anew: release them all at once and restore them to the civilian registers.
entries.literal: Let general pardon be granted and self-renewal allowed; they may all be released together and restored to civilian registers.

entries.zh: 已賞賜者，亦皆爲贖。」
entries.en: Those who have already been given bounty may also buy their way back to freedom."
entries.literal: Those already rewarded with gifts shall also be redeemed."

entries.zh: 辛丑，詔曰：「往歲蠻虜協謀，志擾邊服，羣帥授略，大殲凶醜。
entries.en: Day xinchou: an edict said: "Last year the southern tribes conspired and meant to harry the frontier; our generals took their measures and crushed the foe.
entries.literal: Day xinchou: An edict said: "Last year the southern barbarians plotted together, intending to trouble the border; commanders were given strategy and the vicious enemy was greatly destroyed.

entries.zh: 革城克捷，及舞陰固守，二處勞人，未有沾爵賞者，可分遣選部，往彼序用。」
entries.en: Gecheng fell quickly and Wuyin held firm—two places whose soldiers toiled yet have not received rank or bounty. Send selection officers to list merits and appoint rewards on the spot."
entries.literal: At Gecheng victory was swift, and at Wuyin's stubborn defense—two places whose men labored yet have not tasted rank or reward—selection officers may be sent to record merits and appoint them there."

entries.zh: 閏月乙丑，以南東海太守蕭穎胄爲青、冀二州刺史。
entries.en: Intercalary month, day yichou: Xiao Yingzhou, administrator of east Donghai, took Qing and Ji.
entries.literal: Intercalary month, day yichou: Administrator of East Donghai Xiao Yingzhou was made inspector of Qing and Ji.

entries.zh: 丁卯，鎮軍大將軍鸞卽本號開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Day dingmao: Xiao Luan, suppressing-army general, kept his rank with secretariat parity equal to the three excellencies.
entries.literal: Day dingmao: Suppressing-Army General Luan kept his original title with ceremonial parity equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 戊辰，以中軍將軍新安王昭文爲揚州刺史。
entries.en: Day wuchen: Zhaowen, prince of Xin'an and central-army general, took Yangzhou.
entries.literal: Day wuchen: Central-Army General Prince Zhaowen of Xin'an was made inspector of Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 中書舍人綦母珍之、朱隆之，直閤將軍曹道剛、周奉叔，竝爲帝羽翼。
entries.en: Qimu Zhenzhi and Zhu Longzhi, gentlemen of the secretariat, and Cao Daogang and Zhou Fengshu, direct-pavilion generals—all were the emperor's wings.
entries.literal: Secretariat Gentlemen Qimu Zhenzhi and Zhu Longzhi, Direct-Pavilion Generals Cao Daogang and Zhou Fengshu—all were the emperor's wings.

entries.zh: 高宗屢諫不納，先啓誅龍駒，次誅奉叔及珍之，帝竝不能違。
entries.en: The High Ancestor warned him again and again, and was not heard. He asked first for Longju's head, then for Fengshu's and Zhenzhi's—and the emperor could refuse none of it.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor remonstrated again and again but was not heeded; he first memorialized to execute Longju, then to execute Fengshu and Zhenzhi—the emperor could not go against any of it.

entries.zh: 旣而尼媼外入，頗傳異語，乃疑高宗有異志。
entries.en: Soon a nun from outside brought odd rumors, and the emperor began to suspect the High Ancestor of other designs.
entries.literal: Before long a Buddhist nun came in from outside and spread strange talk; he then suspected the High Ancestor of a different intent.

entries.zh: 中書令何胤以皇后從叔見親，使直殿省，嘗隨後呼胤爲三父，與胤謀誅高宗，令胤受事，胤不敢當，依違杜諫，帝意復止。
entries.en: He Yin of the Secretariat, the empress's collateral paternal uncle, was kept close and set to attend in the Hall of Direct Service. Once the emperor walked behind him calling him "Three Fathers." They plotted to kill the High Ancestor and put Yin in charge; Yin would not take it, stalled and talked him down, and the plan died away.
