entries.literal: Director of the Secretariat He Yin, as the empress's cousin by marriage, was treated as kin; he was made to attend in the Hall of Direct Service, and the emperor once followed behind calling Yin "Three Fathers." He plotted with Yin to kill the High Ancestor and have Yin take charge; Yin did not dare accept, hedged and remonstrated to block it, and the emperor's intent again ceased.

entries.zh: 乃謀出高宗於西州，中勑用事，不復關諮。
entries.en: Next he plotted to banish the High Ancestor to the Western Quarter and rule by inner edict alone, without further counsel.
entries.literal: He then plotted to send the High Ancestor out to the Western Quarter; central edicts would govern affairs and no longer pass through consultation.

entries.zh: 高宗慮變，定謀廢帝。
entries.en: Fearing a coup, the High Ancestor set his mind to depose the emperor.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor, fearing change, fixed a plan to depose the emperor.

entries.zh: 二十二日壬辰，使蕭諶、坦之等於省誅曹道剛、朱隆之等，率兵自尚書入雲龍門，戎服加朱衣於上。
entries.en: On the twenty-second, day renchen, he sent Xiao Chen, Tanzhi, and others to kill Cao Daogang and Zhu Longzhi at the Secretariat, then led troops from the Secretariat through the Cloud Dragon Gate—armor under scarlet robes.
entries.literal: On the twenty-second day, day renchen, he had Xiao Chen, Tanzhi, and others at the Secretariat execute Cao Daogang, Zhu Longzhi, and the rest; he led troops from the Secretariat in through the Cloud Dragon Gate, battle dress with scarlet robes worn over it.

entries.zh: 比入門，三失履。
entries.en: At the gate he lost his shoes three times.
entries.literal: As he entered the gate, he lost his shoes three times.

entries.zh: 王晏、徐孝嗣、蕭坦之、陳顯達、王廣之、沈文季系進。
entries.en: Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Xiao Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, and Shen Wenji followed in turn.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, Xu Xiaosi, Xiao Tanzhi, Chen Xianda, Wang Guangzhi, and Shen Wenji advanced in succession.

entries.zh: 帝在壽昌殿，聞外有變，使閉內殿諸房閣，令閹人登興光樓望，還報云：「見一人戎服，從數百人，急裝，在西鐘樓下。」
entries.en: The emperor was in Shouchang Hall. Hearing trouble outside, he shut the inner halls and sent a eunuch up Xingguang Tower to look. The man came back and said, "I see one man in armor, with several hundred followers, armed in haste, below the Western Bell Tower."
entries.literal: The emperor was in Shouchang Hall; hearing disturbance outside, he had the inner halls and chambers closed and ordered a eunuch to climb Xingguang Tower to look; returning he reported: "I see one man in battle dress, with several hundred men, armed in haste, below the Western Bell Tower."

entries.zh: 須臾，蕭諶領兵先入宮，截壽昌閣，帝走向愛姬徐氏房，拔劔自刺不中，以帛纏頸，輿接出延德殿。
entries.en: A moment later Xiao Chen led the van into the palace and sealed Shouchang Pavilion. The emperor fled to his favorite Lady Xu's room, drew a sword and missed his own throat, bound his neck in silk, and was borne out on a litter to Yande Hall.
entries.literal: In a moment Xiao Chen led troops in first, cut off Shouchang Pavilion; the emperor ran toward his favorite Lady Xu's chamber, drew a sword and stabbed himself but missed, wrapped silk about his neck, and was carried out on a litter to Yande Hall.

entries.zh: 諶初入殿，宿衛將士皆操弓盾欲拒戰，諶謂之曰：「所取自有人，卿等不須動！」
entries.en: As Chen entered, the night guards seized bow and shield to fight. Chen told them, "We take whom we mean to take—you need not move!"
entries.literal: When Chen first entered the hall, the night guards all took up bow and shield intending to resist; Chen said to them: "Those taken have their man—you need not stir!"

entries.zh: 宿衛信之，及見帝出，各欲自奮，帝竟無一言。
entries.en: They believed him. When they saw the emperor carried out, each man would have fought—but the emperor never spoke a word.
entries.literal: The guards believed him; when they saw the emperor brought out, each wished to rouse himself, yet the emperor in the end did not speak a word.

entries.zh: 出西弄，殺之，時年二十一，輿尸出徐龍駒宅，殯葬以王禮。
entries.en: They took him to the Western Lane and killed him. He was twenty-one. His body was borne to Xu Longju's house and buried with the rites due a prince.
entries.literal: He was taken out to the Western Lane and killed; he was twenty-one. The corpse was carried out to Xu Longju's house and buried with princely rites.

entries.zh: 餘黨亦見誅。
entries.en: The rest of the faction were put to death as well.
entries.literal: The remaining partisans were also executed.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第四 本紀第四
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 4, Annals 4
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 4, Annals 4

entries.zh: 海陵恭王昭文，字季尚，文惠太子第二子也。
entries.en: The Reverent Prince of Hailing, Zhaowen, bore the style Jishang and was the second son of Crown Prince Wenhui.
entries.literal: The Reverent Prince of Hailing, Zhaowen, styled Jishang, was the second son of Crown Prince Wenhui.

entries.zh: 永明四年，封臨汝公，邑千五百戶。
entries.en: Yongming 4: he was made duke of Linru with a fief of 1,500 households.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Linru with a fief of 1,500 households.

entries.zh: 初爲輔國將軍、濟陽太守。
entries.en: At first he served as general who assists the state and administrator of Jiyang.
entries.literal: At first he was made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Jiyang.

entries.zh: 十年，轉持節、督南豫州諸軍事、南豫州刺史，將軍如故。
entries.en: In the tenth year he took the staff, supervised South Yuzhou's armies, and became inspector of South Yuzhou, keeping his rank.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of all military affairs of South Yuzhou, and Inspector of South Yuzhou, his generalship unchanged.

entries.zh: 十一年，進號冠軍將軍。
entries.en: In the eleventh year his title was raised to general who establishes might.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he was advanced in title to General Who Establishes Might.

entries.zh: 文惠太子薨，還都。
entries.en: After Crown Prince Wenhui died, he returned to the capital.
entries.literal: When Crown Prince Wenhui died, he returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 鬱林王卽位，爲中軍將軍，領兵置佐。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yulin ascended, he became central-army general with troops and a full staff.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, he was made Central-Army General with troops and staff officers appointed.

entries.zh: 封新安王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: He was made prince of Xin'an with a fief of 2,000 households.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an with a fief of 2,000 households.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，爲使持節、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、揚州刺史，將軍如故。
entries.en: Longchang 1: he bore the staff with full powers, commanded Yang and South Xu, and took Yangzhou, keeping his rank.
entries.literal: Longchang 1, he was made Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs of Yang and South Xu, and Inspector of Yangzhou, his generalship unchanged.

entries.zh: 其年，鬱林王廢，尚書令西昌侯鸞議立昭文爲帝。
entries.en: That year, after the Prince of Yulin was removed, Xiao Luan, marquis of Xichang and director of the masters of writing, urged that Zhaowen be made emperor.
entries.literal: That year, when the Prince of Yulin was deposed, Director of the Masters of Writing Marquis Luan of Xichang proposed establishing Zhaowen as emperor.

entries.zh: 延興元年秋七月丁酉，即皇帝位。
entries.en: Yanxing 1, autumn, seventh month, day dingyou: he ascended the imperial throne.
entries.literal: Yanxing 1, autumn, seventh month, day dingyou: he took the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 以尚書令鎮軍大將軍西昌侯鸞為驃騎大將軍、錄尚書事、揚州刺史、宣城郡公。
entries.en: Xiao Luan, marquis of Xichang, director of the masters of writing and suppressing-army general-in-chief, was made general of agile cavalry, recorder of the masters of writing, inspector of Yangzhou, and duke of Xuancheng.
entries.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing, Suppressing-Army General-in-Chief, Marquis Luan of Xichang was made General of Agile Cavalry, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Inspector of Yangzhou, and Duke of Xuancheng.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「太祖高皇帝英謀光大，受命作齊；
entries.en: An edict said: "The Grand Progenitor, the High Emperor, had brilliant plans grandly enlarged and received the mandate to found Qi;
entries.literal: An edict said: "The Grand Progenitor, the High Emperor, had brilliant plans grandly enlarged and received the mandate to found Qi;

entries.zh: 世祖武皇帝宏猷冠世，繼暉下武；
entries.en: the Ancestor, the Martial Emperor, had magnificent designs crowning the age and continued the radiance to better the martial;
entries.literal: the Ancestor, the Martial Emperor, had magnificent designs crowning the age and continued the radiance to better the martial;

entries.zh: 世宗文皇帝清明懿鑠，四海宅心：竝德漏下泉，功昭上象，聲教所覃，無思不洽。
entries.en: the Lineage Ancestor, the Cultured Emperor, was clear and bright, virtuous and splendid—the four seas turned their hearts to him: both virtue reached beneath the spring and merit shone in the heavens above; where sound and teaching spread, none was left unpeacefully governed.
entries.literal: the Lineage Ancestor, the Cultured Emperor, was clear and bright, virtuous and splendid—the four seas turned their hearts to him: both virtue reached beneath the spring and merit shone in the heavens above; where sound and teaching spread, none was left unpeacefully governed.

entries.zh: 洪基式固，景祚方融，而天步多阻，運鍾否剝。
entries.en: The great foundation was firmly set and the bright fortune was just merging—yet Heaven's steps met many obstacles and the age struck decline and stripping.
entries.literal: The great foundation was firmly set and the bright fortune was just merging—yet Heaven's steps met many obstacles and the age struck decline and stripping.

entries.zh: 嗣君昏忍，暴戾滋多，棄侮天經，悖滅人紀，朝野重足，遐邇側視，民怨神恫，宗祧如綴。
entries.en: The succeeding lord was dim and cruel; violence and excess grew; he cast aside and insulted Heaven's constants and perversely extinguished human norms—at court and in the wild all stood on tiptoes in fear; far and near watched askance; the people resented and the spirits were alarmed; the ancestral temple seemed about to fall apart.
entries.literal: The succeeding lord was dim and cruel; violence and excess grew; he cast aside and insulted Heaven's constants and perversely extinguished human norms—at court and in the wild all stood on tiptoes in fear; far and near watched askance; the people resented and the spirits were alarmed; the ancestral temple seemed about to fall apart.

entries.zh: 賴忠謨肅舉，霄漢廓清，俾三后之業，絕而更紐，七百之慶，危而復安。
entries.en: By loyal counsel solemnly raised, the azure vault was cleared; the enterprise of the three sovereigns, though severed, was bound anew; the blessing of seven hundred years, though perilous, was made safe again.
entries.literal: By loyal counsel solemnly raised, the azure vault was cleared; the enterprise of the three sovereigns, though severed, was bound anew; the blessing of seven hundred years, though perilous, was made safe again.

entries.zh: 猥以沖人，入纂乾緒，載懷馭朽，若墜諸淵，思與黎元，共綏戬福。」
entries.en: Humbly as a mere youth I enter to continue the Heavenly line; I bear in mind holding rotten wood and feel as if falling into an abyss—I wish with the common folk to share tranquil blessings."
entries.literal: Humbly as a mere youth I enter to continue the Heavenly line; I bear in mind holding rotten wood and feel as if falling into an abyss—I wish with the common folk to share tranquil blessings."

entries.zh: 大赦，改元。
entries.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.
entries.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed.

entries.zh: 文武賜位二等。
entries.en: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks.
entries.literal: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks.

entries.zh: 九月癸酉，詔曰：「頃者以淮關徭戍，勤瘁於行役，故覃以榮階，薄酬厥勞。
entries.en: Ninth month, day guiyou: an edict said: "Lately corvée at the Huai frontier has worn men out on the march; we have therefore spread honors as a modest payment for their toil.
entries.literal: Ninth month, day guiyou, an edict said: "Recently, because of corvée garrison duty at the Huai passes, men have worn themselves out on forced service; therefore we spread rank and title as a slight reward for their labor.

entries.zh: 勳狀淹留，未集王府，非所以急舍爵之典，趣報功之旨。
entries.en: Rolls of merit still lie idle and have not reached the palace—this is no way to hurry the giving of noble rank or repay service in good time.
entries.literal: Meritorious records have lingered and not reached the princely household—this is not the way to hurry the bestowal of noble ranks or swiftly repay achievement.

entries.zh: 便可分遣使部，往彼銓用。」
entries.en: Send envoys at once in separate parties to go there, weigh merit, and appoint rewards."
entries.literal: At once send envoys in groups to go there and assess and appoint rewards."

entries.zh: 辛巳，以前九真太守宋慈明爲交州刺史。
entries.en: Day xinsi: Song Ciming, former administrator of Jiuzhen, took Jiaozhou.
entries.literal: Day xinsi: former Administrator of Jiuzhen Song Ciming was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.

entries.zh: 癸未，誅新除司徒鄱陽王鏘、中軍大將軍隨郡王子隆。
entries.en: Day guiwei: Xiao Chao, newly made minister of education and prince of Poyang, and Xiao Zilong, prince of Suizhou and central-army general-in-chief, were put to death.
entries.literal: Day guiwei: the newly appointed Minister of Education Prince Chao of Poyang and Central-Army General-in-Chief Prince Zilong of Suizhou were executed.

entries.zh: 遣平西將軍王廣之誅南兖州刺史安陸王子敬。
entries.en: Wang Guangzhi, pacifying-west general, was sent to kill Xiao Zijing, prince of Anlu and inspector of South Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Pacifying-West General Wang Guangzhi was sent to execute Inspector of South Yanzhou Prince Zijing of Anlu.

entries.zh: 於是江州刺史晉安王子懋起兵，遣中護軍王玄邈討之。
entries.en: Then Xiao Zimao, prince of Jin'an and inspector of Jiangzhou, rose in arms; Wang Xuanmiao, central colonel, was sent against him.
entries.literal: Thereupon Prince Zimao of Jin'an, Inspector of Jiangzhou, raised troops; Central Colonel Wang Xuanmiao was sent to attack him.

entries.zh: 乙未，驃騎大將軍鸞假黃鋮，內外纂嚴。
entries.en: Day yiwei: Xiao Luan, general of agile cavalry, was granted the yellow battle-axe; court and camp were placed under strict closure.
entries.literal: Day yiwei: General of Agile Cavalry Luan was given the yellow battle-axe; within and without, strict martial law was proclaimed.

entries.zh: 又誅湘州刺史南平王銳、郢州刺史晉熙王銶、南豫州刺史宜都王鏗。
entries.en: Also killed were Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and inspector of Xiangzhou; Xiao Qiu, prince of Jinxi and inspector of Ying; and Xiao Keng, prince of Yidu and inspector of South Yuzhou.
entries.literal: Also executed were Inspector of Xiangzhou Prince Rui of Nanping, Inspector of Yingzhou Prince Qiu of Jinxi, and Inspector of South Yuzhou Prince Keng of Yidu.

entries.zh: 丁亥，以衛將軍廬陵王子卿爲司徒，撫軍將軍桂陽王鑠爲中軍將軍、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Day dinghai: Xiao Ziqing, prince of Luling and guards general, became minister of education; Xiao Shuo, prince of Guiyang and pacifying-army general, became central-army general with secretariat parity equal to the three excellencies.
entries.literal: Day dinghai: Guards General Prince Ziqing of Luling was made Minister of Education; Pacifying-Army General Prince Shuo of Guiyang was made Central-Army General with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 冬十月癸巳，詔曰：「周設媒官，趣及時之制，漢務輕徭，在休息之典，所以布德弘教，寬俗阜民。
entries.en: Winter, tenth month, day guisi: an edict said: "Zhou set matchmakers to hurry timely unions; Han prized light levies in the canon of repose—so virtue might spread, teaching widen, custom soften, and the people grow rich.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, day guisi, an edict said: "Zhou established matchmaker officials to hasten timely marriage; Han stressed light corvée in the doctrine of rest—thus to spread virtue, enlarge teaching, ease customs, and enrich the people.

entries.zh: 朕君制八紘，志敷九德，而習俗之風，爲弊未改，靜言多慍，無忘昏昃。
entries.en: I hold the eight directions and mean to lay out the nine virtues, yet the habits of the age are still uncured; in quiet I brood on much that grieves me and do not forget to labor from dusk to dark.
entries.literal: I rule the eight corners and aim to spread the nine virtues, yet custom's ways remain unreformed; speaking in silence I am much troubled and do not forget to toil from dusk till dawn.

entries.zh: 督勸婚嫁，宜嚴更申明，必使禽幣以時，摽梅息怨。
entries.en: Oversight and urging of marriage should be proclaimed again in strict terms, so that bride-price comes on time and the sighs of waiting maidens fall silent.
entries.literal: Overseeing and urging marriage should be strictly reiterated, so that betrothal gifts come in season and complaints of late marriage cease.

entries.zh: 正廚諸役，舊出州郡，徵吏民以應其數，公獲二旬，私累數朔。
entries.en: Kitchen corvées for the main kitchens once fell on the provinces; clerks and commoners were pressed to fill the count—the public coffers gained twenty days' labor while private homes bore the burden for months.
entries.literal: Regular kitchen corvées of old came from prefectures; officials and commoners were levied to fill the quota—the public domain got two ten-day periods, private households suffered for several months.

entries.zh: 又廣陵年常遞出千人以助淮戍，勞擾爲煩，抑亦苞苴是育。
entries.en: Each year as well Guanglin forwarded a thousand men to the Huai garrisons—a wearisome levy, and one that bred wrapped gifts and graft.
entries.literal: Also, every year Guanglin sent out a thousand men to aid Huai garrison service—a burden of toil and trouble, and also a nursery for gift bribery.

entries.zh: 今竝可長停，別量所出。
entries.en: Let all these be stopped for good, and other sources of supply be reckoned instead.
entries.literal: Now all may be permanently halted; other measures for levies shall be weighed.

entries.zh: 諸縣使村長路都防城直縣，爲劇尤深，亦宜禁斷。」
entries.en: In every county, when village heads, road wardens, and wall-guard duty are billed straight to the magistrate, the harm is worst of all—that too must be forbidden."
entries.literal: In all counties, having village heads, road wardens, and city-defense duty go direct to the county—the hardship is especially severe—and this too should be forbidden."

entries.zh: 丁酉，解嚴。
entries.en: Day dingyou: the strict closure was lifted.
entries.literal: Day dingyou: martial law was lifted.

entries.zh: 進驃騎大將軍、揚州刺史宣城公鸞爲太傅，領大將軍、揚州牧，加殊禮，進爵爲王。
entries.en: Xiao Luan, duke of Xuancheng, general of agile cavalry and inspector of Yang, was raised to grand tutor, great general, and governor of Yangzhou, given extraordinary honors, and advanced to prince.
entries.literal: General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Yangzhou Duke Luan of Xuancheng was advanced to Grand Tutor, bearing the title of Great General and Governor of Yangzhou, with extraordinary honors, and advanced in rank to prince.

entries.zh: 戊戌，誅新除中軍將軍桂陽王鑠、撫軍將軍衡陽王鈞、侍中秘書監江夏王鋒、鎮軍將軍建安王子真、左將軍巴陵王子倫。
entries.en: Day wuxu: Xiao Shuo of Guiyang, newly made central-army general; Xiao Jun of Hengyang, pacifying-army general; Xiao Feng of Jiangxia, attendant-in-ordinary and director of the palace library; Xiao Zizhen of Jian'an, suppressing-army general; and Xiao Zilun of Baling, left general—all were put to death.
entries.literal: Day wuxu: the newly appointed Central-Army General Prince Shuo of Guiyang, Pacifying-Army General Prince Jun of Hengyang, Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Library Prince Feng of Jiangxia, Suppressing-Army General Prince Zizhen of Jian'an, and Left General Prince Zilun of Baling were executed.

entries.zh: 癸卯，以寧朔將軍蕭遙欣爲豫州刺史，新除黃門郎蕭遙昌爲郢州刺史，輔國將軍蕭誕爲司州刺史。
entries.en: Day guimao: Xiao Yaoxin, pacifying-the-north general, took Yuzhou; Xiao Yaochang, newly made gentleman of the yellow gate, took Ying; Xiao Dan, general who assists the state, took Si.
entries.literal: Day guimao: Pacifying-the-North General Xiao Yaoxin was made Inspector of Yuzhou; newly appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xiao Yaochang was made Inspector of Yingzhou; General Who Assists the State Xiao Dan was made Inspector of Sizhou.

entries.zh: 宣城王輔政，帝起居皆諮而後行。
entries.en: With the Xuancheng prince directing the government, the emperor asked his leave on every move of daily life.
entries.literal: As Xuancheng Prince held the regency, the emperor consulted him on all daily matters before acting.

entries.zh: 思食蒸魚菜，太官令答無錄公命，竟不與。
entries.en: Craving steamed fish and vegetables, he was told by the palace kitchen director that without the regent's written command nothing could be served—and in the end he got none.
entries.literal: When he wished to eat steamed fish and greens, the Director of the Palace Kitchen replied that without the regent's recorded order none could be given—and in the end he was not served.

entries.zh: 辛亥，皇太后令曰：「司空、後將軍、丹陽尹、右僕射、中領軍、八座：夫明晦迭來，屯平代有，上靈所以眷命，億兆所以歸懷。
entries.en: Day xinhai: the empress dowager ordered: "To the minister of works, the rear general, the administrator of Danyang, the right vice director, the central army-inspector-in-chief, and the eight seats: light and shadow take turns; hardship and peace succeed one another in their seasons—thus the high spirits bestow the mandate and the myriad folk set their hearts.
entries.literal: Day xinhai, the empress dowager's order said: "To the Minister of Works, Rear General, Administrator of Danyang, Right Vice Director, Central Army-inspector-in-Chief, and the Eight Seats: brightness and dimness alternate in turn; adversity and ease replace each other in their generations—that is why the High Spirit grants the mandate and the myriad people turn their hearts.

entries.zh: 自皇家淳耀，列聖繼軌，諸侯官方，百神受職。
entries.en: From the house's clear radiance, sage after sage has kept the path; feudal lords have held their offices and the hundred spirits their posts.
entries.literal: Since the imperial house's pure splendor, successive sages have continued the track; feudal lords have held their posts and the hundred spirits received their charges.

entries.zh: 而殷憂時啓，多難薦臻，隆昌失德，特紊人鬼，非徒四海解體，乃亦九鼎將移。
entries.en: Yet seasons of deep sorrow have opened and many trials have gathered; Longchang lost its virtue and especially tangled the rites of the living and the dead—not only did the four seas fall apart, but even the nine cauldrons were near to shifting.
entries.literal: Yet times of deep grief have opened and many calamities have piled up; Longchang lost its virtue and especially tangled the bond of human and ghost—not only did the four seas come apart, but even the nine cauldrons were about to shift.

entries.zh: 賴天縱英輔，大匡社稷，崩基重造，墜典再興。
entries.en: By Heaven's gift of a heroic minister the altars were greatly set right; the fallen base was rebuilt and broken rites raised again.
entries.literal: By Heaven's gift of an heroic helper the altars were greatly righted; the toppled foundation was remade and fallen rites revived.

entries.zh: 嗣主幼沖，庶政多昧，且早嬰尪疾，弗克負荷，所以宗正內侮，戚藩外叛，覘天視地，人各有心。
entries.en: The reigning lord is young and weak, and much of government is dim to him; moreover he has long been wasted by illness and cannot bear the weight—so the lineage is mocked within, kinsmen rise without, and each man watches Heaven and earth with a separate heart.
entries.literal: The successor lord is young and tender, and most state affairs are unclear; moreover he has long borne wasting illness and cannot bear the burden—hence the house is insulted from within, kinsmen rebel abroad, and every man looks to Heaven and earth with his own heart.

entries.zh: 雖三祖之德在民，而七廟之危行及。
entries.en: Though the three ancestors' virtue still lives in the people, peril to the seven temples is already at hand.
entries.literal: Though the virtue of the three ancestors remains with the people, the danger to the seven temples is already near.

entries.zh: 自非樹以長君，鎮以淵器，未允天人之望，寧息奸宄之謀！
entries.en: Unless a long-established lord is raised and steadied by a deep measure, Heaven and men will not be content, nor will traitors' plots be stilled!
entries.literal: Unless a mature ruler is set up and steadied by a deep vessel, Heaven and men's hopes will not be satisfied, nor can conspiracies of traitors be stilled!

entries.zh: 太傅宣城王胤體宣皇，鐘慈太祖，識冠生民，功高造物，符表夙著，謳頌有在，宜入承寶命，式寧宗祏。
entries.en: Grand Tutor Xuancheng Prince carries the Proclamation Emperor's line, was beloved of the Grand Progenitor from the first; his wisdom outtops all born men and his merit rises above the made world; omens were long plain and songs of praise already ring—let him enter to take the precious mandate and settle the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: Grand Tutor Xuancheng Prince inherits the body of the Proclamation Emperor, was cherished by the Grand Progenitor from the start; his discernment crowns all living men and his merit towers above creation; signs and portents were long evident and song-praise is already there—he should enter to receive the precious mandate and thereby pacify the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 帝可降封海陵王，吾當歸老別館。
entries.en: The emperor may be lowered to prince of Hailing; I shall retire in age to a separate palace.
entries.literal: The emperor may be demoted and enfeoffed as Prince of Hailing; I shall retire in old age to a separate palace.

entries.zh: 昔宣帝中興漢室，簡文重延晉祀，庶我鴻基，於茲永固。
entries.en: Long ago Emperor Xuan of Han revived the Han house; Emperor Jianwen of Jin renewed Jin's rites—may our great foundation here stand firm forever.
entries.literal: Long ago Emperor Xuan of Han revived the Han house; Emperor Jianwen of Jin prolonged Jin's sacrifice—may our great foundation here be forever firm.

entries.zh: 言念家國，感慶載懷。」
entries.en: Thinking of house and realm, gratitude and joy fill the breast."
entries.literal: Speaking with thought of family and state, gratitude and joy fill the heart."

entries.zh: 八月甲辰，以新除衛尉蕭諶爲中領軍，司空王敬則進位太尉，新除車騎大將軍陳顯達爲司空，尚書左僕射王晏爲尚書令，左衛將軍王廣之爲豫州刺史，驃騎大將軍鄱陽王鏘爲司徒。
entries.en: Eighth month, day jiachen: Xiao Chen, newly made commandant of the guard, became central army-inspector-in-chief; Wang Jingze, minister of works, was raised to grand commandant; Chen Xianda, newly made general of chariots and cavalry, became minister of works; Wang Yan, left vice director of the masters of writing, became director; Wang Guangzhi, left guards general, took Yuzhou; Xiao Chao, prince of Poyang and general of agile cavalry, became minister of education.
entries.literal: Eighth month, day jiachen: the newly appointed Commandant of the Guard Xiao Chen was made Central Army-inspector-in-Chief; Minister of Works Wang Jingze was promoted to Grand Commandant; newly appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry Chen Xianda was made Minister of Works; Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was made Director; Left Guards General Wang Guangzhi was made Inspector of Yuzhou; General of Agile Cavalry Prince Chao of Poyang was made Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 詔遣大使巡行風俗。
entries.en: An edict sent grand envoys to tour the realm and report on local custom.
entries.literal: An edict dispatched grand envoys to tour and inspect local customs.

entries.zh: 丁未，詔曰：「新安國五品以上，悉與滿敘；
entries.en: Day dingwei: an edict said: "In the state of Xin'an, all officials of fifth rank and above shall be advanced to the full of their grade;
entries.literal: Day dingwei, an edict said: "In the state of Xin'an, all of fifth rank and above shall receive full advancement in rank;

entries.zh: 自此以下，皆聽解遣。
entries.en: from that rank down, all may be dismissed from office.
entries.literal: from this rank downward, all may be released from service.

entries.zh: 其欲仕者，適其所樂。」
entries.en: Those who wish to serve may take whatever post suits their wish."
entries.literal: those who wish to serve may take posts suited to their inclination."

entries.zh: 以驍騎將軍河東王鉉爲南徐州刺史，西中郎將臨海王昭秀爲車騎將軍，南徐州刺史永嘉王昭粲爲荊州刺史。
entries.en: Xiao Xuan, prince of Hedong and valiant-cavalry general, took South Xuzhou; Zhaoxiu of Linhai, west central-gentleman, became general of chariots and cavalry; Zhaocan of Yongjia, inspector of South Xuzhou, took Jingzhou.
entries.literal: Valiant-Cavalry General Prince Xuan of Hedong was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; West Central-Gentleman Prince Zhaoxiu of Linhai was made General of Chariots and Cavalry; Inspector of South Xuzhou Prince Zhaocan of Yongjia was made Inspector of Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 戊申，以輔國將軍王詡爲廣州刺史，中書郎蕭遙欣爲兖州刺史。
entries.en: Day wushen: Wang Xu, general who assists the state, took Guangzhou; Xiao Yaoxin, secretariat gentleman, took Yanzhou.
entries.literal: Day wushen: General Who Assists the State Wang Xu was made Inspector of Guangzhou; Secretariat Gentleman Xiao Yaoxin was made Inspector of Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 庚戌，以車騎板行參軍李慶綜爲寧州刺史。
entries.en: Day gengxu: Li Qingzong, acting staff clerk on the chariots-and-cavalry general's roster, was made inspector of Ning.
entries.literal: Day gengxu: Staff Clerk on the General-of-Chariots payroll Li Qingzong was made Inspector of Ningzhou.

entries.zh: 辛亥，以安西將軍王玄邈爲中護軍，新除後軍司馬蕭誕爲徐州刺史。
entries.en: Day xinhai: Wang Xuanmiao, pacifying-west general, became central colonel; Xiao Dan, newly made rear-army major, took Xuzhou.
entries.literal: Day xinhai: Pacifying-West General Wang Xuanmiao was made Central Colonel; newly appointed Rear-Army Major Xiao Dan was made Inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 壬子，以冠軍司馬臧靈智爲交州刺史。
entries.en: Day renzi: Zang Lingzhi, major to the general who establishes might, took Jiaozhou.
entries.literal: Day renzi: Major of the General Who Establishes Might Zang Lingzhi was made Inspector of Jiaozhou.

entries.zh: 乙卯，申明織成、金薄、彩花、錦繡履之禁。
entries.en: Day yimao: bans on figured silk, gold leaf, floral appliqué, and brocade shoes were proclaimed again.
entries.literal: Day yimao: the prohibitions on figured weave, gold foil, colored floral trim, and broidered shoes were reiterated.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：郭璞稱永昌之名，有二日之象，而隆昌之號亦同焉。
entries.en: The historian says: Guo Pu held that the name Yongchang bears the sign of two suns—and the era name Longchang is likewise.
entries.literal: The historian says: Guo Pu said the name Yongchang has the image of two suns—and the era name Longchang is the same.

entries.zh: 案漢中平六年，獻帝卽位，便改元爲光熹，張讓、段珪誅後，改元爲昭寧，董卓輔政，改元爲永漢，一歲四號也。
entries.en: It is on record that in Han Zhongping 6, when Emperor Xian ascended, the era was at once changed to Guangxi; after Zhang Rang and Duan Gui were killed it became Zhaoning; when Dong Zhuo seized power it became Yonghan—four era names in one year.
entries.literal: It is recorded that in Han Zhongping 6, when Emperor Xian took the throne he at once changed the era to Guangxi; after the execution of Zhang Rang and Duan Gui it was changed to Zhaoning; when Dong Zhuo held the government it was changed to Yonghan—four era names in one year.

entries.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年，長沙王乂事敗，成都王穎改元爲永安；
entries.en: In Jin, Emperor Hui's Taian 2, when Prince Yi of Changsha fell, Prince Ying of Chengdu changed the era to Yongan;
entries.literal: In Jin Emperor Hui's Taian 2, when Prince Yi of Changsha's affair failed, Prince Ying of Chengdu changed the era to Yongan;

entries.zh: 穎自鄴奪，河間王顒復改元爲永興，一歲三號也。
entries.en: when Ying seized rule from Ye, Prince Yong of Hejian changed the era again to Yongxing—three era names in one year.
entries.literal: when Ying seized power from Ye, Prince Yong of Hejian again changed the era to Yongxing—three era names in one year.

entries.zh: 隆昌、延興、建武，亦三改年號。
entries.en: Longchang, Yanxing, and Jianwu likewise saw three changes of era name.
entries.literal: Longchang, Yanxing, and Jianwu also saw three era changes.

entries.zh: 故知喪亂之軌迹，雖千載而必同矣。
entries.en: Thus one knows that the path of chaos and collapse, though a thousand years lie between, is always the same.
entries.literal: Thus one knows that the track of turmoil and ruin, though a thousand years apart, is sure to be the same.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第五 本紀第五
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 5, Annals 5
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 5, Annals 5

entries.zh: 高宗明皇帝諱鸞，字景栖，始安貞王道生子也。
entries.en: Emperor Ming, canonically titled High Ancestor, bore the name Luan and the style Jingshu; he was born to Prince Zhen of Shi'an, Daosheng.
entries.literal: High Ancestor Emperor Ming, taboo name Luan, style Jingshu, was a son of Prince Zhen of Shi'an, Daosheng.

entries.zh: 小諱玄度。
entries.en: In childhood he was called Xuandu.
entries.literal: Childhood taboo Xuandu.

entries.zh: 少孤，太祖撫育，恩過諸子。
entries.en: He lost his parents early; the Grand Ancestor brought him up and loved him more than his own children.
entries.literal: Orphaned while young, the Grand Ancestor raised him and favored him beyond his own sons.

entries.zh: 宋泰豫元年，爲安吉令，有嚴能之名。
entries.en: Song Taiyu 1: he became magistrate of Anji and won repute for strict, capable rule.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiyu of Song, he was made magistrate of Anji and gained a name for stern competence.

entries.zh: 補武陵王左常侍，不拜。
entries.en: He was named left attendant to the Prince of Wuling and declined.
entries.literal: He was appointed left attendant to the Prince of Wuling but did not accept the post.

entries.zh: 元徽二年，爲永世令。
entries.en: Yuanhui 2: he was made magistrate of Yongshi.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui, he was made magistrate of Yongshi.

entries.zh: 昇明二年，爲邵陵王安南記室參軍，未拜，仍遷寧朔將軍、淮南宣城二郡太守。
entries.en: Shengming 2: he was named recorder on the pacifying-south staff of the Prince of Shaoling; before he reported, he was moved to general who pacifies the north and administrator of Huainan and Xuancheng.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shengming, he was made recorder on the Pacifying-South staff of the Prince of Shaoling; before he took office he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and administrator of the two commanderies of Huainan and Xuancheng.

entries.zh: 尋進號輔國將軍。
entries.en: Soon his rank was raised to general who assists the state.
entries.literal: Soon afterward his title was advanced to General Who Assists the State.

entries.zh: 太祖踐阼，遷侍中，封西昌侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, he became palace attendant and was enfeoffed as marquis of Xichang with 1,000 households.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor ascended the throne, Luan was transferred to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xichang with a fief of 1,000 households.

entries.zh: 建元二年，爲持節、督郢州司州之義陽諸軍事、冠軍將軍、郢州刺史，進號征虜將軍。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianyuan: he bore the staff, supervised Ying and Yiyang in Sizhou, became champion general and inspector of Ying, and was raised to general who conquers the barbarians.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of all military affairs of Yingzhou and Yiyang in Sizhou, Champion General, and Inspector of Yingzhou, and advanced to General Who Conquers the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，轉度支尚書，領右軍將軍。
entries.en: At Emperor Wu's accession he became minister of revenue and also right-army general.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and concurrently Right-Army General.

entries.zh: 永明元年，遷侍中，領驍騎將軍。
entries.en: Yongming 1: he was made palace attendant and valiant-cavalry general.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrently Valiant-Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 王子侯舊乘纏帷車，高宗獨乘下帷，儀從如素士。
entries.en: Princes and marquises had always traveled in curtained coaches; Luan alone used lowered screens, his train no grander than a common officer's.
entries.literal: Princes and marquises of old rode carriages with wrapped curtains; the High Ancestor alone rode with lowered curtains, his escort like that of a plain gentleman.

entries.zh: 公事混撓，販食人擔火誤燒牛鼻，豫章王白世祖，世祖笑焉。
entries.en: Government was in disorder; a peddler's brazier set an ox's nose afire by mistake. The Prince of Yuzhang reported it to Emperor Wu, who only laughed.
entries.literal: Official business was in confusion; a food vendor's carrying-fire accidentally burned an ox's nose. The Prince of Yuzhang told Emperor Wu, and the emperor laughed.

entries.zh: 轉爲散騎常侍、左衛將軍，清道而行，上甚悅。
entries.en: He became irregular cavalry attendant and left guards general, had the streets cleared when he passed, and the throne was much pleased.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Irregular Cavalry Attendant and Left Guards General; he had the road cleared when he went out, and the sovereign was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 二年，出爲征虜將軍、吳興太守。
entries.en: In the second year he left the capital as general who conquers the barbarians and administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: In the second year, he went out as General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 四年，遷中領軍，常侍竝如故。
entries.en: In the fourth year he became central army-inspector-in-chief, keeping his attendant titles.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to Central Army-inspector-in-Chief, his attendant posts unchanged.

entries.zh: 五年，爲持節、監豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡軍事、右將軍、豫州刺史。
entries.en: In the fifth year he took the staff, supervised Yuzhou together with Xiyang in Yingzhou and Runan in Sizhou, became right general and inspector of Yu.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, he was made Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs of Yuzhou, Xiyang in Yingzhou, and Runan in Sizhou, Right General, and Inspector of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 七年，爲尚書右僕射。
entries.en: In the seventh year he became right vice director of the masters of writing.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 八年，加領衛尉。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was also made commandant of the guard.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, he was additionally made Commandant of the Guard.

entries.zh: 十年，轉左僕射。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was moved to left vice director.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, he was transferred to Left Vice Director.

entries.zh: 十一年，領右衛將軍。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he also commanded the right guards.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year, he additionally led the Right Guards.

entries.zh: 世祖遺詔爲侍中、尚書令，尋加鎮軍將軍，給班劔二十人。
entries.en: Emperor Wu's final testament made him palace attendant and director of the masters of writing; soon he was also general who stabilizes the army, with twenty sword-bearers in his train.
entries.literal: By Emperor Wu's deathbed will he was made Palace Attendant and Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he was additionally made General Who Stabilizes the Army and given twenty ceremonial sword-guards.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，卽本號爲大將軍，給鼓吹一部，親兵五百人。
entries.en: Longchang 1: his present rank was raised to great general; he received a band of martial pipes and five hundred household guards.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was promoted on his existing title to Great General and given one set of martial pipes and five hundred personal troops.

entries.zh: 尋又加中書監、開府儀同三司。
entries.en: Soon he was also supervisor of the secretariat with honors equal to the three excellencies.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally made Supervisor of the Secretariat and given secretariat parity equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 郁林王廢，海陵王立，爲使持節、都督揚南徐二州軍事、驃騎大將軍、錄尚書事、揚州刺史，開府如故，增班劔爲三十人，封宣城郡公，二千戶。
entries.en: After the Prince of Yulin was removed and the Prince of Hailing made emperor, Luan bore the staff with full powers, commanded Yang and South Xu, recorded the masters of writing, and became inspector of Yangzhou, retaining his secretariat office; his guard of swords rose to thirty, and he was made duke of Xuancheng with 2,000 households.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yulin was deposed and the Prince of Hailing enthroned, Luan was made Bearer of the Staff with full credentials, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs of Yang and South Xu, Chief Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yangzhou, his secretariat office unchanged, his sword-guards increased to thirty, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xuancheng with a fief of 2,000 households.

entries.zh: 鎮東府城。
entries.en: He held the eastern palace fortress.
entries.literal: He garrisoned the Eastern Palace city.

entries.zh: 給兵五千人，錢二百萬，布千匹。
entries.en: Five thousand soldiers, two million cash, and a thousand bolts of cloth were granted him.
entries.literal: He was given five thousand troops, two million in cash, and a thousand bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 九江作難，假黃皞，事寧，表送之。
entries.en: During the Jiujiang rebellion he was lent the yellow battle-axe; when peace returned, he submitted it back.
entries.literal: When Jiujiang rose in revolt, he was lent the yellow battle-axe; when the affair was settled, he memorialized to return it.

entries.zh: 尋加黃皞、都督中外諸軍事、太傅，領大將軍、揚州牧，增班劔爲四十人，給幢絡三望車，前後部羽葆鼓吹，劔履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎、掾、屬各四人，封宣城王，邑五千戶，持節、侍中、中書監、錄尚書並如故。
entries.en: Soon he received the yellow axe again, overall command within and without, and the grand tutorship, while keeping great general and Yangzhou; forty sword-guards, a triple-canopy coach with banners, pipes fore and aft, sword and shoes in audience, unhurried entry, praise without naming, and staffs of four chief clerks, marshals, secretariat aides, and clerks on each flank; he was made prince of Xuancheng with 5,000 households, and kept the staff, palace attendance, secretariat supervision, and chief recordership as before.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally given the yellow battle-axe, command of all armies within and without, and the post of Grand Tutor, while retaining Great General and Governor of Yangzhou; his sword-guards were increased to forty; he was given a triple-canopy carriage with pennons, martial pipes before and behind, permission to wear sword and shoes in court and enter without hastening, to be praised without having his name spoken, and a full staff of left and right chief clerks, marshals, secretariat attendants, and aides four each; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng with a fief of 5,000 households; Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Chief Recorder—all unchanged.

entries.zh: 未拜，太后令廢海陵王，以上入纂太祖爲第三子，羣臣三請，乃受命。
entries.en: Before he took office, the empress dowager removed the Prince of Hailing and set Luan in the line as the Grand Ancestor's third son; only after three rounds of pleading from the court did he accept.
entries.literal: Before he accepted these honors, the empress dowager deposed the Prince of Hailing and installed Luan as the Grand Ancestor's third son; the ministers begged three times before he accepted the mandate.

entries.zh: 建武元年冬十月癸亥，卽皇帝位。
entries.en: Jianwu 1, winter, tenth month, day guihai: he took the throne.
entries.literal: Winter, tenth month, day guihai of the first year of Jianwu: he ascended the imperial throne.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「皇齊受終建極，握鏡臨宸，神武重輝，欽明懿鑠，七百攸長，磐石斯固。
entries.en: An edict said: "Qi took heaven's end and built the height, holding the mirror and ruling from the hall; martial spirit burns bright again, wise grace gleams; seven hundred years should stand firm as bedrock.
entries.literal: An edict said: "The house of Qi received the mandate, established the pinnacle, holds the mirror and faces the throne; divine martial radiance shines anew, reverent brilliance is splendid; seven hundred years would be long, and bedrock thus firm.

entries.zh: 而王度中蹇，天階荐阻，嗣命多違，蕃釁孔棘，宏圖景曆，將墜諸淵。
entries.en: Yet the royal way stumbled, heaven's stair met one obstruction after another, heirs were set aside, and frontier feuds bristled; the great plan and shining calendar nearly sank into the deep.
entries.literal: Yet the royal measure faltered mid-course, heaven's steps met repeated blocks, the succession was often violated, and border troubles grew desperately sharp; the grand design and bright calendar were about to fall into the abyss.

entries.zh: 宣德皇后遠鑒崇替，憲章舊典，疇咨台揆，允定靈策，用集寶命于予一人。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Xuande, seeing far how dynasties turn, held to statute and ancient rule, asked counsel of the chief ministers, fixed the sacred design, and laid the precious charge on me alone.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Xuande, discerning far the rise and fall, took the statutes and old canon, consulted the chief ministers, truly settled the divine plan, and gathered the precious mandate upon me alone.

entries.zh: 猥以虛薄，纘承大業，仰繫鴻丕，顧臨兆民，永懷先構，若履春冰，寅憂夕惕，罔識攸濟，思與萬國播此惟新。
entries.en: Humble and thin as I am, I take up the great work, tie myself to heaven's vast favor, and face the million lives below; I think always of the work of old as on spring ice; worry fills my mornings and fear my nights, and I do not see the ford; I would spread this renewal through every realm.
entries.literal: I am mean and slight, yet inherit the great enterprise; I look up to the vast blessing and down upon the myriad people; I forever recall the former foundation as if treading spring ice; from dawn I worry and at dusk I tremble, not knowing what will carry me through; I wish with all lands to spread this renewal.

entries.zh: 大赦天下，改元。
entries.en: All under heaven was pardoned, and the era name was changed.
entries.literal: A great amnesty was proclaimed for all under heaven, and the era name was changed.

entries.zh: 宿衛身普轉一階，其餘文武，賜位二等。
entries.en: Palace guards and body servants each rose one step in rank; the rest of civil and military service gained two.
entries.literal: Palace guards and personal attendants were each advanced one rank; all other civil and military officers received two ranks.

entries.zh: 逋租宿責，換負官物，在建武元年以前，悉原除。
entries.en: Back rent, old arrears, and goods owed to the state before Jianwu 1 were all forgiven.
entries.literal: Overdue rents and old debts, and goods owed to government offices, incurred before the first year of Jianwu—all were wholly remitted.

entries.zh: 劫賊餘口在臺府者，可悉原放。
entries.en: Kin left from bandit gangs held in capital prisons might all be freed.
entries.literal: Surviving dependents of bandits held in the capital offices might all be pardoned and released.

entries.zh: 負釁流徙，竝還本鄉。」
entries.en: Debtors and criminals in exile were all returned home."
entries.literal: Those exiled for debt or crime were all sent back to their native districts."

entries.zh: 太尉王敬則爲大司馬，司空陳顯達爲太尉，尚書令王晏加驃騎大將軍，中領軍蕭諶爲領軍將軍、南徐州刺史，皇子寶義爲揚州刺史，中護軍王玄邈爲南兖州刺史，新除右將軍張瑰爲右光祿大夫，平北將軍王廣之爲江州刺史。
entries.en: Wang Jingze, grand commandant, became grand marshal; Chen Xianda, minister of works, became grand commandant; Wang Yan, director of the masters of writing, was also made general of chariots and cavalry; Xiao Chen, central army-inspector-in-chief, became commandant of the guards and inspector of South Xu; Prince Bao Yi was made inspector of Yangzhou; Wang Xuanmiao, central army-protector, was made inspector of South Yanzhou; Zhang Gui, newly made right general, became right grandee of splendor; Wang Guangzhi, pacifying-north general, was made inspector of Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Jingze was made Grand Marshal; Minister of Works Chen Xianda was made Grand Commandant; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was additionally made General of Chariots and Cavalry; Central Army-inspector-in-Chief Xiao Chen was made Commandant of the Guards and Inspector of South Xuzhou; the prince Bao Yi was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Central Army-protector Wang Xuanmiao was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; the newly appointed Right General Zhang Gui was made Right Grandee of Splendor; Pacifying-North General Wang Guangzhi was made Inspector of Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 乙丑，詔斷遠近上禮。
entries.en: Day yichou: an edict forbade congratulatory offerings from far and near.
entries.literal: Day yichou: an edict cut off distant and near congratulatory gifts.

entries.zh: 丁卯，詔「自今雕文篆刻，歲時光新，可悉停省。
entries.en: Day dingmao: an edict said, "Hereafter figured carving, seal script, and inlay, and every seasonal novelty in dress—all are to cease.
entries.literal: Day dingmao: an edict said, "From now on carved ornament and seal-cut inlay, and yearly novelties in dress—let all be stopped and reduced.

entries.zh: 蕃牧守宰，或有薦獻，事非任土，嚴加禁斷。」
entries.en: Where border princes, prefects, or magistrates send tribute not proper to their land, forbid it in the strictest terms."
entries.literal: Where frontier lords, governors, or magistrates make offerings not native to their soil, strictly forbid and cut them off."

entries.zh: 追贈安陸昭侯緬爲安陸王。
entries.en: Mian, Marquis Zhao of Anlu, was posthumously raised to prince of Anlu.
entries.literal: Mian, Marquis Zhao of Anlu, was posthumously advanced to Prince of Anlu.

entries.zh: 己巳，以安陸侯子寶晊爲湘州刺史。
entries.en: Day jisi: Bao Zhi, son of the marquis of Anlu, was made inspector of Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: Day jisi: the son of the Marquis of Anlu, Bao Zhi, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「頃守職之吏，多違舊典，存私害公，實興民蠹。
entries.en: An edict said: "Of late magistrates have broken old law, served themselves and hurt the public, and become a true plague on the people.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Lately officials in office have often violated the old statutes, kept private ends and harmed the public, and truly become parasites on the people.

entries.zh: 今商旅稅石頭後渚及夫鹵借倩，一皆停息。
entries.en: The merchant toll at Shitou rear ford and every salt-field rent and lease—stop them all.
entries.literal: Now the merchant tax at Shitou rear ford and every levy on salt pans and leases—all are halted.

entries.zh: 所在凡厥公宜，可卽符斷。
entries.en: Wherever such public levies remain, cut them off at once by order.
entries.literal: Everywhere, whatever such public exactions exist, cut them off at once by warrant.

entries.zh: 主曹詳爲其制，憲司明加聽察。」
entries.en: Chief clerks shall draft the rules in full; the censorate shall hear cases and investigate openly."
entries.literal: The chief clerks shall draw up detailed rules; the censorate shall listen and investigate with clarity."

entries.zh: 十一月癸酉，以西中郎長史始安王遙光爲揚州刺史，晉壽太守王洪範爲青、冀二州刺史，尚書令王晏領太子少傅。
entries.en: Eleventh month, day guiyou: Xiao Yaoguang, prince of Shi'an and staff clerk of the west central corps, was made inspector of Yangzhou; Wang Hongfan, administrator of Jinshou, was made inspector of Qing and Ji; Wang Yan, director of the masters of writing, concurrently served as the crown prince's junior tutor.
entries.literal: Eleventh month, day guiyou: Staff Clerk of the West Central Corps Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an was made Inspector of Yangzhou; Administrator of Jinshou Wang Hongfan was made Inspector of Qing and Ji; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan additionally held the Crown Prince's Junior Tutor.

entries.zh: 甲戌，大司馬尋陽公王敬則等十三人進爵邑各有差。
entries.en: Day jiaxu: Wang Jingze, grand marshal and duke of Xunyang, and twelve others were raised in rank and fief, each by a set amount.
entries.literal: Day jiaxu: Grand Marshal Duke Jingze of Xunyang and twelve others were advanced in noble rank and fief, each by a different measure.

entries.zh: 詔省新林苑，先是民地，悉以還主，原責本直。
entries.en: An edict closed the New Forest Park; former peasant holdings were returned to their owners, and old dues were remitted.
entries.literal: An edict abolished the New Forest Park; the former commoners' land was all returned to its owners, and original payments were forgiven.

entries.zh: 庚辰，立皇子寶義爲晉安王，寶玄爲江夏王，寶源爲廬陵王，寶夤爲建安王，寶融爲隨郡王，寶攸爲南平王。
entries.en: Day gengchen: Bao Yi was made prince of Jin'an; Bao Xuan, prince of Jiangxia; Bao Yuan, prince of Luling; Bao Yin, prince of Jian'an; Bao Rong, prince of Suizhou; Bao You, prince of Nanping.
entries.literal: Day gengchen: the princes Bao Yi, Bao Xuan, Bao Yuan, Bao Yin, Bao Rong, and Bao You were enfeoffed as Princes of Jin'an, Jiangxia, Luling, Jian'an, Suizhou, and Nanping.

entries.zh: 甲申，詔曰：「邑宰祿薄俸微，不足代耕，雖任土恒貢，亦爲勞費，自今悉斷。」
entries.en: Day jiashen: an edict said, "Magistrates' pay is thin and will not feed a household; even fixed local tribute is a burden—henceforth end it all."
entries.literal: Day jiashen: an edict said, "District magistrates receive thin salaries too small to replace farming; though tribute fixed by their soil is constant, it is still labor and expense—from now on cut it all off."

entries.zh: 又詔「宣城國五品以上，悉與滿敘。
entries.en: A second edict said, "In Xuancheng, all of fifth rank and above shall be advanced to the full of their grade;
entries.literal: Another edict said, "In the state of Xuancheng, all of fifth rank and above shall receive full advancement in rank;

entries.zh: 自此以下，皆聽解遣。
entries.en: from that rank down, all may be dismissed from office.
entries.literal: from this rank downward, all may be released from service.

entries.zh: 其欲仕，適所樂。」
entries.en: Those who wish to serve may take whatever post suits their wish."
entries.literal: Those who wish to serve may take posts suited to their inclination."

entries.zh: 乙酉，追尊始安貞王爲景皇，妃爲懿后。
entries.en: Day yiyou: Prince Zhen of Shi'an was posthumously titled Emperor Jing, and his consort Empress Yi.
entries.literal: Day yiyou: Prince Zhen of Shi'an was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, and his consort as Empress Yi.

entries.zh: 丙戌，以輔國將軍聞喜公遙欣爲荊州刺史，寧朔將軍豐城公遙昌爲豫州刺史。
entries.en: Day bingxu: Xiao Yaoxin, duke of Wenxi and general who assists the state, was made inspector of Jingzhou; Xiao Yaochang, duke of Fengcheng and general who pacifies the north, was made inspector of Yuzhou.
entries.literal: Day bingxu: General Who Assists the State Duke Yaoxin of Wenxi was made Inspector of Jingzhou; General Who Pacifies the North Duke Yaochang of Fengcheng was made Inspector of Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 丁亥，詔「細作中署、材官、車府，凡諸工，可悉開番假，遞令休息」。
entries.en: Day dinghai: an edict said, "Fine crafts, the arsenal, and the chariot office—every workshop may rotate furloughs and rest in turn."
entries.literal: Day dinghai: an edict said, "The fine-crafts central office, the arsenal, and the chariot office—all workshops may open rotating leave and pass rest in turn."

entries.zh: 戊子，立皇太子寶卷，賜天下爲父後者爵一級，孝子順孫、義夫節婦，普加甄賜明揚。
entries.en: Day wuzi: Bao Juan was made crown prince; every man who stood as heir to his father gained one rank; filial sons, worthy grandsons, righteous men, and faithful widows were sought out, praised, and rewarded.
entries.literal: Day wuzi: the crown prince Bao Juan was established; all who were heirs to their fathers received one rank; filial sons, obedient grandsons, men of righteousness, and chaste wives were broadly singled out, commended, and promoted.

entries.zh: 表其衡閭，賚以束帛。
entries.en: Their neighborhoods were posted in honor, and they were given silk.
entries.literal: Their lanes were marked on the registers and they were given bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 己丑，詔「東宮肇建，遠近或有慶禮，可悉斷之。」
entries.en: Day jichou: an edict said, "The heir's palace is new; gifts of congratulation from far and near are forbidden."
entries.literal: Day jichou: an edict said, "The eastern palace is newly founded; distant and near may wish to send congratulatory gifts—all such are cut off."

entries.zh: 壬辰，以新除征虜將軍江夏王寶玄爲郢州刺史。
entries.en: Day renchen: Bao Xuan, newly made general who conquers the barbarians and prince of Jiangxia, was made inspector of Yingzhou.
entries.literal: Day renchen: the newly appointed General Who Conquers the Barbarians Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia was made Inspector of Yingzhou.

entries.zh: 永明中，御史中丞沈淵表百官年登七十，皆令致仕，竝窮困私門。
entries.en: In Yongming, Censor-in-Chief Shen Yuan urged that every official who turned seventy be retired, noting that many were destitute at home.
entries.literal: In the Yongming era, Censor-in-Chief Shen Yuan memorialized that all officials who reached seventy years should be made to retire, and that they were all in want in their private households.

entries.zh: 庚子，詔曰：「日者百司耆齒，許以自陳，東西二省，猶沾微俸，辭事私庭，榮祿兼謝，興言愛老，實有矜懷。
entries.en: Day gengzi: an edict said, "Lately elders in the hundred offices were permitted to step down; yet men in the two secretariats still drew a slender pay while they left business to their homes and refused both rank and salary—such love of age moves us to pity.
entries.literal: Day gengzi: an edict said, "Lately the hundred offices, at advanced age, were allowed to declare themselves; the eastern and western secretariats still drew a small salary, yet they resigned affairs to their private gates and refused both honor and stipend—speaking of love for the aged, this truly stirs pity.

entries.zh: 自縉紳年及，可一遵永明七年以前銓敘之科。」
entries.en: From the gentry upward, when they reach that age, let all follow the advancement code of before Yongming 7."
entries.literal: From gentry who reach that age onward, let all follow the advancement rules used before the seventh year of Yongming."

entries.zh: 上輔政所誅諸王，是月復屬籍，各封子爲侯。
entries.en: The princes killed in his regency were readmitted to the clan roll this month, and a son of each was made marquis.
entries.literal: The princes put to death during his regency had their names restored to the imperial clan this month, and each had a son enfeoffed as marquis.

entries.zh: 四年春正月庚午，大赦。
entries.en: Fourth year, spring, first month, day gengwu: a general amnesty.
entries.literal: Fourth year, spring, first month, day gengwu: a general amnesty.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「嘉肴停俎，定方旨於必甘；
entries.en: An edict said: "Fine dishes may rest on the stand, yet the right flavor must prove sweet at last;
entries.literal: An edict said: "Fine dishes may rest on the stand, yet the right flavor must be sweet in the end;

entries.zh: 良玉在攻，表圭璋於旣就。
entries.en: good jade may lie under the chisel, yet the scepter-gem shines only when the shaping is done.
entries.literal: good jade may lie under the chisel, yet the scepter-gem shows itself only when the work is done.

entries.zh: 是以陶鈞萬品，務本爲先；
entries.en: Therefore in shaping the myriad kinds, to hold to the root comes first;
entries.literal: Therefore in shaping the myriad kinds, to hold to the root comes first;

entries.zh: 經緯九區，學斅爲大。
entries.en: in ordering the nine regions, learning and culture are the greatest thing.
entries.literal: in ordering the nine regions, learning and culture are the greatest thing.

entries.zh: 往因時康，崇建庠序，屯虞薦有，權從省廢，謳誦寂寥，倏移年稔，永言古昔，無忘旰昃。
entries.en: In easier times the school halls were raised in splendor; when hardship came they were cut back for a season; song and recitation fell silent, and years piled up before one knew it—yet to speak of the ancients is never to forget the lamp at dusk.
entries.literal: In former days, when the times were at ease, the school halls were raised in splendor; when hardship followed in turn, they were provisionally cut back; songs and recitation fell silent, and years heaped up before one knew it—yet to speak of the ancients is never to forget the lamp at dusk.

entries.zh: 今華夏乂安，要荒慕向，締脩東序，實允適時。
entries.en: Now within the four seas there is peace, and the far marches turn their faces in longing; to bind and repair the Eastern Hall is truly fit for the hour.
entries.literal: Now within the four seas there is peace, and the far marches turn their faces in longing; to bind and repair the Eastern Hall is truly fit for the hour.

entries.zh: 便可式依舊章，廣延國胄，弘敷景業，光被後昆。」
entries.en: Let the old statutes be taken as model, the imperial kin widely enrolled, the bright enterprise spread abroad, and its light cast upon generations to come."
entries.literal: Let the old statutes be taken as model, the imperial kin widely enrolled, the bright enterprise spread abroad, and its light cast upon generations to come."

entries.zh: 壬寅，詔「民產子者，蠲其父母調役一年，又賜米十斛。
entries.en: Day renyin: an edict said, "When the people bear a child, their parents' levies and corvée are forgiven for one year, and ten hu of grain are granted besides.
entries.literal: Day renyin: an edict said, "When the people bear a child, their parents' levies and corvée are remitted for one year, and ten hu of grain are also granted.

entries.zh: 新婚者，蠲夫役一年」。
entries.en: When they newly marry, the husband's corvée is forgiven for one year."
entries.literal: When they newly marry, the husband's corvée is remitted for one year."

entries.zh: 丙辰，尚書令王晏伏誅。
entries.en: Day bingchen: Wang Yan, director of the masters of writing, was put to death.
entries.literal: Day bingchen: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan was executed.

entries.zh: 帝明審有吏才，持法無所借。
entries.en: The emperor was clear-sighted and had the talent of an administrator; in holding to the law he spared no one.
entries.literal: The emperor was clear-sighted and had the talent of an administrator; in holding to the law he showed favor to none.

entries.zh: 制御親幸，臣下肅清。
entries.en: He reined in the ruler's favorites, and his ministers were brought to order.
entries.literal: He controlled those the ruler favored, and his ministers were brought to order.

entries.zh: 驅使寒人不得用四幅傘，大存儉約。
entries.en: He drove men of humble birth hard and would not let them carry four-panel umbrellas; he held hard to thrift.
entries.literal: He drove and used men of humble birth and would not let them use four-panel umbrellas; he greatly preserved thrift.

entries.zh: 罷世祖所起新林苑，以地還百姓；
entries.en: He abolished the New Forest Park that Emperor Wu had built and returned the land to the people;
entries.literal: He abolished the New Forest Park that Shizu had built and returned the land to the people;

entries.zh: 廢文帝所起太子東田，斥賣之；
entries.en: he abolished the crown prince's Eastern Fields that Emperor Wen had built and sold them off;
entries.literal: he abolished the crown prince's Eastern Fields that Emperor Wen had built and sold them off;

entries.zh: 永明中輿輦舟乘，悉剔取金銀還主衣庫。
entries.en: in the Yongming era all carriages and boats had their gold and silver stripped and returned to the master-of-garments storehouse.
entries.literal: in the Yongming era all carriages and boats had their gold and silver stripped and returned to the master-of-garments storehouse.

entries.zh: 太官進御食，有裹蒸，帝曰：「我食此不盡，可四片破之，餘充晚食。」
entries.en: When the grand kitchen sent up wrapped steam-cakes, the emperor said, "I cannot finish this; break it into four and keep the rest for the evening meal."
entries.literal: When the Grand Kitchen presented imperial food with wrapped steam-cakes, the emperor said, "I cannot finish this; it may be broken into four pieces, and the rest kept for the evening meal."

entries.zh: 而世祖掖庭中宮殿服御，一無所改。
entries.en: Yet in Shizu's inner palaces not a single garment or fitting was changed.
entries.literal: Yet in the inner palaces of Shizu not a single garment or fitting was changed.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第六 本紀第六
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 6, Annals 6
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 6, Annals 6

entries.zh: 夏四月己巳，立皇太子誦，大赦，賜民為父後爵一級。
entries.en: Fourth month of summer, day jisi: Crown Prince Song was installed; the realm was amnestied; commoners serving as their fathers' heirs received one step in rank.
entries.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jisi: Crown Prince Song was installed; general amnesty; commoners who were heirs for their fathers were given one rank of nobility.

entries.zh: 甲戌，以寧朔將軍柳惔為梁、南秦二州刺史。
entries.en: Day jiaxu: Liu Yan, pacifying-the-north general, took Liang and South Qin.
entries.literal: Day jiaxu: Pacifying-the-North General Liu Yan was made Inspector of the two provinces of Liang and South Qin.

entries.zh: 後宮遭火之後，更起仙華、神仙、玉壽諸殿，刻畫雕綵，青
entries.en: After fire in the inner palaces, he raised again the halls Xianhua, Shendian, and Yushou, carved and painted in color—green
entries.literal: After the rear palace suffered fire, he rebuilt the Xianhua, Shendian, and Yushou halls, carved and painted in colors, green

entries.zh: 〈青
entries.en: 〈(lacquer; source corrupt here)
entries.literal: 〈green lacquer; text damaged

entries.en: 〈reading restored from parallel texts〉
entries.literal: 〈doubtful reading〉

entries.zh: 金口帶，麝香塗壁，錦幔珠簾，窮極綺麗。
entries.en: lacquer, gilded trim at the openings, musk on the walls, brocade hangings and pearl blinds—splendor taken as far as it could go.
entries.literal: lacquer with gilded mouths and bands, musk smeared on the walls, brocade curtains and pearl screens—luxury pushed to the limit.

entries.zh: 縶役工匠，自夜達曉，猶不副速，乃剔取諸寺佛剎殿藻井仙人騎獸以充足之。
entries.en: Artisans were pressed to work night through dawn and still could not finish fast enough; they stripped the temple halls—coffered ceilings, ceiling immortals, riders on beasts—to make up the shortfall.
entries.literal: Craftsmen were bound to labor from night till dawn; still they could not keep pace, so ornaments were stripped from Buddhist halls in the temples—the coffered ceilings, immortals, and beast-mounted riders—to fill the need.

entries.zh: 世祖興光樓上施青漆，世謂之「青樓」。
entries.en: Emperor Shizu's Xingguang Tower was finished in green lacquer; people called it the "Green Tower."
entries.literal: On Emperor Shizu's Xingguang Tower green lacquer was applied; the age called it the "Green Tower."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「武帝不巧，何不純用瑠璃。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Emperor Wu had no craft—why not build it all in glass?"
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Emperor Wu was unskilled—why not use glass alone?"

entries.zh: 宣德太后令曰：「皇室受終，祖宗齊聖，太祖高皇帝肇基駿命，膺籙受圖，世祖武皇帝係明下武，高宗明皇帝重隆景業，咸降年不永，宮車係晏。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Xuande proclaimed: "The throne passed in turn; our forebears were sages together. The High Ancestor laid the splendid foundation and took heaven's register; the Martial Ancestor continued the bright mandate in martial succession; the Luminous High Ancestor renewed the bright estate—each died young, the palace carriage halted at dusk.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Xuande issued an order: "The imperial house received the mandate; the ancestors were jointly sage. The High Ancestor founded the splendid mandate, received the tally and accepted the chart; the Martial Ancestor continued Ming and brought down Wu; the Luminous High Ancestor again raised the glorious enterprise—all had years cut short; the imperial carriage was tethered at twilight.

entries.zh: 皇祚之重，允屬儲元。
entries.en: The weight of the realm rightly fell on the crown prince.
entries.literal: The weight of imperial fortune properly belonged to the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 而稟質凶愚，發於稚齒。
entries.en: Yet from baby teeth he showed a savage, witless nature.
entries.literal: Yet he was endowed with vicious stupidity from his milk teeth.

entries.zh: 爰自保姆，迄至成童，忍戾昏頑，觸途必著。
entries.en: From nurse to grown boy he was savage, twisted, and dull—every step left a wound.
entries.literal: From wet-nurse to full boyhood he was cruel, perverse, dull, and stubborn—wherever he touched the path he left a mark.

entries.zh: 高宗留心正嫡，立嫡惟長，輔以羣才，閒以賢戚，內外維持，冀免多難，未及朞稔，便逞屠戮。
entries.en: Gaozong fixed on the true heir, set the eldest son of the proper line, backed him with able men and worthy kin, braced court and camp to spare the state—yet before a year was out the boy turned butcher.
entries.literal: The High Ancestor attended to the legitimate heir, established the eldest legitimate son, aided by a host of talents and leavened with worthy kin, maintaining inside and outside, hoping to avoid many calamities—before one full year he unleashed slaughter.

entries.zh: 密戚近親，元勳良輔，覆族殲門，旬月相係。
entries.en: Kinsmen near and far, founding ministers and loyal aides—clans wiped out, gates sealed in blood, one month after another.
entries.literal: Close kin and near relatives, founding ministers and good aides—families overturned, gates destroyed, month after month in succession.

entries.zh: 凡所任仗，盡慝窮姦，皆營伍屠販，容狀險醜，身秉朝權，手斷國命，誅戮無辜，納其財產，睚眦之閒，屠覆比屋。
entries.en: Every man he trusted was a villain to the bone—camp riffraff and market butchers, faces foul and feral; he held the court in his fist and the realm by his whim, killed the guiltless for their gold, and over a trifle razed whole lanes.
entries.literal: All he relied on were utterly wicked and treacherous—all camp soldiers and butcher peddlers, features dangerous and ugly; holding court power in person, cutting off the state's life with his hand; executing the innocent and seizing their goods; in the space of a resentful glance, slaughtering whole households.

entries.zh: 身居元首，好是賤事，危冠短服，坐臥以之。
entries.en: Though he wore the crown he loved low work—tall caps and short jackets for sitting and sleeping.
entries.literal: Though he sat as supreme head, he loved base tasks—dangerous caps and short coats, sitting and lying in them.

entries.zh: 晨出夜反，無復已極，驅斥氓庶，巷無居人，老細奔遑，寘身無所，東邁西屏，北出南驅，負疾輿屍，填街塞陌。
entries.en: He left at dawn and returned at night without end, drove the people from their lanes till no one dwelt there; young and old ran with nowhere to stand, driven east and west, north and south; the sick were carried, corpses shouldered—streets and alleys choked full.
entries.literal: Out at dawn, back at night, without limit; driving off the common folk until lanes held no dwellers; old and young fled in panic with nowhere to set body; east marched, west herded, north out, south driven; the sick borne, corpses carried—filling streets and blocking lanes.

entries.zh: 興築繕造，日夜不窮，晨構夕毀，朝穿暮塞，絡以隨珠，方斯已陋，飾以璧璫，曾何足道。
entries.en: Building and repair knew no rest—raised by morning, torn down by night, dug at dawn, filled by dusk; even ropes of pearls seemed shabby, jade pendants hardly worth a word.
entries.literal: Construction and repair never ceased day or night—built in the morning, destroyed at evening, pierced at dawn, stopped up at dusk; strung with loose pearls was already crude; adorned with jade ear-studs—how could that even be worth mentioning.

entries.zh: 時暑赫曦，流金鑠石，移竹藝果，匪日伊夜，根未及植，葉已先枯，畚鍤紛紜，勤倦無已。
entries.en: In heat that melted metal and scorched stone he moved bamboo and fruit trees day and night alike; roots had not taken hold before leaves withered; spades and baskets never stopped.
entries.literal: In blazing summer heat, when metal flowed and stones melted, he transplanted bamboo and planted fruit—not by day but by night; roots not yet set, leaves already withered; shovels and baskets in chaos, toil without end.

entries.zh: 散費國儲，專事浮飾，逼奪民財，自近及遠，兆庶恇恇，流宂道路。
entries.en: He emptied the treasury for frippery, robbed the people near and far, and the masses fled in terror along every road.
entries.literal: Squandering the national stores, devoting himself to vain ornament, seizing the people's wealth from near to far—the myriad folk in fear, aimless along the roads.

entries.zh: 府帑既竭，肆奪市道，工商裨販，行號道泣。
entries.en: When the coffers ran dry he looted the markets in the open; craftsmen, traders, and hawkers wept as they walked.
entries.literal: The treasury exhausted, he plundered the markets openly; artisans, merchants, and peddlers cried their trade along the roads.

entries.zh: 屈此萬乘，躬事角抵，昂首翹肩，逞能橦木，觀者如堵，曾無怍容。
entries.en: The ruler of ten thousand chariots wrestled in person—head high, shoulders hunched, daring feats on the pole—while crowds packed like a wall and he never blushed.
entries.literal: This lord of ten thousand chariots stooped to wrestling himself—craning head, lifting shoulders, showing skill on the pole; spectators thick as a wall, yet not a trace of shame.

entries.zh: 芳樂、華林，竝立闤闠，踞肆鼓刀，手銓輕重。
entries.en: At Fangyue and Hualin he pitched market booths side by side, squatted in stalls, beat knives, and weighed goods in his palm.
entries.literal: At Fangyue and Hualin alike they set up market stalls, sat squat in shops, drummed blades, and weighed light and heavy by hand.

entries.zh: 干戈鼓譟，昏曉靡息，無戎而城，豈足云譬。
entries.en: Weapons and drums roared night and day; a capital without an enemy—words fail the likeness.
entries.literal: Arms and drums clamored from dusk to dawn without cease; a city without war—how could words suffice for comparison.

entries.zh: 至於居喪淫讌之愆，三年載弄之醜，反道違常之釁，牝鷄晨鳴之慝，於事已細，故可得而略也。
entries.en: Debauch in mourning, childish games through three years of rule, breaches of rite and reversal of right, the hen that crows at dawn—these are small beside the rest and may be set aside.
entries.literal: As for feasting during mourning, the shame of toys across three years, offenses against the Way and violation of norms, the wickedness of the hen crowing at dawn—these matters are already minor and may be passed over briefly.

entries.zh: 罄楚、越之竹，未足以言，校辛、癸之君，豈或能匹。
entries.en: Strip every bamboo in Chu and Yue and you could not record it all; set him beside the tyrants Xin and Gui—he would still outdo them.
entries.literal: Exhaust all the bamboo of Chu and Yue yet it would not suffice for words; compare him to the lords Xin and Gui—could they even match.

entries.zh: 征東將軍忠武奮發，投袂萬里，光奉明聖，翊成中興。
entries.en: The loyal, martial campaign-east general roused himself, cast his sleeve aside, and marched ten thousand li to serve the bright sage and lift the restoration.
entries.literal: The campaign-east general, loyal and martial, roused in valor, throwing his sleeve for ten thousand li, brightly serving the bright and sage, assisting to complete the central restoration.

entries.zh: 乘勝席卷，掃清京邑，而羣小靡識，嬰城自固，緩戮稽誅，焂彌旬月，宜速勦定，寧我邦家。
entries.en: He swept the capital on the tide of victory, yet these small men would not see reason, clung to the walls, and stalled justice week after week—it is time to crush them and give the realm peace.
entries.literal: Riding victory to sweep all and clear the capital—yet petty men would not see, clinging to the city in self-defense, delaying punishment and deferring execution, dragging on for weeks; he should swiftly annihilate and settle, bringing peace to our state and house.

entries.zh: 可潛遣閒介，密宣此旨，忠勇齊奮，遄加蕩撲，放斥昏凶，衞送外第。
entries.en: Send trusted men in secret to proclaim this will; let the loyal and brave rise together, strike at once, drive out the blind and cruel, and guard him to the outer palace.
entries.literal: Covert agents may be sent in secret to proclaim this intent; loyal and brave together striving, swiftly add sweeping destruction, cast out the dulled and vicious, guard and escort to the outer residence.

entries.zh: 未亡人不幸，驟此百罹，感念存沒，心焉如割。
entries.en: I, who remain, am wretched to meet such hundredfold grief; thinking of the quick and the dead, my heart is torn.
entries.literal: The surviving woman is unlucky, suddenly meeting these hundred calamities; recalling the living and dead, my heart is as if cut.

entries.zh: 奈何！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 奈何！」
entries.en: Alas!"
entries.literal: Alas!"

entries.zh: 又令依漢海昏侯故事，追封東昏侯。
entries.en: She further ordered, on the Han model of Marquis Haihun, that he be posthumously titled Marquess of Eastern Darkness.
entries.literal: She also ordered that, following the Han precedent of Marquis Haihun, he be posthumously ennobled as Marquess of Eastern Darkness.

entries.zh: 茹法珍、梅蟲兒、王咺之等伏誅。
entries.en: Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Wang Xuanzhi, and the rest were put to death.
entries.literal: Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Wang Xuanzhi, and others were executed.

entries.zh: 豐勇之原死。
entries.en: Feng Yongzhi was spared execution.
entries.literal: Feng Yongzhi was pardoned from the death sentence.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：漢宣帝時，南郡獲白虎，獲之者張武，言武張而猛服也。
entries.en: The historian writes: Under Han Emperor Xuan, Nan commandery took a white tiger; the man who caught it was named Zhang Wu—"Wu" for arms wide and the beast tamed.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: In the time of Han Emperor Xuan, Nan commandery captured a white tiger; the capturer was Zhang Wu—the name Wu meant arms spread and fierce submission.

entries.zh: 東昏侯亡德橫流，道歸拯亂，躬當翦戮，實啟太平，推閹竪之名字，亦天意也。
entries.en: The Marquess of Eastern Darkness poured out vice; the Way turned to save the age; his own body had to fall to open peace—even the eunuchs' names, read backward, show heaven's hand.
entries.literal: The Marquess of Eastern Darkness had virtue lost and wickedness overflowing; the Way returned to rescue chaos; he himself should be cut down and truly opened great peace—to infer from eunuchs' names is also Heaven's intent.

entries.zh: 東昏侯寶卷字智藏，高宗第二子也。
entries.en: The Marquess of Eastern Darkness, Xiao Baojuan, styled Zhizang, was the High Ancestor's second son.
entries.literal: Marquess of Eastern Darkness Baojuan, style Zhizang, was the second son of the High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 本名明賢，高宗輔政後改焉。
entries.en: He was first named Mingxian and took his new name after the High Ancestor began ruling as regent.
entries.literal: His original name was Mingxian; it was changed after the High Ancestor assumed the regency.

entries.zh: 建武元年，立為皇太子。
entries.en: Jianwu 1: he was installed as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, he was made crown prince.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷第八 本紀第八
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 8, Annals 8
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 8, Annals 8

entries.zh: 和帝諱寶融，字智昭，高宗第八子也。
entries.en: Emperor He was named Baorong, courtesy name Zhizhao; he was the eighth son of Emperor Gaozong.
entries.literal: Emperor He was named Baorong, courtesy name Zhizhao; he was the eighth son of Emperor Gaozong.

entries.zh: 建武元年，封隨郡王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Sui Commandery, with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Sui Commandery, with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 三年，為冠軍將軍，領石頭戍軍事。
entries.en: In the third year, he became General Who Vanquishes the Foe and took charge of military affairs at the Shitou garrison.
entries.literal: In the third year, he became General Who Vanquishes the Foe and took charge of military affairs at the Shitou garrison.

entries.zh: 永元元年，改封南康王，為持節、督荊雍益寧梁南北秦七州軍事、西中郎將、荊州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongyuan, his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Nankang, and he became Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin provinces, General of the Western Household, and governor of Jing Province.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan, his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Nankang, and he became Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, Southern Qin, and Northern Qin provinces, General of the Western Household, and governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 二年十一月甲寅，長史蕭穎冑殺輔國將軍、巴西梓潼二郡太守劉山陽，奉梁王舉義。
entries.en: On jiayin, in the eleventh month of the second year, Chief Clerk Xiao Yingzhou killed Liu Shanyang, General of the Household for All Purposes and governor of Baxi and Zitong commanderies, and raised arms in support of the Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: On jiayin, in the eleventh month of the second year, Chief Clerk Xiao Yingzhou killed Liu Shanyang, General of the Household for All Purposes and governor of Baxi and Zitong commanderies, and raised arms in support of the Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 乙卯，教纂嚴。
entries.en: On yimao, an edict ordered troops mustered.
entries.literal: On yimao, an edict ordered a general muster.

entries.zh: 又教曰：「吾躬率晉陽，翦此凶孽，戎事方勤，宜覃澤惠。
entries.en: Another edict said: "I am personally leading the host from Jinyang to cut down these criminals; with war at hand, mercy should be spread abroad.
entries.literal: Another edict said: "I am personally leading the host from Jinyang to cut down these criminals; with military affairs pressing, favors should be widely extended.

entries.zh: 所領內繫囚見徒，罪無輕重，殊死已下，皆原遣。
entries.en: All prisoners and convicts in our jurisdiction, whatever the crime, down to and including capital offenses, are pardoned and released.
entries.literal: All prisoners and convicts at labor within our jurisdiction, regardless of the gravity of the offense, from capital crimes downward, are pardoned and released.

entries.zh: 先有位署，卽復本職。
entries.en: Those who previously held office are restored to their former posts at once.
entries.literal: Those who previously held office shall at once resume their original posts.

entries.zh: 將吏轉一階。
entries.en: Officers and clerks advance one rank.
entries.literal: Officers and clerks are promoted one rank.

entries.zh: 從征身有家口停鎮，給廩食。
entries.en: For soldiers on campaign whose families remain in garrison posts, rations are provided.
entries.literal: For those on campaign whose families remain in garrison towns, grain rations are supplied.

entries.zh: 凡諸雜役見在諸軍帶甲之身，克定之後，悉免爲民。
entries.en: All miscellaneous laborers now serving in the armies in armor, once the realm is settled, are wholly freed to civilian status.
entries.literal: All miscellaneous laborers now serving in the armies in armor, once victory is secured, are wholly freed to become commoners.

entries.zh: 其功效賞報，別有科條。」
entries.en: Rewards for merit are set forth in separate regulations."
entries.literal: Rewards for merit and achievement are set forth in separate regulations."

entries.zh: 丙辰，以雍州刺史梁王爲使持節、都督前鋒諸軍事、左將軍。
