entries.en: On bingchen, the Prince of Liang, governor of Yong Province, was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard Armies, and General of the Left.
entries.literal: On bingchen, the Prince of Liang, Governor of Yong Province, was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard Armies, and General of the Left.

entries.zh: 丁巳，以蕭穎胄爲右將軍、都督行留諸軍事。
entries.en: On dingsi, Xiao Yingzhou was made General of the Right and commander of the rear and garrison forces.
entries.literal: On dingsi, Xiao Yinghou was made General of the Right and Commander-in-Chief of the Rear and Garrison Forces.

entries.zh: 戊午，梁王上表勸進。
entries.en: On wuwu, the Prince of Liang submitted a memorial urging advancement to the throne.
entries.literal: On wuwu, the Prince of Liang submitted a memorial urging [the throne] to advance.

entries.zh: 十二月乙亥，羣僚勸進，並不許。
entries.en: On yihai of the twelfth month, the assembled officials urged him to take the throne, but he refused each time.
entries.literal: On yihai of the twelfth month, the assembled officials urged advancement, but he refused each time.

entries.zh: 壬辰，驍騎將軍夏侯亶自京師至江陵，稱宣德太后令：「西中郎將南康王宜纂承皇祚，光臨億兆。
entries.en: On renchen, Swift-as-Steeds General Xiahou Dan arrived from the capital at Jiangling and announced an order of Empress Dowager Xuande: "The Western Palace Attendant, the Prince of Nankang, should succeed to the throne and rule the myriad people.
entries.literal: On renchen, the Swift-as-Steeds General Xiahou Dan arrived from the capital at Jiangling and announced an order of the Empress Dowager Xuande: "The Western Palace Attendant, the Prince of Nankang, should succeed to the imperial dignity and preside over the myriad people.

entries.zh: 方俟清宮，未卽大號，可且封宣城、南琅邪、南東海、東陽、臨海、新安、尋陽、南郡、竟陵、宜都十郡爲宣城王，相國、荊州牧，加黃皞，置僚屬，選百官，西中郎府南康國並如故。
entries.en: The palace must first be cleansed before he assumes the imperial title; for now he is enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng over ten commanderies—Xuancheng, Nanlangye, Nandonghai, Dongyang, Linhai, Xin'an, Xunyang, Nanjun, Jingling, and Yidu—made chancellor and governor of Jing Province, granted yellow imperial regalia, with a full staff and officials chosen; the Southern Palace and the state of Nankang remain as before.
entries.literal: We await the cleansing of the palace before assuming the great title; for the present he may be enfeoffed as Prince of Xuancheng over ten commanderies—Xuancheng, Nanlangye, Nandonghai, Dongyang, Linhai, Xin'an, Xunyang, Nanjun, Jingling, and Yidu—made Chancellor and Governor of Jing Province, granted yellow imperial regalia, with a full staff appointed and all officials chosen; the Southern Palace and the state of Nankang are to remain as before.

entries.zh: 須軍次近路，主者詳依舊典，法駕奉迎。」
entries.en: When the army draws near on the main road, the responsible offices are to follow the old precedents and escort him with the imperial equipage."
entries.literal: When the army approaches by the main road, the responsible offices are to follow the old precedents in detail and escort him with the imperial equipage."

entries.zh: 三年正月乙巳，王受命，大赦，唯梅蟲兒、茹法珍等不在赦例。
entries.en: On yisi of the first month of year 3, the Prince accepted the mandate; a general amnesty was proclaimed, excluding only Mei Chong'er, Ru Fazhen, and the like.
entries.literal: On yisi of the first month of the third year, the Prince accepted the mandate, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and only Mei Chong'er, Ru Fazhen, and the like were excluded from the pardon.

entries.zh: 右將軍蕭穎胄爲左長史，進號鎮軍將軍，梁王進號征東將軍。
entries.en: General of the Right Xiao Yingzhou was made left chief clerk and advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army; the Prince of Liang was advanced to General Who Subdues the East.
entries.literal: General of the Right Xiao Yinghou was made Left Chief Clerk and advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the Army; the Prince of Liang was advanced to General Who Subdues the East.

entries.zh: 甲戌，以冠軍將軍楊公則爲湘州刺史。
entries.en: On jiaxu, General Who Vanquishes the Foe Yang Gongze was made governor of Xiang Province.
entries.literal: On jiaxu, the General Who Vanquishes the Foe Yang Gongze was made Governor of Xiang Province.

entries.zh: 甲寅，建牙于城南。
entries.en: On jiayin, military banners were raised south of the city.
entries.literal: On jiayin, military banners were raised south of the city.

entries.zh: 二月乙丑，以冠軍長史王茂先爲江州刺史，冠軍將軍曹景宗爲郢州刺史，右將軍邵陵王寶攸爲荊州刺史。
entries.en: On yichou of the second month, Wang Maoxian, chief clerk to the General Who Vanquishes the Foe, was made governor of Jiang Province; General Who Vanquishes the Foe Cao Jingzong was made governor of Ying Province; and General of the Right the Prince of Shaoling, Bao You, was made governor of Jing Province.
entries.literal: On yichou of the second month, the Chief Clerk of the General Who Vanquishes the Foe, Wang Maoxian, was made Governor of Jiang Province; General Who Vanquishes the Foe Cao Jingzong was made Governor of Ying Province; and General of the Right the Prince of Shaoling, Bao You, was made Governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 己巳，羣僚上尊號，立宗廟及南北郊。
entries.en: On jisi, the assembled officials offered the honorific title, and the ancestral temple and the southern and northern suburban altars were established.
entries.literal: On jisi, the assembled officials offered the honorific title, and the ancestral temple and the southern and northern suburban altars were established.

entries.zh: 甲申，梁王率大衆屯沔口，郢州刺史張沖拒守。
entries.en: On jiashen, the Prince of Liang led the main army to camp at Hankou; Ying Province governor Zhang Chong held the city in resistance.
entries.literal: On jiashen, the Prince of Liang led the main host to camp at Hankou; the Governor of Ying Province, Zhang Chong, held the city in resistance.

entries.zh: 三月丁酉，張沖死，驃騎將軍薛元嗣等固城。
entries.en: On dingyou of the third month, Zhang Chong died; General of Agile Cavalry Xue Yuansi and others held the city fast.
entries.literal: On dingyou of the third month, Zhang Chong died; the General of Agile Cavalry Xue Yuansi and others held the city fast.

entries.zh: 中興元年春三月乙巳，即皇帝位，大赦，改元。
entries.en: In spring, on yisi of the third month of the first year of Zhongxing, he ascended the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.
entries.literal: In spring, on yisi of the third month of the first year of Zhongxing, he ascended the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name.

entries.zh: 文武賜位二等；鰥寡孤獨不能自存者穀，人五斛。
entries.en: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks; widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless who could not support themselves were given grain, five hu per person.
entries.literal: Civil and military officials were granted two ranks; widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless who could not support themselves were given grain, five hu per person.

entries.zh: 即永元三年也。
entries.en: This was the third year of Yongyuan.
entries.literal: This was the third year of Yongyuan.

entries.zh: 以相國左長史蕭穎冑為尚書令，晉安王寶義為司空，廬陵王寶源為車騎將軍、開府儀同三司，建安王寶寅為徐州刺史，散騎常侍夏侯詳為中領軍，領軍將軍蕭偉為雍州刺史。
entries.en: Xiao Yingzhou, left chief clerk to the Chancellor, was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Baoyi of Jin'an was made Minister of Works; Prince Baoyuan of Luling was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with a staff office equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies; Prince Baoyin of Jian'an was made governor of Xu Province; Palace Attendant Xiahou Xiang was made Commander of the Palace Guards; and General of the Palace Guards Xiao Wei was made governor of Yong Province.
entries.literal: Xiao Yingzhou, left chief clerk to the Chancellor, was made Director of the Masters of Writing; Prince Baoyi of Jin'an was made Minister of Works; Prince Baoyuan of Luling was made General of Chariots and Cavalry with a staff office equal in ceremony to the Three Excellencies; Prince Baoyin of Jian'an was made governor of Xu Province; Palace Attendant Xiahou Xiang was made Commander of the Palace Guards; and General of the Palace Guards Xiao Wei was made governor of Yong Province.

entries.zh: 丙午，有司奏封庶人寶卷為零陽侯，詔不許。
entries.en: On bingwu, the responsible offices memorialized to enfeoff the commoner Baojuan as Marquis of Lingyang; the edict did not permit it.
entries.literal: On bingwu, the responsible offices memorialized to enfeoff the commoner Baojuan as Marquis of Lingyang; the edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 又奏為涪陵王，詔可。
entries.en: They again memorialized to make him Prince of Fuling, and the edict approved.
entries.literal: They again memorialized to make him Prince of Fuling, and the edict approved.

entries.zh: 乙酉，尚書令蕭穎冑行荊州刺史，假梁王黃鉞。
entries.en: On yiyou, Director of the Masters of Writing Xiao Yingzhou was made acting governor of Jing Province, and the yellow axe was provisionally granted to the Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: On yiyou, Director of the Masters of Writing Xiao Yingzhou was made acting governor of Jing Province, and the yellow axe was provisionally granted to the Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 壬子，以征虜將軍柳惔為益、寧二州刺史。
entries.en: On renzi, General Who Subdues Caitiffs Liu Tan was made governor of Yi and Ning provinces.
entries.literal: On renzi, General Who Subdues Caitiffs Liu Tan was made governor of Yi and Ning provinces.

entries.zh: 己未，以冠軍將軍莊丘黑為梁、南秦二州刺史，冠軍將軍鄧元起為廣州刺史。
entries.en: On jiwei, General Who Vanquishes the Foe Zhuangqiu Hei was made governor of Liang and Southern Qin provinces, and General Who Vanquishes the Foe Deng Yuanqi was made governor of Guang Province.
entries.literal: On jiwei, General Who Vanquishes the Foe Zhuangqiu Hei was made governor of Liang and Southern Qin provinces, and General Who Vanquishes the Foe Deng Yuanqi was made governor of Guang Province.

entries.zh: 建元四年，高帝山陵，昭皇后應遷祔。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jianyuan the High Emperor's tomb was finished and Empress Zhao was due to be transferred for collateral enshrinement.
entries.literal: Jianyuan year 4: the High Emperor's imperial tomb was completed; Empress Zhao was to be moved for collateral enshrinement.

entries.zh: 祠部疑有祖祭及遣啟諸奠九飯之儀不？
entries.en: The Sacrificial Affairs bureau asked whether ancestral sacrifice was required, and whether the rites for dispatching the opening presentation, presentation offerings, and nine food servings applied.
entries.literal: The Sacrificial Affairs bureau questioned whether there should be ancestral sacrifice and the rites of dispatching the opening presentation, the various presentation offerings, and the nine servings of food.

entries.zh: 左僕射王儉議：「奠如大斂。
entries.en: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Presentation offerings should be handled like the greater encoffinment.
entries.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Presentation offerings should follow the model of the greater encoffinment.

entries.zh: 賀循云『從墓之墓皆設奠，如將葬廟朝之禮』。
entries.en: He Xun said "Whenever the grave is moved, offerings are set out, as when the coffin is about to be buried and the court pays temple audience."
entries.literal: He Xun said "When moving from tomb to tomb, presentation offerings are always set out, as with the rites of the temple audience before burial."

entries.zh: 范寧云『將窆而奠』。
entries.en: Fan Ning said "Offerings are made when the coffin is about to be interred."
entries.literal: Fan Ning said "Presentation offerings are made when the coffin is about to be lowered."

entries.zh: 雖不稱為祖，而不得無祭。」
entries.en: Even if one does not call it ancestral sacrifice, an offering cannot be omitted."
entries.literal: Though it is not called ancestral sacrifice, sacrifice cannot be omitted."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court accepted his view.
entries.literal: The court adopted it.

entries.zh: 祠部郎何佟之議曰：「春秋之旨，臣子繼君親，雖恩義有殊，而其禮則一，所以敦資敬之情，篤方喪之義。
entries.en: He Tongzhi argued: "The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that ministers and sons succeed lords and parents; obligations differ, but the rites are one—to deepen nourishing respect and firm the meaning of proper mourning.
entries.literal: He Tongzhi of the Directorate of Sacrifices argued: "The intent of the Spring and Autumn is that ministers and sons succeed lords and parents; though favor and obligation differ, the rites are one—thereby to deepen the feeling of nourishing respect and make firm the meaning of square mourning.

entries.zh: 主上雖仰嗣高皇，嘗經北面，方今聖曆御宇，垂訓無窮，在三之恩，理不容替。
entries.en: Though the sovereign succeeded Gaohuang and once faced north to him, the sage reign now governs without end—the threefold obligation cannot be set aside.
entries.literal: Though the sovereign succeeded Gaohuang and once faced north to him, now the sage reign governs the realm and his teachings are endless—the threefold obligation cannot, in principle, be set aside.

entries.zh: 竊謂世
entries.en: I hold that for the dynastic founder's
entries.literal: I submit privately that the dynastic

entries.en: Zong
entries.literal: (Received text: zu; emended to zong.)

entries.zh: 宗祥忌，至尊宜弔服升殿，羣臣同致哀感，事畢，百官詣宣德宮拜表，仍致哀陵園，以弘追遠之慕。」
entries.en: For Shizong, on xiang taboo days the sovereign should wear condolence dress and ascend the hall; ministers should share his grief; when the rite ends, officials should go to Xuande Palace to present a memorial and still mourn at the imperial tomb—to deepen the longing for those long gone."
entries.literal: For the dynastic founder Zong, on xiang taboo days the sovereign should wear condolence dress and ascend the hall; ministers should share his grief; when the rite ends, officials should go to Xuande Palace to present a memorial and still mourn at the imperial tomb—to deepen the longing for those long gone."

entries.zh: 尚書令王晏等十九人同佟之議。
entries.en: Wang Yan, director of the Masters of Writing, and nineteen colleagues sided with He Tongzhi.
entries.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yan and nineteen others alike agreed with Tongzhi's deliberation.

entries.zh: 詔「可」。
entries.en: The edict read: "Approved."
entries.literal: An edict said "Approved."

entries.zh: 有司又奏：「昭皇后神主在廟，今遷祔葬，
entries.en: The relevant offices submitted again: "Empress Zhao's spirit tablet is already in the temple; for the transfer and collateral enshrinement burial,
entries.literal: The relevant offices memorialized again: "The spirit tablet of Empress Zhao is in the temple; now, for the move and collateral enshrinement burial,

entries.en: Collation note: the text supplies the character 廣 here.
entries.literal: Collation note: the character 廣 is supplied here.

entries.zh: 廟有虞以安神，神既已處廟，改葬出靈，豈應虞祭？
entries.en: At the temple the yu rite settles the spirit. The spirit is already in the temple; if one reinterrs and removes the soul-seat, should there still be a yu sacrifice?
entries.literal: At the temple the yu rite settles the spirit. The spirit is already in the temple; if one reinterrs and removes the soul-seat, should there still be a yu sacrifice?

entries.zh: 鄭注改葬云『從廟之廟，禮宜同從墓之墓』。
entries.en: Zheng Xuan's note on reburial says "Moving from temple to temple should follow the same rule as moving from grave to grave."
entries.literal: Zheng's commentary on reburial says "When moving from temple to temple, ritual propriety should match moving from tomb to tomb."

entries.zh: 事何容異！
entries.en: How could the cases differ!
entries.literal: How could the affair be treated differently!

entries.zh: 前代謂應無虞。」
entries.en: Earlier practice held that no yu rite was required."
entries.literal: Earlier ages held that there should be no yu rite."

entries.zh: 左僕射王儉議：「范寧云『葬必有魂車』。
entries.en: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Fan Ning said "Every burial requires a soul cart."
entries.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Fan Ning said "Burial must have a soul cart."

entries.zh: 若不為其歸，神將安舍？
entries.en: If you do not receive it home, where will the spirit rest?
entries.literal: If one does not provide for its return, where will the spirit lodge?

entries.zh: 世中改葬，即墓所施靈設祭，何得不祭而毀耶？
entries.en: When graves are moved in our time, a soul-seat is installed at the tomb and offerings are made—how can one destroy the seat without sacrificing?
entries.literal: In this age, when graves are moved, a soul-seat is set up at the tomb and sacrifices are performed—how can one offer no sacrifice and yet destroy the seat?

entries.zh: 賀循云『既窆，設奠於墓，以終其事』。
entries.en: He Xun said "After interment, set offerings at the grave to finish the rite."
entries.literal: He Xun said "Once the coffin is lowered, set presentation offerings at the grave to complete the affair."

entries.zh: 雖非正虞，亦粗相似。
entries.en: It is not a full yu rite, but it is close enough.
entries.literal: Though it is not a proper yu rite, it is roughly similar.

entries.zh: 晉氏脩復五陵，宋朝敬后改葬，皆有虞。
entries.en: Jin's restoration of the five imperial tombs and Song's reburial of Empress Jing both included yu rites.
entries.literal: When Jin restored the five imperial tombs, and when Song reinterred Empress Jing, both had yu rites.

entries.zh: 今設虞非疑。」
entries.en: There is no question that a yu rite should be held now."
entries.literal: To set up a yu rite now is not in doubt."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court accepted his view.
entries.literal: The court adopted it.

entries.zh: 建元二年，皇太子妃薨，前宮臣疑所服。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianyuan the crown prince's consort died, and former palace staff disputed the mourning they should wear.
entries.literal: Jianyuan year 2: the crown prince's consort died; former palace officers questioned what mourning garb to wear.

entries.zh: 左僕射王儉議：「禮記文王世子『父在斯為子，君在斯為臣』。
entries.en: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "The Book of Rites, King Wen as Crown Prince, says "While the father lives you are a son; while the ruler lives you are a subject."
entries.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "The Book of Rites, King Wen as Crown Prince, says "While the father lives one is a son; while the lord lives one is a subject."

entries.zh: 且漢魏以來，宮僚充備，臣隸之節，具體在三。
entries.en: From Han and Wei on, palace offices have been fully staffed; the duties of subject and servant are complete in every bond.
entries.literal: Moreover, from Han and Wei onward palace staff have been fully appointed; the protocol of subject and servant is complete in all three bonds.

entries.zh: 昔庾翼妻喪，王允、滕弘謂府吏宜有小君之服，況臣節之重邪？
entries.en: When Yu Yi's wife died, Wang Yun and Teng Hong said prefectural clerks should mourn the master's wife; how much more when the bond of subjecthood is in question?
entries.literal: When Yu Yi's wife died, Wang Yun and Teng Hong held that prefectural clerks should wear mourning for the lesser lady—how much more when the weight of subjecthood is at stake?

entries.zh: 宜依禮為舊君妻齊衰三月，居官之身，竝合屬假，朝晡臨哭，悉繫東宮。
entries.en: They should observe three months' second-degree mourning for a former lord's wife. All who hold office should receive leave, wail morning and evening at the Eastern Palace, and remain attached to that quarter.
entries.literal: They should follow ritual and wear three months' second-degree mourning for a former lord's wife; those in office should all be granted leave, attend morning and evening wailing at the Eastern Palace, and keep to that quarter entirely.

entries.zh: 今臣之未從官在遠者，於居官之所，屬寧二日半，仍行喪成服，遣牋表，不得奔赴。」
entries.en: Officers not yet in post who are distant should, at their place of service, take two and a half days' leave for rest, then complete mourning dress, send a memorial, and not travel to attend in person."
entries.literal: As for officers not yet in post who are far away, at the place where they hold office they should observe two and a half days of leave for rest, then complete the mourning garb, send a written report, and not rush to attend in person."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court accepted his view.
entries.literal: The court adopted it.

entries.zh: 太子妃斬草乘黃，議建銘旌。
entries.en: When the crown prince's consort cut the mourning staff and took the yellow carriage, officials debated whether to raise the name pennant.
entries.literal: When the crown prince's consort cut the mourning staff and rode the yellow carriage, there was debate over erecting the name pennant.

entries.zh: 僕射王儉議：「禮，既塗棺，祝取銘置于殯東，大斂畢，便應建于西階之東。」
entries.en: Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Ritual requires that once the coffin is sealed, the invoker places the inscription east of the bier; when the greater encoffinment is finished, the pennant should be raised east of the western steps."
entries.literal: Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Ritual says: once the coffin is coated, the invoker takes the inscription and places it east of the bier; when the greater encoffinment is complete, it should at once be set up east of the western steps."

entries.zh: 宋大明二年，太子妃薨，建九旒。
entries.en: In Song Daming 2, when a crown prince's consort died, a nine-tassel canopy was used.
entries.literal: In Song, Daming year 2, when a crown prince's consort died, nine tassels were erected.

entries.zh: 有司又議：「斬草日建旒與不？
entries.en: The relevant offices debated again: "On the day the mourning staff is cut, should tassels be erected?
entries.literal: The relevant offices debated again: "On the day of cutting the mourning staff, should tassels be erected or not?

entries.zh: 若建旒，應幾旒？
entries.en: If they are, how many tassels?
entries.literal: If tassels are erected, how many tassels should there be?

entries.zh: 及畫龍升降云何？
entries.en: And how should the painted dragon rise and fall?
entries.literal: And how should the painted dragon ascend and descend?

entries.zh: 又用幾翣？」
entries.en: And how many feather screens?"
entries.literal: And how many feather screens should be used?"

entries.zh: 僕射王儉議：「旒本是命服，無關於凶事，今公卿以下，平存不能備禮，故在凶乃建耳。
entries.en: Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Tassels belong to insignia of rank, not to mourning; today even the highest ministers cannot keep full ritual in normal times, so tassels are raised only in mourning.
entries.literal: Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Tassels are originally insignia of conferred rank and have no bearing on inauspicious affairs; today, from the highest ministers down, in ordinary times they cannot fully observe ritual, so only in mourning are tassels erected.

entries.zh: 東宮秩同上公九命之儀，妃與儲君一體，義不容異，無緣未同常例，別立凶旒。
entries.en: The Eastern Palace ranks with a lord of ninefold dignity, like the Three Dukes; consort and heir are one—by right they cannot differ. There is no ground to break from ordinary usage and invent a special mourning tassel.
entries.literal: The Eastern Palace's rank follows the nine-rank protocol of a lord equal to the Three Dukes; the consort and the heir are one body—in principle they cannot differ. There is no reason to depart from the usual rule and set up a separate mourning tassel.

entries.zh: 大明舊事，是不經詳議，率爾便行耳。
entries.en: The Daming precedent was never fully debated; it was done in haste.
entries.literal: The Daming precedent was not the product of careful deliberation; it was carried out hastily.

entries.zh: 今宜考以禮典，不得効尤從失。
entries.en: The canon should govern now, not a faulty precedent copied again.
entries.literal: Now one should consult the ritual canon and not follow a bad example into error.

entries.zh: 吉部伍自有桁輅，凶部別有銘旌，若復立旒，復置何處？
entries.en: The auspicious procession already has its framed carriage; the mourning train has its name pennant—if tassels are added, where would they go?
entries.literal: The auspicious train already has its framed carriage; the mourning train has its own name pennant—if tassels are erected again, where would they be placed?

entries.zh: 翣自用八。」
entries.en: Use eight feather screens."
entries.literal: Eight feather screens should be used."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court accepted his view.
entries.literal: The court adopted it.

entries.zh: 有司奏：「穆妃卒哭後，靈還在道，遇朔望，當須設祭不？」
entries.en: The relevant offices submitted: "After Consort Mu completed the end of wailing, the spirit journey was still underway; should new- and full-moon offerings be held?"
entries.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "After Consort Mu's zui ku, the spirit-seat was still on the road; on new- and full-moon days, should offerings be set out or not?"

entries.zh: 王儉議：「既虞卒哭，祭之於廟，本是祭序昭穆耳，未全同卒吉四時之祭也，所以有朔望殷事。
entries.en: Wang Jian replied: "After yu and zui ku, temple sacrifice only sets zhao-mu order; it is not the same as the four seasonal rites after mourning ends—hence the elaborate new- and full-moon observances.
entries.literal: Wang Jian argued: "After the yu and zui ku, sacrifice in the ancestral temple is only fixing the order of zhao and mu; it is not wholly the same as the four seasonal sacrifices when mourning is fully ended, which is why there are elaborate new- and full-moon rites.

entries.zh: 蕃國不行權制，宋江夏王妃卒哭以後，朔望設祭。
entries.en: Feudal kingdoms did not follow the crown's expedients; in Song, the Jiangxia princess continued new- and full-moon offerings after zui ku.
entries.literal: Feudatory states do not follow expedient regulations; under Song, after the Princess of Jiangxia finished zui ku, they set out offerings on new and full moon.

entries.zh: 帝室既以卒哭除喪，無緣方有朔望之祭。
entries.en: The imperial line ends mourning at zui ku; there is no ground for new- and full-moon rites afterward.
entries.literal: The imperial house, having removed mourning at zui ku, has no reason then to hold new- and full-moon sacrifice.

entries.zh: 靈筵雖未升廟堂，而舫中即成行廟，猶如桓玄及宋高祖長沙、臨川二國，竝有移廟之禮。
entries.en: Though the spirit-seat had not reached the temple, the barge itself served as a traveling shrine—as with Huan Xuan and, under Song Gaozu, the Changsha and Linchuan domains, which all observed temple-transfer rites.
entries.literal: Though the spirit-seat had not yet ascended to the temple hall, on the boat it already formed a traveling temple, as when Huan Xuan and under Song Gaozu the states of Changsha and Linchuan both had the rite of moving the temple.

entries.zh: 豈復謂靈筵在途，便設殷事耶？
entries.en: Surely one does not hold elaborate new- and full-moon rites merely because the spirit-seat is still en route?
entries.literal: How could one say that because the spirit-seat is on the road, one should set up elaborate rites?

entries.zh: 推此而言，朔望不復俟祭。
entries.en: On that reasoning, new- and full-moon offerings need not be observed.
entries.literal: Pushing this reasoning further, one need not wait for new and full moon to sacrifice.

entries.zh: 宋懿后時舊事不及此，益可知時議。」
entries.en: Under Song's Empress Yi the old precedent did not go so far, which shows what contemporaries thought."
entries.literal: Former practice under Empress Yi of Song did not reach this point, which further shows the opinion of the time."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court accepted his view.
entries.literal: The court adopted it.

entries.zh: 建元三年，有司奏：「皇太子穆妃以去年七月薨，其年閏九月。
entries.en: In the third year of Jianyuan the relevant offices submitted: "Crown Prince Consort Mu died last July; the year also had an intercalary ninth month.
entries.literal: Jianyuan year 3, the relevant offices memorialized: "The crown prince's Consort Mu died last seventh month; that year had an intercalary ninth month.

entries.zh: 未審當月數閏？
entries.en: Should the intercalary month count toward the month tally?
entries.literal: Should the intercalary month be counted in the month-tally?

entries.zh: 為應以閏附正月？
entries.en: Or should it be folded into the first month?
entries.literal: Or should the intercalary be attached to the first month?

entries.zh: 若用月數數閏者，南郡王兄弟便應以此四月晦小祥，至於祥月，不為有疑不？」
entries.en: If months are counted and the intercalary is included, the Nanjun princes should hold xiaoxiang on the last day of the fourth month—would that leave the xiang month in doubt?"
entries.literal: If one counts months and counts the intercalary, the Prince of Nanjun's brothers should observe xiaoxiang on the last day of this fourth month; as for the month of xiang—is there any doubt?"

entries.zh: 左僕射王儉議：「三百六旬，尚書明義，文公納幣，春秋致譏。
entries.en: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Three hundred and sixty days—the Documents state it plainly; Duke Wen's betrothal gifts drew the Spring and Autumn Annals' rebuke.
entries.literal: Left Vice Director Wang Jian argued: "Three hundred and sixty days—the Documents make the meaning plain; Duke Wen's betrothal gifts drew the Spring and Autumn Annals' rebuke.

entries.zh: 穀梁云『積分而成月』。
entries.en: Guliang said: "Months form from accumulated fractional days."
entries.literal: Guliang said "Months are formed by accumulated fractions."

entries.zh: 公羊云『天無是月』。
entries.en: Gongyang said: "Heaven has no intercalary month as such."
entries.literal: Gongyang said "Heaven has no such month."

entries.zh: 雖然，左氏謂告朔為得禮。
entries.en: Still, the Zuo tradition treats announcing the new moon as ritually correct.
entries.literal: Nevertheless, Zuoshi holds that announcing the new moon is proper ritual.

entries.zh: 是故先儒咸謂三年朞喪，歲數沒閏，大功以下，月數數閏。
entries.en: Early Ru thus held: three-year term mourning counts by years and absorbs the intercalary; for lesser grades, count months and include the intercalary.
entries.literal: Therefore the early Ru all say that for the three-year term mourning, years absorb the intercalary month, while for lesser grades one counts months and counts the intercalary.

entries.zh: 夫閏者，蓋是年之餘日，而月之異朔，所以吳商云『含閏以正朞，允協情理』。
entries.en: An intercalary month is surplus days in a year and an extra reckoning in the month; Wu Shang said: "Wrap the intercalary into the term—that best fits reason."
entries.literal: Intercalary, in general, is the year's surplus days and the month's variant new moon; hence Wu Shang said "Include the intercalary to correct the term—it truly fits reason."

entries.zh: 今杖朞之喪，雖以十〔一〕月而小祥，至於祥縞，必須周歲。
entries.en: For staff-and-one-year mourning, xiaoxiang may fall in the eleventh month, but xiang and hemp mourning require a full cycle of the year.
entries.literal: For staff-and-term mourning today, though xiaoxiang comes in the eleventh month (received text: ten [one]), for xiang and hemp mourning a full year is required.

entries.zh: 凡厭屈之禮，要取象正服。
entries.en: Compressed mourning mirrors the normal garment stages.
entries.literal: In all compressed mourning rites, the key is to mirror the normal garment stages.

entries.zh: 祥縞相去二月，厭降小祥，亦以則之。
entries.en: Xiang and hemp are two months apart; compressed xiaoxiang follows that spacing.
entries.literal: Xiang and hemp mourning are two months apart; compressing xiaoxiang follows the same rule.

entries.zh: 又且求之名義，則小祥本以年限，考於倫例，則相去必應二朔。
entries.en: By name, xiaoxiang is reckoned by years; by parallel cases, two new moons must separate the stages.
entries.literal: Moreover, by its name and meaning xiaoxiang is fundamentally by yearly limit; checked against parallel cases, the interval must be two new moons.

entries.zh: 今以厭屈而先祥，不得謂此事之非朞，事既同條，情無異貫，沒閏之理，固在言先。
entries.en: Compression moves xiang earlier, but the case is still term mourning under the same rule and feeling; absorbing the intercalary was already argued.
entries.literal: Now, because mourning is compressed the xiang comes early; one cannot say this is not term mourning—the matter falls under the same rubric, the feeling is not different in kind, and the logic of absorbing the intercalary is already stated above.

entries.zh: 設令祥在此晦，則去縞三月，依附准例，益復為礙。
entries.en: If xiang fell on this month's last day, hemp would be only three months away—again at odds with precedent.
entries.literal: Suppose xiang fell on this month's last day; then only three months to hemp—by precedent that would again be obstructed.

entries.zh: 謂應須五月晦乃祥。
entries.en: Xiang should fall on the last day of the fifth month.
entries.literal: They held that xiang should be on the last day of the fifth month.

entries.zh: 此國之大典，宜共精詳。
entries.en: This is a state ritual of the first order and deserves joint, careful review.
entries.literal: This is a great statute of the state and should be examined together in detail.

entries.zh: 並通關八座丞郎，研盡同異。」
entries.en: Circulate it to the Eight Seats, aides, and directors to settle every point of agreement and difference."
entries.literal: It should be circulated to the Eight Seats, aides, and directors for thorough study of agreement and difference."

entries.zh: 皇太子穆妃服，尚書左丞兼著作郎王逡問左僕射王儉：「中軍南郡王小祥，應待聞喜不？
entries.en: During mourning for the crown prince's Consort Mu, Wang Xun—left director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent director of composition—asked Vice Director Wang Jian: "For the Central Army prince of Nan Commandery, should minor felicity wait on Wenxi?
entries.literal: For mourning the crown prince's Consort Mu, Left Director of the Masters of Writing and concurrent Director of Composition Wang Xun asked Left Vice Director Wang Jian: "The Central Army, the Prince of Nan Commandery—on minor felicity, should he wait for Wenxi or not?

entries.zh: 穆妃七月二十四日薨，聞喜公八月發哀，計十一月之限，應在六月。
entries.en: Consort Mu died on the twenty-fourth of the seventh month; the duke of Wenxi began mourning in the eighth; by an eleven-month count, minor felicity should land in the sixth month.
entries.literal: Consort Mu died on the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month; the Duke of Wenxi began mourning in the eighth month; reckoning the eleventh-month limit, it should fall in the sixth month.

entries.zh: 南郡王為當同取六月，則大祥復申一月，應用八月，非復正月，在存親之義，若各自為祥，廬堊相閒，玄素雜糅，未審當有此疑不？」
entries.en: If the prince of Nan were to share the sixth month, major felicity would slip another month to the eighth—not back to the first month; and if each brother kept his own felicity schedule, thatched mourning huts and whitewashed walls would alternate, black and white interleaved—is that really in doubt?"
entries.literal: If the Prince of Nan Commandery is to take the same sixth month, then major felicity would again be extended one month and should fall in the eighth—not the first month again; in the meaning of cherishing kin, if each observes felicity on his own, thatched huts and plastered walls would alternate, black and white mixed together—has there ever been such a doubt?"

entries.zh: 儉曰：「送往有已，復生有節，罔極非服制所申，祥縞明示終之斷。
entries.en: Jian replied: "The dead are sent off to their limit; the living return on fixed seasons. Boundless grief is not what the garment code is for—xiang and hemp mark where mourning ends.
entries.literal: Jian said: "Sending off the dead has its end; returning to life has its seasons; boundless grief is not what garment rules express—xiang and hemp mark the clear break of finality.

entries.zh: 相待之義，經記無聞。
entries.en: The classics and commentaries nowhere speak of waiting for one another.
entries.literal: The meaning of waiting for one another is nowhere heard in the classics and records.

entries.zh: 世人多以廬室衰麻，不宜有異，故相去一二月者，或申以俱除。
entries.en: Most people think thatched huts and hemp dress ought not to differ, so when dates fall a month or two apart they sometimes stretch the schedule to end mourning together.
entries.literal: People mostly hold that thatched rooms and hemp garments should not differ, so when dates fall one or two months apart they sometimes extend so as to remove mourning together.

entries.zh: 此所謂任情徑行，未達禮旨。
entries.en: That is indulging private feeling, not grasping what ritual intends.
entries.literal: This is what is called following feeling and going straight—not reaching the aim of ritual.

entries.zh: 昔撰喪記，已嘗言之。
entries.en: I said as much when I compiled the Mourning Record.
entries.literal: When I compiled the Mourning Record, I already spoke of this.

entries.zh: 遠還之人，自有為而未祭，在家之子，立何辭以不變？
entries.en: A man returning from afar may still owe rites he has not performed; a son at home—what excuse has he to keep old garments unchanged?
entries.literal: One who returns from afar may have duties yet unperformed in sacrifice; a son at home—on what grounds would he refuse to change garments?

entries.zh: 禮有除喪而歸者，此則經記之遺文，不待之明據。
entries.en: The rites allow removing mourning garments on return—that is a surviving line in the classics, not something needing explicit proof.
entries.literal: Ritual has one who removes mourning and returns home—this is a surviving line in the classics and records, not something that awaits clear proof.

entries.zh: 假使應待，則相去彌年，亦宜必待，乃為衰絰永服以窮生，吉蠲長絕於宗廟，斯不可矣。
entries.en: If waiting were required, even a year's gap would demand waiting—then one would wear hemp to the grave and cut off sacrifice at the ancestral temple forever; that is impossible.
entries.literal: If one should wait, then even when separated by a full year one ought still to wait—then hemp would be worn to the end of life and auspicious purification long cut off from the ancestral temple; that cannot be.

entries.zh: 苟曰非宜，則旬月之閒，亦不容申。
entries.en: If it is wrong in principle, it is wrong whether the gap is ten days or ten months.
entries.literal: If it is said to be improper, then within the space of ten days or a month it also cannot be extended.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 禮有倫序，義無徒設。
entries.en: Ritual has its order; meaning is never set up for nothing.
entries.literal: Ritual has order and sequence; the meaning does not stand alone without purpose.

entries.zh: 今遠則不待，近必相須，禮例既乖，即心無取。
entries.en: Today the distant mourner need not wait, yet the near must—precedent is already twisted, and the heart will not follow.
entries.literal: Now the distant does not wait, yet the near must depend on one another—ritual precedent is already at odds, and the heart cannot accept it.

entries.zh: 若疑兄弟同居，吉凶舛雜，則古有異宮之義。
entries.en: If the worry is brothers under one roof with joy and mourning tangled, antiquity allowed separate households.
entries.literal: If the doubt is brothers dwelling together with auspicious and inauspicious mixed, antiquity had the principle of separate residences.

entries.zh: 設無異宮，則遠還之子，自應開立別門，以終喪事。
entries.en: Without separate residences, the son back from afar should set up his own gate and finish mourning apart.
entries.literal: If there is no separate residence, then the son returning from afar should himself open a separate gate and finish mourning there.

entries.zh: 靈筵祭奠，隨在家之人，再朞而毀。
entries.en: The spirit mat and offerings stay with whoever remains at home and are dismantled after two mourning periods.
entries.literal: Spirit mats and offerings follow whoever is at home; after two periods they are destroyed.

entries.zh: 所以然者，奔喪禮云『為位不奠』，鄭玄云『以其精神不存乎此也』。
entries.en: Rush-mourning rites say: "One sets a place but does not offer"—Zheng Xuan: "Because the spirit is not present there."
entries.literal: The reason is that Rites for Rush Mourning says "Setting a place but not offering", and Zheng Xuan says "Because the spirit is not present here."

entries.zh: 聞哀不時，寔緣在遠。
entries.en: Hearing the news out of season is simply because one was far away.
entries.literal: Hearing of the bereavement not in season truly comes from being far away.

entries.zh: 為位不奠，益有可安。
entries.en: Setting a place without offering is all the more reason to be at ease about it.
entries.literal: Setting a place but not offering—all the more may one be at ease.

entries.zh: 此自有為而然，不關嫡庶。
entries.en: That follows from one's own obligations; it has nothing to do with primary wife or concubine.
entries.literal: This follows from having duties of one's own; it does not concern primary wife and concubine.

entries.zh: 庶子在家，亦不待嫡矣。
entries.en: A secondary son at home does not wait on the heir either.
entries.literal: A secondary son at home also does not wait for the primary heir.

entries.zh: 而況儲妃正體王室，中軍長嫡之重，天朝又行權制，進退彌復非疑。
entries.en: How much more when the crown prince's consort is the orthodox wife of the house, the Central Army heir is the eldest son, and the court itself applies expedient mourning—there is no real doubt left.
entries.literal: How much more the crown prince's consort as the orthodox body of the royal house, the weight of the Central Army heir as eldest son, and the court moreover applying expedient rules—going forward or back is doubly beyond doubt.

entries.zh: 謂不應相待。
entries.en: They should not wait on one another.
entries.literal: I hold that they should not wait for one another.

entries.zh: 中軍祥縞之日，聞喜致哀而已，不受弔慰。
entries.en: On the Central Army prince's xiang-and-hemp day, Wenxi begins mourning only—he does not receive callers.
entries.literal: On the Central Army's day of xiang and hemp, Wenxi only begins mourning; he does not receive condolence visits.

entries.zh: 及至忌辰變除，昆弟亦宜相就寫情而不對客。
entries.en: When the death anniversary comes and garments change, brothers may visit each other privately but should not receive guests.
entries.literal: When the anniversary of death arrives and garments change, brothers too should visit one another to pour out feeling but not receive guests.

entries.zh: 此國之大典，宜通關八座丞郎，共盡同異，然後奏御。」
entries.en: This is a great statute of the realm; it should go to the eight excellencies and all directors and aides for full debate, then be memorialized."
entries.literal: This is a great statute of the state; it should be circulated to the eight excellencies and directors and aides to exhaust agreement and difference, then〔afterward〕 present to the throne."

entries.zh: 司徒褚淵等二十人竝同儉議為允，請以為永制。
entries.en: Minister of Works Chu Yuan and twenty colleagues endorsed Jian's view and asked that it be fixed as permanent rule.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Chu Yuan and twenty others together agreed with Jian's proposal as fitting and asked that it be made permanent regulation.

entries.zh: 詔「可」。
entries.en: The edict read: "Approved."
entries.literal: An edict said "Approved."

entries.zh: 尚書令褚淵難儉議曰：「厭屈之典，由所尊奪情，故祥縞備制，而年月不申。
entries.en: Director Chu Yuan objected to Jian: "Compressed mourning exists because respect for the honored curtails grief, so xiang and hemp keep full form while years and months are not fully expressed.
entries.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Chu Yuan objected to Jian's argument: "The statute of compressed mourning exists because respect for the honored curtails grief, so xiang and hemp keep full form while years and months are not fully expressed.

entries.zh: 今以十一月而祥，從朞可知。
entries.en: Holding xiang in the eleventh month already shows term reckoning.
entries.literal: Now to hold xiang in the eleventh month shows it follows the term.

entries.zh: 既計以月數，則應數閏以成典。
entries.en: If reckoning is by months, the intercalary should be counted to complete the rule.
entries.literal: Since one reckons by months, one should count the intercalary to complete the statute.

entries.zh: 若猶含之，何以異於縞制。
entries.en: If the intercalary is still absorbed, how is that different from hemp mourning?
entries.literal: If one still absorbs it, how does that differ from the hemp-mourning rule?

entries.zh: 疑者正以祥之當閏，月數相縣。
entries.en: The doubt is precisely that xiang should coincide with an intercalary month while month-counts stand apart.
entries.literal: Doubters precisely because xiang should fall in an intercalary month, and month-counts are far apart.

entries.zh: 積分餘閏，曆象所弘。
entries.en: Fractional days and surplus intercalary are what calendrical science upholds.
entries.literal: Accumulating fractional days and surplus intercalary is what the calendar promotes.

entries.zh: 計月者數閏，故有餘月，計年者苞含，故致盈積。
entries.en: Month-reckoning counts the intercalary and leaves extra months; year-reckoning encompasses and yields surplus.
entries.literal: Those who count months count the intercalary, hence leftover months; those who count years encompass, hence surplus accumulation.

entries.zh: 稱理從制，有何不可？」
entries.en: If reason and statute align, what objection remains?"
entries.literal: To follow statute as reason dictates—what could be wrong?"

entries.zh: 儉又荅淵難曰：「含閏之義，通儒所難。
entries.en: Jian answered Yuan again: "The meaning of including the intercalary—even leading Ru find it hard.
entries.literal: Jian again answered Yuan's objection: "The meaning of including the intercalary—even comprehensive Ru find it hard.

entries.zh: 但祥本應朞，屈而不遂。
entries.en: Xiang should come at term's end but was bent short.
entries.literal: Yet xiang originally should fall at the term and was bent short of completion.

entries.zh: 語事則名體具存，論哀則情無以異。
entries.en: In form the names and stages remain; in grief the feeling is unchanged.
entries.literal: In speaking of the matter, names and forms are fully preserved; in speaking of grief, feeling is not different.

entries.zh: 迹雖數月，義實計年，閏是年之歸餘，故宜總而苞之。
entries.en: The calendar shows months, but the meaning is years; the intercalary is the year's remainder and should be wrapped into the whole.
entries.literal: The trace is months, but the meaning is truly years; the intercalary is the year's remainder and should be gathered and encompassed.

entries.zh: 朞而兩祥，緣尊故屈，祥則沒閏，象年所申，屈申兼著，二途具舉。
entries.en: One term, two xiang: respect compresses; at xiang the intercalary is absorbed to express the year—compression and full expression both appear, both paths named.
entries.literal: Term and two xiang—because of respect, compression; at xiang, absorb intercalary, expressing the year—compression and expression both shown, both paths set forth.

entries.zh: 經記之旨，其在茲乎！
entries.en: Is this not the thrust of the classics?
entries.literal: The point of the classics and records—is it not here!

entries.zh: 如使五月小祥，六月乃閏，則祥之去縞，事成二月，是為十一月以象前朞，二朔以放後歲，名有區域，不得相參。
entries.en: If xiaoxiang fell in the fifth month and the sixth were intercalary, only two months would remain to hemp—making the eleventh month stand for the prior term and two new moons discharge the later year; the categories differ and cannot be combined.
entries.literal: If xiaoxiang came in the fifth month and the sixth were intercalary, then from xiang to hemp would be only two months—that would use the eleventh month to mirror the prior term and two new moons to discharge the later year; names have separate domains and cannot be mixed.

entries.zh: 魯襄二十八年『十二月乙未，楚子卒』。
entries.en: Lu Xiang year 28: "In the twelfth month, on yiwei, the Chu ruler died."
entries.literal: Lu Xiang year 28: "Twelfth month, day yiwei, the Chu ruler died."

entries.zh: 唯書上月，初不言閏，此又附上之明義也。
entries.en: It names only the recorded month and never the intercalary—a clear rule for how the upper month is written.
entries.literal: It records only the upper month and at first does not speak of intercalary—this again is clear meaning attached to the upper month.

entries.zh: 鄭、射、王、賀唯云朞則沒閏，初不復區別杖朞之中祥，將謂不俟言矣。
entries.en: Zheng, She, Wang, and He said only that term mourning absorbs the intercalary; they did not separate xiang within staff-and-term mourning—that surely needs no argument.
entries.literal: Zheng, She, Wang, and He only said that at the term one absorbs the intercalary; they did not further distinguish xiang within staff-term mourning—one may suppose it goes without saying.

entries.zh: 成休甫云『大祥後禫，有閏別數之』。
entries.en: Cheng Xiufu said: "After great xiang, yong and the offering rites count the intercalary separately."
entries.literal: Cheng Xiufu said "After da xiang, yong and sacrificial service—if there is intercalary, count it separately."

entries.zh: 明杖朞之祥，不得方於綅縞之末。
entries.en: The minor felicity of staff-period mourning cannot be measured against the tail of coarse hemp and sackcloth.
entries.literal: The clear xiang of staff-period mourning cannot be equated with the end of sackcloth-and-hemp.

entries.zh: 即恩如彼，就例如此。」
entries.en: If favor worked that way, precedent should work the same."
entries.literal: As the grace there was such, so by precedent it is thus."

entries.zh: 淵又據舊義難儉十餘問，儉隨事解釋。
entries.en: Chu Yuan pressed on with a dozen more objections drawn from older commentators; Jian rebutted each in turn.
entries.literal: Yuan again raised more than ten objections from old interpretations against Jian; Jian answered each point as it arose.

entries.zh: 祠部郎中王珪之議，謂「喪以閏施，功衰以下小祥值閏，則略而不言。
entries.en: Wang Guizhi of the sacrifices bureau argued: "Where mourning reckons leap months, for merit-mourning and lower grades a leap-month minor felicity is simply not named.
entries.literal: Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices Wang Guizhi memorialized, saying "When mourning is calculated with leap months, for merit-mourning and below, if minor felicity falls in a leap month it is passed over in silence.

entries.zh: 今雖厭屈，祥名猶存，異於餘服。
entries.en: Even when mourning is compressed, the term xiang still stands—unlike other grades of dress.
entries.literal: Now though compressed〔abbreviated〕, the name of xiang still remains, differing from other garments.

entries.zh: 計月為數，屈追慕之心，以遠為邇。
entries.en: To count by months is to shorten grief and pull what should be far back to what feels near.
entries.literal: Counting by months as the number compresses the heart of longing, making the distant near.

entries.zh: 日既餘分，月非正朔，含而全制，於情唯允。
entries.en: Leap days are the year's remainder; leap months are not true first days of the month—yet folding them in to finish the full mourning term is what feeling allows.
entries.literal: Days are already surplus fractions; months are not proper new moons—embracing them to complete the rule is alone fitting to feeling.

entries.zh: 僕射儉議，理據詳博，謹所附同。
entries.en: Vice Director Wang Jian's argument is thorough; I respectfully concur.
entries.literal: Vice Director Jian's proposal, with reasons detailed and broad—I respectfully attach myself to agreement.

entries.zh: 今司徒淵始雖疑難，再經往反，未同儉議。
entries.en: Minister of Works Chu Yuan first objected; after two exchanges he still did not accept Jian's view.
entries.literal: Now Minister of Works Yuan at first doubted and objected; after two rounds of exchange he still does not agree with Jian's proposal.

entries.zh: 依舊八座丞郎通共博議為允。
entries.en: By old custom the eight excellencies and all directors and aides should debate the matter together and settle what is right.
entries.literal: According to old precedent, the eight excellencies and directors and aides should jointly debate to find what is fitting.

entries.zh: 以來五月晦小祥，其祥禫自依常限。
entries.en: Henceforth minor felicity on the last day of the fifth month; xiang and chan thereafter on the ordinary schedule.
entries.literal: From now on, minor felicity on the last day of the fifth month; xiang and chan themselves follow the usual limits.

entries.zh: 奏御，班下內外。」
entries.en: The memorial went up; the decision was issued court and realm."
entries.literal: Memorial presented to the throne; promulgated within and without."

entries.zh: 詔「可」。
entries.en: The edict read: "Approved."
entries.literal: An edict said "Approved."

entries.zh: 建元三年，太子穆妃薨，南郡王聞喜公國臣疑制君母服。
entries.en: In the third year of Jianyuan, the crown prince's Consort Mu died; retainers of the prince of Nan Commandery and the duke of Wenxi disputed how to mourn a lord's mother.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan, the crown prince's Consort Mu died; officials of the Prince of Nan Commandery and the Duke of Wenxi questioned mourning dress for a stepmother of the lord.

entries.zh: 儉又議：「禮『庶人為國君齊衰』，先儒云『庶人在官若府史之屬是也』。
entries.en: Jian argued again: "The rites say "Commoners in office wear equated mourning for the lord of the state", and early scholars explain "in office" as clerks on a prince's or commandery staff.
entries.literal: Jian again memorialized: "The rites say "Commoners wear equated mourning for the lord of the state", and early scholars say "Commoners in office means clerks such as prefectural and commandery staff."

entries.zh: 又諸侯之大夫妻為夫人服繐衰七月，以此輕微疏遠，故不得盡禮。
entries.en: A great feudal lord's wife wears fine hemp seven months for the lord's wife—being remote and slight in rank, she does not receive the full rite.
entries.literal: Again, a great feudal lord's wife wears fine hemp for seven months for the lord's wife—because she is slight and distant, she cannot receive the full rite.

entries.zh: 今皇孫自是蕃國之王公，太子穆妃是天朝之嫡婦。
entries.en: The imperial grandson is a feudal king in his own domain; Consort Mu was the crown prince's orthodox wife in the heavenly court.
entries.literal: Now the imperial grandson is himself a feudal king of a border state; the crown prince's Consort Mu is the orthodox daughter-in-law of the heavenly court.

entries.zh: 宮臣得申小君之禮，國官豈敢為夫人之敬。
entries.en: Palace staff may perform rites for a lesser lady; domain officials dare not perform rites for a full lady of the house.
entries.literal: Palace retainers may perform the rites due a lesser lady; how dare state officials perform the rites due a lady of the domain?

entries.zh: 當單衣白帢素帶哭于中門外，每臨輒入，與宮官同。」
entries.en: They should wear plain dress, white headcloth, and plain belt and weep outside the middle gate, entering only when called—as palace officers do."
entries.literal: They should wear plain clothes, white headcloth, and plain belt and weep outside the middle gate; each time they attend they enter, the same as palace officers."

entries.zh: 建武二年，朝會，時世祖遏密未終，朝議疑作樂不？
entries.en: In Jianwu 2, at court assembly, Emperor Shizu's mourning taboo was not yet over, and the court debated whether music should be played.
entries.literal: Jianwu 2, at court assembly—the Shizu emperor's mourning taboo was not yet ended, and court debate doubted whether to perform music.

entries.zh: 祠部郎何佟之議：「昔舜受終文祖，義非胤堯，及放勛徂落，遏密三祀。
entries.en: He Tongzhi, directorate-of-sacrifices attendant, argued: "When Shun received the mandate from Wenzu he did not, in principle, inherit Yao; when Fangxun died, he suppressed music for three years.
entries.literal: He Tongzhi of the Directorate of Sacrifices argued: "In antiquity Shun received the mandate from Wenzu; in principle he did not inherit Yao; when Fangxun passed away, he suppressed music for three years.

entries.zh: 近代晉康帝繼成帝，于時亦不作樂。
entries.en: In Jin, Emperor Kang succeeded Emperor Cheng and likewise made no music.
entries.literal: In recent times Jin Emperor Kang succeeded Emperor Cheng; at that time likewise no music was performed.

entries.zh: 懷帝永嘉元年，惠帝喪制未終，于時江充議云，古帝王相承，雖世及有異，而輕重同禮。」
entries.en: In Huai's Yongjia 1, while Emperor Hui's mourning was unfinished, Jiang Chong held that successive rulers, though succession differed, observed the same rites in weight."
entries.literal: In Yongjia 1 of Emperor Huai, Emperor Hui's mourning was not yet ended; at that time Jiang Chong argued that from antiquity successive emperors, though succession differed, shared the same rites in weight."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court followed him.
entries.literal: This was followed.

entries.zh: 永明十一年，文惠太子薨，右僕射王晏等奏：「案喪服經『為君之父、長子，同齊衰朞』。
entries.en: Yongming 11: Crown Prince Wenhui died. Vice Director Wang Yan and others wrote: "The Mourning Garments classic says: "For the lord's father and eldest son, the same equated mourning period."
entries.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongming, Crown Prince Wenhui died; Right Vice Director Wang Yan and others memorialized: "According to the Mourning Garments classic, "For the lord's father and eldest son, the same equated mourning period."

entries.zh: 今至尊既不行三年之典，止服朞制，羣臣應降一等，便應大功。
entries.en: Since the sovereign does not observe the full three-year rite but only the one-year mourning, the ministers should drop one grade and wear greater processed hemp.
entries.literal: Now the Supreme Sovereign, since he does not perform the three-year rite, stops at period mourning, the assembled ministers should drop one grade and thus wear greater processed hemp.

entries.zh: 九月功衰，是兄弟之服，不可以服尊。
entries.en: Nine-month diminished labor is brothers' mourning; it cannot be worn for a superior.
entries.literal: Nine-month diminished labor is the dress of brothers; one may not wear it for a superior.

entries.zh: 臣等參議，謂宜重其衰裳，減其月數，同服齊衰三月。
entries.en: We submit that the sackcloth should be heavier and the months fewer—everyone alike in three months of dressed sackcloth.
entries.literal: We your ministers, deliberating together, hold that one should make the sackcloth heavier and reduce the number of months, all wearing dressed sackcloth for three months.

entries.zh: 至於太孫三年既申，南郡國臣，宜備齊衰朞服。
entries.en: Once the imperial grandson's three-year term is complete, the Nan Commandery domain's ministers should wear the full one-year dressed sackcloth.
entries.literal: As for the imperial grandson, once his three years are complete, the ministers of the Nankang principality should fully prepare one-year dressed sackcloth.

entries.zh: 臨汝、曲江既非正嫡，不得禰先儲，二公國臣，竝不得服。」
entries.en: Linru and Qujiang were not legitimate heirs and could not honor the former heir; neither princedom's ministers should mourn."
entries.literal: Linru and Qujiang, not being legitimate heirs, may not enshrine the former heir designate; the ministers of the two princedoms alike may not wear mourning."

entries.zh: 詔依所議。
entries.en: The edict approved their proposal.
entries.literal: An edict followed the deliberation.

entries.zh: 又奏：「伏尋御服文惠太子朞內不奏樂，諸王雖本服朞，而儲皇正體宗廟，服者一同，釋服，奏樂姻娶，便應竝通。
entries.en: They memorialized again: "In imperial mourning for Crown Prince Wenhui, no music is played during the year; though the princes themselves are in period mourning, the heir is the temple's proper body and the grade is one—when mourning ends, music and marriage should be allowed alike.
entries.literal: They memorialized again: "We reflect that in imperial mourning for Crown Prince Wenhui, within the period no music is performed; though the princes' own mourning is period mourning, the heir designate is the proper body of the ancestral temple—the wearers are one; when mourning is released, music and marriage should likewise be permitted together.

entries.zh: 竊謂二等誠俱是嘉禮，輕重有異。
entries.en: I hold that both are joyous rites, but not of the same weight.
entries.literal: I submit that both grades are indeed joyous rites, but their weight differs.

entries.zh: 娶婦思嗣，事非全吉，三日不樂，禮有明文。
entries.en: Marriage to secure an heir is not wholly auspicious; three days without music—the rites say so plainly.
entries.literal: Taking a wife to think of heirs is not wholly auspicious; three days without music—the rites have explicit text.

entries.zh: 宋世朞喪降在大功者，婚禮廢樂，以申私戚，通以前典。」
entries.en: Under Song, mourners reduced from the year to greater processed hemp still laid music aside at weddings to show private grief—following older precedent."
entries.literal: In Song, those whose period mourning was reduced to greater processed hemp still suspended music at weddings, to express private grief—this accords with earlier precedent."

entries.zh: 詔「依議」。
entries.en: Edict: "Approved."
entries.literal: Edict: "Follow the deliberation."

entries.zh: 建武二年正月，有司以世
entries.en: In the first month of Jianwu 2, the relevant offices reported that Shizong
entries.literal: In the first month of Jianwu 2, the relevant offices, regarding the dynastic

entries.en: Zong
entries.literal: (Received text: zu; emended to zong.)

entries.zh: 宗文皇帝今二年正月二十四日再忌日，二十九日大祥，三月二十九日祥禫，至尊及羣臣泄哀之儀，應定准。
entries.en: Emperor Wen (temple name Shizong): in the second year, the twenty-fourth day of the first month is the second death anniversary; the twenty-ninth is major xiang; the twenty-ninth of the third month is xiang removal. The rites by which sovereign and ministers pour forth grief should be set by precedent.
entries.literal: Zong Emperor Wen: in the second year, the twenty-fourth day of the first month is the second death anniversary, the twenty-ninth is major xiang, the twenty-ninth of the third month is xiang removal; the rites for the sovereign and assembled ministers to pour forth grief should be fixed by precedent.

entries.zh: 下二學八座丞郎。
entries.en: The matter was circulated to the two academies, the eight seats, and the directorate and attendant ranks.
entries.literal: The matter was sent down to the two academies, the eight seats, directors, and attendants.

entries.zh: 博士陶韶以為「名立義生，自古之制。
entries.en: Erudite Tao Shao held: "When the title is fixed the obligation follows—that is ancient regulation.
entries.literal: Erudite Tao Shao held that "when the name is established the duty arises—this is the regulation from antiquity.

entries.zh: 文帝正號祖宗，式序昭穆，祥忌禫日，皇帝宜服祭服，出太極泄哀，百僚亦祭服陪位」。
entries.en: Emperor Wen now stands properly among ancestors; on xiang, memorial, and removal days the emperor should wear sacrificial robes, leave the Supreme Ultimate hall to pour forth grief, and the hundred offices should attend in sacrificial dress likewise."
entries.literal: Emperor Wen has the proper title among ancestors and founders, ordering the zhao and mu; on xiang, death-day, and removal days the emperor should wear sacrificial dress, go out from the Supreme Ultimate to pour forth grief, and the hundred offices should also attend in sacrificial dress."

entries.zh: 太常丞李撝議曰：「尋尊號既追，重服宜正，但已從權制，故苴杖不說。
entries.en: Li Huo, aide in the chamberlainate for ceremonials, argued: "Once the posthumous title was granted, full mourning would be proper; but the court already followed an expedient rule, so the hemp staff is not discussed.
entries.literal: Aide Li Huo of the Chamberlain for Ceremonials argued: "Examining the matter, once the honorific title was granted, full mourning should be correct; but having already followed expedient regulation, the hemp staff is not mentioned.

entries.zh: 至於鑽燧既同，天地亦變，容得無感乎。
entries.en: Yet when the fire-drill is the same, Heaven and Earth change too—how could one feel nothing?
entries.literal: Yet when fire-sticks are alike, Heaven and Earth also change—can one be without feeling?

entries.zh: 且晉景獻皇后崩，羣臣備小君之服。
entries.en: When Jin's Jingxian empress died, the ministers wore the dress owed a lesser mistress.
entries.literal: Moreover, when Jin's Jingxian empress died, the assembled ministers prepared the dress for a lesser mistress.

entries.zh: 追尊之后，無違后典，追尊之帝，固宜同帝禮矣。
entries.en: After posthumous elevation to empress there is no breach of empress precedent; a posthumously elevated emperor should follow emperor rites all the more.
entries.literal: After posthumous elevation to empress, one does not violate empress precedent; a posthumously elevated emperor should likewise follow emperor rites.

entries.zh: 雖臣子一例，而禮隨時異，至尊龍飛中興，事非嗣武，理無深衣之變。
entries.en: Ministers and sons may share one rule, but rites shift with the age; the sovereign's restoration is not succession in the manner of continuing Wu—there is no call for deep-garment mourning.
entries.literal: Though ministers and sons share one rule, rites vary with the times; the Supreme Sovereign's dragon flight at restoration is not succession like continuing Wu—there is no reason for a change to deep garments.

entries.zh: 但王者體國，亦應弔服出正殿舉哀，百寮致慟，一如常儀。」
entries.en: Yet the king embodies the state: he should wear condolence dress, go out to the main hall to lament, and the hundred offices express grief as in ordinary rites."
entries.literal: Yet the king embodies the state; he should also wear condolence dress, go out to the main hall to lament, and the hundred offices express grief—just as in the usual rites."

entries.zh: 給事中領國子助教謝
entries.en: Attendant gentleman and acting national university assistant instructor Xie
entries.literal: Attendant gentleman and acting national university assistant instructor Xie

entries.en: (Mo)
entries.literal: (Mo)

entries.zh: 曇濟議：「夫喪禮一制，限節兩分。
entries.en: Xie Tanji argued: "Mourning is one system, but its limits divide in two.
entries.literal: Tan Ji argued: "Mourning rites are one system, but the limits split in two.

entries.zh: 虞祔追亡之情，小祥抑存之禮，斯蓋至愛可申，極痛宜屈耳。
entries.en: Yu and fu pursue the dead; minor xiang restrains remembrance of the living—there utmost love may extend and utmost pain should yield.
entries.literal: The feeling of yu and fu pursues the dead; the rite of minor xiang restrains remembrance of the living—this is where utmost love may extend and utmost pain should bend.

entries.zh: 文皇帝雖君德早凝，民化未洽，追崇尊極，寔緣于性。
entries.en: Emperor Wen's virtue was early formed though the people were not yet fully transformed; posthumous exaltation sprang from nature alone.
entries.literal: Emperor Wen, though his lordly virtue was early set, the people's transformation was not yet complete, yet posthumous exaltation to the utmost sprang from nature.

entries.zh: 今言臣則無實，論己則事虛。
entries.en: As ministers we have no real standing here; for ourselves the matter is hollow.
entries.literal: Speaking now as a minister lacks substance; speaking of oneself the matter is empty.

entries.zh: 聖上馭㝢，更奉天眷，祗禮七廟，非從三后，周忌祥禫，無所依設。」
entries.en: The sage sovereign rules the realm under Heaven's renewed favor, reverently tends the seven temples—not as heir to three empresses—so the cycle of memorial, xiang, and removal has no footing."
entries.literal: The sage sovereign rules the realm, again receives Heaven's favor, reverently serves the seven temples—not following three empresses; the cycle of memorial, xiang, and removal has nothing on which to be set."

entries.zh: 太學博士崔愝同陶韶議，太常沈倓同李撝議，國子博士劉警等同謝
entries.en: National university erudite Cui Tan sided with Tao Shao; chamberlain Shen Tan sided with Li Huo; national university erudite Liu Jing and others sided with Xie
entries.literal: National university erudite Cui Tan agreed with Tao Shao's deliberation; chamberlain Shen Tan agreed with Li Huo's deliberation; national university erudite Liu Jing and others agreed with Xie

entries.en: (Mo)
entries.literal: (Mo)

entries.zh: 曇濟議。
entries.en: Tanji's deliberation.
entries.literal: Tan Ji's deliberation.

entries.zh: 海陵王薨，百官會哀，時纂嚴，朝議疑戎服臨會。
entries.en: When the prince of Hailing died, officials gathered to mourn; the court was under strict assembly rules, and men debated whether to appear in military dress.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Hailing died, the hundred officials gathered for mourning; at that time the court was in strict assembly order, and court debate doubted whether to attend in military dress.

entries.zh: 祠部郎何佟之議：「羔裘玄冠不以弔。
entries.en: He Tongzhi of the sacrifices directorate argued: "Lamb-fur robe and black cap are not for condolence calls.
entries.literal: He Tongzhi, attendant of the directorate of sacrifices, argued: "The lamb-fur robe and black ceremonial cap are not worn for condolence visits.

entries.zh: 理不容以兵服臨喪。
entries.en: In principle one cannot stand at a funeral in arms.
entries.literal: In principle one cannot attend a funeral in military dress.

entries.zh: 宋泰始二年，孝武大祥之日，于時百寮入臨，皆於宮門變戎服，著衣𢂿，入臨畢出外，還襲戎衣。」
entries.en: In Song's the second year of Taishi, on Emperor Xiaowu's major-xiang day, the hundred offices came to mourn: at the palace gate they changed out of military dress, put on mourning border-robes, entered to mourn and left when done, then resumed military dress."
entries.literal: In the second year of Taishi of Song, on Emperor Xiaowu's day of major xiang, at that time the hundred offices entered for condolence, all changed out of military dress at the palace gate, put on border mourning garments, entered for condolence and when finished went out, then put on military dress again."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The court followed him.
entries.literal: This was followed.

entries.zh: 永明二年，尚書殿中曹奏：「太祖高皇帝廟神室奏《高德宣烈之舞》，未有歌詩，郊應須歌辭。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongming, the Secretariat's Director of Palace Affairs reported: 「At Grand Ancestor Gaozu's temple chamber they perform "Dance Proclaiming Lofty Virtue and Martial Glory," but there is no hymn yet; the suburban rite still needs words.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongming, the Director of Palace Affairs in the Secretariat memorialized: 「Grand Ancestor Emperor Gaozu's temple chamber performs "Dance Proclaiming Lofty Virtue and Martial Glory"—no hymn yet; suburban sacrifice needs hymn text.

entries.zh: 穆皇后廟神室，亦未有歌辭。
entries.en: Empress Mu's temple chamber likewise has no hymn text.
entries.literal: Empress Mu's temple chamber likewise has no hymn text yet.

entries.zh: 案傅玄云：『登歌廟異其文，饗神七室同辭。』
entries.en: On Fu Xuan's view: 『Ascent hymns differ in wording from temple to temple, but the seven chambers share one text for spirit-feasting.』
entries.literal: Examining Fu Xuan's statement: 『Ascent hymns differ in text for each temple; feasting-spirit songs use the same wording for all seven chambers.』

entries.zh: 此議爲允。
entries.en: This view was accepted.
entries.literal: This opinion is approved.

entries.zh: 又尋漢世歌篇，多少無定，皆稱事立文，竝多八句，然後轉韻。
entries.en: Reviewing Han song-cycles shows no fixed length: each was shaped to its subject, usually eight lines before the rhyme turned.
entries.literal: Again searching Han-era song chapters, their length was unset; all were titled to the occasion and composed accordingly, mostly eight lines, then rhyme shifted.

entries.zh: 時有兩三韻而轉，其例甚寡。
entries.en: Occasionally the rhyme shifted after two or three stanzas, but that was rare.
entries.literal: At times two or three rhymes would shift; such cases were very few.

entries.zh: 張華、夏侯湛亦同前式。
entries.en: Zhang Hua and Xiahou Zhan followed the same earlier form.
entries.literal: Zhang Hua and Xiahou Zhan likewise followed the earlier pattern.

entries.zh: 傅玄改韻頗數，更傷簡節之美。
entries.en: Fu Xuan changed rhyme too often, which further marred the grace of compact restraint.
entries.literal: Fu Xuan shifted rhyme rather often, further harming the beauty of brevity and rhythm.

entries.zh: 近世王韶之、顏延之並四韻乃轉，得賒促之中。
entries.en: Recently Wang Shao-zhi and Yan Yan-zhi both turned rhyme after four stanzas, hitting the mean between long and short.
entries.literal: In recent times Wang Shao-zhi and Yan Yan-zhi both shifted after four rhymes, achieving a balance between extended and compressed.

entries.zh: 顏延之、謝莊作三廟歌，皆各三章章八句，此于序述功業詳略爲宜，今宜依之。
entries.en: Yan Yan-zhi and Xie Zhuang wrote hymns for three temples, each in three eight-line chapters—fitting for fuller or briefer accounts of merit—and that pattern should be adopted now.
entries.literal: Yan Yan-zhi and Xie Zhuang composed three-temple songs, each with three chapters of eight lines apiece—this suits narrating achievements in greater or lesser detail; it should be followed now.

entries.zh: 郊配之日，改降尊作主，禮殊宗廟；
entries.en: On suburban-sacrifice days, when the honored one is demoted to preside, the rite differs from ancestral-temple ceremony;
entries.literal: On suburban sacrifice days, when the honored is lowered in rank to serve as host, the rite differs from the ancestral temple;

entries.zh: 穆后母儀之化，事異經綸。
entries.en: Empress Mu's maternal transforming grace is a matter apart from governance.
entries.literal: Empress Mu's maternal exemplary transforming influence—the matter differs from statecraft.

entries.zh: 此二歌爲一章八句，別奏事御奉行。」
entries.en: These two hymns are to be one eight-line chapter each, performed separately as the ceremony requires."
entries.literal: These two songs are one chapter of eight lines each; they are to be performed separately as ceremonial officers carry out the rite."

entries.zh: 詔「可」。
entries.en: The edict said "Granted."
entries.literal: An edict read "Approved."

entries.zh: 尚書令王儉造太廟二室及郊配辭。
entries.en: Wang Jian, Minister Over the Masses, composed hymn texts for two ancestral-temple chambers and the suburban rite.
entries.literal: Minister Over the Masses Wang Jian composed hymn texts for two Imperial Ancestral Temple chambers and suburban sacrifice.

entries.zh: 元會大饗四廂樂歌辭，晉泰始五年太僕傅玄撰。
entries.en: Lyrics for the New Year's Grand Assembly feast in the four galleries, composed by Jin Grand Master of the Household Fu Xuan in the fifth year of Taishi.
entries.literal: New Year's grand feast four-gallery music hymn texts, composed in the fifth year of Taishi by Jin Grand Master of the Household Fu Xuan.

entries.zh: 正旦大會行禮歌詩四章，壽酒詩一章，食舉東西廂樂十三章，黃門郎張華作。
entries.en: For the New Year's Day grand assembly: four ceremonial hymn-poems, one longevity-wine poem, and thirteen food-raising gallery pieces east and west, by Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua.
entries.literal: New Year's Day grand assembly ceremonial hymn-poems four chapters, longevity wine poem one chapter, food-raising east-west gallery music thirteen chapters, Yellow Gate Gentleman Zhang Hua composed.

entries.zh: 上壽食舉行禮詩十八章，中書監荀勗、侍郎成公綏，言數各異。
entries.en: Eighteen hymn-poems for longevity presentation and food-raising were credited to Secretariat Director Xun Xu and Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Gong-sui, but with differing line counts.
entries.literal: Longevity presentation and food-raising ceremonial poems eighteen chapters, Secretariat Director Xun Xu and Attendant-in-Ordinary Cheng Gong-sui—the line counts each differ.

entries.zh: 宋黃門郎王韶之造《肆夏》四章，行禮一章，上壽一章，登歌三章，食舉十章，《前後舞歌》一章。
entries.en: In Song, Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Shao-zhi composed four "Si Xia" chapters, one ceremonial piece, one longevity presentation, three ascent hymns, ten food-raising pieces, and one "Front and Rear Dance Song."
entries.literal: Song Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Shao-zhi made "Si Xia" four chapters, ceremonial one chapter, longevity presentation one chapter, ascent hymns three chapters, food-raising ten chapters, "Front and Rear Dance Song" one chapter.

entries.zh: 齊微改革，多仍舊辭。
entries.en: Qi made slight revisions, largely keeping the old wording.
entries.literal: Qi slightly reformed, mostly retaining old texts.

entries.zh: 其《前後舞》二章新改。
entries.en: Its two "Front and Rear Dance" chapters were newly rewritten.
entries.literal: Its "Front and Rear Dance" two chapters newly revised.

entries.zh: 其臨軒樂，亦奏《肆夏·於鑠》四章。
entries.en: For music at the facing-the-gallery audience, four chapters of "Si Xia: Imposing Splendor" were also played.
entries.literal: Its facing-the-gallery music also performed "Si Xia: Imposing Splendor" four chapters.

entries.zh: 《前舞》、《後舞》，晉泰始九年造。
entries.en: "Front Dance" and "Rear Dance"—created in the ninth year of Taishi under Jin.
entries.literal: "Front Dance" and "Rear Dance"—created in the ninth year of Taishi under Jin.

entries.zh: 《正德大豫舞》，傅玄、張華各爲歌辭。
entries.en: "Correct Virtue" and "Great Abundance Dance"—Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua each supplied song words.
entries.literal: "Correct Virtue" and "Great Abundance Dance" — Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua each wrote song lyrics.

entries.zh: 宋元嘉中，改《正德》爲《前舞》，《大豫》爲《後舞》。
entries.en: In Song's Yuanjia reign, "Correct Virtue" became "Front Dance" and "Great Abundance" became "Rear Dance."::
entries.literal: In Song's Yuanjia era, "Correct Virtue" was changed to "Front Dance," "Great Abundance" to "Rear Dance."::

entries.zh: 樂
entries.en: Music
entries.literal: Music

entries.zh: 太師、太保、太傅，周舊官。
entries.en: Grand Preceptor, Grand Guardian, and Grand Tutor were offices of the Zhou.
entries.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Guardian, and Grand Tutor were Zhou old offices.

entries.zh: 漢末，董卓爲太師。
entries.en: Late in Han, Dong Zhuo held the Grand Preceptorship.
entries.literal: At the end of Han, Dong Zhuo was Grand Preceptor.

entries.zh: 晉惠帝初，衞瓘爲太保。
entries.en: At the start of Jin Huidi's reign, Wei Guan was made Grand Guardian.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jin Emperor Hui's reign, Wei Guan was Grand Guardian.

entries.zh: 自後無太師，而太保爲贈。
entries.en: Thereafter no one held Grand Preceptor; Grand Guardian survived only as a posthumous grant.
entries.literal: Afterward there was no Grand Preceptor, and Grand Guardian became posthumous.

entries.zh: 齊唯置太傅。
entries.en: Qi kept only the Grand Tutor among them.
entries.literal: Qi established only the Grand Tutor.

entries.zh: 建元四年，有司奏置國學，祭酒准諸曹尚書，博士准中書郎，助教准南臺御史。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jianyuan the ministries proposed a national academy: its director ranked with a bureau director of the masters of writing, its erudites with a secretariat gentleman, its assistants with a Southern Bureau censor.
entries.literal: In Jianyuan year 4 the relevant offices memorialized to establish the national academy: the director's rank equaled directors of the masters of writing in other bureaus, erudites equaled secretariat gentlemen, and assistants equaled censors of the Southern Bureau.

entries.zh: 選經學爲先。
entries.en: Candidates were chosen first for mastery of the classics.
entries.literal: Classical learning came first in selection.

entries.zh: 若其人難備，給事中以還明經者，以本位領。
entries.en: When no one qualified could be found, a palace attendant who had passed the classics examination might serve concurrently in his present rank.
entries.literal: If suitable men were hard to find, a palace attendant who had passed the classics examination might lead in his existing post.

entries.zh: 其下典學二人，三品，准太常主簿；
entries.en: Below them stood two academy directors of third rank, equal to the Minister of Ceremonies' chief clerk;
entries.literal: Below them were two academy directors, third rank, equivalent to the Minister of Ceremonies' chief clerk;

entries.zh: 戶曹、儀曹各二人，五品；
entries.en: two household clerks and two ritual clerks each, fifth rank;
entries.literal: two household clerks and two ritual clerks each, fifth rank;

entries.zh: 白簿治禮吏八人，六品；
entries.en: eight white-register clerks for ritual paperwork, sixth rank;
entries.literal: eight white-register clerks for ritual administration, sixth rank;

entries.zh: 保學醫二人；
entries.en: two academy physicians;
entries.literal: two academy physicians;

entries.zh: 威儀二人。
entries.en: two masters of ceremony.
entries.literal: two masters of ceremony.

entries.zh: 其夏，國諱廢學，有司奏省助教以下。
entries.en: That summer mourning for the late emperor closed the schools; the ministries proposed cutting every post below teaching assistant.
entries.literal: That summer, because of the imperial mourning taboo the schools were suspended; the ministries memorialized to abolish posts below teaching assistant.

entries.zh: 永明三年，立學，尚書令王儉領祭酒。
entries.en: In Yongming 3 the academy was restored; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian served as its director.
entries.literal: In Yongming year 3 the academy was re-established; Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian headed it as director.

entries.zh: 八年，國子博士何胤單爲祭酒，疑所服，陸澄等皆不能據，遂以玄服臨試。
entries.en: In year 8 the academy erudite He Yin became sole director; with no precedent for his robes, Lu Cheng and the rest could not decide, and he examined candidates in black dress.
entries.literal: In year 8 the academy erudite He Yin alone became director; uncertain what robes to wear, Lu Cheng and others could cite no precedent, so he presided over examinations in black garb.

entries.zh: 月餘日，博議定，乃服朱衣。
entries.en: After a month of debate among scholars, he took vermilion robes.
entries.literal: After a month and more of broad deliberation, he donned vermilion robes.

entries.zh: 皆銀章青綬，詔加金章紫綬者，爲金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: All bore silver seals and green ribbons; when an edict added a golden seal and purple ribbon, the holder became a Grandee of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
entries.literal: All had silver seals and green ribbons; those whom an edict added a golden seal and purple ribbon became Grandees of Splendor with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 樂安任遐爲光祿，就王晏乞一片金，晏乃啓轉爲金紫，不行。
entries.en: Ren Xia of Le'an held the grandeeship of splendor; he asked Wang Yan for a piece of gold, and Yan memorialized to promote him to golden seal and purple ribbon, but the request failed.
entries.literal: Ren Xia of Le'an was grandee of splendor; he asked Wang Yan for a piece of gold, and Yan memorialized to transfer him to golden seal and purple ribbon, but it did not go through.

entries.zh: 府置丞一人。
entries.en: The bureau had one aide.
entries.literal: The bureau had one aide.

entries.zh: 掌宮城管籥。
entries.en: He oversaw the palace city's gates and keys.
entries.literal: He oversaw the palace city's gates and keys.

entries.zh: 張衡西京賦曰「衞尉八屯，警夜巡晝」。
entries.en: Zhang Heng's Western Capital Rhapsody says, "The commandant of the guards' eight garrisons—alert at night, patrol by day."
entries.literal: Zhang Heng's Western Capital Rhapsody says, "The Commandant of the Guards' eight garrisons—alert at night, patrol by day."

entries.zh: 宮城諸却敵樓上本施鼓，持夜者以應更唱，太祖以鼓多驚眠，改以鐵磬云。
entries.en: On every parapet tower of the palace city drums had once been set up, and night watchmen answered the watch-change call with them. The Founder, saying the drums too often broke sleep, is said to have replaced them with iron chimes.
entries.literal: On all the parapet towers of the palace city drums had originally been installed; night watchmen answered the change of watch by drumming. The Founder, finding the drums often startled sleep, changed them to iron chimes, it is said.

entries.zh: 漢世爲親近之職。
