entries.literal: The heir apparent, as master of his palace, should in any case receive the imperial carriage when it visits his quarters in the usual form of attendance.

entries.zh: 旣當成服之日，吉凶不容相干，宜以衰幘行事。
entries.en: On the day mourning dress is completed, joy and grief must not mingle—he should go in hemp cap and headband.
entries.literal: On a day when mourning dress is completed, auspicious and inauspicious rites must not clash; he should act wearing hemp cap and headband.

entries.zh: 望拜止哭，率由舊章。
entries.en: Cease weeping to bow toward the carriage—that follows old precedent.
entries.literal: Stopping tears to perform the bow toward the carriage—all according to established precedent.

entries.zh: 尊駕不以臨吊，奉迎則惟常體，求之情禮，如爲可安。」
entries.en: The supreme carriage does not come to mourn; to meet it is only ordinary courtesy. Judged by feeling and rite, that should suffice."
entries.literal: Since the supreme carriage does not come for condolence, welcoming it is only the ordinary courtesy. Weighing feeling and rite, that seems acceptable."

entries.zh: 解侍中。
entries.en: He was relieved of palace attendant.
entries.literal: He was relieved of palace attendant.

entries.zh: 上以太子哀疾，不宜居石頭山障，移鎮西州。
entries.en: The emperor, finding the prince in grief and poor health, thought Stone City's mountain redoubts unsuitable and shifted him to West Province.
entries.literal: The emperor, because the crown prince was in mourning and ill, thought Stone City's mountain defenses unsuitable and moved him to garrison West Province.

entries.zh: 四年，遷使持節、都督南徐兗二州諸軍事、征北將軍、南徐州刺史。
entries.en: In year 4 he was transferred bearer of the staff, superintendent of southern Xu and Yan, general who campaigns north, and inspector of southern Xu.
entries.literal: In year 4 he was transferred as bearer of the staff of authority, superintendent of military affairs in the two provinces of southern Xu and Yan, general who campaigns north, and inspector of southern Xu province.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，爲皇太子。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu acceded, Xiao Zhangmao was made crown prince.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was made crown prince.

entries.zh: 初，太祖好《左氏春秋》，太子承旨諷誦，以爲口實。
entries.en: In his youth Xiao Daocheng loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; the prince recited it at his bidding until the text lived on his tongue.
entries.literal: At first the Grand Ancestor loved the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals; the crown prince carried out his intent by reciting it until it became a favorite topic.

entries.zh: 旣正位東儲，善立名尚，禮接文士，畜養武人，皆親近左右，布在省闥。
entries.en: Once he held the eastern palace he courted a fine name, welcomed men of letters, and kept fighting men near—all of them in his inner circle, stationed through the palace offices.
entries.literal: Once installed as heir apparent, he cultivated reputation and esteem, received scholars with courtesy, and kept martial men about him—all close at hand, placed throughout the palace offices.

entries.zh: 永明三年，於崇正殿講《孝經》，少傅王儉以擿句令太子僕周顒撰爲義疏。
entries.en: In Yongming year 3 he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of Correct Reverence; Junior Tutor Wang Jian picked out passages and had Palace Adjutant Zhou Yong draft a commentary.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongming, he lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety in the Hall of Correct Reverence; Junior Tutor Wang Jian, by selecting passages, had Palace Adjutant Zhou Yong compile a commentary.

entries.zh: 五年冬，太子臨國學，親臨策試諸生，於坐問少傅王儉曰：「《曲禮》云『無不敬』。
entries.en: That winter in the fifth year the crown prince went to the National Academy, sat in person to examine the students, and asked Junior Tutor Wang Jian from his seat: "The Qu Li says, 'There is nothing to which one is not reverent.'
entries.literal: In the winter of the fifth year the crown prince attended the National Academy, personally presided over the written examination of the students, and from his seat asked Junior Tutor Wang Jian: "The Qu Li chapter of the Record of Rites says, 'There is nothing to which one is not reverent.'

entries.zh: 尋下之奉上，可以盡禮，上之接下，慈而非敬。
entries.en: From below to above one may exhaust every rite; from above to those below there is kindness, not reverence.
entries.literal: Serving from below upward can exhaust ritual; receiving those below from above is kindness, not reverence.

entries.zh: 今總同敬名，將不爲昧？」
entries.en: To call both by the single name 'reverence'—will that not blur what is distinct?"
entries.literal: To use the same name 'reverence' for both—will that not obscure the distinction?"

entries.zh: 儉曰：「鄭玄云『禮主於敬』，便當是尊卑所同。」
entries.en: Wang Jian replied: "Zheng Xuan says 'Ritual takes reverence as its foundation'—then high and low should share it alike."
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: "Zheng Xuan says 'Ritual takes reverence as its foundation'—that should hold for superior and inferior alike."

entries.zh: 太子曰：「若如來通，則忠惠可以一名，孝慈不須另稱。」
entries.en: The crown prince said: "If that holds all the way through, loyalty and kindness could be one name, and filial piety and compassion would need no second term."
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "If one follows that through, loyalty and generosity could share one name, and filial piety and compassion would need no separate terms."

entries.zh: 儉曰：「尊卑號稱，不可悉同，愛敬之名，有時相次。
entries.en: Wang Jian said: "Titles for high and low cannot all match; the names love and reverence sometimes come one after the other.
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: "Titles for superior and inferior cannot all be identical; the names love and reverence sometimes follow in sequence.

entries.zh: 忠惠之異，誠以聖旨，孝慈互舉，竊有徵據。
entries.en: Loyalty and kindness differ by the sage's meaning; filial piety and compassion are set side by side—I have warrant for that.
entries.literal: The difference between loyalty and generosity truly rests on the sage's intent; filial piety and compassion are raised in turn—I have private evidence for this.

entries.zh: 《禮》云『不勝喪比於不慈不孝』，此則其義。」
entries.en: The Record of Rites says, 'One who cannot bear mourning is like one unkind and unfilial'—that is the proof."
entries.literal: The Record of Rites says 'One who cannot bear mourning is like one who is unkind and unfilial'—that is the point."

entries.zh: 太子曰：「資敬奉君，資愛事親，兼此二塗，唯在一極。
entries.en: The crown prince said: "Reverence feeds service to the ruler, love feeds service to parents—both roads meet at one pole.
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "Drawing on reverence to serve the ruler and on love to serve one's parents—both paths share a single pole.

entries.zh: 今乃移敬接下。
entries.en: Yet now reverence is moved down to those below.
entries.literal: Yet now reverence is shifted to receiving those below.

entries.zh: 豈復在三之義？」
entries.en: How does that still fit the meaning of 'three'?"
entries.literal: How can that still accord with the sense of 'three'?"

entries.zh: 儉曰：「資敬奉君，必同至極，移敬逮下，不慢而已。」
entries.en: Wang Jian said: "Reverence in serving the ruler must reach the same pole; carrying reverence down to those below means only not to slight them."
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: "Drawing on reverence to serve the ruler must reach the same pole; extending reverence to those below means only not to be disrespectful."

entries.zh: 太子曰：「敬名雖同，深淺旣異，而文無差別，彌復增疑。」
entries.en: The crown prince said: "The name is one, but depth and shallowness differ—and the wording shows no gap, which only adds doubt."
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "Though the name is the same, the depth and shallowness clearly differ—yet the text makes no distinction, which only deepens the doubt."

entries.zh: 儉曰：「繁文不可備設，略言深淺已見。
entries.en: Wang Jian said: "Full phrasing cannot all be laid out; in brief, depth and shallowness are already clear.
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: "Elaborate wording cannot all be set forth; stated briefly, the depth and shallowness are already plain.

entries.zh: 《傳》云『不忘恭敬，民之主也』。
entries.en: The Commentary says, 'Never forget reverence and respect—such a one is lord of the people.'
entries.literal: The Commentary says 'Never forget reverence and respect—such a one is lord of the people.'

entries.zh: 《書》云『奉先思孝，接下思恭』。
entries.en: The Documents say, 'In serving the ancestors, think of filial piety; in receiving those below, think of respect.'
entries.literal: The Documents say 'In serving the ancestors, think of filial piety; in receiving those below, think of respect.'

entries.zh: 此又經典明文，互相起發。」
entries.en: Here again the classics speak plainly, each line drawing the other out."
entries.literal: Here again is explicit scripture, each passage calling forth the other."

entries.zh: 太子問金紫光祿大夫張緒，緒曰：「愚謂恭敬是立身之本，尊卑所以竝同。」
entries.en: The crown prince asked Zhang Xu, minister of the palace with the golden seal and purple cord. Zhang said: "I take reverence and respect as the root of standing in the world—that is why high and low share them."
entries.literal: The crown prince asked Zhang Xu, Minister of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Cord. Zhang said: "I hold that reverence and respect are the root of taking one's stand in the world—hence superior and inferior share them alike."

entries.zh: 太子曰：「敬雖立身之本，要非接下之稱。
entries.en: The crown prince said: "Reverence may be the root of the person, but it is not the name for receiving those below.
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "Though reverence is the root of self-cultivation, it is hardly the term for receiving those below.

entries.zh: 《尚書》云『惠鮮鰥寡』，何不言恭敬鰥寡邪？」
entries.en: The Documents say, 'Be kind to widowers and widows'—why not say, 'be reverent and respectful to widowers and widows'?"
entries.literal: The Documents say 'Be kind to widowers and widows'—why not say 'be reverent and respectful to widowers and widows'?"

entries.zh: 緒曰：「今別言之，居然有恭惠之殊，總開記首，所以共同斯稱。」
entries.en: Zhang said: "Spoken apart, respect and kindness plainly differ; at the head of a record they are opened together, and so share one name."
entries.literal: Zhang said: "When spoken of separately, the difference between respect and kindness is plain; at the opening of a record they are taken together, and therefore share one designation."

entries.zh: 竟陵王子良曰：「禮者敬而已矣。
entries.en: The prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, said: "Ritual is reverence, nothing beyond it.
entries.literal: The prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, said: "Ritual is reverence and nothing more.

entries.zh: 自上及下，愚謂非嫌。」
entries.en: From top to bottom—I see no problem in that."
entries.literal: From highest to lowest—I see no difficulty."

entries.zh: 太子曰：「本不謂有嫌，正欲使言與事符，輕重有別耳。」
entries.en: The crown prince said: "I never called it a problem—I only want speech to fit the deed, with light and heavy kept apart."
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "I never said there was difficulty—I only want words to match affairs, with lighter and heavier clearly distinguished."

entries.zh: 臨川王映曰：「先舉必敬，以明大體，尊卑事數，備列後章，亦當不以總略而礙。」
entries.en: The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, said: "To open with reverence is to show the great pattern; the counts of rank and rite are spelled out in later chapters—a summary should not stand in the way."
entries.literal: The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, said: "To lead with reverence is to clarify the larger frame; the details of rank and ritual are fully set out in later chapters—one should not let a general summary block that."

entries.zh: 太子又以此義問諸學生，謝幾卿等十一人，竝以筆對。
entries.en: The crown prince put the same question to the students; Xie Jiqing and eleven others all answered in writing.
entries.literal: The crown prince again put this question to the students; Xie Jiqing and eleven others all answered in writing.

entries.zh: 太子問王儉曰：「《周易乾卦》本施天位，而《說卦》云『帝出乎《震》』。
entries.en: The crown prince asked Wang Jian: "The Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes is set for Heaven's place, yet the Explanation of the Trigrams says, 'The Lord emerges from Zhen.'
entries.literal: The crown prince asked Wang Jian: "The Qian hexagram of the Book of Changes originally applies to Heaven's position, yet the Explanation of the Trigrams says 'The Lord emerges from Zhen.'

entries.zh: 《震》本非天，義豈相主？」
entries.en: Zhen is not Heaven by nature—how can one meaning rule the other?"
entries.literal: Zhen is not Heaven by nature—how can the meanings preside over each other?"

entries.zh: 儉曰：「《乾》健《震》動，天以運動爲德，故言『帝出《震》』。」
entries.en: Wang Jian said: "Qian is firm, Zhen is movement; Heaven's virtue is movement, hence 'the Lord emerges from Zhen.'"
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: "Qian is strength, Zhen is motion; Heaven takes motion as its virtue, hence 'the Lord emerges from Zhen.'"

entries.zh: 太子曰：「天以運動爲德，君自體天居位，《震》雷爲象，豈體天所出？」
entries.en: The crown prince said: "If Heaven's virtue is movement, the ruler bodies forth Heaven in his seat—yet Zhen, Thunder, is the image. How is that the bodying-forth of Heaven?"
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "If Heaven takes motion as its virtue, the ruler himself embodies Heaven in his station—yet Zhen, Thunder, is the image. How can that be what embodies Heaven's emergence?"

entries.zh: 儉曰：「主器者莫若長子，故受之以《震》。
entries.en: Wang Jian said: "He who holds the vessel—none like the eldest son—so he receives Zhen.
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: "He who holds the vessel is none so fit as the eldest son—hence he receives Zhen.

entries.zh: 萬物出乎《震》，故亦帝所與焉。」
entries.en: The ten thousand things come from Zhen—so the Lord's share is there too."
entries.literal: All things emerge from Zhen—thus the Lord's portion lies there as well."

entries.zh: 儉又諮太子曰：「《孝經》『仲尼居，曾子侍』。
entries.en: Wang Jian went on to ask the crown prince: "In the Classic of Filial Piety, 'Confucius was at rest and Zengzi attended.'
entries.literal: Wang Jian further addressed the crown prince: "In the Classic of Filial Piety, 'Confucius was at rest and Zengzi attended him.'

entries.zh: 夫孝理弘深，大賢方盡其致，何故不授顏子，而寄曾生？」
entries.en: Filial piety runs wide and deep; only a great sage can reach its limit. Why not give it to Yan Hui, but lodge it with Master Zeng?"
entries.literal: The principle of filial piety is vast and deep; only a great sage can exhaust its reach. Why was it not given to Yan Hui but entrusted to Master Zeng?"

entries.zh: 太子曰：「曾生雖德慚體二，而色養盡禮，去物尚近，接引非隔，弘宣規教，義在於此。」
entries.en: The crown prince said: "Master Zeng's virtue did not match the Sage in body, yet he nourished his parents' looks to the full of ritual; he was still close to things, with no break in the line—to spread the teaching's rule, the reason is here."
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "Though Master Zeng's virtue fell short of matching the Sage in stature, his nourishing his parents' countenance fulfilled the rites in full; he was still near to things, without a gap in transmission—to spread and proclaim the regulations of the teaching, the point lies here."

entries.zh: 儉曰：「接引非隔，弘宣雖易，去聖轉遠，其事彌輕。
entries.en: Wang Jian said: "No break in the line, and spreading the teaching is easy—but the farther from the Sage, the lighter the thing grows.
entries.literal: Wang Jian said: "Without a gap in transmission, spreading the teaching is easy—but the farther one stands from the Sage, the lighter the matter becomes.

entries.zh: 旣云『人能弘道』，將恐人輕道廢。」
entries.en: It is said, 'Man can enlarge the Way'—I fear men will slight the Way and let it die."
entries.literal: Since it is said 'it is man who enlarges the Way,' I fear men will slight the Way and let it fall into disuse."

entries.zh: 太子曰：「理旣有在，不容以人廢言，而況中賢之才，弘上聖之教，寧有壅塞之嫌？」
entries.en: The crown prince said: "The principle stands—you cannot throw away the words because of the man; and when a middling talent spreads the highest Sage's teaching, is there any fear of blockage?"
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "Since the principle exists, one cannot discard the words because of the man—and when a man of middling talent spreads the teaching of the highest Sage, could there be any suspicion of obstruction?"

entries.zh: 臨川王映諮曰：「孝爲德本，常是所疑。
entries.en: The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, asked: "Filial piety as the root of virtue is often doubted.
entries.literal: The prince of Linchuan, Xiao Ying, addressed him: "Filial piety as the root of virtue is often in doubt.

entries.zh: 德施萬善，孝由天性，自然之理，豈因積習？」
entries.en: Virtue pours into ten thousand goods; filial piety comes from inborn nature—the way of what is so. How could it rest on long practice?"
entries.literal: Virtue extends to ten thousand goods; filial piety springs from inborn nature—it is the law of what is natural. How could it depend on accumulated habit?"

entries.zh: 太子曰：「不因積習而至，所以可爲德本。」
entries.en: The crown prince said: "It is because it is not reached by practice that it can be the root of virtue."
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "Precisely because it is not reached through accumulated habit that it can serve as the root of virtue."

entries.zh: 映曰：「率由斯至，不俟明德，大孝榮親，衆德光備，以此而言，豈得爲本？」
entries.en: Ying said: "Follow this and you arrive without waiting for bright virtue; great filial piety honors kin and every virtue gleams—on that reading, how is it the root?"
entries.literal: Ying said: "Following this one arrives without awaiting bright virtue; great filial piety brings glory to one's parents and all virtues shine complete—for that reason, how can it be called the root?"

entries.zh: 太子曰：「孝有深淺，德有小大，因其分而爲本，何所稍疑？」
entries.en: The crown prince said: "Filial piety has depth and shallowness, virtue has large and small—each takes its measure as root; what is left to doubt?"
entries.literal: The crown prince said: "Filial piety has depth and shallowness, virtue has small and great—taking one's portion as root, what room for doubt remains?"

entries.zh: 太子以長年臨學，亦前代未有也。
entries.en: A crown prince of mature years presiding over the academy was likewise unheard of in earlier times.
entries.literal: That the crown prince in mature years should preside over the academy was likewise without precedent in former ages.

entries.zh: 明年，上將訊丹陽所領囚，及南北二百里內獄，詔曰：「獄訟之重，政化所先。
entries.en: The next year the emperor was to hear cases for prisoners under Danyang and jails within two hundred li north and south, and decreed: "The weight of prison and suit comes first in rule and reform.
entries.literal: The following year the emperor was to review prisoners under Danyang's jurisdiction and jails within two hundred li north and south, and issued an edict: "The weight of imprisonment and litigation comes first in government and transformation.

entries.zh: 太子立年作貳，宜時詳覽，此訊事委以親決。」
entries.en: The crown prince has come to years as second heir; he should look through these in good time—this hearing is entrusted to his own judgment."
entries.literal: The crown prince has reached the years to serve as second to the throne; he should review these matters in timely detail—this review is entrusted to him for personal decision."

entries.zh: 太子乃於玄圃園宣猷堂錄三署囚，原宥各有差。
entries.en: The crown prince then, in the Hall of Proclaimed Teachings in the Mystic Enclosure Garden, entered the prisoners of the three offices and granted pardon each in measure.
entries.literal: The crown prince then, in the Hall of Proclaimed Teachings in the Mystic Enclosure Garden, recorded prisoners from the three offices and granted pardons each according to degree.

entries.zh: 上晚年好游宴，尚書曹事亦分送太子省視。
entries.en: In his later years the emperor loved feasts and tours; Secretariat business was also split off and sent to the crown prince to review.
entries.literal: In his later years the emperor favored feasts and outings; business from the Secretariat offices was also divided and sent to the crown prince for review.

entries.zh: 太子與竟陵王子良俱好釋氏，立六疾館以養窮民。
entries.en: The crown prince and the prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, both favored the Buddhist teaching and founded the Six Diseases Hospices to nourish the poor.
entries.literal: The crown prince and the prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, both favored Buddhism and established the Six Diseases Hospices to care for the destitute.

entries.zh: 風韻甚和而性頗奢麗，宮內殿堂，皆雕飾精綺，過於上宮。
entries.en: His manner was gracious and easy, yet he was extravagant by nature; halls and chambers throughout his palace were carved and hung with fine brocade, outdoing even the emperor's own quarters.
entries.literal: His bearing was very harmonious, yet his nature was rather luxurious; within the palace, every hall and chamber was carved and adorned with fine brocade, surpassing the upper palace.

entries.zh: 開拓玄圃園，與臺城北塹等，其中樓觀塔宇，多聚奇石，妙極山水。
entries.en: He laid out the Mystic Enclosure Garden to rival the capital's north moat; pavilions, belvederes, and pagodas rose among heaps of curious stone, the landscape wrought to a pitch of artifice.
entries.literal: He opened and extended the Mystic Enclosure Garden, equal to the north moat of Jiankang; within it, towers, belvederes, and pagodas gathered many strange stones, achieving landscape to the utmost of wonder.

entries.zh: 慮上宮望見，乃傍門列脩竹，內施高鄣，造游牆數百間，施諸機巧：宜須鄣蔽，須臾成立；
entries.en: Lest the imperial palace look down upon it, he lined the gates with tall bamboo, raised high screens within, and built hundreds of touring wall-panels fitted with clever devices—when a screen was wanted, it rose in an instant;
entries.literal: Fearing the upper palace might see it, he planted tall bamboo beside the gates, set high screens within, and built hundreds of movable wall-sections fitted with every sort of mechanism: when screening was needed, they stood up in a moment;

entries.zh: 若應毀撤，應手遷徙。
entries.en: when they were to come down, they moved aside at a touch.
entries.literal: if they were to be taken down, they shifted away at a touch.

entries.zh: 善制珍玩之物，織孔雀毛爲裘，光彩金翠，過於雉頭矣。
entries.en: He excelled at precious novelties and wove peacock down into robes whose gold-green sheen outshone even zhichidou fur.
entries.literal: He was skilled at making rare curios; he wove peacock feathers into robes whose gold-green brilliance surpassed even zhichidou fur.

entries.zh: 以晉明帝爲太子時立西池，乃啓世祖引前例，求東田起小苑，上許之。
entries.en: Citing the precedent of Jin Emperor Ming's Western Pool when he was heir, he petitioned Shizu to build a small park on the Eastern Fields; the emperor assented.
entries.literal: Because when Emperor Ming of Jin was crown prince he had built the Western Pool, he memorialized Shizu citing that precedent and asked to raise a small park on the Eastern Fields; the emperor granted it.

entries.zh: 永明中，二宮兵力全實，太子使宮中將吏更番役築，宮城苑巷，制度之盛，觀者傾京師。
entries.en: During Yongming, both palaces kept their forces at full strength; the crown prince rotated palace officers through corvée labor on his works—palace wards, parks, and lanes—until the scale of the layout made the whole capital gape.
entries.literal: In the Yongming era, both palaces' military strength stood at full muster; the crown prince had palace officers and clerks take turns on corvée to build—within the palace city, parks and lanes—the splendor of the layout made all Jiankang stare.

entries.zh: 上性雖嚴，多布耳目，太子所爲，無敢啓者。
entries.en: The emperor was stern by nature and kept many informants, yet no one dared speak of what the crown prince was doing.
entries.literal: Though the emperor's nature was severe and he posted many eyes and ears, none dared report what the crown prince did.

entries.zh: 後上幸豫章王宅，還過太子東田，見其彌亘華遠，莊麗極目，於是大怒，收監作主帥；
entries.en: Later the emperor called on the prince of Yuzhang; returning by way of the crown prince's Eastern Fields, he saw splendor stretching without end, gorgeous to the horizon, and in a rage had the project overseers seized and jailed;
entries.literal: Later, when the emperor visited the Prince of Yuzhang's residence and on his return passed the crown prince's Eastern Fields, he saw them sprawling in splendor, magnificent to the horizon, and in great wrath arrested and imprisoned the overseers in charge;

entries.zh: 太子懼，皆藏匿之，由是見責。
entries.en: the crown prince, afraid, hid them all away—and was rebuked for it.
entries.literal: the crown prince, in fear, hid them all away and was rebuked for it.

entries.zh: 先是，梁州刺史范柏年誘降晉壽亡命李烏奴，討平氐賊楊城、蘇道熾等，頗著威名。
entries.en: Earlier Fan Bonian, inspector of Liang, had won over Li Wunu, a Jinshou outlaw, and put down the Di chiefs Yang Cheng and Su Daoshi, until his name carried weight.
entries.literal: Earlier, Fan Bonian, inspector of Liang province, had induced the fugitive Li Wunu of Jinshou to surrender and had crushed the Di bandits Yang Cheng, Su Daoshi, and others, winning considerable renown.

entries.zh: 沈攸之事起，柏年遣將陰廣宗領軍出魏興聲援京師，而候望形勢。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi rose, Bonian sent Yin Guangzong out of Weixing with an army, ostensibly to aid the capital while he read the wind.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi's rebellion arose, Bonian sent his general Yin Guangzong to lead troops out from Weixing to signal support for the capital while watching how events unfolded.

entries.zh: 事平，朝廷遣王玄邈代之。
entries.en: Once the revolt was crushed, the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to relieve him.
entries.literal: When the affair was pacified, the court sent Wang Xuanmiao to replace him.

entries.zh: 烏奴勸柏年據漢中不受命，柏年計未決，玄邈已至，柏年遲回魏興不肯下。
entries.en: Li Wunu urged Bonian to seize Hanzhong and defy the summons. Bonian wavered; Xuanmiao was already on the road, yet Bonian hung back at Weixing and would not descend.
entries.literal: Li Wunu urged Bonian to hold Hanzhong and refuse the order; Bonian had not yet decided when Xuanmiao arrived. Bonian lingered at Weixing and would not come down.

entries.zh: 太子慮其爲變，乃遣說柏年，許啓爲府長史，柏年乃進襄陽，因執誅之。
entries.en: The prince, fearing a mutiny, sent envoys promising to name Bonian chief steward of his staff if he came in. Bonian marched to Xiangyang—and was seized and put to death.
entries.literal: The crown prince, fearing he might rebel, sent someone to persuade Bonian, promising to recommend him as chief steward of the princely establishment. Bonian then advanced to Xiangyang, where he was seized and executed.

entries.zh: 柏年，梓潼人，徙居華陽，世爲土豪，知名州里。
entries.en: Bonian came from Zitong and had settled in Huayang; for generations his clan had been great landlords, famed in the province.
entries.literal: Bonian was a native of Zitong who had moved to live at Huayang; for generations his family had been local magnates, known throughout the province.

entries.zh: 宋泰始中，氐寇斷晉壽道，柏年以倉部郎假節領數百人慰勞通路，自益州道報命。
entries.en: In Song's Taishi era Di raiders severed the Jinshou road. Bonian, then gentleman of the grain bureaus, took the staff and led several hundred men to reopen the route and hearten the garrisons, then returned by the Yizhou road to report.
entries.literal: In the Taishi era of Song, Di raiders cut the road to Jinshou. Bonian, as gentleman of the bureaus of grain, took the staff of authority and led several hundred men to comfort troops and reopen the route, returning by way of Yizhou to report.

entries.zh: 除晉壽太守。
entries.en: He was made administrator of Jinshou.
entries.literal: He was appointed administrator of Jinshou.

entries.zh: 討平氐賊，遂爲梁州。
entries.en: When the Di were pacified he became inspector of Liang.
entries.literal: After he had put down the Di bandits, he became inspector of Liang province.

entries.zh: 柏年強立，善言事，以應對爲宋明帝所知。
entries.en: Bonian was imposing in person and quick in counsel; Emperor Ming of Song prized his repartee.
entries.literal: Bonian was forceful in bearing and skilled in speech; his ready replies won him notice from Emperor Ming of Song.

entries.zh: 旣被誅，巴西太守柳弘稱啓太祖，敕答曰：「柏年幸可不爾，爲之恨恨！」
entries.en: After the execution Liu Hong of Baxi memorialized Xiao Daocheng. The reply read, "Bonian might have been spared this—I grieve for it!"
entries.literal: After he was executed, Liu Hong, administrator of Baxi, submitted a memorial to the Grand Ancestor. The edict in reply read: "It would have been fortunate if Bonian had not come to this; I deeply regret it!"

entries.zh: 初，太子內懷惡明帝，密謂竟陵王子良曰：「我意色中殊不悅此人，當由其福德薄所致。」
entries.en: Earlier the crown prince had secretly loathed Emperor Ming and told the prince of Jingling, Ziliang: "Something in my heart utterly rejects this man—surely his merit is thin."
entries.literal: Earlier, the crown prince inwardly hated Emperor Ming and secretly told the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang: "In my heart I am wholly displeased with this man—it must be because his fortune is thin."

entries.zh: 子良便苦救解。
entries.en: Ziliang then begged hard that he be spared.
entries.literal: Ziliang then pleaded earnestly to spare him.

entries.zh: 後明帝立，果大相誅害。
entries.en: Later, when Emperor Ming acceded, he did indeed kill on a vast scale.
entries.literal: Later, when Emperor Ming took the throne, he indeed slaughtered many on a great scale.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：上古之世，父不哭子。
entries.en: The historian writes: In high antiquity a father did not mourn his son.
entries.literal: The historian writes: In high antiquity, a father did not weep for his son.

entries.zh: 壽夭悠悠，尚嗟恆事。
entries.en: Life long or short drifts on—yet even that men still mourn as the common way.
entries.literal: Long or short, life drifts on—yet even that we still lament as the common lot.

entries.zh: 況夫正體東儲，方樹年德；
entries.en: How much more when the rightful heir in the Eastern Palace was only beginning to grow in years and virtue;
entries.literal: How much more the legitimate heir in the Eastern Palace, just setting out his years and virtue;

entries.zh: 重基累葉，載茂皇家；
entries.en: foundation laid generation on generation, glory heaped on the royal line;
entries.literal: a foundation laid through generations, glory heaped on the imperial house;

entries.zh: 守器之君，已知耕稼，雖溫文具美，交弘盛迹，武運將終，先期夙殞，傳之幼少，以速顛危。
entries.en: an heir who already knew the plough—though his gentle learning was full and he shared in a flourishing age, the martial fortune was ending, he died before his season, and rule passed to a child, hastening collapse.
entries.literal: a lord who guarded the vessel and already knew the plough—though gentle learning and letters were complete, and he joined in spreading a great record, the martial fortune was near its end, he perished early before his time, and the succession passed to the young, hastening ruin.

entries.zh: 推此而論，亦有冥數矣。
entries.en: Reasoned thus far, there is doom in the unseen too.
entries.literal: Pushed to this conclusion, there is fate in the dark as well.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷二十一‧列傳第二
entries.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 21 — Biographies 2
entries.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 21 — Biographies 2

entries.zh: 蒼梧酷暴稍甚，太祖與淵及袁粲言世事，粲曰：「主上幼年微過易改，伊、霍之事，非季代所行，縱使功成，亦終無全地。」
entries.en: Cangwu's cruelty grew sharper; the Grand Ancestor spoke with Yuan and Yuan Can about affairs of state; Can said: "The sovereign is young; small faults are easy to mend; deeds like Yi Yin and Huo Guang belong to a fallen age—even if they succeeded, in the end there would be no safe footing for you."
entries.literal: Cangwu's cruelty and violence grew somewhat worse; the Grand Ancestor spoke with Yuan and Yuan Can about affairs of state; Can said: "The sovereign is young; minor faults are easy to amend; affairs like Yi Yin and Huo Guang are not for an age's decline—even if they succeeded, in the end there would be no safe footing."

entries.zh: 淵默然，歸心太祖。
entries.en: Yuan was silent; his heart turned to the Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: Yuan was silent; his heart turned to the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 及廢蒼梧，羣公集議，袁粲、劉秉旣不受任，淵曰：「非蕭公無以了此。」
entries.en: When Cangwu was deposed the lords assembled in counsel; Yuan Can and Liu Bing had already refused office; Yuan said: "Without Duke Xiao this cannot be brought to an end."
entries.literal: When Cangwu was deposed the assembled lords deliberated; Yuan Can and Liu Bing had already refused office; Yuan said: "Without Duke Xiao this cannot be brought to conclusion."

entries.zh: 手取書授太祖。
entries.en: He took the document in hand and gave it to the Grand Ancestor.
entries.literal: He took the document by hand and handed it to the Grand Ancestor.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「相與不肯，我安得辭！」
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor said: "When you all refuse, how can I decline!"
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor said: "When you all refuse, how can I decline!"

entries.zh: 事乃定。
entries.en: The matter was thereby settled.
entries.literal: The matter was thereby settled.

entries.zh: 順帝立，改號衞將軍、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Shun was enthroned, Yuan was made general of the guard, bearer of the staff equal to the Three Excellencies; palace attendant unchanged.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shun was enthroned, Yuan's title was changed to general of the guard, bearer of the staff equal to the Three Excellencies; palace attendant unchanged.

entries.zh: 甲仗五十人入殿。
entries.en: Fifty suit-armed attendants entered the palace hall with him.
entries.literal: Fifty suit-armed attendants entered the palace hall with him.

entries.zh: 頃之寢疾。
entries.en: Before long he fell gravely ill.
entries.literal: Before long he took to his bed with illness.

entries.zh: 上相星連有變，淵憂之，表遜位。
entries.en: The Superior Minister star showed linked disturbances; troubled, Yuan memorialized to yield his post.
entries.literal: The Superior Minister star showed linked changes; Yuan was troubled and memorialized to yield his post.

entries.zh: 又因王儉及侍中王晏口陳於世祖，世祖不許。
entries.en: He also had Wang Jian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan plead in person before Shizu; Shizu refused.
entries.literal: He also had Wang Jian and Palace Attendant Wang Yan speak orally before Shizu; Shizu did not consent.

entries.zh: 又啓曰：「臣顧惟凡薄，福過災生，未能以正情自安，遠慚彥輔。
entries.en: He wrote again: "Your servant knows himself common and slight—favor has outstripped desert and trouble follows; I cannot quiet my heart in truth and am ashamed before worthy counselors.
entries.literal: He memorialized again, saying, "Your servant reflects on his common mediocrity—blessing has outrun merit and calamity is born; unable to settle his heart in rectitude, far ashamed before worthy counselors.

entries.zh: 旣內懷耿介，便覺晷刻難推。
entries.en: Outward duty sits ill on an inward stiffness; hour by hour drags.
entries.literal: Inwardly unyielding, each instant becomes hard to bear.

entries.zh: 叨職未久，首歲便嬰疾篤，爾來沈痼，頻經危殆，彌深憂震。
entries.en: I have not long held office; in the first year I was stricken gravely ill; since then lingering sickness, again and again at death's door, and dread only deepens.
entries.literal: Your servant bore office not long; in the first year he fell gravely ill; since then chronic ailments, passing danger again and again, worry and dread ever deeper.

entries.zh: 陛下曲存遲回，或謂僉議同異，此出於留慈每過，愛欲其榮。
entries.en: Your Majesty has indulged my delay, or some will say the councils are divided—but this is only excess of kindness, love wishing me honor I do not merit.
entries.literal: Your Majesty bent to allow delay; some say the collective deliberations differ—this comes from lingering affection exceeding measure, love wishing him honor.

entries.zh: 臣年四十有八，叨忝若此，以疾陳遜，豈駭聽察。
entries.en: At forty-eight, with honors heaped on me, to plead illness and withdraw—would that shock your ears?
entries.literal: Your servant is forty-eight, bearing such honor at fault; to cite illness and yield—is that to startle imperial hearing?

entries.zh: 總錄之任，江左罕授，上隣亞台，升降蓋微。
entries.en: The overall Recordership is rarely granted in our age; its holder stands next to the Secretariat itself, and between rise and fall there is little distance.
entries.literal: The charge of overall recording is rarely granted south of the Yangtze; it borders the secondary terrace, promotion and demotion scarcely distinct.

entries.zh: 今受祿弗辭，退絀斯願，於臣名器，非曰貶少，萬物耳目，皎然共見，寧足仰延聖慮，稍垂矜惜。
entries.en: To keep the stipend and refuse to step down, to choke off this request—for my name and rank that is no real demotion; every eye under heaven sees it plain. Why should it draw your concern or the least pity?
entries.literal: Now to accept salary without declining, to withdraw and cut short this wish—for your servant's name and rank it is not called a belittling reduction; all eyes under heaven see it clearly—how could it merit extending imperial concern or slight pity?

entries.zh: 臣若內飾廉譽，外循謙後，此則憲書行劾，刑綱是肅。
entries.en: If I papered myself with a show of integrity while playing at humility, the statutes would impeach me and the law would tighten its net.
entries.literal: If your servant adorned himself inwardly with reputation for integrity and outwardly followed humility, then the statutes would move to impeachment and the penal net would be tightened.

entries.zh: 臣赤誠不能行，亦幽明所不宥。
entries.en: My naked heart cannot do that; neither the living nor the dead would forgive it.
entries.literal: Your servant's naked sincerity cannot perform that; neither the visible nor invisible worlds would pardon it.

entries.zh: 區區寸心，歸啓以實。
entries.en: In this inch of heart I lay the truth before you.
entries.literal: This paltry inch of heart returns to declare in truth.

entries.zh: 自吝寸陰，寔願方倍堯世。
entries.en: Grudging every inch of daylight, I would only wish to serve twice the years of Yao's age.
entries.literal: Cherishing each inch of shadow, truly wishing to match doubled the era of Yao.

entries.zh: 昔王弘固請，乃於司徒爲衞將軍，宋氏行之不疑，當時物無異議，以臣方之，曾何足說。
entries.en: Wang Hong once pressed his plea and was made Defender-General under the Minister of Works; the Song court granted it without a murmur. Set beside me, what is my case worth speaking of?
entries.literal: Formerly Wang Hong firmly petitioned and became Defender-General under the Minister of Works; the Song house did it without doubt and none objected—compared with your servant, how could words suffice?

entries.zh: 伏願恢闡宏猷，賜開亭造，則臣死之日，猶生之年。」
entries.en: I beg you to widen your great design and grant me leave; then the day I die would still count as a day I lived."
entries.literal: Bowing head, hoping to broaden great design, grant opening and release—then the day of your servant's death would still be as a day of life."

entries.zh: 乃改授司空，領驃騎將軍，侍中、錄尚書如故。
entries.en: He was then reassigned Minister of Works, retaining Supernal General, Palace Attendant, and Recorder as before.
entries.literal: He was then reassigned Minister of Works, with Supernal General, Palace Attendant and Recorder unchanged.

entries.zh: 上遣侍中王晏黃門郎王秀之問疾。
entries.en: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Wang Yan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Xiuzhi to ask after his health.
entries.literal: The emperor sent Palace Attendant Wang Yan and Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Xiuzhi to inquire after his illness.

entries.zh: 薨，家無餘財，負債至數十萬。
entries.en: He died; the family left no surplus, and debts ran into the hundreds of thousands.
entries.literal: He died; the household had no surplus wealth, debts running to hundreds of thousands.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「司徒奄至薨逝，痛怛慟懷，比雖尪瘵，便力出臨哭。
entries.en: An edict read, "The Minister of Works has suddenly died; grief wounds the heart. Though lately I have been ill and frail, I went myself to mourn at his bier.
entries.literal: An edict said, "The Minister of Works suddenly reached death's end; grief and anguish pierce the heart. Though lately wasting ill, I went in person to mourn at his bier.

entries.zh: 給東園祕器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢二十萬，布二百疋，蠟二百斤。」
entries.en: Grant eastern-garden funerary coffinware, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, two hundred thousand in cash, two hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred jin of wax."
entries.literal: Granted eastern garden secret coffinware, one set court robes, one suit of clothing, two hundred thousand cash, two hundred bolts cloth, two hundred jin wax."

entries.zh: 其年疾，上親臨視，薨，年三十八。
entries.en: That year he sickened; the emperor came in person to his bedside. He died at thirty-eight.
entries.literal: That year he fell ill; the emperor personally visited him. He died, aged thirty-eight.

entries.zh: 吏部尚書王晏啓及儉喪，上答曰：「儉年德富盛，志用方隆，豈意暴疾，不展救護，便爲異世，奄忽如此，痛酷彌深。
entries.en: Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel, wrote on Jian's death. The emperor answered: "Jian's years and virtue stood at their height, his will and work just ascending—who could have thought a sudden sickness, with no room for cure, would cast him so quickly into another world? The pain cuts unbearably deep.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, Minister of the Masters of Personnel, memorialized on Jian's death. The emperor replied, "Jian's years and virtue were in fullest flower, his ambition and use just rising—who could have thought a sudden illness, with no scope for healing, would place him in another world so abruptly? The pain is unbearably deep.

entries.zh: 其契闊艱運，義重常懷，言尋悲切，不能自勝。
entries.en: His shared trials through hard times, the weight of right feeling I always bore—to speak of it is grief I cannot hold in.
entries.literal: His trials through hard fates, his constant weight of right feeling—to speak of them is grief that cuts; I cannot master myself.

entries.zh: 痛矣奈何！
entries.en: Pain—what can be done!
entries.literal: Pain—what can be done!

entries.zh: 往矣奈何！」
entries.en: Gone—what can be done!"
entries.literal: Gone—what can be done!"

entries.zh: 詔衞軍文武及臺所兵仗可悉停待葬。
entries.en: An edict ordered all civil and military staff of the Guard General and all arms of the central offices to stand idle until the burial.
entries.literal: Edict: All civil and military officers of the Guard General and all central-office arms and equipment shall halt until the burial.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：褚淵、袁粲，俱受宋明帝顧託，粲旣死節於宋氏，而淵逢興運，世之非責淵者衆矣。
entries.en: The historian writes: Chu Yuan and Yuan Can both received Emperor Ming of Song's deathbed charge. Can died in loyalty to the Song house; Yuan met the rising fortune—and the world has been quick to blame him.
entries.literal: The historian writes: Chu Yuan and Yuan Can both received Emperor Ming of Song's deathbed entrustment. Can already died in loyalty for the Song house, while Yuan met the rising fortune—many in the world blame Yuan.

entries.zh: 臣請論之：夫湯、武之迹，異乎堯、舜，伊、呂之心，亦非稷、契。
entries.en: Let me argue the point: Tang and Wu walked a different path from Yao and Shun; the hearts of Yi Yin and Tai Gong were not those of Hou Ji and Qi.
entries.literal: Your subject begs to discuss it: The tracks of Tang and Wu differ from those of Yao and Shun; the hearts of Yi Yin and Tai Gong are not those of Hou Ji and Qi.

entries.zh: 降此風規，未足爲證也。
entries.en: To judge by that lower measure of conduct is no fair ground for blame.
entries.literal: To lower this standard of conduct is not enough to serve as proof.

entries.zh: 自金、張世族，袁、楊鼎貴，委質服義，皆由漢氏，膏腴見重，事起於斯。
entries.en: From the Jin and Zhang lines, the Yuan and Yang houses at the summit of rank—each pledged service and loyalty under the Han; fertile estates were prized, and the custom took root there.
entries.literal: From the Jin and Zhang great clans, Yuan and Yang at the height of honor—all submitted in loyalty through the Han house; fertile domains won esteem, and the matter began there.

entries.zh: 魏氏君臨，年祚短促，服褐前代，宦成後朝。
entries.en: When Wei held the throne its years were few; men still wore the brown of the former house even as they finished their careers under the court that followed.
entries.literal: When Wei ruled, its reign was brief; they wore coarse cloth for the former dynasty and won office under the later court.

entries.zh: 晉氏登庸，與之從事，名雖魏臣，實爲晉有，故主位雖改，臣任如初。
entries.en: When Jin took the throne they went on in its service; on paper they were Wei's ministers, in truth they were Jin's men—so though the ruler changed, the minister's post stayed the same.
entries.literal: When the Jin house ascended to office, they went on in its service; though in name they were ministers of Wei, in fact they belonged to Jin—so though the sovereign's seat changed, a minister's charge remained as before.

entries.zh: 自是世祿之盛，習爲舊準，羽儀所隆，人懷羨慕，君臣之節，徒致虛名。
entries.en: Hereditary wealth became the fixed pattern; men coveted whatever the panoply exalted—loyalty between lord and minister was loyalty in name only.
entries.literal: From this the splendor of hereditary stipends became the old standard; what regalia honored, men envied—the bond of lord and minister was reduced to an empty name.

entries.zh: 貴仕素資，皆由門慶，平流進取，坐至公卿，則知殉國之感無因，保家之念宜切。
entries.en: Rank came from pedigree; riding the ordinary tide of promotion, men took their seats among the Three Dukes without stir—so zeal to die for the state had no foothold, and guarding the clan should have weighed more.
entries.literal: Qualifications for high office all rested on family glory; riding the common stream of advancement, one sat till he reached minister or grandee—thus one sees there was no ground for dying for the state, and the wish to preserve the clan ought to have been keen.

entries.zh: 市朝亟革，寵貴方來，陵闕雖殊，顧眄如一。
entries.en: Thrones turned over fast; new favor and new dignity arrived—though dynastic tombs and palaces changed, the look cast backward was the same.
entries.literal: Court and market changed again and again; favor and rank newly arrived; though tombs and palaces differed, the backward glance was still one.

entries.zh: 中行、智伯，未有異遇。
entries.en: Even Zhonghang and Zhibo would have found no special treatment.
entries.literal: Not even Zhonghang or Zhibo received different treatment.

entries.zh: 褚淵當泰始初運，清塗已顯，數年之閒，不患無位，旣以民望而見引，亦隨民望而去之。
entries.en: Chu Yuan at the rise of Taishi was already on a bright track; within a few years he need not fear lacking a post—lifted by public renown, he also left as public renown turned.
entries.literal: Chu Yuan, at the opening of the Taishi fortune, already stood on a clear path; within a few years he need not fear lacking office—brought forward by popular acclaim, he also withdrew as popular acclaim willed.

entries.zh: 夫爵祿旣輕，有國常選，恩非己獨，責人以死，斯故人主之所同謬，世情之過差也。
entries.en: When titles and stipends weigh little and the realm chooses by rule, when the grace is not his alone yet men are asked to die for it—that is a mistake rulers commonly make and a bias the age runs to.
entries.literal: When rank and stipend are already light, the state has its regular choice; favor is not his alone—yet men are charged to die for it. This is a common error of rulers and an excess of the age's sentiment.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷二十三‧列傳第四
entries.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 23 — Biographies 4
entries.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 23 — Biographies 4

entries.zh: 尋爲晉熙王安西司馬，加寧朔將軍。
entries.en: Soon after he was chief of staff on Prince of Jinxi's pacifying-west staff, with the additional rank general who pacifies the north.
entries.literal: Soon after he was made chief of staff on the pacifying-west staff of Prince of Jinxi, with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.

entries.zh: 時世祖爲長史，與世隆相遇甚懽。
entries.en: Shizu was then chief of staff; he and Shilong took to each other at once.
entries.literal: At that time Shizu was chief of staff, and he and Shilong met with great mutual delight.

entries.zh: 太祖之謀渡廣陵也，令世祖率衆下，同會京邑，世隆與長流蕭景先等戒嚴待期，事不行。
entries.en: When the Grand Ancestor plotted a crossing at Guangling, he told Shizu to bring the army downriver to the capital; Shilong, with Xiao Xianxian and other senior commanders, stood to arms for the appointed day—but the scheme came to nothing.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor planned to cross to Guangling, he ordered Shizu to lead troops downstream to meet at the capital; Shilong, with the senior commander Xiao Xianxian and others, stood to arms awaiting the day—but the plan was not carried out.

entries.zh: 冬，攸之反，遣輔國將軍中兵參軍孫同、寧朔將軍中兵參軍武寶、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍朱君拔、寧朔將軍沈惠眞、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍王道起三萬人爲前驅，又遣司馬冠軍劉攘兵領寧朔將軍外兵參軍公孫方平、龍驤將軍騎兵參軍朱靈眞、沈僧敬、龍驤將軍高茂二萬人次之，又遣輔國將軍王靈秀、丁珍東、寧朔將軍中兵參軍王彌之、寧朔將軍外兵參軍楊景穆二千匹騎分兵出夏口，據魯山。
entries.en: That winter Youzhi rose in revolt. He sent Sun Tong, pacifying state general and central corps staff officer; Wu Bao, pacifying north general and central corps staff officer; Zhu Junba, flying dragon general and cavalry corps staff officer; Shen Huizhen, pacifying north general; and Wang Daoqi, flying dragon general and cavalry corps staff officer—with thirty thousand men as vanguard. He sent champion marshal Liu Rangbing at the head of Gongsun Fangping, pacifying north general and outer corps staff officer; Zhu Lingzhen and Shen Sengjing, flying dragon generals and cavalry corps staff officers; and Gao Mao, flying dragon general—with twenty thousand in the second wave. He sent pacifying state general Wang Lingxiu, Ding Zhendong, pacifying north general and central corps staff officer Wang Mizhi, and pacifying north general and outer corps staff officer Yang Jingmu with two thousand horse to split from Xiakou and hold Lushan.
entries.literal: In winter Youzhi rebelled. He sent Pacifying State General and central corps staff officer Sun Tong, Pacifying North General and central corps staff officer Wu Bao, Flying Dragon General and cavalry corps staff officer Zhu Junba, Pacifying North General Shen Huizhen, and Flying Dragon General and cavalry corps staff officer Wang Daoqi—thirty thousand men as vanguard. He also sent Champion Marshal Liu Rangbing leading Pacifying North General and outer corps staff officer Gongsun Fangping, Flying Dragon General and cavalry corps staff officers Zhu Lingzhen and Shen Sengjing, and Flying Dragon General Gao Mao—twenty thousand as the second echelon. He further sent Pacifying State General Wang Lingxiu, Ding Zhendong, Pacifying North General and central corps staff officer Wang Mizhi, and Pacifying North General and outer corps staff officer Yang Jingmu with two thousand horse to divide forces out from Xiakou and seize Lushan.

entries.zh: 攸之乘輕舸從數百人先大軍下住白螺洲，坐胡牀以望其軍，有自驕色。
entries.en: Youzhi went ahead in a light boat with a few hundred men, moored at White Snail Islet before the main host, and sat on a camp chair to watch his army—plainly pleased with himself.
entries.literal: Youzhi took a light boat with several hundred men and went ahead of the main army to moor at White Snail Islet; he sat on a folding camp chair to watch his troops, with a look of self-satisfaction.

entries.zh: 旣至郢，以郢城弱小不足攻，遣人告世隆曰：「被太后令，當蹔還都。
entries.en: At Ying he thought the town too small and weak to bother with; he sent word to Shilong: "The empress dowager has ordered me to return to the capital for the moment.
entries.literal: When he reached Ying he judged the city small and weak and not worth attacking; he sent a man to tell Shilong: 「By the empress dowager's order I am to return to the capital for a time.

entries.zh: 卿旣相與奉國，想得此意。」
entries.en: You serve the realm as I do—you will surely take my meaning."
entries.literal: You, who serve the state with me, will surely grasp my meaning.」

entries.zh: 世隆使人答曰：「東下之師，久承聲問。
entries.en: Shilong answered: "We have long had word of your host coming east.
entries.literal: Shilong sent a reply: 「Your army marching east has long been heard of.

entries.zh: 郢城小鎮，自守而已。」
entries.en: This little fortress of Ying can only defend itself."
entries.literal: This little town of Ying can only hold itself.」

entries.zh: 攸之將去，世隆遣軍於西渚挑戰，攸之果怒，令諸軍登岸燒郭邑，築長圍攻道，顧謂人曰：「以此攻城，何城不剋！」
entries.en: When Youzhi was ready to go, Shilong provoked a fight at the western crossing; Youzhi flew into a rage, had his men land and burn the outer town, threw up a long siege line, and told his officers: "With this way of war, what wall will not fall!"
entries.literal: As Youzhi was about to leave, Shilong sent troops to challenge him at the western ford; Youzhi grew angry as expected, ordered his armies ashore to burn the suburbs, built a long encirclement and assault works, and said to those about him: 「With this we take cities—what city would not fall!」

entries.zh: 晝夜攻戰，世隆隨宜拒應，衆皆披却。
entries.en: They attacked day and night; Shilong answered each thrust as the moment required, and the enemy was beaten back again and again.
entries.literal: Day and night they fought; Shilong met each move as needed, and the assailants were driven back on every side.

entries.zh: 世祖初下，與世隆別，曰：「攸之一旦爲變，焚夏口舟艦沿流而東，則坐守空城，不可制也。
entries.en: When Shizu first marched downstream he took leave of Shilong and said: "If Youzhi turns rebel at once, burns the fleet at Xiakou, and drifts east on the current, you will sit in an empty city with no hold on him.
entries.literal: When Shizu first went downstream he parted from Shilong and said: 「If Youzhi should suddenly turn traitor, burn the ships at Xiakou and drift east with the current, you would sit in an empty city and be beyond control.

entries.zh: 雖留攻城，不可卒拔。
entries.en: Even if he stays to besiege you, he cannot storm it in a day.
entries.literal: Even if he stays to besiege you, he cannot take the place at a stroke.

entries.zh: 卿爲其內，我爲其外，乃無憂耳。」
entries.en: You inside and I outside—then we need not worry."
entries.literal: You hold the inside and I the outside—then there is nothing to fear.」

entries.zh: 至是世祖遣軍主桓敬、陳胤叔、苟元賔等八軍據西塞，令堅壁以待賊疲。
entries.en: Now Shizu sent Huan Jing, Chen Yingshu, Gou Yuanbin, and other commanders with eight armies to hold the western forts, with orders to stand behind strong walls until the rebels were spent.
entries.literal: Now Shizu sent the army commanders Huan Jing, Chen Yingshu, Gou Yuanbin, and others with eight armies to hold the western passes, ordering them to strengthen their walls and wait until the rebels were worn down.

entries.zh: 慮世隆危急，遣腹心胡元直潛使入郢城通援軍消息，內外竝喜。
entries.en: Afraid Shilong was hard pressed, he sent his intimate Hu Yuanzhi secretly into Ying with news of the relief force; city and camp alike took heart.
entries.literal: Fearing Shilong was in peril, he sent his trusted man Hu Yuanzhi in secret into Ying to carry word of the relief armies; inside and outside alike rejoiced.

entries.zh: 尚書符曰：
entries.en: The ministry dispatch reads:
entries.literal: A dispatch from the Masters of Writing reads:

entries.zh: 是時朝廷疑憚沈攸之，密爲之防，府州器械，皆有素蓄。
entries.en: The court then feared Shen Youzhi and quietly braced against him; arms and gear were stockpiled in every prefecture and province.
entries.literal: At that time the court feared Shen Youzhi and secretly made preparations against him; every prefecture and province had long stored arms and equipment.

entries.zh: 世祖將下都，劉懷珍白太祖曰：「夏口是兵衝要地，宜得其人。」
entries.en: As Shizu prepared to go to the capital, Liu Huaizhen said to the Grand Ancestor: "Xiakou is the hinge of the armies; the man there must be the right one."
entries.literal: When Shizu was about to go down to the capital, Liu Huaizhen told the Grand Ancestor: 「Xiakou is a military choke point; it needs the right man.」

entries.zh: 太祖納之，與世祖書曰：「汝旣入朝，當須文武兼資人與汝意合者，委以後事，世隆其人也。」
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor agreed and wrote to Shizu: "When you come to court you will need someone who unites civil and martial gifts and thinks as you do, to leave affairs in his hands—and that is Shilong."
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor accepted this and wrote to Shizu: 「Once you enter court you will need a man of both civil and martial gifts whose mind matches yours, to entrust with what follows—and that man is Shilong.」

entries.zh: 世祖舉世隆自代。
entries.en: Shizu put Shilong forward in his own place.
entries.literal: Shizu nominated Shilong to replace himself.

entries.zh: 轉爲武陵王前軍長史、江夏內史、行郢州事。
entries.en: He was made chief of staff on Prince of Wuling's vanguard staff, interior minister of Jiangxia, and acting inspector of Ying.
entries.literal: He was transferred to chief of staff on the vanguard staff of Prince of Wuling, Interior Minister of Jiangxia, and acting Inspector of Ying province.

entries.zh: 柳世隆字彥緒，河東解人也。
entries.en: Liu Shilong, styled Yanxu, was a man of Jie in Hedong.
entries.literal: Liu Shilong, styled Yanxu, was a native of Jie in Hedong.

entries.zh: 祖憑，馮翊太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Ping had been administrator of Fengyi.
entries.literal: His grandfather Ping was Administrator of Fengyi.

entries.zh: 父叔宗，早卒。
entries.en: His father Shuzong died young.
entries.literal: His father Shuzong died young.

entries.zh: :　　沈攸之出自壟畝，寂寥累世。
entries.en: Shen Youzhi came up from the plowlands; his line had been obscure for generations.
entries.literal: Shen Youzhi rose from the fields; for generations his house was obscure.

entries.zh: 故司空沈公，以從父宗廕，愛之若子，羽翼吹噓，得昇官次。
entries.en: The late minister of works Lord Shen took him in under a kinsman's wing and loved him as a son; favored and pushed forward, he rose rung by rung in office.
entries.literal: The late Minister of Works Lord Shen, taking him into the clan shelter of a paternal uncle, loved him as a son; with wings spread and breath behind him, he climbed the ladder of office.

entries.zh: 景和昏悖，猜畏柱臣，而攸之凶忍，趣利樂禍，請銜詔旨，躬行反噬。
entries.en: Jinghe was mad and cruel, fearful of his great ministers; Youzhi was savage and greedy, eager for gain and glad of ruin—he begged the edict and with his own hand turned on the man who had raised him.
entries.literal: Jinghe was benighted and perverse, suspicious of the pillar ministers; Youzhi was fierce and cruel, greedy for profit and glad of disaster—he asked to bear the imperial command and himself turned to bite his benefactor.

entries.zh: 又攸之與譚金、童泰壹等暴寵狂朝，竝爲心膂，同功共體，世號「三侯」。
entries.en: Youzhi, Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and others had been wildly favored in that deranged court; they were heart and sinew together, one body in merit—the age named them the "Three Marquises."
entries.literal: Again, Youzhi with Tan Jin, Tong Taiyi, and others were violently favored in that frantic court; together they were heart and backbone, sharing merit and one body—the age called them the 「Three Marquises.」

entries.zh: 當時親昵，情過管、鮑，仰遭革運，凶黨懼戮，攸之反善圖全，用得自免。
entries.en: Their bond then outdid Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya; when the throne changed, the guilty feared the axe, and Youzhi turned every trick to save himself and walked away.
entries.literal: In those days their intimacy surpassed Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya; then the revolution came, the wicked feared execution, and Youzhi turned to schemes of self-preservation and so slipped free.

entries.zh: 旣殺從父，又虐良朋，雖呂布販君，酈寄賣友，方之斯人，未足爲酷。
entries.en: He killed a kinsman and tormented true friends; Lü Bu who sold his ruler and Li Ji who sold his friend—beside this man they hardly count as cruel.
entries.literal: He had already killed a paternal uncle and abused good friends; though Lü Bu sold out his lord and Li Ji betrayed his friend, set beside this man they are not cruel enough.

entries.zh: 泰始開闢，網漏吞舟，略其凶險，取其搏噬，故階亂獲全，因禍興福。
entries.en: At the opening of Taishi the law forgave the great offender; his violence was passed over and only his teeth were used—so he rose whole from rebellion and made calamity his ladder:
entries.literal: When Taishi opened the reign, the net let the great fish pass; his ferocity was overlooked and only his bite was taken—so he climbed through chaos unscathed and turned disaster into fortune:

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: When Shizu took the throne, Shilong was made Supernumerary Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, Shilong was made Supernumerary Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 世隆善卜，別龜甲，價至一萬。
entries.en: Shilong was skilled at divination; for a choice tortoise carapace he would pay as much as ten thousand cash.
entries.literal: Shilong was skilled at divination; for special turtle shells he paid up to ten thousand.

entries.zh: 永明建號，世隆題州齋壁曰「永明十一年」。
entries.en: When the Yongming reign title was proclaimed, Shilong inscribed the wall of his prefectural study with the words "the eleventh year of Yongming."
entries.literal: When the Yongming reign title was proclaimed, Shilong wrote on the wall of his prefectural study, "the eleventh year of Yongming."

entries.zh: 謂典籤李黨曰：「我不見也。」
entries.en: He told the registry clerk Li Dang, "I shall not live to see it."
entries.literal: He told the registry clerk Li Dang, 「I shall not live to see it.」

entries.zh: 入爲侍中、護軍將軍，遷尚書右僕射，領太子右率，雍州大中正，不拜，改授散騎常侍，尚書左僕射，中正如故。
entries.en: He entered court as Palace Attendant and Defender-General, was moved to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and was also named Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Chief Rectifier of Yong Province. He declined, and was instead made Supernumerary Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with Chief Rectifier unchanged.
entries.literal: He entered court as Palace Attendant and Defender-General, was moved to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and concurrently served as Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Guard and Chief Rectifier of Yong Province; he did not accept, and was reassigned Supernumerary Palace Attendant and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, retaining Chief Rectifier as before.

entries.zh: 九年，卒，時年五十。
entries.en: In the ninth year he died, at the age of fifty.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he died, aged fifty.

entries.zh: 詔給東園祕器，朝服一具，衣一襲，錢一十万，布三百匹，蠟三百斤。
entries.en: An edict granted him Eastern Garden funeral regalia, a full set of court robes, one suit of garments, a hundred thousand cash, three hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax.
entries.literal: An edict granted Eastern Garden secret rites regalia, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, a hundred thousand coins, three hundred bolts of cloth, and three hundred jin of wax.

entries.zh: 又詔曰：「故侍中左光祿大夫貞陽公世隆，秉德居業，才兼經緯。
entries.en: Another edict read: "The late Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, bore virtue in his work and joined talent to the warp and woof of rule.
entries.literal: Another edict said: 「The late Palace Attendant, Left Household Grandee, Duke of Zhenyang Shilong, upheld virtue in his station and united talent with statecraft.

entries.zh: 少播清徽，長弘美譽。
entries.en: In youth he cast a clear name abroad; in his prime he widened a fair renown.
entries.literal: In youth he spread a clear repute; in maturity he enlarged a fair renown.

entries.zh: 入參內禁，出贊西牧，專寄郢郊，剋挫巨猾，超越前勳，功著一代。
entries.en: Within he served the inner palace; without he aided the western governor; left alone to hold the approaches to Ying, he broke a great villain, outdid former merit, and fixed his fame for a generation.
entries.literal: Within he served the inner palace; without he aided the western governor; entrusted alone with the approaches to Ying, he crushed a great villain, surpassing earlier merit, his achievement marked for a generation.

entries.zh: 及總任方州，民頌寬德，翼教崇闥，朝稱元正。
entries.en: When he held a whole province, the people sang of his gentle rule; at the high gates he helped shape the teaching, and the court hailed him as the court's standard.
entries.literal: When he bore overall charge of a province, the people praised his lenient virtue; at the lofty gates he aided instruction, and the court called him the chief rectifier.

entries.zh: 忠謨嘉猷，簡于朕心，雅志素履，邈不可踰。
entries.en: His loyal counsel and fine designs were plain to Our heart; his high purpose and plain walk were beyond reach.
entries.literal: Loyal counsels and fine plans were plain to Our heart; his lofty aim and plain conduct were beyond surpassing.

entries.zh: 將登鉉味，用燮鴻化，奄至薨殞，震慟良深。
entries.en: He was on the verge of tasting the cauldron of state and harmonizing the great transformation, when death came suddenly—Our grief is very deep.
entries.literal: He was about to mount to the seasoning of state and harmonize the great transformation, when suddenly he passed—Our shock is very deep.

entries.zh: 贈司空，班劔三十人，鼓吹一部，侍中如故。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Palace Attendant as before.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Works, with thirty halberd-bearers, one suite of ceremonial music, and Palace Attendant as before.

entries.zh: 諡曰忠武。」
entries.en: His posthumous name was Zhongwu."
entries.literal: His posthumous name was Zhongwu.」

entries.zh: 上又敕吏部尚書王晏曰：「世隆雖抱疾積歲，志氣未衰，冀醫藥有效，痊差可期。
entries.en: The emperor again instructed Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel: "Though Shilong had been ill for years, his spirit had not waned; We hoped the physicians would prevail and recovery was still in sight.
entries.literal: The emperor again instructed Wang Yan, Minister of Personnel: 「Though Shilong bore illness for years, his spirit had not flagged; We hoped medicine would avail and recovery might be expected.

entries.zh: 不謂一旦便爲異世，痛怛之深，此何可言。
entries.en: We never thought that in a single morning he would pass to another world—the depth of pain is beyond words.
entries.literal: We did not think he would in a single morning pass to another world—the depth of anguish is beyond words.

entries.zh: 其昔在郢，誠心夙悃，全保一蕃，勳業克著。
entries.en: Long ago at Ying he showed old and earnest loyalty and kept a whole frontier safe; his merit stood clear.
entries.literal: Formerly at Ying he had long shown sincere devotion and wholly preserved the frontier; his merit stood clear.

entries.zh: 尋准契闊，增泣悲咽。
entries.en: Now, to Our sorrow, We must part again, and Our weeping only deepens.
entries.literal: Now, to Our sorrow, We part again, and Our weeping redoubles.

entries.zh: 卿同在情，亦當無已已耶！」
entries.en: You share this bond—surely your grief knows no end either!"
entries.literal: You share this feeling—surely your grief has no end either!」

entries.zh: 張瓌，字祖逸，吳郡吳人也。
entries.en: Zhang Gui, styled Zuyi, came from Wu in Wu Commandery.
entries.literal: Zhang Gui, styled Zuyi, was a man of Wu Commandery, Wu.

entries.zh: 祖裕，宋金紫光祿大夫。
entries.en: His grandfather Yu had been Song Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yu was Song Household Grandee with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

entries.zh: 父永，右光祿大夫。
entries.en: His father Yong was Right Household Grandee.
entries.literal: His father Yong was Right Household Grandee.

entries.zh: 曉音律，宋孝武問永以太極殿前鍾聲嘶，永答「鍾有銅滓」。
entries.en: Yong understood music; Emperor Xiaowu of Song asked him why the bell before the Hall of Supreme Pole sounded hoarse, and Yong answered, "The bell still has copper slag in it."
entries.literal: He understood music; Emperor Xiaowu of Song asked Yong why the bell before the Hall of Supreme Pole had a hoarse tone, and Yong answered, 「The bell has copper slag.」

entries.zh: 乃扣鍾求其處，鑿而去之，聲遂清越。
entries.en: He struck the bell to find the flaw, chiseled it out, and the tone rang clear and bright.
entries.literal: He struck the bell to find the spot, chiseled it away, and the tone grew clear and bright.

entries.zh: 除冠軍將軍、東海東莞二郡太守，不拜，
entries.en: He was named Champion General and Administrator of Donghai and Dongguan, but declined.
entries.literal: He was appointed Champion General and Administrator of the two commanderies Donghai and Dongguan, but did not accept,

entries.zh: 建元元年，增邑二百戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, his fief was raised by two hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, the fief was increased by two hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋改封平都。
entries.en: Soon he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu.
entries.literal: Soon he was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingdu.

entries.zh: 遷侍中，加領步兵校尉。
entries.en: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and additionally put in charge as Commandant of Footsoldiers.
entries.literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and additionally put in charge of the Footsoldiers.

entries.zh: 二年，遷都官尚書，領校尉如故。
entries.en: In the second year he became Director of Capital Officials while keeping his commandant post.
entries.literal: In the second year he became Director of Capital Officials while keeping his commandant post.

entries.zh: 出爲征虜將軍、吳興太守。
entries.en: He went out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: He went out as General Who Punishes the Barbarians and Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 三年，烏程令顧昌玄有罪，瓌坐不糾，免官。
entries.en: In the third year Gu Changxuan, magistrate of Wucheng, was guilty of a crime; Gui was faulted for not investigating and was removed from office.
entries.literal: In the third year the magistrate of Wucheng, Gu Changxuan, was guilty of a crime; Gui was punished for failing to investigate and was removed from office.

entries.zh: 明年，爲度支尚書。
entries.en: The following year he became Director of Revenue.
entries.literal: The next year he became Director of Revenue.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，爲冠軍將軍、鄱陽王北中郎長史、襄陽相、行雍州府州事，隨府轉征虜長史。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu took the throne, he was Champion General, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang as Northern Palace Cadet, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; when the headquarters moved he became chief aide of the expeditionary force.
entries.literal: When the Shizu Emperor acceded, he was Champion General, chief aide to the Prince of Poyang as Northern Palace Cadet, Administrator of Xiangyang, and acting head of Yongzhou and its headquarters; he shifted with the headquarters to chief aide of the expeditionary force.

entries.zh: 四年，仍爲持節、督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、輔國將軍、雍州刺史，尋領寧蠻校尉。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was again made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, the Jingling sector of Yingzhou, and the Suixiang sector of Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the State, and Governor of Yongzhou, and soon also Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was again made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, North and South Qin, the Jingling sector of Yingzhou, and the Suixiang sector of Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the State, and Governor of Yongzhou, and soon also made Commandant Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 還爲左民尚書，領右軍將軍，遷冠軍將軍、大司馬長史。
entries.en: He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army, then was promoted to Champion General and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.
entries.literal: He returned as Director of the Left Secretariat and also commanded the Right Army; he was promoted to Champion General and chief aide to the Grand Marshal.

entries.zh: 柳世隆
entries.en: Liu Shilong
entries.literal: Liu Shilong

entries.zh: 太祖出頓新亭，報攸之書曰：
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor moved out to camp at Xinting and answered Youzhi in a letter, saying:
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor went out to camp at Xinting and wrote back to Youzhi, saying:

entries.zh: 辱足下誚書，交道不終，爲恥已足。
entries.en: I received your letter of reproach. That our friendship has not lasted is shame enough.
entries.literal: I received your letter of reproach. That our friendship has not lasted is shame enough.

entries.zh: 欲下便來，何故多罔君子。
entries.en: If you wish to come down, then come; why so often wrong a gentleman?
entries.literal: If you wish to come down, then come; why so often wrong a gentleman?

entries.zh: 吾結髮入仕，豈期遠大，蓋感子路之言，每不擇官而宦。
entries.en: From youth I entered service; how could I have expected great things? I was moved by Zilu's words and never chose office before serving.
entries.literal: From youth I entered service; how could I have expected great things? I was moved by Zilu's words and never chose office before serving.

entries.zh: 逮文帝之世，初被聖明鑒賞；
entries.en: By Emperor Wen's time, I first received the sage and enlightened ruler's recognition and favor;
entries.literal: By Emperor Wen's time, I first received the sage and enlightened ruler's recognition and favor;

entries.zh: 及孝武之朝，復蒙英主顧眄。
entries.en: and in Emperor Xiaowu's court, I again received the heroic ruler's regard.
entries.literal: and in Emperor Xiaowu's court, I again received the heroic ruler's regard.

entries.zh: 因此感激，未能自反。
entries.en: Because of this I was moved with gratitude and could not turn back upon myself.
entries.literal: Because of this I was moved with gratitude and could not turn back upon myself.

entries.zh: 及與足下斂袂定交，款著分好，何嘗不勸慕古人國士之心，務重前良忠貞之節。
entries.en: When I joined sleeves with you and fixed our friendship, our affection was clear and our bond distinct; did we ever fail to admire the hearts of ancient state heroes and prize the loyal integrity of former worthies?
entries.literal: When I joined sleeves with you and fixed our friendship, our affection was clear and our bond distinct; did we ever fail to admire the hearts of ancient state heroes and prize the loyal integrity of former worthies?

entries.zh: 至於契闊杯酒，殷勤攜袖，薦女成姻，志相然諾，義信之篤，誰與閒之。
entries.en: As for our hard times and cups of wine, our earnest clasping of sleeves, my offering a daughter to make a marriage, and our wills pledging assent to each other, who could come between such deep duty and trust?
entries.literal: As for our hard times and cups of wine, our earnest clasping of sleeves, my offering a daughter to make a marriage, and our wills pledging assent to each other, who could come between such deep duty and trust?

entries.zh: 又乃景和陵虐，事切憂畏，明帝正位，運同休顯，啓臆論心，安危豈貳。
entries.en: Then during Jinghe's oppressive cruelty, matters pressed us with fear and anxiety. When Emperor Ming took his proper place, our fortunes shared in his rest and splendor; opening our breasts and speaking our hearts, how could we differ in danger or safety?
entries.literal: Then during Jinghe's oppressive cruelty, matters pressed us with fear and anxiety. When Emperor Ming took his proper place, our fortunes shared in his rest and splendor; opening our breasts and speaking our hearts, how could we differ in danger or safety?

entries.zh: 元徽之季，聽高道慶邪言，欲相討伐，發威施敕，已行外內。
entries.en: At the end of Yuanhui, he listened to Gao Daoqing's crooked words and wished to attack us, issuing threats and edicts already carried out inside and outside the court.
entries.literal: At the end of Yuanhui, he listened to Gao Daoqing's crooked words and wished to attack us, issuing threats and edicts already carried out inside and outside the court.

entries.zh: 于時臣子鉗口，道路以目。
entries.en: At that time ministers and subjects clamped their mouths, and people on the roads spoke only with their eyes.
entries.literal: At that time ministers and subjects clamped their mouths, and people on the roads spoke only with their eyes.

entries.zh: 吾以分交義重，患難宜均，犯陵白刃，以相任保。
entries.en: Because the duty of our shared friendship was weighty and hardship should be borne equally, I faced naked blades and guaranteed your safety.
entries.literal: Because the duty of our shared friendship was weighty and hardship should be borne equally, I faced naked blades and guaranteed your safety.

entries.zh: 悖主手敕，今封送相示。
entries.en: The perverse ruler's handwritten edict is now sealed and sent for your inspection.
entries.literal: The perverse ruler's handwritten edict is now sealed and sent for your inspection.

entries.zh: 豈不畏威，念周旋之義耳。
entries.en: Was I not afraid of his power? I simply thought of the duty by which we had moved together.
entries.literal: Was I not afraid of his power? I simply thought of the duty by which we had moved together.

entries.zh: 推此陰惠，何愧懷抱，不云足下猥含禍詖。
entries.en: Considering this hidden favor, what shame is there in my breast? I did not say you vilely harbored calamitous deceit.
entries.literal: Considering this hidden favor, what shame is there in my breast? I did not say you vilely harbored calamitous deceit.

entries.zh: 前遣王思文所牒朝事，蓋情等家國，共詳衷否，虛心小大，必以先輸。
entries.en: Earlier I sent Wang Siwen with a note on court affairs; my feeling was that family and state were alike, and that we should examine together whether the plan was sincere. With an empty heart, in great matters and small, I always laid my thoughts before you first.
entries.literal: Earlier I sent Wang Siwen with a note on court affairs; my feeling was that family and state were alike, and that we should examine together whether the plan was sincere. With an empty heart, in great matters and small, I always laid my thoughts before you first.

entries.zh: 問張雍州遷代之日，將欲誰擬？
entries.en: I asked, when Zhang of Yongzhou was to be replaced, whom did you intend to propose?
entries.literal: I asked, when Zhang of Yongzhou was to be replaced, whom did you intend to propose?

entries.zh: 本是逆論來事，非欲代張，乃封此示張，激使見怒。
entries.en: This was originally advance discussion of future affairs, not a wish to replace Zhang, yet you sealed it and showed it to Zhang, stirring him to anger.
entries.literal: This was originally advance discussion of future affairs, not a wish to replace Zhang, yet you sealed it and showed it to Zhang, stirring him to anger.

entries.zh: 若張惑一言，果興怨恨，事負雅素，君子所不可爲，況張之奉國，忠亮有本，情之見與，意契不貳邪？
entries.en: If Zhang was misled by one phrase and truly became resentful, that betrayed our ordinary refinement and is something a gentleman would not do. Moreover, Zhang's service to the state has a foundation in loyalty and clarity, and his feeling toward me and his accord in intention are not divided.
entries.literal: If Zhang was misled by one phrase and truly became resentful, that betrayed our ordinary refinement and is something a gentleman would not do. Moreover, Zhang's service to the state has a foundation in loyalty and clarity, and his feeling toward me and his accord in intention are not divided.

entries.zh: 又張雍州啓事，稱彼中蠻動，兼民遭水患，敕令足下思經拯之計。
entries.en: Again, Zhang of Yongzhou memorialized that the Man there were moving and that the people had also suffered flooding; an edict ordered you to consider plans to manage and rescue them.
entries.literal: Again, Zhang of Yongzhou memorialized that the Man there were moving and that the people had also suffered flooding; an edict ordered you to consider plans to manage and rescue them.

entries.zh: 吾亦有白，論國如家，布情而往，每思虛達。
entries.en: I too had a statement: discussing the state as one would a family, I set out my feelings and sent them, always hoping for open understanding.
entries.literal: I too had a statement: discussing the state as one would a family, I set out my feelings and sent them, always hoping for open understanding.

entries.zh: 事之相接，恒必猜離。
entries.en: Yet whenever matters touched each other, there was always suspicion and separation.
entries.literal: Yet whenever matters touched each other, there was always suspicion and separation.

entries.zh: 反謂無故遣信，此乃覘察。
entries.en: Instead you said that sending a messenger without cause was spying.
entries.literal: Instead you said that sending a messenger without cause was spying.

entries.zh: 平諒之襟，動則相阻，傷負心期，自誰作故？
entries.en: A level and honest breast was obstructed whenever it moved; who caused this injury to the trust of our hearts?
entries.literal: A level and honest breast was obstructed whenever it moved; who caused this injury to the trust of our hearts?

entries.zh: 先時足下遣信，尋盟敦舊，厲以篤終，吾止附還白，申罄情本，契然遠要，方固金石。
entries.en: Previously you sent a letter, seeking our covenant and strengthening old bonds, urging that we end with sincerity. I merely attached a reply, fully stating the root of my feelings, and our distant pledge was then firm as metal and stone.
entries.literal: Previously you sent a letter, seeking our covenant and strengthening old bonds, urging that we end with sincerity. I merely attached a reply, fully stating the root of my feelings, and our distant pledge was then firm as metal and stone.

entries.zh: 今日舉錯，定是誰恧久言邪？
entries.en: In today's conduct, who is truly ashamed before those long-standing words?
entries.literal: In today's conduct, who is truly ashamed before those long-standing words?

entries.zh: 元徽末德，埶亡禋祀，足下備聞，無待亟述。
entries.en: The failed virtue at the end of Yuanhui and the situation in which sacrifice was about to perish are things you fully heard; there is no need to repeat them urgently.
entries.literal: The failed virtue at the end of Yuanhui and the situation in which sacrifice was about to perish are things you fully heard; there is no need to repeat them urgently.

entries.zh: 太后惟憂，式遵前誥，興毀之略，事屬鄙躬。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager was anxious and followed the former command; the plan of raising up and casting down fell to my humble person.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager was anxious and followed the former command; the plan of raising up and casting down fell to my humble person.

entries.zh: 黜昏樹明，實惟前則，寧宗靜國，何愧前脩。
entries.en: Deposing darkness and establishing brightness truly followed former models; calming the clan and quieting the state, how did I shame earlier worthies?
entries.literal: Deposing darkness and establishing brightness truly followed former models; calming the clan and quieting the state, how did I shame earlier worthies?

entries.zh: 廢立有章，足下所允，冠弊之譏，將以何語？
