entries.en: Deposition and enthronement had proper order, and you approved it. With what words will you make the reproach about a worn-out cap?
entries.literal: Deposition and enthronement had proper order, and you approved it. With what words will you make the reproach about a worn-out cap?

entries.zh: 封爲郡王，寧爲失禮？
entries.en: Was enfeoffing him as a commandery prince really a loss of ritual?
entries.literal: Was enfeoffing him as a commandery prince really a loss of ritual?

entries.zh: 景和無名，方之不愈乎？
entries.en: Jinghe had no title; compared with that, was this not better?
entries.literal: Jinghe had no title; compared with that, was this not better?

entries.zh: 龍逢自匹夫之美，伊、霍則社稷之臣，同異相乘，非吾所受也。
entries.en: Longfeng possessed the beauty of a common man, while Yi Yin and Huo Guang were ministers of the altars. To multiply sameness and difference together is not something I accept.
entries.literal: Longfeng possessed the beauty of a common man, while Yi Yin and Huo Guang were ministers of the altars. To multiply sameness and difference together is not something I accept.

entries.zh: 登齋有賞，壽寂已蒙之於前；
entries.en: There were rewards for entering the chamber; Shouji had already received them before.
entries.literal: There were rewards for entering the chamber; Shouji had already received them before.

entries.zh: 同謀獲功，明皇亦行之於昔。
entries.en: Those who shared the plan obtained merit; the Ming Emperor had also done this in the past.
entries.literal: Those who shared the plan obtained merit; the Ming Emperor had also done this in the past.

entries.zh: 此則接踵成事，誰敢異之。
entries.en: These are accomplished precedents following one upon another; who would dare object?
entries.literal: These are accomplished precedents following one upon another; who would dare object?

entries.zh: 謂其大收宮女，劫奪天藏，器械金寶，必充私室。
entries.en: You say that I made a great seizure of palace women, plundered the imperial stores, and surely filled my private rooms with weapons, gold, and treasure.
entries.literal: You say that I made a great seizure of palace women, plundered the imperial stores, and surely filled my private rooms with weapons, gold, and treasure.

entries.zh: 必若虛設市虎，亦可不翅此言；
entries.en: If one falsely creates a tiger in the marketplace, it can be more than these words;
entries.literal: If one falsely creates a tiger in the marketplace, it can be more than these words;

entries.zh: 若以此詐民，天下豈患無眼。
entries.en: but if this is used to deceive the people, need the realm fear it has no eyes?
entries.literal: but if this is used to deceive the people, need the realm fear it has no eyes?

entries.zh: 心苟無瑕，非所耿介。
entries.en: If the heart has no flaw, this is not something to trouble over.
entries.literal: If the heart has no flaw, this is not something to trouble over.

entries.zh: 甲杖之授，事旣舊典，豈見有任鎮邦家，勳經定主，而可得出入輕單，不資寵衞！
entries.en: The granting of armor and weapons is an old institution. Have you ever seen one entrusted with guarding the state and family, whose merit passed through settling the ruler, yet who could come and go lightly and alone, without relying on favored guards?
entries.literal: The granting of armor and weapons is an old institution. Have you ever seen one entrusted with guarding the state and family, whose merit passed through settling the ruler, yet who could come and go lightly and alone, without relying on favored guards?

entries.zh: 斯之患慮，豈直身憂。
entries.en: This concern and anxiety was not merely worry for my own person.
entries.literal: This concern and anxiety was not merely worry for my own person.

entries.zh: 祗奉此恩，職惟事理。
entries.en: Reverently receiving this favor, my duty lay only in the principle of the matter.
entries.literal: Reverently receiving this favor, my duty lay only in the principle of the matter.

entries.zh: 朱方之牧，公卿僉意，吾亦謂微勳之次，無忝一州。
entries.en: The governorship of Zhufang was the unanimous view of the dukes and ministers; I too thought that, after my slight merit, I would not disgrace one province.
entries.literal: The governorship of Zhufang was the unanimous view of the dukes and ministers; I too thought that, after my slight merit, I would not disgrace one province.

entries.zh: 且魏、晉舊事，帝郷蕃職，何嘗豫州必曹，司州必馬？
entries.en: Moreover, in the old affairs of Wei and Jin, when the imperial homeland was a provincial office, when did Yuzhou always have to be held by a Cao or Sizhou by a Sima?
entries.literal: Moreover, in the old affairs of Wei and Jin, when the imperial homeland was a provincial office, when did Yuzhou always have to be held by a Cao or Sizhou by a Sima?

entries.zh: 折膠受柱，在體非愧。
entries.en: Receiving the post as a bent glue support is no shame in substance.
entries.literal: Receiving the post as a bent glue support is no shame in substance.

entries.zh: 袁粲據石頭，足下無不可；
entries.en: When Yuan Can held Shitou, you found nothing unacceptable;
entries.literal: When Yuan Can held Shitou, you found nothing unacceptable;

entries.zh: 吾之守東府，來告便謂非。
entries.en: but when I guarded the Eastern Office, your letter immediately called it wrong.
entries.literal: but when I guarded the Eastern Office, your letter immediately called it wrong.

entries.zh: 動容見疾，頻笑入戾，乃如是乎！
entries.en: Every movement of my face is met with hatred, and repeated smiles are taken as crimes. Has it come to this?
entries.literal: Every movement of my face is met with hatred, and repeated smiles are taken as crimes. Has it come to this?

entries.zh: 袁粲、劉秉，受遇深重，家國旣安，不思撫鎮，遂與足下表裏潛規，據城之夜，豈顧社稷。
entries.en: Yuan Can and Liu Bing had received deep and weighty treatment; once family and state were secure, they did not think to soothe and stabilize them, but instead secretly plotted with you inside and outside. On the night they occupied the city, how did they care for the altars?
entries.literal: Yuan Can and Liu Bing had received deep and weighty treatment; once family and state were secure, they did not think to soothe and stabilize them, but instead secretly plotted with you inside and outside. On the night they occupied the city, how did they care for the altars?

entries.zh: 幸天未長亂，宗廟有靈，卽與褚衞軍協謀義斷，以時殄滅。
entries.en: Fortunately Heaven did not prolong the disorder, and the ancestral temple had spirit; I immediately joined plans with Chu, General of the Guard, made a righteous decision, and destroyed them in time.
entries.literal: Fortunately Heaven did not prolong the disorder, and the ancestral temple had spirit; I immediately joined plans with Chu, General of the Guard, made a righteous decision, and destroyed them in time.

entries.zh: 想足下聞之，悵然孤沮。
entries.en: I imagine that when you heard of it, you were disappointed, isolated, and dejected.
entries.literal: I imagine that when you heard of it, you were disappointed, isolated, and dejected.

entries.zh: 小兒忝侍中，代來之澤，遇直上臺，便呼一家兩錄。
entries.en: My young son shamefully held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary, a grace passed down through generations; when he happened to serve on duty in the upper offices, you immediately called it one family holding two recorderships.
entries.literal: My young son shamefully held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary, a grace passed down through generations; when he happened to serve on duty in the upper offices, you immediately called it one family holding two recorderships.

entries.zh: 發不擇言，良以太甚。
entries.en: You spoke without choosing your words; truly this was excessive.
entries.literal: You spoke without choosing your words; truly this was excessive.

entries.zh: 吾之方寸，古列共言，乃以陶、庾往賢，大見譏責，足下自省，詎得以此見貽邪？
entries.en: My heart is something men of old have all spoken of, yet you use former worthies such as Tao and Yu to reproach me greatly. Examine yourself: how could you present me with this?
entries.literal: My heart is something men of old have all spoken of, yet you use former worthies such as Tao and Yu to reproach me greatly. Examine yourself: how could you present me with this?

entries.zh: 比蹤夷、叔，論吾則可，行過桀、蹠，無乃近誣哉！
entries.en: To compare my tracks with Boyi and Shuqi may be acceptable when speaking of me; to say my conduct surpasses Jie and Zhi is surely close to slander.
entries.literal: To compare my tracks with Boyi and Shuqi may be acceptable when speaking of me; to say my conduct surpasses Jie and Zhi is surely close to slander.

entries.zh: 謂吾不朝，此則良誨，朝之與否，想更問之。
entries.en: You say I did not attend court; this is good instruction. As to whether I attended or not, I expect you should ask again.
entries.literal: You say I did not attend court; this is good instruction. As to whether I attended or not, I expect you should ask again.

entries.zh: 足下受先帝之恩施，擁戎西州，鼎湖之日，率土載奔，而宴安中流，酣飲自若，卽懷狼望，陵侮皇朝。
entries.en: You received the Former Emperor's grace and held troops in the western province. On the day of Dinghu, all the land rushed in mourning, yet you feasted at ease in midstream and drank heavily as if nothing had happened, already harboring a wolf's ambition and insulting the imperial court.
entries.literal: You received the Former Emperor's grace and held troops in the western province. On the day of Dinghu, all the land rushed in mourning, yet you feasted at ease in midstream and drank heavily as if nothing had happened, already harboring a wolf's ambition and insulting the imperial court.

entries.zh: 晉熙殿下，以皇弟代鎮，而斷割候迎，罔蔑宗子，驅略士馬，悉以西上，郢中所遺，僅餘劣弱。
entries.en: His Highness of Jinxi, as the emperor's younger brother, went to replace you in the command, but you cut off the welcoming parties, slighted the imperial kinsman, drove off and seized soldiers and horses, and sent them all westward, leaving in Ying only the inferior and weak.
entries.literal: His Highness of Jinxi, as the emperor's younger brother, went to replace you in the command, but you cut off the welcoming parties, slighted the imperial kinsman, drove off and seized soldiers and horses, and sent them all westward, leaving in Ying only the inferior and weak.

entries.zh: 昔徵茅不入，猶動義師；
entries.en: In the past, when tribute grass was not sent in, righteous armies were still mobilized;
entries.literal: In the past, when tribute grass was not sent in, righteous armies were still mobilized;

entries.zh: 況荊州物產，雍、崏、交、梁之會，自足下爲牧，薦獻何品？
entries.en: how much more when Jingzhou, with its products and its meeting point with Yong, Min, Jiao, and Liang, has offered what goods since you became its governor?
entries.literal: how much more when Jingzhou, with its products and its meeting point with Yong, Min, Jiao, and Liang, has offered what goods since you became its governor?

entries.zh: 良馬勁卒，彼中不無，良皮美罽，商賂所聚，前後貢奉，多少何如？
entries.en: Fine horses and strong soldiers are not lacking there; good hides and beautiful rugs gather through trade and gifts. How much tribute has been offered before and after?
entries.literal: Fine horses and strong soldiers are not lacking there; good hides and beautiful rugs gather through trade and gifts. How much tribute has been offered before and after?

entries.zh: 唯聞太官時納飲食耳。
entries.en: I have heard only that food has sometimes been sent to the Grand Provisioner.
entries.literal: I have heard only that food has sometimes been sent to the Grand Provisioner.

entries.zh: 桂陽之難，坐觀成敗，自以雍容漢南，西伯可擬。
entries.en: During the Guiyang crisis, you sat watching success or failure, considering yourself so composed south of the Han that you could be compared to the Earl of the West.
entries.literal: During the Guiyang crisis, you sat watching success or failure, considering yourself so composed south of the Han that you could be compared to the Earl of the West.

entries.zh: 賴原卽天世，非望亦消。
entries.en: Thanks to the fact that Yuan soon died, your improper hopes also vanished.
entries.literal: Thanks to the fact that Yuan soon died, your improper hopes also vanished.

entries.zh: 又招集逋亡，斷遏行侶，治舟試艦，恒以朝廷爲旗的，秣馬桉劔，常願天下有風塵，爲人臣者，固若是邪！
entries.en: You also gathered fugitives, cut off travelers, repaired boats and tested warships, constantly took the court as your target, fed horses and gripped your sword, and always wished for dust storms under Heaven. Is this truly how a subject acts?
entries.literal: You also gathered fugitives, cut off travelers, repaired boats and tested warships, constantly took the court as your target, fed horses and gripped your sword, and always wished for dust storms under Heaven. Is this truly how a subject acts?

entries.zh: 至乃不遵制書，敕下如空，國恩莫行，命令擁隔，詔除郡縣，輙自板代，罷官去職，禁還京師。
entries.en: You even failed to obey imperial documents, treated edicts as empty, blocked the state's grace from being carried out, obstructed commands, replaced appointments to commanderies and counties with your own temporary commissions, and forbade dismissed officials returning to the capital.
entries.literal: You even failed to obey imperial documents, treated edicts as empty, blocked the state's grace from being carried out, obstructed commands, replaced appointments to commanderies and counties with your own temporary commissions, and forbade dismissed officials returning to the capital.

entries.zh: 凶人出境，無不千里尋躡，而反募臺將，來必厚加給賞。
entries.en: When wicked men left your territory, you always pursued them a thousand li, yet you recruited generals from the court, richly rewarding any who came.
entries.literal: When wicked men left your territory, you always pursued them a thousand li, yet you recruited generals from the court, richly rewarding any who came.

entries.zh: 太妃遣使市馬，齎寶往蜀，足下悉皆斷折，以爲私財，此皆遠邇共聞，暴於視聽。
entries.en: When the Grand Consort sent envoys to buy horses and carry valuables to Shu, you cut them all off and took them as private wealth. All this has been heard far and near and is exposed to sight and hearing.
entries.literal: When the Grand Consort sent envoys to buy horses and carry valuables to Shu, you cut them all off and took them as private wealth. All this has been heard far and near and is exposed to sight and hearing.

entries.zh: 主上叡明當璧，宇縣同慶，絕域奉贄，萬國通書，而盤桓百日，始有單騎，事存送往，於此可徵。
entries.en: When the sovereign, in his brilliant wisdom, held the jade disk, the realm rejoiced together, distant lands offered gifts, and ten thousand states sent letters; yet you lingered a hundred days before there was even a single rider. That your intent lay merely in seeing off the past can be proven from this.
entries.literal: When the sovereign, in his brilliant wisdom, held the jade disk, the realm rejoiced together, distant lands offered gifts, and ten thousand states sent letters; yet you lingered a hundred days before there was even a single rider. That your intent lay merely in seeing off the past can be proven from this.

entries.zh: 不朝如此，誰應受誚？
entries.en: With nonattendance like this, who should receive reproach?
entries.literal: With nonattendance like this, who should receive reproach?

entries.zh: 反以見呵，非所反側。
entries.en: For you instead to scold me is not something I can rest easy with.
entries.literal: For you instead to scold me is not something I can rest easy with.

entries.zh: 今乃勒兵以闚象館，長戟以指魏闕，不亦爲忠臣孝子之所痛心疾首邪？
entries.en: Now you marshal troops to peer into the Elephant Hall and point long halberds at the palace gates. Is this not something to make loyal ministers and filial sons grieve in heart and ache in head?
entries.literal: Now you marshal troops to peer into the Elephant Hall and point long halberds at the palace gates. Is this not something to make loyal ministers and filial sons grieve in heart and ache in head?

entries.zh: 賢子元琰獲免虎口，及凌波西邁，吾所發遣。
entries.en: Your worthy son Yuanyan escaped the tiger's mouth, and when he crossed the waves westward, I was the one who sent him off.
entries.literal: Your worthy son Yuanyan escaped the tiger's mouth, and when he crossed the waves westward, I was the one who sent him off.

entries.zh: 猶推素懷，不畏嗤嗤。
entries.en: I still extended my old feelings and did not fear ridicule.
entries.literal: I still extended my old feelings and did not fear ridicule.

entries.zh: 足下尚復滅君臣之紀，況吾布衣之交乎？
entries.en: Yet you still destroy the order between ruler and subject; how much more my common-cloth friendship with you?
entries.literal: Yet you still destroy the order between ruler and subject; how much more my common-cloth friendship with you?

entries.zh: 遂事不諫，旣往難咎。
entries.en: What is already done cannot be remonstrated against, and what is past is hard to blame.
entries.literal: What is already done cannot be remonstrated against, and what is past is hard to blame.

entries.zh: 今六師西向，爲足下憂之。
entries.en: Now the six armies face west, and I worry for you.
entries.literal: Now the six armies face west, and I worry for you.

entries.zh: 垣崇祖
entries.en: Yuan Chongzu
entries.literal: Yuan Chongzu

entries.zh: 二年，虜寇邊，上遣安國出司州，安集民戶。
entries.en: In the second year the northern enemy struck the border; the throne sent Anguo into Si to settle the people.
entries.literal: In the second year the northerners raided the border; the emperor sent Anguo out to Si Province to settle the people and households.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「郢、司之閒，流雜繁廣，宜竝加區判，定其隷屬。
entries.en: An edict said: "Between Ying and Si the displaced are many and scattered; they should be sorted by district and their allegiance fixed.
entries.literal: An edict said: 「Between Ying and Si, dispersed settlers are many and broad; they should all be marked off by district and their subordination fixed.

entries.zh: 參詳兩州，事無專任，安國可蹔往經理。」
entries.en: Look to both provinces: no one holds sole charge—Anguo may go for a time to put things in order."
entries.literal: Review both provinces; no one bears sole charge—Anguo may go temporarily to oversee it.」

entries.zh: 以本官使持節、總荊郢諸軍北討事，屯義陽西關。
entries.en: At his present rank he was made envoy with credentials, overall commander of Jing and Ying for the northern campaign, and camped at Yiyang's western pass.
entries.literal: With his existing rank, envoy with credentials, overall commander of Jing and Ying military affairs for the northern campaign, encamped at Yiyang's western pass.

entries.zh: 虜未至，安國移屯沔口以俟應接。
entries.en: The enemy never came; Anguo shifted camp to the mouth of the Mian to stand ready for relief.
entries.literal: The enemy did not come; Anguo moved his camp to the Mian mouth to await support.

entries.zh: 改封湘郷。
entries.en: He was re-enfeoffed at Xiangxiang.
entries.literal: He was re-enfeoffed at Xiangxiang.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，授使持節、散騎常侍、平西將軍、司州刺史，領義陽太守，
entries.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne he received credentials as envoy, supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, and inspector of Si, still holding Yiyang as administrator.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne he was granted envoy with credentials, supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, inspector of Si Province, still administrator of Yiyang,

entries.zh: 永明二年，徙都督南兖兖徐青冀五州諸軍事、平北將軍、南兖州刺史，仍爲都督、湘州刺史。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongming, he was then made overseer of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of South Yan, while still overseeing Xiang as inspector.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongming, he was moved to oversee South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, inspector of South Yan; still overseer and inspector of Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 四年，湘川蠻動，安國督州兵討之。
entries.en: In the fourth year the tribes of Xiang rose; Anguo led provincial troops to put them down.
entries.literal: In the fourth year Xiangxiang barbarians stirred; Anguo oversaw provincial troops to suppress them.

entries.zh: 有疾，徵爲光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: Illness brought him to court as Grandee of Splendid Happiness with added supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry.
entries.literal: He fell ill and was summoned as Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with added supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry.

entries.zh: 安國欣有文授，謂其子曰：「汝後勿作褶驅使，單衣猶恨不稱，當爲朱衣官也。」
entries.en: Anguo rejoiced that his sons had learning; he told his son: "Hereafter do not serve as a pleated-coat driver—even plain robes still feel unworthy; you should wear vermilion and hold office."
entries.literal: Anguo delighted that he had literary learning for his sons; he told his son: 「After me do not become a pleated-coat driver; plain dress still seems not fitting—you should be a vermilion-robed official.」

entries.zh: 上遣中書舍人茹法亮敕安國曰：「吾恒憂卿疾病，應有所須，勿致難也。」
entries.en: The emperor sent Secretarial Attendant Ru Faliang to tell Anguo: "I always fret over your sickness; if you need anything, do not hold back."
entries.literal: The emperor sent Secretarial Attendant Ru Faliang to instruct Anguo: 「I constantly worry over your illness; should you need anything, do not make it difficult.」

entries.zh: 明年，遷都官尚書，領太子左率。
entries.en: The next year he was made minister of justice and led the crown prince's left guard.
entries.literal: The next year he was moved to Minister of Justice, leading the crown prince's left guard.

entries.zh: 六年，遷領軍將軍。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was made General of the Army.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to General of the Army.

entries.zh: 安國累居將率，在朝以宿舊見遇。
entries.en: Anguo had long stood at the head of armies; at court he was honored as an old companion.
entries.literal: Anguo long held command ranks; in court he was treated as an elder of long standing.

entries.zh: 尋遷散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫、兖州中正，給扶。
entries.en: Soon he was raised to supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, household minister with golden seal and purple ribbon, and impartial nominee for Yan, with attendants to lean on.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved to supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, Household Minister with golden seal and purple ribbon, impartial nominee for Yan Province, with support staff provided.

entries.zh: 上又敕茹法亮曰：「吾見呂安國疾狀，自不宜勞，且脚中旣恒惡，扶人至吾前，於禮望殊成有虧，吾難敕之。
entries.en: The emperor again told Ru Faliang: "I have read Lu Anguo's medical notes—he is plainly unfit for exertion; his feet have long troubled him, and to be led before me would shame his standing in ritual; I cannot bring myself to command it.
entries.literal: The emperor again instructed Ru Faliang: 「I have seen Lu Anguo's medical reports—by himself he is unfit for labor; moreover his feet have long been bad, and to be helped before me is a great loss to ceremonial bearing; I find it hard to order him.

entries.zh: 其人甚諱病，卿可作私意向，其若好差不復須扶人，依例入，幸勿牽勉。」
entries.en: He hides his sickness deeply; speak to him privately—if he improves enough to walk unaided, let him come in as usual; do not force him."
entries.literal: The man greatly hides his illness; you may make a private inquiry—if he is somewhat better and no longer needs support, let him enter by precedent; do not press him.」

entries.zh: 八年，卒，年六十四。
entries.en: In the eighth year he died, at sixty-four.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he died, at age sixty-four.

entries.zh: 贈使持節、鎮北將軍、南兖州刺史，常侍如故。
entries.en: Posthumously he was granted credentials as envoy, General Who Guards the North, and inspector of South Yan, with attendant rank unchanged.
entries.literal: Posthumously granted envoy with credentials, General Who Guards the North, inspector of South Yan Province, attendant as before.

entries.zh: 給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: He was given one suite of martial music.
entries.literal: Given one set of martial music instruments.

entries.zh: 諡肅侯。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.
entries.literal: Posthumous title Marquis Su.

entries.zh: 呂安國
entries.en: Lu Anguo
entries.literal: Lu Anguo

entries.zh: 薛淵，河東汾陰人也。
entries.en: Xue Yuan was a man of Fenyin in Hedong.
entries.literal: Xue Yuan was a native of Fenyin in Hedong.

entries.zh: 宋徐州刺史安都從子。
entries.en: He was nephew to An Du, inspector of Xuzhou under the Song.
entries.literal: He was a nephew of An Du, Song's inspector of Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 本名道淵，避太祖偏諱改。
entries.en: His birth name was Dao Yuan; he changed it to avoid the Founder's partial taboo on the character dao.
entries.literal: His original name was Dao Yuan; to avoid the Founder's partial taboo he changed it.

entries.zh: 安都以彭城降虜，親族皆入北。
entries.en: When An Du gave up Pengcheng to the northern enemy, the whole clan went north.
entries.literal: When An Du surrendered Pengcheng to the northerners, his kin all went north.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮淮陰，淵遁來南，委身自結。
entries.en: While the Founder was posted at Huaiyin, Yuan stole south and threw himself on the Founder's favor.
entries.literal: While the Founder held Huaiyin, Yuan fled south and pledged himself in close bond.

entries.zh: 果幹有氣力。
entries.en: He was bold and able, with great bodily strength.
entries.literal: He was resolute and capable, full of physical strength.

entries.zh: 太祖使領部曲，備衞帳內，從征伐。
entries.en: The Founder set him at the head of his household troops, guarding the inner quarters, and sent him on campaign after campaign.
entries.literal: The Founder had him lead his own followers, guard the inner camp, and take part in campaigns.

entries.zh: 元徽末，以勳官至輔國將軍，右軍將軍，驍騎將軍、軍主，封竟陵侯。
entries.en: Late in the Yuanhui reign, by merit he reached General Who Supports the State, general of the right army, general of agile cavalry and army commander, and was enfeoffed marquis of Jingling.
entries.literal: Late in the Yuanhui era, by merit he rose to General Who Supports the State, General of the Right Army, General of Agile Cavalry and army commander, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Jingling.

entries.zh: 沈攸之難起，太祖入朝堂，豫章王嶷代守東府，使淵領軍屯司徒左府，分備京邑。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi rose, the Founder went into the hall of court; Prince of Yuzhang Yi held the eastern headquarters in his place and set Yuan at the head of troops encamped at the minister of public works' left quarters, dividing the capital for defense.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, the Founder entered the hall of court; the Prince of Yuzhang, Yi, held the Eastern headquarters in his stead and had Yuan lead troops to encamp at the Minister of Public Works' left quarters, dividing forces to guard the capital.

entries.zh: 袁粲據石頭，豫章王嶷夜登西門遙呼淵，淵驚起，率軍赴難，先至石頭焚門攻戰。
entries.en: Yuan Can held Stone citadel; Prince of Yuzhang Yi climbed the western gate at night and hailed Yuan from afar; Yuan started up in alarm, led his host to the crisis, and was first at Stone citadel—burning the gate and fighting through.
entries.literal: Yuan Can held Stone citadel; the Prince of Yuzhang, Yi, climbed the western gate at night and called Yuan from afar; Yuan sprang up in alarm, led his army to the crisis, and was first to reach Stone citadel—burning the gate and fighting through.

entries.zh: 事平，明旦衆軍還集杜姥宅，街路皆滿，宮門不開，太祖登南掖門樓處分衆軍各還本頓，至食後，城門開，淵方得入見太祖，且喜且泣。
entries.en: When the affair was settled, at dawn the next day the hosts gathered at Old Woman Du's house; every street was full, the palace gates stayed shut, the Founder mounted the southern side-gate tower to send each army back to its post, and only after the meal hour did the gates open—then Yuan could enter and see the Founder, weeping between joy and relief.
entries.literal: When affairs were settled, at dawn the next day the armies assembled at Old Woman Du's residence; the streets were packed, the palace gates would not open, the Founder mounted the southern side-gate tower to assign each army to its own post, and only after the meal hour did the city gates open—then Yuan could enter to see the Founder, weeping for joy.

entries.zh: 太祖卽位，增邑爲二千五百戶。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Yuan's fief rose to two thousand five hundred households.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Yuan's fief was increased to two thousand five hundred households.

entries.zh: 除淮陵太守，加寧朔將軍，驍騎將軍如故。
entries.en: He was named administrator of Huailing, with added General Who Pacifies the North, general of agile cavalry unchanged.
entries.literal: He was made administrator of Huailing, with added rank as General Who Pacifies the North, General of Agile Cavalry unchanged.

entries.zh: 尋爲直閤將軍，冠軍將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was made commander of the straight guard and general who commands the champions.
entries.literal: Soon he was made commander of the straight guard and General Who Commands the Champions.

entries.zh: 仍轉太子左率。
entries.en: He was then moved to lead the crown prince's left guard.
entries.literal: He was then transferred to the crown prince's left guard leader.

entries.zh: 虜遣偽將薛道摽寇壽春，太祖以道摽淵之親近，敕齊郡太守劉懷慰曰：「聞道摽分明來，其兒婦竝在都，與諸弟無復同生者，凡此類，無爲不多方誤之，縱不全信，足使豺狼疑惑。」
entries.en: The northern enemy sent the false general Xue Daobiao against Shouchun; because Daobiao was Yuan's close kin, the Founder instructed Liu Huaiwei, administrator of Qi: "I hear Daobiao is plainly on his way; his sons and daughters-in-law are all in the capital, and with his brothers he will no longer live as one household. For men like this, spare no trick from every side—even if they do not wholly believe you, it is enough to set wolves and jackals doubting one another."
entries.literal: The northerners sent the false general Xue Daobiao to raid Shouchun; because Daobiao was close kin to Yuan, the Founder instructed Liu Huaiwei, administrator of Qi commandery: "I hear Daobiao is plainly coming; his sons and daughters-in-law are all in the capital, and with his brothers he will no longer live as one family. For men of this sort, do not spare many-sided deceptions—even if they do not fully believe them, it is enough to sow doubt among the wolves and jackals."

entries.zh: 令爲淵書與道摽示購之之意，虜得書，果追道摽，遣他將代之。
entries.en: He had a letter drafted in Yuan's name to Daobiao showing intent to buy him over; the northerners got the letter, recalled Daobiao, and sent another general in his stead.
entries.literal: He had a letter written in Yuan's name to Daobiao showing intent to win him over; the northerners got the letter, indeed recalled Daobiao, and sent another general in his place.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，遷左衞將軍。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Yuan was moved to general of the left guard.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Yuan was moved to General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 初，淵南奔，母索氏不得自拔，改嫁長安楊氏，淵私遣購贖，梁州刺史崔慧景報淵云：「索在界首，遣信拘引，已得拔難。」
entries.en: Earlier, when Yuan fled south, his mother Lady Suo could not break free and remarried into the Yang clan of Chang'an; Yuan secretly sent men to ransom her, and Cui Huijing, inspector of Liang, reported to Yuan: "Suo is at the frontier post; I have sent a messenger to seize and lead her out—she is already past the danger."
entries.literal: Earlier, when Yuan fled south, his mother Lady Suo could not pull herself free and remarried into the Yang clan of Chang'an; Yuan privately sent men to ransom her, and Inspector of Liangzhou Cui Huijing reported to Yuan: "Suo is at the border post; I have sent a messenger to detain and lead her out—she is already beyond the danger."

entries.zh: 淵表求解職至界上迎之，見許。
entries.en: Yuan memorialized to resign his post and go to the border to receive her; the court granted it.
entries.literal: Yuan memorialized asking to resign his post and go to the frontier to receive her; permission was granted.

entries.zh: 改授散騎常侍、征虜將軍。
entries.en: He was reassigned supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry and general who campaigns against the barbarians.
entries.literal: He was reassigned supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry and General Who Campaigns against the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 淵母南歸事竟無實，
entries.en: In the end the tale of Yuan's mother coming south proved untrue.
entries.literal: The matter of Yuan's mother returning south in the end had no truth to it,

entries.zh: 永明元年，淵上表解職送貂蟬。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming, Yuan then memorialized to resign and sent back his court regalia.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, Yuan submitted a memorial resigning his post and sending back his court regalia.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「遠隔殊方，聲問難審。
entries.en: An edict said: "Far apart in a foreign land, word and inquiry are hard to trust.
entries.literal: The edict said: "Separated by a distant region, word and inquiry are hard to verify.

entries.zh: 淵憂迫之深，固辭朝列。
entries.en: Yuan's grief presses deep; he firmly declines the court ranks.
entries.literal: Yuan's anguish presses deep; he firmly declines the court ranks.

entries.zh: 昔東關舊典，猶通婚宦；
entries.en: In old precedent at the Eastern Pass, marriage and office still passed between the two sides;
entries.literal: In old precedent at the Eastern Pass, marriage and office still passed between the two sides;

entries.zh: 況母出有差，音息時至，依附前例，不容申許。
entries.en: how much more when a mother has gone out with only a gap in degree—news still reaches him from time to time; by the earlier example, his plea cannot be granted.
entries.literal: how much more when a mother has gone out with only a gap in degree—news reaches him from time to time; following the earlier example, his plea cannot be granted.

entries.zh: 便可斷表，速還章服。」
entries.en: Let him at once withdraw the memorial and quickly return to his seals and robes."
entries.literal: Let him at once withdraw the memorial and quickly return to his seals and robes."

entries.zh: 淵以贖母旣不得，又表陳解職，詔不許。
entries.en: Because Yuan could not ransom his mother, he again memorialized to resign; the edict would not allow it.
entries.literal: Because Yuan could not ransom his mother, he again memorialized to resign; the edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 後虜使至，上爲淵致與母書。
entries.en: Later, when a northern envoy came, the throne had a letter written to Yuan's mother on his behalf.
entries.literal: Later when a northern envoy came, the emperor had a letter written to Yuan's mother on his behalf.

entries.zh: 八年，爲右將軍、大司馬，領軍討巴東王子響。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was made general of the right and grand marshal, leading the host to suppress Prince Zixiang of Badong.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was made general of the right and grand marshal, leading the army to suppress Prince Zixiang of Badong.

entries.zh: 子響軍主劉超之被捕急，以眠褥雜物十餘種賂淵自逃，淵匿之軍中，爲有司所奏，詔原。
entries.en: Liu Chaozhi, Zixiang's army commander, was hard pressed in arrest and bribed Yuan with a dozen sleeping mats and other goods to slip away; Yuan hid him in the host—impeached, and the edict pardoned him.
entries.literal: Liu Chaozhi, army commander under Zixiang, was pressed in arrest and bribed Yuan with a dozen sleeping mats and other goods to escape on his own; Yuan hid him in the army—impeached, and the edict pardoned him.

entries.zh: 十年，爲散騎常侍，將軍如故。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was made supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, general unchanged.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was made supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, general unchanged.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，朝廷慮虜南寇，假淵節，軍主、本官如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu died, the court feared a southern raid from the north and granted Yuan credentials, army commander and former rank unchanged.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu died, the court feared a southern raid from the north and granted Yuan credentials, army commander and former rank unchanged.

entries.zh: 尋加驍騎將軍，假節、本官如故，
entries.en: Soon he was raised to general of agile cavalry, with acting credentials and former rank unchanged.
entries.literal: Soon he was raised to General of Agile Cavalry, with acting credentials and former rank unchanged,

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，出爲持節、督司州軍事、司州刺史，右將軍如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang, he went out bearing the staff, overseeing Si military affairs as inspector of Si, general of the right unchanged.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he went out bearing the staff, overseeing Si Province military affairs, inspector of Si, general of the right unchanged.

entries.zh: 延興元年，進號平北將軍，未拜，卒。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing, he was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the North, but before investiture he died.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, he was advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the North, but before investiture he died.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，方有詔賻錢五萬，布五百匹，剋日舉哀。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, an edict had already granted fifty thousand cash and five hundred bolts of cloth for his funeral, with mourning set for a fixed day.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, there was already an edict for funeral gift of fifty thousand cash and five hundred bolts of cloth, with mourning to begin on the set day.

entries.zh: 僧靜少有膽力，便弓馬。
entries.en: In youth Sengjing had courage and strength and was skilled with bow and horse.
entries.literal: Sengjing in youth had courage and strength, skilled with bow and horse.

entries.zh: 事刺史沈文秀，俱沒虜。
entries.en: He served Inspector Shen Wenxiu and together fell into northern hands.
entries.literal: He served Inspector Shen Wenxiu and together fell into northern captivity.

entries.zh: 後將家屬叛還淮陰，太祖撫畜之，常在左右。
entries.en: Later he led his household in revolt back to Huaiyin; the Founder sheltered and kept him, always at his side.
entries.literal: Later he led his household in revolt back to Huaiyin; the Founder sheltered and nourished him, keeping him always at his side.

entries.zh: 僧靜於都載錦出，爲歐陽戍所得，繫兖州獄，太祖遣薛淵餉僧靜酒食，以刀子置魚腹中。
entries.en: Seng Jing was carrying brocade out of the capital when Ouyang Shu took him and threw him into Yanzhou jail. The founding emperor sent Xue Yuan with food and wine, a knife tucked inside a fish.
entries.literal: Seng Jing was hauling brocade out of the capital when Ouyang Shu seized him and had him bound in Yanzhou prison; the Founder sent Xue Yuan with food and wine for Seng Jing, with a knife hidden in a fish's belly.

entries.zh: 僧靜與獄吏飲酒，旣醉，以刀刻械，手自折鏁，發屋而出。
entries.en: He drank with the jailers until they were drunk, then carved through his fetters with the knife, snapped the locks himself, tore through the roof, and fled.
entries.literal: Seng Jing drank with the jailers; once drunk, he used the knife to carve through his shackles, broke the locks by hand, broke through the roof, and escaped.

entries.zh: 歸，太祖匿之齋內，以其家貧，年給穀千斛。
entries.en: Back in camp, the founding emperor hid him in his private quarters and, because the household was poor, gave them a thousand piculs of grain every year.
entries.literal: On his return the Founder hid him in his private quarters; because the family was poor, he granted them a thousand piculs of grain each year.

entries.zh: 虜圍角城，遣僧靜戰盪，數捷，補帳內軍主。
entries.en: When the enemy besieged Jiaocheng, he sent Seng Jing to fight them off; after several victories Seng Jing was made chief of the inner guard.
entries.literal: When the northerners besieged Jiaocheng, he sent Seng Jing to strike and repel them; after several victories he was made inner-tent army chief.

entries.zh: 隨還京師，勳階至積射將軍、羽林監。
entries.en: On the return to the capital his merit ranks rose to general who accumulates shots and supervisor of the feathered forest.
entries.literal: When they returned to the capital, his merit ranks rose to General Who Accumulates Shots and Supervisor of the Feathered Forest.

entries.zh: 沈攸之事起，太祖入朝堂，僧靜爲軍主，從袁粲據石頭。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, the founding emperor entered the audience hall. Seng Jing was an army chief and followed Yuan Can in holding Stone citadel.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair broke out, the Founder entered the audience hall; Seng Jing was an army chief and followed Yuan Can in holding Stone citadel.

entries.zh: 太祖遣僧靜將腹心先至石頭，時蘇烈據倉城，僧靜射書與烈，夜縋入城。
entries.en: The founding emperor sent Seng Jing ahead with his trusted men. Su Lie then held the granary quarter; Seng Jing shot a letter to him and was hauled into the city by rope that night.
entries.literal: The Founder sent Seng Jing with his inner circle to reach Stone citadel first; at the time Su Lie held the granary city. Seng Jing shot a letter to Lie and was lowered into the city by rope at night.

entries.zh: 粲登城西南門，列燭火處分，臺軍至，射之，火乃滅，回登東門。
entries.en: Can climbed the southwest gate and set torches to direct the fight; when the palace troops came up he shot at them, the fires went dark, and he withdrew to the east gate.
entries.literal: Can mounted the southwest gate of the city, arrayed torch-lights for disposition; when the palace troops arrived he shot at them, the fires went out, and he returned to mount the east gate.

entries.zh: 其黨輔國將軍孫曇瓘驍勇善戰，每盪一合，輙大殺傷，官軍死者百餘人。
entries.en: His ally, supporting-the-state general Sun Tanhuan, was fierce in battle; every charge left a great slaughter, and more than a hundred government men fell.
entries.literal: His partisan, Supporting-the-State General Sun Tanhuan, was fierce and skilled in battle; every time he charged once, he would inflict heavy slaughter—a hundred and more government troops dead.

entries.zh: 軍主王天生殊死拒戰，故得相持。
entries.en: Army chief Wang Tiansheng fought with desperate courage, and so the two sides held each other off.
entries.literal: Army chief Wang Tiansheng resisted with desperate valor, and so they were able to stalemate.

entries.zh: 自亥至丑，有流星赤色照地墜城中，僧靜率力攻倉門，身先士卒，衆潰，僧靜手斬粲，於是外軍燒門入。
entries.en: Between the hours of hai and chou a crimson meteor flared along the ground and fell inside the walls. Seng Jing stormed the granary gate at the head of his men; the host broke; he cut down Can with his own hand, and the outer force burned the gate and poured in.
entries.literal: From the hour hai to the hour chou, a crimson meteor blazed to the ground and fell within the city. Seng Jing led a forced assault on the granary gate, taking the lead before his men; the mass broke; Seng Jing personally beheaded Can, and then the outer army burned the gate and entered.

entries.zh: 初，粲大明中與蕭惠開、周朗同車行，逢大桁開，駐車共語。
entries.en: Long before, in the Daming era, Can rode in one carriage with Xiao Huikai and Zhou Lang. The Great Drawbridge stood open; they halted and spoke together.
entries.literal: Earlier, during Daming in Can's day, he rode in the same carriage with Xiao Huikai and Zhou Lang; they met the Great Drawbridge open, stopped the carriage, and spoke together.

entries.zh: 惠開取鏡自照曰：「無年可仕。」
entries.en: Huikai took a mirror, looked at himself, and said, "No years are left in which to serve."
entries.literal: Huikai took a mirror to look at himself and said: "No years remain in which to take office."

entries.zh: 朗執鏡良久曰：「視死如歸。」
entries.en: Lang held the mirror a long while and said, "To look upon death as going home."
entries.literal: Lang held the mirror a long while and said: "To look upon death as going home."

entries.zh: 粲最後曰：「當至三公而不終也。」
entries.en: Can spoke last: "I shall reach the three highest offices but not see the end."
entries.literal: Can spoke last: "I shall reach the Three Dukes but not complete my course."

entries.zh: 僧靜以功除前軍將軍，寧朔將軍。
entries.en: For merit Seng Jing was made general of the forward army and general who stabilizes the north.
entries.literal: Seng Jing, for merit, was made General of the Forward Army and General Who Stabilizes the North.

entries.zh: 將士戰亡者，太祖爲歛祭焉，
entries.en: For officers and men who died in the fighting, the founding emperor gathered the dead and made offering.
entries.literal: For officers and men who fell in battle, the Founder performed funeral rites and sacrifice,

entries.zh: 昇明二年，除游擊將軍。
entries.en: In the second year of Shengming, he was appointed general who roams and strikes.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shengming, he was made General Who Roams and Strikes.

entries.zh: 沈攸之平，論封諸將，以僧靜爲興平縣侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: After Shen Youzhi was crushed, rewards were debated for the generals; Seng Jing was enfeoffed Marquis of Xingping at a thousand households.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi was pacified, merit enfeoffments were debated for the generals; Seng Jing was made Marquis of Xingping with a fief of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 太祖卽位，增邑千二百戶。
entries.en: When the founding emperor took the throne, his fief grew by twelve hundred households.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, his fief was increased by twelve hundred households.

entries.zh: 除南濟陰太守，本官如故。
entries.en: He was made administrator of southern Jiyin, his former rank unchanged.
entries.literal: He was made Administrator of Southern Jiyin, his former office unchanged.

entries.zh: 除輔國將軍，改封建昌，
entries.en: He was made general who supports the state and his fief was moved to Jianchang.
entries.literal: He was made General Who Supports the State and his title was changed to enfeoffment at Jianchang,

entries.zh: 建元二年，遷驍騎將軍，加員外常侍，轉太子左衞率。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianyuan, he was promoted to general of valiant cavalry, given supernumerary regular attendant, and made left guard of the heir.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he was promoted to General of Valiant Cavalry, given supernumerary regular attendant, and transferred to Left Guard of the Heir.

entries.zh: 僧靜同郡餘姚人陳胤叔，本名承叔，避宣帝諱改。
entries.en: Chen Yinchu of Yuyao, in the same commandery as Seng Jing, had borne the name Chengshu and changed it to avoid the taboo of Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: Chen Yinchu of Yuyao in the same commandery as Seng Jing—his original name was Chengshu, changed to avoid the taboo of Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 彊辯果捷，便刀楯。
entries.en: Sharp-tongued and quick with blade and shield.
entries.literal: Strong in debate, quick of hand with blade and shield.

entries.zh: 初爲左夾轂隊將。
entries.en: At first he was commander of the left flank-chariot company.
entries.literal: At first he was commander of the Left Flank-Chariot Company.

entries.zh: 泰始初，隨太祖東討，遂歸身隨從征伐，小心慎事，以功見賞。
entries.en: At the opening of the Taishi reign he followed the founding emperor east on campaign, then gave himself to the field; careful in every duty, he was rewarded for merit.
entries.literal: At the opening of Taishi he followed the Founder east on campaign, then gave himself to follow on expeditions; careful and attentive in affairs, he was rewarded for merit.

entries.zh: 封當陽縣子。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed viscount of Dangyang.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Dangyang.

entries.zh: 官至太子左率。
entries.en: His office rose to left guard of the heir.
entries.literal: His office rose to Left Guard of the Heir.

entries.zh: 啓世祖以鍜箭鏃用鐵多，不如鑄作。
entries.en: He reported to Shizu that hammered arrowheads eat too much iron and fall short of cast work.
entries.literal: He memorialized Shizu that forged arrowheads consume too much iron and are inferior to casting.

entries.zh: 東冶令張候伯以鑄＜金禁＞鈍，不合用，事不行，
entries.en: Zhang Houbo, magistrate of the Eastern Smelting Works, found the cast metal points blunt and unfit for use, and the plan was not adopted.
entries.literal: The magistrate of the Eastern Smelting Works, Zhang Houbo, found that the cast arrowheads came out dull and unfit for use; the proposal was not adopted,

entries.zh: 永明三年，卒。
entries.en: In the third year of Yongming, he died.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yongming, he died.

entries.zh: 世祖踐阼，出爲持節、督徐州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、北徐州刺史。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu succeeded, he went out as bearer of the staff, overseer of military affairs in Xu, general who chastises the foe, and governor of northern Xuzhou.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu succeeded, he went out as Bearer of the Staff, overseer of military affairs in Xu, General Who Chastises the Foe, and Governor of Northern Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 買牛給貧民令耕種，甚得荒情。
entries.en: He bought oxen for poor farmers to plow with and won deep goodwill among the frontier people.
entries.literal: He bought cattle and gave them to poor peasants for cultivation, winning much good will among the wasteland folk.

entries.zh: 遷給事中、太子右率。
entries.en: He was moved to palace attendant and right guard of the heir.
entries.literal: He was moved to Palace Attendant and Right Guard of the Heir.

entries.zh: 尋加通直常侍，
entries.en: Soon he was given the added title direct-and-plain regular attendant.
entries.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Direct-and-Plain Regular Attendant,

entries.zh: 永明五年，隷護軍陳顯達，討荒賊桓天生於比陽。
entries.en: In the fifth year of Yongming, he was placed under protector of the army Chen Xianda to campaign against the wasteland rebel Huan Tiansheng at Biyang.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming, he was placed under Protector of the Army Chen Xianda to campaign against the wasteland rebel Huan Tiansheng at Biyang.

entries.zh: 僧靜與平西司馬韓孟度、華山太守康元隆前進，未至比陽四十里，頓深橋。
entries.en: Seng Jing marched with pacifying-the-west staff officer Han Mengdu and Huashan administrator Kang Yuanlong. Still forty li from Biyang, they halted at Deep Bridge.
entries.literal: Seng Jing advanced with Pacifying-the-West staff officer Han Mengdu and Huashan Administrator Kang Yuanlong; forty li short of Biyang they halted at Shenqiao.

entries.zh: 天生引虜步騎十萬奄至，僧靜合戰大破之，殺獲萬計。
entries.en: Tiansheng brought a hundred thousand northern foot and horse in a sudden rush. Seng Jing met them and broke them utterly, killing and capturing by the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Tiansheng led a hundred thousand northern infantry and cavalry in a sudden onset; Seng Jing joined battle and routed them utterly, slaying and capturing by the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 天生退還比陽，僧靜進圍之。
entries.en: Tiansheng fell back on Biyang; Seng Jing pressed the siege.
entries.literal: Tiansheng fell back on Biyang; Seng Jing pressed on and besieged him.

entries.zh: 天生軍出城外，僧靜又擊破之，天生閉門不復出，僧靜力疲乃退。
entries.en: Tiansheng's men came out beyond the walls and Seng Jing beat them again. Tiansheng shut the gates and would not stir; only when Seng Jing's strength was spent did he pull back.
entries.literal: Tiansheng's army came outside the walls; Seng Jing defeated them again; Tiansheng shut the gates and would not come out; only when Seng Jing's strength was spent did he withdraw.

entries.zh: 除征虜將軍、南中郎司馬、淮南太守。
entries.en: He was made general who campaigns against the barbarians, chief of staff to the southern central commandant, and administrator of Huainan.
entries.literal: He was made General Who Campaigns Against the Barbarians, chief of staff of the Southern Central Commandant, and Administrator of Huainan.

entries.zh: 八年，巴東王子響殺僚佐，世祖召僧靜使領軍向江陵，僧靜面啓上曰：「巴東王年少，長史捉之太急，忿不思難故耳。
entries.en: In the eighth year Prince of Badong Zi Xiang killed his staff. Emperor Wu summoned Seng Jing to lead troops toward Jiangling. Seng Jing spoke to the throne: "The Prince of Badong is young; the chief administrator seized him too hard. Anger outran caution, that is all.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, Prince of Badong Zi Xiang killed his staff officers; Emperor Wu summoned Seng Jing to lead troops toward Jiangling. Seng Jing spoke to the throne in person: "The Prince of Badong is young; the chief administrator seized him too hastily—his fury outran his thought of consequences, that is all.

entries.zh: 天子兒過誤殺人，有何大罪。
entries.en: A son of the Son of Heaven who kills a man in a passing error—what grave crime is that?
entries.literal: A son of the Son of Heaven who kills a man in a passing error—what grave crime is there?

entries.zh: 官忽遣軍西上，人情惶懼，無所不至，僧靜不敢奉敕。」
entries.en: If the court suddenly sends armies west, panic will spread and worse may follow. I dare not obey."
entries.literal: If the court suddenly sends troops west, fear will run everywhere and worse may follow; I dare not accept this order."

entries.zh: 上不荅而心善之。
entries.en: The emperor gave no answer but was pleased in his heart.
entries.literal: The emperor did not reply but inwardly approved.

entries.zh: 徙爲廬陵王中軍司馬、高平太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was shifted to staff officer of the Prince of Luling's central army and administrator of Gaoping, his general rank unchanged.
entries.literal: He was shifted to staff officer of the Prince of Luling's central army and Administrator of Gaoping, his general rank unchanged.

entries.zh: 九年，卒。
entries.en: In the ninth year he died.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he died.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「僧靜志懷貞果，誠著艱難。
entries.en: An edict said: "Seng Jing's will was steadfast and his loyalty stood firm through hardship.
entries.literal: An edict read: "Seng Jing's will was steadfast and his loyalty proved in hardship.

entries.zh: 剋殄西墉，勳彰運始。
entries.en: He broke the western rampart; his merit shone at the dawn of the realm.
entries.literal: He crushed the western rampart; his merit shone at the founding hour.

entries.zh: 奄致殞喪，惻愴傷懷。
entries.en: Sudden death has taken him; sorrow cuts deep.
entries.literal: Sudden death has overtaken him; sorrow and grief wound the heart.

entries.zh: 賻錢五萬，布百匹。
entries.en: Funerary gift: fifty thousand cash, a hundred bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: Funerary gift: fifty thousand in cash, a hundred bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 諡壯侯。」
entries.en: Posthumous title: Marquis Zhuang."
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Marquis Zhuang."

entries.zh: 桓康，北蘭陵承人也。
entries.en: Huan Kang came from Cheng in North Lanling.
entries.literal: Huan Kang was a native of Cheng in North Lanling.

entries.zh: 勇果驍悍。
entries.en: He was bold, savage, and feared in the fight.
entries.literal: Brave, fierce, and valiant in battle.

entries.zh: 宋大明中，隨太祖爲軍容。
entries.en: Under Song's Daming reign he entered the Grand Ancestor's service on the army staff.
entries.literal: In the Daming era of Song he followed the Grand Ancestor as army equipage.

entries.zh: 從世祖在贛縣。
entries.en: He marched with Shizu at Gan county.
entries.literal: He followed Shizu at Gan county.

entries.zh: 泰始初，世祖起義，爲郡所縶，衆皆散。
entries.en: When Taishi opened and Shizu rose, the commandery seized him and his followers broke apart.
entries.literal: At the opening of Taishi, when Shizu raised the standard, the commandery bound him and his men scattered.

entries.zh: 康裝檐，一頭貯穆后，一頭貯文惠太子及竟陵王子良，自負置山中。
entries.en: Kang rigged shoulder-poles—Empress Mu in one basket, Crown Prince Wenhu and Prince Ziliang of Jingling in the other—and carried them himself into the mountains.
entries.literal: Kang rigged carrying-poles: one end held Empress Mu, the other the Crown Prince Wenhu and the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang; he bore them on his back and hid them in the hills.

entries.zh: 與門客蕭欣祖、楊瑑之、皐分喜、潛三奴、向思奴四十餘人相結，破郡獄出世祖。
entries.en: He joined Xiao Xinzu, Yang Zhuanzhi, Gao Fenxi, Qian San'nu, Xiang Sinu, and forty-odd other clients, smashed the county jail, and brought Shizu out.
entries.literal: With more than forty retainers—Xiao Xinzu, Yang Zhuanzhi, Gao Fenxi, Qian San'nu, Xiang Sinu, and the rest—he allied, broke the commandery prison, and freed Shizu.

entries.zh: 郡追兵急，康等死戰破之。
entries.en: The commandery's pursuers closed in; Kang and his band fought till they bled and drove them off.
entries.literal: Commandery pursuit troops pressed hard; Kang and his men fought to the death and broke them.

entries.zh: 隨世祖起義，摧堅陷陣，膂力絕人，所經村邑，恣行暴害。
entries.en: On Shizu's rising he tore through walled posts and enemy arrays, and no man could match his strength. Every hamlet on his road paid in plunder and fear.
entries.literal: Following Shizu in the uprising, he smashed strongpoints and broke enemy lines; his bodily strength was unmatched. In every village he passed he indulged in violence and outrage.

entries.zh: 江南人畏之，以其名怖小兒，畫其形以辟瘧，無不立愈。
entries.en: South of the Yangtze they dreaded his name and scared children with it; they painted his figure to break malaria, and the fever always broke.
entries.literal: The people of the south feared him; they used his name to frighten children, and painted his likeness to ward off malaria—none failed to recover at once.

entries.zh: 見擢爲世祖冠軍府參軍，除殿中將軍，武騎常侍，出補襄賁令。
entries.en: Shizu took him onto the champion staff, named him Palace General and Martial Cavalry Attendant-in-ordinary, and later sent him out as magistrate of Xiangben.
entries.literal: He was selected as a staff officer in Shizu's champion headquarters, made Palace General and Martial Cavalry Attendant-in-ordinary, then went out to serve as magistrate of Xiangben.

entries.zh: 桂陽事起，康棄縣還都就太祖，會事平，除員外郎。
entries.en: When Guiyang rose, Kang quit his post and hurried to the capital for the Grand Ancestor; after the trouble passed he received a supernumerary appointment.
entries.literal: When the Guiyang affair broke out, Kang abandoned his county and returned to the capital to join the Grand Ancestor; once the crisis was settled he was made supernumerary gentleman.

entries.zh: 除後軍將軍，直閤將軍，南濮陽太守，寧朔如故，
entries.en: He received Rear Army General, Direct Gate General, and southern Puyang, while General Who Tranquilizes the North stayed on his tally.
entries.literal: He was made Rear Army General, Direct Gate General, and administrator of southern Puyang; his rank as Tranquilizes the North stood unchanged,

entries.zh: 建元元年，封吳平縣伯，五百戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu Ping, with a fief of five hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wu Ping county, with a fief of five hundred households.

entries.zh: 轉輔國將軍，左軍將軍，游擊將軍，太守如故。
entries.en: He was shifted to General Who Assists the State, Left Army General, and Mobile-Strike General, still holding his prefecture.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General Who Assists the State, Left Army General, and Mobile-Strike General; his prefecture was unchanged.

entries.zh: 太祖謂康曰：「卿隨我日久，未得方伯，亦當未解我意，政欲與卿先共滅虜耳。」
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor said to Kang: "You have marched at my side for years without a commandery of your own—you may still miss my meaning. I want you beside me when we break the northerners."
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor told Kang: "You have followed me long without receiving a frontier post; you may still fail to read my mind. I mean to destroy the northerners with you first."

entries.zh: 虜動，遣康行，假節。
entries.en: When the barbarians moved, he sent Kang to the field with acting credentials.
entries.literal: When the northerners stirred, he sent Kang on campaign with acting credentials.

entries.zh: 尋進冠軍將軍。
entries.en: Before long he was raised to Champion General.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced to Champion General.

entries.zh: 三年春，於淮陽與虜戰，大破之，進兵攻陷虜樊諧城。
entries.en: In the third year's spring he met the northerners at Huaiyang, shattered them, and pressed on to storm Fan Xie.
entries.literal: In the spring of the third year he fought the northerners at Huaiyang, broke them utterly, and advanced to storm and take their fortress of Fan Xie.

entries.zh: 太祖喜，敕康迎淮北義民，不剋。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor rejoiced and told Kang to bring in the righteous bands north of the Huai; he could not break through.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor was pleased and ordered Kang to welcome the loyalists north of the Huai; he could not overcome the obstacles.

entries.zh: 明年，以康爲持節、督青冀二州東徐之東莞琅邪二郡朐山戍北徐之東海漣口戍諸軍事、青冀二州刺史，冠軍如故。
entries.en: The following year he went out with credentials to command Qing and Ji, eastern Xu's Dongguan and Langya, the Qushan post, and northern Xu's Donghai and Lian Mouth, as inspector of both provinces—Champion still on his title.
entries.literal: The next year Kang was made bearer of credentials, overseer of military affairs for Qing and Ji, eastern Xu's Dongguan and Langya, the Qushan garrison, and northern Xu's Donghai and Lian Mouth garrison, and inspector of Qing and Ji; his rank as Champion stood as before.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，轉驍騎將軍，復前軍郡。
entries.en: At Shizu's accession he became Valiant Cavalry General and regained his old front-army districts.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Kang was transferred to Valiant Cavalry General and restored to his former front-army commanderies.

entries.zh: 其年，卒。
entries.en: That same year he died.
entries.literal: That year he died.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「康昔預南勳，義兼常懷，倍深惻愴。
entries.en: The throne wrote: "Kang stood in the southern rising; his faith was long in our hearts, and his fall cuts twice as deep.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Kang once shared in the southern merit; his loyalty was always cherished, and our grief is doubly deep.

entries.zh: 凶事所須，厚加料理。」
entries.en: Whatever the rites required, the court would provide in full."
entries.literal: For the funeral, generous arrangements were to be made."

entries.zh: 年五十七。
entries.en: He was fifty-seven.
entries.literal: He was fifty-seven.

entries.zh: 子世榮，永明中爲巴東王防閤。
entries.en: His son Shirong, in the Yongming era, was guard to the Prince of Badong.
entries.literal: His son Shirong in Yongming served as guard to the Prince of Badong.

entries.zh: 子響事，世榮避奔雍州，世祖嘉之，以爲始興中兵參軍。
entries.en: When Prince Zixiang rebelled, Shirong ran to Yongzhou; Shizu commended him and named him middle staff officer of Shixing.
entries.literal: When Zixiang's affair broke out, Shirong fled to Yongzhou; Shizu praised him and made him middle staff officer of Shixing.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，除員外常侍，遷南中郎司馬，加寧朔將軍、南新蔡太守，
entries.en: At Shizu's accession he became supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, then Southern Center Army major, with Pacifying-the-North General and administrator of South Xincai added to his title.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Hu was made supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary, moved to Southern Center Army major, and given added rank as Pacifying-the-North General and Administrator of South Xincai,

entries.zh: 永明元年，徙爲安成王征虜司馬，餘官如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming, he was then shifted to Campaign-against-the-Barbarians major on the Prince of Ancheng's staff, his other offices unchanged.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he was transferred to Campaign-against-the-Barbarians major on the Prince of Ancheng's staff; his other posts were unchanged.

entries.zh: 明年，江州蠻動，敕虎領兵戍尋陽，板輔國將軍，伐蠻軍主。
entries.en: Next year the Jiangzhou tribes rose; the throne ordered Hu to hold Xunyang, raised him to Supporting-the-State General, and made him commander against the tribes.
entries.literal: The next year, when the Jiangzhou tribes rebelled, an edict had Hu lead troops to garrison Xunyang; he was appointed Supporting-the-State General and commander against the tribes.

entries.zh: 又領尋陽相。
entries.en: He also took charge of Xunyang prefecture.
entries.literal: He also held the prefecture of Xunyang.

entries.zh: 尋除游擊將軍，輔國、軍主如故。
entries.en: Before long he was named General of Mobile Warfare; his Supporting-the-State rank and tribal command stayed as they were.
entries.literal: Soon he was made General of Mobile Warfare; Supporting-the-State and tribal-war commander posts were unchanged.

entries.zh: 世祖以虎頭名鄙，敕改之。
entries.en: Shizu judged the childhood name Tiger Head coarse and commanded a change.
entries.literal: Shizu found the name Tiger Head vulgar and ordered it changed.

entries.zh: 七年，遷冠軍將軍，驍騎如故。
entries.en: In year 7 he was raised to Champion General; his Valiant Cavalry post stood.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Champion General; Valiant Cavalry was unchanged.

entries.zh: 明年，遷太子左率，轉西陽王冠軍司馬、廣陵太守。
entries.en: The year after, he became Crown Prince's Left Commander, then Champion major to the Prince of Xiyang and administrator of Guangling.
entries.literal: The next year he was promoted to Crown Prince's Left Commander, then shifted to Champion major on the Prince of Xiyang's staff and Administrator of Guangling.

entries.zh: 上敕虎曰：「廣陵須心腹，非吾意可委者，不可得處此任。」
entries.en: The emperor told Hu: "Guangling requires a bosom confidant; anyone I cannot sincerely entrust may not hold this post."
entries.literal: The emperor issued an edict to Hu: "Guangling requires a trusted intimate; one I cannot sincerely entrust may not hold this post."

entries.zh: 隨郡王子隆代巴東王子響爲荊州，備軍容西上，以虎爲輔國將軍、鎮西司馬、南平內史。
entries.en: Prince Zilong of Suizhou took Jingzhou from Prince Zixiang of Badong; the court sent the full martial train west and named Hu Supporting-the-State General, Pacify-the-West major, and interior administrator of Nanping.
entries.literal: When Prince Zilong of Suizhou replaced Prince Zixiang of Badong in Jingzhou, the court sent full military display westward and made Hu Supporting-the-State General, Pacify-the-West major, and interior administrator of Nanping.

entries.zh: 十一年，收雍州剌史王奐，敕領步騎數百，步道取襄陽。
entries.en: In year 11 Wang Huan, inspector of Yongzhou, was taken; Hu was ordered to lead a few hundred horse and foot by back paths into Xiangyang.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year Wang Huan, inspector of Yongzhou, was seized; an edict had Hu lead several hundred foot and horse by mountain paths to take Xiangyang.

entries.zh: 仍除持節、督梁南北秦沙四州諸軍事、西戎校尉、梁南秦二州刺史，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was then given credentials, command of the four provinces Liang, North Qin, South Qin, and Sha, the colonelcy of the Western Rong, and the two inspectorships of Liang and South Qin, while keeping his general ranks.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was made bearer of credentials, overseer of all military affairs in Liang, North and South Qin, and Sha's four provinces, Colonel of the Western Rong, and inspector of Liang and South Qin; his general posts were unchanged.

entries.zh: 尋進號征虜將軍。
entries.en: Before long his title rose to Campaign-against-the-Barbarians General.
entries.literal: Soon he was advanced to Campaign-against-the-Barbarians General.

entries.zh: 鬱林卽位，進號前將軍。
entries.en: At the Prince of Yulin's accession he was raised to Front General.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne, Hu was advanced to Front General.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，遷督雍州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、冠軍將軍、雍州刺史，
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang he took overall command of Yongzhou, Jingling in Yingzhou, and Suizhou in Sizhou, as Champion General and inspector of Yongzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was moved to oversee Yongzhou and Yingzhou's Jingling and Suizhou of Sizhou military affairs, as Champion General and inspector of Yongzhou,

entries.zh: 建武元年，進號右將軍。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu, his rank was raised to Right General.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, he was advanced to Right General.

entries.zh: 二年，進督爲監，進號平北將軍，爵爲侯，增邑三百戶。
entries.en: In year 2 his command became a superintendency; he was made Pacify-the-North General, enfeoffed as marquis, and given three hundred more households.
entries.literal: In the second year his overseer post became superintendent; he was advanced to Pacify-the-North General, enfeoffed as marquis, and his fief increased by three hundred households.

entries.zh: 薛淵
entries.en: Xue Yuan
entries.literal: Xue Yuan

entries.zh: 江謐字令和，濟陽考城人也。
entries.en: Jiang Mi, styled Linghe, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
entries.literal: Jiang Mi styled Linghe was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

entries.zh: 祖秉之，臨海太守，宋世清吏。
entries.en: His grandfather Bingzhi had been administrator of Linhai, a scrupulous officer under the Song.
entries.literal: His grandfather Bingzhi was administrator of Linhai, an upright officer of the Song.

entries.zh: 父徽，尚書都官郎，吳令，爲太初所殺。
entries.en: His father Hui served as an aide in the ministry of works' punishment bureau and as magistrate of Wu, and was slain in the Taichu reign.
entries.literal: His father Hui was an aide in the Ministry of Works' punishment bureau and magistrate of Wu, and was killed in the Taichu turmoil.

entries.zh: 謐繫尚方，孝武平京邑，乃得出。
entries.en: Mi was detained in the imperial workshops; when Emperor Xiaowu pacified the capital he was let out.
entries.literal: Mi was held in the imperial workshops; when Emperor Xiaowu pacified the capital region he was released.

entries.zh: 解褐奉朝請，輔國行參軍，于湖令，強濟稱職。
entries.en: On leaving lacquer he became attendant at court, acting aide to the general who supports the state, and magistrate of Yuhu—bold and capable, he was held to have done the office justice.
entries.literal: Leaving lacquer he became attendant at court, acting aide to the general who supports the state, and magistrate of Yuhu—resolute and able, he was praised as fit for his post.

entries.zh: 宋明帝爲南豫州，謐傾身奉之，爲帝所親待。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming of Song was posted at Southern Yu, Mi threw himself into the prince's service and won intimate favor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming of Song held Southern Yuzhou, Mi devoted himself wholly to the prince and was treated with close favor.

entries.zh: 卽位，以爲驃騎參軍。
entries.en: When the emperor took the throne, Mi was named aide to the general who spreads might.
entries.literal: Upon his accession, Mi was made aide to the general who spreads might.

entries.zh: 弟蒙貌醜，帝常召見狎侮之。
entries.en: His younger brother Meng had an ugly face; the emperor would often call him in to tease him familiarly.
entries.literal: His younger brother Meng was ugly of face; the emperor would often summon him for familiar mockery.

entries.zh: 太祖領南兖州，謐爲鎮軍長史、廣陵太守，入爲游擊將軍。
entries.en: When the Founder held Southern Yan, Mi was chief clerk of the army that guards the state and administrator of Guangling, then entered court as general of raiding attack.
entries.literal: When the Founder took Southern Yan, Mi was chief clerk of the army that guards the state and administrator of Guangling, then entered court as general of raiding attack.

entries.zh: 性流俗，善趨勢利。
entries.en: By nature he was commonplace and skilled at courting power and profit.
entries.literal: By nature he was commonplace and skilled at courting power and profit.

entries.zh: 元徽末，朝野咸屬意建平王景素，謐深自委結，景素事敗，僅得免禍。
entries.en: Late in the Yuanhui era court and countryside alike looked to Prince of Jianping Jingsu; Mi threw himself into a deep bond with him. When Jingsu's affair failed he barely escaped ruin.
entries.literal: Late in the Yuanhui era court and countryside alike looked to Prince of Jianping Jingsu; Mi threw himself into a deep bond with him. When Jingsu's affair failed he barely escaped disaster.

entries.zh: 蒼梧王廢後，物情尚懷疑惑，謐獨竭誠歸事太祖，以本官領尚書左丞。
entries.en: After the Prince of Cangwu was deposed, popular feeling still hung in doubt; Mi alone gave himself wholly to the Founder and, in his present office, also led the ministry as left vice director.
entries.literal: After the Prince of Cangwu was deposed, popular feeling still wavered in doubt; Mi alone gave himself wholly to the Founder and, in his present office, also led the ministry as left vice director.

entries.zh: 昇明元年，遷黃門侍郎，左丞如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Shengming he was moved to gentleman of the yellow gate, left vice director unchanged.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shengming he was moved to gentleman of the yellow gate, left vice director unchanged.

entries.zh: 沈攸之事起，議加太祖黃鉞，謐所建也。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi rose, the grant of the golden battle-axe to the Founder was Mi's proposal.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi's revolt broke out, the grant of the golden battle-axe to the Founder was Mi's proposal.

entries.zh: 事平，遷吏部郎，稍被親待。
entries.en: When the affair was settled he was moved to director of the ministry of personnel and gradually won intimate favor.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled he was moved to director of the ministry of personnel and gradually won intimate favor.

entries.zh: 遷太尉諮議，領錄事參軍。
entries.en: He was moved to adviser of the grand marshal and led the recording aide.
entries.literal: He was moved to adviser of the grand marshal and led the recording aide.

entries.zh: 齊臺建，爲右衞將軍。
entries.en: When the Qi regime was established he became general of the right guard.
entries.literal: When the Qi regime was established he became general of the right guard.

entries.zh: 建元元年，遷侍中，出爲臨川王平西長史、冠軍將軍、長沙內史、行湘州留事，先遣之鎮，旣而驃騎豫章王嶷領湘州，以謐爲長史，將軍、內史、知州留事如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Yi took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was moved to attendant, then went out as chief clerk on Prince of Linchuan's western-campaign staff, general who commands champions, interior administrator of Changsha, and acting head of Xiang while remaining in the province. He was sent to the command first; soon after, Prince of Yuzhang Yi took Xiang, and Mi was made his chief clerk, with general, interior administrator, and charge of the province while remaining unchanged.

entries.zh: 封永新縣伯，四百戶。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed baron of Yongxin, four hundred households.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed Baron of Yongxin, four hundred households.

entries.zh: 三年，爲左民尚書。
entries.en: In the third year he became minister of the left populace.
entries.literal: In the third year he became minister of the left populace.

entries.zh: 諸皇子出閤用文武主帥，皆以委謐。
entries.en: Whenever the imperial sons left the inner quarters and needed civil and military commanders, the choice fell to Mi.
entries.literal: Whenever the imperial sons left the inner quarters and needed civil and military commanders, the choice fell to Mi.

entries.zh: 尋敕曰：「江謐寒士，誠當不得競等華儕。
entries.en: Soon an edict said: "Jiang Mi is a man of humble birth and truly ought not to vie with the splendid peers.
entries.literal: Soon an edict said: "Jiang Mi is a man of humble birth and truly ought not to vie with the splendid peers.

entries.zh: 然甚有才幹，堪爲委遇，可遷掌吏部。」
entries.en: Yet he is very able and fit to be entrusted; he may be moved to head the ministry of personnel."
entries.literal: Yet he is very able and fit to be entrusted; he may be moved to head the ministry of personnel."

entries.zh: 初，太祖在淮南，伯玉假還廣陵，夢上廣陵城南樓上，有二青衣小兒語伯玉云：「草中肅，九五相追逐。」
entries.en: Early on, while the founding emperor was in Huainan, Boyu went home on leave to Guangling and dreamed he stood on the city's south tower; two boys in blue called to him, "Amid the grass, su—nine-fives in pursuit."
entries.literal: At first, while the founding emperor was in Huainan, Boyu took leave to Guangling and dreamed that he was on the south tower of Guangling city; two boys in blue said to Boyu: "Su in the grass; nine-fives pursue each other."

entries.zh: 伯玉視城下人頭上皆有草。
entries.en: He looked down and saw every man in the streets with grass on his head.
entries.literal: Boyu looked below the city and saw grass on every man's head.

entries.zh: 泰始七年，伯玉又夢太祖乘船在廣陵北渚，見上兩掖下有翅不舒。
entries.en: In Taishi year seven he dreamed again that the founding emperor sailed a boat at Guangling's north ford, wings folded under both arms.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi Boyu again dreamed that the founding emperor was in a boat at the north ford of Guangling and that under both armpits were wings not yet spread.

entries.zh: 伯玉問何當舒，上曰：「却後三年。」
entries.en: Boyu asked when they would open; the emperor said, "Three years hence."
entries.literal: Boyu asked when they would spread; the emperor said: "Three years from now."

entries.zh: 伯玉夢中自謂是呪師，向上唾呪之，凡六呪，有六龍出，兩掖下翅皆舒，還而復斂。
entries.en: In the dream Boyu thought himself a curse-master, spat six curses upward, six dragons rose, the wings under both arms opened, then folded shut again.
entries.literal: In the dream Boyu took himself for a curse-master, spat curses upward six times, six dragons emerged, the wings under both armpits spread and then closed again.

entries.zh: 元徽二年，而太祖破桂陽，威名大震。
entries.en: In Yuanhui year two the founding emperor broke Guiyang, and his name thundered across the realm.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui the founding emperor crushed Guiyang and his renown shook greatly.

entries.zh: 五年而廢蒼梧。
entries.en: Five years on, the throne cast down the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu.
entries.literal: After five years the Deposed Emperor of Cangwu was removed.

entries.zh: 太祖謂伯玉曰：「卿時乘之夢，今且效矣。」
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor told Boyu: "That dream of yours about riding—see how it is being fulfilled."
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor said to Boyu: "The dream you once had of riding—now it is coming true."

entries.zh: 謐才長刀筆，所在事辦。
entries.en: Mi's talent lay in clerical and legal work; wherever he was posted, affairs were handled.
entries.literal: Mi's talent lay in clerical and legal work; wherever he was posted, affairs were handled.

entries.zh: 太祖崩，謐稱疾不入，衆頗疑其怨不豫顧命也。
entries.en: When the Founder died, Mi claimed illness and did not attend; many suspected he resented not being named in the deathbed testament.
entries.literal: When the Founder died, Mi claimed illness and did not attend; many suspected he resented not being named in the deathbed testament.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，謐又不遷官，以此怨望。
entries.en: When Shizu took the throne, Mi was again not promoted, and from this he bore resentment.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Mi was again not promoted, and from this he bore resentment.

entries.zh: 時世祖不豫，謐詣豫章王嶷請閒曰：「至尊非起疾，東宮又非才，公今欲作何計？」
entries.en: At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Yi and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern-palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"
entries.literal: At the time Shizu was unwell; Mi went to Prince of Yuzhang Yi and asked for a private word, saying: "The Supreme One is not recovering from his illness, and the eastern palace heir lacks talent—what plan do you intend now?"

entries.zh: 世祖知之，出謐爲征虜將軍、鎮北長史、南東海太守。
entries.en: Shizu learned of it and sent Mi out as general who campaigns against barbarians, chief clerk of the army that guards the north, and administrator of Southern Donghai.
entries.literal: Shizu learned of it and sent Mi out as general who campaigns against barbarians, chief clerk of the army that guards the north, and administrator of Southern Donghai.

entries.zh: 未發，上使御史中丞沈沖奏謐前後罪曰：「謐少懷輕躁，長習諂薄，交無義合，行必利動。
entries.en: Before he set out, the throne had the censor-in-chief Shen Chong impeach Mi's offenses past and present, saying: "From youth Mi has harbored levity and rashness; grown, he has made a habit of flattery and shallowness. His associations lack righteous bond; his conduct always follows profit.
entries.literal: Before he set out, the throne had the censor-in-chief Shen Chong impeach Mi's offenses past and present, saying: "From youth Mi has harbored levity and rashness; grown, he has made a habit of flattery and shallowness. His associations lack righteous bond; his conduct always follows profit.

entries.zh: 特以奕世更局，見擢宋朝，而阿諛內外，貨賂公行，咎盈憲簡，戾彰朝聽，輿金輦寶，取容近習。
entries.en: His line had merely ridden a change of dynasties into Song service, yet he flattered court and camp alike, bribes ran in the open, fault piled up in the statutes, outrage broke through at every hearing, and he hauled gold and jewels to buy favor from the emperor's intimates.
entries.literal: Only because generations had changed dynasties was he advanced under the Song; yet he flattered inside and out, gifts and bribes ran openly, faults overflowed the legal records, offenses showed in court hearings, and he carted gold and lavished treasures to win favor from intimate attendants.

entries.zh: 以沈攸之地勝兵強，終當得志，委心託身，歲暮相結。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi held rich lands and a strong army, Mi judged that he would prevail in the end and threw in his lot, binding himself to him as the year closed.
entries.literal: Because Shen Youzhi's territory was strong in troops and would in the end prevail, he entrusted heart and body and bonded with him at year's end.

entries.zh: 以劉景素親屬望重，物應樂推，獻誠薦子，窺窬非望。
entries.en: When Liu Jingsu, Prince Jingsu of Jianping, stood high in kinship and men were ready to lift him, Mi offered his loyalty, pushed forward his son, and eyed what was not his to take.
entries.literal: Because Liu Jingsu, as imperial kin, bore heavy expectation and the world ought to joyously raise him, he offered sincerity and recommended his son, peering at improper ambition.

entries.zh: 時艱網漏，得全首領。
entries.en: In those troubled days the law had gaps, and he alone kept his head.
entries.literal: Times were hard and the net had holes; he kept his head.

entries.zh: 太祖匡飭天地，方弘遠圖，薄其難洗之瑕，許其革音之效，加以非分之寵，推以不次之榮，列迹勳良，比肩朝德。
entries.en: The founding emperor was setting heaven and earth in order and laying distant plans; he passed over stains that would not wash clean, credited Mi with a change of heart, heaped on him favor beyond his due, raised him to honors out of turn, and ranked him among the meritorious, shoulder to shoulder with the court's best.
