entries.literal: The founding emperor was rectifying heaven and earth and opening a far-reaching design; he overlooked stains hard to wash away, granted the effect of reforming his tone, added favor beyond measure, pushed unscheduled glory, ranked him among meritorious worthies, and set him shoulder to shoulder with court virtue.

entries.zh: 以往者微勤，刀筆小用，賞廁河山，任忝出入。
entries.en: For trifling past service and a knack with the brush he was enfeoffed among river and hill, and given posts he was unfit to hold at court.
entries.literal: For past slight diligence and petty clerkly use he was rewarded with enfeoffment in river and mountain, and office unworthy of moving in and out of court.

entries.zh: 輕險之性，在貴彌彰；
entries.en: His reckless, treacherous temper grew only sharper once he rose;
entries.literal: A nature of lightness and danger showed all the more once he was elevated;

entries.zh: 貪昧之情，雖富無滿。
entries.en: his greed, for all his wealth, was never filled.
entries.literal: greedy obtuseness, though rich, was never satisfied.

entries.zh: 重莅湘部，顯行斷盜；
entries.en: Posted again to Xiang, he openly plundered and stole;
entries.literal: Returning again to the Xiang command he openly practiced extortion and robbery;

entries.zh: 及居銓衡，肆意受納。
entries.en: and once he held the ministry scales he took gifts as he pleased.
entries.literal: when he took the personnel scales he accepted bribes at will.

entries.zh: 連席同乘，皆詖黷舊侶；
entries.en: Whoever shared his mat or his carriage was an old crony grown bold in presumption;
entries.literal: Those who shared mat and carriage were all sycophantic old companions;

entries.zh: 密筵閑讌，必貨賄常客。
entries.en: at private feasts he always paid off the men who kept coming back.
entries.literal: at secret feasts and leisurely banquets he always bribed his regular guests.

entries.zh: 理合升進者，以爲己惠；
entries.en: Men who deserved promotion he treated as personal debts owed to him;
entries.literal: Whoever by reason ought to be promoted he treated as a personal favor;

entries.zh: 事宜貶退者，竝稱中旨。
entries.en: men who ought to fall he dismissed as carrying out the throne's will.
entries.literal: whoever by affairs ought to be demoted he all declared to match the center's intent.

entries.zh: 謂販鬻威權，姦自不露，欺主罔上，謗議可掩。
entries.en: He believed he could trade in power without exposure, deceive his sovereign and hoodwink his superiors, and smother every whisper against him.
entries.literal: He thought that selling power and authority, his wickedness would not show, that deceiving the lord and deceiving superiors, slander could be covered.

entries.zh: 先帝寢疾彌留，人神憂震。
entries.en: When the late emperor lay long in his sickness, heaven and earth trembled with fear.
entries.literal: The former emperor's illness lingered; men and spirits were shaken with alarm.

entries.zh: 謐託病私舍，曾無變容。
entries.en: Mi pleaded illness at home and never once altered his face.
entries.literal: Mi feigned illness in a private residence and never once changed expression.

entries.zh: 國諱經旬，甫蹔入殿，參訪遺詔，覘忖時旨。
entries.en: Not until mourning had run ten days did he slip into the hall, inquire after the testament, and probe what the moment would bear.
entries.literal: National mourning ran ten days before he briefly entered the hall, consulted on the surviving will, and peered at the timely intent.

entries.zh: 以身列朝流，宜蒙兼帶，先顧不逮，舊位無加，遂崇飾惡言，肆醜縱悖，譏誹朝政，訕毀皇猷，徧蚩忠賢，歷詆台相。
entries.en: As a man of standing in court he should have gained added offices; when favor passed him by and his old rank stood still, he dressed up malice, let loose every ugly excess, mocked the government, defamed the throne's design, slandered loyal men wherever he could, and tore down the ministers one after another.
entries.literal: As one ranked in the court stream he ought to have received concurrent posts; early care did not reach him and his old rank was not raised, so he exalted wicked words, unleashed ugliness and rash rebellion, mocked court administration, defamed the imperial design, everywhere slandered loyal worthies, and repeatedly slandered ministry chancellors.

entries.zh: 至於蕃岳入授，列代恒規，勳戚出撫，前王彝則。
entries.en: Princes entering court to receive their charge was the rule of age after age; kinsmen of merit going out to govern was the law the former kings had set.
entries.literal: As for feudal princes entering to receive instruction, that was the constant rule of successive generations; merit kin going out to soothe was the former kings' permanent law.

entries.zh: 而謐妄發樞機，坐構囂論。
entries.en: Yet Mi meddled with the hinges of power and sat stirring noisy quarrels.
entries.literal: Yet Mi rashly raised pivotal mechanisms and sat constructing clamorous debate.

entries.zh: 復敢貶謗儲后，不顧辭端，毀折宗王，每窮舌杪。
entries.en: He dared again to run down the heir, reckless of how far his words went, and bent and broke the imperial princes until his tongue had no room left to twist.
entries.literal: Again he dared denigrate the heir apparent, heedless of rhetorical edge, ruined and bent imperial clan princes, and every time drove speech to the tip of the tongue.

entries.zh: 皆云誥誓乖禮，崇樹失宜，仰指天，俯畫地，希幸災故，以申積憤。
entries.en: He cried that edicts and oaths broke ritual, that honors and appointments were wrong; he pointed at heaven, traced lines on the earth, and prayed for disaster to pour out the spite he had stored up.
entries.literal: All said imperial commands and oaths violated ritual, that elevation and planting were improper; pointing up at heaven and drawing on the earth below, he hoped for calamity and disaster to vent accumulated resentment.

entries.zh: 犯上之迹旣彰，反噬之情已著。
entries.en: His defiance of superiors was plain to see; his urge to turn and bite was plain as well.
entries.literal: Signs of offending superiors were already clear; the will to bite back was already plain.

entries.zh: 請免官削爵土，收送廷尉獄治罪。」
entries.en: We ask that he be removed from office, stripped of his fief, seized, and sent to the Minister of Justice for trial."
entries.literal: We ask that he be dismissed from office, his fief lands stripped, seized and sent to the Minister of Justice prison for punishment."

entries.zh: 詔賜死，時年五十二。
entries.en: An edict ordered him to take his own life. He was fifty-two.
entries.literal: An edict granted death by suicide; he was fifty-two.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮淮陰，伯玉歸身結事，爲太祖冠軍刑獄參軍。
entries.en: While the founding emperor was posted at Huaiyin, Boyu threw himself on his service and became adjutant for prisons under the champion army.
entries.literal: When the founding emperor held Huaiyin, Boyu pledged himself and served him, and was made the founding emperor's Champion Army adjutant for prisons and punishment.

entries.zh: 太祖爲明帝所疑，及徵爲黃門郎，深懷憂慮。
entries.en: The founding emperor fell under Emperor Ming's suspicion; when the summons came to make him a yellow gate gentleman, his heart was full of dread.
entries.literal: The founding emperor was suspected by Emperor Ming; when he was summoned as Yellow Gate Gentleman he was deeply anxious.

entries.zh: 伯玉勸太祖遣數十騎入虜界，安置標榜，於是虜游騎數百履行界上，太祖以聞，猶懼不得留，令伯玉卜，伯玉斷卦不成行，而明帝詔果復太祖本任，由是見親待。
entries.en: Boyu urged him to send a few dozen riders into the northern marches and set up boundary markers; soon hundreds of enemy patrols were riding the line. The founding emperor reported it, yet still feared the court would recall him and had Boyu cast the hexagrams; Boyu read that the journey would not succeed, and Emperor Ming's edict in fact restored him to his old command. From that day he was held close.
entries.literal: Boyu urged the founding emperor to send several dozen horsemen into the enemy frontier to set up markers; thereupon several hundred enemy patrol horsemen rode the border. The founding emperor reported it, yet still feared he could not remain; he had Boyu divine, and Boyu read the hexagram as unfit to travel; Emperor Ming's edict indeed restored the founding emperor to his former post, and from this he was treated with intimacy.

entries.zh: 從太祖還都，除奉朝請。
entries.en: When the founding emperor returned to the capital, Boyu was made a palace scholar.
entries.literal: Following the founding emperor back to the capital, he was appointed Palace Scholar.

entries.zh: 令伯玉看宅，知家事。
entries.en: The founding emperor set him to watch the mansion and run the household.
entries.literal: The founding emperor had Boyu watch the residence and manage household affairs.

entries.zh: 世祖罷廣興還，立別宅，遣人於大宅掘樹數株，伯玉不與，馳以聞。
entries.en: When Shizu left Guangxing and came back he built a separate house and sent men to dig up several trees from the main estate; Boyu refused and rode at once to report it.
entries.literal: When Shizu ended Guangxing and returned, he established a separate residence and sent men to dig up several trees from the great mansion; Boyu would not allow it and hurried to report.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「卿執之是也。」
entries.en: The founding emperor said, "You were right to stand firm."
entries.literal: The founding emperor said: "Your holding firm is right."

entries.zh: 轉太祖平南府，晉熙王府參軍。
entries.en: He was moved to the pacify-the-south headquarters and made staff officer in the Prince of Jinxi's household.
entries.literal: He was shifted to the founding emperor's Pacify-the-South headquarters and staff officer of the Prince of Jinxi's mansion.

entries.zh: 太祖爲南兖州，伯玉轉爲上鎮軍中兵參軍，帶廣陵令。
entries.en: When the founding emperor took southern Yanzhou, Boyu became adjutant of the upper camp and served concurrently as magistrate of Guangling.
entries.literal: When the founding emperor held southern Yanzhou, Boyu became adjutant of the upper camp army and concurrently magistrate of Guangling.

entries.zh: 除羽林監，不拜。
entries.en: He was named director of the feathered forest and declined the post.
entries.literal: He was appointed Director of the Feathered Forest and did not accept.

entries.zh: 上嘉伯玉盡心，愈見親信，軍國密事，多委使之。
entries.en: The throne prized Boyu's wholehearted service and drew him closer still; military and state secrets went largely through his hands.
entries.literal: The throne praised Boyu's wholehearted service and trusted him all the more; military and state secrets were largely entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 時人爲之語曰：「十敕五令，不如荀伯玉命。」
entries.en: A saying ran: "Ten throne edicts and five orders weigh less than one word from Xun Boyu."
entries.literal: Men of the time made a saying of it: "Ten imperial edicts and five orders are not as good as one command from Xun Boyu."

entries.zh: 世祖深怨伯玉。
entries.en: Shizu hated Boyu to the bone.
entries.literal: Shizu deeply resented Boyu.

entries.zh: 上臨崩，指伯玉謂世祖曰：「此人事我忠，我身後，人必爲其作口過，汝勿信也。
entries.en: On his deathbed the throne pointed at Boyu and told Shizu: "This man was loyal to me; after I am gone men will surely slander him—do not heed them.
entries.literal: As the throne lay dying he pointed at Boyu and told Shizu: "This man served me with loyalty; after I am gone people will surely speak ill of him—do not believe them.

entries.zh: 可令往東宮長侍白澤，小却以南兖州處之。」
entries.en: Send him to the Eastern Palace as chief attendant to Baize; later, with a small step down, give him southern Yanzhou."
entries.literal: You may have him go to the Eastern Palace as chief attendant to Baize; later, with a slight demotion, place him in southern Yanzhou."

entries.zh: 世祖在東宮，專斷用事，頗不如法。
entries.en: While Shizu was crown prince he ruled the Eastern Palace by fiat, and much of what he did sat outside the law.
entries.literal: While Shizu held the Eastern Palace he acted on his own authority and largely outside the law.

entries.zh: 任左右張景真，使領東宮主衣食官穀帛，賞賜什物，皆御所服用。
entries.en: He put his favorite Zhang Jingzhen in charge of the Eastern Palace commissaries for food, clothing, grain, and cloth; every gift and good was of the kind reserved for the inner palace.
entries.literal: He entrusted his favorite Zhang Jingzhen and had him oversee the Eastern Palace offices for food, clothing, grain, and cloth; rewards and goods were all of the sort the inner palace used.

entries.zh: 景真於南澗寺捨身齋，有元徽紫皮袴褶，餘物稱是。
entries.en: Jingzhen took a body-offering fast at Nanjian Temple in Yuanhui purple leather coat and trousers, with the rest of his gear to match.
entries.literal: At Nanjian Temple Jingzhen held a body-offering fast; he wore Yuanhui-era purple leather trousers and jacket, and his other things matched them.

entries.zh: 於樂遊設會，伎人皆著御衣。
entries.en: He held a feast at Leyou, and every performer wore robes from the imperial wardrobe.
entries.literal: At Leyou he gave a feast, and the performers all wore imperial dress.

entries.zh: 又度絲錦與崑崙舶營貨，輙使傳令防送過南州津。
entries.en: He also shipped silk brocade to Kunlun merchant vessels for trade, and each time had runners posted to see the cargo through the Southern Province crossing.
entries.literal: He also sent silk brocade out to Kunlun ships for trade, and whenever he did so he had runners posted to escort the goods past the Southern Province ferry.

entries.zh: 世祖拜陵還，景真白服乘畫舴艋，坐胡牀，觀者咸疑是太子。
entries.en: On Shizu's return from the tombs, Jingzhen went in white, rode a painted skiff, and lolled on a camp-chair; the crowd mistook him for the crown prince.
entries.literal: When Shizu returned from paying respects at the tombs, Jingzhen wore white dress, rode a painted skiff, and sat on a folding camp-chair; onlookers all took him for the crown prince.

entries.zh: 內外祗畏，莫敢有言。
entries.en: Court and capital alike stood in awe, and no one dared raise a word.
entries.literal: Inside and outside the palace all stood in awe, and none dared speak.

entries.zh: 伯玉謂親人曰：「太子所爲，官終不知，豈得顧死蔽官耳目。
entries.en: Boyu told his family: "The crown prince is doing what the throne will never hear of in the end—who dies to blind the court to it?
entries.literal: Boyu told his kin: "What the crown prince is doing, the throne will never know of in the end—how can one choose death to cover the throne's eyes and ears?

entries.zh: 我不啓聞，誰應啓者？」
entries.en: If I do not speak, who will?"
entries.literal: If I do not report it, who should?"

entries.zh: 因世祖拜陵後密啓之。
entries.en: So after Shizu came back from the tombs he sent a secret memorial.
entries.literal: Accordingly, after Shizu returned from the tombs he secretly memorialized the throne.

entries.zh: 上大怒，檢校東宮。
entries.en: The throne flew into a rage and sent men to search the Eastern Palace.
entries.literal: The throne was furious and inspected the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: 世祖還至方山，日暮將泊。
entries.en: Shizu came back as far as Mount Fang and at dusk meant to put in.
entries.literal: Shizu returned as far as Mount Fang; at dusk he was about to moor.

entries.zh: 豫章王於東府乘飛東迎，具白上怒之意。
entries.en: The Prince of Yuzhang came out from the Eastern Mansion on Flying East to meet him and told him plainly how furious the throne was.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, from the Eastern Mansion, rode Flying East to meet him and fully explained the throne's anger.

entries.zh: 世祖夜歸，上亦停門籥待之，二更盡，方入宮。
entries.en: Shizu came in by night; the throne kept the gates barred open for him, and not until the second watch was spent did he enter the palace.
entries.literal: Shizu returned that night; the throne too held the gate-bars open waiting for him, and only after the second watch had ended did he enter the palace.

entries.zh: 上明日遣文惠太子、聞喜公子良宣敕，以景真罪狀示世祖。
entries.en: Next day the throne sent Crown Prince Wenhu and Prince Ziliang of Wenxi to read the edict and lay Jingzhen's crimes before Shizu.
entries.literal: The next day the throne sent Crown Prince Wenhu and Prince Ziliang of Wenxi to proclaim the edict and show Shizu Jingzhen's offenses.

entries.zh: 稱太子令，收景真殺之。
entries.en: In the crown prince's name they took Jingzhen in and killed him.
entries.literal: In the crown prince's name Jingzhen was seized and killed.

entries.zh: 世祖憂懼，稱疾月餘日。
entries.en: Shizu lived in fear and pleaded illness for more than a month.
entries.literal: Shizu was anxious and afraid, and pleaded illness for more than a month.

entries.zh: 上怒不解。
entries.en: The throne's wrath would not break.
entries.literal: The throne's anger did not lift.

entries.zh: 晝卧太陽殿，王敬則直入，叩頭啓上曰：「官有天下日淺，太子無事被責，人情恐懼，願官往東宮解釋之。」
entries.en: At noon he lay down in the Hall of the Great Sun. Wang Jingze walked straight in, kowtowed, and said: "Your Majesty has had the realm only a little while; the crown prince was punished without cause, and hearts are afraid—go to the Eastern Palace and make peace."
entries.literal: At midday he lay down in the Hall of the Great Sun; Wang Jingze entered straight in, knocked his head to the floor, and reported: "Your Majesty has held the realm only a short while; the crown prince has been blamed without cause, and men's hearts are afraid—may Your Majesty go to the Eastern Palace and set things right."

entries.zh: 太祖乃幸宮，召諸王以下於玄圃園爲家宴，致醉乃還。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor then went to the palace, called every prince down to a family feast in the Mystic Garden, and left only when all were drunk.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor then visited the palace, summoned all the princes down to a family feast in the Mystic Garden, and only when all were drunk did he return.

entries.zh: 昇明初，仍爲太祖驃騎中兵參軍，除步兵校尉，不拜。
entries.en: When Shengming opened he again held central-troop aide in the Grand Ancestor's marshal staff; Colonel of the Footsoldiers was offered, and he declined.
entries.literal: At the opening of Shengming he again served the Grand Ancestor as central-troop aide in the Marshal's headquarters; he was named Colonel of the Footsoldiers but did not accept.

entries.zh: 仍帶濟陽太守，中兵如故。
entries.en: He still carried Jiyang as concurrent prefect; his central-troop duty was unchanged.
entries.literal: He still held concurrent office as administrator of Jiyang; his central-troop post stood unchanged.

entries.zh: 霸業旣建，伯玉忠勤盡心，常衞左右。
entries.en: When the founding cause was won, Boyu gave himself over in loyal, tireless service and never left the Grand Ancestor's side.
entries.literal: Once the founding enterprise was secure, Boyu served with loyal, tireless devotion and constantly guarded the Grand Ancestor's person.

entries.zh: 加前軍將軍。
entries.en: He was raised to Front Army General.
entries.literal: He was advanced to Front Army General.

entries.zh: 隨太祖太尉府轉中兵，將軍、太守如故。
entries.en: With the Grand Ancestor's transfer to the Grand Commandant's office, Boyu moved to the central troops; his general's title and prefecture stayed the same.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor moved to the Grand Commandant's mansion, Boyu was shifted to central troops; his general's rank and prefecture stood as before.

entries.zh: 建元元年，封南豐縣子，四百戶。
entries.en: In Jianyuan's first year he was enfeoffed Viscount of Nanfeng, with four hundred households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Nanfeng, with a fief of four hundred households.

entries.zh: 轉輔國將軍，武陵王征虜司馬，太守如故。
entries.en: He became General Who Assists the State and army aide to the Prince of Wuling on the Pacify-the-Barbarians staff, still holding his prefecture.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General Who Assists the State and army aide on the Prince of Wuling's Pacify-the-Barbarians staff; his prefecture was unchanged.

entries.zh: 徙爲安成王冠軍司馬，轉豫章王司空諮議，太守如故。
entries.en: He was shifted to champion aide for the Prince of Ancheng, then to staff adviser to the Prince of Yuzhang as Minister of Works, with his prefecture unchanged.
entries.literal: He was moved to champion army aide for the Prince of Ancheng, then to staff adviser under the Prince of Yuzhang as Minister of Works; his prefecture stood as before.

entries.zh: 伯玉遭父憂，除冠軍將軍、南濮陽太守，未拜，除黃門郎，本官如故。
entries.en: In mourning for his father Boyu was named Champion General and southern Puyang; before he took up the post he was named Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, his other titles unchanged.
entries.literal: When Boyu entered mourning for his father he was named Champion General and administrator of southern Puyang; before he could accept he was named Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, his former offices standing as before.

entries.zh: 世祖轉爲豫章王太尉諮議，太守如故。
entries.en: Shizu transferred him to staff adviser under the Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant; his prefecture was unchanged.
entries.literal: Shizu transferred him to be staff adviser to the Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Commandant; his prefecture stood as before.

entries.zh: 俄遷散騎常侍，太守如故。
entries.en: Before long he was shifted to Regular Attendant, still holding his prefecture.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved to Regular Attendant; his prefecture stood as before.

entries.zh: 伯玉憂懼無計，上聞之，以其與垣崇祖善，慮相扇爲亂，加意撫之，伯玉乃安。
entries.en: Boyu was trapped in fear. The throne heard of it; knowing his tie to Yuan Chongzu, he feared the two would rouse each other to revolt and soothed him with special care—only then did Boyu grow calm.
entries.literal: Boyu was anxious and at his wits' end; when the throne heard of it, because he was close to Yuan Chongzu he feared they would stir each other to revolt and treated him with added care—only then did Boyu settle.

entries.zh: 永明元年，垣崇祖誅，伯玉并伏法。
entries.en: In Yongming's first year Yuan Chongzu was killed, and Boyu died by the same sentence.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, Yuan Chongzu was executed, and Boyu was put to death with him.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷三十一‧列傳第十二
entries.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 31 — Biography 12
entries.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 31 — Biography 12

entries.zh: 琨少謹篤，爲從伯司徒謐所愛。
entries.en: From youth Kun was careful and steadfast, and his father's cousin Grand Steward Mi doted on him.
entries.literal: Kun from youth was careful and steadfast, and was beloved by his father's cousin, Grand Steward Mi.

entries.zh: 宋永初中，武帝以其娶桓脩女，除郎中，駙馬都尉，奉朝請。
entries.en: At the opening of the Song Yongchu era, Emperor Wu, because Kun had married Huan Xiu's daughter, named him gentleman of the palace, commandant-escort for the imperial son-in-law, and attendant at court.
entries.literal: In the beginning of the Yongchu era under Song, Emperor Wu, because Kun had married the daughter of Huan Xiu, appointed him gentleman of the palace, commandant-escort for the imperial son-in-law, and attendant at court.

entries.zh: 元嘉初，從兄侍中華有權寵，以門戶衰弱，待琨如親，數相稱薦。
entries.en: Early in Yuanjia his cousin Hua, attendant-in-chief, held power and favor; with the clan's standing enfeebled, he treated Kun as close kin and often praised him for office.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia his cousin Hua, attendant-in-chief, held power and favor; because the family standing was weak, he treated Kun as kin and often spoke him up for recommendation.

entries.zh: 爲尚書儀曹郎，州治中。
entries.en: He became a gentleman in the ministry of rites' ceremony bureau and a provincial aide.
entries.literal: He became a gentleman in the ministry of rites' ceremony bureau and provincial aide.

entries.zh: 累至左軍諮議，領錄事，出爲宣城太守，司徒從事中郎，義興太守。
entries.en: He rose by stages to left-army adviser, leading the recording aide, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng, gentleman-attendant of the grand steward, and administrator of Yixing.
entries.literal: He rose in stages to left-army adviser, with charge as recording aide, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng, gentleman-attendant of the grand steward, and administrator of Yixing.

entries.zh: 歷任皆廉約。
entries.en: In every post he was frugal and sparing.
entries.literal: In every post he was frugal and sparing.

entries.zh: 還爲北中郎長史，黃門郎，寧朔將軍，東陽太守。
entries.en: He returned as chief clerk of the northern central commandant, gentleman of the yellow gate, general who stills the north, and administrator of Dongyang.
entries.literal: He returned to serve as chief clerk of the northern central commandant, gentleman of the yellow gate, general who stills the north, and administrator of Dongyang.

entries.zh: 孝建初，遷廷尉卿，竟陵王驃騎長史，加臨淮太守，轉吏部郎。
entries.en: At the opening of Xiaojian he was moved to director of the court of justice, chief clerk to Prince of Jingling's grand marshal, with added duty as administrator of Linhuai, then transferred to director of the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was moved to director of the court of justice, chief clerk to Prince of Jingling's grand marshal, with added duty as administrator of Linhuai, then transferred to director of the ministry of personnel.

entries.zh: 吏曹選局，貴要多所屬請，琨自公卿下至士大夫，例爲用兩門生。
entries.en: In the personnel bureau's selection office the great often pressed requests for their clients; Kun, from grand ministers down to gentlemen-scholars, as a rule took on only two local recruits.
entries.literal: In the personnel bureau's selection office the powerful often submitted requests on behalf of others; Kun, from grand ministers down to gentlemen-scholars, as a rule employed only two local recruits.

entries.zh: 江夏王義恭嘗屬琨用二人，後復遣屬琨，答不許。
entries.en: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong once asked Kun to place two men; when he sent the request again, Kun refused.
entries.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong once asked Kun to employ two men; later he sent another request, and Kun answered that he would not grant it.

entries.zh: 明帝臨崩，出爲督會稽東陽新安臨海永嘉五郡軍事、左軍將軍、會稽太守，常侍如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming lay dying, Kun was sent out as supervisor of military affairs for Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, general of the left army, and administrator of Kuaiji, attendant unchanged.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming lay dying, Kun was sent out as supervisor of military affairs for the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, general of the left army, and administrator of Kuaiji, attendant-in-chief unchanged.

entries.zh: 坐誤竟囚，降號冠軍。
entries.en: For an error involving a prisoner whose term had run out, he was reduced in rank to general who commands champions.
entries.literal: Because of an error involving a prisoner who had completed his sentence, he was reduced in rank to general who commands champions.

entries.zh: 元徽中，遷金紫光祿，弘訓太僕，常侍如故。
entries.en: In the Yuanhui era he was moved to grand master for splendid virtue with golden seal and purple ribbon, grand coachman of glorious instruction, attendant unchanged.
entries.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was moved to grand master for splendid virtue with golden seal and purple ribbon, grand coachman of glorious instruction, attendant unchanged.

entries.zh: 本州中正，加特進。
entries.en: He was comparison bureau chief for his home province, with added extraordinary promotion.
entries.literal: He was comparison bureau chief for his home province, with added extraordinary promotion.

entries.zh: 從帝卽位，進右光祿大夫，常侍餘如故。
entries.en: When the deposed emperor took the throne, Kun was advanced to right splendid-virtue grand master, his attendancies otherwise unchanged.
entries.literal: When the deposed emperor took the throne, Kun was advanced to grand master for splendid virtue of the right, attendancies otherwise unchanged.

entries.zh: 從帝遜位，琨陪位及辭廟，皆流涕。
entries.en: When the deposed emperor yielded the throne, Kun was present at the investiture and at the farewell at the ancestral temple, and wept both times.
entries.literal: When the deposed emperor yielded the throne, Kun was present at the investiture and at the farewell at the ancestral temple, and wept both times.

entries.zh: 太祖卽位，領武陵王師，加侍中，給親信二十人。
entries.en: When the Founder took the throne, Kun led Prince of Wuling's tutoring staff, with added attendant-in-chief, and was given twenty intimate guardsmen.
entries.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Kun led Prince of Wuling's tutoring staff, with added attendant-in-chief, and was given twenty intimate guardsmen.

entries.zh: 時王儉爲宰相，屬琨用東海郡迎吏。
entries.en: At the time Wang Jian was prime minister and asked Kun to place the welcome officer of Donghai commandery.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Jian was prime minister and asked Kun to employ the welcome officer of Donghai commandery.

entries.zh: 琨謂信人曰：「語郎，三臺五省，皆是郎用人；
entries.en: Kun told a trusted man: "Tell the gentleman: the Three Platforms and Five Bureaus are all places where the gentleman places his men;
entries.literal: Kun told a trusted man: "Tell the gentleman: the Three Platforms and Five Bureaus are all places where the gentleman places his men;

entries.zh: 外方小郡，當乞寒賤，省官何容復奪之。」
entries.en: a petty outer commandery ought to beg for someone humble and poor—how can a court officer be allowed to seize him again?"
entries.literal: a petty outer commandery ought to beg for someone humble and poor—how can a court officer be allowed to seize him again?"

entries.zh: 遂不過其事。
entries.en: And so he did not forward the matter.
entries.literal: And so he did not forward the matter.

entries.zh: 明帝初，四方反，帝以岱堪幹舊才，除使持節、督西豫州諸軍事、輔國將軍、西豫州刺史。
entries.en: When Mingdi first took the throne and rebellion flared on every side, the emperor deemed Dai a tested man of affairs and named him bearer of the staff, commander of western Yuzhou, general who supports the state, and inspector of western Yuzhou.
entries.literal: At the opening of Mingdi's reign, with rebellion on four sides, the emperor judged Dai a man of old capacity and made him bearer of the staff, commander of the military affairs of western Yuzhou, general who supports the state, and inspector of western Yuzhou.

entries.zh: 尋徙爲冠軍將軍、北徐州刺史，都督北討諸軍事，竝不之官。
entries.en: He was soon moved to general of the champion and inspector of northern Xuzhou, with command of the northern campaign, but never took up either post.
entries.literal: Soon he was shifted to general of the champion and inspector of northern Xuzhou, commander of the northern campaign forces, and in both cases did not take up the posts.

entries.zh: 泰始末，爲吳興太守。
entries.en: Late in the Taishi reign he served as administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: At the end of the Taishi reign he was administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 元徽中，遷使持節、督益寧二州軍事、冠軍將軍、益州刺史。
entries.en: In the Yuangui era he was made bearer of the staff, commander of Yi and Ning, general of the champion, and inspector of Yi.
entries.literal: In the Yuangui era he was shifted to bearer of the staff, commander of the military affairs of Yi and Ning, general of the champion, and inspector of Yi.

entries.zh: 數年，益土安其政。
entries.en: Within a few years the people of Yi had settled under his rule.
entries.literal: After several years the people of Yi were at ease under his government.

entries.zh: 徵侍中，領長水校尉，度支尚書，領左軍，遷吏部尚書。
entries.en: He was recalled as palace attendant, then held in turn the everlasting water guard, the revenue superintendency, and command of the left army, and was promoted to director of the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: He was summoned as palace attendant, concurrently director of the everlasting water guard, revenue superintendent, and commander of the left army, then moved to director of the ministry of personnel.

entries.zh: 王儉爲吏部郎，時專斷曹事，岱每相違執，及儉爲宰相，以此頗不相善。
entries.en: Wang Jian, as gentleman of the ministry of personnel, had long run the bureau on his own; Dai often stood against him, and after Jian rose to chief minister the two were scarcely on good terms.
entries.literal: Wang Jian was gentleman of the ministry of personnel and then monopolized bureau business; Dai often opposed him, and once Jian became chief minister they were rather ill disposed.

entries.zh: 隨王誕於會稽起義，以岱爲建威將軍，輔國長史，行縣事。
entries.en: When Prince Sui Dan rose in arms at Kuaiji, Dai was named general who establishes might and chief of staff who supports the state, and handled the county's business in his stead.
entries.literal: When Prince Sui Dan raised arms at Kuaiji, Dai was made general who establishes might, chief of staff who supports the state, and acted in county affairs.

entries.zh: 事平，爲司徒左西曹。
entries.en: Once the rising was put down he entered the minister of state's left western bureau.
entries.literal: When the affair was settled he became an officer of the minister of state's left western bureau.

entries.zh: 母年八十，籍注未滿，岱便去官從實還養，有司以岱違制，將欲糾舉。
entries.en: His mother was eighty, but the household register had not yet caught up; Dai resigned at once and went home in earnest to care for her. The authorities judged that he had broken the rules and were ready to prosecute.
entries.literal: His mother was eighty; the household register had not yet been brought up to date, and Dai at once left office and went home in truth to support her. The authorities held that Dai had violated regulations and were about to investigate.

entries.zh: 宋孝武曰：「觀過可以知仁，不須案也。」
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu of Song said, "From a man's lapses you may read his heart; let there be no inquiry."
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song said, "By watching faults one can know benevolence; there is no need for a case."

entries.zh: 累遷撫軍諮議參軍，領山陰令，職事閑理。
entries.en: He advanced to military advisor on the pacification army staff and served concurrently as magistrate of Shanyin, where the work ran calm and clear.
entries.literal: He rose in stages to military advisor on the pacification army staff, concurrently magistrate of Shanyin; his duties were leisurely and well ordered.

entries.zh: 入爲黃門郎，遷驃騎長史，領廣陵太守。
entries.en: He entered court as a yellow gate gentleman, then became chief of staff to the swift cavalry and concurrently administrator of Guangling.
entries.literal: He entered court as yellow gate gentleman, moved to chief of staff of the swift cavalry, and concurrently held Guangling as administrator.

entries.zh: 新安王子鸞以盛寵爲南徐州，割吳郡屬焉。
entries.en: Prince Xin'an Ziluan, deep in imperial favor, took southern Xuzhou, and Wu commandery was cut away to fall under him.
entries.literal: Prince Xin'an Ziluan, in the height of favor, held southern Xuzhou, and Wu commandery was carved out to belong to it.

entries.zh: 高選佐史，孝武帝召岱謂之曰：「卿美效夙著，兼資宦已多。
entries.en: The prince sought men of high rank for his staff; Emperor Xiaowu called Dai in and said, "Your merit has shown for years, and you have already filled many posts.
entries.literal: High-ranking aides were sought; Emperor Xiaowu summoned Dai and told him, "Your fine service has long been plain, and you have already held many offices.

entries.zh: 今欲用卿爲子鸞別駕，總刺史之任，無謂小屈，終當大伸也。」
entries.en: Now I mean to make you Ziluan's vice administrator with full charge of the prefecture. Do not take it as a slight setback; in time you will rise far higher."
entries.literal: Now I wish to use you as Ziluan's vice administrator, with overall charge of the prefecture—do not call it a small bending; in the end you will be greatly extended."

entries.zh: 帝崩，累遷吏部郎。
entries.en: After the emperor's death he advanced step by step to gentleman in the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, Dai rose in stages to gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，復以岱爲散騎常侍、吳興太守，秩中二千石。
entries.en: When Shizu came to the throne, Dai was again named Cavalier Regular Attendant and administrator of Wuxing, with rank at the middle two-thousand-bushel level.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Dai was again made Cavalier Regular Attendant and administrator of Wuxing, with rank at the middle two-thousand-bushel level.

entries.zh: 岱晚節在吳興，更以寬恕著名。
entries.en: In his later years Dai held Wuxing and grew still more famous for his leniency.
entries.literal: In his later years Dai was posted at Wuxing and became still more famed for leniency.

entries.zh: 遷使持節監南兖兖徐青冀五州諸軍事、後將軍、南兖州刺史，常侍如故。
entries.en: He was raised to Bearer of the Staff over Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, Rear General, and governor of Nan Yan, while keeping his seat as regular attendant.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Bearer of the Staff supervising military affairs of Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, Rear General, and administrator of Nan Yan; his regular attendant post stood as before.

entries.zh: 未拜，卒。
entries.en: He died before he could take up the post.
entries.literal: Before he could accept the appointment, he died.

entries.zh: 年七十一。
entries.en: He was seventy-one.
entries.literal: He was seventy-one.

entries.zh: 岱初作遺命，分張家財，封置箱中，家業張減，隨復改易，如此十數年。
entries.en: Early on Dai made his last wishes, parceling the Zhang family wealth into sealed chests; as the estate waxed and waned he redrew the shares again and again—for more than ten years.
entries.literal: Dai early drew up a testament, divided the Zhang family property, and sealed it in chests; as the estate swelled and shrank he revised the division again and again—thus for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 贈本官，諡貞子。
entries.en: His former offices were granted posthumously; he was given the posthumous name Viscount Zhen.
entries.literal: He was posthumously granted his former offices; his posthumous name was Viscount Zhen.

entries.zh: 景和世，山陰主就帝求吏部郎褚淵入內侍己，淵見拘逼，終不肯從，與戢同居止月餘日，由是特申情好。
entries.en: In the Jinghe reign the Princess of Shanyin asked the throne to place Chu Yuan of the ministry of personnel in her inner service; Yuan felt himself cornered and refused; he shared Ji's roof for more than a month, and from that their friendship grew singularly close.
entries.literal: In the Jinghe era the Princess of Shanyin asked the emperor to have Chu Yuan of the Ministry of Personnel enter the inner quarters to attend her; Yuan saw himself pressed and would not yield; he lodged with Ji for more than a month, and their bond deepened thereby.

entries.zh: 明帝立，遷司徒從事中郎，從建安王休仁征赭圻，板轉戢司馬，除黃門郎，出爲宣威將軍、東陽太守，吏部郎。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming acceded, Ji became attendant gentleman to the Minister over the Masses; he followed Prince of Jian'an Xiuren against Zhuchi, was board-appointed as army marshal, named gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then sent out as general who proclaims might and governor of Dongyang, and made director of the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne Ji was moved to attendant gentleman to the Minister over the Masses; he followed Prince of Jian'an Xiuren on the Zhuchi campaign, was board-appointed as army marshal, named gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then sent out as general who proclaims might and administrator of Dongyang, and made director of the ministry of personnel.

entries.zh: 元徽初，褚淵參朝政，引戢爲侍中，時年二十九。
entries.en: At the opening of Yuanhui, Chu Yuan took a hand in government and drew Ji in as regular attendant; he was twenty-nine.
entries.literal: Early in Yuanhui, Chu Yuan joined in governing and brought Ji in as regular attendant; he was twenty-nine.

entries.zh: 戢以年未三十，苦辭內侍，表疏屢上，時議許之。
entries.en: Still short of thirty, Ji pressed hard to decline inner service; he sent memorial after memorial, and men of the day thought him right.
entries.literal: Because he was not yet thirty Ji earnestly declined inner service; memorials went up again and again, and opinion of the day approved.

entries.zh: 改授司徒左長史。
entries.en: He was given instead the grand commandant's left chief aide.
entries.literal: He was reassigned as the grand commandant's left chief aide.

entries.zh: 太祖爲領軍，與戢來往，數置歡讌。
entries.en: When the Grand Ancestor was Army Commander, he associated with Ji and repeatedly held joyous banquets.
entries.literal: When the Grand Ancestor was Army Commander, he associated with Ji and repeatedly held joyous banquets.

entries.zh: 上好水引，戢令婦女躬自執事以設上焉。
entries.en: The sovereign liked water-pulled noodles, and Ji had the women of his household personally attend to serving them to him.
entries.literal: The sovereign liked water-pulled noodles, and Ji had the women of his household personally attend to serving them to him.

entries.zh: 久之，復爲侍中，遷安成王車騎長史，加輔國將軍、濟陰太守，行府、州事。
entries.en: After some time, Ji again became Attendant-in-Ordinary. He was transferred to chief clerk on the staff of the Prince of Ancheng, General of Chariots and Cavalry; he was additionally made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Jiyin, and acted in the affairs of the headquarters and province.
entries.literal: After some time, Ji again became Attendant-in-Ordinary. He was transferred to chief clerk on the staff of the Prince of Ancheng, General of Chariots and Cavalry; he was additionally made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Jiyin, and acted in the affairs of the headquarters and province.

entries.zh: 出爲吳郡太守，以疾歸。
entries.en: He went out as Administrator of Wujun and returned because of illness.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Wujun and returned because of illness.

entries.zh: 爲侍中，祕書監，仍轉中書令，太祖相國左長史。
entries.en: He became Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Library Supervisor, then was transferred to Secretariat Director and Left Chief Clerk to the Grand Ancestor as Chancellor of State.
entries.literal: He became Attendant-in-Ordinary and Palace Library Supervisor, then was transferred to Secretariat Director and Left Chief Clerk to the Grand Ancestor as Chancellor of State.

entries.zh: 建元元年，遷散騎常侍，太子詹事，尋改侍中，詹事如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan, he was transferred to Cavalier Regular Attendant and Household Steward to the Crown Prince; soon he was changed to Attendant-in-Ordinary, while remaining Household Steward as before.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, he was transferred to Cavalier Regular Attendant and Household Steward to the Crown Prince; soon he was changed to Attendant-in-Ordinary, while remaining Household Steward as before.

entries.zh: 上欲轉戢領選，問尚書令褚淵，以戢資重，欲加常侍。
entries.en: The sovereign wanted to transfer Ji to head selection and asked Director of the Masters of Writing Chu Yuan. Because Ji's standing was weighty, he wanted to add the post of Regular Attendant.
entries.literal: The sovereign wanted to transfer Ji to head selection and asked Director of the Masters of Writing Chu Yuan. Because Ji's standing was weighty, he wanted to add the post of Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 淵曰：「宋世王球從侍中中書令單作吏部尚書，資與戢相似。
entries.en: Yuan said: "In Song times, Wang Qiu went from Attendant-in-Ordinary and Secretariat Director to serve only as Minister of Personnel; his standing was similar to Ji's.
entries.literal: Yuan said: "In Song times, Wang Qiu went from Attendant-in-Ordinary and Secretariat Director to serve only as Minister of Personnel; his standing was similar to Ji's.

entries.zh: 頃選職方昔小輕，不容頓加常侍。
entries.en: Recently the office of selection has only just been somewhat lighter than in the past, and it would not do to add Regular Attendant all at once.
entries.literal: Recently the office of selection has only just been somewhat lighter than in the past, and it would not do to add Regular Attendant all at once.

entries.zh: 聖旨每以蟬冕不宜過多，臣與王儉旣已左珥，若復加戢，則八座便有三貂。
entries.en: Your sacred will has always held that cicada caps should not be too numerous. Since your servant and Wang Jian already wear the left ornament, if Ji is added too, then among the Eight Seats there will be three sable tails.
entries.literal: Your sacred will has always held that cicada caps should not be too numerous. Since your servant and Wang Jian already wear the left ornament, if Ji is added too, then among the Eight Seats there will be three sable tails.

entries.zh: 若帖以驍、游，亦爲不少。」
entries.en: If he is attached as Agile Cavalry or Mobile Cavalry, that too would not be little."
entries.literal: If he is attached as Agile Cavalry or Mobile Cavalry, that too would not be little."

entries.zh: 乃以戢爲吏部尚書，加驍騎將軍。
entries.en: He was therefore made Minister of Personnel and additionally General of Agile Cavalry.
entries.literal: He was therefore made Minister of Personnel and additionally General of Agile Cavalry.

entries.zh: 上頗好畫扇，宋孝武賜戢蟬雀扇，善畫者顧景秀所畫。
entries.en: The throne doted on painted fans; Emperor Xiaowu of Song had once given Ji a cicada-and-sparrow fan by the master Gu Jingxiu.
entries.literal: The sovereign greatly loved painted fans; Emperor Xiaowu of Song had given Ji a cicada-and-sparrow fan painted by the skilled artist Gu Jingxiu.

entries.zh: 時陸探微、顧彥先皆能畫，歎其巧絕。
entries.en: Lu Tanwei and Gu Yanxian were both painters of note, and they gasped at its supreme craft.
entries.literal: At the time Lu Tanwei and Gu Yanxian could both paint, and they marveled at its supreme artistry.

entries.zh: 戢因王晏獻之，上令晏厚酬其意。
entries.en: Ji presented it through Wang Yan; the throne had Yan reward him handsomely.
entries.literal: Ji offered it up through Wang Yan; the sovereign had Yan richly repay his intent.

entries.zh: 戢美容儀，動止與褚淵相慕，時人呼爲「小褚公」。
entries.en: Ji was fair of face and figure; in bearing and gait he modeled himself on Chu Yuan, and the age called him "Little Lord Chu."
entries.literal: Ji had a handsome bearing; in movement and deportment he took Chu Yuan as his model, and men of the time called him "Little Lord Chu."

entries.zh: 家業富盛，性又華侈，衣被服飾，極爲奢麗。
entries.en: The house was rich and his taste extravagant; dress and adornment were carried to the utmost.
entries.literal: His household was wealthy and his nature lavish; clothing and ornaments were of the utmost luxury.

entries.zh: 三年，出爲左將軍、吳興太守。
entries.en: In the third year he went out as left general and governor of Wuxing.
entries.literal: In the third year he was sent out as left general and administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 四年，遷中書令，右光祿大夫，本州大中正。
entries.en: In year four he was made director of the secretariat, right grand master of splendid honour, and chief equitable judge of his home province.
entries.literal: In year four he was made director of the Secretariat, right grand master of splendid honour, and chief equitable judge of his home province.

entries.zh: 轉左僕射，光祿、中正如故。
entries.en: He was moved to left vice director; his grand master title and chief judgeship stood as before.
entries.literal: He was shifted to left vice director; his grand master title and chief judgeship were unchanged.

entries.zh: 尋領竟陵王師。
entries.en: Soon he also took charge as tutor to the Prince of Jingling.
entries.literal: Soon he also served as tutor to the Prince of Jingling.

entries.zh: 永明二年，陳疾解職，世祖許之。
entries.en: In Yongming year two he pleaded illness and asked to leave office; Emperor Shizu allowed it.
entries.literal: In Yongming year two he pleaded illness to resign; the Shizu emperor granted it.

entries.zh: 轉特進，右光祿大夫，王師、中正如故。
entries.en: He was made extraordinary privy counselor and right grand master; his tutorship and chief judgeship remained as they were.
entries.literal: He was made extraordinary privy counselor and right grand master; his tutorship and chief judgeship were unchanged.

entries.zh: 其年卒，年六十四。
entries.en: That same year he died, at sixty-four.
entries.literal: That year he died, aged sixty-four.

entries.zh: 追贈散騎常侍，右光祿大夫、特進如故。
entries.en: After death he was given the post of regular attendant at the scattered cavalry service, with right grand master and extraordinary counselor unchanged.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given the office of regular attendant at the scattered cavalry service, with right grand master and extraordinary counselor unchanged.

entries.zh: 諡簡子。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Master of Refinement.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Master of Refinement.

entries.zh: 延之家訓方嚴，不妄見子弟，雖節歲問訊，皆先克日。
entries.en: Yanzhi's household rule was severe: he would not see sons or nephews without cause, and even festival greetings had to be booked in advance.
entries.literal: Yanzhi's household instruction was stern; he would not casually see his sons and nephews—even holiday greetings required a fixed day in advance.

entries.zh: 子倫之，見兒子亦然。
entries.en: His son Lunzhi dealt with his own sons in the same way.
entries.literal: His son Lunzhi treated his own sons the same way.

entries.zh: 永明中，爲侍中。
entries.en: In the Yongming reign he served as palace attendant.
entries.literal: During Yongming he served as palace attendant.

entries.zh: 世祖幸琅邪城，倫之與光祿大夫全景文等二十一人坐不參承，爲有司所奏。
entries.en: When Emperor Shizu visited Langye city, Lunzhi and twenty others, among them the grand master Quan Jingwen, were impeached for failing to attend the imperial progress.
entries.literal: When Shizu visited Langye city, Lunzhi and twenty others including the grand master Quan Jingwen were charged for failing to attend the reception.

entries.zh: 詔倫之親爲陪侍之職，而同外惰慢，免官，景文等贖論。
entries.en: An edict said Lunzhi held close attendance yet had been as slack as the rest; he was stripped of office, while Jingwen and the others were allowed to redeem their cases with fines.
entries.literal: An edict held that Lunzhi held close attendance duty yet shared in outer negligence; he was dismissed from office; Jingwen and others were allowed to pay fines instead.

entries.zh: 建武中，至侍中，領前軍將軍，都官尚書，領游擊將軍，卒。
entries.en: Under Jianwu he reached palace attendant, commander of the forward army, director of justice, and raiding army commander, then died.
entries.literal: During Jianwu he rose to palace attendant, commander of the forward army, director of justice, and raiding army commander, then died.

entries.zh: 宋孝武選侍中四人，竝以風貌。
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowu of Song picked four palace attendants, every one chosen for face and bearing.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song chose four palace attendants—all for their bearing and looks.

entries.zh: 王彧、謝莊爲一雙，韜與何偃爲一雙。
entries.en: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang were paired; Tao and He Yan were paired.
entries.literal: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang were one pair; Tao and He Yan were one pair.

entries.zh: 常充兼假。
entries.en: He was often named to concurrent and acting posts.
entries.literal: He often held concurrent and acting posts.

entries.zh: 泰始末，爲征南江州長史。
entries.en: At the close of Taishi he served as chief aide to the Pacify-the-South General for Jiangzhou.
entries.literal: At the end of Taishi he was chief aide on the Pacify-the-South staff for Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 桂陽王休範在鎮，數出行遊，韜性方峙，未嘗隨從。
entries.en: While the Prince of Guiyang, Xiufan, was in command he went out on pleasure tours again and again; Tao, upright and unyielding by nature, never went along.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan, held the post, he often went out touring; Tao's nature was upright and stern, and he never followed along.

entries.zh: 至散騎常侍，金紫光祿大夫，領始興王師。
entries.en: He rose to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Household Minister with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and preceptor to the Prince of Shixing.
entries.literal: He reached Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Household Minister with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and tutored the Prince of Shixing.

entries.zh: 永明二年，卒。
entries.en: In Yongming year 2 he died.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongming he died.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷三十二‧列傳第十三
entries.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 32 — Biography 13
entries.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 32 — Biography 13

entries.zh: 太祖善書，及卽位，篤好不已。
entries.en: The Grand Ancestor wrote well, and once he held the throne his passion only deepened.
entries.literal: The Grand Ancestor was skilled at calligraphy, and after taking the throne his deep love did not cease.

entries.zh: 與僧虔賭書畢，謂僧虔曰：「誰爲第一？」
entries.en: When a calligraphy match with Sengqian was done, he asked him: "Who is first?"
entries.literal: Having finished a calligraphy wager with Sengqian, he said to Sengqian: "Who ranks first?"

entries.zh: 僧虔曰：「臣書第一，陛下亦第一。」
entries.en: Sengqian said: "Mine ranks first, and Your Majesty's ranks first as well."
entries.literal: Sengqian said: "My calligraphy is first, and Your Majesty's is also first."

entries.zh: 上笑曰：「卿可謂善自爲謀矣。」
entries.en: The emperor laughed: "You know how to scheme on your own behalf."
entries.literal: The emperor laughed: "You may be said to know how to look out for yourself."

entries.zh: 示僧虔古迹十一袠，就求能書人名。
entries.en: He showed Sengqian eleven fascicles of ancient work and bade him list who wrote well.
entries.literal: He showed Sengqian eleven bundles of ancient works and asked at once for the names of able calligraphers.

entries.zh: 僧虔得民閒所有，袠中所無者，吳大皇帝、景帝、歸命侯書，桓玄書，及王丞相導、領軍洽、中書令珉、張芝、索靖、衞伯儒、張翼十二卷奏之。
entries.en: What Sengqian found in the world but not in the bundles were pieces by Wu's Great Emperor, Emperor Jing, the Marquis of Guiming, Huan Xuan, Chancellor Wang Dao, Leader of the Army Wang Qia, Secretariat Director Wang Min, Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Boyu, and Zhang Yi—twelve fascicles in all, which he submitted.
entries.literal: Sengqian obtained what was in common circulation but absent from the bundles—the Great Emperor of Wu, Emperor Jing, the script of the Marquis of Guiming, Huan Xuan's script, and Chancellor of State Dao, Pacification Army Qia, Secretariat Director Min, Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Boyu, Zhang Yi—twelve fascicles in all, and memorialized them.

entries.zh: 又上羊欣所撰《能書人名》一卷。
entries.en: He also submitted Yang Xin's one-fascicle Names of Able Calligraphers.
entries.literal: He also submitted one fascicle of Yang Xin's Names of Able Calligraphers.

entries.zh: 其論書曰：「宋文帝書，自云可比王子敬，時議者云『天然勝羊欣，功夫少於欣』。
entries.en: In his discourse on calligraphy he wrote: "Emperor Wen of Song claimed his hand could stand beside Wang Zijing's; men of the time said, "By native gift he outdoes Yang Xin, yet in practiced craft he trails Xin."
entries.literal: His treatise on calligraphy says: "Emperor Wen of Song's writing—he himself said it could match Wang Zijing; critics of the day said, "His natural gift surpasses Yang Xin's, but trained skill falls short of Xin's."

entries.zh: 王平南廙、右軍叔，過江之前以爲最。
entries.en: Wang Pingnan Yi, uncle to the Right General, was reckoned the best before the river crossing.
entries.literal: Wang Pingnan Yi, the Right General's uncle, was held the finest before the crossing south.

entries.zh: 亡曾祖領軍書，右軍云『弟書遂不減吾』。
entries.en: Of my late great-grandfather the commandant-in-chief's hand, the Right General said, "The younger brother's writing in no way diminishes mine."
entries.literal: My deceased great-grandfather the commandant-in-chief's writing—the Right General said, "Younger brother's script does not fall short of mine."

entries.zh: 變古制，今唯右軍。
entries.en: He broke with the old forms; today only the Right General has done the same.
entries.literal: He changed the ancient manner; today only the Right General does so.

entries.zh: 領軍不爾，至今猶法鍾、張。
entries.en: The commandant-in-chief did not; even now his line still follows Zhong and Zhang.
entries.literal: The commandant-in-chief did not; to this day he still takes Zhong and Zhang as his model.

entries.zh: 亡從祖中書令書，子敬云『弟書如騎騾，駸駸恒欲度驊騮前』。
entries.en: My late collateral forebear the director of the Secretariat—Zijing said of his hand, "The younger brother writes as one rides a mule, forever lunging to get past the thoroughbred in front."
entries.literal: My deceased collateral ancestor the director of the Secretariat's writing—Zijing said, "Younger brother's script is like riding a mule, always straining to pass the bay ahead."

entries.zh: 庾征西翼書，少時與右軍齊名，右軍後進，庾猶不分，在荊州與都下人書云：『小兒輩賤家雞，皆學逸少書，須吾下，當比之。』
entries.en: Western campaigning general Yu Yi—in his youth he stood even with the Right General; the Right General later outpaced him, yet Yu would still not yield. From Jingzhou he wrote someone in the capital: "Every wretched barnyard fowl among the young imitates Yi Shao's hand. Wait until I come down—then they may be compared."
entries.literal: Western Campaigning General Yu Yi's writing—in youth he ranked with the Right General; the Right General later pulled ahead, yet Yu still would not concede. Writing from Jingzhou to someone at court he said: "Those wretched village chickens of the younger set all study Yi Shao's script. It will take me to come down before they can be matched."

entries.zh: 張翼，王右軍自書表，晉穆帝令翼寫題後答，右軍當時不別，久後方悟，云『小人幾欲亂真』。
entries.en: Zhang Yi: when the Right General Wang drafted a memorial himself, Emperor Mu of Jin had Yi copy it and pen the heading on the reply; at the time the Right General could not tell which was which; only much later did he see through it and say, "The little man nearly turned truth upside down."
entries.literal: Zhang Yi: when the Right General Wang personally wrote a memorial, Emperor Mu of Jin had Yi copy it and write the heading for the reply; at the time the Right General could not tell them apart; only long afterward did he realize and say, "The fellow nearly passed for the genuine article."

entries.zh: 張芝、索靖、韋誕、鍾會、二衞竝得名前代，無以辨其優劣，唯見其筆力驚異耳。
entries.en: Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Dan, Zhong Hui, and the two Weis all made names in former times; one cannot sort their ranks—only that their brushwork struck the eye as uncanny.
entries.literal: Zhang Zhi, Suo Jing, Wei Dan, Zhong Hui, and the two Weis all won fame in earlier ages—there is no distinguishing their relative merit; one only sees their brush strength was startling and extraordinary.

entries.zh: 張澄當時亦呼有意。
entries.en: Zhang Cheng in his day was likewise called a man of purpose.
entries.literal: Zhang Cheng at the time was also said to have intent.

entries.zh: 郗愔章草亞於右軍。
entries.en: Xi Kai's draft clerical stood beneath the Right General's.
entries.literal: Xi Kai's draft-clerical script ranked below the Right General.

entries.zh: 郗嘉賔草亞於二王，緊媚過其父。
entries.en: Xi Jiabin's cursive trailed the Two Wangs, yet was more compact and graceful than his father's.
entries.literal: Xi Jiabin's cursive ranked below the Two Wangs, but was tighter and more delicate than his father's.

entries.zh: 桓玄自謂右軍之流，論者以比孔琳之。
entries.en: Huan Xuan called himself of the Right General's line; reviewers set him beside Kong Linzhi.
entries.literal: Huan Xuan styled himself of the Right General's school; critics compared him to Kong Linzhi.

entries.zh: 謝安亦入能書錄，亦自重，爲子敬書嵇康詩。
entries.en: Xie An too made the roll of able calligraphers, prized his own hand, and wrote out Xi Kang's poems for Zijing.
entries.literal: Xie An also entered the register of able calligraphers; he too thought highly of himself and wrote Xi Kang's poetry for Zijing.

entries.zh: 羊欣書見重一時，親受子敬，行書尤善，正乃不稱名。
entries.en: Yang Xin's hand was honored for a season; he studied face to face with Zijing; in running script he shone, yet in regular script he never won a name.
entries.literal: Yang Xin's writing was esteemed for a time; he received instruction personally from Zijing; running script he excelled at especially; regular script simply did not earn him a name.

entries.zh: 孔琳之書天然放縱，極有筆力，規矩恐在羊欣後。
entries.en: Kong Linzhi wrote with native abandon and fearsome stroke; in measure and rule he likely stood behind Yang Xin.
entries.literal: Kong Linzhi's writing was naturally free and unrestrained, with extreme brush strength; in formal rules he probably fell behind Yang Xin.

entries.zh: 丘道護與羊欣俱面受子敬，故當在欣後。
entries.en: Qiu Daohu and Yang Xin both sat before Zijing in person; Daohu therefore belongs after Xin.
entries.literal: Qiu Daohu and Yang Xin both received Zijing face to face, so he should rank after Xin.

entries.zh: 范曅與蕭思話同師羊欣，後小叛，旣失故步，爲復小有意耳。
entries.en: Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua shared Yang Xin as teacher; later Ye slipped a little from the path, lost his old step, and kept only a trace of purpose.
entries.literal: Fan Ye and Xiao Sihua studied under Yang Xin together; later Ye departed a little from the model; having lost his former footing, he only retained a little intent.

entries.zh: 蕭思話書，羊欣之影，風流趣好，殆當不減，筆力恨弱。
entries.en: Xiao Sihua's hand is Yang Xin's shadow: in ease and taste he nearly does not fall short, yet his stroke power is painfully thin.
entries.literal: Xiao Sihua's writing is Yang Xin's shadow—in elegant taste nearly not inferior, but brush strength regrettably weak.

entries.zh: 謝綜書，其舅云『緊生起，是得賞也，恨少媚好』。
entries.en: On Xie Zong's writing his uncle said, "He is tightening up—that wins praise—but alas, too little sweetness."
entries.literal: Xie Zong's writing—his uncle said, "Tightness arises in him—that earns praise—but regrettably little charm."

entries.zh: 謝靈運乃不倫，遇其合時，亦得入流。
entries.en: Xie Lingyun was simply not of the same breed; when the fit was right, he too could join the stream.
entries.literal: Xie Lingyun was simply out of category; when he hit his moment, he too could enter the current.

entries.zh: 賀道力書亞丘道護。
entries.en: He Daoli's hand stood beneath Qiu Daohu's.
entries.literal: He Daoli's writing ranked below Qiu Daohu.

entries.zh: 庾昕學右軍，亦欲亂真矣。」
entries.en: Yu Xin trained on the Right General and likewise came close to passing for the real thing."
entries.literal: Yu Xin studied the Right General and also nearly passed for genuine."

entries.zh: 又著《書賦》，傳於世。
entries.en: He also wrote Rhapsody on Calligraphy, which circulated in his time.
entries.literal: He also authored Rhapsody on Calligraphy, transmitted in the world.

entries.zh: 第九子寂，字子玄，性迅動，好文章，讀《范滂傳》，未常不歎挹。
entries.en: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was swift and restless by nature and loved letters; whenever he read the biography of Fan Pang he could not keep from sighing in wonder.
entries.literal: His ninth son Ji, styled Zixuan, was quick and restless by nature, loved literature; reading the biography of Fan Pang, he never failed to sigh in admiration.

entries.zh: 王融敗後，賔客多歸之。
entries.en: After Wang Rong's fall, many of his former guests attached themselves to Ji.
entries.literal: After Wang Rong's defeat, many clients turned to him.

entries.zh: 建武初，欲獻《中興頌》，兄志謂之曰：「汝膏粱年少，何患不達，不鎮之以靜，將恐貽譏。」
entries.en: At the opening of Jianwu he meant to offer an Ode on Restoration; his elder brother Zhi told him, "You are young, well-fed, and born to rank—what fear that you will not arrive? Without quiet to anchor you, you will only buy mockery."
entries.literal: Early in Jianwu, he wished to present Ode on Restoration; his elder brother Zhi told him: "You are a young man of fattened grain—what need to worry you will not rise? If you do not steady yourself with quiet, you will probably invite ridicule."

entries.zh: 寂乃止。
entries.en: Ji dropped the plan.
entries.literal: Ji then stopped.

entries.zh: 初爲祕書郎，卒，年二十一。
entries.en: He had first been made secretariat gentleman; he died at twenty-one.
entries.literal: At first made Secretariat Gentleman; he died, aged twenty-one.

entries.zh: 緒長於《周易》，言精理奧，見宗一時。
entries.en: Xu was master of the Book of Changes—his speech subtle and its principles deep—and for a season the age looked up to him.
entries.literal: Xu excelled in the Book of Changes; his discourse was refined and its principles profound, and he was honored for a time.

entries.zh: 常云何平叔所不解《易》中七事，諸卦中所有時義，是其一也。
entries.en: He often remarked that of the seven points in the Changes He Yan could not fathom, the timely import within each hexagram was one of them.
entries.literal: He would often say that among the seven matters in the Changes He Yan could not grasp, the timely meanings found in the various hexagrams were one.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，轉吏部尚書，祭酒如故。
entries.en: When Shizu ascended, Xu became minister of personnel, while keeping the directorship as before.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Xu was transferred to Minister of Personnel, while remaining Director as before.

entries.zh: 永明元年，遷金紫光祿大夫，領太常。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming he became grandee of splendid happiness with gold seal and purple ribbon and concurrently headed the ceremonies ministry.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he was transferred to Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and concurrently headed the Ministry of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 明年，領南郡王師，加給事中，太常如故。
entries.en: The next year he became tutor to the Prince of Nan Commandery and palace attendant, while keeping the ceremonies post.
entries.literal: The next year, he became tutor to the Prince of Nan Commandery and was additionally made Palace Attendant, while remaining Minister of Ceremonies as before.

entries.zh: 三年，轉太子詹事，師、給事如故。
entries.en: In the third year he became household steward to the crown prince, while keeping the tutoring and palace attendant posts.
entries.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Household Steward to the Crown Prince, while his posts as tutor and Palace Attendant remained as before.

entries.zh: 緒每朝見，世祖目送之。
entries.en: Whenever Xu appeared at court, Shizu watched him go.
entries.literal: Whenever Xu attended court audience, Shizu followed him with his eyes as he departed.

entries.zh: 謂王儉曰：「緒以位尊我，我以德貴緒也。」
entries.en: He told Wang Jian, "Xu honors me by office; I honor Xu for his virtue."
entries.literal: He told Wang Jian, "Xu honors me by rank; I esteem Xu for his virtue."

entries.zh: 遷散騎常侍，金紫光祿大夫、師如故。
entries.en: He became regular attendant, while keeping the grandee rank and tutoring post.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, while remaining Grandee of Splendid Happiness with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and tutor as before.

entries.zh: 給親信二十人。
entries.en: He was assigned twenty trusted attendants.
entries.literal: He was granted twenty trusted attendants.

entries.zh: 復領中正。
entries.en: He again served as rectifier.
entries.literal: He again held the rectifiercy.

entries.zh: 長沙王晃屬選用吳興聞人邕爲州議曹，緒以資藉不當，執不許。
entries.en: Prince Huang of Changsha pressed the selection office to appoint Wenren Yong of Wuxing as provincial deliberative clerk, but Xu insisted that his rank and background were unsuitable and refused.
entries.literal: Prince Huang of Changsha entrusted selection officials to use Wenren Yong of Wuxing as provincial deliberative clerk, but Xu held firmly against allowing it because his qualifications and standing were unsuitable.

entries.zh: 晃遣書佐固請之，緒正色謂晃信曰：「此是身家州郷，殿下何得見逼！」
entries.en: Huang sent a clerk to press the request. Xu faced Huang's messenger sternly and said, "This is my own home province and village. How can Your Highness force me in this?"
entries.literal: Huang sent a clerk to request it insistently; Xu, with stern expression, told Huang's messenger, "This is the province and village of my own person and household. How can Your Highness press me so?"

entries.zh: 七年，竟陵王子良領國子祭酒，世祖敕王晏曰：「吾欲令司徒辭祭酒以授張緒，物議以爲云何？」
entries.en: In the seventh year, Prince Ziliang of Jingling held the directorship of the imperial university. Shizu instructed Wang Yan, "I want the minister of education to give up the directorship so it can be granted to Zhang Xu. What would opinion make of that?"
entries.literal: In the seventh year, Prince Ziliang of Jingling held the post of Director of the Imperial University; Shizu ordered Wang Yan, "I wish to have the Minister of Education relinquish the directorship and give it to Zhang Xu. What would public opinion think of this?"

entries.zh: 子良竟不拜。
entries.en: In the end Ziliang never took the post.
entries.literal: In the end, Ziliang did not receive the appointment.

entries.zh: 以緒領國子祭酒，光祿、師、中正如故。
entries.en: Xu was then made director of the imperial university, while keeping his grandee rank, tutoring post, and rectifiercy.
entries.literal: Xu was made concurrent Director of the Imperial University, while his posts as grandee, tutor, and rectifier remained as before.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷三十三‧列傳第十四
entries.en: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 33 — Biography 14
entries.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 33 — Biography 14

entries.zh: 元徽中，爲右丞。
entries.en: In the Yuanhui era he served as right vice director.
entries.literal: In the Yuanhui era he served as right vice director.

entries.zh: 時太祖參政，與玩之書曰：「張華爲度支尚書，事不徒然。
entries.en: At the time the founding sovereign was directing affairs of state and wrote to Wanzhi: "When Zhang Hua served as minister of revenue, his work was not in vain.
entries.literal: At the time the founding sovereign held real power in government and wrote to Wanzhi: "When Zhang Hua served as minister of revenue, his work was not in vain.

entries.zh: 今漕藏有闕，吾賢居右丞，已覺金粟可積也。」
entries.en: Now the transport treasuries show gaps; with you, my worthy, as right vice director, I already sense gold and grain may begin to accumulate."
entries.literal: Now the transport treasuries have gaps; with you, my worthy, in the right vice director's post, I already sense that gold and grain may be piled up."

entries.zh: 玩之上表陳府庫錢帛，器械役力，所懸轉多，興用漸廣，慮不支歲月。
entries.en: Wanzhi memorialized that the palace treasury's cash, silk, equipment, and labor levies were ever more entangled in suspense, new outlays steadily widened, and he feared the year could not be sustained.
entries.literal: Wanzhi memorialized on the palace treasury's cash, silk, equipment, and labor levies: what hung in suspense grew ever greater, new outlays steadily widened, and he feared the year could not be sustained.

entries.zh: 朝議優報之。
entries.en: Court deliberation returned him a favorable reply.
entries.literal: Court deliberation gave him a favorable reply.

entries.zh: 遷安成王車騎錄事，轉少府。
entries.en: He was moved to recorder on the Prince of Ancheng's chariot-and-cavalry staff, then to the lesser treasury.
entries.literal: He was moved to recorder on the Prince of Ancheng's chariot-and-cavalry staff, then to the lesser treasury.

entries.zh: 太祖鎮東府，朝野致敬，玩之猶躡屐造席。
entries.en: When the founding sovereign held the eastern palace, court and countryside paid him homage; Wanzhi still wore clogs and came straight to his mat.
entries.literal: When the founding sovereign held the eastern palace, court and countryside paid him homage; Wanzhi still wore clogs and came to his mat.

entries.zh: 太祖取屐視之，訛黑斜銳，蒵斷，以芒接之。
entries.en: The founding sovereign picked up the clogs to look at them—worn black, toes slanted and sharp, the vamp split and patched with straw.
entries.literal: The founding sovereign took up the clogs to look at them—worn black, toes slanted and sharp, the vamp split and spliced with straw.

entries.zh: 問曰：「卿此屐已幾載？」
entries.en: He asked: "How many years have you had these clogs?"
entries.literal: He asked: "How many years have you had these clogs?"

entries.zh: 玩之曰：「初釋褐拜征北行佐買之，著已二十年，貧土竟不辦易。」
entries.en: Wanzhi said: "When I first took office as northern-campaign staff aide I bought them; I have worn them twenty years, and this poor fellow never managed to replace them."
entries.literal: Wanzhi said: "When I first left coarse cloth and took appointment as northern-campaign staff aide, I bought them; I have worn them twenty years now, and this poor fellow never managed to replace them."

entries.zh: 太祖善之，引爲驃騎諮議參軍。
entries.en: The founding sovereign was pleased with him and brought him in as fierce-cavalry staff adviser.
entries.literal: The founding sovereign approved of him and brought him in as fierce-cavalry staff adviser.

entries.zh: 霸府初開，賓客輻湊，太祖留意簡接，玩之與樂安任遐，俱以應對有席上之美，齊名見遇。
entries.en: When the hegemon's office first opened, guests crowded in like wheel spokes; the founding sovereign took care whom he admitted. Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an alike were famed for the grace of their table talk and were equally favored.
entries.literal: When the hegemon's office first opened, guests crowded in like wheel spokes; the founding sovereign took care to choose whom he received. Wanzhi and Ren Xia of Le'an alike won renown for the grace of their table talk and were equally favored.

entries.zh: 遐字景遠，好學，有義行，兼與太祖素游，褚淵、王儉竝見親愛。
entries.en: Xia, styled Jingyuan, loved learning and had a sense of duty; he had long been the founding sovereign's companion, and Chu Yuan and Wang Jian alike held him dear.
entries.literal: Xia, styled Jingyuan, loved learning and had a sense of duty; he had long been the founding sovereign's companion, and Chu Yuan and Wang Jian alike held him dear.

entries.zh: 官至光祿大夫，永元初卒。
entries.en: He reached grandee for splendid happiness and died at the opening of Yongyuan.
entries.literal: He reached the post of grandee for splendid happiness and died at the opening of Yongyuan.

entries.zh: 玩之遷驍騎將軍，黃門郎，領本部中正。
entries.en: Wanzhi was moved to rampant-cavalry general, gentleman of the yellow gate, and concurrently led his home-district rectifier.
entries.literal: Wanzhi was moved to rampant-cavalry general, gentleman of the yellow gate, and concurrently led his home-district rectifier.

entries.zh: 上患民間欺巧，及卽位，敕玩之與驍騎將軍傅堅意檢定簿籍。
entries.en: The emperor worried over popular fraud and trickery; upon his accession he ordered Wanzhi and rampant-cavalry general Fu Jianyi to examine and fix the registers.
entries.literal: The emperor worried over popular fraud and trickery; upon his accession he ordered Wanzhi and rampant-cavalry general Fu Jianyi to examine and fix the registers.

entries.zh: 建元二年，詔朝臣曰：「黃籍，民之大紀，國之治端。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianyuan he issued an edict to the court ministers: "The yellow register is the people's great charter and the state's hinge of order.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan he issued an edict to the court ministers: "The yellow register is the people's great charter and the state's hinge of order.

entries.zh: 自頃氓俗巧偽，爲日已久，至乃竊注爵位，盜易年月，增損三狀，貿襲萬端。
entries.en: Of late the common folk's cunning fraud has gone on long indeed—to the point of secretly entering noble ranks, stealing and altering birth years, adding or subtracting the three registers, and trading false entries by the myriad.
entries.literal: Of late the common folk's cunning fraud has gone on long indeed—to the point of secretly entering noble ranks, stealing and altering birth years, adding or subtracting the three registers, and trading false entries by the myriad.

entries.zh: 或戶存而文書已絕，或人在而反託死叛，停私而云隸役，身強而稱六疾。
entries.en: Some households still exist while their documents are already dead; some men still live while they are recorded as dead or defected; they halt private service yet claim corvée duty; their bodies are strong yet they plead the six illnesses.
entries.literal: Some households still exist while their documents are already dead; some men still live while they are recorded as dead or defected; they halt private service yet claim corvée duty; their bodies are strong yet they plead the six illnesses.

entries.zh: 編戶齊家，少不如此。
entries.en: Among registered households and ordered families, few are not like this.
entries.literal: Among registered households and ordered families, few are not like this.

entries.zh: 皆政之巨蠹，教之深疵。
entries.en: All are great worms in government and deep flaws in teaching.
entries.literal: All are great worms in government and deep flaws in teaching.

entries.zh: 比年雖卻籍改書，終無得實。
entries.en: In recent years, though registers were rejected and books altered, in the end the truth was never obtained.
entries.literal: In recent years, though registers were rejected and books altered, in the end the truth was never obtained.

entries.zh: 若約之以刑，則民偽已遠；
entries.en: If we bind them with punishments, the people's fraud is already far gone;
entries.literal: If we bind them with punishments, the people's fraud is already far gone;

entries.zh: 若綏之以德，則勝殘未易。
entries.en: if we soothe them with virtue, transforming the cruel is not easy.
entries.literal: if we soothe them with virtue, transforming the cruel is not easy.

entries.zh: 卿諸賢竝深明治體，可各獻嘉謀，以振澆化。
entries.en: You worthies alike are deeply versed in the principles of rule—each may offer a fine plan to rectify shallow customs.
entries.literal: You worthies alike are deeply versed in the principles of rule—each may offer a fine plan to rectify shallow customs.

entries.zh: 又臺坊訪募，此制不近，優刻素定，閒劇有常。
entries.en: Again, bureau-yard recruitment: this system is not near at hand; preferential carve-outs were long since fixed, and light and heavy duties have their constants.
entries.literal: Again, bureau-yard recruitment: this system is not near at hand; preferential carve-outs were long since fixed, and light and heavy duties have their constants.

entries.zh: 宋元嘉以前，茲役恆滿，大明以後，樂補稍絕。
entries.en: Before Liu Song's Yuanjia, this service was always full; after the Daming era, glad substitution gradually ceased.
entries.literal: Before Liu Song's Yuanjia, this service was always full; after the Daming era, glad substitution gradually ceased.

entries.zh: 或緣寇難頻起，軍蔭易多，民庶從利，投坊者寡。
entries.en: Sometimes because raids and troubles arose often, military shelter was easily multiplied; the people followed profit, and those who entered the yards were few.
entries.literal: Sometimes because raids and troubles arose often, military shelter was easily multiplied; the people followed profit, and those who entered the yards were few.

entries.zh: 然國經未變，朝紀恆存，相揆而言，隆替何速！
entries.en: Yet the state's warp was unchanged and the court's warp still stood—measure them against each other: how swift the rise and fall!
entries.literal: Yet the state's warp was unchanged and the court's warp still stood—measure them against each other: how swift the rise and fall!

entries.zh: 此急病之洪源，晷景之切患，以何科算，革斯弊邪？」
entries.en: This is the great source of acute disease, the pressing ailment of the sundial's shadow—by what statute shall we reckon it and reform this abuse?"
entries.literal: This is the great source of acute disease, the pressing ailment of the sundial's shadow—by what statute shall we reckon it and reform this abuse?"

entries.zh: 玩之上表曰：「宋元嘉二十七年八條取人，孝建元年書籍，衆巧之所始也。
entries.en: Wanzhi memorialized: "The Yuanjia year 27 eight-article levy of men and the Xiaojian year 1 book-register were where the crowd's tricks began.
entries.literal: Wanzhi memorialized: "The Yuanjia year 27 eight-article levy of men and the Xiaojian year 1 book-register were where the crowd's tricks began.

entries.zh: 元嘉中，故光祿大夫傅隆，年出七十，猶手自書籍，躬加隱校。
entries.en: In the Yuanjia era the late grandee for splendid happiness Fu Long, though past seventy, still copied the registers by hand and personally added hidden verification.
entries.literal: In the Yuanjia era the late grandee for splendid happiness Fu Long, though past seventy, still copied the registers by hand and personally added hidden verification.

entries.zh: 隆何必有石建之愼，高柔之勤，蓋以世屬休明，服道脩身故耳。
entries.en: Did Long need Shi Jian's caution or Gao Rou's diligence? It was only that the age belonged to radiant peace and he cultivated the Way and his person.
entries.literal: Did Long need Shi Jian's caution or Gao Rou's diligence? It was only that the age belonged to radiant peace and he cultivated the Way and his person.

entries.zh: 今陛下日旰忘食，未明求衣，詔逮幽愚，謹陳妄說。
entries.en: Now Your Majesty, the sun at the zenith yet forgetting food, seeks his robes before dawn—the edict reaches even this obscure fool; I venture my reckless counsel.
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty, the sun at the zenith yet forgetting food, seeks his robes before dawn—the edict reaches even this obscure fool; I venture my reckless counsel.

entries.zh: 古之共治天下，唯良二千石，今欲求治取正，其在勤明令長。
entries.en: In antiquity to govern the realm together, only good two-thousand-dan administrators mattered; now if we seek order and take the straight measure, it lies in diligent, clear magistrates.
entries.literal: In antiquity to govern the realm together, only good two-thousand-dan administrators mattered; now if we seek order and take the straight measure, it lies in diligent, clear magistrates.

entries.zh: 凡受籍，縣不加檢合，但封送州，州檢得實，方卻歸縣。
entries.en: Whenever registers were received, the county did not add verification but only sealed and sent them to the province; only when the province's check found truth were they returned to the county.
entries.literal: Whenever registers were received, the county did not add verification but only sealed and sent them to the province; only when the province's check found truth were they returned to the county.

entries.zh: 吏貪其賂，民肆其姦，姦彌深而卻彌多，賂愈厚而答愈緩。
entries.en: Clerks greedily took bribes, the people freely practiced fraud—the deeper the fraud, the more rejections; the thicker the bribe, the slower the reply.
entries.literal: Clerks greedily took bribes, the people freely practiced fraud—the deeper the fraud, the more rejections; the thicker the bribe, the slower the reply.

entries.zh: 自泰始三年至元徽四年，揚州等九郡四號黃籍，共卻七萬一千餘戶。
entries.en: From Taishi year 3 to Yuanhui year 4, in nine commanderies of Yang province four rounds of yellow-register rejections totaled more than seventy-one thousand households.
entries.literal: From Taishi year 3 to Yuanhui year 4, in nine commanderies of Yang province four rounds of yellow-register rejections totaled more than seventy-one thousand households.

entries.zh: 于今十一年矣，而所正者猶未四萬。
entries.en: Eleven years have passed since, yet those corrected still fall short of forty thousand.
entries.literal: Eleven years have passed since, yet those corrected still fall short of forty thousand.

entries.zh: 神州奧區，尚或如此，江、湘諸部，倍不可念。
