entries.en: In the sacred heartland it is still so; the Jiang and Xiang regions are doubly beyond reckoning.
entries.literal: In the sacred heartland it is still so; the Jiang and Xiang regions are doubly beyond reckoning.

entries.zh: 愚謂宜以元嘉二十七年籍爲正。
entries.en: I humbly hold that the Yuanjia year 27 register should be taken as standard.
entries.literal: I humbly hold that the Yuanjia year 27 register should be taken as standard.

entries.zh: 民惰法旣久，今建元元年書籍，宜更立明科，一聽首悔，迷而不反，依制必戮。
entries.en: The people have grown lax toward the law for many years; for the Jianyuan year-one register we should lay down clear statutes anew, grant a general amnesty to all who confess first, and execute without mercy those who persist in fraud.
entries.literal: The people have been lax toward the law for a long time; for the Jianyuan year-one register we should establish clear statutes anew, allow all who come forward first to repent, and for those who stray and do not turn back, by regulation they must be put to death.

entries.zh: 使官長審自檢校，必令明洗，然後上州，永以爲正。
entries.en: Magistrates should conduct their own thorough audits, scrub every entry clean, and only then forward the registers to the prefecture — and let that stand as the permanent rule.
entries.literal: Have the magistrates carefully inspect on their own, require that everything be made clear and clean, and only then send up to the prefecture — let that forever be the standard.

entries.zh: 若有虛昧，州縣同咎。
entries.en: Any remaining concealment or falsification shall be punished alike in prefecture and county.
entries.literal: If anything remains concealed or false, prefecture and county shall share the blame.

entries.zh: 今戶口多少，不減元嘉，而板籍頓闕，弊亦有以。
entries.en: Household counts today are no lower than under Yuanjia, yet the board registers have collapsed — and there are clear reasons for the rot.
entries.literal: Today the number of households is no less than under Yuanjia, yet the board registers are suddenly depleted — the abuses have their reasons.

entries.zh: 自孝建已來，入勳者衆，其中操干戈衛社稷者，三分殆無一焉。
entries.en: Since the Xiaojian era the merit rolls have swollen with names, yet of those entered scarcely one in three ever bore arms in defense of the realm.
entries.literal: Since Xiaojian, those entered on the merit rolls have been many; of them, those who bore arms and guarded the altars of state — scarcely one in three.

entries.zh: 勳簿所領而詐注辭籍，浮遊世要，非官長所拘錄，復爲不少。
entries.en: Men claim merit-book privileges while their household entries are forged, drift among the great families of the day, and escape magistrates' scrutiny — and their number is not small.
entries.literal: Merit rolls claimed while registers were fraudulently annotated, drifting among the powerful of the age, beyond what magistrates could seize and record — also not a few.

entries.zh: 尋蘇峻平後，庾亮就溫嶠求勳簿，而嶠不與，以爲陶侃所上，多非實錄。
entries.en: After Su Jun's defeat, Yu Liang asked Wen Qiao for the merit rolls, but Qiao refused, saying Tao Kan's submissions were largely fictitious.
entries.literal: After Su Jun was pacified, Yu Liang asked Wen Qiao for the merit rolls, but Qiao would not give them, holding that what Tao Kan had submitted was largely not a true record.

entries.zh: 尋物之懷私，無世不有，宋末落紐，此巧尤多。
entries.en: Self-seeking has never been absent in any age; but when Song neared its fall the bonds loosened, and this sort of fraud flourished as never before.
entries.literal: Seeking gain with a private heart — no age lacks it; at the end of Song the reins slackened, and this trickery was especially rife.

entries.zh: 又將位旣衆，舉卹爲祿，實潤甚微，而人領數萬，如此二條，天下合役之身，已據其太半矣。
entries.en: Generalships have multiplied, men claim mourning stipends as salary though the real gain is trifling, and thousands draw pay under each title — these two abuses alone already consume more than half the empire's conscriptable manpower.
entries.literal: Also, general ranks are already numerous; mourning stipends are raised as salary, yet the actual benefit is very slight, while men draw stipends in the tens of thousands — these two items alone already account for more than half of all conscripted bodies in the realm.

entries.zh: 又有改注籍狀。
entries.en: Registers are also altered wholesale.
entries.literal: There is also the altering of registered household status.

entries.zh: 詐入仕流，昔爲人役者，今反役人。
entries.en: Men fraudulently enter the official class: yesterday they served others; today they command servants of their own.
entries.literal: Fraudulently entering the official class — once men's servants, now in turn they enslave others.

entries.zh: 又生不長髮，便謂爲道人，塡街溢巷，是處皆然。
entries.en: Men who never grow hair declare themselves Daoist priests and fill every street and alley — the same fraud in every district.
entries.literal: Also, those who from birth do not grow hair are at once called Daoist priests — filling the streets and overflowing the alleys; everywhere it is so.

entries.zh: 或抱子幷居，竟不編戶，遷徙去來，公違土斷。
entries.en: Some live with wives and children yet never register a household, roaming from place to place in open defiance of the land-allotment laws.
entries.literal: Some hold their children and live together yet never register as households; they migrate back and forth and openly violate the land-allotment statutes.

entries.zh: 屬役無滿，流亡不歸，寧喪終身，疾病長臥。
entries.en: Conscripts fail to report for service; exiles refuse to return; some would rather die abroad than obey summons, others plead chronic illness and never rise.
entries.literal: Attached service goes unfulfilled; exiles do not return; they would rather die in exile than come home, or lie abed with chronic illness.

entries.zh: 法令必行，自然競反。
entries.en: Enforce the statutes in earnest and men will rush to comply of their own accord.
entries.literal: If laws and orders are truly enforced, men will naturally compete to return.

entries.zh: 又四鎮戍將，有名寡實，隨才部曲，無辨勇懦，署位借給，巫媼比肩，彌山滿海，皆是私役。
entries.en: The four frontier garrison generals too keep grand titles and empty ranks, enroll retainers without testing courage or cowardice, lend out offices on paper, and surround themselves with shamans and sorceresses mountain-high and sea-wide — all private servants, every one.
entries.literal: Also the four frontier garrison generals: names many, substance few; retainers taken at whim with no distinction of brave or coward; posts lent out on paper; shamans shoulder to shoulder, filling mountains and seas — all are private servants.

entries.zh: 行貨求位，其塗甚易，募役卑劇，何爲投補？
entries.en: A bribe buys a commission with ease, while conscript duty is mean and brutal — why would anyone volunteer to fill the ward rolls?
entries.literal: Bribery wins a post — the path is very easy; conscript service is base and harsh — why throw oneself in to fill the rolls?

entries.zh: 坊吏之所以盡，百里之所以單也。
entries.en: That is why ward clerks are run to exhaustion and districts lie stripped of men.
entries.literal: This is why ward clerks are exhausted and hundred-li districts stand empty.

entries.zh: 今但使募制明信，滿復有期，民無逕路，則坊可立表而盈矣。
entries.en: Make the conscription system transparent and binding, set a fixed term for fulfillment and release, and close every loophole — then the wards can post full rosters once more.
entries.literal: Now if only the conscription system were made trustworthy and clear, fulfillment and restoration were given a fixed term, and the people had no side path, then the wards could post their rosters and be full again.

entries.zh: 爲治不患無制，患在不行，不患不行，患在不久。」
entries.en: Good government is not undone by want of rules but by failure to enforce them; not by failure to enforce them but by failure to persevere."
entries.literal: In governing one does not fear lacking systems; one fears they are not carried out. One does not fear they are not carried out; one fears they will not last."

entries.zh: 上省玩之表，納之。
entries.en: The emperor reviewed Wanzhi's memorial and adopted it.
entries.literal: The emperor reviewed Wanzhi's memorial and accepted it.

entries.zh: 乃別置板籍官，置令史，限人一日得數巧，以防懈怠。
entries.en: A separate board-register office was established with clerks, each required to expose a set quota of frauds per day lest they grow slack.
entries.literal: Thereupon a separate board-register office was set up with clerks, each man limited to uncovering several frauds in a day, to guard against laxity.

entries.zh: 於是貨賂因緣，籍注雖正，猶強推卻，以充程限。
entries.en: Bribes soon bought exemption; even honest entries were forced back into dispute so clerks could meet their daily quota.
entries.literal: Then bribes worked through connections; though the register entries were correct, they were still forcibly rejected to meet the quota.

entries.zh: 至世祖永明八年，謫巧者戍緣淮各十年，百姓怨望。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Yongming, Emperor Wu banished registry fraudsters to garrison the Huai frontier for ten years apiece, and popular resentment boiled over.
entries.literal: By the eighth year of Yongming under Emperor Shizu, those convicted of registry fraud were banished to garrison the Huai frontier for ten years each, and the people groaned with resentment.

entries.zh: 世祖乃詔曰：「夫簡貴賤，辨尊卑者，莫不取信於黃籍。
entries.en: The emperor then decreed: "Rank and station rest on the yellow register;
entries.literal: The emperor then issued an edict: "In sorting noble from base and distinguishing high from low, all take their trust from the yellow register.

entries.zh: 豈有假器濫榮，竊服非分。
entries.en: how could men borrow titles, abuse honors, and usurp rank beyond their due?
entries.literal: How could one borrow titles and abuse honor, steal rank beyond one's measure?

entries.zh: 故所以澄革虛妄，式允舊章。
entries.en: We purge the false and restore the old statutes.
entries.literal: Therefore we clarify and reform the false, to accord with the old statutes.

entries.zh: 然釁起前代，過非近失，旣往之諐，不足追咎。
entries.en: Yet these abuses arose in earlier reigns, not in yesterday's lapse; past wrongs shall not be punished retroactively.
entries.literal: Yet the taint arose in former ages; the fault is not a recent slip. Wrongs already past are not worth pursuing to punishment.

entries.zh: 自宋昇明以前，皆聽復注。
entries.en: All who registered before Song's Shengming era may re-enter the rolls.
entries.literal: Before Shengming of Song, all are permitted to re-register.

entries.zh: 其有謫役邊疆，各許還本。
entries.en: Those banished to frontier labor may each return home.
entries.literal: Those banished to frontier service are each permitted to return to their native place.

entries.zh: 此後有犯，嚴加翦治。」
entries.en: Hereafter, offenders shall be punished without leniency."
entries.literal: After this, offenders shall be sternly cut down and disciplined."

entries.zh: 玩之以久宦衰疾，上表告退，曰：「臣聞負重致遠，力窮則困，竭誠事君，智盡必傾，理固然也。
entries.en: Wanzhi, worn out by long service and illness, asked to retire, writing: "I have heard that a man who bears a heavy load on a long road is trapped when his strength fails; a man who serves his lord with all his heart must lean when his wit is spent — such is the way of things.
entries.literal: Wanzhi, long in office and worn by illness, submitted a memorial asking to retire, saying: "Your servant has heard that he who bears a heavy load on a long road, when strength is spent, is trapped; he who serves his lord with utmost loyalty, when wisdom is exhausted, must lean — such is the way of things.

entries.zh: 四十仕進，七十懸車，壯則驅馳，老宜休息。
entries.en: At forty one takes office; at seventy one hangs up the carriage — youth may drive on, age should rest.
entries.literal: At forty one enters office; at seventy one hangs up the carriage — in strength one drives on, in age one should rest.

entries.zh: 臣生於晉，長於宋，老於齊，世歷三代，朝市再易。
entries.en: I was born under Jin, grew up under Song, and grow old under Qi — three dynasties in one lifetime, two overturnings of throne and market.
entries.literal: Your servant was born under Jin, grew up under Song, and grows old under Qi — three dynasties in one life, the court and market twice transformed.

entries.zh: 臣以宋元嘉二十八年爲王府行佐，於茲三十年矣。
entries.en: In Song's twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia I became staff aide to a princely household — thirty years have passed since.
entries.literal: Your servant in the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia of Song became staff aide to a princely establishment — thirty years have passed since.

entries.zh: 自頃以來，衰耗漸篤。
entries.en: Of late my decline has grown steep.
entries.literal: In recent times decline and exhaustion have grown severe.

entries.zh: 爲性不懶惰，而倦怠頓來。
entries.en: I am not lazy by nature, yet exhaustion has seized me all at once.
entries.literal: By nature I am not lazy, yet weariness has suddenly come on.

entries.zh: 耳目本聰明，而聾矒轉積。
entries.en: My ears and eyes were once sharp; now deafness and dim sight mount day by day.
entries.literal: Ears and eyes were once keen, yet deafness and dimness have steadily piled up.

entries.zh: 腳不支身，喘不緒氣。
entries.en: My legs will not bear me; my breath comes in broken gasps.
entries.literal: The feet cannot support the body; the breath cannot thread the qi.

entries.zh: 景刻不推，朝晝不保。
entries.en: The sundial's shadow scarcely moves; I cannot count on seeing another noon.
entries.literal: The sun's shadow will not advance; morning and noon are not assured.

entries.zh: 大功兄弟，四十有二人，通塞壽夭，唯臣獨存。
entries.en: Of forty-two brothers and cousins within the nine-month mourning degree, through fortune and ruin, long life and early death, I alone remain.
entries.literal: Brothers of the same great-grief mourning grade, forty-two in all — through fortune and misfortune, long life and early death, only your servant remains.

entries.zh: 朝露末光，寧堪長久！
entries.en: I am morning dew at its last gleam — how could I endure?
entries.literal: Morning dew's last gleam — how could it endure long!

entries.zh: 且知足不辱，臣已足矣。
entries.en: And he who knows when he has enough is not disgraced — I have had enough.
entries.literal: Moreover, he who knows sufficiency is not shamed — your servant has had enough.

entries.zh: 稟命饑寒，不求富貴，銅山由命，臣何恨焉，久甘之矣。
entries.en: Heaven gave me hunger and cold, not wealth; whether fate grants a copper mountain or not, I bear no grudge — I have been content long since.
entries.literal: Heaven's allotment is hunger and cold; I do not seek wealth and honor. Copper mountains lie in fate's hand — what resentment could your servant harbor? Long I have been content.

entries.zh: 直道事人，不免縲紲，屬遇聖明，知其非罪，臣之幸厚矣。
entries.en: Serving others on the straight path I could not escape the halter; under a sage reign the court knew my innocence — my fortune was already great.
entries.literal: Serving men on the straight path, I could not escape the halter; meeting a sage reign, the court knew I was not guilty — your servant's fortune was already great.

entries.zh: 授命於道消之晨，效節於百揆之日，臣忠之效也。
entries.en: I took office as the Jin Way faded, and served faithfully when the hundred offices were first assembled — that was my loyalty fulfilled.
entries.literal: Receiving mandate in the dawn when the Way declined, showing loyalty on the day when all chiefs gathered — that was your servant's effect of loyalty.

entries.zh: 降慶於文明之初，荷澤於天飛之運，臣命之偶也。
entries.en: Blessing came at the opening of Wenming; I bore favor in the fortune of the dynasty's rise — that was my lot in fate.
entries.literal: Blessing descended at the opening of Wenming, favor was borne on the fortune of heaven's flight — that was your servant's chance of fate.

entries.zh: 不謀巧宦而位至九卿，德慙李陵而忝居門下。
entries.en: Without scheming for preferment I rose to the nine ministers; in virtue I am ashamed before Li Ling, yet I presumptuously hold a Menxia post.
entries.literal: Without scheming for clever office I reached the nine ministers; in virtue I am ashamed before Li Ling, yet I occupy a post at the gate.

entries.zh: 堯舜無窮，臣亦通矣。
entries.en: Yao and Shun's blessings know no end — and I too have passed through them.
entries.literal: Yao and Shun are without end — your servant too has passed through.

entries.zh: 年過六十，不爲夭矣。
entries.en: Past sixty — that is no early death.
entries.literal: Past sixty years — that is not an early death.

entries.zh: 榮期之三樂，東平之一善，臣俱盡之矣。
entries.en: Rongqi's three joys and Dongping's one good deed — I have attained them all.
entries.literal: Rongqi's three joys and Dongping's one virtue — your servant has attained them all.

entries.zh: 經昏踐亂，涉艱履危，仰聖德以求全，憑賢輔以申節，未嘗厭屈於勳權，畏溺於狐鼠，臣立身之本，於斯不虧。
entries.en: I passed through dark reigns and trampled chaos, forded hardship and walked on danger; I looked up to sage virtue to keep myself whole and leaned on worthy aides to hold my station. I never demeaned myself by yielding to merit and power, never feared drowning among foxes and rats—and the ground I stand on has not given way.
entries.literal: Having passed through dark reigns and trampled chaos, forded hardship and walked on danger, I looked up to sage virtue to keep myself whole and leaned on worthy aides to hold my measure; I never tired of bending before merit and power, never feared drowning among foxes and rats—the ground on which I stand has not cracked here.

entries.zh: 在其壯也，當官不讓；
entries.en: In my strength I would not yield an office;
entries.literal: In my prime I would not yield an office;

entries.zh: 及其衰矣，豪露靡因。
entries.en: in my waning years, swagger and show have nothing left to lean on.
entries.literal: in my decline, swagger and display have nothing left to lean on.

entries.zh: 伏願慈臨，賜臣骸骨。
entries.en: I bow low and beg your kindness to look upon me and grant me my bones.
entries.literal: I humbly beg your kindness to look upon me and grant me my bones.

entries.zh: 非爲希高慕古，愛好泉林，特以丁運孤貧，養禮多闕，風樹之感，夙自纏心。
entries.en: Not that I court loftiness or pine for forests and springs—only that fate left me solitary and poor, my rites of nurture much broken; the wind-and-tree grief has gnawed at me since long ago.
entries.literal: Not that I court loftiness or pine for forests and springs—only that fate left me solitary and poor, my rites of nurture much broken; the wind-and-tree grief has gnawed at me since long ago.

entries.zh: 庶天假其辰，得二三年間，掃守丘墓，以此歸全，始終之報遂矣。」
entries.en: May Heaven lend me a span—two or three years—to sweep and keep my parents' mound; thus I may return whole, and my debt from first to last be paid."
entries.literal: May Heaven lend me a span—two or three years—to sweep and keep my parents' mound; thus I may return whole, and my debt from first to last be paid."

entries.zh: 上省玩之表，許之。
entries.en: The throne read Wan's memorial and granted it.
entries.literal: The emperor reviewed Wan's memorial and granted it.

entries.zh: 玩之於人物好臧否。
entries.en: Wan was keen to judge men, for good or ill.
entries.literal: Wan was fond of judging people, for good or ill.

entries.zh: 宋末，王儉舉員外郎孔襜使虜，玩之言論不相饒，襜、儉竝恨之。
entries.en: Late in Song, Wang Jian recommended Outer Court Gentleman Kong Can as envoy to the north; Wan's remarks showed no mercy, and Can and Jian both hated him for it.
entries.literal: Late in Song, Wang Jian recommended Outer Court Gentleman Kong Can as envoy to the north; Wan's remarks showed no mercy, and Can and Jian both hated him for it.

entries.zh: 至是玩之東歸，儉不出送，朝廷無祖餞者。
entries.en: When Wan went home east, Jian would not come out to see him off; the court held no farewell for him.
entries.literal: When Wan returned east, Jian did not come out to see him off; the court held no farewell feast for him.

entries.zh: 玩之歸家起大宅，數年卒。
entries.en: Wan raised a great house at home and died within a few years.
entries.literal: Wan returned home and raised a great mansion; within a few years he died.

entries.zh: 其後員外郎孔瑄就儉求會稽五官，儉方盥，投皂莢於地，曰：「卿鄉俗惡。
entries.en: Later Outer Court Gentleman Kong Xuan asked Jian for the Five Offices in Kuaiji; Jian was at his washstand and flung his soap pod to the floor, saying: "The ways of your homeland are foul.
entries.literal: Later Outer Court Gentleman Kong Xuan asked Jian for the Five Offices in Kuaiji; Jian was at his washstand and flung his soap pod to the floor, saying: "The ways of your homeland are foul.

entries.zh: 虞玩之至死煩人。」
entries.en: Yu Wanzhi was a pest to the very end."
entries.literal: Yu Wanzhi was a pest to the very end."

entries.zh: 孔襜字世遠，玩之同郡人，好典故學。
entries.en: Kong Can, styled Shiyuan, was Wan's fellow townsman and doted on statutes and precedent.
entries.literal: Kong Can, styled Shiyuan, was Wan's fellow townsman and loved learning in statutes and precedent.

entries.zh: 與王儉至交。
entries.en: He and Wang Jian were fast friends.
entries.literal: He and Wang Jian were close friends.

entries.zh: 昇明中爲齊臺尚書儀曹郎，太祖謂之曰：「卿儀曹才也。」
entries.en: In Shengming he served the Qi headquarters as Director of Ceremonial in the Secretariat; the Grand Ancestor told him: "You are Ceremonies Office talent."
entries.literal: In Shengming he served the Qi headquarters as Director of Ceremonial in the Secretariat; the Grand Ancestor told him: "You are Ceremonies Office talent."

entries.zh: 儉爲宰相，襜嘗謀議帷幕，每及選用，頗失鄉曲情。
entries.en: When Jian was chief minister, Can often counseled behind the curtain; whenever appointments arose, he often slighted hometown ties.
entries.literal: When Jian was chief minister, Can often counseled behind the curtain; whenever appointments arose, he often slighted hometown ties.

entries.zh: 儉從容啓上曰：「臣有孔襜，猶陛下之有臣也。」
entries.en: Jian calmly told the throne: "Your servant has Kong Can, as Your Majesty has your servant."
entries.literal: Jian calmly told the throne: "Your servant has Kong Can, as Your Majesty has your servant."

entries.zh: 永明中爲太子家令，卒。
entries.en: In Yongming he was Heir Apparent Household Steward; he died.
entries.literal: In Yongming he was Heir Apparent Household Steward; he died.

entries.zh: 時人呼孔襜、何憲爲王儉三公。
entries.en: Men of the day called Kong Can and He Xian the three dukes at Wang Jian's side.
entries.literal: Men of the day called Kong Can and He Xian the three dukes at Wang Jian's side.

entries.zh: 建元初，爲御史中丞。
entries.en: When Jianyuan began he was made censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: At the opening of Jianyuan he was made Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 頃之，休啓曰：「臣自塵榮南憲，星晷交春，謬聞弱奏，劾無空月。
entries.en: Soon after, Xiu memorialized: "Since I took this southern censor's seat, a year has turned; feeble denunciations were credited, and not one month passed without an impeachment.
entries.literal: Before long Xiu memorialized, saying: "Since I took office stained by southern censorial glory, stars and seasons have crossed spring; weak reports were wrongly heard, and impeachments never left a month empty.

entries.zh: 豈唯不能使蕃邦斂手，豪右屏氣，乃遣聽已暴之辜，替網觸羅之鳥。
entries.en: I could not even make the borderlands stand down or the great houses quail; I only turned loose men who heard out crimes already plain, and birds that had touched the net in someone else's stead.
entries.literal: Not only could I not make frontier states fold their hands and powerful houses hold their breath, I even sent forth those who listened to guilt already exposed, birds that brushed the net in another's place.

entries.zh: 而猶以此，里失鄉黨之和，朝絕比肩之顧，覆背騰其喉唇，武人厲其觜吻。
entries.en: Even so, villages lost the peace of the lane, the court lost the glance of equals; back-turners filled the air with accusation, and soldiers sharpened their tongues for attack.
entries.literal: Yet because of this, hamlets lost neighborhood harmony, the court lost shoulder-to-shoulder regard; turncoats raised throat and lips, military men whet beak and mouth.

entries.zh: 怨之所聚，勢難久堪；
entries.en: Where hatred pools, no man can stand it for long;
entries.literal: Where resentment gathers, the situation is hard to bear long;

entries.zh: 議之所裁，孰懷其允？
entries.en: where judgment falls, who believes it just?
entries.literal: where deliberation cuts, who holds its fairness?

entries.zh: 臣竊尋宋世載祀六十，歷職斯任者五十有三，校其年月，不過盈歲。
entries.en: I have looked back through the Song's sixty reign-years: fifty-three men held this post, and none of them, by the count of years and months, lasted more than one.
entries.literal: I privately trace the Song age's sixty years of sacrifice: fifty-three men held this office; compare their years and months, and none exceeded a full year.

entries.zh: 于臣叨濫，宜請骸骨。」
entries.en: For my own presumption, I ought to ask leave to go home."
entries.literal: As for my presumptuous excess, I should ask leave to resign and return home."

entries.zh: 上曰：「卿職當國司，以威裁爲本，而忽憚世誚。
entries.en: The emperor said, "Your post is the state's inspector; its root is awe and judgment—yet now you flinch at the world's mockery.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Your office stands as national inspector; awe and judgment are its foundation—yet you suddenly fear worldly ridicule.

entries.zh: 卿便應辭之事始，何可獲惰晚節邪？」
entries.en: You should have quit when you began. How can you coast into a soft old age?"
entries.literal: You should have resigned at the start; how can you slack into a lazy late season?"

entries.zh: 休初爲駙馬都尉，奉朝請，宋明帝湘東國常侍。
entries.en: Xiu first served as Commandant of Escort Cavalry, Court Attendant for Imperial Audiences, and regular attendant in the Xiangdong establishment of the future Emperor Ming of Song.
entries.literal: Xiu first served as Commandant of Escort Cavalry, Court Attendant for Imperial Audiences, and regular attendant of the future Emperor Ming of Song's Xiangdong establishment.

entries.zh: 好學諳憶，不爲帝所知。
entries.en: He loved learning and had a retentive memory, yet the emperor did not know him.
entries.literal: He loved learning and had a retentive memory, yet the emperor did not know him.

entries.zh: 襲祖封南鄉侯。
entries.en: He inherited his grandfather's fief as Marquis of Nanxiang.
entries.literal: He inherited his grandfather's fief as Marquis of Nanxiang.

entries.zh: 友人陳郡謝儼同丞相義宣反，休坐匿之，被繫尚方七年，孝武崩，乃得出。
entries.en: His friend Xie Yan of Chen joined Chancellor Yixuan's rebellion; Xiu was convicted of hiding him and held in the Imperial Workshop seven years, coming out only when Emperor Xiaowu died.
entries.literal: His friend Xie Yan of Chen joined Chancellor Yixuan's rebellion; Xiu was convicted of hiding him and held in the Imperial Workshop seven years, coming out only when Emperor Xiaowu died.

entries.zh: 隨弟欽爲羅縣。
entries.en: He followed his younger brother Qin to Luo county.
entries.literal: He followed his younger brother Qin to Luo county.

entries.zh: 泰始初，諸州反，休筮明帝當勝，靜處不預異謀。
entries.en: In early Taishi, when the provinces rose in revolt, Xiu divined that Emperor Ming would prevail and kept apart, taking no part in the plotters.
entries.literal: In early Taishi, when the provinces rose in revolt, Xiu divined that Emperor Ming would prevail and kept apart, taking no part in the plotters.

entries.zh: 數年，還投吳喜爲輔師府錄事參軍。
entries.en: After several years he returned and entered Wu Xi's staff as recorder in the Supporting Army headquarters.
entries.literal: After several years he returned and entered Wu Xi's staff as recorder in the Supporting Army headquarters.

entries.zh: 喜稱其才，進之明帝，得在左右。
entries.en: Xi praised his gifts and recommended him to Emperor Ming; he won a place at the sovereign's side.
entries.literal: Xi praised his gifts and recommended him to Emperor Ming; he won a place at the sovereign's side.

entries.zh: 板桂陽王征北參軍。
entries.en: He was commissioned Northern Campaign aide to the Prince of Guiyang.
entries.literal: He was commissioned Northern Campaign aide to the Prince of Guiyang.

entries.zh: 尋除員外郎，領輔國司馬、中書通事舍人，帶南城令。
entries.en: Before long he was made an aide, with concurrent posts as Pacification Army aide, secretariat communication attendant, and intendant of Southern City.
entries.literal: Soon he was made aide, with concurrent aide to the Pacification Army, secretariat communication attendant, and Intendant of Southern City.

entries.zh: 除尚書中兵郎，給事中，舍人、令如故。
entries.en: He was made secretariat central troops officer and attendant at the bureau; his attendant and intendant posts were unchanged.
entries.literal: He was made Secretariat Central Troops Officer and attendant at the bureau; attendant and intendant stood as before.

entries.zh: 除安成王撫軍參軍，出爲都水使者，南康相。
entries.en: He was made staff officer on the Prince of Ancheng's pacification army, then sent out as commissioner of waters and chancellor of Nankang.
entries.literal: He was made staff officer to the Prince of Ancheng's Pacification Army, then sent out as Commissioner of Waters and Chancellor of Nankang.

entries.zh: 休善言治體，而在郡無異績。
entries.en: Xiu talked fluently about how states should be run, yet in office he left no mark worth naming.
entries.literal: Xiu spoke well on governing principles, but in the commandery achieved nothing distinctive.

entries.zh: 還爲正員郎，邵陵王南中郎錄事、建威將軍、新蔡太守。
entries.en: He came back as a regular officer, recorder on the Prince of Shaoling's southern staff, Jianwei general, and grand administrator of Xincai.
entries.literal: He returned as a regular officer, Prince of Shaoling's Southern Center Staff recorder, Jianwei general, and Grand Administrator of Xincai.

entries.zh: 隨轉左軍府，加鎮蠻護軍，將軍、太守如故。
entries.en: He moved with the left army headquarters and was given the added title protector-general for pacifying the barbarians; his generalship and grand administration stayed the same.
entries.literal: He transferred with the Left Army headquarters, was given the added title Pacification of the Barbarians Protector-General; general and grand administrator stood as before.

entries.zh: 遷諮議，司馬，進寧朔將軍，鎮蠻護軍、太守如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to adviser and military aide and advanced to Ningshuo general; his barbarian-pacification and grand administration posts were unchanged.
entries.literal: He was promoted to adviser and military aide, advanced to Ningshuo general; Pacification of the Barbarians and grand administrator stood as before.

entries.zh: 徙尋陽太守，將軍、司馬如故。
entries.en: He was transferred to grand administrator of Xunyang; his generalship and military aide post remained.
entries.literal: He was moved to Grand Administrator of Xunyang; general and military aide stood as before.

entries.zh: 後遷長史。
entries.en: Later he was made chief aide.
entries.literal: Later he was promoted to chief aide.

entries.zh: 沈攸之難，世祖挾晉熙邵陵二王軍府鎮盆城，休承奉軍費，事寧，仍遷邵陵王安南長史，除黃門郎，寧朔將軍，前軍長史，齊臺散騎常侍。
entries.en: When Shen Youzhi rose, Emperor Wu of Qi took the Jinxi and Shaoling princely headquarters and garrisoned Pencheng; Xiu handled military funds. After peace returned he became the Prince of Shaoling's pacification-of-the-south chief aide, then yellow gate officer, Ningshuo general, front-army chief aide, and Qi platform regular attendant.
entries.literal: During Shen Youzhi's rebellion, Shizu, Emperor Wu of Qi, took the military headquarters of the Princes of Jinxi and Shaoling and garrisoned Pencheng; Xiu managed military expenses; when the matter was settled, he was moved to the Prince of Shaoling's Pacification of the South chief aide, made Yellow Gate Officer, Ningshuo general, front army chief aide, and Qi Platform Regular Attendant.

entries.zh: 沈沖字景綽，吳興武康人也。
entries.en: Shen Chong, styled Jingchuo, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery.
entries.literal: Shen Chong styled Jingchuo and was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.

entries.zh: 祖宣，新安太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Xuan had been grand administrator of Xin'an.
entries.literal: His grandfather Xuan was Grand Administrator of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 父懷文，廣陵太守。
entries.en: His father Huaiwen had been grand administrator of Guangling.
entries.literal: His father Huaiwen was Grand Administrator of Guangling.

entries.zh: 沖解褐衛尉五官，轉揚州主簿。
entries.en: Chong entered service as five officials under the guard commandant, then became Yangzhou chief clerk.
entries.literal: Chong began office as Five Officials of the Guard Commandant and transferred to Yangzhou chief clerk.

entries.zh: 宋大明中，懷文有文名，沖亦涉獵文義。
entries.en: In Song's Daming reign Huaiwen won a name for letters, and Chong too dipped into literary studies.
entries.literal: In Song's Daming period Huaiwen had literary fame, and Chong also ranged in literary meaning.

entries.zh: 轉西陽王撫軍法曹參軍，尋舉秀才，還爲撫軍正佐，兼記室。
entries.en: He became law-cao staff officer on the Prince of Xiyang's pacification army, was soon nominated as xiucai, and came back as the army's principal aide, doubling as secretary.
entries.literal: He transferred to Prince of Xiyang's Pacification Army Law Cao staff officer, was soon nominated as xiucai, and returned as Pacification Army principal aide, also secretary.

entries.zh: 及懷文得罪被繫，沖兄弟行謝，情哀貌苦，見者傷之。
entries.en: When Huaiwen fell into guilt and was bound, Chong and his brothers went to beg mercy, grief in their voices and ruin on their faces, and all who saw them wept.
entries.literal: When Huaiwen offended and was imprisoned, Chong and his brothers went to plead; emotion was sorrowful and face bitter—viewers were moved.

entries.zh: 柳元景欲救懷文，言于帝曰：「沈懷文三子塗炭不可見，願陛下速正其罪。」
entries.en: Liu Yuanjing tried to save Huaiwen and told the emperor, "Shen Huaiwen's three sons are in the fire—no eye can bear them; let Your Majesty settle his case at once."
entries.literal: Liu Yuanjing wished to save Huaiwen and spoke to the emperor, saying: "Shen Huaiwen's three sons are in charcoal—unbearable to see; I beg Your Majesty quickly to rectify his crime."

entries.zh: 帝竟殺之。
entries.en: The emperor killed him all the same.
entries.literal: The emperor in the end killed him.

entries.zh: 元景爲之嘆息。
entries.en: Yuanjing mourned it in silence.
entries.literal: Yuanjing sighed for it.

entries.zh: 沖兄弟以此知名。
entries.en: Chong and his brothers won their fame from that hour.
entries.literal: Chong and his brothers became famous because of this.

entries.zh: 泰始初，以母老家貧，啓明帝得爲永興令。
entries.en: When Taishi began, his mother was old and his house was poor; he petitioned Emperor Ming and was given Yongxing magistrate.
entries.literal: At the opening of Taishi, because his mother was old and his home poor, he memorialized Ming Emperor and obtained the post of Magistrate of Yongxing.

entries.zh: 遷巴陵王主簿，除尚書殿中郎。
entries.en: He became chief clerk to the Prince of Baling, then Palace Gentleman in the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk to the Prince of Baling and appointed Palace Gentleman in the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 元徽中，出爲晉安王安西記室參軍，還爲司徒主簿，山陰令，轉司徒錄事參軍。
entries.en: Under Yuanhui he went out as secretary on the Prince of Jin'an's pacification of the west, came back as Situ chief clerk and magistrate of Shanyin, then became Situ recorder.
entries.literal: In the Yuanhui period he was sent out as Prince of Jin'an's Pacification of the West secretary, returned as Situ chief clerk and Magistrate of Shanyin, and transferred to Situ recorder staff officer.

entries.zh: 世祖爲江州，沖爲征虜長史、尋陽太守，甚見委遇。
entries.en: When the future Emperor Wu of Qi governed Jiangzhou, Chong served as chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and grand administrator of Xunyang, and was deeply trusted.
entries.literal: When Shizu, the future Emperor Wu of Qi, governed Jiangzhou, Chong was chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs and Grand Administrator of Xunyang, and was greatly trusted.

entries.zh: 世祖還都，使沖行府、州事。
entries.en: When the future Emperor Wu returned to the capital, he left Chong in charge of headquarters and provincial affairs.
entries.literal: When Shizu returned to the capital, he had Chong administer the headquarters and provincial affairs.

entries.zh: 遷領軍長史。
entries.en: He was promoted to chief aide of the army leader.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Army Leader chief aide.

entries.zh: 建元初，轉驃騎諮議參軍，領錄事，未及到任，轉黃門郎，仍遷太子中庶子。
entries.en: When Jianyuan opened he was made rapid-cavalry adviser and put in charge of recording; before he took up the post he was made yellow gate officer, then crown prince central attendant.
entries.literal: At the opening of Jianyuan he was transferred to Rapid Cavalry adviser staff officer and led recorder duties; before he reached the post he was transferred to Yellow Gate Officer, then promoted to Crown Prince Central Attendant.

entries.zh: 世祖在東宮，待以恩舊。
entries.en: While the future Emperor Wu was crown prince, he treated Chong with the favor due an old retainer.
entries.literal: When Shizu was in the Eastern Palace, he treated Chong with the favor due an old retainer.

entries.zh: 及卽位，轉御史中丞，侍中。
entries.en: Once enthroned, the emperor moved Chong to censor-in-chief and attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, Chong was transferred to Censor-in-Chief and Attendant-in-Ordinary.

entries.zh: 冠軍廬陵王子卿爲郢州，以沖爲長史、輔國將軍、江夏內史，行府、州事。
entries.en: When Ziqing, Champion General and Prince of Luling, became Inspector of Yingzhou, Chong served as his chief clerk, General Who Assists the State, and interior minister of Jiangxia, with charge of headquarters and provincial affairs.
entries.literal: When Ziqing, Champion General and Prince of Luling, became Inspector of Yingzhou, he appointed Chong chief clerk, General Who Assists the State, and interior minister of Jiangxia, with charge of headquarters and provincial affairs.

entries.zh: 隨府轉爲安西長史、南郡內史，行荊州府事，將軍如故。
entries.en: When the headquarters was transferred, Chong became chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West and interior minister of Nan Commandery, with charge of Jingzhou headquarters affairs; his general's title remained unchanged.
entries.literal: When the headquarters was transferred, Chong became chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the West and interior minister of Nan Commandery, administering Jingzhou headquarters affairs; his general's title remained unchanged.

entries.zh: 永明四年，徵爲五兵尚書。
entries.en: In Yongming's fourth year he was recalled as minister of the five arms.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming he was summoned as Minister of the Five Arms.

entries.zh: 世祖方欲任沖，沖西下至南州而卒。
entries.en: The emperor was on the verge of giving Chong greater trust when Chong went west toward the southern provinces and died on the journey.
entries.literal: The Emperor was just about to employ Chong when Chong went west to the southern provinces and died on the road.

entries.zh: 時年五十一。
entries.en: He was fifty-one.
entries.literal: He was fifty-one.

entries.zh: 上甚惜之。
entries.en: The throne mourned him deeply.
entries.literal: The emperor deeply regretted it.

entries.zh: 喪還，詔曰：「沖喪柩至止，惻愴良深。
entries.en: When the coffin came home, an edict ran: "Now that Chong's bier has halted, my grief cuts deep.
entries.literal: When the coffin returned, an edict said: "Chong's bier has reached its halt; my sorrow is profound.

entries.zh: 以其昔在南蕃，特兼憫悼。」
entries.en: He once held the southern marches, and I grant him a further measure of pity."
entries.literal: Because he once served in the southern marches, I add special pity."

entries.zh: 車駕出臨沖喪，詔曰：「沖貞詳閒理，志局淹正。
entries.en: The emperor went in person to Chong's mourning; the edict said: "Chong was upright and exact in principle, his vision wide and his bearing straight.
entries.literal: The imperial carriage went out to attend Chong's mourning; an edict said: "Chong was upright, thorough, and versed in principle; his aims were broad and his conduct correct.

entries.zh: 誠著蕃朝，績彰出守。
entries.en: Loyalty marked him in the southern court; achievement marked him in posts beyond the capital.
entries.literal: His loyalty showed in the southern court; his achievements shone in office outside the capital.

entries.zh: 不幸早世，朕甚悼之。」
entries.en: To lose him young is bitter grief, and I mourn him deeply."
entries.literal: His early death is a bitter loss; I grieve deeply."

entries.zh: 追贈太常，諡曰恭子。
entries.en: He was posthumously made grand minister of ceremonies, with the posthumous name Gongzi, the Reverent.
entries.literal: Posthumously he was given Grand Minister of Ceremonies; his posthumous title was Gongzi, the Reverent.

entries.zh: 杲之少而貞立，學涉文義。
entries.en: From youth Gaozhi stood upright and unbending, and he ranged through letters and moral argument.
entries.literal: Gaozhi from youth was upright and firm, and his studies ranged through literary meaning.

entries.zh: 起家奉朝請，巴陵王征西參軍。
entries.en: He entered service as a court gentleman and staff officer on the Prince of Baling's west-expedition army.
entries.literal: He began office as a court gentleman, staff officer on the Prince of Baling's west-expedition army.

entries.zh: 郢州舉秀才，除晉熙王鎮西外兵參軍，世祖徵虜府功曹，尚書駕部郎。
entries.en: Yingzhou nominated him as xiucai; he became outer military staff officer to the Prince of Jinxi as General Who Pacifies the West, merit officer in the future Emperor Wu of Qi's headquarters as General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs, and Gentleman of the Chariot Bureau in the Department of State Affairs.
entries.literal: Yingzhou nominated him as xiucai; he was appointed outer military staff officer to the Prince of Jinxi as General Who Pacifies the West, merit officer in Shizu's headquarters as General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs, and Gentleman of the Chariot Bureau in the Department of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 清貧自業，食唯有韭菹、𤅢韭、生韭雜菜，或戲之曰：「誰謂庾郎貧，食鮭常有二十七種。」
entries.en: He lived in poverty by choice; his table held only chive pickle, vinegared chives, raw chives, and humble greens. A wit said: "Who calls Minister Yu poor? When he dines on fish dishes he still has twenty-seven kinds."
entries.literal: Poor and self-reliant, his fare was only chive pickle, vinegared chives, raw chives, and mixed vegetables; someone jested: "Who says Minister Yu is poor? When he eats salmon there are always twenty-seven kinds."

entries.zh: 言三九也。
entries.en: —three dishes, three nines.
entries.literal: —meaning three times nine.

entries.zh: 仍爲世祖撫軍中軍記室，遷員外散騎常侍，正員郎，遷中書郎，領荊、湘二州中正。
entries.en: He then served as recorder in the future Emperor Wu of Qi's headquarters as General of Pacification and General of the Central Army, rose to supernumerary Regular Mounted Attendant and then Regular Gentleman, became Secretariat Gentleman, and concurrently served as rectifier for Jingzhou and Xiangzhou.
entries.literal: He then served as recorder in Shizu's headquarters as General of Pacification and General of the Central Army, was promoted to supernumerary Regular Mounted Attendant and then Regular Gentleman, moved to Secretariat Gentleman, and concurrently served as rectifier for Jingzhou and Xiangzhou.

entries.zh: 杲之風範和潤，善音吐。
entries.en: Gaozhi's manner was mild and harmonious, and his speech was beautifully clear.
entries.literal: Gaozhi's bearing was mild and harmonious, and he was skilled in clear delivery.

entries.zh: 世祖令對虜使，兼侍中。
entries.en: The emperor ordered him to receive the barbarian envoys, with added rank as attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered him to face the barbarian envoys, with added rank as attendant-in-ordinary.

entries.zh: 上每嘆其風器之美，王儉在座，曰：「杲之爲蟬冕所照，更生風采。
entries.en: The emperor often sighed over the grace of his person; Wang Jian, seated beside him, said: "Gaozhi looks all the more distinguished beneath the cicada crown.
entries.literal: The emperor often sighed over the beauty of his presence; Wang Jian, seated nearby, said: "When Gaozhi's cicada crown catches the imperial light, his bearing shines all the more.

entries.zh: 陛下故當與其卽眞。」
entries.en: Your Majesty should give him the full post at last."
entries.literal: Your Majesty ought to grant him the real appointment."

entries.zh: 帝意未用也。
entries.en: The emperor had not yet made up his mind.
entries.literal: The emperor's mind had not yet settled on it.

entries.zh: 永明中，諸王年少，不得妄與人接，敕杲之與濟陽江淹五日一詣諸王，使申游好。
entries.en: In Yongming the princes were still young and might not receive visitors freely; the court ordered Gaozhi and Jiang Yan of Jiyang to call on them every five days and keep cordial ties alive.
entries.literal: In Yongming the princes were young and might not receive visitors at will; the throne ordered Gaozhi and Jiang Yan of Jiyang to call on the princes every five days, so that friendly ties might be kept.

entries.zh: 尋又遷廬陵王中軍長史，遷尚書吏部郎，參大選事。
entries.en: Soon he became chief clerk on the Prince of Luling's central army, then director of the ministry of personnel, sharing charge of the great selection.
entries.literal: Soon he was again moved to chief clerk on the Prince of Luling's central army, then to director of the ministry of personnel, sharing charge of the great selection.

entries.zh: 轉太子右衛率，加通直常侍。
entries.en: He was made right commander of the heir apparent's guard, with added rank as unimpeded regular attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to right commander of the heir apparent's guard, with added rank as unimpeded regular attendant.

entries.zh: 九年，卒。
entries.en: In the ninth year he died.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he died.

entries.zh: 臨終上表曰：「臣昨夜及旦，更增氣疾，自省綿痼，頃刻危殆，無容復臥。
entries.en: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial: "Last night and this dawn my breath-sickness worsened; I know this chronic ailment, and moment by moment I edge toward death—I can no longer keep to my couch.
entries.literal: On his deathbed he submitted a memorial: "Last night and this morning my breath-sickness grew worse; seeing my long illness, I am in peril from moment to moment and can no longer lie abed.

entries.zh: 任居隆顯，玷塵明世，乞解所忝，待終私庭。
entries.en: I hold a lofty, glaring post and soil a bright reign; I beg release from my offices and leave to meet the end in my own hall.
entries.literal: My post is lofty and bright, yet I stain a luminous age; I beg to be released from what I hold and await the end in my own house.

entries.zh: 臣以凡庸，謬徼昌運，獎擢之厚，千載難逢。
entries.en: I am a common mediocrity who stumbled into a prosperous age; the favor the throne has shown me comes once in a thousand years.
entries.literal: I am a common mediocrity who wrongly caught a prosperous age; the favor shown me is a bounty met once in a thousand years.

entries.zh: 且年逾知命，志事榮顯，脩夭有分，無所厝言。
entries.en: I have already passed the age of knowing Heaven's mandate; I sought honor and a shining name; life and death have their measure, and I have no further plea.
entries.literal: I have already passed the age of knowing mandate; my aims were honor and eminence; length of life has its portion, and I have nothing left to say.

entries.zh: 若天鑒微誠，暫借餘歷，傾宗殞元，陳力無遠。
entries.en: If Heaven reads my slight sincerity and grants me a little more time, I would spend house and kin and lay down my life, serving with all my strength and never at a distance.
entries.literal: If Heaven looks on my slight sincerity and lends me a little more time, I would spend my clan and give my life, serving with all my strength and never from afar.

entries.zh: 仰違庭闕，伏枕鯁戀。
entries.en: I look up and leave the palace gate behind; pillow-bound, my throat knots with longing.
entries.literal: I look up and turn from the palace court; prostrate on my pillow, my throat tight with longing.

entries.zh: 送貂蟬及章。」
entries.en: He sent in his cicada crown and seal of office."
entries.literal: He sent in his cicada crown and seal."

entries.zh: 詔不許。
entries.en: The throne would not allow it.
entries.literal: The edict did not grant it.

entries.zh: 杲之歷在上府，以文學見遇。
entries.en: Gaozhi had risen through the great households and won notice for letters.
entries.literal: Gaozhi had long served in the upper offices and was favored for his literary learning.

entries.zh: 上造崇虛館，使爲碑文。
entries.en: The emperor raised the Chongxu Pavilion and set him to write the stone.
entries.literal: The emperor built the Chongxu Pavilion and had him compose its memorial inscription.

entries.zh: 卒時年五十一，上甚惜之。
entries.en: He died at fifty-one, and the throne mourned him deeply.
entries.literal: When he died he was fifty-one; the emperor deeply regretted it.

entries.zh: 諡曰貞子。
entries.en: His posthumous title was Zhenzi, Master Upright.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Master Upright.

entries.zh: 轉尚書左丞，常侍、領中正如故。
entries.en: He became Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs while retaining his posts as Regular Mounted Attendant and rectifier.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; his Regular Mounted Attendant and rectifier posts remained as before.

entries.zh: 出爲王儉衛軍長史，時人呼入儉府爲芙蓉池。
entries.en: He went out as chief clerk on Wang Jian's guard-army staff; contemporaries called service in Jian's house "the Lotus Pond."
entries.literal: He went out as chief clerk on Wang Jian's guard-army staff; men of the day called entering Jian's office "the Lotus Pond."

entries.zh: 儉謂人曰：「昔袁公作衛軍，欲用我爲長史，雖不獲就，要是意向如此。
entries.en: Jian told others: "When Yuan Gong ran the guard army he wanted me as chief clerk; I never took the post, but the wish was plain.
entries.literal: Jian told others: "In the past Yuan Gong held the guard army and wished to make me chief clerk; though I did not take it, that was the intent.

entries.zh: 今亦應須如我輩人也。」
entries.en: Now he ought to have men of our stamp again."
entries.literal: Now he should likewise have men of our sort."

entries.zh: 乃用杲之。
entries.en: So Gaozhi was chosen.
entries.literal: And so Gaozhi was appointed.

entries.zh: 遷黃門郎，兼御史中丞，尋卽正。
entries.en: He was made gentleman at the Yellow Gate and acting censor-in-chief; before long the censorate was his in full.
entries.literal: He was moved to gentleman at the Yellow Gate, with concurrent censor-in-chief; soon he held the censorate in full.

entries.zh: 世祖與諶相遇於宋明之世，欲委任，爲輔國將軍、晉安王南中郎長史、淮南太守，行府、州事。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Qi had known Chen in Emperor Ming of Song's reign and meant to entrust him with office. Chen became General Who Assists the State, chief clerk to the Prince of Jin'an as General of the Household for the South, and grand administrator of Huainan, with charge of both headquarters and provincial affairs.
entries.literal: Shizu had known Chen in Emperor Ming of Song's time and wished to entrust him with office; Chen was made General Who Assists the State, chief clerk to the Prince of Jin'an as General of the Household for the South, and grand administrator of Huainan, acting for both headquarters and province.

entries.zh: 五年，除黃門郎，領驍騎將軍，遷太子中庶子，驍騎如故。
entries.en: In year five he was yellow gate officer with added valiant cavalry general, then crown prince central attendant, valiant cavalry unchanged.
entries.literal: In year five he was made Yellow Gate Officer, with added rank as valiant cavalry general, moved to crown prince central attendant, valiant cavalry as before.

entries.zh: 諶貞正和謹，朝廷稱爲善人，多與之厚。
entries.en: Chen was upright, even-tempered, and careful; the court named him a good man, and many kept him near.
entries.literal: Chen was upright, harmonious, and careful; the court called him a good man, and many drew close to him.

entries.zh: 八年，轉冠軍將軍、長沙王車騎長史，徙廬陵王中軍長史，將軍如故。
entries.en: In year eight he became champion general and chief staff officer to the Prince of Changsha's chariot-and-cavalry command, then staff officer on the Prince of Luling's central army, his generalship unchanged.
entries.literal: In year eight he was moved to champion general and chief staff officer to the Prince of Changsha's chariot-and-cavalry command, then staff officer on the Prince of Luling's central army; his generalship stood as before.

entries.zh: 西陽王子明在南兖州，長史沈憲去職，上復徙諶爲征虜長史，行南兖府、州事，將軍如故。
entries.en: When Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, was Inspector of Southern Yanzhou and his chief clerk Shen Xian left office, the emperor transferred Chen there as chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs, with charge of headquarters and provincial affairs; his general's title remained unchanged.
entries.literal: When Ziming, Prince of Xiyang, was Inspector of Southern Yanzhou and chief clerk Shen Xian left office, the emperor transferred Chen there as chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs, with charge of Southern Yanzhou headquarters and provincial affairs; his general's title remained unchanged.

entries.zh: 虞玩之
entries.en: Yu Wanzhi
entries.literal: Yu Wanzhi

entries.zh: 武陵昭王曄，字宣照，太祖第五子也。
entries.en: Prince Zhao of Wuling, Ye, styled Xuanzhao, was the founding emperor's fifth son.
entries.literal: Prince Zhao of Wuling Ye, styled Xuanzhao, was the founding emperor's fifth son.

entries.zh: 母羅氏，從太祖在淮陰，以罪誅，曄年四歲，思慕不異成人，故每見愛。
entries.en: His mother was Lady Luo; she had followed the founding emperor at Huaiyin and was executed; at four Ye grieved like a grown man — and was always cherished for it.
entries.literal: His mother was the Luo clan; she followed the founding emperor at Huaiyin and was executed for a crime; Ye at four years mourned with longing no different from an adult — therefore he was always loved.

entries.zh: 初除冠軍將軍，轉征虜將軍。
entries.en: He was first champion general, then General Who Punishes the Barbarians.
entries.literal: He was first made champion general, then transferred General Who Punishes the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 曄剛穎俊出， 工弈棋，與諸王共作短句，詩學謝靈運體，以呈上，報曰：「見汝二十字，諸兒作中最為優者。
entries.en: Ye was sharp and outstanding, skilled at chess; with his brothers he wrote short verses in Xie Lingyun's style and presented them; the emperor replied: "In your twenty characters this is the best of the boys' work.
entries.literal: Ye was forceful and outstanding, skilled at chess; with the other princes he composed short verses in Xie Lingyun's manner and presented them; the reply said: "Seeing your twenty characters — among the boys' work this is finest.

entries.zh: 但康樂放蕩，作體不辨有首尾，安仁、士衡深可宗尚，顏延之抑 其次也。」
entries.en: Yet Lingyun is unrestrained — his pieces lack clear beginning and end; Pan Yue and Lu Ji are truly worth emulating; Yan Yanzhi ranks beneath them."
entries.literal: Yet Lingyun is unrestrained — his pieces have no clear head or tail; Anren and Shiheng are truly to be honored; Yan Yanzhi ranks below them."

entries.zh: 建元三年，出為持節、都督會稽東陽新安永嘉臨海五郡軍事、會稽太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: In Jianyuan year three he went out bearer of credentials, commander of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, and governor of Kuaiji, rank unchanged.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jianyuan he went out bearer of credentials, commander of military affairs in five commanderies — Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai — and governor of Kuaiji, general as before.

entries.zh: 上遣儒士劉瓛往郡，為曄講《五經》。
entries.en: The emperor sent the scholar Liu Huan to lecture Ye on the Five Classics in his commandery.
entries.literal: The emperor sent the scholar Liu Huan to the commandery to lecture Ye on the Five Classics.

entries.zh: 建武之世，高、武子孫憂危，鉉每朝見，常鞠躬俯僂，不敢平行直視。
entries.en: In the Jianwu era the Gao and Wu descendants lived in fear; at each court audience Xuan bowed deeply and stooped, not daring to walk level or look straight ahead.
entries.literal: In the Jianwu era the Gao and Wu descendants lived in fear; at each court audience Xuan would bow deeply and stoop, not daring to walk level or look straight ahead.

entries.zh: 尋遷侍中、衛將軍。
entries.en: Soon he was moved attendant and Defender General.
entries.literal: Soon he was moved attendant and Defender General.

entries.zh: 鉉年稍長。
entries.en: Xuan grew somewhat older.
entries.literal: Xuan grew somewhat older.

entries.zh: 四年，誅王晏，以謀立鉉為名，免鉉官，以王還第，禁不得與外人交通。
entries.en: In year four Wang Yan was executed; on the charge of plotting to enthrone Xuan, Xuan was stripped of office, sent back to his mansion, and forbidden contact with outsiders.
entries.literal: In year four Wang Yan was executed; on the charge of plotting to enthrone Xuan, Xuan was stripped of office, sent back to his mansion as a prince, and forbidden to have contact with outsiders.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，上疾暴甚，遂害鉉，時年十九。
entries.en: In Yongtai year one the emperor's illness suddenly worsened; he then killed Xuan, who was nineteen.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai the emperor's illness suddenly worsened; he then killed Xuan, who was then nineteen.

entries.zh: 二子在孩抱，亦見殺。
entries.en: His two infant sons were also killed.
entries.literal: His two sons, still in infancy, were also killed.

entries.zh: 太祖諸王，鉉獨無後，眾竊冤之。
entries.en: Among the founding emperor's princes, Xuan alone left no heirs; many privately considered it unjust.
entries.literal: Among the founding emperor's princes, Xuan alone left no heirs; many privately considered it unjust.

entries.zh: 乃使揚州刺史始安王遙光、臨川王子晉、竟陵王昭胄、太尉陳顯達、尚書令徐孝嗣、右僕射沈文季、尚書沈淵、沈約、王亮奏論鉉，帝答不許，再奏，乃從之。
entries.en: Thereupon Governor of Yang Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang, Prince of Linchuan Zijin, Prince of Jingling Zhaozhou, Grand Commandant Chen Xianda, Director Xu Xiaosi, Right Vice Director Shen Wenji, and Directors Shen Yuan, Shen Yue, and Wang Liang memorialized on Xuan's behalf; the emperor refused; on a second memorial he assented.
entries.literal: Thereupon the governor of Yang, Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang; Prince of Linchuan Zijin; Prince of Jingling Zhaozhou; Grand Commandant Chen Xianda; director of the Secretariat Xu Xiaosi; right vice director Shen Wenji; and directors Shen Yuan, Shen Yue, and Wang Liang memorialized arguing for Xuan; the emperor replied refusing; on a second memorial he assented.

entries.zh: 高帝十九男：昭皇后生武帝、豫章文獻王嶷；
entries.en: Emperor Gao had nineteen sons: Empress Zhao bore Emperor Wu and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang, Ni;
entries.literal: Emperor Gao had nineteen sons: Empress Zhao bore Emperor Wu and Prince Wenxian of Yuzhang Ni;

entries.zh: 謝貴嬪生臨川獻王映、長沙威王晃；
entries.en: Noble Consort Xie bore Prince Xian of Linchuan, Ying, and Prince Wei of Changsha, Huang;
entries.literal: Noble Consort Xie bore Prince Xian of Linchuan Ying and Prince Wei of Changsha Huang;

entries.zh: 羅太妃生武陵昭王曄；
entries.en: Consort Dowager Luo bore Prince Zhao of Wuling, Ye;
entries.literal: Consort Dowager Luo bore Prince Zhao of Wuling Ye;

entries.zh: 任太妃生安成恭王暠；
entries.en: Consort Dowager Ren bore Prince Gong of Ancheng, Gao;
entries.literal: Consort Dowager Ren bore Prince Gong of Ancheng Gao;

entries.zh: 陸修儀生鄱陽王鏘、晉熙王 銶；
entries.en: Lady of Cultivated Rites Lu bore the Prince of Poyang, Qiang, and the Prince of Jinxi, Qiu;
entries.literal: Lady of Cultivated Rites Lu bore Prince of Poyang Qiang and Prince of Jinxi Qiu;

entries.zh: 袁修容生桂陽王鑠；
entries.en: Lady of Cultivated Appearance Yuan bore the Prince of Guiyang, Shuo;
entries.literal: Lady of Cultivated Appearance Yuan bore Prince of Guiyang Shuo;

entries.zh: 何太妃生始興簡王鑒、宜都王鏗；
entries.en: Consort Dowager He bore Prince Jian of Shixing, Jian, and the Prince of Yidu, Keng;
entries.literal: Consort Dowager He bore Prince Jian of Shixing Jian and Prince of Yidu Keng;

entries.zh: 區貴人生衡陽王鈞；
entries.en: Honorable Lady Qu bore the Prince of Hengyang, Jun;
entries.literal: Lady of the District Qu bore Prince of Hengyang Jun;

entries.zh: 張淑妃生江夏王鋒、河東王鉉；
entries.en: Imperial Beauty Zhang bore the Prince of Jiangxia, Feng, and the Prince of Hedong, Xuan;
entries.literal: Imperial Beauty Zhang bore Prince of Jiangxia Feng and Prince of Hedong Xuan;

entries.zh: 李美人生南平王銳；
entries.en: Lady of Beauty Li bore the Prince of Nanping, Rui;
entries.literal: Lady of Beauty Li bore Prince of Nanping Rui;

entries.zh: 第九、第十三、第十四、第 十七皇子早亡。
entries.en: The ninth, thirteenth, fourteenth, and seventeenth princes died in childhood.
entries.literal: The ninth, thirteenth, fourteenth, and seventeenth princes died young.

entries.zh: 衡陽王鈞出繼元王后。
entries.en: The Prince of Hengyang, Jun, was given in adoption to succeed the Prince of Yuan.
entries.literal: Prince of Hengyang Jun was adopted out to succeed the Prince of Yuan.

entries.zh: 新安王子鸞，孝武帝寵子，超宗以選補王國常侍。
entries.en: Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, Emperor Xiaowu's favorite son, took Chaozong as constant attendant in his household.
entries.literal: Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, the Xiaowu emperor's favored son — Chaozong by selection was made constant attendant in the princedom.

entries.zh: 王母殷淑儀卒，超宗作誄奏之，帝大嗟賞。
entries.en: When the prince's mother Lady Yin Shuyi died, Chaozong wrote a dirge and presented it; the emperor was deeply impressed.
entries.literal: When the prince's mother Lady Yin Shuyi died, Chaozong composed a dirge and presented it; the emperor greatly sighed in admiration.

entries.zh: 曰：「超宗殊有鳳毛，恐靈運復出。」
entries.en: He said: "Chaozong truly has phoenix plumage — I fear Lingyun has been reborn."
entries.literal: He said: "Chaozong truly has phoenix down — I fear Lingyun is born again."

entries.zh: 轉新安王撫軍行參軍。
entries.en: He was made staff officer on the Prince of Xin'an's Pacification Army.
entries.literal: He was transferred staff officer on the Pacification Army of the Prince of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 謝超宗，陳郡陽夏人也。
entries.en: Xie Chaozong was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
entries.literal: Xie Chaozong was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.

entries.zh: 祖靈運，宋臨川內史。
entries.en: His grandfather Lingyun had been Song governor of Linchuan.
entries.literal: His grandfather Lingyun was Song grand administrator of Linchuan.

entries.zh: 父鳳，元嘉中坐靈運事，同徙嶺南，早卒。
entries.en: His father Feng, in the Yuanjia era was exiled to Lingnan with Lingyun and died young.
entries.literal: His father Feng, in the Yuanjia era because of Lingyun's affair was exiled to Lingnan together with him and died early.

entries.zh: 超宗元嘉末得還。
entries.en: Chaozong returned home at the end of the Yuanjia reign.
entries.literal: Chaozong was able to return at the end of Yuanjia.

entries.zh: 與慧休道人來往，好學，有文辭，盛得名譽。
entries.en: He kept company with the monk Huixiu, loved learning, wrote well, and won great renown.
entries.literal: He associated with the monk Huixiu, loved learning, had literary talent, and gained great renown.

entries.zh: 解褐奉朝請。
entries.en: He left coarse cloth as a court gentleman attending audience.
entries.literal: He left coarse cloth as court gentleman attending audience.

entries.zh: 遷司徒主簿，丹陽丞。
entries.en: He was made chief clerk of the secretariat and aide of Danyang.
entries.literal: He was moved chief clerk of the secretariat and aide of Danyang.

entries.zh: 建安王休仁引爲司徒記室，正員郎，兼尚書左丞中郎。
entries.en: Prince Xiuren of Jian'an brought him in as Record-Office Officer for the Minister over the Masses, Regular Gentleman, and acting Left Assistant Director Gentleman in the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Prince Jian'an Xiuren took him as secretariat recorder, regular gentleman, and acting left director of the Secretariat among the gentlemen.

entries.zh: 以直言忤僕射劉康，左遷通直常侍。
entries.en: Blunt speech offended Vice Director Liu Kang; he was demoted to regular attendant of unimpeded communication.
entries.literal: Because blunt speech offended Vice Director Liu Kang, he was demoted regular attendant of unimpeded communication.

entries.zh: 太祖爲領軍，數與超宗共屬文，愛其才翰。
entries.en: When the founding emperor was Defender General they often wrote together; he cherished Chaozong's talent.
entries.literal: When the founding emperor was Defender General they often composed texts together and he loved Chaozong's literary gift.

entries.zh: 衞將軍袁粲聞之，謂太祖曰：「超宗開亮迥悟，善可與語。」
entries.en: Defender General Yuan Can heard and told the founding emperor: "Chaozong is open, bright, and penetrating — good to talk with."
entries.literal: Defender General Yuan Can heard of it and told the founding emperor: "Chaozong is open, bright, and far-seeing — pleasant to speak with."

entries.zh: 取爲長史、臨淮太守。
entries.en: He was made chief clerk and governor of Linhuai.
entries.literal: He was taken as chief clerk and grand administrator of Linhuai.

entries.zh: 粲旣誅，太祖以超宗爲義興太守，
entries.en: After Can was executed the founding emperor made Chaozong governor of Yixing.
entries.literal: When Can was executed the founding emperor made Chaozong grand administrator of Yixing,

entries.zh: 昇明二年，坐公事免。
entries.en: In the second year of Shengming, he was dismissed for a public-affairs offense.
entries.literal: In the second year of Shengming, he was dismissed for a public-affairs offense.

entries.zh: 詣東府門自通，其日風寒慘厲，太祖謂四座曰：「此客至，使人不衣自暖矣。」
entries.en: He presented himself at the eastern mansion gate; the wind that day was bitterly cold; the founding emperor told the company: "This guest arrives and one grows warm without dressing."
entries.literal: He presented himself at the eastern mansion gate; that day the wind was bitterly cold; the founding emperor told the seated company: "This guest's arrival makes one warm without putting on clothes."

entries.zh: 超宗旣坐，飲酒數甌，辭氣橫出，太祖對之甚歡。
entries.en: Once seated, after several cups Chaozong's eloquence burst forth; the founding emperor delighted in him.
entries.literal: Chaozong having sat, after several cups his words poured forth; the founding emperor was very pleased with him.

entries.zh: 板爲驃騎諮議。
entries.en: He was appointed by patent adviser to the Rapid Cavalry.
entries.literal: He was appointed by patent adviser to the Rapid Cavalry.

entries.zh: 及卽位，轉黃門郎。
entries.en: When the emperor ascended he was transferred to the yellow gate.
entries.literal: When the emperor took the throne he was transferred gentleman of the yellow gate.

entries.zh: 祥宋世解褐爲巴陵王征西行參軍，歷驃騎中軍二府，太祖太尉東閣祭酒，驃騎主簿。
entries.en: Under Song he was western-campaign staff officer to the Prince of Baling, served both central and rapid-cavalry staffs, sacrifice officer to the founding emperor as Grand Mentor, and rapid-cavalry chief clerk.
entries.literal: In Song times Xiang left coarse cloth as western-campaign staff officer to the Prince of Baling, served both central and rapid-cavalry staffs, eastern-pavilion sacrifice officer to the founding emperor as Grand Mentor, and chief clerk to the Rapid Cavalry.

entries.zh: 建元中，爲冠軍征虜功曹，爲府主武陵王曅所遇。
entries.en: In Jianyuan he was merit officer on the champion's barbarian-pacification staff and was favored by Prince Zhao of Wuling.
entries.literal: In the Jianyuan era he was merit officer on the champion general's barbarian-pacification staff and was favored by his lord Prince Zhao of Wuling Ye.

entries.zh: 除正員外。
entries.en: He was made regular outside gentleman.
entries.literal: He was made regular outside gentleman.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，使掌國史，除竟陵王征北諮議參軍，領記室。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended he managed the national history and was adviser on the Prince of Jingling's northern campaign with charge of the records office.
entries.literal: When the Shizu took the throne he was made to manage the national history, and made adviser to the Prince of Jingling's northern campaign with charge of the records office.

entries.zh: 愈不得志。
entries.en: He grew still more thwarted.
entries.literal: He grew still more thwarted in his aims.

entries.zh: 超宗娶張敬兒女爲子婦，上甚疑之。
entries.en: Chaozong married his son to Zhang Jing'er's daughter; the emperor grew suspicious.
entries.literal: Chaozong took Zhang Jing'er's daughter as his son's wife; the emperor was very suspicious.

entries.zh: 永明元年，敬兒誅，超宗謂丹陽尹李安民曰：「往年殺韓信，今年殺彭越，尹欲何計？」
entries.en: In Yongming year one, when Jing'er was executed, Chaozong told Li Anmin: "Last year Han Xin; this year Peng Yue — what will you do, Governor?"
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, when Jing'er was executed, Chaozong told Danyang governor Li Anmin: "Last year they killed Han Xin; this year Peng Yue — what plan does the governor intend?"

entries.zh: 安民具啓之。
entries.en: Anmin reported everything.
entries.literal: Anmin reported it fully.

entries.zh: 上積懷超宗輕慢，使兼中丞袁彖奏曰：
entries.en: The emperor's long resentment of Chaozong's insolence led acting censor Yuan Can to memorialize:
entries.literal: The emperor's long resentment of Chaozong's insolence made him have acting censor Yuan Can memorialize, saying:

entries.zh: 爲人仗才使酒，多所陵忽。
entries.en: He relied on talent and wine and often slighted others.
entries.literal: By nature he relied on talent and drank wine, and often slighted others.

entries.zh: 在直省常醉，上召見，語及北方事，超宗曰：「虜動來二十年矣，佛出亦無如何！」
entries.en: In the direct offices he was often drunk; summoned to discuss the north he said: "The barbarians have stirred twenty years — even the Buddha could do nothing!"
entries.literal: In the direct-service offices he was often drunk; the emperor summoned him and spoke of northern affairs; Chaozong said: "The barbarians have been stirring twenty years — even if the Buddha appeared, what could be done!"

entries.zh: 以失儀出爲南郡王中軍司馬。
entries.en: For breach of decorum he was sent out as army supervisor to the Prince of Nanjun.
entries.literal: For breach of decorum he was sent out as army supervisor of the Prince of Nanjun.

entries.zh: 超宗怨望，謂人曰：「我今日政應爲司驢。」
entries.en: Chaozong resented it and said: "Today I ought to be Director of Mules."
entries.literal: Chaozong resented it and told others: "Today I ought rightly to be Director of Mules."

entries.zh: 爲省司所奏，以怨望免官，禁錮十年。
entries.en: The provincial office memorialized; for resentful speech he was dismissed and confined ten years.
entries.literal: The provincial office memorialized; for resentful speech he was dismissed and confined ten years.

entries.zh: 司徒褚淵送湘州刺史王僧虔，閣道壞，墜水；
entries.en: Chancellor Chu Yuan saw off Xiang governor Wang Sengqian; the gallery bridge broke and Yuan fell into the water;
entries.literal: Chancellor Chu Yuan saw off Xiang governor Wang Sengqian; the gallery bridge broke and Yuan fell into the water;

entries.zh: 僕射王儉嘗牛驚，跣下車。
entries.en: Vice Director Wang Jian's ox once bolted and he leapt from the carriage barefoot.
entries.literal: Vice Director Wang Jian once when his ox bolted leapt from the carriage barefoot.

entries.zh: 超宗撫掌笑戲曰：「落水三公，墮車僕射。」
entries.en: Chaozong clapped and mocked: "The third duke in the water, the vice director off his carriage."
entries.literal: Chaozong clapped his hands in mockery: "The third duke who fell in the water, the vice director who fell from his carriage."

entries.zh: 前後言誚，稍布朝野。
entries.en: His jests and sneers gradually spread through court and town.
entries.literal: Before and after, jests and sneers gradually spread through court and common.

entries.zh: 祥少好文學，性韻剛疏，輕言肆行，不避高下。
entries.en: Xiang in youth loved literature; he was stiff and unrestrained, speaking and acting freely without regard for rank.
entries.literal: Xiang in youth loved literature; his nature was stiff and loose; he spoke lightly and acted freely, not avoiding high or low.

entries.zh: 司徒褚淵入朝，以腰扇鄣日，祥從側過，曰：「作如此舉止，羞面見人，扇鄣何益？」
entries.en: Chu Yuan entered court fanning the sun; Xiang passed and said: "Gestures like that — ashamed to show your face — what good is the fan?"
entries.literal: Chancellor Chu Yuan entered court shading the sun with a waist fan; Xiang passed by the side and said: "Making such gestures — ashamed to show your face to people — what good is shading?"

entries.zh: 淵曰：「寒士不遜。」
entries.en: Yuan said: "The poor scholar lacks deference."
entries.literal: Yuan said: "The cold scholar is not deferential."

entries.zh: 祥曰：「不能殺袁、劉，安得免寒士？」
entries.en: Xiang said: "You could not kill Yuan Can and Liu — how are you not a cold scholar?"
entries.literal: Xiang said: "Unable to kill Yuan and Liu — how can you escape being a cold scholar?"

entries.zh: 永明初，遷長沙王鎮軍，板諮議參軍，撰《宋書》，譏斥禪代，尚書令王儉密以啓聞，上銜而不問。
entries.en: Early in Yongming he advised the Prince of Changsha's Pacification Army and compiled the Song History, mocking the abdication; Wang Jian secretly reported; the emperor resented but did not pursue it.
entries.literal: At the start of Yongming he was moved to the Prince of Changsha's Pacification Army as adviser and compiled the Song History, mocking the abdication; Director Wang Jian secretly reported; the emperor harbored resentment but did not inquire.

entries.zh: 歷鄱陽王征虜，豫章王大司馬諮議，臨川王驃騎從事中郎。
entries.en: He served the Prince of Poyang, the Prince of Yuzhang's Grand Marshal staff, and the Prince of Linchuan's Rapid Cavalry as attendant gentleman.
entries.literal: He served the Prince of Poyang's barbarian-pacification staff, the Prince of Yuzhang's Grand Marshal staff, and the Prince of Linchuan's Rapid Cavalry attendant gentleman.

entries.zh: 獄鞫祥辭。
entries.en: The tribunal examined Xiang's defense.
entries.literal: The prison examined Xiang's words.

entries.zh: 祥對曰：「被問『少習狡異，長而不悛，頃來飲酒無度，輕議乘輿，歷貶朝望，每肆醜言，無避尊賤』。
entries.en: Xiang replied: "Asked about cunning youth, unrepentant age, drunkenness, slighting the throne, mocking court figures, venting ugliness without regard to rank.'
entries.literal: Xiang replied: "Questioned: 'from youth learned cunning and strangeness, in age unrepentant; of late drinks without limit, lightly discusses the imperial carriage, deprecates court hope, each time vents ugliness without avoiding noble or base.'

entries.zh: 迂答奉旨。
entries.en: He answered evasively as ordered.
entries.literal: Circuitous answer following the charge.

entries.zh: 囚出身入官，二十餘年，沈悴草萊，無明天壤。
entries.en: Your prisoner entered office twenty-odd years from coarse cloth, sunk in hardship without heaven's clarity.
entries.literal: Your prisoner left coarse cloth and entered office twenty-odd years, sunk in hardship in the grass and fields, without heaven-and-earth's clarity.

entries.zh: 皇運初基，便蒙抽擢，祭酒主簿，竝皆先朝相府。
entries.en: When the new dynasty was first established, I was promptly promoted, serving as Libationer and Chief Clerk in the former dynasty's chancellery.
entries.literal: When the imperial destiny was first established, I was promptly selected and promoted; my posts as Libationer and Chief Clerk were both in the former dynasty's chancellery.

entries.zh: 聖明御宇，榮渥彌隆，諮議中郎，一年再澤。
entries.en: Now that Your enlightened Majesty rules the realm, imperial favor has grown still greater: as a consultant and palace gentleman, I received grace twice in a single year.
entries.literal: Now that Your enlightened Majesty rules the realm, imperial favor has grown still greater; as a consultant and palace gentleman, I received grace twice in a single year.

entries.zh: 廣筵華宴，必參末列，朝半問訊，時奉天暉。
entries.en: At grand banquets and splendid feasts, I was always admitted among the last ranks; at the court's semi-monthly audiences, I sometimes beheld the imperial radiance.
entries.literal: At broad banquets and splendid feasts, I always joined the last rank; at the court's semi-monthly audiences, I sometimes received the heavenly radiance.

entries.zh: 囚雖頑愚，豈不識恩？
entries.en: Though I am foolish and obtuse, how could I fail to recognize this favor?
entries.literal: Though your prisoner is stubborn and foolish, how could he not recognize this favor?

entries.zh: 有何怨望，敢生譏議？
entries.en: What resentment could I harbor that I would dare make mocking criticisms?
entries.literal: What resentment could I harbor that I would dare give rise to mocking criticism?

entries.zh: 囚歷府以來，伏事四王：武陵功曹，凡涉二載；
entries.en: Since I began serving on princely staffs, I have attended four princes: two years as merit officer to the Prince of Wuling;
entries.literal: Since your prisoner began serving on princely staffs, he has attended four princes: as merit officer to the Prince of Wuling, for two years in all;

entries.zh: 長沙諮議，故經少時；
entries.en: a short time as consultant to the Prince of Changsha;
entries.literal: a short time as consultant to the Prince of Changsha;

entries.zh: 奉隷大司馬，竝被恩拂，驃騎中郎，親職少日；
entries.en: then under the Grand Marshal, where I received gracious treatment, and as Palace Gentleman in the Cavalry command, where I held a trusted post for only a few days;
entries.literal: then in service under the Grand Marshal, where I received gracious treatment, and as Palace Gentleman in the Cavalry command, where I held a trusted post for only a few days;

entries.zh: 臨川殿下不遺蟲蟻，賜參辭華。
entries.en: The Prince of Linchuan did not disdain one as low as an insect, but allowed me to join his literary circle.
entries.literal: The Prince of Linchuan did not cast aside one as low as an insect, but granted me a place among men of letters.

entries.zh: 司徒殿下文德英明，四海傾屬。
entries.en: The Prince of Jingling, serving as Minister over the Masses, is brilliant in civil virtue, and all within the four seas turn toward him.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jingling, serving as Minister over the Masses, is brilliant in civil virtue, and all within the four seas incline toward him.

entries.zh: 囚不涯卑遠，隨例問訊，時節拜覲，亦沾眄議。
entries.en: Though I knew myself lowly and distant, I followed precedent in paying my respects, attending audiences at the seasons, and sometimes received a glance and a word.
entries.literal: Your prisoner did not measure how lowly and distant he was; following precedent, he paid his respects, attended audiences at the seasons, and sometimes received a glance and a word.

entries.zh: 自餘令王，未被祗拜，旣不經伏節，理無厚薄。
entries.en: As for the other princes, I was never received in audience; since I never served under their standards, there was no question of partiality toward them.
entries.literal: As for the other princes, I was never received in audience; since I never served beneath their standards, there was no question of favoring or slighting them.

entries.zh: 敕旨制書，令有疑則啓。
entries.en: Imperial edicts and statutes command that any doubt be reported.
entries.literal: Imperial edicts and statutes command that whenever there is doubt, it be reported.

entries.zh: 囚以天日懸遠，未敢塵穢。
entries.en: Because the imperial sun hung far above, I did not dare trouble it.
entries.literal: Because the imperial sun hung far above, your prisoner did not dare trouble or defile it.

entries.zh: 私之疑事，衞將軍臣儉，宰輔聖朝，令望當世，囚自斷才短，密以諮儉，儉爲折衷，紙迹猶存。
entries.en: In private matters that troubled me, I turned to Wang Jian, General of the Guard, chief assistant to the sacred court and a man of commanding reputation in this age. I knew my own abilities were slight, so I consulted him privately; he gave a balanced judgment, and the written record still survives.
entries.literal: In private matters that troubled me, I turned to Your servant Wang Jian, General of the Guard, chief assistant to the sacred court and a man of commanding reputation in this age. I knew my own abilities were slight, so I consulted him privately; Jian gave a balanced judgment, and the written record still survives.

entries.zh: 未解此理云何敢爲『歷貶朝望』。
entries.en: Not understanding this — how dare he 'mock court figures'?
entries.literal: Not understanding this principle — how dare he 'deprecate court hope'?

entries.zh: 云囚『輕議乘輿』，爲向誰道？
entries.en: Saying 'slighting the throne' — to whom did he speak?
entries.literal: Saying your prisoner 'lightly discusses the imperial carriage' — to whom did he speak?

entries.zh: 若向人道，則應有主甲，豈有事無髣彿，空見羅謗？
entries.en: If to others there should be an accuser; how can empty slander stand without likeness?
entries.literal: If he spoke to others there should be a chief accuser; how can matters be without likeness, empty slander alone?

entries.zh: 囚性不耐酒，親知所悉，強進一升，便已迷醉。」
entries.en: Your prisoner cannot bear wine — kin know it; one cup and he is drunk."
entries.literal: Your prisoner's nature cannot bear wine — close kin know it; forced to one sheng he is already drunk."

entries.zh: 其餘事事自申。
entries.en: The rest he answered item by item.
entries.literal: The rest he answered item by item.

entries.zh: 乃徙廣州。
entries.en: He was exiled to Guangzhou.
entries.literal: He was then exiled to Guangzhou.

entries.zh: 世祖雖可其奏，以彖言辭依違，大怒，使左丞王逡之奏曰：
entries.en: Emperor Wu approved the memorial but was furious because Can's wording was evasive, and he had Left Assistant Director Wang Qunzhi memorialize:
entries.literal: The Shizu though he approved the memorial, because Can's words were evasive, was greatly angered and had left director Wang Junzhi memorialize:

entries.zh: 詔曰：「超宗釁同大逆，罪不容誅。
entries.en: The edict said: "Chaozong's guilt equals great treason; the crime cannot be pardoned.
entries.literal: The edict said: "Chaozong's guilt equals great treason; crime cannot bear pardon.

entries.zh: 彖匿情欺國，愛朋罔主，事合極法，特原收治，免官如案，禁錮十年。」
entries.en: Can hid facts and deceived the state — the affair fits extreme law; specially pardoned to seizure; removal as memorialized, confinement ten years."
entries.literal: Can hid facts and deceived the state, loving faction and misleading the ruler — the affair fits extreme law; specially pardoned to seizure and treatment; removal as memorialized, confinement ten years."

entries.zh: 超宗下廷尉，一宿髮白皓首。
entries.en: Chaozong was sent to the tribunal; in one night his hair turned white.
entries.literal: Chaozong was sent down to the tribunal; in one night his hair turned white.

entries.zh: 詔徙越州，行至豫章，上敕豫章內史虞悰曰：「謝超宗令於彼賜自盡，勿傷其形骸。」
entries.en: An edict exiled him to Yue Province. When he reached Yuzhang, the emperor ordered Yu Cong, Interior Minister of Yuzhang: "Have Xie Chaozong take his own life there; do not injure his body."
