entries.literal: An edict exiled him to Yue; reaching Zhang commandery the emperor issued an edict Zhang interior governor Yu Cong: "Order Chaozong to take his own life there — do not harm his body."

entries.zh: 上別遣敕祥曰：「卿素無行檢，朝野所悉。
entries.en: The emperor separately issued an edict to Xiang: "You have long lacked conduct — known to all.
entries.literal: The emperor separately issued an edict to Xiang: "You from of old had no conduct — known to court and common.

entries.zh: 輕棄骨肉，侮蔑兄嫂，此是卿家行不足，乃無關他人。
entries.en: You abandoned kin and insulted your sister-in-law — your family's failing, not others' affair.
entries.literal: Lightly abandoning flesh and bone, insulting elder brother's wife — this is your family's insufficient conduct, not others' affair.

entries.zh: 卿才識所知，蓋何足論。
entries.en: The talent you possess — how is it worth discussion?
entries.literal: The talent and insight you know — how is it worth discussion?

entries.zh: 位涉清途，於分非屈。
entries.en: Your rank touched the clear path — not bent in allotment.
entries.literal: Your rank touched the clear path — in allotment not bent.

entries.zh: 何意輕肆口噦，詆目朝士，造席立言，必以貶裁爲口實。
entries.en: Why vent your mouth and sneer at court gentlemen, always deprecating as habit?
entries.literal: Why lightly vent your mouth and sneer at court gentlemen, making seats and standing speech — must depreciation be the mouth's substance?

entries.zh: 冀卿年齒已大，能自感厲，日望悛革。
entries.en: I hoped age would make you reform; I looked for repentance daily.
entries.literal: I hoped your years were already great and you could reform yourself; day by day I looked for repentance.

entries.zh: 如此所聞，轉更增甚，諠議朝廷，不避尊賤，肆口極辭，彰暴物聽。
entries.en: Reports grow worse, clamoring in court, not avoiding rank, speech to the extreme, exposing violence to all who hear.
entries.literal: Such reports as heard grow worse, clamor in court, not avoiding noble or base, venting words to the extreme, exposing violence to all who hear.

entries.zh: 近見卿影《連珠》，寄意悖慢，彌不可長。
entries.en: Recently your Linked Pearls — intent rebellious and slow, unbearable.
entries.literal: Recently seeing your Linked Pearls — intent rebellious and slow, more cannot be borne.

entries.zh: 卿不見謝超宗，其才地二三，故在卿前，事殆是百分不一。
entries.en: Have you not seen Xie Chaozong? His talent stands two or three ranks above yours — yet his case was perhaps one hundredth unlike yours.
entries.literal: Have you not seen Xie Chaozong? His talent and standing are two or threefold yours — he stands before you — the affair is perhaps one percent unlike you.

entries.zh: 我當原卿性命，令卿萬里思諐。
entries.en: I will spare your life and send you far away to reflect on your faults.
entries.literal: I shall spare your life and let you reflect on faults ten thousand li away.

entries.zh: 卿若能改革，當令卿得還。」
entries.en: If you can reform, you may return."
entries.literal: If you can reform, I shall let you return."

entries.zh: 明年，超宗門生王永先又告超宗子才卿死罪二十餘條。
entries.en: The next year his student Wang Yongxian reported his son Caiqing for more than twenty capital crimes.
entries.literal: The next year Chaozong's student Wang Yongxian again reported Chaozong's son Caiqing for more than twenty capital crimes.

entries.zh: 上疑其虛妄，以才卿付廷尉辯，以不實見原。
entries.en: The emperor doubted the charges; Caiqing was tried and cleared.
entries.literal: The emperor doubted the falsehood; Caiqing was given to the tribunal and cleared as untrue.

entries.zh: 永先於獄自盡。
entries.en: Yongxian killed himself in prison.
entries.literal: Yongxian killed himself in prison.

entries.zh: 有以祥《連珠》啓上者，上令御史中丞任遐奏曰：「祥少而狡異，長不悛徙，請謁絕於私館，反脣彰於公庭，輕議乘輿，歷貶朝望，肆醜無避，縱言自若。
entries.en: Someone presented Xiang's Linked Pearls to the emperor; the emperor ordered censor Ren Xia to memorialize: "Xiang from youth was cunning and strange, in age unrepentant; private visits, public back talk; he slighted the throne and mocked court figures without restraint.
entries.literal: Someone presented Xiang's Linked Pearls to the emperor; the emperor ordered reviewing censor Ren Xia to memorialize: "Xiang from youth was cunning and strange, in age unrepentant; visits ended at private lodges, back talk showed in public halls; lightly discussing the imperial carriage, repeatedly deprecating court hope; venting ugliness without avoidance, letting words run as they would.

entries.zh: 厥兄浮櫬，天倫無一日之悲，南金弗獲，嫂姪致其輕絕，孤舟敻反，存沒相捐，遂令暴客掠奪骸柩，行路流歎，有識傷心。
entries.en: His brother's coffin floated — no kin grief; he fought his sister-in-law for goods; living and dead abandoned — robbers plundered the coffin; travelers sighed, the knowing were wounded.
entries.literal: His elder brother floated the coffin — one day of human kinship without grief; southern gold not obtained — sister-in-law and nephew met his light severance; lone boat far returned — living and dead abandoned each other — thus violent guests plundered the coffin; travelers sighed; the knowing were wounded.

entries.zh: 攝祥門生孫狼兒列『祥頃來飲酒無度，言語闌逸，道說朝廷，亦有不遜之語，實不避左右，非可稱紙墨。
entries.en: Student Sun Lang'er listed: 'Xiang drinks without limit, speech reckless, discusses court with insolent words, not fit for record.
entries.literal: Your servant took Xiang's student Sun Lang'er's list: 'Xiang of late drinks without limit, words reckless and excessive, speaks of court — also insolent words, truly not avoiding bystanders, not fit for paper and ink.

entries.zh: 兄整先爲廣州，於職喪亡，去年啓求迎喪，還至大雷，聞祥與整妻孟爭計財物瞋忿，祥仍委前還，後未至鵲頭，其夜遭劫，內人竝爲凶人所淫略』。
entries.en: Brother Zheng died in Guangzhou; Xiang fought Zheng's wife Meng over goods, abandoned the coffin, and later met robbery where household members were violated.'
entries.literal: Elder brother Zheng was first in Guangzhou and died in office; last year he memorialized to bring the coffin; returning to Dalei he heard Xiang and Zheng's wife Meng contending over goods in rage; Xiang then left the coffin and did not come; later he did not reach Que'tou — that night met robbery and inner people were all violated by villains.'

entries.zh: 如所列與風聞符同。
entries.en: As listed it matches reports.
entries.literal: As listed it matches what was heard.

entries.zh: 請免官付廷尉。」
entries.en: Request removal and delivery to the tribunal."
entries.literal: Request removal from office and delivery to the tribunal."

entries.zh: 祥兄整爲廣州，卒官，祥就整妻求還資，事聞朝廷。
entries.en: His brother Zheng died as Guangzhou governor; Xiang demanded Zheng's wife return assets; the matter reached court.
entries.literal: Xiang's elder brother Zheng was in Guangzhou and died in office; Xiang demanded return of assets from Zheng's wife; the matter reached court.

entries.zh: 於朝士多所貶忽。
entries.en: He slighted many court gentlemen.
entries.literal: Toward court gentlemen he was much deprecating and slighting.

entries.zh: 王奐爲僕射，祥與奐子融同載，行至中堂，見路人驅驢，祥曰：「驢！
entries.en: Wang Huan was vice director; Xiang rode with Huan's son Rong; in the middle hall they saw a man driving a donkey. Xiang said: "Donkey!
entries.literal: Wang Huan was vice director; Xiang rode with Huan's son Rong; reaching the middle hall they saw a passerby driving a donkey. Xiang said: "Donkey!

entries.zh: 汝好爲之，如汝人才，皆已令僕。」
entries.en: Keep at it — men of your talent are already all servants."
entries.literal: You do well to do this — men of talent like you are already all made servants."

entries.zh: 著《連珠》十五首以寄其懷。
entries.en: He composed fifteen Linked Pearls to voice his feelings.
entries.literal: He composed fifteen Linked Pearls to lodge his feelings.

entries.zh: 辭曰：
entries.en: The text says:
entries.literal: The text says:

entries.zh: :　　蓋聞鼓鼖懷音，待揚桴以振響；
entries.en: A great drum holds its sound until the drumstick rises and makes it ring;
entries.literal: The great drum holds sound within, awaiting the raised drumstick to make it resound;

entries.zh: 天地涵靈，資昏明以垂位。
entries.en: Heaven and earth harbor numinous power, relying on darkness and light to establish their order.
entries.literal: Heaven and earth contain numinous power, relying on darkness and light to establish their positions.

entries.zh: 是以俊乂之臣，借湯、武而隆；
entries.en: Thus worthy ministers rose to greatness through King Tang and King Wu;
entries.literal: Therefore worthy ministers borrow Tang and Wu to rise;

entries.zh: 英達之君，假伊、周而治。
entries.en: and enlightened rulers governed with the aid of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou.
entries.literal: and enlightened rulers rely on Yi and Zhou to govern.

entries.zh: 謝超宗
entries.en: Xie Chaozong
entries.literal: Xie Chaozong

entries.zh: 宋代太祖輔政，有意欲鑄錢，以禪讓之際，未及施行，
entries.en: During the Song, when the Founding Emperor was regent he intended to cast new coinage, but at the moment of the abdication he had not yet put the plan into effect.
entries.literal: In Song times, when the Founding Emperor was regent, he intended to cast coinage, but at the juncture of the abdication he had not yet carried it out.

entries.zh: 建元四年，奉朝請孔覬上鑄錢均貨議，辭證甚博。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, Court Attendant Kong Gu submitted a memorial entitled "On Casting Coinage and Equalizing Currency," supported by very extensive argument.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan, Court Attendant Kong Gu submitted a memorial on casting coinage and equalizing currency, with argumentation very extensive.

entries.zh: 其略以爲「食貨相通，理勢自然。
entries.en: Its gist was that "food and currency circulate together by natural principle and tendency.
entries.literal: Its gist held that "food and currency interflow—the principle and tendency are natural.

entries.zh: 李悝曰『糴甚貴傷民，甚賤傷農』。
entries.en: Li Kui said, 'When grain is bought too dear it harms the people; when too cheap it harms the farmers.'
entries.literal: Li Kui said: 'When grain is bought at too high a price it harms the people; when too cheap it harms the farmers.'

entries.zh: 民傷則離散，農傷則國貧。
entries.en: When the people suffer they disperse; when farmers suffer the state grows poor.
entries.literal: When the people are harmed they scatter; when farmers are harmed the state grows poor.

entries.zh: 甚賤與甚貴，其傷一也。
entries.en: Extremes of cheapness and dearness inflict the same injury.
entries.literal: Being too cheap and being too expensive do the same harm.

entries.zh: 三吳國之關閫，比歲被水潦而糴不貴，是天下錢少，非穀穰賤，此不可不察也。
entries.en: The Three Wu are the nation's gateway; though flooded in recent years, grain prices have not risen—showing that coin in the realm is scarce, not that harvests are abundant and grain cheap. This cannot be overlooked.
entries.literal: The Three Wu are the nation's gates; in recent years they have suffered floods yet grain prices are not high—this shows coin in the realm is scarce, not that grain is abundantly cheap; this must not go unexamined.

entries.zh: 鑄錢之弊，在輕重屢變。
entries.en: The trouble with coinage lies in the repeated shifting of weight and value.
entries.literal: The defect of coin casting lies in the weight and value repeatedly changing.

entries.zh: 重錢患難用，而難用爲累輕；
entries.en: Heavy coin is hard to use, and difficulty of use drives people toward lighter coin;
entries.literal: Heavy coin worries over difficulty in use, and difficulty in use becomes a burden tending toward lightness;

entries.zh: 輕錢弊盜鑄，而盜鑄爲禍深。
entries.en: light coin invites illicit casting, and illicit casting brings deep harm.
entries.literal: light coin has the defect of illicit casting, and illicit casting brings deep calamity.

entries.zh: 民所盜鑄，嚴法不禁者，由上鑄錢惜銅愛工也。
entries.en: The reason strict law cannot stop popular illicit casting is that the government, when minting coin, spares copper and labor.
entries.literal: What the people illicitly cast strict law cannot stop, because those above who cast coin spare copper and cherish labor.

entries.zh: 惜銅愛工者，謂錢無用之器，以通交易，務欲令輕而數多，使省工而易成，不詳慮其爲患也。
entries.en: To "spare copper and labor" is to treat coin as a mere tool of exchange, striving to make it light and plentiful, easy and cheap to produce, without fully weighing the harm.
entries.literal: "Spare copper and cherish labor" means treating coin as a useless vessel for facilitating exchange, striving to make it light and numerous, saving labor and making it easy to produce, without carefully considering the harm.

entries.zh: 自漢鑄五銖錢，至宋文帝，歷五百餘年，制度世有廢興，而不變五銖錢者，明其輕重可法，得貨之宜。
entries.en: From the Han casting of five-zhu coin down to Emperor Wen of Song, more than five hundred years passed; though institutions rose and fell, the five-zhu standard never changed—proof that its weight could serve as law and suited the needs of trade.
entries.literal: From Han's casting of five-zhu coin to Emperor Wen of Song, spanning more than five hundred years, institutions rose and fell with the ages, yet the five-zhu standard never changed—showing its weight and value could serve as law and suited currency.

entries.zh: 以爲宜開置泉府，方牧貢金，大興鎔鑄。
entries.en: He proposed establishing a coin treasury, requiring regional governors to submit gold, and greatly expanding smelting and minting.
entries.literal: He held that it would be fitting to establish a treasury for coin, have regional governors present gold, and greatly expand smelting and casting.

entries.zh: 錢重五銖，一依漢法。
entries.en: Coin should weigh five zhu, following Han practice in full.
entries.literal: Coin should weigh five zhu, entirely following Han law.

entries.zh: 府庫已實，國用有儲，乃量奉祿，薄賦稅，則家給民足。
entries.en: Once the treasuries are filled and state expenses secured, stipends can be measured out and taxes lightened, and households will be supplied and the people content.
entries.literal: Once treasuries are full and state expenses have reserves, then regulate stipends and reduce taxes, and households will be supplied and the people sufficient.

entries.zh: 頃盜鑄新錢者，皆效作翦鑿，不鑄大錢也。
entries.en: Recently illicit minters of new coin simply imitate clipping and carving; they do not cast large pieces.
entries.literal: Recently those who illicitly cast new coin all imitate clipping and chiseling; they do not cast large coin.

entries.zh: 摩澤淄染，始皆類故；
entries.en: Rubbed, dyed, and soaked, they at first look like old coin;
entries.literal: Polishing, dyeing, and soaking—all at first resemble old coin;

entries.zh: 交易之後，渝變還新。
entries.en: but after passing in trade their altered color shows them as new again.
entries.literal: after circulation they change color and appear new again.

entries.zh: 良民弗皆淄染，不復行矣。
entries.en: If honest people do not all dye them, the coins will no longer circulate.
entries.literal: If good citizens do not all dye them, the practice will no longer circulate.

entries.zh: 所鬻賣者，皆徒失其物。
entries.en: Those who sell them simply lose their goods for nothing.
entries.literal: Those who sell them simply lose their goods in vain.

entries.zh: 盜鑄者，復賤買新錢，淄染更用，反覆生詐，循環起姦，此明主尤所宜禁而不可長也。
entries.en: Illicit casters then buy new coin cheaply, dye it, and use it again; fraud breeds in repetition and wickedness in cycles—what an enlightened ruler above all should forbid and never allow to spread.
entries.literal: The illicit casters buy new coin cheaply again, dye them for reuse; fraud arises in repetition, wickedness rises in cycles—this an enlightened ruler above all should forbid and must not allow to grow.

entries.zh: 若官鑄已布於民，便嚴斷翦鑿，小輕破缺無周郭者，悉不得行，官錢細小者，稱合銖兩，銷以爲大。
entries.en: Once official coin has been issued to the people, clipping and carving must be strictly forbidden; small, light, broken, or rimless pieces must not circulate at all; smaller official coin should be weighed to the zhu and liang standard and melted into larger pieces.
entries.literal: If official coin has already been distributed among the people, then strictly forbid clipping and chiseling; small, light, broken, or rimless pieces must none circulate; small official coin, weighed to fit the zhu and liang standard, should be melted down into large pieces.

entries.zh: 利貧良之民，塞姦巧之路。
entries.en: That would benefit poor honest people and block the road of fraud.
entries.literal: This benefits poor upright citizens and blocks the path of crafty wickedness.

entries.zh: 錢貨旣均，遠近若一，百姓樂業，市道無爭，衣食滋殖矣。」
entries.en: Once coin and goods are equalized, near and far will be as one; the people will take joy in their work, markets will be free of strife, and food and clothing will flourish."
entries.literal: Once coin and goods are equalized, near and far are as one; the people rejoice in their work, markets and ways are without contention, and food and clothing flourish."

entries.zh: 時議者多以錢貨轉少，宜更廣鑄，重其銖兩，以防民姦。
entries.en: At the time many in court held that coin was growing scarce, that casting should be expanded, and the zhu and liang weight increased to guard against popular fraud.
entries.literal: At the time many in deliberation held that coinage was growing scarcer and casting should be expanded, increasing the zhu and liang weight to guard against popular fraud.

entries.zh: 太祖使諸州郡大市銅炭，會晏駕事寢。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor ordered the provinces and commanderies to buy up copper and charcoal on a large scale, but when he suddenly died the plan was dropped.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor ordered the various provinces and commanderies to market copper and charcoal on a large scale, but when the emperor suddenly died the matter was shelved.

entries.zh: 永明八年，悛啓世祖曰：「南廣郡界蒙山下，有城名蒙城，可二頃地，有燒鑪四所，高一丈，廣一丈五尺。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Yongming, Quan memorialized Emperor Wu: "Within Nanguang commandery, below Mount Meng, there is a settlement called Meng City on roughly two qing of land, with four smelting furnaces one zhang high and one zhang five chi wide.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Quan memorialized Emperor Wu: "Within the bounds of Nanguang commandery, below Mount Meng, there is a city called Meng City, about two qing of land, with four smelting furnaces one zhang high and one zhang five chi wide.

entries.zh: 從蒙城渡水南百許步，平地掘土深二尺，得銅。
entries.en: Some hundred paces south across the water from Meng City, copper can be obtained by digging two chi deep in level ground.
entries.literal: One hundred odd paces south across the water from Meng City, digging two chi deep in flat ground, one obtains copper.

entries.zh: 又有古掘銅坑，深二丈，竝居宅處猶存。
entries.en: There is also an old copper pit two zhang deep, and the sites of former dwellings still survive.
entries.literal: There is also an ancient copper-mining pit two zhang deep, and dwelling sites still remain.

entries.zh: 鄧通，南安人，漢文帝賜嚴道縣銅山鑄錢，今蒙山近青衣水南，青衣左側竝是故秦之嚴道地。
entries.en: Deng Tong of Nan'an was granted Yandao county's copper mountains by Emperor Wen of Han to cast coin; Mount Meng now lies near the south bank of the Qingyi River, and the area to Qingyi's left is all the old Qin territory of Yandao.
entries.literal: Deng Tong, a native of Nan'an, was granted by Emperor Wen of Han the copper mountains of Yandao county to cast coin; now Mount Meng is near the south of the Qingyi River, and to the left of Qingyi is all ancient Qin territory of Yandao.

entries.zh: 青衣縣又改名漢嘉。
entries.en: Qingyi county was later renamed Hanjia.
entries.literal: Qingyi county was also renamed Hanjia.

entries.zh: 且蒙山去南安二百里，案此必是通所鑄。
entries.en: Moreover Mount Meng is two hundred li from Nan'an; by this evidence it must be where Deng Tong cast coin.
entries.literal: Moreover Mount Meng is two hundred li from Nan'an; judging by this it must be where Tong cast coin.

entries.zh: 近喚蒙山獠出，云『甚可經略』。
entries.en: I recently summoned the tribal people of Mount Meng, who said, 'It can very well be developed.'
entries.literal: Recently summoning the Liao of Mount Meng, they said, 'It can very well be developed.'

entries.zh: 此議若立，潤利無極。」
entries.en: If this plan is adopted, the profit will be boundless."
entries.literal: If this proposal is adopted, profit without limit."

entries.zh: 幷獻蒙山銅一片，又銅石一片，平州鐵刀一口。
entries.en: He also presented a piece of Mount Meng copper, a piece of copper ore, and an iron knife from Ping province.
entries.literal: He also presented a piece of Mount Meng copper, a piece of copper ore, and an iron knife from Ping province.

entries.zh: 上從之。
entries.en: The emperor approved.
entries.literal: The emperor approved.

entries.zh: 遣使入蜀鑄錢，得千餘萬，功費多，乃止。
entries.en: Envoys were sent into Shu to cast coin and produced more than ten million pieces, but costs were too high and the project was halted.
entries.literal: Envoys were sent into Shu to cast coin; they obtained more than ten million, but costs were high, and the effort was stopped.

entries.zh: 鬱林立，改領右軍將軍，揚州大中正，兼大匠卿。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin came to the throne, Cong was transferred to concurrent Right Army General, Grand Rectifier of Yang Province, and concurrently Chamberlain for the Imperial Workshops.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin acceded he was changed to lead the Right Army as general, became Chief Rectifier of Yang province, and concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Workshops.

entries.zh: 起休安陵，於陵所受局下牛酒，坐免官。
entries.en: He supervised construction of the Xiuan Mausoleum and was dismissed for accepting oxen and wine from subordinates at the tomb works.
entries.literal: He oversaw construction of the Xiuan Mausoleum and, for oxen and wine received from subordinates at the tomb site, was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，以白衣領職。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang he resumed his duties in plain clothes.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he held his post in plain clothes.

entries.zh: 鬱林廢，悰竊歎曰：「王、徐遂縛袴廢天子，天下豈有此理邪？」
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed to himself: "Wang and Xu have actually bound up their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—has the world ever known such a thing?"
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin was deposed, Cong sighed privately, saying: "Wang and Xu have actually trussed up their trousers and deposed the Son of Heaven—can there be such a principle under heaven?"

entries.zh: 廷興元年，復領右軍。
entries.en: In Yanxing 1 (AD 494), he again commanded the Right Army.
entries.literal: In Yanxing 1 (AD 494), he again led the Right Army.

entries.zh: 明帝立，悰稱疾不陪位。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming of Qi came to the throne, Cong pleaded illness and did not attend the enthronement.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, Cong claimed illness and did not take his place at the ceremony.

entries.zh: 帝使尚書令王晏賫廢立事示悰，以悰舊人，引參佐命。
entries.en: The emperor sent Minister of Education Wang Yan to show Cong the record of the deposition and enthronement and, as an old associate, sought to draw him into assisting the new regime.
entries.literal: The emperor sent Minister of Education Wang Yan to present the account of deposition and enthronement to Cong and, because Cong was an old associate, drew him in to assist in establishing the new order.

entries.zh: 悰謂晏曰：「主上聖明，公卿戮力，寧假朽老以匡贊惟新乎？
entries.en: Cong said to Yan: "Our lord is sage and enlightened, and the nobles and ministers are all doing their part—why borrow a worn-out old man to help usher in the new order?
entries.literal: Cong said to Yan: "Our lord is sage and enlightened; the nobles and ministers exert themselves together—how could one borrow a decayed old man to help support renewal?

entries.zh: 不敢聞命。」
entries.en: I dare not accept such a commission."
entries.literal: I dare not accept the command."

entries.zh: 朝議欲糾之，僕射徐孝嗣曰：「此亦古之遺直。」
entries.en: The court wished to impeach him, but Vice Director Xu Xiaosi said: "This is also the sort of blunt integrity the ancients prized."
entries.literal: Court deliberation wished to impeach him, but the Left Deputy Director Xu Xiaosi said: "This too is an upright remnant of antiquity."

entries.zh: 衆議乃止。
entries.en: The assembly then dropped the matter.
entries.literal: The assembly's deliberation then ceased.

entries.zh: 到撝
entries.en: Dao Hui
entries.literal: Dao Hui

entries.zh: 子毅，以勳戚子，少歷清官。
entries.en: His son Yi, as the son of a meritorious kinsman, early held respectable posts.
entries.literal: His son Yi, as son of a meritorious kinsman, in youth passed through pure offices.

entries.zh: 太子舍人，洗馬，隨王友，永嘉太守，大司馬諮議參軍，南康太守，中書郎。
entries.en: He served as Gentleman-attendant of the Heir Apparent, Groom, Friend of the Prince of Sui, Administrator of Yongjia, Adviser on the staff of the Grand Marshal, Administrator of Nankang, and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
entries.literal: Gentleman-attendant of the Heir Apparent, Groom, Friend of the Prince of Sui, Administrator of Yongjia, Adviser of the Grand Marshal, Administrator of Nankang, and Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 建武初，爲撫軍司馬，遷北中郎司馬。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he was Marshal of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters, then Marshal of the North Central Commandant headquarters.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he was Marshal of the Pacify-the-Army headquarters and was transferred to Marshal of the North Central Commandant headquarters.

entries.zh: 虜動，領軍守琅邪城。
entries.en: When the northerners moved, he commanded troops in the defense of Langye.
entries.literal: When the barbarians stirred, he led the army in defending Langye city.

entries.zh: 毅性奢豪，好弓馬，爲高宗所疑忌。
entries.en: Yi was extravagant by nature and loved archery and horsemanship; Emperor Ming came to view him with suspicion.
entries.literal: Yi's nature was extravagant and proud; he loved bow and horse and was suspected and envied by Emperor Ming.

entries.zh: 王晏事敗，幷陷誅之。
entries.en: When Wang Yan's plot failed, Yi was implicated and executed along with him.
entries.literal: When Wang Yan's affair failed, Yi was implicated and executed with him.

entries.zh: 遣軍圍宅，毅時會賔客奏伎，聞變，索刀未得，收人突進，挾持毅入與母別，出便殺之。
entries.en: Troops were sent to surround his house while he was entertaining guests with music. When he heard what was happening he reached for a knife but could not find one; the arresters burst in, took him in to bid his mother farewell, and killed him as soon as they led him out.
entries.literal: Troops were sent to surround the residence; Yi at the time was hosting guests with performers playing; hearing the change, he sought a knife but did not obtain it; arresters burst in, seized Yi and brought him in to part from his mother, and once outside killed him at once.

entries.zh: 上慕儉約，欲鑄壞太官元日上壽銀酒鎗，尚書令王晏等咸稱盛德。
entries.en: The emperor admired frugality and wished to melt down the Grand Steward's silver wine ladle used for New Year's longevity toasts; Wang Yan, Minister Over the Masses, and others all praised this as supreme virtue.
entries.literal: The emperor admired frugality and wished to melt down the Grand Steward's silver wine ladle used for New Year's longevity toasts; Minister Over the Masses Wang Yan and others all praised this as supreme virtue.

entries.zh: 穎冑曰：「朝廷盛禮，莫過三元。
entries.en: Yingzhou said: "Of all the court's great ceremonies none surpasses the Triple Origin festival.
entries.literal: Yingzhou said: "Among the court's great ceremonies none surpasses the Triple Origin festival.

entries.zh: 此一器旣是舊物，不足爲侈。」
entries.en: This one vessel is an heirloom and hardly counts as extravagance."
entries.literal: This single vessel is already an old object and is not enough to count as extravagance."

entries.zh: 帝不悅。
entries.en: The emperor was displeased.
entries.literal: The emperor was displeased.

entries.zh: 後預曲宴，銀器滿席。
entries.en: Later, at an informal banquet, silver vessels covered the tables.
entries.literal: Later, at a private banquet, silver vessels filled the mats.

entries.zh: 穎冑曰：「陛下前欲壞酒鎗，恐宜移在此器也。」
entries.en: Yingzhou said: "Your Majesty once wished to destroy the wine ladle—perhaps the effort should have been directed at these vessels instead."
entries.literal: Yingzhou said: "Your Majesty formerly wished to destroy the wine ladle—I fear the effort should have been directed at these vessels instead."

entries.zh: 帝甚有慚色。
entries.en: The emperor was deeply ashamed.
entries.literal: The emperor was deeply ashamed.

entries.zh: 高宗廢立，穎冑從容不爲同異，乃引穎冑預功。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming carried out his depositions and enthronements, Yingzhou remained outwardly unmoved; the emperor therefore counted him among those who had aided the enterprise.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming deposed and enthroned emperors, Yingzhou was composed and made no show of agreement or dissent; therefore the emperor drew him in to share in the merit.

entries.zh: 建武二年，進爵侯，增邑爲六百戶。
entries.en: In the second year of Jianwu he was raised to marquis and his fief increased to six hundred households.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu his noble rank was advanced to marquis and his fief increased to six hundred households.

entries.zh: 賜穎冑以常所乘白＜牜俞＞牛。
entries.en: The emperor gave Yingzhou the white ox he habitually rode.
entries.literal: The emperor bestowed on Yingzhou the white riding ox he habitually used.

entries.zh: 蕭景先
entries.en: Xiao Jingxian
entries.literal: Xiao Jingxian

entries.zh: 永明初，竟陵王子良請爲征北司徒記室。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Yongming era, the Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, requested him as Recorder on the staff of the Pacification General of the North and Minister of Education.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Yongming era, the Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, requested him as Recorder on the staff of the Minister of Education, Pacification General of the North.

entries.zh: 瓛與張融王思遠書曰：「奉教使恭召，會當停公事，但念生平素抱，有乖恩顧。
entries.en: Huan wrote to Zhang Rong and Wang Siyuan: "I have received your instruction and a respectful summons; I ought to set aside official business, but when I reflect on the disposition I have cherished all my life, it runs counter to this gracious attention.
entries.literal: Huan wrote to Zhang Rong and Wang Siyuan: "I have received instruction and a respectful summons; I ought to suspend official business, but I reflect on the lifelong disposition I have cherished, which runs counter to this gracious regard.

entries.zh: 吾性拙人閒，不習仕進，昔嘗爲行佐，便以不能及公事免黜，此皆眷者所共知也。
entries.en: My nature is awkward among men, and I am unused to pursuing office; I once served as a mobile aide and was dismissed for failing to keep up with official business—this is something all who know me are aware of.
entries.literal: My nature is awkward among men and I am unused to advancing in office; formerly I once served as a mobile aide and was dismissed and removed for inability to attend to official business—this is what those who care for me all know together.

entries.zh: 量己審分，不敢期榮。
entries.en: Having measured my abilities and examined my proper place, I dare not hope for glory.
entries.literal: Having measured myself and examined my allotment, I dare not hope for glory.

entries.zh: 夙嬰貧困，加以疏懶，衣裳容髮，有足駭者。
entries.en: I have long suffered poverty and want, and on top of that I am negligent and indolent; my clothing, appearance, and hair are enough to shock anyone who sees them.
entries.literal: From long ago I have been afflicted with poverty and want, and to this I add negligence and indolence; my clothes, appearance, and hair are enough to startle one.

entries.zh: 中以親老供養，褰裳徒步，脫爾逮今，二代一紀。
entries.en: In the meantime, because my parents were elderly and needed support, I went on foot with my robes hitched up; in this way it has continued until today—two reigns and a full generation.
entries.literal: In the midst of this, because my parents were old and needed support, I lifted my robes and went on foot; thus it has continued until today—two reigns and one full cycle of years.

entries.zh: 先朝使其更自脩正，勉厲於階級之次，見其襤縷，或復賜以衣裳，袁、褚諸公咸加勸勵，終不能自反也。
entries.en: The previous court urged him to reform himself and strive within the ranks of office; seeing his ragged clothes, they would sometimes bestow garments upon him. Gentlemen such as Yuan and Chu all encouraged him, yet in the end he could not change his ways.
entries.literal: The previous court had him further correct himself and exert himself in the ranks of office; seeing his ragged clothes, they would again bestow garments upon him. Gentlemen such as Yuan and Chu all added encouragement, yet in the end he could not turn himself around.

entries.zh: 一不復爲，安可重爲哉？
entries.en: Once one has refused to do a thing, how can one do it again?
entries.literal: Once one does not do a thing again, how can one do it a second time?

entries.zh: 昔人有以冠一免不重加於首，每謂此得進止之儀。
entries.en: In antiquity there was a man who, having once removed his cap, would not place it on his head again; I have always held that in this one grasps the proper ritual of advancing and withdrawing.
entries.literal: In antiquity there was one who, having once removed his cap, would not put it on his head again; I always say that in this one grasps the ritual of advancing and stopping.

entries.zh: 古者以賢制爵，或有秩滿而辭老，以庸制祿，或有身病而求歸者，永瞻前良，在己何若。
entries.en: In antiquity worthies were used to regulate noble ranks; some, when their term was complete, resigned on account of age. Merit was used to regulate stipends; some, when ill in body, sought to return home. I forever look up to the worthies of old—how do I measure against them?
entries.literal: In antiquity worthies were used to regulate ranks of nobility; some, when their term was full, resigned on account of age. Merit was used to regulate emoluments; some, when their bodies were ill, sought to return home. I forever look up to the worthies of old—how do I compare to them?

entries.zh: 又上下年尊，益不願居官次，廢晨昏也。
entries.en: Moreover, my elders are advanced in years; all the more do I not wish to hold a place in the official hierarchy and neglect my morning and evening duties to them.
entries.literal: Moreover, my elders above and below me in years are venerable; all the more do I not wish to occupy a place in the official hierarchy and neglect the morning and evening duties.

entries.zh: 先朝爲此，曲申從許，故得連年不拜榮授，而帶帖薄祿。
entries.en: On this account the previous court bent its will and granted permission, so that for years I did not accept honored appointments but held a nominal post with a slender stipend.
entries.literal: The previous court, on this account, bent its will and granted permission, so that for successive years I did not accept honored appointments but carried a nominal post with a slender stipend.

entries.zh: 旣習此歲久，又齒長疾侵，豈宜攝齋河閒之聽，廁迹東平之僚？
entries.en: Having grown accustomed to this for many years, and with my years advanced and illness encroaching, how could it be fitting to observe fasts and take my place in the Prince of Hejian's audience hall, or stand among the Prince of Dongping's staff?
entries.literal: Having grown accustomed to this for many years, and with my years advanced and illness encroaching, how could it be fitting to fast and take my place in the Prince of Hejian's audience hall or stand among the Prince of Dongping's subordinates?

entries.zh: 本無絕俗之操，亦非能偃蹇爲高，此又諸賢所當深察者也。
entries.en: I have no conduct of transcending the world, nor am I able to be proud and aloof to set myself above others—this too is what you gentlemen ought to examine carefully.
entries.literal: I fundamentally have no conduct of transcending the vulgar, nor am I able to be proud and aloof to make myself lofty—this too is what you gentlemen ought to examine deeply.

entries.zh: 近奉初教，便自希得託迹於客遊之末，而固辭榮級，其故何耶？
entries.en: Recently, having received your first instruction, I hoped to place myself among traveling guests at court, yet I firmly decline honored rank—what is the reason?
entries.literal: Recently, having received the first instruction, I myself hoped to entrust my traces to the end of guest wanderers, yet I firmly decline honored rank—what is the reason?

entries.zh: 以古之王侯大人，或以此延四方之士，甚美者則有輻湊燕路，慕君王之義，驤鑣魏闕，高公子之仁，繼有追申、白而入楚，羨鄒枚而遊梁，吾非敢叨夫曩賢，庶欲從九九之遺蹤。
entries.en: Ancient kings, marquises, and great men sometimes used this means to draw scholars from all directions: the finest would gather like spokes on the road to Yan, drawn by a lord's righteousness and prancing their steeds to the Wei Gate; they would honor a prince's benevolence, and in succession men followed Shen and Bai into Chu and envied Zou and Mei in traveling to Liang. I do not dare claim those former worthies; I merely wish to follow their lingering example.
entries.literal: Because ancient kings, marquises, and great men sometimes used this means to draw scholars from the four quarters: the most admirable would gather like spokes on the road to Yan, admiring a lord-king's righteousness and prancing their steeds to the Wei Gate; they would exalt a lord-son's benevolence, and in succession there were those who followed Shen and Bai into Chu and envied Zou and Mei in wandering to Liang. I do not dare claim those former worthies; I merely wish to follow the lingering traces of the nine-nines.

entries.zh: 旣於聞道集泮不殊，而幸無職司拘礙，可得奉溫凊，展私計，志在此爾。」
entries.en: Since in hearing the Way and gathering at the school there is no difference, yet fortunately I am not constrained by official duties, I may attend to my parents' comfort and carry out my private plans—my aim lies in this alone."
entries.literal: Since in hearing the Way and gathering at the school there is no difference, yet fortunately there is no office or duty to constrain me, I may attend to warmth and coolness and carry out private plans—my aim is in this alone."

entries.zh: 除步兵校尉，並不拜。
entries.en: He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and again declined to accept.
entries.literal: He was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers and again did not accept.

entries.zh: 瓛姿狀纖小，儒學冠於當時，京師士子貴遊莫不下席受業。
entries.en: Huan was slight in stature, but his Confucian learning stood at the head of his age; scholars and noble visitors in the capital all sat below his mat to receive instruction.
entries.literal: Huan's stature was slight and small, but his Confucian learning topped his age; the scholars and noble wanderers of the capital all sat below his mat to receive instruction.

entries.zh: 性謙率通美，不以高名自居。
entries.en: By nature he was modest, straightforward, and thoroughly admirable, and did not rest on his lofty reputation.
entries.literal: By nature he was modest, straightforward, and thoroughly admirable, and did not take his lofty reputation upon himself.

entries.zh: 遊詣故人，唯一門生持胡牀隨後，主人未通，便坐問答。
entries.en: When he visited old acquaintances, only one disciple followed behind carrying a folding stool; before the host had even announced him, he would sit down and converse.
entries.literal: When he went to visit old acquaintances, only one disciple followed behind carrying a folding stool; before the host had announced him, he would sit down and engage in question and answer.

entries.zh: 住在檀橋，瓦屋數閒，上皆穿漏。
entries.en: He lived at Tan Bridge in a few tiled rooms whose roofs were all pierced and leaking.
entries.literal: He lived at Tan Bridge in several tiled rooms, all of whose roofs were pierced and leaking.

entries.zh: 學徒敬慕，不敢指斥，呼爲青溪焉。
entries.en: His disciples revered him and did not dare point it out directly, calling his dwelling instead the Green Stream.
entries.literal: His disciples revered and admired him and did not dare point it out directly, calling it instead the Green Stream.

entries.zh: 竟陵王子良親往脩謁。
entries.en: The Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, went in person to pay him a respectful visit.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, went in person to pay a respectful visit.

entries.zh: 七年，表世祖爲瓛立館，以揚烈橋故主第給之，生徒皆賀。
entries.en: In the seventh year he memorialized Emperor Wu to establish a hall for Huan and had the former lord's mansion at Yanglie Bridge assigned to him; all his disciples congratulated him.
entries.literal: In the seventh year, he memorialized Emperor Wu to establish a hall for Huan and had the former lord's mansion at Yanglie Bridge given to him; the disciples all congratulated him.

entries.zh: 瓛曰：「室美爲人災，此華宇豈吾宅邪？
entries.en: Huan said: "A beautiful dwelling becomes a man's disaster—how could this splendid house be my home?
entries.literal: Huan said: "A beautiful dwelling becomes a man's disaster—how could this splendid house be my residence?

entries.zh: 幸可詔作講堂，猶恐見害也。」
entries.en: It would be fortunate if an edict could make it a lecture hall; I still fear I would come to harm by it."
entries.literal: It would be fortunate if an edict could make it a lecture hall; I still fear I would come to harm."

entries.zh: 未及徙居，遇病，子良遣從瓛學者彭城劉繪、從陽范縝將曅於瓛宅營齋。
entries.en: Before he could move in he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to take Ye to conduct the fast at Huan's house.
entries.literal: Before he could move his residence he fell ill. Ziliang sent Liu Hui of Pengcheng and Fan Zhen of Congyang, who had studied under Huan, to take Ye to lead the fast at Huan's house.

entries.zh: 及卒，門人受學者並弔服臨送。
entries.en: When he died, his disciples and students all wore mourning dress and came to escort him to the grave.
entries.literal: When he died, his disciples and those who had received instruction from him all wore mourning dress and came to escort him to the grave.

entries.zh: 時年五十六。
entries.en: He was fifty-six at the time.
entries.literal: He was fifty-six years old at the time.

entries.zh: 陸澄字彥淵，吳郡吳人也。
entries.en: Lu Cheng, styled Yanyuan, was a native of Wu in Wu Commandery.
entries.literal: Lu Cheng, styled Yanyuan, was a man of Wu in Wu Commandery.

entries.zh: 祖邵，臨海太守。
entries.en: His grandfather Shao had served as Grand Administrator of Linhai.
entries.literal: His grandfather Shao was Grand Administrator of Linhai.

entries.zh: 父瑗，州從事。
entries.en: His father Yuan had served as a provincial aide.
entries.literal: His father Yuan was a provincial aide.

entries.zh: 泰始六年，詔皇太子朝賀服衮冕九章，澄與儀曹郎丘仲起議：「服冕以朝，實著經文。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Taishi, an edict ordered the crown prince to wear the nine-emblem robe and tasseled cap when attending court congratulations. Cheng and Qiu Zhongqi of the Rituals Section argued: "Wearing the tasseled cap at court is in fact prescribed in the canonical texts.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi, an edict ordered that the crown prince wear the nine emblems of the robe and cap with tassels when attending court congratulations. Cheng and Qiu Zhongqi of the Rituals Section discussed: "Wearing the cap with tassels to attend court is in fact set forth in the canonical texts.

entries.zh: 秦除六冕，漢明還備。
entries.en: The Qin abolished the six tasseled caps; Emperor Ming of Han restored them in full.
entries.literal: Qin abolished the six caps with tassels; Han Ming restored them in full.

entries.zh: 魏晉以來，不欲令臣下服衮冕，故位公者加侍官。
entries.en: From Wei and Jin onward, they did not wish subjects to wear the robe and tasseled cap, so men of duke rank were given additional attendant offices instead.
entries.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, they did not wish to let subjects below wear robe and cap with tassels, so those of duke rank were given attendant offices in addition.

entries.zh: 今皇太子禮絕羣后，宜遵聖王盛典，革近代之制。」
entries.en: The crown prince's ritual now stands above all consorts; he ought to follow the great models of the sage kings and reform the institutions of recent times."
entries.literal: Now the crown prince's ritual stands above all the consorts; he ought to follow the great models of the sage kings and reform the institutions of recent times."

entries.zh: 尋轉著作正員郎，兼官如故。
entries.en: Soon he was transferred to Regular Gentleman of the Composition Office, retaining his concurrent posts as before.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Regular Gentleman of the Composition Office, with his concurrent posts as before.

entries.zh: 除安成太守，轉劉韞撫軍長史，加綏遠將軍、襄陽太守，竝不拜。
entries.en: He was appointed Grand Administrator of Ancheng, then transferred to Chief Clerk on Liu Yun's Pacification Army staff, and additionally offered the posts of General Who Pacifies the Distance and Grand Administrator of Xiangyang—all of which he declined.
entries.literal: He was appointed Grand Administrator of Ancheng, transferred to Chief Clerk on the Pacification Army staff of Liu Yun, and additionally made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Grand Administrator of Xiangyang—all of which he declined to accept.

entries.zh: 仍轉劉秉後軍長史、東海太守。
entries.en: He was then transferred to Chief Clerk of the Rear Army under Liu Bing and Grand Administrator of Donghai.
entries.literal: He was then transferred to Chief Clerk of the Rear Army under Liu Bing and Grand Administrator of Donghai.

entries.zh: 遷御史中丞。
entries.en: He was promoted to Palace Assistant Imperial Censor.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Palace Assistant Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 明年，轉給事中，祕書監，遷吏部。
entries.en: The following year he was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to Supervising Attendant and Director of the Palace Library, and promoted to the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 四年，復爲祕書監，領國子博士。
entries.en: In the fourth year he again became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Erudite of the Imperial University.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he again became Director of the Palace Library and concurrently Erudite of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 遷都官尚書。
entries.en: He was promoted to Minister of Justice.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Minister of Justice.

entries.zh: 出爲輔國將軍、鎮北鎮軍二府長史，廷尉，領驍騎將軍。
entries.en: He went out to serve as Chief Clerk of the offices of the General Who Assists the State and the Pacification Generals of the North and the Army, as Minister of Punishments, and concurrently as General of Valiant Cavalry.
entries.literal: He went out as Chief Clerk of the two offices of the General Who Assists the State and the Pacification Generals of the North and the Army, Minister of Punishments, and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 永明元年，轉度支尚書。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 尋領國子博士。
entries.en: Soon he also served concurrently as Erudite of the Imperial University.
entries.literal: Soon he concurrently held Erudite of the Imperial University.

entries.zh: 時國學置鄭王《易》，杜服《春秋》，何氏《公羊》，麋氏《穀梁》，鄭玄《孝經》。
entries.en: At that time the Imperial University taught Zheng and Wang commentaries on the Changes, Du and Fu on the Spring and Autumn, the He clan on the Gongyang, the Mi clan on the Guliang, and Zheng Xuan on the Classic of Filial Piety.
entries.literal: At that time the Imperial University established Zheng and Wang commentaries on the Changes, Du and Fu on the Spring and Autumn, the He clan on the Gongyang, the Mi clan on the Guliang, and Zheng Xuan on the Classic of Filial Piety.

entries.zh: 澄謂尚書令王儉曰：「《孝經》，小學之類，不宜列在帝典。」
entries.en: Cheng said to Wang Jian, Minister of the Masters of Writing: "The Classic of Filial Piety belongs to elementary learning and ought not to be listed among the emperor's canons."
entries.literal: Cheng said to Wang Jian, Minister of the Masters of Writing: "The Classic of Filial Piety belongs to the category of elementary learning and ought not to be listed among the emperor's canons."

entries.zh: 乃與儉書論之曰：
entries.en: Thereupon he wrote to Jian discussing the matter, stating:
entries.literal: Thereupon he wrote to Jian discussing it, saying:

entries.zh: 時東海王摛，亦史學博聞，歷尚書左丞。
entries.en: At the time Wang Chi of Donghai was also renowned for historical learning and had served as Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: At the time Wang Chi of Donghai was also broad in historical learning and had served as Left Assistant in the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 竟陵王子良校試諸學士，唯摛問無不對。
entries.en: The Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, examined the various scholars; only Chi answered every question correctly.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jingling, Xiao Ziliang, examined and tested the various scholars; only Chi answered every question without fail.

entries.zh: 永明中，天忽黃色照地，衆莫能解。
entries.en: During the Yongming era the sky suddenly turned yellow and illuminated the earth; no one could explain it.
entries.literal: During Yongming the sky suddenly turned yellow and illuminated the earth; none could explain it.

entries.zh: 摛云是榮光。
entries.en: Chi said it was auspicious radiance.
entries.literal: Chi said it was glorious radiance.

entries.zh: 世祖大悅，用爲永陽郡。
entries.en: Emperor Wu was greatly pleased and appointed him to Yongyang Commandery.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu was greatly pleased and employed him in Yongyang Commandery.

entries.zh: 劉瓛
entries.en: Liu Huan
entries.literal: Liu Huan

entries.zh: 王晏 蕭諶 蕭坦之 江祏
entries.en: Wang Yan, Xiao Chen, Xiao Tanzhi, and Jiang Shi
entries.literal: Wang Yan, Xiao Chen, Xiao Tanzhi, Jiang Shi

entries.zh: 王晏字士彥，琅邪臨沂人也。
entries.en: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shiyan, was a native of Linyi in Langya Commandery.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, courtesy name Shiyan, was a man of Langya, Linyi.

entries.zh: 祖弘之，通直常侍。
entries.en: His grandfather Wang Hongzhi served as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
entries.literal: His grandfather Hongzhi was a Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.

entries.zh: 父普曜，祕書監。
entries.en: His father Wang Puyao was Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: His father Puyao was Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 晏，宋大明末起家臨賀王國常侍，員外郎，巴陵王征北板參軍，安成王撫軍板刑獄，隨府轉車騎。
entries.en: At the end of the Liu Song Daming era, Yan began his career as a regular attendant in the princedom of Linhe, then served as an outside-section gentleman, as a staff officer on the northern expedition board of the Prince of Baling, and as a penal officer on the pacification army board of the Prince of Ancheng; when that establishment became the Chariots and Cavalry staff, he transferred with it.
entries.literal: Yan, at the end of the Song era of Daming, first entered service as a regular attendant in the princedom of Linhe, then as an outside-section gentleman, as a staff officer on the northern expedition board of the Prince of Baling, as a penal officer on the pacification army board of the Prince of Ancheng, and followed the establishment when it became the Chariots and Cavalry staff.

entries.zh: 永明元年，領步兵校尉，遷侍中祭酒，校尉如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongming, he was made colonel of the Footsoldiers Guard and promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and libationer, retaining his colonelcy.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he headed the Footsoldiers Guard, was promoted to attendant-in-ordinary and libationer, and retained his colonelcy.

entries.zh: 遭母喪，起爲輔國將軍、司徒左長史。
entries.en: After his mother's death, he was recalled from mourning to serve as General Who Assists the State and left chief administrator of the Minister of Education.
entries.literal: When his mother died, he was recalled from mourning to be a general who assists the state and left chief administrator of the Minister of Education.

entries.zh: 晏父普曜藉晏勢宦，多歷通官。
entries.en: Yan's father Wang Puyao, relying on his son's influence, held a succession of high offices.
entries.literal: Yan's father Puyao, relying on Yan's power in office, passed through many high offices.

entries.zh: 晏尋遷左衞將軍，加給事中。
entries.en: Yan was soon made General of the Left Guard with the additional title of supervisor of attendance.
entries.literal: Yan was soon transferred to be General of the Left Guard and was given the additional title of supervisor of attendance.

entries.zh: 未拜，而普曜卒，居喪有稱。
entries.en: Before he could take up the post, Puyao died; Yan's conduct in mourning won praise.
entries.literal: Before he took up the appointment, Puyao died; in mourning he won praise.

entries.zh: 起冠軍將軍、司徒左長史、濟陽太守，未拜，遷衞尉，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was recalled from mourning as Champion General, left chief administrator of the Minister of Education, and Administrator of Jiyang; before accepting those posts he was transferred to Commandant of the Guard, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: He was recalled as Champion General, left chief administrator of the Minister of Education, and Administrator of Jiyang; before he took up the posts he was transferred to be Commandant of the Guard, retaining his generalship.

entries.zh: 四年，轉太子詹事，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: In the fourth year, he was made steward of the heir apparent's household with the additional title of irregular attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to be steward of the heir apparent's household, with the additional title of irregular attendant-in-ordinary.

entries.zh: 六年，轉丹陽尹，常侍如故。
entries.en: In the sixth year, he was made intendant of Danyang, retaining his title as irregular attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, he was transferred to be intendant of Danyang, retaining his irregular attendant title.

entries.zh: 晏位任親重，朝夕進見，言論朝事，自豫章王嶷、尚書令王儉皆降意以接之，而晏每以疏漏被上呵責，連稱疾久之。
entries.en: Yan held an intimate and weighty position, seeing the emperor morning and evening and discussing state affairs. Even the Prince of Yuzhang, Xie, and the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Wang Jian, treated him with deference—yet Yan was often rebuked for careless mistakes and repeatedly pleaded illness for extended periods.
entries.literal: Yan's position and appointment were intimate and weighty; morning and evening he was received in audience and discussed court affairs. From the Prince of Yuzhang, Xie, to the Director of the Department of State Affairs, Wang Jian, all lowered their manner to receive him—but Yan was often rebuked by the emperor for oversights and repeatedly claimed illness for long periods.

entries.zh: 上以晏須祿養，七年，轉爲江州刺史，晏固辭不願出外，見許，留爲吏部尚書，領太子右衞率。
entries.en: The emperor felt Yan needed an income to support himself, so in the seventh year he was appointed governor of Jiang Province. Yan firmly declined to leave the capital; the emperor agreed and kept him on as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently heading the heir apparent's right guard.
entries.literal: Because the emperor thought Yan needed salary to support himself, in the seventh year he was transferred to be governor of Jiang Province; Yan firmly declined and did not wish to go outside the capital. Permission was granted, and he was retained as Director of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrently heading the heir apparent's right guard.

entries.zh: 終以舊恩見寵。
entries.en: He continued to enjoy favor on account of their long-standing bond.
entries.literal: In the end he was favored because of old kindness.

entries.zh: 時尚書令王儉雖貴而疏，晏旣領選，權行臺閣，與儉頗不平。
entries.en: At the time Director Wang Jian, though eminent, stood somewhat apart from the emperor; once Yan took charge of personnel selection, he exercised secretariat power and clashed with Jian.
entries.literal: At the time the Director Wang Jian, though eminent, was distant; once Yan headed selection, he exercised power in the secretariat and was rather at odds with Jian.

entries.zh: 儉卒，禮官議諡，上欲依王導諡爲「文獻」，晏啓上曰：「導乃得此諡，但宋以來，不加素族。」
entries.en: When Jian died, the ritual officers debated his posthumous title. The emperor wished to follow Wang Dao's example and grant the title "Literary and Presented." Yan memorialized the throne: "Only Dao deserved that title—and since the Song, plain families have not received it."
entries.literal: When Jian died, the ritual officers debated his posthumous title; the emperor wished to follow Wang Dao and give the title "Literary and Presented," and Yan memorialized the throne, saying: "Dao alone could receive this title, but since the Song, plain families have not been given it."

entries.zh: 出謂親人曰：「平頭憲事已行矣。」
entries.en: Leaving the audience, he told his intimates, "That business with flat-top Xian is settled."
entries.literal: Going out, he said to his intimates: "The affair of the flat-topped Xian is already done."

entries.zh: 八年，改領右衞將軍，陳疾自解。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was made to head the Right Guard, then pleaded illness and resigned.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, he was changed to head the Right Guard, and pleaded illness to resign.

entries.zh: 世祖崩，遺旨以尚書事付晏及徐孝嗣，令久於其職。
entries.en: When Emperor Wudi died, his testament entrusted Department of State Affairs affairs to Yan and Xu Xiaosi, instructing them to hold their posts for the long term.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, his testamentary instruction entrusted Department of State Affairs affairs to Yan and Xu Xiaosi, ordering them to hold their offices long.

entries.zh: 鬱林卽位，轉左僕射，中正如故。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Yan was made left vice director, retaining his assessor title.
entries.literal: When Yulin took the throne, Yan was transferred to left vice director, retaining his assessor title.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，加侍中。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang he was given the additional title of attendant-in-ordinary.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was given the additional title of attendant-in-ordinary.

entries.zh: 高宗謀廢立，晏便響應推奉。
entries.en: When Xiao Luan plotted to depose the emperor and enthrone himself, Yan immediately supported the move.
entries.literal: When Gaozong plotted deposition and enthronement, Yan at once responded and promoted his elevation.

entries.zh: 延興元年，轉尚書令，加後將軍，侍中、中正如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing he was made Director of the Department of State Affairs with the additional title of rear general, retaining his titles as attendant-in-ordinary and chief assessor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, he was transferred to Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the additional title of rear general; his attendant and assessor titles remained.

entries.zh: 封曲江縣侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang County, with a fief of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 給鼓吹一部，甲仗五十人入殿。
entries.en: He was granted a full set of martial music and fifty armed retainers permitted to enter the palace halls.
entries.literal: He was given one set of martial music and fifty armed men allowed to enter the palace hall.

entries.zh: 高宗與晏宴於東府，語及時事，晏扺掌曰：「公常言晏怯，今定何如？」
entries.en: At a feast in the Eastern Establishment, Gaozong and Yan discussed current affairs. Yan clapped his hands and said, "Your Grace always called me timid—what do you think now?"
entries.literal: Gaozong feasted with Yan at the Eastern Establishment and spoke of current affairs; Yan clapped his hands and said: "Your Grace always said Yan was timid—how about now?"

entries.zh: 建武元年，進號驃騎大將軍，給班劔二十人，侍中、令、中正如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu his title was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief; he was given twenty ceremonial guards with blades and retained his titles as attendant-in-ordinary, director, and chief assessor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, his title was advanced to Rapid Cavalry General-in-Chief; he was given twenty ceremonial guards with blades, and retained his attendant, director, and assessor titles.

entries.zh: 又加兵百人，領太子少傅，進爵爲公，增邑爲二千戶。
entries.en: He was further given a hundred troops, appointed junior mentor of the heir apparent, advanced to duke, and his fief increased to two thousand households.
entries.literal: He was further given a hundred troops, made to head the heir apparent's junior mentor, advanced in rank to duke, and his fief increased to two thousand households.

entries.zh: 以虜動，給兵千人。
entries.en: Because of northern incursions, he was given an additional thousand troops.
entries.literal: Because the barbarians were active, he was given a thousand troops.

entries.zh: 晉熙王燮爲郢州，晏爲安西主簿。
entries.en: When Prince Xie of Jinxing was assigned to Ying Province, Yan served as his western pacification chief clerk.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jinxing, Xie, was made governor of Ying Province, Yan was his western pacification chief clerk.

entries.zh: 世祖爲長史，與晏相遇。
entries.en: The future Emperor Wudi of Qi was chief administrator there, and he and Yan became acquainted.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent was chief administrator, and met Yan.

entries.zh: 府轉鎮西，板晏記室諮議。
entries.en: When the establishment was reorganized as the western pacification staff, Yan was appointed recorder and adviser on its board.
entries.literal: When the establishment became western pacification, Yan was appointed on its board as recorder and adviser.

entries.zh: 沈攸之事難，鎮西職僚皆隨世祖鎮盆城，上時權勢雖重，而衆情猶有疑惑，晏便專心奉事，軍旅書翰皆委焉。
entries.en: During the crisis of Shen Youzhi's rebellion, the western pacification staff followed the Heir Apparent to garrison Pencheng. Though his power was already formidable, many still hesitated; Yan devoted himself wholeheartedly to his service, and all military correspondence was placed in his hands.
entries.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair brought crisis, the western pacification staff all followed the Heir Apparent to garrison Pencheng; though his power was already weighty, popular sentiment still harbored doubts, and Yan then devoted himself to service—military and documentary matters were all entrusted to him.

entries.zh: 性甚便僻，漸見親侍。
entries.en: He was clever and obliging by nature, and gradually won intimate favor.
entries.literal: His nature was very adaptable and accommodating, and he gradually came to be treated with intimate attendance.

entries.zh: 乃留爲上征虜撫軍府板諮議，領記室。
entries.en: He was then kept on as a board adviser on the Heir Apparent's Campaigning-Caitiffs and Pacification Army staff, concurrently heading the Record Office.
entries.literal: He was then retained as a board adviser of the Heir Apparent's northern expedition and pacification army staff, concurrently heading the recorder's office.

entries.zh: 從還都，遷領軍司馬，中軍從事中郎。
entries.en: On their return to the capital, he was promoted to marshal of the Palace Guard and attendant gentleman of the central army.
entries.literal: When they returned to the capital, he was transferred to be marshal of the Palace Guard, and an attendant gentleman of the central army.

entries.zh: 常在上府，參議機密。
entries.en: He was constantly at the Heir Apparent's establishment, participating in confidential deliberations.
entries.literal: He was constantly at the Heir Apparent's establishment, taking part in confidential deliberation.

entries.zh: 建元初，轉太子中庶子。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era, he was transferred to junior mentor of the heir apparent.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyuan era, he was transferred to be a junior mentor of the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 世祖在東宮，專斷朝事，多不聞啓，晏慮及罪，稱疾自疏。
entries.en: While the Heir Apparent held court from the Eastern Palace, he often decided state affairs on his own without reporting them upward. Yan feared he would be held accountable and pleaded illness to keep his distance.
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent in the Eastern Palace made sole decisions on court affairs and often did not report them; Yan feared he would be implicated in guilt and claimed illness to distance himself.

entries.zh: 尋領射聲校尉，不拜。
entries.en: He was soon appointed colonel of the Archers' Guard but declined to take up the post.
entries.literal: Soon he was made to head the Archers' Guard, but he did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，轉長兼侍中，意任如舊。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Yan was transferred to acting Attendant-in-Ordinary, with the same trust and favor as before.
entries.literal: When the Heir Apparent took the throne, Yan was transferred to acting regular attendant-in-ordinary, with trust and appointment as before.

entries.zh: 上欲以高宗代晏領選，手敕問之。
entries.en: The emperor wished to have Xiao Luan replace Yan in charge of selection and sent a handwritten edict to ask Yan's opinion.
entries.literal: The emperor wished to have Gaozong replace Yan in heading selection, and sent a handwritten edict to ask him.

entries.zh: 晏啓曰：「鸞清幹有餘，然不諳百氏，恐不可居此職。」
entries.en: Yan replied, "Luan is certainly capable and upright, but he is not versed in the great families—I fear he cannot hold this post."
entries.literal: Yan memorialized: "Luan has more than enough purity and capacity, yet he is not versed in the hundred clans—I fear he cannot hold this office."

entries.zh: 上乃止。
entries.en: The emperor dropped the plan.
entries.literal: The emperor then stopped.

entries.zh: 明年，遷侍中，領太子詹事，本州中正，又以疾辭。
entries.en: The following year he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Rectifier of his home province, but again resigned citing illness.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary, heading the heir apparent's household and serving as chief assessor of his native province, and again resigned on grounds of illness.

entries.zh: 十年，改授散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，給親信二十人，中正如故。
entries.en: In the tenth year he was reassigned as irregular attendant-in-ordinary and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, given twenty trusted attendants, and retained his assessor title.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was reassigned as irregular attendant-in-ordinary and as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, given twenty trusted attendants, and retained his assessor title.

entries.zh: 十一年，遷右僕射，領太孫右衞率。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he was made right vice director, concurrently heading the crown prince's right guard.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to be right vice director, concurrently heading the heir apparent of the heir apparent's right guard.

entries.zh: 晏爲人篤於親舊，爲世祖所稱。
entries.en: Yan was devoted to kin and old friends, a quality the late emperor had praised.
entries.literal: Yan as a man was devoted to kin and old friends, and was praised by the late emperor.

entries.zh: 至是自謂佐命惟新，言論常非薄世祖故事，衆始怪之。
entries.en: From then on he regarded himself as a founder of the new regime and often spoke slightingly of the late emperor's ways, to the astonishment of many.
entries.literal: From this point he considered himself a founder of the new order; in speech he often disparaged the late emperor's ways, and people first found it strange.

entries.zh: 高宗雖以事際須晏，而心相疑斥，料簡世祖中詔，得與晏手敕三百餘紙，皆是論國家事，以此愈猜薄之。
entries.en: Though Gaozong still needed Yan for the moment, he distrusted him inwardly. Reviewing the late emperor's confidential edicts, he found more than three hundred handwritten orders to Yan on state affairs, which only deepened his suspicion and coldness toward him.
entries.literal: Although Gaozong needed Yan because of the circumstances, in his heart he suspected and rejected him; sorting through the late emperor's confidential edicts, he found more than three hundred sheets of handwritten orders to Yan, all discussing state affairs—by this he grew still more suspicious and cold toward him.

entries.zh: 初卽位，始安王遙光便勸誅晏，帝曰：「晏於我有勳，且未有罪。」
entries.en: Soon after his accession, Prince Yaoguang of Shian urged that Yan be executed. The emperor said, "Yan has served me well, and he has committed no crime."
entries.literal: When he first took the throne, the Prince of Shian, Yaoguang, at once urged executing Yan; the emperor said: "Yan has merit toward me, and as yet has no crime."

entries.zh: 遙光曰：「晏尚不能爲武帝，安能爲陛下。」
entries.en: Yaoguang replied, "If he could not even be loyal to Emperor Wu, how can he be loyal to you?"
entries.literal: Yaoguang said: "If Yan could not even serve Emperor Wu, how can he serve Your Majesty?"

entries.zh: 帝默然變色。
entries.en: The emperor fell silent, his expression darkening.
entries.literal: The emperor fell silent and changed color.

entries.zh: 時帝常遣心腹左右陳世範等出塗巷採聽異言，由是以晏爲事。
entries.en: The emperor often sent trusted attendants such as Chen Shifan into the streets to listen for rumors, and through them Yan became the focus of suspicion.
entries.literal: At the time the emperor often sent trusted personal attendants such as Chen Shifan into the lanes to gather and listen for unusual talk; by this they made Yan their target.

entries.zh: 晏輕淺無防慮，望開府，數呼相工自視，云當大貴。
entries.en: Yan was careless and indiscreet. Hoping for appointment as grand minister, he repeatedly summoned fortune-tellers to read his features and declared that he was destined for great rank.
entries.literal: Yan was frivolous and without precaution; he hoped for an establishment as a grand minister, repeatedly summoned physiognomists to examine himself, and said he would attain great eminence.

entries.zh: 與賔客語，好屏人清間，上聞之，疑晏欲反，遂有誅晏之意。
entries.en: When talking with guests he liked to dismiss attendants for private conversation. When the emperor heard of this, he suspected Yan of plotting rebellion and resolved to kill him.
entries.literal: When speaking with guests he liked to dismiss others for a quiet private talk; when the emperor heard of it, he suspected Yan intended rebellion and thus formed the intention to execute him.

entries.zh: 傖人鮮于文粲與晏子德元往來，密探朝旨，告晏有異志。
entries.en: The northern subject Xianyu Wencan associated with Yan's son Deyuan, secretly probed court intentions, and reported that Yan harbored treasonous designs.
entries.literal: The barbarian-subject Xianyu Wencan had dealings with Yan's son Deyuan, secretly probed court intentions, and reported that Yan harbored a different will.

entries.zh: 世範等又啓上云：「晏謀因四年南郊，與世祖故舊主帥於道中竊發。」
entries.en: Shifan and others further reported, "Yan plans to use the southern suburban sacrifice in the fourth year to launch a surprise attack on the road with the late emperor's old commanders."
entries.literal: Shifan and others further memorialized the throne: "Yan plots, taking advantage of the southern suburban sacrifice in the fourth year, to launch a surprise attack on the road with the late emperor's old commanders."

entries.zh: 會虎犯郊壇，帝愈懼。
entries.en: When a tiger appeared at the suburban altar, the emperor grew still more alarmed.
entries.literal: It happened that a tiger invaded the suburban altar, and the emperor grew still more fearful.

entries.zh: 未郊一日，敕停行。
entries.en: One day before the sacrifice, an edict canceled the ceremony.
entries.literal: One day before the sacrifice, an edict halted the ceremony.

entries.zh: 元會畢，乃召晏於華林省誅之。
entries.en: After the New Year's audience concluded, he summoned Yan to the Hualin Pavilion and had him executed.
entries.literal: When the New Year's audience was finished, he summoned Yan to the Hualin Pavilion and executed him.

entries.zh: 下詔曰：「晏閭閻凡伍，少無持操，階緣人乏，班齒官途。
entries.en: An edict was issued: "Yan came from common stock, showed no firm character in youth, and climbed the official ladder by exploiting others' weaknesses.
entries.literal: An edict was issued: "Yan was of common lanes and ordinary ranks, in youth without settled conduct; he climbed by others' want and took his place on the official ladder.

entries.zh: 世祖在蕃，搜揚擢用，弃略疵瑕，遂升要重。
entries.en: While still a prince, the late emperor sought him out and promoted him, overlooking his faults, until he rose to the highest offices.
entries.literal: When the late emperor was in his princedom, he sought and promoted him, overlooking flaws and blemishes, and thus raised him to crucial weight.

entries.zh: 而輕跳險銳，在貴彌著，猜忌反覆，觸情多端。
entries.en: Yet he was frivolous, rash, and treacherous; the higher he rose, the worse these traits became—suspicious, changeable, and driven by whim.
entries.literal: Yet he was frivolous, rash, dangerous, and sharp; the higher his rank, the more evident it became—suspicious, changeable, and touching feelings in many ways.

entries.zh: 故以兩宮所弗容，十手所共指。
entries.en: For this reason neither palace could tolerate him, and all pointed him out as a danger.
entries.literal: Therefore both palaces could not tolerate him, and ten hands pointed at him together.

entries.zh: 旣內愧于心，外懼憲牘，掩迹陳痾，多歷年載。
entries.en: Feeling guilty within and fearing prosecution without, he hid himself behind repeated claims of illness for many years.
entries.literal: Having inward shame in his heart and outward fear of the law's documents, he concealed his tracks and claimed illness for many years.

entries.zh: 頻授蕃任，輙辭請不行，事似謙虛，情實詭伏。
entries.en: Repeatedly offered provincial posts, he always declined to leave the capital—an appearance of modesty that masked deceit.
entries.literal: Repeatedly given provincial appointments, he always declined and would not go—outwardly seeming modest, inwardly truly deceitful and hidden.

entries.zh: 隆昌以來，運集艱難，匡贊之功，頗有心力。
entries.en: Since the Longchang era, when the dynasty faced grave trials, he had contributed real effort to restoring order.
entries.literal: Since Longchang, when fortune gathered in hardship, his merit in supporting and assisting showed considerable effort of heart.

entries.zh: 迺爵冠通侯，位登元輔，綢繆恩寄，朝莫均焉。
entries.en: He was then ennobled as a full marquis, raised to chief minister, and showered with favor morning and evening alike.
entries.literal: Then his noble rank crowned full marquisates, his office reached chief minister, and intimate favor bound him morning and evening alike.

entries.zh: 谿壑可盈，無厭將及。
entries.en: Yet ravines may be filled, but his greed knew no limit.
entries.literal: Ravines and gullies can be filled—his lack of satiety was about to reach its limit.

entries.zh: 視天畫地，遂懷異圖。
entries.en: He looked to heaven and plotted on earth, harboring treasonous designs.
entries.literal: Looking to heaven and tracing on earth, he then harbored a different design.

entries.zh: 廣求卜相，取信巫覡。
entries.en: He sought out diviners and fortune-tellers and put his faith in shamans.
entries.literal: He widely sought divination and physiognomy and put faith in shamans.

entries.zh: 論薦黨附，徧滿臺府。
entries.en: He packed the secretariat with his own faction through recommendations and patronage.
entries.literal: He discussed recommendations and formed factions until they filled the secretariat.

entries.zh: 令大息德元淵藪亡命，同惡相濟，劔客成羣。
entries.en: His eldest son Deyuan harbored fugitives and outlaws; villains aided one another until swordsmen gathered in gangs.
entries.literal: He had his eldest son Deyuan harbor fugitives in deep lairs; evildoers aided one another and swordsmen formed gangs.

entries.zh: 弟詡凶愚，遠相脣齒，信驛往來，密通要契。
entries.en: His younger brother Xu was brutal and foolish; though far apart, they acted as mutual allies, exchanging couriers and secret agreements.
entries.literal: His younger brother Xu was fierce and foolish; from afar they were lip and teeth to each other, with couriers going back and forth and secret communications of crucial pacts.

entries.zh: 去歲之初，奉朝請鮮于文粲備告姦謀。
entries.en: Early last year the court gentleman Xianyu Wencan reported the full details of the conspiracy.
entries.literal: At the beginning of last year, the court gentleman Xianyu Wencan fully reported the treacherous plot.

entries.zh: 朕以信必由中，義無與貳，推誠委任，覬能悛改。
entries.en: Believing that trust must come from the heart and that loyalty admits no division, We extended Our trust to him, hoping he would reform.
entries.literal: We, believing trust must come from within and that in righteousness there is no divided loyalty, extended sincerity and entrusted him, hoping he could reform.

entries.zh: 而長惡易流，構扇彌大，與北中郎司馬蕭毅、臺隊主劉明達等剋期竊發。
entries.en: Instead he clung to evil and spread unrest ever wider, setting a date for a surprise rising with the northern central army's staff officer Xiao Yi, the palace guard commander Liu Mingda, and others.
entries.literal: Yet he long cherished evil and easily spread it; his agitation grew ever greater, and with the northern central army's staff officer Xiao Yi, the palace guard commander Liu Mingda, and others he set a date for a surprise rising.

entries.zh: 以河東王鉉識用微弱，可爲其主，得志之日，當守以虛器。
entries.en: They intended to make Prince Xuan of Hedong, whose abilities were slight, their puppet ruler, keeping him as a figurehead once they seized power.
entries.literal: Taking the Prince of Hedong, Xuan, whose knowledge and capacity were weak, as one who could serve as their lord—on the day they succeeded, he would be kept as an empty vessel.

entries.zh: 明達諸辭列，炳然具存。
entries.en: Mingda's confessions and lists of accomplices remain fully on record.
entries.literal: Mingda's various statements and lists are clear and fully preserved.

entries.zh: 昔漢后以反脣致討，魏臣以虯鬚爲戮，況無君之心旣彰，陵上之迹斯著，此而可容，誰寘刑辟。
entries.en: In former times the Han empress was punished for insolent speech and a Wei minister was executed for his arrogance—how much more when disloyalty is plain and the crime of lèse-majesté is evident? If this can be tolerated, who would ever face the law?
entries.literal: Formerly the Han empress was punished for turning her lip against authority, and a Wei minister was executed for his curling beard—how much more when a heart without a ruler is already manifest and traces of climbing above one's lord are thus clear: if this can be tolerated, who would be placed within the penal code?

entries.zh: 竝可收付廷尉，肅明國典。」
entries.en: Let all of them be handed over to the Minister of Justice so that the law may be enforced."
entries.literal: All may be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice to clarify the state's statutes."

entries.zh: 晏未敗數日，於北山廟答賽，夜還，晏旣醉，部伍人亦飲酒，羽儀錯亂，前後十餘里中，不復相禁制，識者云「此勢不復久也」。
entries.en: Several days before his downfall, Yan offered thanks at the Beishan temple. Returning at night drunk, with his escort also drinking, his ceremonial guard fell into disorder for more than ten li in every direction. Observers said, "Such power cannot last."
entries.literal: Several days before Yan's fall, he made a thanksgiving offering at the Beishan temple; returning at night, Yan was already drunk, and his escort men also drank wine—the ceremonial guard fell into disorder, and for more than ten li before and behind, restraint was no longer kept. Observers said, "This power will not last long."

entries.zh: 晏子德元，有意尚。
entries.en: Yan's son Deyuan had ability and refinement.
entries.literal: Yan's son Deyuan had aspiration and refinement.

entries.zh: 至車騎長史。
entries.en: He rose to chief administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry staff.
entries.literal: He reached the post of chief administrator of the Chariots and Cavalry staff.

entries.zh: 德元初名湛，世祖謂晏曰：「劉湛、江湛，竝不善終，此非佳名也。」
entries.en: Deyuan's original name was Zhan. The late emperor told Yan, "Liu Zhan and Jiang Zhan both came to bad ends—this is not an auspicious name."
entries.literal: Deyuan's original name was Zhan; the late emperor said to Yan: "Liu Zhan and Jiang Zhan both did not end well—this is not a fine name."

entries.zh: 晏乃改之。
entries.en: Yan then changed his son's name.
entries.literal: Yan then changed it.

entries.zh: 至是與弟晉安王友德和俱被誅。
entries.en: At this time he and his younger brother Dehe, a friend of the Prince of Jin'an, were both executed.
entries.literal: At this time he and his younger brother, the Prince of Jin'an's friend Dehe, were both executed.

entries.zh: 晏弟詡，永明中爲少府卿。
entries.en: Yan's younger brother Xu served as Minister of the Privy Purse during the Yongming era.
entries.literal: Yan's younger brother Xu, in the Yongming era, was Minister of the Privy Purse.

entries.zh: 六年，敕位未登黃門郎，不得畜女妓。
entries.en: In the sixth year an edict declared that officials below the rank of Yellow Gate Gentleman might not keep female entertainers.
entries.literal: In the sixth year, an edict ordered that those whose rank had not reached Yellow Gate Gentleman might not keep female entertainers.

entries.zh: 詡與射聲校尉陰玄智坐畜妓免官，禁錮十年。
entries.en: Xu and Colonel Yin Xuanzhi of the Archers' Guard were dismissed for keeping entertainers and confined for ten years.
entries.literal: Xu and the Archers' Guard colonel Yin Xuanzhi were dismissed from office for keeping entertainers and confined for ten years.

entries.zh: 敕特原詡禁錮。
entries.en: An edict specially remitted Xu's confinement.
entries.literal: An edict specially remitted Xu's confinement.

entries.zh: 後出爲輔國將軍、始興內史。
entries.en: He was later appointed General Who Assists the State and interior minister of Shixing.
entries.literal: Later he went out as General Who Assists the State and interior minister of Shixing.

entries.zh: 廣州刺史劉纘爲奴所殺，詡率郡兵討之。
entries.en: When Administrator Liu Zuan of Guang Province was killed by a slave, Xu led commandery troops to punish the killers.
entries.literal: The Administrator of Guang Province, Liu Zuan, was killed by a slave; Xu led commandery troops to punish them.

entries.zh: 延興元年，授詡持節廣州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing, Xu was appointed Administrator of Guang Province with credentials bearing the imperial staff.
