entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, Xu was given the staff of authority as Administrator of Guang Province.

entries.zh: 詡亦篤舊。
entries.en: Xu, too, was devoted to old friends and kin.
entries.literal: Xu, too, was devoted to old ties.

entries.zh: 晏誅，上又遣南中郎司馬蕭季敞襲詡殺之。
entries.en: After Yan's execution, the emperor sent the southern central army's staff officer Xiao Jichang to strike down and kill Xu.
entries.literal: When Yan was executed, the emperor also sent the southern central army's staff officer Xiao Jichang to strike Xu and kill him.

entries.zh: 海陵立，轉中領軍，進爵爲公，二千戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Hailing was enthroned, Chen was made central palace guard general, advanced to duke, with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: When Hailing was enthroned, Chen was transferred to central palace guard general, advanced in rank to duke, two thousand households.

entries.zh: 甲仗五十人。
entries.en: He was given fifty armed retainers.
entries.literal: Fifty armed men.

entries.zh: 入直殿內，月十日還府。
entries.en: He kept watch within the palace halls, returning to his residence on the tenth of each month.
entries.literal: He entered duty within the palace halls; every month on the tenth day he returned to his establishment.

entries.zh: 建武元年，轉領軍將軍，左將軍，南徐州刺史，給扶，進爵衡陽郡公，食邑三千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu he was made palace guard general and left general, appointed governor of southern Xu Province with a support staff, and advanced to Duke of Hengyang with a fief of three thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was transferred to palace guard general, left general, governor of southern Xu Province, given a staff for support, and advanced to Duke of Hengyang Commandery with a fief of three thousand households.

entries.zh: 高宗初許事克用諶爲揚州，及有此授，諶恚曰：「見炊飯熟，推以與人。」
entries.en: Xiao Luan had initially promised Chen the governorship of Yang Province once the coup succeeded; when this lesser appointment came instead, Chen said angrily, "You see the rice cooked and hand the pot to someone else."
entries.literal: Gaozong had at first promised that when the affair succeeded Chen would be used for Yang Province; when this appointment came instead, Chen said in anger: "Seeing the cooked rice ready, you push the pot to someone else."

entries.zh: 王晏聞之曰：「誰復爲蕭諶作甌箸者。」
entries.en: Wang Yan heard of it and said, "Who will set the table for Xiao Chen now?"
entries.literal: Wang Yan heard of it and said: "Who will make bowls and chopsticks for Xiao Chen again?"

entries.zh: 諶恃勳重，干豫朝政，諸有選用，輙命議尚書使爲申論。
entries.en: Relying on his meritorious service, Chen meddled in court affairs; whenever there were appointments, he ordered the deliberating director of the Department of State Affairs to plead his case.
entries.literal: Chen relied on the weight of his merit and interfered in court government; whenever there were selections and appointments, he always ordered the deliberating director of the Department of State Affairs to argue the case for him.

entries.zh: 上新卽位，遣左右要人於外聽察，具知諶言，深相疑阻。
entries.en: When the new emperor took the throne, he sent trusted attendants to listen in the capital, learned all of Chen's remarks, and grew deeply suspicious of him.
entries.literal: When the new emperor took the throne, he sent trusted personal attendants outside to listen and observe, fully learned Chen's words, and deeply suspected and blocked him.

entries.zh: 二年六月，上幸華林園，宴諶及尚書令王晏等數人盡歡。
entries.en: In the sixth month of the second year, the emperor visited the Hualin Garden and feasted with Chen, Director Wang Yan, and several others until all were merry.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the second year, the emperor visited the Hualin Garden and feasted with Chen, the Director Wang Yan, and several others to full merriment.

entries.zh: 坐罷，留諶晚出，至華林閤，仗身執還入省，上遣左右莫智明數諶曰：「隆昌之際，非卿無有今日。
entries.en: When the feast ended, the emperor kept Chen behind. At the Hualin pavilion, armed attendants seized him and brought him back into the secretariat. The emperor sent his attendant Mo Zhiming to tell Chen, "In the Longchang era, without you there would be no today for me.
entries.literal: When the seating ended, he kept Chen to leave late; reaching the Hualin pavilion, armed attendants seized him and brought him back into the secretariat. The emperor sent his attendant Mo Zhiming to enumerate to Chen: "In the Longchang era, without you there would be no today.

entries.zh: 今一門二州，兄弟三封，朝廷相報，政可極此。
entries.en: Now your household holds two provinces and three brothers are enfeoffed—the court's repayment can go no further than this.
entries.literal: Now one household holds two provinces, three brothers are enfeoffed—the court's repayment can rightly reach only this far.

entries.zh: 卿恒懷怨望，乃云炊飯已熟，合甑與人邪？
entries.en: Yet you constantly harbor resentment, even saying the rice is cooked and asking whether the pot should be handed to others?
entries.literal: You constantly harbor resentment, and even say the cooked rice is ready—should the pot be given to others?

entries.zh: 今賜卿死。」
entries.en: Now We grant you death."
entries.literal: Now We grant you death."

entries.zh: 諶謂智明曰：「天去人亦復不遠，我與至尊殺高、武諸王，是君傳語來去。
entries.en: Chen told Zhiming, "Heaven is not far from man. I and the emperor killed the princes of Gao and Wu—you were the one who carried messages between us.
entries.literal: Chen said to Zhiming: "Heaven and man are not far apart; I and the Supreme One killed the princes of Gao and Wu—it was you who passed messages back and forth.

entries.zh: 我今死，還取卿。」
entries.en: I die today—you will be next."
entries.literal: I die today—you will be taken next."

entries.zh: 於省殺之，至秋而智明死，見諶爲祟。
entries.en: He was executed in the secretariat. By autumn Zhiming died, claiming that Chen's ghost was haunting him.
entries.literal: He was killed in the secretariat; by autumn Zhiming died, seeing Chen as a haunting spirit.

entries.zh: 詔曰：「蕭諶擢自凡庸，識用輕險，因藉倖會，早預驅馳。
entries.en: An edict said, "Xiao Chen rose from common stock, his talents frivolous and dangerous; by fortunate chance he early joined the emperor's service.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Xiao Chen was raised from the commonplace, his knowledge and conduct frivolous and dangerous; relying on fortunate chance, he early joined the driven ranks.

entries.zh: 永明之季，曲頒恩紀。
entries.en: At the end of Yongming he was showered with special favor.
entries.literal: At the end of Yongming, favor was bent and bestowed upon him.

entries.zh: 鬱林昏悖，頗立誠效。
entries.en: Though Emperor Yulin was benighted and perverse, Chen rendered loyal service.
entries.literal: Yulin was benighted and perverse, yet Chen showed considerable loyal effect.

entries.zh: 寵靈優渥，期遇兼隆，內總戎柄，外暢蕃威，兄弟榮貴，震灼朝野。
entries.en: He was showered with favor, held military power within and provincial authority without; his brothers were ennobled, and their glory dazzled court and countryside.
entries.literal: Favor and blessing were rich and deep, his appointed meetings doubly exalted; within he held the military handle, without he extended princely power; his brothers were honored and eminent, dazzling court and countryside.

entries.zh: 曾不感佩殊荷，少答萬一。
entries.en: Yet he never felt gratitude and repaid scarcely a fraction of what he owed.
entries.literal: He never felt moved by special grace or repaid even one part in ten thousand.

entries.zh: 自以勳高伊、霍，事均難賞，才冠當時，恥居物後。
entries.en: He deemed his merit greater than Yi Yin and Huo Guang's, his deeds beyond reward, his talent unmatched in the age—and was ashamed to stand behind others.
entries.literal: He considered his merit higher than Yi Yin and Huo Guang, his deeds equal to what is hard to reward, his talent foremost in the age, and was ashamed to stand behind others.

entries.zh: 矯制王權，與奪由己。
entries.en: He usurped royal authority, making appointments at his own will.
entries.literal: He falsified the royal system and made giving and taking depend on himself.

entries.zh: 空懷疑懼，坐構嫌猜。
entries.en: Harborng groundless suspicion and fear, he bred distrust.
entries.literal: Emptily harboring suspicion and fear, he sat and built up dislike and mistrust.

entries.zh: 覘候宮掖，希覬非望。
entries.en: He spied on the inner palace and coveted what was not his due.
entries.literal: He spied on the palace women's quarters and hoped for what was not his due.

entries.zh: 蔽上罔下之心，誣君不臣之迹，固以彰暴民聽，喧聒遐邇。
entries.en: His heart screened the ruler and deceived those below; his disloyalty was plain to all, and rumor of it spread far and wide.
entries.literal: A heart that screened the ruler and deceived those below, traces of slandering the lord and disloyalty to subjecthood—these were already manifest to the violent populace's hearing and clamorous near and far.

entries.zh: 遂潛散金帛，招集不逞，交結禁衞，互爲脣齒，密契戚邸，將肆姦逆。
entries.en: He secretly scattered gold and silk, gathered malcontents, won over the palace guard, made secret pacts with imperial kin, and was about to launch treason.
entries.literal: Then he secretly scattered gold and silk, gathered the unbridled, joined with the palace guard, became lip and teeth to one another, made secret pacts with imperial kin establishments, and was about to unleash treachery and rebellion.

entries.zh: 朕以其任寄旣重，爵列河山，每加彌縫，弘以大信，庶能懷音，翻然悛改。
entries.en: Because his commission was weighty and his rank eminent, We repeatedly smoothed matters over and extended great trust, hoping he would reform.
entries.literal: We, because his commission was already weighty and his noble rank listed among the hills and rivers, repeatedly added smoothing patches and extended great trust, hoping he could embrace good faith and suddenly reform.

entries.zh: 而豺狼其性，凶謀滋甚。
entries.en: Yet his wolfish nature only grew worse, and his treacherous plots intensified.
entries.literal: Yet his nature was that of wolf and jackal, and his vicious plots grew ever worse.

entries.zh: 夫無將必戮，陽秋明義，況釁積禍盈，若斯之大。
entries.en: When rebellion is afoot, execution is inevitable—the Spring and Autumn makes the principle clear; how much more when guilt had accumulated to such a degree.
entries.literal: When there is no general, execution is certain—the Spring and Autumn makes the principle clear; how much more when offenses accumulated and calamity overflowed to such a degree.

entries.zh: 可收付廷尉，速正刑書。
entries.en: Let him be handed over to the Minister of Justice so that sentence may be swiftly pronounced.
entries.literal: He may be taken and delivered to the Minister of Justice to swiftly rectify the penal documents.

entries.zh: 罪止元惡，餘無所問。」
entries.en: Punishment shall fall only on the chief villain; the rest shall not be questioned."
entries.literal: Guilt stops at the chief villain; the rest are not to be questioned."

entries.zh: 史臣曰：士死知己，蓋有生所共情，雖愚智之品有二，而逢迎之運唯一。
entries.en: The Historian says: For a gentleman to die for one who knows him is a feeling common to all who live; though wit and folly divide men into two kinds, the fortune of winning favor is singular.
entries.literal: The Historian says: For a gentleman to die for one who knows him is an emotion shared by all who live; though in wit and folly there are two grades, the fortune of winning favor is one alone.

entries.zh: 夫懷可知之才，受知人之眄，無慚外物，此固天理，其猶藏在中心，銜恩念報。
entries.en: When one possesses talent that can be recognized and receives the favor of one who knows men, unashamed before the world—this is the way of heaven itself, as though grace were stored in the heart and repayment always in mind.
entries.literal: When one harbors talent that can be known and receives the glance of one who knows men, without shame before outward things—this is indeed the way of heaven; it is as though stored within the heart, cherishing grace and thinking of repayment.

entries.zh: 況乎義早蕃僚，道同遇合，踰越勝己，顧邁先流，弃子如遺，曾微舊德，使狗之喻，人致前譏，慚包疚心，我無其事。
entries.en: How much more when men were joined early as feudal staff, united in purpose through mutual encounter, surpassing those above them and looking back beyond those who came before, casting off their sons as though they were nothing and scarcely remembering old kindness—the simile of the dog invites reproach from others; ashamed and guilty in heart, I for my part have no such deed.
entries.literal: How much the more when they were bound early as feudal staff, united in the Way through mutual encounter, surpassing those better than themselves, looking back and exceeding those who came before, casting off sons as though forgotten, scarcely heeding old grace—the simile of the dog makes others bring forward reproof; burdened with shame and guilt in heart, I for my part have no such deed.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 陸機所以賦豪士也。
entries.en: This is why Lu Ji wrote his rhapsody on the proud knight.
entries.literal: This is why Lu Ji composed his rhapsody on the proud knight.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷四十二‧列傳第二十三
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 42, Biographies 23

entries.zh: 七年，徙爲侍中，領驍騎將軍，尋轉都官尚書，領驍騎將軍。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Yongming he was made Palace Attendant and General of Valiant Cavalry; soon he was transferred to Minister of Justice while retaining the post of General of Valiant Cavalry.
entries.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Palace Attendant and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry; soon he was moved to Minister of Justice while still holding General of Valiant Cavalry.

entries.zh: 王晏啓世祖曰：「江斆今重登禮閣，兼掌六軍，慈渥所覃，寔有優忝。
entries.en: Wang Yan reported to Emperor Wu, "Jiang Xiao now returns to the Ritual Pavilion and concurrently commands the Six Armies; the gracious favor shown him is truly more than fitting.
entries.literal: Wang Yan reported to Emperor Wu: "Jiang Xiao now returns to the Ritual Pavilion and concurrently commands the Six Armies; the gracious favor lavished on him is truly more than fitting.

entries.zh: 但語其事任，殆同閑輩。
entries.en: Yet in terms of his duties and responsibilities, they are nearly those of an idle functionary.
entries.literal: Yet speaking of his duties and responsibilities, they are nearly those of an idle functionary.

entries.zh: 天旨旣欲升其名位，愚謂以侍中領驍騎，望實清顯，有殊納言。」
entries.en: Since Your Majesty already wishes to raise his rank and position, I humbly suggest that Palace Attendant with Valiant Cavalry is in station clear and prominent, distinct from Director of the Secretariat."
entries.literal: Since Heaven's intent is already to raise his rank and position, I humbly suggest that holding Palace Attendant with Valiant Cavalry is in station clear and prominent, distinct from Director of the Secretariat."

entries.zh: 上曰：「斆常啓吾，爲其鼻中惡。
entries.en: The emperor said, "Xiao often reported to me that he suffers from nasal affliction.
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Xiao often reported to me that he suffers from nasal affliction.

entries.zh: 今旣以何胤、王瑩還門下，故有此回換耳。」
entries.en: Now that He Yin and Wang Ying have been restored to the Secretariat, there is this reshuffling of posts."
entries.literal: Now that He Yin and Wang Ying have been restored to the Secretariat, there is this change of posts."

entries.zh: 鬱林卽位，遷掌吏部。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Xiao was transferred to head the Bureau of Personnel.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin took the throne, Xiao was transferred to head the Bureau of Personnel.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，爲侍中，領國子祭酒。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang he was made Palace Attendant and Rector of the National University.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he became Palace Attendant and concurrently Rector of the National University.

entries.zh: 鬱林廢，朝臣皆被召入宮，斆至雲龍門，託藥醉吐車中而去。
entries.en: When Emperor Yulin was deposed, all court ministers were summoned into the palace; Xiao reached the Cloud Dragon Gate, feigned illness and drunkenness, vomited in his carriage, and left.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yulin was deposed, all court ministers were summoned into the palace; Xiao reached the Cloud Dragon Gate, claimed illness and drunkenness, vomited in his carriage, and departed.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，改領祕書監，又改領晉安王師。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was reassigned as Director of the Palace Library and then as tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was changed to Director of the Palace Library and then changed to tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.

entries.zh: 服闋，爲吏部尚書。
entries.en: When mourning ended he was made Minister of the Bureau of Personnel.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he became Minister of the Bureau of Personnel.

entries.zh: 高宗廢鬱林，領兵入殿，左右驚走報𤅢。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao deposed the Prince of Yulin and led troops into the palace, attendants fled in alarm to report to Yao.
entries.literal: Emperor Gao deposed the Prince of Yulin and led troops into the palace; attendants fled in alarm to report to Yao.

entries.zh: 與客圍棊，每下子，輙云「其當有意」。
entries.en: He was playing weiqi with a guest and with each move would say, "They must have some purpose in this."
entries.literal: He was playing weiqi with a guest; with each stone placed he would say, "There must be some intent in this."

entries.zh: 竟局，乃還齋卧，竟不問外事也。
entries.en: When the game ended he returned to his quarters to sleep and never asked about outside affairs.
entries.literal: When the game ended he returned to his quarters to sleep and never inquired into outside affairs.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，𤅢又屬疾不視事。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming acceded, Yao again pleaded illness and declined to attend to affairs.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Yao again pleaded illness and did not attend to affairs.

entries.zh: 後上讌會，功臣上酒，尚書令王晏等興席，𤅢獨不起，曰：「陛下受命，應天從民，王晏妄叨天功以爲己力。」
entries.en: Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Yan and others rose; Yao alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—yet Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement."
entries.literal: Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Yan and others rose from their seats; Yao alone did not rise and said: "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own power."

entries.zh: 上大笑解之。
entries.en: The emperor laughed loudly and let the matter pass.
entries.literal: The emperor laughed greatly and smoothed the matter over.

entries.zh: 座罷，晏呼𤅢共載還令省，欲相撫悅。
entries.en: When the banquet ended, Yan invited Yao to ride back with him to the Directorate of the Imperial Secretariat, hoping to win him over.
entries.literal: When the seating ended, Yan called Yao to ride together back to the office of the Director of the Imperial Secretariat, wishing to soothe and please him.

entries.zh: 又正色曰：「君巢窟在何處？」
entries.en: Yao said sternly, "Where is your nest and den?"
entries.literal: Yao again said with stern countenance: "Where is your nest and den?"

entries.zh: 晏初得班劔，𤅢謂之曰：「身家太傅裁得六人。
entries.en: Yan had just received ceremonial swords; Yao told him, "Our family's Grand Tutor received only six sword-bearers.
entries.literal: Yan had just received ceremonial swords; Yao said to him: "Our family's Grand Tutor received only six men.

entries.zh: 君亦何事一朝至此。」
entries.en: What business of yours brings you to this in a single morning?"
entries.literal: What business of yours brings you to this in a single morning?"

entries.zh: 晏甚憚之。
entries.en: Yan feared him greatly.
entries.literal: Yan feared him greatly.

entries.zh: 初，兄朏爲吳興，𤅢於征虜渚送別，朏指𤅢口曰：「此中唯宜飲酒。」
entries.en: Earlier, when his elder brother Tiao was leaving for Wuxing, Yao saw him off at Zhengliu Ford; Tiao pointed at Yao's mouth and said, "This is fit for nothing but drinking wine."
entries.literal: Earlier, when his elder brother Fei was taking up the post at Wuxing, Yao saw him off at Zhengliu Ford; Fei pointed at Yao's mouth and said: "In this there is only what suits drinking wine."

entries.zh: 𤅢建武之初，專以長酣爲事，與劉瑱沈昭略以觴酌交飲，各至數斗。
entries.en: At the start of Jianwu, Yao devoted himself to long drinking bouts; with Liu Zhen and Shen Zhaolüe he exchanged cups and drank together, each consuming several dou.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, Yao devoted himself solely to long drinking as his occupation; with Liu Zhen and Shen Zhaolüe he exchanged cups and drank together, each reaching several dou.

entries.zh: 宋建平王景素辟爲南徐州主簿，深見禮遇。
entries.en: Jingsu, Prince Jianping of Song, recruited him as Master of Records for Southern Xuzhou and treated him with great respect.
entries.literal: Prince Jianping Jingsu of Song invited him as Master of Records for Southern Xuzhou and treated him with deep courtesy.

entries.zh: 景素被誅，左右離散，思遠親視殯葬，手種松柏。
entries.en: When Jingsu was executed his attendants scattered; Siyuan personally oversaw the funeral and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.
entries.literal: When Jingsu was executed his attendants scattered; Siyuan personally oversaw the encoffining and burial and planted pine and cypress with his own hands.

entries.zh: 與廬江何昌宇、沛郡劉璡上表理之，事感朝廷。
entries.en: Together with He Changyu of Lujiang and Liu Zhen of Pei Commandery he submitted a memorial to clear the prince's name, and the affair moved the court.
entries.literal: Together with He Changyu of Lujiang and Liu Zhen of Pei commandery he submitted a memorial to clear the case; the affair moved the court.

entries.zh: 景素女廢爲庶人，思遠分衣食以相資贍，年長，爲備笄總，訪求素對，傾家送遣。
entries.en: When Jingsu's daughter was reduced to commoner status, Siyuan shared his food and clothing to support her; when she came of age he prepared her hairpin ceremony, sought a suitable husband, and sent her off at the cost of his entire estate.
entries.literal: Jingsu's daughter was demoted to commoner status; Siyuan shared food and clothing to support her; when she grew older he prepared her hairpin and coming-of-age rites, sought a suitable match, and sent her off at the cost of his whole household.

entries.zh: 王思遠，琅邪臨沂人。
entries.en: Wang Siyuan came from Linyi in Langya Commandery.
entries.literal: Wang Siyuan was a man of Linyi in Langya.

entries.zh: 尚書令晏從弟也。
entries.en: He was a younger cousin of Wang Yan, Prefect of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: He was a younger cousin of Minister of Works Yan.

entries.zh: 父羅雲，平西長史。
entries.en: His father Wang Luoyun was Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West.
entries.literal: His father Luoyun was Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West.

entries.zh: 思遠八歲，父卒，祖弘之及外祖新安太守羊敬元，竝栖退高尚，故思遠少無仕心。
entries.en: When Siyuan was eight his father died; his grandfather Wang Hongzhi and his maternal grandfather Yang Jingyuan, Administrator of Xin'an, both lived in lofty retirement, and so from youth Siyuan had little desire for office.
entries.literal: Siyuan at eight years lost his father; his grandfather Hongzhi and his maternal grandfather Yang Jingyuan, Administrator of Xin'an, both dwelt in retirement and lofty virtue; therefore Siyuan from youth had no mind for office.

entries.zh: 世祖詔舉士，竟陵王子良薦思遠及吳郡顧暠之、陳郡殷叡。
entries.en: Emperor Wu ordered scholars to be recommended; Prince Jingling of Ziliang recommended Siyuan, Gu Haozhi of Wu Commandery, and Yin Rui of Chen Commandery.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu ordered the recommendation of scholars; Prince Jingling of Ziliang recommended Siyuan, Gu Haozhi of Wu commandery, and Yin Rui of Chen commandery.

entries.zh: 邵陵王子貞爲吳郡，世祖除思遠爲吳郡丞，以本官行郡事，論者以爲得人。
entries.en: When Prince Shaoling of Zizhen held Wu Commandery, Emperor Wu appointed Siyuan as Assistant Administrator and had him run the commandery in his existing capacity; commentators judged this an excellent appointment.
entries.literal: Prince Shaoling Zizhen was in charge of Wu commandery; Emperor Wu appointed Siyuan as Assistant Administrator of Wu and had him conduct commandery affairs in his existing office; commentators considered this a proper choice of man.

entries.zh: 以疾解職，還爲司徒諮議參軍，領錄事，轉黃門郎。
entries.en: He resigned on grounds of illness, returned as Adviser Adjutant to the Minister of Works and Recorder, and was then made Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: On grounds of illness he resigned his post, returned as Adviser Adjutant to the Minister of Works, concurrently Recorder, and was transferred to Yellow Gate Attendant.

entries.zh: 出爲使持節、都督廣交越三州諸軍事、寧朔將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。
entries.en: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Guang, Jiao, and Yue, General Who Pacifies the North, Central Commandant Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guang Province.
entries.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces of Guang, Jiao, and Yue, General Who Pacifies the North, Central Commandant Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guang province.

entries.zh: 高宗輔政，不之任，仍遷御史中丞。
entries.en: When Emperor Gao assumed the regency Siyuan did not take up the post and was instead made Imperial Censor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Gao assisted in government he did not go to the appointment and was instead transferred to Imperial Censor.

entries.zh: 臨海太守沈昭略贓私，思遠依事劾奏，高宗及思遠從兄晏、昭略叔父文季請止之，思遠不從，案事如故。
entries.en: When Shen Zhaolüe, Administrator of Linhai, was found corrupt, Siyuan impeached him on the evidence; Emperor Gao, Siyuan's cousin Wang Yan, and Zhaolüe's uncle Wenji asked him to desist, but he refused and pursued the case.
entries.literal: Shen Zhaolüe, Administrator of Linhai, was corrupt for private gain; Siyuan impeached him according to the facts; Emperor Gao, Siyuan's cousin Yan, and Zhaolüe's uncle Wenji asked him to stop; Siyuan did not comply and pursued the case as before.

entries.zh: 建武中，遷吏部郎。
entries.en: During the Jianwu era he was made Director of the Bureau of Personnel.
entries.literal: During Jianwu he was transferred to Director of the Bureau of Personnel.

entries.zh: 思遠以從兄晏爲尚書令，不欲竝居內臺權要之職，上表固讓。
entries.en: Because his cousin Wang Yan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Siyuan did not wish to hold a key inner-court post alongside him and submitted a firm memorial declining the appointment.
entries.literal: Because his cousin Yan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Siyuan did not wish to hold together with him key posts in the inner administration and submitted a firm memorial of declination.

entries.zh: 曰：「近頻煩歸啓，實有微概。
entries.en: He wrote, "I have recently troubled Your Majesty with repeated petitions to withdraw, and I do have a private concern.
entries.literal: He said: "Recently I have repeatedly troubled you with memorials of return; I truly have a slight grievance.

entries.zh: 陛下矜遇之厚，古今罕儔。
entries.en: Your Majesty's gracious treatment of me is rarely matched in history.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's generous treatment is thick—rarely matched in past and present.

entries.zh: 臣若孤恩，誰當戮力。
entries.en: If I turn my back on such grace, who will serve with full devotion?
entries.literal: If your subject isolates this grace, who will exert strength?

entries.zh: 旣自誓輕軀命，不復以塵黷爲疑，正以臣與晏地惟密親，必不宜俱居顯要。
entries.en: I have sworn to hold my life lightly and no longer fear worldly stain; it is precisely because Yan and I are close kin that we must not both hold prominent posts at court.
entries.literal: Having sworn to hold my body lightly, I no longer doubt worldly defilement; it is precisely because your subject and Yan are only close kin by station that we must not both hold prominent posts.

entries.zh: 慺慺丹赤，守之以死。
entries.en: With earnest loyalty I will guard this principle unto death.
entries.literal: Earnest and red-hearted, I guard this unto death.

entries.zh: 臣實庸鄙，無足獎進。
entries.en: I am truly mediocre and unworthy of promotion.
entries.literal: Your subject is truly mediocre and base, unworthy of reward and promotion.

entries.zh: 陛下甄拔之旨，要是許其一節。
entries.en: Your Majesty's intent in elevating me was to recognize one merit in me.
entries.literal: Your Majesty's intent in selecting and elevating was after all to grant one of my qualities.

entries.zh: 臣果不能以理自固，有乖則哲之明。
entries.en: If I cannot hold firm by principle, I would offend Your Majesty's discerning judgment.
entries.literal: If your subject truly cannot hold firm by principle, I would go against the clarity of the discerning sage.

entries.zh: 犯冒之尤，誅責在己，謬賞之私，惟塵聖鑒。
entries.en: The fault of presumption is mine alone to bear; any mistaken reward would only cloud Your Majesty's judgment.
entries.literal: The fault of offense and presumption—punishment and blame rest on myself; the private error of mistaken reward may only cloud the sage mirror.

entries.zh: 權其輕重，寧守福心。
entries.en: Weighing the matter, I would rather keep peace of mind.
entries.literal: Weighing light and heavy, I would rather keep a heart of blessing.

entries.zh: 且亦緣陛下以德御下，故臣可得以禮進退。
entries.en: It is because Your Majesty rules with virtue that I may advance or withdraw according to propriety.
entries.literal: Moreover it is because Your Majesty rules subordinates with virtue that your subject may advance and withdraw according to ritual.

entries.zh: 伏願思垂拯宥，不使零墜。
entries.en: I humbly beg Your Majesty to extend your mercy and not let me fall to ruin.
entries.literal: I humbly wish you to think of extending rescue and pardon, and not let me fall to ruin.

entries.zh: 今若祗膺所忝，三公不足爲泰，犯忤之後，九泉未足爲劇。
entries.en: If I now accept this shameful post, even the rank of the Three Excellencies would bring me no joy; after such an offense, even death would not be punishment enough.
entries.literal: If now I reverently accept what shames me, the Three Excellencies are not enough for pride; after offending, the Nine Springs are not enough for severity.

entries.zh: 而臣苟求刑戮，自弃富榮，愚夫不爲，臣亦庶免。
entries.en: Yet for me to court punishment and throw away wealth and glory is something even a fool would not do, and I too hope to avoid it.
entries.literal: Yet your subject seeks punishment and execution, abandoning wealth and glory—what a fool would not do, your subject also hopes to avoid.

entries.zh: 此心此志，可怜可矜。
entries.en: This heart and this resolve are pitiable indeed.
entries.literal: This heart, this will—pitiable and deserving compassion.

entries.zh: 如其上命必行，請罪非理，聖恩方置之通塗，而臣固求擯壓，自愍自悼，不覺涕流。
entries.en: If Your Majesty's command must stand, my plea is unreasonable; Your grace has just cleared my path, yet I stubbornly seek rejection; grieving for myself, I cannot keep back my tears.
entries.literal: If your superior command must be carried out, pleading guilt is unreasonable; sacred grace has just placed me on the open road, yet your subject stubbornly seeks rejection and suppression; pitying and grieving myself, I do not notice tears flowing.

entries.zh: 謹冒鈇鉞，悉心以請。
entries.en: I respectfully risk your displeasure and pour out my whole heart in this plea.
entries.literal: I respectfully dare the axe and halberd and pour out my heart in request.

entries.zh: 窮則呼天，仰祈一照。」
entries.en: In extremity one cries to Heaven; I look up and beg for a single ray of light."
entries.literal: In extremity one calls to Heaven; I look up hoping for one beam of light."

entries.zh: 上知其意，乃改授司徒左長史。
entries.en: The emperor understood his intent and transferred him to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.
entries.literal: The emperor understood his intent and thereupon transferred him to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 初，高宗廢立之際，思遠與晏閑言，謂晏曰：「兄荷世祖厚恩，今一旦贊人如此事，彼或可以權計相須，未知兄將來何以自立。
entries.en: Earlier, when Emperor Gao was deposing and enthroning emperors, Siyuan spoke privately with Yan and said, "Brother, you received great favor from Emperor Wu; now you have aided others in such a coup—they may need you for their schemes; I do not know how you will stand on your own afterward.
entries.literal: Earlier, at the time of Emperor Gao's deposition and enthronement, Siyuan spoke with Yan in private and said to Yan: "Elder brother, you received thick grace from Emperor Wu; now in a single morning you have assisted others in such an affair—they may need you for schemes of power; I do not know how you will establish yourself in the future.

entries.zh: 若及此引決，猶可不失後名。」
entries.en: If you act now, you may still preserve your good name."
entries.literal: If you take resolution at this point, you may still not lose your later reputation."

entries.zh: 晏不納。
entries.en: Yan did not heed him.
entries.literal: Yan did not accept it.

entries.zh: 及拜驃騎，集會子弟，謂思遠兄思微曰：「隆昌之末，阿戎勸吾自裁，若從其語，豈有今日。」
entries.en: When Yan was appointed Rapid Cavalry Commander he gathered his kin and said to Siyuan's elder brother Siwei, "At the end of Longchang, your brother urged me to take my own life; had I listened, would I be here today?"
entries.literal: When he was appointed Rapid Cavalry Commander he gathered his sons and nephews and said to Siyuan's elder brother Siwei: "At the end of Longchang, Arong urged me to take my own life; if I had followed his words, how could there be today?"

entries.zh: 思遠遽應曰：「如阿戎所見，猶未晚也。」
entries.en: Siyuan immediately replied, "In your brother’s view, it is still not too late."
entries.literal: Siyuan immediately replied: "As Arong saw it, it is still not too late."

entries.zh: 及晏敗，故得無他。
entries.en: When Yan fell, Siyuan therefore escaped further harm.
entries.literal: When Yan was ruined, he therefore suffered no other harm.

entries.zh: 上旣誅晏，遷爲侍中，掌優策及起居注。
entries.en: After the emperor executed Yan, Siyuan was made Palace Attendant, in charge of court policy and the Daily Records.
entries.literal: After the emperor had executed Yan, Siyuan was transferred to Palace Attendant, in charge of superior policy and the Daily Records.

entries.zh: 永元二年，遷度支尚書。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongyuan he was made Minister of Revenue.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan he was transferred to Minister of Revenue.

entries.zh: 未拜，卒。
entries.en: Before he could assume the post he died.
entries.literal: Before he accepted the appointment he died.

entries.zh: 年四十九。
entries.en: He was forty-nine years old.
entries.literal: He was forty-nine.

entries.zh: 贈太常，謚貞子。
entries.en: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Ceremonies, with the posthumous title Upright Son.
entries.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies; his posthumous title was Upright Son.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷四十三‧列傳第二十四
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 43, Biographies 24
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 43, Biographies 24

entries.zh: 世祖崩，遺詔轉右僕射。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu died, a testamentary edict transferred him to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu died; a testamentary edict transferred him to Right Vice Director.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，遷散騎常侍、前將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang he was transferred to Attendant Cavalier at Large, General of the Vanguard, and Governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang he was transferred to Attendant Cavalier at Large, General of the Vanguard, and Governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 高宗謀廢鬱林，以告孝嗣，孝嗣奉旨無所釐贊。
entries.en: Emperor Gao plotted to depose Emperor Yulin and informed Xiaosi; Xiaosi received the command without raising any objection.
entries.literal: Emperor Gao plotted to depose Emperor Yulin and informed Xiaosi; Xiaosi received the command without raising any objection.

entries.zh: 高宗入殿，孝嗣戎服隨後。
entries.en: Emperor Gao entered the hall and Xiaosi followed in military dress.
entries.literal: Emperor Gao entered the hall and Xiaosi followed in military dress.

entries.zh: 鬱林旣死，高宗須太后令，孝嗣於袖中出而奏之，高宗大悅。
entries.en: After Yulin was dead, Emperor Gao needed the empress dowager's order; Xiaosi produced it from his sleeve and presented it, and Emperor Gao was greatly pleased.
entries.literal: After Yulin was dead, Emperor Gao needed the empress dowager's order; Xiaosi produced it from his sleeve and presented it, and Emperor Gao was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 以廢立功，封枝江縣侯，食邑千戶。
entries.en: For his merit in the deposition he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang County with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: For his merit in the deposition he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhijiang County with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 給鼓吹一部，甲仗五十人入殿。
entries.en: He was granted one set of trumpets and drums and fifty armed men authorized to enter the hall.
entries.literal: He was granted one set of trumpets and drums and fifty armed men to enter the hall.

entries.zh: 轉左僕射，常侍如故。
entries.en: He was transferred to Left Vice Director, retaining his post as Attendant Cavalier.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Left Vice Director, Attendant Cavalier as before.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，加侍中、中軍大將軍，定策勳，進爵爲公，增封二千戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was additionally made Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Central Army; for his merit in settling the succession he was advanced in rank to duke with two thousand added households in his fief.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was additionally made Palace Attendant and Grand General of the Central Army; for merit in settling the succession he was advanced in rank to duke with two thousand added households.

entries.zh: 給班劔二十人，加兵百人。
entries.en: He was given twenty ceremonial guards and one hundred added troops.
entries.literal: He was given twenty ceremonial guards and one hundred added troops.

entries.zh: 舊拜三公乃臨軒，至是帝特詔與陳顯達、王晏竝臨軒拜授。
entries.en: Formerly investiture as one of the Three Excellencies alone warranted approaching the imperial steps; on this occasion the emperor specially ordered that he, Chen Xianda, and Wang Yan together receive investiture before the imperial steps.
entries.literal: Formerly only when invested as one of the Three Excellencies did one approach the imperial steps; on this occasion the emperor specially ordered that he, Chen Xianda, and Wang Yan together receive investiture before the imperial steps.

entries.zh: 北虜動，詔孝嗣假節頓新亭。
entries.en: When the northern enemy stirred, an edict appointed Xiaosi with provisional credentials to hold Xinting.
entries.literal: When the northern barbarians stirred, an edict appointed Xiaosi with provisional credentials to hold Xinting.

entries.zh: 時王晏爲令，民情物望，不及孝嗣也。
entries.en: At that time Wang Yan was chief minister, yet in popular esteem he did not match Xiaosi.
entries.literal: At that time Wang Yan was chief minister; in popular esteem he did not match Xiaosi.

entries.zh: 晏誅，轉尚書令，領本州中正，餘悉如故。
entries.en: When Yan was executed, Xiaosi was transferred to Director of the Secretariat and retained his post as nativist zhongzheng for his home province; all other appointments remained unchanged.
entries.literal: When Yan was executed, Xiaosi was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, heading the nativist zhongzheng of his home province, all else unchanged.

entries.zh: 孝嗣愛好文學，賞託清勝。
entries.en: Xiaosi loved literature and prized refined literary accomplishment.
entries.literal: Xiaosi loved literature and prized literary distinction.

entries.zh: 器量弘雅，不以權勢自居，故見容建武之世。
entries.en: His bearing was broad and refined, and he did not comport himself by rank—hence he was tolerated through the Jianwu era.
entries.literal: His capacity was broad and refined, and he did not comport himself by rank—hence he was tolerated in the Jianwu period.

entries.zh: 恭己自保，朝野以此稱之。
entries.en: He kept himself deferential and secure, and court and countryside alike praised him for it.
entries.literal: He kept himself deferential and secure; court and countryside praised him for it.

entries.zh: 晉平王休祐爲南徐州，帝問褚淵須幹事人爲上佐，淵舉文季。
entries.en: When Prince of Jinping Xiu You was assigned to Southern Xuzhou, the emperor asked Chu Yuan for a capable man as chief aide; Yuan recommended Wenji.
entries.literal: Prince of Jinping Xiu You was assigned to Southern Xuzhou; the emperor asked Chu Yuan who was a capable man for chief aide, and Yuan recommended Wenji.

entries.zh: 轉寧朔將軍、驃騎長史、南東海太守。
entries.en: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk to the Cavalry General, and Administrator of Southern Donghai.
entries.literal: He was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk to the Cavalry General, and Administrator of Southern Donghai.

entries.zh: 休祐被殺，雖用薨禮，僚佐多不敢至。
entries.en: Xiu You was killed; although the rites for a prince's death were observed, many of his staff did not dare attend.
entries.literal: Xiu You was killed; although the rites for a prince's death were used, many staff members did not dare attend.

entries.zh: 文季獨往省墓展哀。
entries.en: Wenji alone went to visit the tomb and express mourning.
entries.literal: Wenji alone went to visit the tomb and express mourning.

entries.zh: 出爲臨海太守。
entries.en: He went out as Administrator of Linhai.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Linhai.

entries.zh: 元徽初，遷散騎常侍，領後軍將軍，轉祕書監。
entries.en: At the beginning of the Yuanhui era he was transferred to Attendant Cavalier at Large and head of the Rear Army, then made Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhui he was transferred to Attendant Cavalier at Large, heading the Rear Army General, then made Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 出爲吳興太守。
entries.en: He went out as Administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 文季飲酒至五斗，妻王氏，王錫女，飲酒亦至三斗。
entries.en: Wenji could drink up to five dou; his wife was a Wang, daughter of Wang Xi, and she too could drink up to three dou.
entries.literal: Wenji drank up to five dou; his wife was of the Wang clan, daughter of Wang Xi, and she too drank up to three dou.

entries.zh: 文季與對飲竟日，而視事不廢。
entries.en: Wenji would drink with her facing each other all day long, yet never neglected his official duties.
entries.literal: Wenji would drink facing her all day long yet never neglected his official duties.

entries.zh: 昇明元年，沈攸之反，太祖加文季爲冠軍將軍，督吳興錢塘軍事。
entries.en: In the first year of Shengming, when Shen Youzhi rebelled, Grand Marshal Xiao Daocheng additionally made Wenji General Who Conquers Champions and supervisor of military affairs in Qiantang, Wuxing.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shengming Shen Youzhi rebelled; Grand Marshal Xiao Daocheng additionally made Wenji General Who Conquers Champions and supervisor of military affairs in Qiantang, Wuxing.

entries.zh: 攸之先爲景和銜使殺慶之。
entries.en: Youzhi had earlier, bearing Emperor Jinghe's grudge, caused Qingzhi's death.
entries.literal: Youzhi had earlier, bearing Emperor Jinghe's grudge, caused Qingzhi's death.

entries.zh: 至是文季收殺攸之弟新安太守登之，誅其宗族。
entries.en: At this time Wenji seized and killed Youzhi's younger brother Dengzhi, Administrator of Xin'an, and executed his entire clan.
entries.literal: At this time Wenji seized and killed Youzhi's younger brother Dengzhi, Administrator of Xin'an, and executed his entire clan.

entries.zh: 加持節，進號征虜將軍，改封略陽縣侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: He was given staff of authority, promoted to General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Lueyang County with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: He was given staff of authority, promoted to General Who Punishes the Barbarians, and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Lueyang County with a fief of one thousand households.

entries.zh: 明年，遷丹陽尹，將軍如故。
entries.en: The next year he was transferred to Governor of Danyang, retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to Governor of Danyang, general's rank as before.

entries.zh: 齊國初建，爲侍中，領祕書監。
entries.en: When the Qi state was first established he was made Palace Attendant and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When the Qi state was first established he was made Palace Attendant and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 建元元年，轉太子右衞率，侍中如故。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan he was transferred to Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was transferred to Right Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guard, Palace Attendant as before.

entries.zh: 改封西豐縣侯，食邑千二百戶。
entries.en: He was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng County with a fief of twelve hundred households.
entries.literal: He was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Xifeng County with a fief of twelve hundred households.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，加領太子詹事，增邑五百戶。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Wenji was additionally appointed concurrent Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with five hundred added households in his fief.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne Wenji was additionally made concurrent Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent with five hundred added households.

entries.zh: 尚書令王晏嘗戲文季爲吳興僕射。
entries.en: Director of the Secretariat Wang Yan once teased Wenji as the "Wuxing Vice Director."
entries.literal: Director of the Secretariat Wang Yan once teased Wenji as the Wuxing Vice Director.

entries.zh: 文季答曰：「琅邪執法，似不出卿門。」
entries.en: Wenji replied, "Langye's law enforcement—seems not to come from your own gate."
entries.literal: Wenji replied, "Langye's law enforcement—seems not to come from your gate."

entries.zh: 尋加散騎常侍，僕射如故。
entries.en: Soon he was additionally appointed Attendant Cavalier, retaining his post as Vice Director.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally made Attendant Cavalier, Vice Director as before.

entries.zh: 建武二年，虜寇壽春，豫州刺史豐城公遙昌嬰城固守，數遣輕兵相抄擊，明帝以爲憂，詔文季領兵鎮壽春。
entries.en: In the second year of the Jianwu era the northern enemy raided Shouchun; the Governor of Yu Province, Prince Yaochang of Fengcheng, held the city firm and repeatedly sent light troops on raiding strikes; Emperor Ming was troubled and ordered Wenji to lead troops to garrison Shouchun.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu the barbarians raided Shouchun; Governor of Yu Province the Prince of Fengcheng Yaochang held the city firm, repeatedly sending light troops on mutual raids; Emperor Ming was troubled and ordered Wenji to lead troops to garrison Shouchun.

entries.zh: 文季入城，止游兵不聽出，洞開城門，嚴加備守，虜軍尋退，百姓無所傷損。
entries.en: Wenji entered the city, halted roaming troops and would not let them sally forth, opened the gates wide, and strictly prepared the defense; the enemy army soon withdrew, and the populace suffered no harm.
entries.literal: Wenji entered the city, halted roaming troops and would not let them out, opened the gates wide, strictly prepared defense; the barbarian army soon withdrew and the people suffered no harm.

entries.zh: 增封爲千九百戶。
entries.en: His fief was increased to one thousand nine hundred households.
entries.literal: His fief was increased to one thousand nine hundred households.

entries.zh: 尋加護軍將軍，僕射、常侍如故。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was additionally appointed General Who Protects the Army, retaining his posts as Vice Director and Attendant Cavalier.
entries.literal: Soon he was additionally made General Who Protects the Army, Vice Director and Attendant Cavalier as before.

entries.zh: 兄子昭略，有剛氣。
entries.en: His elder brother's son Zhaolue had a forceful nature.
entries.literal: His elder brother's son Zhaolue had a forceful nature.

entries.zh: 昇明末，爲相國西曹掾，太祖賞之，及卽位，謂王儉曰：「南士中有沈昭略，何職處之？」
entries.en: At the end of Shengming he served as Western Bureau Adjutant to the Chancellor of State; the founding emperor admired him, and upon taking the throne said to Wang Jian, "Among southerners there is Shen Zhaolue—what post should he fill?"
entries.literal: At the end of Shengming he was Western Bureau Adjutant to the Chancellor of State; the founding emperor admired him, and upon taking the throne said to Wang Jian, "Among southerners there is Shen Zhaolue—what post should he fill?"

entries.zh: 儉曰：「臣已有擬。」
entries.en: Jian said, "Your servant already has a candidate in mind."
entries.literal: Jian said, "Your servant already has a candidate in mind."

entries.zh: 奏轉前軍將軍，上不欲違，可其奏。
entries.en: He memorialized to transfer him to General of the Vanguard; the emperor did not wish to refuse and approved the memorial.
entries.literal: He memorialized to transfer him to General of the Vanguard; the emperor did not wish to refuse and approved the memorial.

entries.zh: 尋遷爲中書郎。
entries.en: Soon he was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 永明初，歷太尉大司馬從事中郎，驃騎司馬，黃門郎。
entries.en: At the beginning of Yongming he successively served as Attendant in the household of the Grand Commandant and Grand Marshal, Cavalry General's staff major, and Yellow Gate Gentleman.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he successively served as Attendant in the household of the Grand Commandant and Grand Marshal, Cavalry General's staff major, and Yellow Gate Gentleman.

entries.zh: 南郡王友、學華選，以昭略爲友，尋兼左丞。
entries.en: As Companion to the Prince of Nanjun and a graduate of the Hua selection, Zhaolue was appointed companion; soon he also served concurrently as Left Assistant Director.
entries.literal: Companion to the Prince of Nanjun and a graduate of the Hua selection—Zhaolue was made his companion, soon concurrently serving as Left Assistant Director.

entries.zh: 元年，出爲臨海太守，御史中丞。
entries.en: In the first year of the reign he went out as Administrator of Linhai and Censor-in-Chief.
entries.literal: In the first year of the reign he went out as Administrator of Linhai and Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 昭略建武世嘗酣酒以自晦，與謝善。
entries.en: During the Jianwu era Zhaolue would drink heavily to conceal himself, and was on good terms with Xie.
entries.literal: During the Jianwu era Zhaolue would drink heavily to conceal himself, and was on good terms with Xie.

entries.zh: 累遷侍中，冠軍將軍，撫軍長史。
entries.en: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers Champions, and chief clerk of the Pacification Army.
entries.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant, General Who Conquers Champions, and chief clerk of the Pacification Army.

entries.zh: 永元元年，始安王遙光起兵東府，執昭略於城內。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongyuan Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an raised troops at the Eastern Palace and seized Zhaolue inside the city.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan Prince Yaoguang of Shi'an raised troops at the Eastern Palace and seized Zhaolue inside the city.

entries.zh: 昭略潛自南出，濟淮還臺。
entries.en: Zhaolue secretly went out from the south, crossed the Huai, and returned to the Secretariat.
entries.literal: Zhaolue secretly went out from the south, crossed the Huai, and returned to the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 至是與文季俱被召入華林省。
entries.en: At this time he and Wenji were both summoned into Hualin Park.
entries.literal: At this time he and Wenji were both summoned into Hualin Park.

entries.zh: 茹法珍等進藥酒，昭略怒罵徐孝嗣曰：「廢昏立明，古今令典。
entries.en: Ru Fazhen and others brought poisoned wine; Zhaolue angrily cursed Xu Xiaosi, saying, "Deposing the benighted and installing the enlightened is a worthy model of past and present.
entries.literal: Ru Fazhen and others brought poisoned wine; Zhaolue angrily cursed Xu Xiaosi, saying, "Deposing the benighted and installing the enlightened is a worthy model of past and present.

entries.zh: 宰相無才，致有今日。」
entries.en: The chief minister lacked talent and brought about this day."
entries.literal: The chief minister lacked talent and brought about this day."

entries.zh: 以甌擲面破，曰「作破面鬼」。
entries.en: He hurled a bowl, breaking Xiaosi's face, and said, "Become a face-broken ghost."
entries.literal: He hurled a bowl, breaking Xiaosi's face, and said, "Become a face-broken ghost."

entries.zh: 死時年四十餘。
entries.en: He died aged a little over forty.
entries.literal: He died aged a little over forty.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷四十四‧列傳第二十五
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 44, Biographies 25
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 44, Biographies 25

entries.zh: 鈞字宣禮，
entries.en: Jun, whose courtesy name was Xuanli.
entries.literal: Jun, styled Xuanli.

entries.zh: 永明四年，爲江州刺史，加散騎常侍。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Yongming, he was appointed Governor of Jiang Province and promoted to Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, he was made Governor of Jiang Province and promoted to Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 母區貴人卒，居喪盡禮。
entries.en: When his mother, Lady Qu, died, he observed the mourning rites in full.
entries.literal: When his mother Lady Qu died, he observed mourning with full propriety.

entries.zh: 六年，遷爲征虜將軍。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was made General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 八年，遷驍騎將軍，常侍如故。
entries.en: In the eighth year he was made General of Valiant Cavalry while retaining his post as regular attendant.
entries.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to General of Valiant Cavalry, with his regular attendant post unchanged.

entries.zh: 仍轉左衞將軍。
entries.en: He was then made General of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: He was then transferred to General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 鈞有好尚，爲世祖所知。
entries.en: Jun had cultivated tastes and won Emperor Wu's regard.
entries.literal: Jun had refined tastes and was appreciated by Emperor Wu.

entries.zh: 兄弟中意遇次鄱陽王鏘。
entries.en: Among his brothers in imperial favor he ranked second only to the Prince of Poyang, Qiang.
entries.literal: Among the brothers in favor he ranked second only to the Prince of Poyang, Qiang.

entries.zh: 十年，轉中書令，領石頭戍事。
entries.en: In the tenth year he became Director of the Imperial Secretariat and took charge of the Shitou garrison.
entries.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Secretariat and put in charge of the Shitou garrison.

entries.zh: 遷散騎常侍，祕書監，領驍騎如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat and Director of the Imperial Library while retaining his post as General of Valiant Cavalry.
entries.literal: He was moved to Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat and Director of the Imperial Library, still holding the valiant cavalry command.

entries.zh: 不拜，
entries.en: He declined to take up the post.
entries.literal: He did not accept the appointment.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，改加侍中，給扶。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang, he was instead made Palace Attendant and granted a support staff.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was instead made Palace Attendant and given a staff for support.

entries.zh: 海陵立，轉撫軍將軍，侍中如故。
entries.en: When the Prince of Hailing was enthroned, he was made General Who Pacifies the Army while retaining his post as palace attendant.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Hailing was enthroned, he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the Army, with his palace attendant post unchanged.

entries.zh: 尋遇害，年二十二。
entries.en: He was soon murdered, at the age of twenty-two.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was murdered; he was twenty-two.

entries.zh: 子珉字雲璵，世祖第二十子也，
entries.en: Zimin, whose courtesy name was Yunyu, was Emperor Wu's twentieth son.
entries.literal: Zimin, styled Yunyu, was Emperor Wu's twentieth son.

entries.zh: 永明七年，封義安王，後改永陽。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi'an, later redesignated Prince of Yongyang.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi'an, later changed to Prince of Yongyang.

entries.zh: 永泰元年見害，年十四。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai he was put to death, at the age of fourteen.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was killed; he was fourteen.

entries.zh: 復以武陵昭王曄第三子子坦奉元王後。
entries.en: Zitan, third son of Prince Ye of Wuling (posthumous title Zhao), was then appointed to continue the Prince of Yuan's line.
entries.literal: Again Zitan, the third son of Prince Ye of Wuling (posthumous title Zhao), was made to continue the Prince of Yuan's line.

entries.zh: 明帝卽位，以永陽王子珉仍本國，繼元王爲孫。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Zimin, the Prince of Yongyang, was left in his original fief and made to succeed the Prince of Yuan as his grandson-heir.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Prince Zimin of Yongyang was kept in his original fief and made to succeed the Prince of Yuan as grandson-heir.

entries.zh: 鳳字景慈，官至正員郎。
entries.en: Feng, whose courtesy name was Jingci, rose to the post of Regular Gentleman.
entries.literal: Feng, styled Jingci, reached the office of Regular Gentleman.

entries.zh: 卒於宋世。
entries.en: He died during the Song.
entries.literal: He died in the Song period.

entries.zh: 謚靖世子。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Heir Apparent Jing.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Heir Apparent Jing.

entries.zh: 明帝建武元年，贈侍中、驃騎將軍，開府儀同三司、始安靖王。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu under Emperor Ming he was posthumously made Palace Attendant and General of Agile Cavalry with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies, and given the title Prince Jing of Shian.
entries.literal: In Emperor Ming's first year of Jianwu he was posthumously given Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies; he was titled Prince Jing of Shian.

entries.zh: 改華林鳳莊門爲望賢門，太極東堂畫鳳鳥，題爲神鳥，而改鸞鳥爲神雀。
entries.en: The Fengzhuang Gate of Hualin Park was renamed Wangxian Gate; in the eastern hall of the Taiji Palace a phoenix was painted and inscribed "Divine Bird," and the luan bird motif was changed to "Divine Sparrow."
entries.literal: The Fengzhuang Gate of Hualin was renamed Wangxian Gate; in the eastern hall of the Taiji Palace a phoenix was painted and titled Divine Bird, and the luan bird was changed to Divine Sparrow.

entries.zh: 子遙光嗣。
entries.en: His son Yaoguang succeeded to the title.
entries.literal: His son Yaoguang succeeded.

entries.zh: 始安貞王道生字孝伯，太祖次兄也。
entries.en: Prince Daosheng of Shian (posthumous title Zhen), whose courtesy name was Xiaobo, was Emperor Gao's second elder brother.
entries.literal: Prince Zhen of Shian Daosheng, styled Xiaobo, was the founding emperor's second elder brother.

entries.zh: 宋世爲奉朝請，卒。
entries.en: During the Song he served as a court attendant and died in office.
entries.literal: In the Song period he was a court attendant and died.

entries.zh: 建元元年，追封謚。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan he received a posthumous enfeoffment and title.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title.

entries.zh: 建武元年，追尊爲景皇，妃江氏爲后。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu he was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, and his consort, Lady Jiang, was made empress.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing; his consort, Lady Jiang, was made empress.

entries.zh: 立寢廟於御道西，陵曰脩安。
entries.en: A spirit temple was established west of the imperial avenue, and his tomb was named Xiuan.
entries.literal: A spirit temple was established west of the imperial avenue; his tomb was called Xiuan.

entries.zh: 生子鳳、高宗、安陸昭王緬。
entries.en: His sons were Feng, Xiao Luan (later Emperor Ming), and Prince Mian of Anlu (posthumous title Zhao).
entries.literal: His sons were Feng, Xiao Luan, and Prince Zhao of Anlu, Mian.

entries.zh: 始安貞王道生
entries.en: Prince Daosheng of Shian (posthumous title Zhen)
entries.literal: Prince Zhen of Shian, Daosheng

entries.zh: 遙光字元暉。
entries.en: Yaoguang, whose courtesy name was Yuanhui.
entries.literal: Yaoguang, styled Yuanhui.

entries.zh: 生有躄疾，太祖謂不堪奉拜祭祀，欲封其弟，世祖諫，乃以遙光襲爵。
entries.en: Born lame, he was judged by Emperor Gao unfit to perform sacrificial worship; the emperor wished to enfeoff his younger brother instead, but Emperor Wu remonstrated, and Yaoguang was allowed to inherit the title.
entries.literal: Born with crippled legs, the founding emperor said he was unfit to perform sacrificial worship and wished to enfeoff his younger brother; Emperor Wu remonstrated, and so Yaoguang inherited the title.

entries.zh: 初爲員外郎，轉給事郎，太孫洗馬，轉中書郎，豫章內史，不拜。
entries.en: He began as an outside attendant, then became supervisor of attendants, groom of the heir apparent, and secretariat gentleman; he was appointed Interior Minister of Yuzhang but declined.
entries.literal: He first served as Outside Attendant, then Supervisor of Attendants, Groom of the Heir Apparent, then Secretariat Gentleman; he was appointed Interior Minister of Yuzhang but declined.

entries.zh: 高宗輔政，遙光好天文候道，密懷規贊，
entries.en: While Xiao Luan was regent, Yaoguang cultivated astronomy and omen-reading and secretly plotted to advance his cause.
entries.literal: When Xiao Luan assisted in government, Yaoguang loved astronomy and omen-reading and secretly harbored plans to aid him.

entries.zh: 隆昌元年，除驍騎將軍、冠軍將軍、南東海太守，行南徐州事。
entries.en: In the first year of Longchang, he was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry and General Who Vanquishes the Foe and Administrator of Southern Donghai, with acting authority over Southern Xuzhou.
entries.literal: In the first year of Longchang, he was made General of Valiant Cavalry and General Who Vanquishes the Foe and Administrator of Southern Donghai, acting for Southern Xuzhou.

entries.zh: 仍除南彭城太守，將軍如故。
entries.en: He was then made Administrator of Southern Pengcheng while retaining his general's rank.
entries.literal: He was then made Administrator of Southern Pengcheng, his generalships unchanged.

entries.zh: 又除輔國將軍、吳興太守。
entries.en: He was further appointed General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Wuxing.
entries.literal: He was again made General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Wuxing.

entries.zh: 高宗廢鬱林，又除冠軍將軍、南蠻校尉、西中郎長史、南郡太守。
entries.en: After Xiao Luan deposed the Prince of Yulin, he was again appointed General Who Vanquishes the Foe, Commandant of Southern Man, chief clerk on the Western Center Army staff, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
entries.literal: When Xiao Luan deposed the Prince of Yulin, he was again made General Who Vanquishes the Foe, Commandant of Southern Man, chief clerk on the Western Center Army staff, and Administrator of Nan Commandery.

entries.zh: 一歲之內，頻五除，竝不拜。
entries.en: Within a single year he received five successive appointments, and declined every one.
entries.literal: Within one year he was appointed five times in succession, and each time he declined.

entries.zh: 是時高宗欲卽位，誅賞諸事唯遙光共謀議。
entries.en: At that time, as Xiao Luan prepared to take the throne, Yaoguang alone shared his counsel on whom to execute and whom to reward.
entries.literal: At that time Xiao Luan wished to take the throne; in matters of execution and reward only Yaoguang joined him in deliberation.

entries.zh: 建武元年，以爲持節、都督揚南徐二州諸軍事、前將軍、揚州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu he was made Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Yang and Southern Xu provinces, Forward General, and Governor of Yang Province.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Yang and Southern Xu Provinces, Forward General, and Governor of Yang Province.

entries.zh: 晉安王寶義爲南徐州，遙光求解督，見許。
entries.en: When Prince Bao of Jin'an took Southern Xuzhou, Yaoguang asked to be relieved of overall command, and his request was granted.
entries.literal: When Prince Bao of Jin'an became governor of Southern Xu, Yaoguang asked to be relieved of overall command and was permitted.

entries.zh: 二年，進號撫軍將軍，加散騎常侍，給通幰車鼓吹。
entries.en: In the second year he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, made Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, and granted a canopy carriage with martial music.
entries.literal: In the second year he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army, made Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat, and given a canopy carriage with martial music.

entries.zh: 遙光好吏事，稱爲分明。
entries.en: Yaoguang took to administrative work and was praised for his clarity and decisiveness.
entries.literal: Yaoguang loved administrative affairs and was said to be clear and decisive.

entries.zh: 頗多慘害。
entries.en: His punishments were often cruel.
entries.literal: He was rather cruel in his punishments.

entries.zh: 足疾不得同朝列，常乘輿自望賢門入。
entries.en: His foot ailment kept him from standing in the court ranks, so he usually entered by carriage through Wangxian Gate.
entries.literal: Because of his foot ailment he could not stand in court ranks and usually entered by carriage through Wangxian Gate.

entries.zh: 每與上久清閑，言畢，上索香火，明日必有所誅殺。
entries.en: Whenever he lingered in private conversation with the emperor, the emperor would call for incense when they finished; the next day someone was always put to death.
entries.literal: Whenever he spent a long time in quiet talk with the emperor, when the talk ended the emperor would ask for incense; the next day there were always executions.

entries.zh: 上以親近單少，憎忌高、武子孫，欲竝誅之，遙光計畫參議，當以次施行。
entries.en: Finding his own close kin few in number, the emperor resented the descendants of the Gao and Wu lines and wished to execute them all; Yaoguang helped plan the killings, to be carried out in sequence.
entries.literal: Because his close kin were few, the emperor hated the descendants of the Gao and Wu emperors and wished to execute them all; Yaoguang joined in planning, to be carried out in order.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，卽本位爲大將軍，給油絡車。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai he was promoted from his current rank to Grand General and granted an oiled-canopy carriage.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he was promoted from his present rank to Grand General and given an oiled-canopy carriage.

entries.zh: 帝不豫，遙光數入侍疾，帝漸甚，河東王鉉等七王一夕見殺，遙光意也。
entries.en: When the emperor fell ill, Yaoguang attended him repeatedly; as the illness worsened, Prince Xuan of Hedong and six other princes were killed in a single night—at Yaoguang's instigation.
entries.literal: When the emperor fell ill, Yaoguang repeatedly attended him in his sickness; as the illness worsened, the Prince of Hedong Xuan and six other princes were killed in one night—Yaoguang's doing.

entries.zh: 帝崩，遺詔加遙光侍中、中書令，給扶。
entries.en: When the emperor died, his final edict made Yaoguang Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat and granted him a support staff.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, his final edict added Yaoguang as Palace Attendant and Director of the Imperial Secretariat and gave him a support staff.

entries.zh: 永元元年，給班劔二十人，卽本號開府儀同三司。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongyuan he was granted twenty sword-bearing guards and, at his existing rank, privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he was given twenty guards with swords and, at his present rank, the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 遙光旣輔政，見少主卽位，潛與江祏兄弟謀自樹立。
entries.en: Once Yaoguang was regent and saw the young emperor enthroned, he secretly plotted with the Jiang Shi brothers to seize power for himself.
entries.literal: Once Yaoguang was assisting in government and saw the young ruler enthroned, he secretly plotted with the Jiang Shi brothers to set himself up.

entries.zh: 弟遙欣在荊楚，擁兵居上流，密相影響。
entries.en: His younger brother Yaoxin held troops in the Jing-Chu region on the upper Yangzi and secretly coordinated with him.
entries.literal: His younger brother Yaoxin was in Jing-Chu, holding troops on the upper reaches, and they secretly supported each other.

entries.zh: 遙光當據東府號令，使遙欣便星速急下。
entries.en: Yaoguang was to hold the Eastern Mansion and issue orders while Yaoxin rushed downriver at utmost speed.
entries.literal: Yaoguang was to hold the Eastern Mansion and issue orders, while Yaoxin was to hurry down at star speed.

entries.zh: 潛謀將發，而遙欣病死。
entries.en: Their secret plot was about to be launched when Yaoxin died of illness.
entries.literal: Their secret plot was about to be launched when Yaoxin died of illness.

entries.zh: 江祏被誅，東昏侯召遙光入殿，告以祏罪，遙光懼，還省便陽狂號哭，自此稱疾不復入臺。
entries.en: When Jiang Shi was executed, the Marquis of Donghun summoned Yaoguang to the hall and told him of Shi's crimes. Yaoguang, terrified, returned to his office and at once feigned madness, wailing aloud; from then on he claimed illness and never again entered the Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Jiang Shi was executed, the Marquis of Donghun summoned Yaoguang to the hall and told him of Shi's crimes; Yaoguang was afraid, returned to his office and at once feigned madness, wailing; from then on he claimed illness and no longer entered the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 先是遙光行還入城，風飄儀繖出城外。
entries.en: Earlier, as Yaoguang was returning into the city, the wind blew his ceremonial canopy out beyond the walls.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Yaoguang was returning into the city on a journey, the wind blew the ceremonial canopy out beyond the walls.

entries.zh: 至日中，臺軍稍至，尚書符遙光曰：「逆從之數，皎然有徵，干紀亂常，刑茲罔赦。
entries.en: By midday the Secretariat troops were arriving in force. The Imperial Secretariat issued a warrant against Yaoguang: "The ranks of rebels and followers are plainly evident; those who violate discipline and disturb order shall be punished without pardon.
entries.literal: By midday the Secretariat troops gradually arrived; the Imperial Secretariat issued a warrant to Yaoguang: "The number of rebels and followers is plainly evident; those who violate discipline and disturb order—punish them without pardon.

entries.zh: 蕭遙光宗室蚩庸，才行鄙薄，緹裙可望，天路何階。
entries.en: Xiao Yaoguang of the imperial clan is stupid and base, his talent and conduct contemptible; he may gaze at the emperor's robe, but what stair leads to Heaven's road?
entries.literal: Xiao Yaoguang of the imperial clan is stupid and base, his talent and conduct mean; he may gaze at the emperor's skirt, but what stair leads to Heaven's road?

entries.zh: 受遇自昔，恩加猶子，禮絕帝體，寵越皇季。
entries.en: Favored from of old, he was treated with grace as to an emperor's nephew; ritual honors surpassed those due the imperial person, and favor exceeded that shown an imperial younger brother.
entries.literal: Favored from old, grace added as to a son of an uncle, ritual surpassing the imperial body, favor exceeding an imperial younger brother.

entries.zh: 旗章車服，窮千乘之尊；
entries.en: His banners, insignia, carriages, and robes exhausted the honors of a lord of a thousand chariots;
entries.literal: Banners, insignia, carriages, and robes exhausted the honor of a lord of a thousand chariots;

entries.zh: 闉隍爽闓，踰百雉之制。
entries.en: his gate-towers and double gates exceeded the measure prescribed for a hundred-perch wall.
entries.literal: his gate-towers and double gates exceeded the measure of a hundred perches.

entries.zh: 及聖后在天，親受顧託，話言在耳，德音猶存，侮蔑天明，罔畏不義，無君之心，履霜有日。
entries.en: When the sage sovereign was in Heaven he personally received his entrustment; his words still ring in the ear, his virtuous voice still lingers—yet he insults Heaven's clarity, fears no injustice, and harbors a heart without a sovereign; the day he treads on frost has long been at hand.
entries.literal: When the sage sovereign was in Heaven he personally received his entrustment; his words still ring in the ear, his virtuous voice still remains—yet he insults Heaven's clarity, fears not injustice, has a heart without a ruler; the day he treads on frost has long been coming.

entries.zh: 遂乃稱兵內犯，竊發京畿，自古巨舋，莫斯爲甚。
entries.en: He then raised troops and struck within the realm, stealthily attacking the capital region—of great outrages since antiquity, none surpasses this.
entries.literal: He then raised troops and invaded within, stealthily striking the capital region—of great outrages since antiquity, none surpasses this.

entries.zh: 今便分命六師，弘宣九伐。
entries.en: Now we shall divide command among the six armies and proclaim the nine punitive campaigns.
entries.literal: Now we shall divide command among the six armies and proclaim the nine punitive campaigns.

entries.zh: 皇上當親御戎軒，弘此廟略。
entries.en: The emperor shall personally mount the war chariot and execute this strategy ordained in the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: The emperor shall personally mount the war chariot and carry out this temple strategy.

entries.zh: 信賞必罰，有如大江。」
entries.en: Rewards for the faithful and certain punishment—as the great river bears witness."
entries.literal: Rewards for faith, punishments certain—as the great river witnesses."

entries.zh: 於是戒嚴，曲赦京邑。
entries.en: Thereupon martial law was declared and a partial amnesty granted in the capital region.
entries.literal: Thereupon martial law was declared and a partial amnesty granted in the capital.

entries.zh: 領軍蕭坦之屯湘宮寺，鎮軍司馬曹虎屯清溪大橋，太子右衞率左興盛屯東府東籬門。
entries.en: Commander-in-Chief Xiao Tanzhi encamped at Xianggong Temple; Major Cao Hu of the Pacification Army at Qingxi Great Bridge; and the Heir Apparent's Right Guard Commander Zuo Xingsheng at the eastern hedge gate of the Eastern Mansion.
entries.literal: Commander-in-Chief Xiao Tanzhi encamped at Xianggong Temple; the Pacification Army's Major Cao Hu at Qingxi Great Bridge; the Heir Apparent's Right Guard Commander Zuo Xingsheng at the Eastern Mansion's eastern hedge gate.

entries.zh: 遙欣字重暉。
entries.en: Yaoxin, whose courtesy name was Chonghui.
entries.literal: Yaoxin, styled Chonghui.

entries.zh: 宣帝兄西平太守奉之無後，以遙欣繼爲曾孫。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan's elder brother Fengzhi, administrator of Xiping, had no heir; Yaoxin was adopted to continue the line as his great-grandson.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan's elder brother, Administrator of Xiping Fengzhi, had no heir; Yaoxin was made to succeed as great-grandson.

entries.zh: 除祕書郎，太子舍人，巴陵王文學，中書郎。
entries.en: He was appointed Secretariat Gentleman, attendant of the heir apparent, literary aide to the Prince of Baling, and secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: He was made Secretariat Gentleman, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, literary aide to the Prince of Baling, and Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 延興元年，高宗樹置，以遙欣爲持節、督兖州緣淮軍事、寧朔將軍、兖州刺史。
entries.en: In the first year of Yanxing, as Xiao Luan built his power structure, Yaoxin was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yan Province's military affairs along the Huai, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Yan Province.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, as Xiao Luan established his power structure, Yaoxin was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of Yan Province's military affairs along the Huai, General Who Pacifies the North, and Governor of Yan Province.

entries.zh: 仍爲督豫州郢州之西陽司州之汝南二郡、輔國將軍、豫州刺史，持節如故。
entries.en: He was then made commander of Yuzhou and of Xiyang in Yingzhou and Runan in Sizhou, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Yuzhou, retaining his staff of authority.
entries.literal: He was then made commander of Yuzhou and the two commanderies Xiyang in Yingzhou and Runan in Sizhou, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Yuzhou, with the staff unchanged.

entries.zh: 未之任。
entries.en: He did not take up the appointment.
entries.literal: He did not take up the post.

entries.zh: 建武元年，進號西中郎將，封聞喜縣公。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu he was promoted to Western Center Army General and enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was advanced to Western Center Army General and enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.

entries.zh: 遷使持節、都督荊雍益寧梁南北秦七州軍事、右將軍、荊州刺史。
entries.en: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of military affairs in Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, Right General, and Governor of Jing Province.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the seven provinces Jing, Yong, Yi, Ning, Liang, and Northern and Southern Qin, Right General, and Governor of Jing Province.

entries.zh: 改封曲江公。
entries.en: His title was changed to Duke of Qujiang.
entries.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Qujiang.

entries.zh: 高宗子弟弱小，晉安王寶義有廢疾，故以遙光爲揚州居中，遙欣居陝西在外，權勢竝在其門。
entries.en: Xiao Luan's sons and younger brothers were still young; Prince Bao of Jin'an was crippled by illness; therefore Yaoguang held Yang Province at the center while Yaoxin held the west-of-the-pass region on the outside—power and influence alike rested in their house.
entries.literal: Xiao Luan's sons and younger brothers were young and weak; Prince Bao of Jin'an had a crippling illness; therefore Yaoguang held Yang Province at the center and Yaoxin held the region west of the passes on the outside—power and influence were both in their house.

entries.zh: 遙欣好勇，聚畜武士，以爲形援。
entries.en: Yaoxin loved martial prowess and gathered fighting men as a visible source of strength.
entries.literal: Yaoxin loved valor and gathered and kept fighting men as a visible support.

entries.zh: 四年，進號平西將軍。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.

entries.zh: 永泰元年，以雍州虜寇，詔遙欣以本官領刺史，寧蠻校尉，移鎮襄陽，虜退不行。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongtai, when barbarians raided Yong Province, an edict ordered Yaoxin, at his existing rank, to take the governorship and the post of Commandant Who Pacifies the Man and move his headquarters to Xiangyang; when the raiders withdrew he did not go.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, because barbarians raided Yong Province, an edict ordered Yaoxin, at his present rank, to take the governorship and the post of Commandant Who Pacifies the Man, and move his headquarters to Xiangyang; when the barbarians withdrew he did not go.

entries.zh: 永元元年卒，年三十一。
entries.en: He died in the first year of Yongyuan, at the age of thirty-one.
entries.literal: He died in the first year of Yongyuan; he was thirty-one.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、司空，謚康公。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Duke Kang.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given Palace Attendant and Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Duke Kang.

entries.zh: 葬用王禮。
entries.en: He was buried with princely rites.
entries.literal: His burial used princely rites.

entries.zh: 二年，虜主元宏寇壽春，遣使呼城內人，遙昌遣參軍崔慶遠、朱選之詣宏。
entries.en: In the second year the Northern Wei ruler Yuan Hong attacked Shouchun and sent envoys to summon the city's defenders; Yaochang sent his staff officers Cui Qingyuan and Zhu Xuanzhi to meet Hong.
entries.literal: In the second year the barbarian ruler Yuan Hong attacked Shouchun and sent envoys to summon the people within the city; Yaochang sent his staff officers Cui Qingyuan and Zhu Xuanzhi to go to Hong.

entries.zh: 慶遠曰：「旌蓋飄颻，遠涉淮、泗，風塵慘烈，無乃上勞？」
entries.en: Qingyuan said, "Your banners and canopies flutter in the wind on this long march across the Huai and Si—the dust and hardship are severe. Is this not too great a burden for Your Majesty?"
entries.literal: Qingyuan said: "Your banners and canopies flutter in the wind, having come far across the Huai and Si—dust and hardship are bitter; is this not too great a labor for Your Majesty?"

entries.zh: 宏曰：「六龍騰躍，倏忽千里，經途未遠，不足爲勞。」
entries.en: Hong said, "The six dragons leap and soar—a thousand li in an instant. The journey is not yet long; it hardly counts as labor."
entries.literal: Hong said: "The six dragons leap and soar; in an instant a thousand li—the journey is not yet far; it is not enough to count as labor."

entries.zh: 慶遠曰：「川境旣殊，遠勞軒駕。
entries.en: Qingyuan said, "Our river realms are already different, yet Your Majesty's carriage has been troubled from afar.
entries.literal: Qingyuan said: "The river realms are already different; Your Majesty's carriage has been troubled from afar.

entries.zh: 屈完有言：『不虞君之涉吾地也，何故？』」
entries.en: Qu Wan once said, 'We did not expect Your Lordship to cross our territory—what is the reason?'"
entries.literal: Qu Wan once said: 'We did not expect Your Lordship to cross our territory—what is the reason?'"

entries.zh: 宏曰：「故當有故。
entries.en: Hong said, "Of course there is a reason.
entries.literal: Hong said: "Of course there is a reason.

entries.zh: 卿欲使我含瑕依違；
entries.en: Do you wish me to harbor a flaw and speak ambiguously,
entries.literal: Do you wish me to harbor a flaw and yield ambiguously;

entries.zh: 爲欲指斥其事？」
