entries.en: or do you wish to speak to the matter directly?"
entries.literal: or do you wish to point and reprove the matter directly?"

entries.zh: 慶遠曰：「君包荒之德，本施北政，未承來議，無所含瑕。」
entries.en: Qingyuan said, "Your Lordship's virtue of embracing all within the waste is shown in governing the north; we have not yet received your embassy—there is no flaw to harbor."
entries.literal: Qingyuan said: "Your Lordship's virtue of embracing the wasteland is originally shown in governing the north; we have not yet received your coming deliberation—there is no harboring of flaw."

entries.zh: 宏曰：「朕本欲有言，會卿來問。
entries.en: Hong said, "I had intended to speak; it happens that you have come to ask.
entries.literal: Hong said: "I originally wished to speak; it happens that you have come to ask.

entries.zh: 齊主廢立，有其例不？」
entries.en: The Qi ruler's deposition and enthronement—is there precedent for that?"
entries.literal: The Qi ruler's deposition and enthronement—are there precedents for it?"

entries.zh: 慶遠曰：「廢昏立明，古今同揆。
entries.en: Qingyuan said, "Deposing the benighted and establishing the enlightened—ancient and modern share the same standard.
entries.literal: Qingyuan said: "Deposing the benighted and establishing the enlightened—ancient and modern share one measure.

entries.zh: 中興克昌，豈唯一代？
entries.en: Restoration and triumph—how could that belong to only one age?
entries.literal: Restoration and triumph—how could it be only one generation?

entries.zh: 主上與先武帝，非唯昆季，有同魚水。
entries.en: Our sovereign and the late Emperor Wu were not merely brothers by birth but were as intimate as fish and water.
entries.literal: Our sovereign and the late Emperor Wu were not only brothers by birth but were like fish and water together.

entries.zh: 武皇臨崩，託以後事。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu lay dying he entrusted him with the affairs that followed.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu lay dying he entrusted the affairs that followed.

entries.zh: 嗣孫荒迷，廢爲鬱林，功臣固請，爰立明聖。
entries.en: The heir's grandson was dissolute and confused and was deposed as Prince of Yulin; the meritorious ministers firmly petitioned, and the enlightened sovereign was established in his place.
entries.literal: The heir's grandson was dissolute and confused and was deposed as Prince of Yulin; the meritorious ministers firmly petitioned, and so the enlightened and sage was established.

entries.zh: 上逼太后之嚴令，下迫羣臣之稽顙，俯從億兆，踐登皇極。
entries.en: Pressed from above by the empress dowager's stern command and from below by the ministers bowing their foreheads to the ground, he bowed to the will of the millions and ascended the throne.
entries.literal: Above he was pressed by the empress dowager's stern command; below compelled by the ministers' bowed foreheads; he bowed to the hundred millions and ascended the imperial pinnacle.

entries.zh: 未審聖旨，獨何疑怪？」
entries.en: We have not yet understood Your Majesty's intent—why this doubt alone?"
entries.literal: We have not yet understood the sage intent—why alone this doubt and wonder?"

entries.zh: 宏曰：「聞卿此言，殊解我心。
entries.en: Hong said, "Hearing your words has greatly eased my mind.
entries.literal: Hong said: "Hearing your words, you have especially resolved my heart.

entries.zh: 但哲婦傾城，何足可用。
entries.en: But a wise woman can overturn a state—how could she be worth employing?
entries.literal: But a wise woman overturns a state—how could she be worth employing?

entries.zh: 果如所言，武帝子弟今皆何在？」
entries.en: If it is truly as you say, where are all of Emperor Wu's sons and younger brothers now?"
entries.literal: If it is truly as you say, where are all the sons and younger brothers of Emperor Wu now?"

entries.zh: 慶遠曰：「七王同惡，皆伏管、蔡之誅，其餘列蕃二十餘國，內升清階，外典方牧。
entries.en: Qingyuan said, "Seven princes shared in the same crime and all suffered punishment like Guan and Cai; the rest, more than twenty feudal domains, rose within to high office and governed the regions without.
entries.literal: Qingyuan said: "Seven princes shared the same evil and all suffered the punishment of Guan and Cai; the rest, more than twenty feudal states in the ranks of the domains, rose within to clear ranks and without governed the regions as shepherds.

entries.zh: 哲婦之戒，古人所惑；
entries.en: The warning against a wise woman is what misled the ancients;
entries.literal: The warning against a wise woman is what ancients were misled by;

entries.zh: 然十亂盈朝，實唯文母。」
entries.en: yet with ten able ordering ministers filling the court, in truth it was only Queen Wen."
entries.literal: yet when ten ordering ministers filled the court, in truth it was only Queen Wen."

entries.zh: 宏曰：「如我所聞，靡有孑遺。
entries.en: Hong said, "As I have heard, not one was left alive.
entries.literal: Hong said: "As I have heard, not one was left alive.

entries.zh: 卿言美而乖實，未之全信。」
entries.en: Your words are eloquent but depart from fact; I do not fully believe them."
entries.literal: Your words are fine but depart from fact; I do not fully believe them."

entries.zh: 宏又曰：「雲羅所掩，六合宜一。
entries.en: Hong also said, "Where the cloud-net covers all, the six directions ought to be one.
entries.literal: Hong also said: "Where the cloud-net covers, the six directions ought to be one.

entries.zh: 故往年與齊武有書，言今日之事，書似未達齊主，命也。
entries.en: Therefore in former years I exchanged letters with Emperor Wu of Qi about today's affairs; the letter seems not to have reached the Qi ruler—it is fate.
entries.literal: Therefore in former years I exchanged letters with Emperor Wu of Qi concerning today's affairs; the letter seems not to have reached the Qi ruler—it is fate.

entries.zh: 南使旣反，情有愴然，朕亦休兵。
entries.en: The southern envoy has already returned; I feel somewhat mournful, and I too will rest the armies.
entries.literal: The southern envoy has already returned; my feelings are somewhat mournful, and I too will rest the armies.

entries.zh: 此段猶是本意，不必專爲問罪。
entries.en: This is still my original intent; I need not be here solely to demand accountability.
entries.literal: This passage is still my original intent; it need not be solely to demand accountability.

entries.zh: 若如卿言，便可釋然。」
entries.en: If it is as you say, I can set my mind at ease."
entries.literal: If it is as you say, I can then be released and at ease."

entries.zh: 慶遠曰：「見可而進，知難而退，聖人奇兵。
entries.en: Qingyuan said, "Seeing what may be done and advancing, knowing difficulty and withdrawing—that is the sage's extraordinary weapon.
entries.literal: Qingyuan said: "Seeing what may be done and advancing, knowing difficulty and withdrawing—the sage's extraordinary weapon.

entries.zh: 今旨欲憲章聖人，不失舊好，豈不善哉！」
entries.en: Your present intent is to follow the sage's example and preserve the old friendship—how could that not be excellent!"
entries.literal: Your present intent wishes to take the sage as model and law, not losing the old friendship—how could it not be excellent!"

entries.zh: 宏曰：「卿爲欲朕和親？
entries.en: Hong said, "Do you wish me to make peace by marriage?
entries.literal: Hong said: "Do you wish me to make peace by marriage?

entries.zh: 爲欲不和？」
entries.en: Or do you wish no peace?"
entries.literal: Or do you wish no peace?"

entries.zh: 慶遠曰：「和親則二國交歡，蒼生再賴；
entries.en: Qingyuan said, "If there is peace by marriage, the two states will rejoice together and the common people will again be spared;
entries.literal: Qingyuan said: "If there is peace by marriage, the two states will exchange joy and the common people will again rely on it;

entries.zh: 不和則二國交怨，蒼生塗炭。
entries.en: if there is no peace, the two states will resent each other and the common people will be scorched on the coals.
entries.literal: if there is no peace, the two states will exchange resentment and the common people will be scorched on the coals.

entries.zh: 和與不和，裁由聖衷。」
entries.en: Peace or no peace rests solely with Your Majesty's heart."
entries.literal: Peace or no peace is decided only by the sage heart."

entries.zh: 宏曰：「朕來爲復遊行鹽境，北去洛都，率爾便至。
entries.en: Hong said, "I have come again to tour the salt districts; traveling north toward the Luo capital, I came forth simply and arrived here.
entries.literal: Hong said: "I have come again to tour the salt districts; going north to the Luo capital, I came forth simply and arrived.

entries.zh: 亦不攻城，亦不伐塢，卿勿以爲慮。」
entries.en: I will neither attack the city nor assault the fortified villages—you need not worry on that account."
entries.literal: I will neither attack the city nor assault the fortified villages—you need not take it as a worry."

entries.zh: 宏設酒及羊炙雜果，又謂慶遠曰：「聽卿主克黜凶嗣，不違忠孝。
entries.en: Hong set out wine, roasted mutton, and assorted fruits, and again said to Qingyuan, "I hear your sovereign was able to remove the vicious heir without violating loyalty and filial piety.
entries.literal: Hong set out wine and roasted mutton with assorted fruits, and again said to Qingyuan: "I hear your sovereign was able to remove the vicious heir without violating loyalty and filial piety.

entries.zh: 何以不立近親，如周公輔成王，而苟欲自取？」
entries.en: Why not establish a close kinsman, as the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, instead of casually seeking to take the throne for yourself?"
entries.literal: Why not establish a close kinsman, as the Duke of Zhou assisted King Cheng, but instead wish casually to take it for oneself?"

entries.zh: 慶遠答曰：「成王有亞聖之賢，故周公得輔而相之。
entries.en: Qingyuan replied, "King Cheng had the virtue of a near-sage; therefore the Duke of Zhou was able to assist and serve as his minister.
entries.literal: Qingyuan replied: "King Cheng had the virtue of a near-sage; therefore the Duke of Zhou was able to assist and serve as his minister.

entries.zh: 今近蕃雖無悖德，未有成王之賢。
entries.en: Today's close princes, though without rebellious conduct, do not have King Cheng's worthiness.
entries.literal: Now the close domains, though without rebellious conduct, do not have King Cheng's worthiness.

entries.zh: 霍光亦捨漢蕃親而遠立宣帝。」
entries.en: Huo Guang also set aside the Han imperial clansmen and established Emperor Xuan from afar."
entries.literal: Huo Guang also set aside the Han imperial clansmen and from afar established Emperor Xuan."

entries.zh: 宏曰：「若爾，霍光嚮自立爲君，當復得爲忠臣不？」
entries.en: Hong said, "If so, when Huo Guang formerly established himself as ruler, could he still have counted as a loyal minister?"
entries.literal: Hong said: "If so, when Huo Guang formerly established himself as ruler, could he still have counted as a loyal minister?"

entries.zh: 慶遠曰：「此非其類，乃可言宣帝立與不立義當云何。
entries.en: Qingyuan said, "That is not the same case; one may speak only of whether establishing Emperor Xuan was right—what ought the principle to be?
entries.literal: Qingyuan said: "This is not the same category; one may speak only of whether establishing Emperor Xuan or not was right—what ought the principle to be?

entries.zh: 皇上豈得與霍光爲匹？
entries.en: How could our emperor be matched with Huo Guang?
entries.literal: How could our emperor be matched with Huo Guang?

entries.zh: 若爾，何以不言『武王伐紂，何意不立微子而輔之，苟貪天下？』」
entries.en: If so, why not say, 'When King Wu attacked King Zhou, why did he not establish Weizi and assist him, but greedily seize the realm under Heaven?'"
entries.literal: If so, why not say: 'When King Wu attacked Zhou, why did he not establish Weizi and assist him, but greedily desired the realm under Heaven?'"

entries.zh: 宏大笑。
entries.en: Hong laughed loudly.
entries.literal: Hong laughed greatly.

entries.zh: 明日引軍向城東，遣道登道人進城內施衆僧絹五百匹，慶遠、選之各褶絡帶。
entries.en: The next day he led his army toward the east of the city, sent the religious adept Daodeng into the city to bestow five hundred bolts of silk on the monks, and gave Qingyuan and Xuanzhi each trousers, jackets, and belt ornaments.
entries.literal: The next day he led his army toward the east of the city, sent the Daoist adept Daodeng into the city to bestow five hundred bolts of silk on the monks, and Qingyuan and Xuanzhi each received trousers, jackets, and belt ornaments.

entries.zh: 九年，卒。
entries.en: In the ninth year he died.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he died.

entries.zh: 詔賻錢十萬，布二百匹。
entries.en: An edict granted funeral gifts of a hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of cloth.
entries.literal: An edict granted funeral gifts of a hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of cloth.

entries.zh: 喪還，百姓緣沔水悲泣設祭，於峴山爲立祠。
entries.en: When the funeral cortege returned, the people along the Mian River wept and made offerings; a shrine was built for him on Xian Mountain.
entries.literal: When the funeral cortege returned, the common people along the Mian River wept and set out offerings; on Xian Mountain a shrine was built for him.

entries.zh: 贈侍中、衞將軍，持節、都督、刺史如故。
entries.en: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant and General of the Guard, retaining his staff of authority, overall command, and governorship.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given Palace Attendant and General of the Guard; Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief, and governor were unchanged.

entries.zh: 給鼓吹一部。
entries.en: He was granted one set of martial music.
entries.literal: He was given one set of martial music.

entries.zh: 謚昭侯。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhao.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhao.

entries.zh: 年三十七。
entries.en: He was thirty-seven.
entries.literal: He was thirty-seven.

entries.zh: 高宗少相友愛，時爲僕射，領衞尉，表求解衞尉，私第展哀，詔不許。
entries.en: Xiao Luan had loved him since they were young; at the time he was Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Commandant of the Guard; he memorialized asking to be relieved of the guard command so he could mourn at his private residence, but the edict refused.
entries.literal: Xiao Luan had been fond of him from youth; at the time he was Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and held the post of Commandant of the Guard; he memorialized asking to be relieved of the guard command to mourn at his private residence, but an edict did not permit it.

entries.zh: 每臨緬靈，輙慟哭不成聲。
entries.en: Whenever he came before Mian's coffin he would wail until he could no longer speak.
entries.literal: Whenever he came before Mian's coffin he would wail until he could not form sound.

entries.zh: 建武元年，贈侍中，司徒，安陸王，邑二千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianwu he was posthumously made Palace Attendant and Minister of Works and given the title Prince of Anlu with a fief of two thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was posthumously given Palace Attendant, Minister of Works, and the title Prince of Anlu with a fief of two thousand households.

entries.zh: 子寶晊嗣，爲持節、督湘州軍事、輔國將軍、湘州刺史。
entries.en: His son Baozhi succeeded and was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Xiang Province, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Xiang Province.
entries.literal: His son Baozhi succeeded and was made Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Xiang Province, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Xiang Province.

entries.zh: 弟寶覽爲江陵公，寶宏汝南公，邑各千五百戶。
entries.en: His younger brother Baolan was made Duke of Jiangling and Baohong Duke of Runan, each with a fief of fifteen hundred households.
entries.literal: His younger brother Baolan was Duke of Jiangling and Baohong Duke of Runan, each with a fief of fifteen hundred households.

entries.zh: 二年，寶晊進號冠軍將軍。
entries.en: In the second year Baozhi was promoted to General Who Vanquishes the Foe.
entries.literal: In the second year Baozhi was advanced to General Who Vanquishes the Foe.

entries.zh: 三年，寶宏改封宵城。
entries.en: In the third year Baohong was redesignated to Xiaocheng.
entries.literal: In the third year Baohong's enfeoffment was changed to Xiaocheng.

entries.zh: 永元元年，以安陸郡邊虜，寶晊改封湘東王。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongyuan, because Anlu Commandery bordered barbarian raiders, Baozhi was redesignated Prince of Xiangdong.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan, because Anlu Commandery bordered barbarian raiders, Baozhi's enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Xiangdong.

entries.zh: 進號征虜將軍。
entries.en: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
entries.literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

entries.zh: 二年，爲左衞將軍。
entries.en: In the second year he was made General of the Left Guard.
entries.literal: In the second year he was made General of the Left Guard.

entries.zh: 高宗兄弟一門皆尚吏事，寶晊粗好文章。
entries.en: Throughout Xiao Luan's house his brothers all valued administrative work; Baozhi had a rough liking for literary composition.
entries.literal: Xiao Luan's brothers throughout the house all valued administrative affairs; Baozhi was roughly fond of literary composition.

entries.zh: 義師下，寶晊在城內，東昏廢，寶晊望物情歸己，坐待法駕，旣而城內送首詣梁王。
entries.en: When the army of righteousness marched south, Baozhi was inside the city; after the Marquis of Donghun was deposed, Baozhi hoped popular sentiment would turn to him and sat waiting for the imperial carriage; soon afterward the city sent a head to the Prince of Liang.
entries.literal: When the army of righteousness descended, Baozhi was within the city; the Marquis of Donghun was deposed; Baozhi hoped popular sentiment would turn to him and sat waiting for the imperial carriage; soon afterward the city sent a head to the Prince of Liang.

entries.zh: 宣德太后臨朝，以寶晊爲太常。
entries.en: When the Empress Dowager of Xuande presided over the court, Baozhi was made Minister of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: When the Empress Dowager of Xuande presided over the court, Baozhi was made Minister of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 寶晊不自安，謀反，兄弟皆伏誅。
entries.en: Baozhi, ill at ease, plotted rebellion; he and his brothers were all executed.
entries.literal: Baozhi did not feel secure and plotted rebellion; the brothers all suffered execution.

entries.zh: 遙昌，永泰元年卒。
entries.en: Yaochang died in the first year of Yongtai.
entries.literal: Yaochang died in the first year of Yongtai.

entries.zh: 上愛遙昌兄弟如子，甚痛惜之。
entries.en: The emperor loved Yaochang and his brothers as his own sons and grieved for them deeply.
entries.literal: The emperor loved Yaochang and his brothers as sons and grieved for them deeply.

entries.zh: 贈車騎將軍、儀同三司。
entries.en: He was posthumously made General of the Chariots and Cavalry with privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: He was posthumously given General of the Chariots and Cavalry and privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 帝以問徐孝嗣，孝嗣曰：「豐城本資尚輕，贈以班台，如爲小過。」
entries.en: The emperor asked Xu Xiaosi, who said, "Fengcheng's original endowment was still modest; to posthumously grant him court rank would be a slight excess."
entries.literal: The emperor asked Xu Xiaosi; Xiaosi said: "Fengcheng's original endowment was still light; to posthumously give him court rank is like a small excess."

entries.zh: 帝曰：「卿乃欲存萬代准則，此我孤兄子，不得與計。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "You wish to preserve standards for ten thousand generations, but this was my orphaned elder brother's son—he cannot be reckoned by ordinary measure."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "You wish to preserve standards for ten thousand generations; this is my orphaned elder brother's son—he cannot be reckoned by measure."

entries.zh: 謚憲公。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Duke Xian.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Xian.

entries.zh: 安陸昭王緬字景業。
entries.en: Prince Mian of Anlu (posthumous title Zhao), whose courtesy name was Jingye.
entries.literal: Prince Zhao of Anlu Mian, styled Jingye.

entries.zh: 善容止。
entries.en: He was distinguished in bearing and deportment.
entries.literal: He was skilled in bearing and deportment.

entries.zh: 初爲祕書郎，宋邵陵王文學，中書郎。
entries.en: He began as Secretariat Gentleman, literary aide to the Prince of Shaoling in the Song, and secretariat gentleman.
entries.literal: He first served as Secretariat Gentleman, literary aide to the Prince of Shaoling in Song, and Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 建元元年，封安陸侯，邑千戶。
entries.en: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anlu with a fief of one thousand households.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anlu with a fief of a thousand households.

entries.zh: 轉太子中庶子，遷侍中。
entries.en: He was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and then Palace Attendant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，遷五兵尚書，領前軍將軍，仍出爲輔國將軍、吳郡太守，少時，大著風績。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was made Minister of the Five Armies and Forward General, then sent out as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Wu Commandery; in a short time he won a great reputation for his governance.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he was moved to Minister of the Five Armies, held the post of Forward General, and then went out as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Wu Commandery; in a short time he achieved great reputation for his conduct.

entries.zh: 竟陵王子良與緬書曰：「竊承下風，數十年來未有此政。」
entries.en: Prince Ziliang of Jingling wrote to Mian, "I have heard of your excellent influence from afar; in several decades there has not been such governance."
entries.literal: Prince Ziliang of Jingling wrote to Mian: "I have privately received your excellent influence; in several decades there has not been such administration."

entries.zh: 世祖嘉其能，轉持節、都督郢州司州之義陽軍事、冠軍將軍、郢州刺史，
entries.en: Emperor Wu praised his ability and made him Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Ying Province and Yiyang in Sizhou, General Who Vanquishes the Foe, and Governor of Ying Province.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu praised his ability and transferred him to Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Ying Province and Yiyang in Sizhou, General Who Vanquishes the Foe, and Governor of Ying Province.

entries.zh: 衡陽元王道度
entries.en: Prince Daodu of Hengyang (posthumous title Yuan)
entries.literal: Prince Yuan of Hengyang, Daodu

entries.zh: 慈患脚，世祖敕王晏曰：「慈在職未久，旣有微疾，不堪朝，又不能騎馬，聽乘車在仗後。」
entries.en: Ci suffered from foot ailment. Emperor Wu instructed Wang Yan: "Ci has not long held office and already has a slight illness—he cannot attend court and cannot ride horseback; permit him to ride in a carriage behind the guard."
entries.literal: Ci suffered from foot ailment; Emperor Shizu instructed Wang Yan: "Ci has not long been in office and already has a slight illness—he cannot manage court, and also cannot ride horseback; allow him to ride in a carriage behind the guard."

entries.zh: 江左來少例也。
entries.en: Such indulgence had been rare since the Eastern Jin.
entries.literal: Since the Eastern Jin such cases have been few.

entries.zh: 以疾從閑任，轉冠軍將軍、司徒左長史。
entries.en: Given lighter duties on account of illness, he was transferred to General Champion and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of State Affairs.
entries.literal: On account of illness he was given lighter duties and was transferred to General Champion and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 慈妻劉秉女。
entries.en: Ci's wife was a daughter of Liu Bing.
entries.literal: Ci's wife was a daughter of Liu Bing.

entries.zh: 子觀，尚世祖長女吳縣公主，脩婦禮，姑未嘗交答。
entries.en: His son Guan married Emperor Wu's eldest daughter, the Princess of Wuxian; observing all the rites of a daughter-in-law, he never once exchanged pleasantries with his mother-in-law.
entries.literal: His son Guan married the eldest daughter of Emperor Shizu, the Princess of Wuxian; he observed the rites of a daughter-in-law, and his mother-in-law never once exchanged replies with him.

entries.zh: 江夏王鋒爲南徐州，妃，慈女也，以慈爲冠軍將軍、東海太守，加秩中二千石，行南徐州府事。
entries.en: When the Prince of Jiangxia, Feng, held Southern Xuzhou and his consort was Ci's daughter, Ci was appointed General Champion and Administrator of Donghai, with rank of 2000 bushels, acting for the Southern Xuzhou headquarters.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Jiangxia, Feng, was assigned to Southern Xuzhou and his consort was Ci's daughter, Ci was made General Champion and Administrator of Donghai, with rank equivalent to 2000 bushels, acting for the Southern Xuzhou headquarters.

entries.zh: 還爲冠軍將軍、廬陵王中軍長史，未拜，永明九年，卒。
entries.en: He was reassigned as General Champion and Chief Clerk of the Central Army on the staff of the Prince of Luling, but before taking up the post he died in the ninth year of Yongming.
entries.literal: He returned as General Champion and Chief Clerk of the Central Army on the staff of the Prince of Luling; before taking appointment, in the ninth year of Yongming, he died.

entries.zh: 年四十一。
entries.en: He was forty-one.
entries.literal: He was forty-one years old.

entries.zh: 慧曉清介正立，不雜交游。
entries.en: Huixiao was pure, upright, and aloof from casual socializing.
entries.literal: Huixiao was pure and upright, not mixing in socializing.

entries.zh: 會稽內史同郡張暢見慧曉童幼，便嘉異之。
entries.en: Zhang Chang, Interior Administrator of Kuaiji and a fellow native, saw Huixiao as a child and immediately marked him out as exceptional.
entries.literal: Zhang Chang, Interior Administrator of Kuaiji and a man of the same commandery, saw Huixiao in childhood and at once admired him as extraordinary.

entries.zh: 張緒稱之曰：「江東裴、樂也。」
entries.en: Zhang Xu praised him, saying: "He is the Pei and Yue of the Jiangdong."
entries.literal: Zhang Xu praised him saying: "The Pei and Yue of the Jiangdong."

entries.zh: 初應州郡辟，舉秀才，衞尉史，歷諸府行參軍。
entries.en: He first answered summonses from the provinces and commanderies, was nominated as Cultivated Talent, served as clerk to the Commandant of the Guard, and held various acting military aide posts on princes' staffs.
entries.literal: At first he responded to provincial and commandery summonses, was nominated as Cultivated Talent, served as Clerk to the Commandant of the Guard, and passed through various headquarters as acting military aide.

entries.zh: 以母老還家侍養，十餘年不仕。
entries.en: When his mother grew old he returned home to care for her and did not hold office for more than ten years.
entries.literal: Because his mother was old he returned home to serve and support her, and for more than ten years did not take office.

entries.zh: 太祖輔政，除爲尚書殿中郎。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor assumed the regency, Huixiao was appointed Clerk in the Palace Division of the Ministry of State Affairs.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor assisted in government, he was appointed Clerk in the Palace Division of the Ministry of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 隣族來相賀，慧曉舉酒曰：「陸慧曉年踰三十，婦父領選，始作尚書郎，卿輩乃復以爲慶邪？」
entries.en: Neighbors came to congratulate him. Huixiao raised his cup and said: "Lu Huixiao is past thirty, his father-in-law runs personnel appointments, and he has only just become a Clerk in the Ministry of State Affairs—and you still call this worth celebrating?"
entries.literal: Neighbors came to congratulate him; Huixiao raised his cup and said: "Lu Huixiao, past thirty, with his father-in-law in charge of appointments, only now becoming a Clerk in the Ministry of State Affairs—and you still take this as celebration?"

entries.zh: 廬江何點薦慧曉於豫章王嶷，補司空掾，加以恩禮。
entries.en: He Dian of Lujiang recommended Huixiao to the Prince of Yuzhang, Yi, who appointed him aide on the staff of the Minister of Works and treated him with special favor.
entries.literal: He Dian of Lujiang recommended Huixiao to the Prince of Yuzhang, Yi; he was appointed aide to the Minister of Works and accorded favor and ceremony.

entries.zh: 轉長沙王鎮軍諮議參軍。
entries.en: He was transferred to advisory military aide on the staff of the Prince of Changsha as General Guarding the Army.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Advisory Military Aide on the staff of the Prince of Changsha as General Guarding the Army.

entries.zh: 安陸侯緬爲吳郡，復禮異慧曉，慧曉求補緬府諮議參軍。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Anlu, Mian, held Wu commandery, he again showed Huixiao exceptional courtesy, and Huixiao asked to serve as advisory military aide on his staff.
entries.literal: When the Marquis of Anlu, Mian, was assigned to Wu commandery, he again treated Huixiao with special courtesy; Huixiao requested appointment as advisory military aide on Mian's staff.

entries.zh: 遷始興王前將軍安西諮議，領冠軍錄事參軍，轉司徒從事中郎，遷右長史。
entries.en: He was transferred to advisory officer on the staff of the Prince of Shixing as Forward General and General Pacifying the West, concurrently as Recorder on the staff of the Champion, then Attendant of the Minister of State Affairs, and finally Right Chief Clerk.
entries.literal: He was transferred to advisory officer under the Prince of Shixing as Forward General and General Pacifying the West, concurrently Recorder on the staff of the Champion; transferred to Attendant of the Minister of State Affairs, then transferred to Right Chief Clerk.

entries.zh: 時陳郡謝朏爲左長史，府公竟陵王子良謂王融曰：「我府二上佐，求之前世，誰可爲比？」
entries.en: At the time Xie Tiao of Chen served as Left Chief Clerk; the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, said to Wang Rong: "My headquarters' two senior aides—searching through past ages, with whom can they be compared?"
entries.literal: At the time Xie Tiao of Chen commandery was Left Chief Clerk; the Prince of the headquarters, the Prince of Jingling, Ziliang, said to Wang Rong: "My headquarters' two senior aides—searching through past ages, with whom can they be compared?"

entries.zh: 融曰：「兩賢同時，便是未有前例。」
entries.en: Wang Rong replied: "Two such worthies serving together—that in itself has no precedent."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Two worthies at once—that in itself has no precedent."

entries.zh: 子良於西邸抄書，令慧曉參知其事。
entries.en: Ziliang had books copied at the Western Lodge and put Huixiao in charge of overseeing the work.
entries.literal: Ziliang had books copied at the Western Lodge and had Huixiao assist in overseeing the matter.

entries.zh: 建武初，除西中郎長史，行事、內史如故。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jianwu he was appointed Chief Clerk of the General of the Right Division, retaining his acting authority and post as Interior Administrator.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the General of the Right Division, with acting authority and Interior Administrator as before.

entries.zh: 俄徵黃門郎，未拜，遷吏部郎。
entries.en: He was soon summoned as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, but before taking up the appointment he was transferred to Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: Soon summoned as Gentleman at the Yellow Gates; before taking appointment, transferred to Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 尚書令王晏選門生補內外要局，慧曉爲用數人而止，晏恨之。
entries.en: Wang Yan, Minister Director of State Affairs, wanted his disciples appointed to key posts throughout the government; Huixiao appointed only a few and stopped, and Yan resented him for it.
entries.literal: Wang Yan, Minister Director of State Affairs, selected his disciples to fill key posts inside and outside; Huixiao used only a few and stopped—Yan resented this.

entries.zh: 送女妓一人，欲與申好，慧曉不納。
entries.en: Yan sent him a female entertainer hoping to win his favor, but Huixiao refused the gift.
entries.literal: Yan sent one female entertainer, wishing to establish goodwill; Huixiao did not accept.

entries.zh: 吏曹都令史歷政以來，諮執選事，慧曉任己獨行，未嘗與語。
entries.en: Under previous administrations the Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel had controlled appointments through consultation; Huixiao exercised his own judgment independently and never once spoke with him.
entries.literal: The Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel under successive administrations had handled selection matters through consultation—but Huixiao acted by his own judgment independently and never once spoke with him.

entries.zh: 帝遣左右單景雋以事誚問，慧曉謂景雋曰：「六十之年，不復能諮都令史爲吏部郎也。
entries.en: The emperor sent his attendant Shan Jingjun to question him about the matter. Huixiao told Jingjun: "At sixty, I am not about to consult the Chief Clerk in order to serve as Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.
entries.literal: The emperor sent his attendant Shan Jingjun to reprove him on the matter; Huixiao said to Jingjun: "At the age of sixty, I can no longer consult the Chief Clerk in order to serve as Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 上若謂身不堪，便當拂衣而退。」
entries.en: If Your Majesty deems me unfit for the post, I shall shake out my robes and resign at once."
entries.literal: If Your Majesty holds that I am unfit, then I should shake out my robes and withdraw."

entries.zh: 帝甚憚之。
entries.en: The emperor was deeply intimidated by him.
entries.literal: The emperor greatly feared him.

entries.zh: 後欲用爲侍中，以形短小，乃止。
entries.en: Later the throne wished to appoint him Attendant-in-Ordinary, but his short stature caused them to reconsider.
entries.literal: Later they wished to appoint him Attendant-in-Ordinary, but because his stature was short, they stopped.

entries.zh: 出爲輔國將軍、晉安王鎮北司馬、征北長史、東海太守，行府州事。
entries.en: He was sent out as General Assisting the State, Army Administrator on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an as General Guarding the North, Chief Clerk Campaigning North, and Administrator of Donghai, acting for both the princely headquarters and the province.
entries.literal: He went out as General Assisting the State, Army Administrator on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an as General Guarding the North, Chief Clerk Campaigning North, Administrator of Donghai, acting for headquarters and province.

entries.zh: 入爲五兵尚書，行揚州事。
entries.en: He was recalled as Minister of the Five Divisions and acting governor of Yang province.
entries.literal: He entered as Minister of War Five Divisions, acting for Yangzhou.

entries.zh: 崔惠景事平，領右軍將軍，出監南徐州，少時，仍遷持節、督南兖兖徐青冀五州軍事、輔國將軍、南兖州刺史。
entries.en: After Cui Huijing's revolt was suppressed, he was additionally appointed General of the Right Army and sent to oversee Southern Xuzhou; soon after he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs in Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Assisting the State, and Inspector of Southern Yan province.
entries.literal: When the affair of Cui Huijing was settled, he additionally held General of the Right Army, went out to oversee Southern Xuzhou; before long he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Supervisor of military affairs of the five provinces Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Assisting the State, and Inspector of Southern Yanzhou.

entries.zh: 至鎮俄爾，以疾歸，卒。
entries.en: He had barely reached his post when illness forced him to return; he died soon after.
entries.literal: Having reached his post only briefly, he returned on account of illness and died.

entries.zh: 年六十二。
entries.en: He was sixty-two.
entries.literal: He was sixty-two years old.

entries.zh: 贈太常。
entries.en: He was posthumously appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies.
entries.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷四十六‧列傳第二十七
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 46 · Biographies 27
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 46, Biographies 27

entries.zh: 王融
entries.en: Wang Rong
entries.literal: Wang Rong

entries.zh: 王融字元長，琅邪臨沂人也。
entries.en: Wang Rong, whose style name was Yuanchang, was a native of Linyi in Langya.
entries.literal: Wang Rong, style name Yuanchang, was a native of Langya commandery in Linyi.

entries.zh: 祖僧達，中書令，曾高竝台輔。
entries.en: His grandfather Wang Sengda had held the post of Secretary Grand Director, and for generations his family had produced ministers at the highest level.
entries.literal: His grandfather Wang Sengda was Secretary Grand Director; his forebears for several generations together had served as director-level ministers.

entries.zh: 僧達答宋孝武云：「亡父亡祖，司徒司空。」
entries.en: When Sengda replied to Emperor Xiaowu of Song, he said, "My deceased father and grandfather were Chamberlain and Minister of Works."
entries.literal: Sengda answered Emperor Xiaowu of Song, saying, "My late father and late grandfather were Chamberlain and Minister of Works."

entries.zh: 父道琰，廬陵內史。
entries.en: His father Wang Daoyan had been Interior Governor of Luling.
entries.literal: His father Wang Daoyan was Interior Governor of Luling.

entries.zh: 母臨川太守謝惠宣女，惇敏婦人也。
entries.en: His mother was the daughter of Linchuan Administrator Xie Huixuan, a conscientious and capable woman.
entries.literal: His mother was the daughter of Administrator of Linchuan Xie Huixuan, a woman of sincere and quick intelligence.

entries.zh: 教融書學。
entries.en: She personally taught Rong to read and write.
entries.literal: She taught Rong reading and writing.

entries.zh: 融少而神明警惠，博涉有文才。
entries.en: Even as a boy, Rong was exceptionally quick-witted, widely read, and gifted as a writer.
entries.literal: Rong in youth was bright and alert, broadly learned and possessed of literary talent.

entries.zh: 舉秀才。
entries.en: He was nominated as a provincial graduate.
entries.literal: He was recommended as a Cultivated Talent.

entries.zh: 晉安王南中郎板行參軍，坐公事免。
entries.en: He was appointed Acting Aide on the staff of the Prince of Jin'an as Southern Commander-in-Chief, but lost the post over a bureaucratic infraction.
entries.literal: He served as Acting Aide in the Southern Staff of the Prince of Jin'an, and was dismissed for an official offense.

entries.zh: 竟陵王司徒板法曹行參軍，遷太子舍人。
entries.en: The Prince of Jingling in his capacity as Grand Minister made him Acting Aide in the Law Section, after which he rose to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
entries.literal: The Prince of Jingling, as Grand Minister, appointed him Acting Aide in the Law Section; he was promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

entries.zh: 融以父官不通，弱年便欲紹興家業，啓世祖求自試。
entries.en: Since his father's career had stalled, Rong even in his youth wanted to restore the family's fortunes and petitioned Emperor Wu to let him prove himself.
entries.literal: Because his father's official career had not prospered, Rong while still young wished to revive the family standing and memorialized Emperor Wu to request a trial of his abilities.

entries.zh: 曰：「臣聞春庚秋蟀，集候相悲，露木風榮，臨年共悅。
entries.en: He wrote: "I have heard that in spring the fifth-month cicada and in autumn the cricket, when the seasons turn, grieve in sympathy; trees bright with dew and wind put forth their glory, and as the year closes all creation shares its joy.
entries.literal: He said: "Your subject has heard that in spring the cicada of the fifth month and in autumn the cricket, when the seasons gather, mourn one another; trees touched by dew and wind flourish, and as the year draws near they rejoice together.

entries.zh: 夫唯動植，且或有心；
entries.en: If even plants and animals can feel,
entries.literal: Even among moving things and plants there is sometimes feeling;

entries.zh: 況在生靈，而能無感。
entries.en: how could a human being remain unmoved?
entries.literal: how much more among living beings could there be no response.

entries.zh: 臣自奉望宮闕，沐浴恩私，拔迹庸虛，參名盛列，纓劔紫復，趨步丹墀，歲時歸來，誇榮邑里。
entries.en: Since I first beheld the imperial precincts and received your personal grace, I was raised from obscurity into the company of the great, belted in purple with sword at my side, walking the vermilion court; each year when I returned home I could boast of honor in my town.
entries.literal: Your subject, since gazing upon the palace towers and bathing in private favor, was lifted from mediocrity to join the ranks of the eminent, girded with purple sash and sword, pacing the vermilion steps; when the seasons turned and he returned home, he boasted of glory in his native place.

entries.zh: 然無懃而官，昔賢曾議；
entries.en: Yet to hold office without real effort—men of old debated that very point;
entries.literal: Yet to hold office without diligence—former worthies debated this;

entries.zh: 不任而祿，有識必譏。
entries.en: to draw salary without performing one's duties—anyone with sense is bound to scorn it.
entries.literal: to receive salary without fulfilling one's charge—those with understanding surely deride it.

entries.zh: 臣所用慷慨憤懣，不遑自晏。
entries.en: That is why I burn with shame and indignation and cannot rest at ease.
entries.literal: For this reason your subject is stirred to generous indignation and has no leisure for ease.

entries.zh: 誠以深恩鮮報，聖主難逢，蒲柳先秋，光陰不待，貪及明時，展悉愚效，以酬陛下不世之仁。
entries.en: Deep grace is seldom repaid, and a sage sovereign is rarely met; like a willow that yellows before autumn, time will not wait—I mean to seize this bright hour and offer whatever poor service I can in return for your unparalleled benevolence.
entries.literal: Truly deep favor is rarely repaid, a sage ruler is hard to meet; the willow withers before autumn, time does not wait—I would greedily seize this bright season and display whatever feeble service I have, to repay Your Majesty's unexampled kindness.

entries.zh: 若微誠獲信，短才見序，文武吏法，唯所施用。
entries.en: If my small sincerity wins your trust and my modest talent is put to use, in civil affairs, military affairs, or the laws of office—employ me as you will.
entries.literal: If this slight sincerity wins trust and my limited talent is given rank, whether in civil, military, or administrative law, I will apply myself as you command.

entries.zh: 夫君道含弘，臣術無隱，翁歸乃居中自是，充國曰『莫若老臣』。
entries.en: The ruler's way is all-embracing, and a minister should conceal nothing: Weng Gui sat in the middle and decided cases himself, and Zhao Chongguo said, 'None better than your old servant.'
entries.literal: For the ruler's way is broad and embracing, and the minister's craft should hide nothing: Weng Gui judged cases from his central seat, and Zhao Chongguo said, 'None better than this old minister.'

entries.zh: 竊景前脩，敢蹈輕節。
entries.en: Taking those earlier models as my guide, I venture this presumptuous request.
entries.literal: Secretly taking the former exemplars as my mirror, I dare tread this light step.

entries.zh: 以冒不媒之鄙，式罄奉公之誠。
entries.en: Though I offend with this uninvited forwardness, I offer the whole of my loyalty to the state.
entries.literal: Though I offend with this uninvited baseness, I would fully exhaust my loyalty in public service.

entries.zh: 抑又唐堯在上，不參二八，管夷吾恥之，臣亦恥之。
entries.en: Moreover, when Emperor Yao sat above, he did not consult his Eight and his Two; Guan Zhong found that shameful, and so do I.
entries.literal: Moreover, when Tang Yao ruled above, he did not consult the Eight and the Two; Guan Zhong was ashamed of that, and your subject is ashamed as well.

entries.zh: 願陛下裁覽。」
entries.en: I beg Your Majesty to consider this petition."
entries.literal: I beg Your Majesty to judge and review."

entries.zh: 遷祕書丞。
entries.en: He was promoted to Secretary Assistant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Secretary Assistant.

entries.zh: 九年，上幸芳林園禊宴朝臣，使融爲《曲水詩序》，文藻富麗，當世稱之。
entries.en: In the ninth year the emperor held the spring purification feast for his ministers at Fanglin Garden and had Rong write the "Preface to the Winding Water Poems"; its prose was rich and splendid, and contemporaries praised it.
entries.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor visited Fanglin Garden for the spring purification feast with his courtiers and had Rong compose the "Preface to the Winding Water Poems"; the literary ornament was rich and beautiful, and the age praised it.

entries.zh: 會虜動，竟陵王子良於東府募人，板融寧朔將軍、軍主。
entries.en: When the barbarians stirred, the Prince of Jingling recruited men at the Eastern Mansion and appointed Rong General Who Pacifies the North and army commander.
entries.literal: When the barbarians stirred, the Prince of Jingling Ziliang recruited men at the Eastern Mansion and appointed Rong General Who Pacifies the North and Army Commander.

entries.zh: 融文辭辯捷，尤善倉卒屬綴，有所造作，援筆可待。
entries.en: Rong was eloquent and quick with words, especially skilled at composing on the spur of the moment—whatever he wrote, he could take up the brush and finish at once.
entries.literal: Rong's literary style was eloquent and quick; he was especially skilled at composing on the spur of the moment—whatever he wrote, he could take up the brush and wait no longer.

entries.zh: 子良特相友好，情分殊常。
entries.en: Ziliang was especially close to him; their bond was unlike any other.
entries.literal: Ziliang was especially friendly with him; their bond was unlike the ordinary.

entries.zh: 晚節大習騎馬。
entries.en: In his later years he trained hard in horsemanship.
entries.literal: In his later years he greatly practiced horsemanship.

entries.zh: 才地旣華，兼藉子良之勢，傾意賔客，勞問周款，文武翕習輻湊之。
entries.en: His talent and birth were already splendid, and with Ziliang's backing he lavished attention on guests; civil and military men flocked to him like spokes to a hub.
entries.literal: His talent and standing being already splendid, and additionally relying on Ziliang's power, he poured out favor on guests, laboring in inquiry with full cordiality; civil and military men accustomed to him converged like wheel spokes.

entries.zh: 招集江西傖楚數百人，竝有幹用。
entries.en: He recruited several hundred tough men from Jiangxi and Chu, all capable and useful.
entries.literal: He recruited several hundred Jiangxi and Chu bondsmen, all capable and useful.

entries.zh: 從叔儉，初有儀同之授，融贈詩及書，儉甚奇憚之，笑謂人曰：「穰侯印詎便可解？」
entries.en: His cousin Wang Jian had just been granted the rank Peer Equal to the Three Dukes; Rong sent him poems and letters, and Jian was both impressed and alarmed, remarking with a smile, "Does the seal of the Marquis of Rang come off that easily?"
entries.literal: His cousin Wang Jian had just received the title of Peer Equal to the Three Dukes; Rong sent him poems and letters, and Jian was greatly struck and wary of him, smiling and saying to others, "Can the seal of the Marquis of Rang be so easily taken away?"

entries.zh: 尋遷丹陽丞，中書郎。
entries.en: Before long he was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Secretariat Gentleman.
entries.literal: Soon he was transferred to Assistant Magistrate of Danyang and Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat.

entries.zh: 虜使遣求書，朝議欲不與。
entries.en: Northern Wei envoys asked for books, and the court debate favored denying them.
entries.literal: The barbarian envoys sent to request books, and court discussion inclined toward refusal.

entries.zh: 融上疏曰：
entries.en: Rong submitted a memorial that read:
entries.literal: Rong submitted a memorial, saying:

entries.zh: 融被收，朋友部曲參問北寺，相繼於道。
entries.en: When Rong was arrested, friends and retainers came in succession to inquire at North Temple along the road.
entries.literal: When Rong was arrested, friends and retainers came to inquire at North Temple, succeeding one another on the road.

entries.zh: 融請救於子良，子良憂懼不敢救。
entries.en: Rong begged Ziliang to save him, but Ziliang was too afraid to intervene.
entries.literal: Rong begged Ziliang to save him; Ziliang was anxious and afraid and did not dare save him.

entries.zh: 融文集行於世。
entries.en: Rong's collected writings circulated in his time.
entries.literal: Rong's collected writings circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 永明末，世祖欲北伐，使毛惠秀畫《漢武北伐圖》，使融掌其事。
entries.en: At the end of the Yongming era Emperor Wu planned a northern campaign and commissioned Mao Huixiu to paint "Emperor Wu of Han's Northern Expedition," putting Rong in charge of the project.
entries.literal: At the end of the Yongming era Emperor Wu wished to campaign north and had Mao Huixiu paint "Emperor Wu of Han's Northern Campaign"; he put Rong in charge of the matter.

entries.zh: 融好功名，因此上疏曰：
entries.en: Rong craved fame and used the occasion to submit a memorial:
entries.literal: Rong loved fame and achievement and therefore submitted a memorial, saying:

entries.zh: 上以融才辯，十一年，使兼主客，接虜使房景高、宋弁。
entries.en: Because the emperor valued Rong's eloquence, in the eleventh year he made him also Director of Guests to receive the Northern Wei envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.
entries.literal: Because the Emperor valued Rong's talent and eloquence, in the eleventh year he had him additionally serve as Director of Guests and receive the barbarian envoys Fang Jinggao and Song Bian.

entries.zh: 弁見融年少，問主客年幾？
entries.en: Bian saw that Rong was young and asked how old the Director of Guests was.
entries.literal: Bian saw that Rong was young and asked how old the Director of Guests was.

entries.zh: 融曰：「五十之年，久踰其半。」
entries.en: Rong said, "Of fifty years, I have long since passed the halfway mark."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Of fifty years, I have long passed the half."

entries.zh: 因問：「在朝聞主客作《曲水詩序》。」
entries.en: He then asked, "At court I heard that the Director of Guests wrote the 'Preface to the Winding Water Poems.'"
entries.literal: He then asked: "At court I heard that the Director of Guests composed the 'Preface to the Winding Water Poems.'"

entries.zh: 景高又云：「在北聞主客此制，勝於顏延年，實願一見。」
entries.en: Jinggao added, "In the north I heard that the Director of Guests wrote this piece, surpassing Yan Yanzhi—I would truly like to see it."
entries.literal: Jinggao also said: "In the north I heard that the Director of Guests composed this piece, surpassing Yan Yanzhi—I truly wish to see it."

entries.zh: 融乃示之。
entries.en: Rong then showed it to him.
entries.literal: Rong then showed it to him.

entries.zh: 後日，宋弁於瑤池堂謂融曰：「昔觀相如《封禪》，以知漢武之德；
entries.en: A few days later Song Bian said to Rong at Yaochi Hall, "When I once read Sima Xiangru's 'Feng and Shan,' I learned Emperor Wu of Han's virtue;
entries.literal: Some days later, Song Bian at Yaochi Hall said to Rong: "Formerly, reading Sima Xiangru's 'Feng and Shan,' I came to know Emperor Wu of Han's virtue;

entries.zh: 今覽王生《詩序》，用見齊王之盛。」
entries.en: now reading your 'Poem Preface,' I see the splendor of the Prince of Qi."
entries.literal: now reading Master Wang's 'Poem Preface,' thereby I see the Prince of Qi's splendor."

entries.zh: 融曰：「皇家盛明，豈直比蹤漢武；
entries.en: Rong said, "The imperial house is radiant—how could it be compared only with Emperor Wu of Han;
entries.literal: Rong said: "The imperial house is splendid and bright—how could it merely be compared in trace to Emperor Wu of Han;

entries.zh: 更慚鄙製，無以遠匹相如。」
entries.en: and I am ashamed that my humble piece cannot remotely match Xiangru."
entries.literal: I am all the more ashamed of my base composition, unable to match Xiangru from afar."

entries.zh: 上以虜獻馬不稱，使融問曰：「秦西冀北，實多駿驥。
entries.en: Because the horses the barbarians presented were unworthy, the emperor had Rong ask, "West of Qin and north of Ji have many fine steeds.
entries.literal: Because the barbarians' presented horses were unworthy, the Emperor had Rong ask: "West of Qin and north of Ji truly have many fine steeds.

entries.zh: 而魏主所獻良馬，乃駑駘之不若。
entries.en: Yet the fine horses your Wei ruler presented are worse than common nags.
entries.literal: Yet the fine horses presented by the Wei ruler are not even equal to nags.

entries.zh: 求名檢事，殊爲未孚。
entries.en: To seek a good name while the facts fail to match is hardly convincing.
entries.literal: Seeking reputation while checking the facts, this is especially unconvincing.

entries.zh: 將旦旦信誓，有時而爽，駉駉之牧，不能復嗣？」
entries.en: Will sworn faith given morning after morning sometimes be broken, and the sleek herds never be matched again?"
entries.literal: Will daily sworn faith at times be broken, and the herds of sleek horses not be succeeded again?"

entries.zh: 宋弁曰：「不容虛偽之名，當是不習土地。」
entries.en: Song Bian said, "A false reputation will not stand—probably they are unaccustomed to the terrain here."
entries.literal: Song Bian said: "It cannot bear a false reputation—probably they are unaccustomed to the terrain."

entries.zh: 融曰：「周穆馬迹徧於天下，若騏驥之性，因地而遷，則造父之策，有時而躓。」
entries.en: Rong said, "King Mu of Zhou's horses ranged over all the world; if fine steeds change with the land, then even Zaofu's skill would sometimes fail."
entries.literal: Rong said: "King Mu of Zhou's horse tracks ranged over all under heaven; if the nature of qiji steeds shifts with the land, then Zaofu's strategies would sometimes stumble."

entries.zh: 弁曰：「王主客何爲懃懃於千里？」
entries.en: Bian said, "Why is Director Wang so eager about a thousand-li horse?"
entries.literal: Bian said: "Why is Director Wang so earnest about a thousand li?"

entries.zh: 融曰：「卿國旣異其優劣，聊復相訪。
entries.en: Rong said, "Since your state already admits they differ in quality, I am simply asking again.
entries.literal: Rong said: "Your state already differs in their excellence and inferiority—I merely inquire again.

entries.zh: 若千里日至，聖上當駕鼓車。」
entries.en: If a thousand-li horse arrives within a day, the emperor will drive the drum carriage to meet it."
entries.literal: If a thousand-li horse arrives within the day, the Sage Emperor will drive the drum carriage."

entries.zh: 弁曰：「向意旣須，必不能駕鼓車也。」
entries.en: Bian said, "Since you already wanted one, he surely will not drive the drum carriage."
entries.literal: Bian said: "Since the intent was already required, he surely cannot drive the drum carriage."

entries.zh: 融曰：「買死馬之骨，亦以郭隗之故。」
entries.en: Rong said, "Buying the bones of a dead horse was also for Guo Wei's sake."
entries.literal: Rong said: "Buying the bones of a dead horse was also because of Guo Wei."

entries.zh: 弁不能答。
entries.en: Bian had no answer.
entries.literal: Bian could not reply.

entries.zh: 世祖疾篤暫絕，子良在殿內，太孫未入，融戎服絳衫，於中書省閤口斷東宮仗不得進，欲立子良。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu was gravely ill and briefly lost consciousness, Ziliang was in the hall and the heir apparent had not yet entered; Rong in military dress and scarlet shirt blocked the Eastern Palace guards at the Secretariat gate, intending to make Ziliang emperor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu was gravely ill and briefly lost consciousness, Ziliang was inside the hall and the Heir Apparent had not yet entered; Rong in military dress and scarlet shirt at the Secretariat gate cut off the Eastern Palace guards from entering, wishing to establish Ziliang.

entries.zh: 上旣蘇，太孫入殿，朝事委高宗。
entries.en: When the emperor revived, the heir apparent entered the hall and court affairs were entrusted to the High Ancestor Xiao Luan.
entries.literal: When the Emperor revived, the Heir Apparent entered the hall and court affairs were entrusted to the High Ancestor.

entries.zh: 融知子良不得立，乃釋服還省。
entries.en: Rong knew Ziliang could not take the throne, removed his military dress, and returned to his office.
entries.literal: Rong knew Ziliang could not be established and then removed his military dress and returned to his office.

entries.zh: 歎曰：「公誤我。」
entries.en: He sighed, "You misled me."
entries.literal: He sighed: "My lord misled me."

entries.zh: 鬱林深忿疾融，卽位十餘日，收下廷尉獄，然後使中丞孔稚珪倚爲奏曰：「融姿性剛險，立身浮競，動迹驚羣，抗言異類。
entries.en: Emperor Yulin deeply hated Rong; within a fortnight of his accession he had Rong imprisoned by the Minister of Justice, then had Censor Kong Zhigui draft the charge: "Rong's nature is harsh and treacherous, his conduct restless and competitive; his actions alarm the court and his words oppose his peers.
entries.literal: Emperor Yulin deeply resented Rong; within ten-odd days of his accession he had him taken to the Minister of Justice prison, then had Censor Kong Zhigui draft the accusation, saying: "Rong's nature is harsh and dangerous, his conduct floating and competitive; his movements startle the crowd and his words oppose his kind.

entries.zh: 近塞外微塵，苦求將領，遂招納不逞，扇誘荒傖。
entries.en: When slight trouble stirred beyond the frontier he eagerly sought command and recruited unruly men, stirring up wild bondsmen.
entries.literal: Recently beyond the frontier slight dust stirred; he bitterly sought commanders and thus recruited unruly men, inciting and seducing wild bondsmen.

entries.zh: 狡筭聲勢，專行權利，反覆脣齒之閒，傾動頰舌之內。
entries.en: He cunningly built his reputation, monopolized power, and with words back and forth stirred up trouble within the court.
entries.literal: Cunning in calculating reputation, monopolizing power and profit, turning back and forth between lips and teeth, overturning within cheeks and tongues.

entries.zh: 威福自己，無所忌憚，誹謗朝政，歷毀王公，謂己才流，無所推下，事曝遠近，使融依源據答。」
entries.en: He wielded power as he pleased, feared nothing, slandered the government, repeatedly defamed princes and dukes, and claimed no one matched his talent; when the matter became known far and wide, Rong was made to answer each charge in turn."
entries.literal: Authority and blessing from himself, nothing feared or dreaded; slandering court governance, repeatedly defaming princes and dukes, claiming his talent flowed with none below him; the matter exposed near and far—he had Rong answer point by point according to the sources."

entries.zh: 融辭曰：「囚寔頑蔽，觸行多諐，但夙忝門素，得奉教君子。
entries.en: Rong replied, "I am truly dull and often err in conduct, yet from childhood I have disgraced a noble house and was taught by gentlemen.
entries.literal: Rong replied: "The prisoner is truly stubborn and blind, and in conduct often errs; yet from old I have disgraced my family's standing and was able to receive instruction from gentlemen.

entries.zh: 爰自總髮，迄將立年，州閭郷黨，見許愚慎，朝廷衣冠，謂無舋咎。
entries.en: From childhood until near my coming of age, neighbors regarded me as cautious, and at court they said I had given no offense.
entries.literal: From tying my hair until nearly the standing year, in district and village I was regarded as foolishly cautious; among court caps and robes they said I had no fault.

entries.zh: 過蒙大行皇帝獎育之恩，又荷文皇帝識擢之重，司徒公賜預士林，安陸王曲垂眄接。
entries.en: I received the late emperor's grace in nurturing me, again the late emperor's favor in promoting me; the Grand Minister admitted me to the scholars, and the Prince of Anlu showed me special regard.
entries.literal: I excessively received the late emperor's grace in nurturing and fostering, again bore the late emperor's weight in recognizing and promoting me; the Grand Minister granted me place in the forest of scholars, the Prince of Anlu bent to bestow his glance and reception.

entries.zh: 旣身被國慈，必欲以死自效，前後陳伐虜之計，亦仰簡先朝。
entries.en: Having received the state's kindness, I wished to repay it with my life; again and again I presented plans against the barbarians, as the former court approved.
entries.literal: Having received the state's kindness on my person, I surely wished to repay with death; before and after I presented plans for campaigning against the barbarians, also looking up to the former court's selection.

entries.zh: 今假犬羊乍擾，紀僧真奉宣先敕，賜語北邊動靜，令囚草撰符詔，于時卽因啓聞，希侍鑾輿。
entries.en: When the barbarians stirred, Ji Sengzhen announced the prior edict and told me of northern movements; I was ordered to draft edicts and at once memorialized, hoping to attend the imperial carriage.
entries.literal: Now under pretense that dogs and sheep suddenly stirred, Ji Sengzhen announced the prior edict, bestowing words on northern movements; the prisoner was ordered to draft talisman edicts, and at that time through memorial sought to attend the imperial carriage.

entries.zh: 及司徒宣敕招募，同例非一，實以戎事不小，不敢承教。
entries.en: When the Grand Minister ordered recruitment, others were treated the same; truly because military affairs were grave, I did not dare refuse.
entries.literal: When the Grand Minister announced an edict to recruit, there were not a few of the same category; truly because military affairs were not small, I did not dare accept the instruction.

entries.zh: 續蒙軍號，賜使招集，銜敕而行，非敢虛扇。
entries.en: I then received a military title and was ordered to recruit; I acted under edict and did not dare stir up trouble on my own.
entries.literal: I continued to receive a military title and was granted commission to recruit; bearing the edict I acted—not daring to stir up emptily.

entries.zh: 且格取亡叛，不限傖楚，『狡笇聲勢』，應有形迹。
entries.en: Moreover, seizing fugitives and rebels was not limited to Chu men; 'cunning reputation-building' should leave visible traces.
entries.literal: Moreover, seizing fugitives and rebels was not limited to Chu bondsmen; 'cunning in calculating reputation' should have visible traces.

entries.zh: 『專行權利』，又無贓賄。
entries.en: 'Monopolizing power'—again there is no bribery.
entries.literal: 'Monopolizing power and profit'—again there is no bribe or theft.

entries.zh: 『反覆脣齒之間』，未審悉與誰言？
entries.en: 'Turning back and forth in words'—with whom exactly did I speak?
entries.literal: 'Turning back and forth between lips and teeth'—I do not yet know fully with whom I spoke?

entries.zh: 『傾動頰舌之內』，不容都無主此。
entries.en: 'Stirring trouble within the court'—surely there must be witnesses.
entries.literal: 'Overturning within cheeks and tongues'—it cannot be that there is altogether no master of this.

entries.zh: 但聖主膺教，實所沐浴，自上《甘露頌》及《銀甕啓》、《三日詩序》、《接虜使語辭》，竭思稱揚，得非『誹謗』？
entries.en: But I bathed in the sage ruler's teaching; from the 'Ode to Sweet Dew' and 'Silver Urn Memorial' to the 'Three-Day Poem Preface' and 'Words on Receiving Barbarian Envoys' I exhausted myself in praise—how is that 'slander'?
entries.literal: But the sage ruler received the teaching—I truly bathed in it; from above the 'Ode to Sweet Dew' and 'Silver Urn Memorial,' the 'Three-Day Poem Preface,' and 'Words on Receiving Barbarian Envoys'—exhausting thought in praise—how could this be 'slander'?

entries.zh: 且王公百司，唯賢是與，高下之敬，等秩有差，不敢踰濫，豈應『訾毀』？
entries.en: Among princes and the hundred offices, only the worthy are advanced; ranks differ in honor—I did not dare overstep; how could I 'revile' them?
entries.literal: Moreover, among princes, dukes, and the hundred offices, only the worthy are given place; respect high and low, ranks have differences—I did not dare exceed or overflow; how could I 'revile and destroy'?

entries.zh: 囚才分本劣，謬被策用，悚怍之情，夙宵兢惕，未嘗誇示里閭，彰曝遠邇，自循自省，竝愧流言。
entries.en: My talent was always inferior and I was wrongly employed; I have been fearful day and night, never boasting in my village or exposing myself far and wide; examining myself, I am ashamed of rumor.
entries.literal: The prisoner's talent and share were originally inferior, wrongly selected for use; a fearful and ashamed feeling, from early to night vigilant and cautious—I never boasted to village and lane, exposed near and far; examining myself, I am together ashamed of floating words.

entries.zh: 良由緣淺寡虞，致貽囂謗。
entries.en: Truly because my ties were shallow and I lacked foresight, I brought clamor and slander upon myself.
entries.literal: Truly because my ties were shallow and I lacked foresight, I caused clamorous slander to be left behind.

entries.zh: 伏惟明皇臨宇，普天蒙澤，戊寅赦恩，輕重必宥。
entries.en: I consider that the bright emperor rules the realm and all heaven receives his grace; the wuyin amnesty must pardon both light and heavy offenses.
entries.literal: Bowingly considering that the bright emperor rules the realm, all heaven receives his grace; the wuyin amnesty, light and heavy must be pardoned.

entries.zh: 百日曠期，始蒙旬日，一介罪身，獨嬰憲劾。
entries.en: The hundred-day grace period had only just begun its ten-day window, yet I alone, a single guilty man, bear punishment.
entries.literal: A hundred days of broad grace, I received only ten days at the start—a single body of guilt, alone bearing punishment.

entries.zh: 若事實有徵，爰對有在，九死之日，無恨泉壤。」
entries.en: If the facts are proved, answers can be given; on the day I die nine deaths over, I will have no regret in the grave."
entries.literal: If the facts have proof, there are answers ready; on the day of nine deaths, I have no regret in the springs and soil."

entries.zh: 詔於獄賜死。
entries.en: An edict ordered him to die in prison.
entries.literal: An edict granted death in prison.

entries.zh: 時年二十七。
entries.en: He was twenty-seven years old.
entries.literal: He was then twenty-seven years old.

entries.zh: 臨死歎曰：「我若不爲百歲老母，當吐一言。」
entries.en: Facing death he sighed, "If it were not for my aged mother, I would speak one word."
entries.literal: Facing death he sighed: "If it were not for my hundred-year-old mother, I would speak one word."

entries.zh: 融意欲指斥帝在東宮時過失也。
entries.en: Rong meant to denounce the emperor's misconduct when he was heir apparent.
entries.literal: Rong meant to denounce the emperor's faults when he was in the Eastern Palace.

entries.zh: :　　臣側聞僉議，疑給虜書，如臣愚情，切有未喻。
entries.en: I have heard the assembly debating whether to give books to the barbarians; in my ignorance I cannot see the sense of it.
entries.literal: Your subject has overheard the collective deliberation and doubts about granting books to the barbarians; in my foolish feeling there is much I fail to understand.

entries.zh: 夫虜人面獸心，狼猛蜂毒，暴悖天經，虧違地義，逋竄燭幽，去來豳朔，綿周、漢而不悛，歷晉、宋其踰梗。
entries.en: The barbarians wear human faces but harbor beast hearts; fierce as wolves and venomous as wasps, they trample heaven's laws and break earth's right order, skulking beyond the frontier between Bin and the northern wastes—unrepentant through Zhou and Han, more stubborn still through Jin and Song.
entries.literal: These barbarians have human faces and beast hearts, wolf-fierce and wasp-venomous; they outrage heaven's norms and violate earth's principles, fleeing to the dark beyond the frontier, coming and going between Bin and the north—through Zhou and Han they did not repent, through Jin and Song they grew only more obstinate.

entries.zh: 豈有愛敬仁智，恭讓廉脩，慚犬馬之馴心，同鷹虎之反目。
entries.en: How could they cherish benevolence and wisdom, practice courtesy and integrity, feel shame at the loyalty of dog and horse, or turn on their masters like hawk and tiger?
entries.literal: How could they possess love, reverence, benevolence, and wisdom, courtesy, yielding, integrity, and cultivation—ashamed of the docile heart of dog and horse, sharing the turning against one of hawk and tiger?

entries.zh: 設槁秣有儲，筋竿足用，必以草竊關燧，寇擾邊疆；
entries.en: Give them fodder in store and bows and poles to spare, and they will surely slip past the beacon fires to harry the borders;
entries.literal: Suppose dry fodder were stored and bowstrings and poles sufficient—they would surely use straw to steal past the beacon fires and raid the frontier;

entries.zh: 寧容款塞卑辭，承衣請朔。
entries.en: never with humble words at the frontier, robes in hand, begging for the imperial calendar.
entries.literal: how could they be allowed to come in sincerity to the passes with humble words, receiving robes and requesting the calendar?

entries.zh: 陛下務存遵養，不時侮亡，許其膜拜之誠，納裘之賮。
entries.en: Your Majesty has chosen to nurture and spare them, not to strike the dying when the moment is wrong, accepting their prostrations and their fur tribute.
entries.literal: Your Majesty has devoted yourself to nurturing and preserving them, not despising the dying at the wrong hour, granting their sincerity in prostration and accepting their fur tribute.

entries.zh: 況復願同文軌，儻見款遣，思奉聲教，方致猜拒。
entries.en: And now they profess to share our script and our ways—if we treat them with courtesy and send them off, while they claim to embrace our civilization, we will only breed suspicion and resistance.
entries.literal: How much more if they now wish to share our script and carriage-tracks—if we should happen to send them off in good faith while they think to receive our civilizing teaching, we would only invite suspicion and refusal.

entries.zh: 將使舊邑遺逸，未知所寘，衰胡餘噍，或能自推。
entries.en: Our loyal subjects in the lost north would not know where to turn, and the last remnants of the barbarians might rally on their own.
entries.literal: This would leave the old cities' scattered remnants with nowhere to settle, and the declining Hu's surviving morsels perhaps able to push themselves forward.

entries.zh: 一令蔓草難鉏，涓流泛酌，豈直疥癢輕痾，容爲心腹重患。
entries.en: Let the weeds run wild and a trickle swell into a flood, and this is no mere rash or passing illness—it may become a mortal threat at the core of the realm.
entries.literal: Once creeping weeds are hard to uproot and a trickling stream overflows its cup, how is this merely a scab or a light ailment—it may become a grave malady of the heart and belly.

entries.zh: :　　抑孫武之言也，困則數罰，窘則多賞，先暴而後畏其衆者，虜之謂乎？
entries.en: Was it not Sun Wu who said that when cornered they multiply punishments, when desperate they multiply rewards, brutal first and only then feared by their followers—is that not exactly the barbarians?
entries.literal: Is this not what Sun Wu said—that when cornered they multiply punishments, when straitened they multiply rewards, first brutal and only then feared by their masses? Is this not the barbarians?

entries.zh: 前中原士庶，雖淪懾殊俗，至於婚葬之晨，猶巾褠爲禮。
entries.en: The people of the Central Plains, though forced under alien rule, still on wedding and funeral mornings wore Chinese dress as ritual demanded.
entries.literal: Formerly the gentry and commoners of the Central Plains, though fallen under alien customs, on mornings of marriage and burial still wore headcloths and robes as ritual.

entries.zh: 而禁令苛刻，動加誅轘。
entries.en: But their prohibitions were savage, and dismemberment by cart-wheel followed every infraction.
entries.literal: Yet prohibitions were harsh and severe, and execution by cart-wheel was added at every turn.

entries.zh: 于時獯粥初遷，犬羊尚結，卽心徒怨，困懼成逃。
entries.en: When the Xiongnu first settled in, the tribes were still bound like dog to sheep; resentment filled every heart, and fear drove men to flee.
entries.literal: At that time the Xiongnu had just moved in, dogs and sheep still bound together; hearts only resented, and fear in distress became flight.

entries.zh: 自其將卒奔離，資待銷闕，北畏勍蠕，西逼南胡，民背如崩，勢絕防斷。
entries.en: Once their commanders and troops scattered, supplies ran out; they feared the powerful Rouran in the north and were squeezed by tribes in the west—the people turned away like a collapsing wall, and their defenses were broken.
entries.literal: Since their officers and soldiers fled in dispersion, supplies and support were exhausted; they feared the mighty Rouran in the north and were pressed by the southern Hu in the west—the people's backs turned like collapse, their strength cut off from defense.

entries.zh: 於是曲從物情，偽竊章服，歷年將絕，隱蔽無聞。
entries.en: So they bent to popular feeling, stole regalia and robes in pretense, and for years on end kept themselves hidden from sight.
entries.literal: Thereupon they bent to follow popular sentiment, falsely stealing regalia and robes; the years nearly ran out, and they hid themselves unheard.

entries.zh: 旣南向而泣者，日夜以覬；
entries.en: Those who had turned south in tears watched day and night for deliverance;
entries.literal: Those who had turned south and wept looked day and night with longing;

entries.zh: 北顧而辭者，江淮相屬。
entries.en: those who looked north and took their farewells lined the Yangzi and Huai.
entries.literal: those who looked north and took leave stretched along the Yangzi and Huai.

entries.zh: 凶謀歲窘，淺慮無方，於是稽顙郊門，問禮求樂。
entries.en: Their plots grew desperate year by year, their shallow counsels failed them, and so they beat their foreheads at the frontier gate, begging for ritual and music.
entries.literal: Their wicked plots grew yearly more straitened, shallow counsel had no method—thereupon they knocked their foreheads at the suburban gate, asking for ritual and seeking music.

entries.zh: 若來之以文德，賜之以副書，漢家軌儀，重臨畿輔，司隷傳節，復入關河，無待八百之師，不期十萬之衆，固其提漿佇俟，揮戈願倒，三秦大同，六漢一統。
entries.en: If we came with civil virtue and gave them duplicate texts, if Han ritual returned to the heartland and the Director of Retainers bore his tally back through the passes—without needing eight hundred men or a hundred thousand soldiers—they would bring provisions and wait, raise spears eager to defect; the Three Qin would reunite and the six regions of Han would be one again.
entries.literal: If we came to them with civil virtue and granted duplicate books, Han ritual and regalia returned to the capital region, the Director of Retainers passed his tally and re-entered the passes and rivers—without waiting for eight hundred troops, without expecting a hundred thousand men—they would surely carry provisions and stand waiting, wave spears wishing to topple over; the Three Qin would be great-unified, the Six Han made one.

entries.zh: :　　又虜前後奉使，不專漢人，必介以匈奴，備諸覘獲。
entries.en: Moreover, in their embassies past and present they never sent only Han men but always mixed in Xiongnu, to guard against every kind of intelligence.
entries.literal: Moreover, in their former and later missions the barbarians did not use only Han men but always interposed Xiongnu, guarding against all reconnaissance.

entries.zh: 且設官分職，彌見其情，抑退舊苗，扶任種戚。
entries.en: In their offices and ranks their intent is plain: they push down the old families and elevate their own kin.
entries.literal: In establishing offices and dividing duties their disposition is all the clearer: they suppress and push back the old clans and support and appoint their own kindred.

entries.zh: 師保則后族馮晉國，總錄則邽姓直勒渴侯，台鼎則丘頹、苟仁端，執政則目凌、鉗耳。
entries.en: Their tutor is Feng Jinguo of the empress's clan; their chief recorder is Zhile Kehou of the Guo clan; their top ministers are Qiu Tui and Gou Renduan; those who govern are Muling and Qian'er.
entries.literal: Tutor and guardian is Feng Jinguo of the empress's clan; chief recorder is the Guo-clan Zhile Kehou; director-level ministers are Qiu Tui and Gou Renduan; those holding power are Muling and Qian'er.

entries.zh: 至於東都羽儀，西京簪帶，崔孝伯、程虞虯久在著作，李元和、郭季祐上于中書，李思沖飾虜清官，游明根泛居顯職。
entries.en: As for the courtiers of the old capitals—Cui Xiaobo and Cheng Yuqiu long served in the Composition Office, Li Yuanhe and Guo Jiyou rose in the Secretariat, Li Sichong held high barbarian office, and You Minggen filled one prominent post after another.
entries.literal: As for the feathered regalia of the Eastern Capital and the capped gentry of the Western Capital—Cui Xiaobo and Cheng Yuqiu long served in the Composition Office, Li Yuanhe and Guo Jiyou rose in the Secretariat, Li Sichong adorned their barbarian pure offices, You Minggen broadly held eminent posts.

entries.zh: 今經典遠被，詩史北流，馮、李之徒，必欲遵尚；
entries.en: Now that the classics reach them and poetry and history flow north, men like Feng and Li will surely wish to honor them;
entries.literal: Now the classics reach far, poetry and histories flow north—the Fengs, Lis, and their kind will surely wish to honor and uphold them;

entries.zh: 直勒等類，居致乖阻。
entries.en: while the Zhile and their kind will only breed obstruction.
entries.literal: the Zhile and their sort will in residence produce estrangement and obstruction.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 匈奴以氈騎爲帷牀，馳射爲糇粮，冠方帽則犯沙陵雪，服左衽則風驤鳥逝。
entries.en: The Xiongnu take felt tents and horsemanship for their home, galloping archery for their sustenance; in square caps they brave sand and snow, in left-lapel dress they ride the wind like birds.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu take felt tents and horsemanship as their bed-curtains, galloping archery as their dry provisions; crowned with square caps they brave sandbanks and snow, clothed in left-lapel dress they ride the wind swift as birds in flight.

entries.zh: 若衣以朱裳，戴之玄頍，節其揖讓，教以翔趨，必同艱桎梏，等懼冰淵，婆娑躄，因而不能前已。
entries.en: Dress them in vermilion robes and dark caps, teach them bowing and measured steps, and they would feel as shackled, as terrified as over an icy abyss, hobbling and shuffling, unable to go forward at all.
entries.literal: If clothed in vermilion robes and capped with dark foreheads, their bowing and yielding regulated, taught the measured pace—they would be alike in hardship as in shackles, equal in fear as before an icy abyss, hobbling and shuffling, and thus unable to advance.

entries.zh: 及夫春草水生，阻散馬之適，秋風木落，絕驅禽之歡，息沸脣於桑墟，別醍乳於冀俗，聽《韶雅》如聾聵，臨方丈若爰居，馮、李之徒，固得志矣，虜之凶族，其如病何？
entries.en: When spring grass rises and waters flow, they cannot scatter their horses; when autumn wind blows and leaves fall, they cannot hunt for sport; they would cease their clamor at the mulberry altars and leave behind the kumis of Ji—hearing the Shaoya would be like deafness, facing a square hall like living among strangers. Men like Feng and Li would have their way, but the barbarians' fierce clans—how could they endure it except as a mortal illness?
entries.literal: When spring grass and waters rise, they block the scattering of horses' ease; when autumn wind and trees fall, they cut off the joy of driving game; they cease chattering lips at mulberry ruins and part from kumis at Ji customs; hearing Shaoya is like deafness, facing a square zhang is like dwelling in Ai—the Fengs and Lis would surely get their wish, but the barbarians' fierce clans—how would they bear it as sickness?

entries.zh: 於是風土之思深，愎戾之情動，拂衣者連裾，抽鋒者比鏃，部落爭于下，酋渠危於上，我一舉而兼吞，卞莊之勢必也。
entries.en: Then homesickness would run deep, rebellious passions would stir; men brushing their robes would stand shoulder to shoulder, men drawing blades would stand arrow to arrow; tribes would fight below and chiefs would totter above—and we with one stroke would take them all, as Bian Zhuangzi took both tigers.
entries.literal: Then longing for native soil would deepen, perverse and violent feelings would stir; those brushing their robes would link hems, those drawing blades would align arrowheads; tribes would contend below, chieftains would be imperiled above—we with one stroke would swallow them both: the momentum of Bian Zhuangzi would be assured.

entries.zh: 且棘寶薦虞，晉疆彌盛，大鍾出智，宿氏以亡。
entries.en: When the thorn treasure was offered to Yu, Jin's borders grew; when the great bell came from Zhi, the Su clan was destroyed.
entries.literal: Moreover, when the thorn treasure was offered to Yu, Jin's borders grew ever greater; when the great bell came forth from Zhi, the Su clan perished.

entries.zh: 帝略遠孚，無思不服，鑾光幸岱，匪暮斯朝。
entries.en: Your imperial strategy reaches far and wins every heart; your sacred radiance will visit Mount Tai—not by evening but by morning.
entries.literal: Your imperial strategy reaches far and wins trust; none who think on it fail to submit; the imperial radiance visits Mount Dai—not by evening but by morning.

entries.zh: 臣請收籍伊瀍，茲書復掌，猶取之內府，藏之外，於理有愜，卽事何損。
entries.en: I ask that we register the texts of the Yi and Luo and hold these books again ourselves—taken from our inner treasury and kept from them abroad—which is reasonable and in practice costs nothing.
entries.literal: Your subject requests to gather and register the Yi and Luo texts, that these books be held again in our keeping—still taking them from the inner treasury, storing them without—this accords with reason and in practice harms nothing.

entries.zh: 若狂言足採，請決敕施行。
entries.en: If this rash speech is worth heeding, I beg Your Majesty to decree and execute it.
entries.literal: If this mad talk is worth adopting, I beg that an edict be decided and carried out.

entries.zh: :　　臣聞情慉自中，事符則感，象構於始，機動斯彰。
entries.en: I have heard that feeling wells up within, and when events accord it stirs response; images are shaped at the outset, and when the mechanism moves they appear.
entries.literal: Your subject has heard that feeling stored within the heart, when affairs accord then moves the response; images are constructed at the beginning, and when the mechanism stirs they are displayed.

entries.zh: 莊敬之道可宗，會揖讓其彌肅，勇烈之士足貴，應鼙鐸以增思。
entries.en: The way of dignity and reverence deserves honor; at gatherings bowing and yielding grow more solemn still; brave men are precious, and answering to drums and bells deepens one's thought.
entries.literal: The way of dignity and reverence may be honored; at gatherings bowing and yielding grow all the more solemn; brave and fierce men are fully to be prized—responding to drums and bells increases reflection.

entries.zh: 肇植生民，厥詳旣緬，降及興運，維道有徵，莫不有所因循而升皇業者也。
entries.en: From the first planting of humankind the record was already remote; down to ages of rising fortune the Way left its traces—none failed to build on precedent and ascend to imperial greatness.
entries.literal: From the first planting of the people its details were already remote; descending to ages of flourishing fortune, only the Way had signs—none failed to follow something and ascend to imperial enterprise.

entries.zh: 若夫膏腴旣稱，天乙知五方之富，皮幣已列，帝劉測四海之尊。
entries.en: When fertile lands were acclaimed, Tianyi knew the wealth of the five directions; when furs and coin were set out, Emperor Liu measured the honor of the four seas.
entries.literal: As for fertile lands already acclaimed, Tianyi knew the wealth of the five directions; fur and coin already arrayed, Emperor Liu gauged the honor of the four seas.

entries.zh: 異封禪之文，則升中之典攸鬯，嘆輿地之圖，乃席卷之庸是立。
entries.en: Unlike the texts of the feng and shan rites, the ceremony of ascending the central peak was thereby enriched; lamenting the map of the realm, the merit of sweeping it up in conquest was established.
