entries.literal: Differing from the feng and shan texts, then the rite of ascending the central peak was thereby enriched; sighing over the map of the realm's terrain, then the merit of rolling it up in a scroll was established.

entries.zh: :　　伏惟陛下窮神盡聖，總極居中，偶化兩儀，均明二耀，拯玄綱於頹絕，反至道於澆淳，可謂區宇儀形，齊民先覺者也。
entries.en: I consider that Your Majesty exhausts spirit and fulfills sagehood, holds the ultimate center, pairs with heaven and earth, balances sun and moon, rescues the cosmic order from collapse and returns the Way from vulgar decline—you are the model of the realm and guide to the people.
entries.literal: Bowingly considering that Your Majesty exhausts spirit and fulfills sagehood, holds the ultimate center, pairs transformation with the Two Modes, balances brightness of the two luminaries, rescues the dark net from collapse, returns the utmost Way from shallow vulgarity—you may be called the model form of the realm, the foreknowing guide of the people.

entries.zh: 臣亦遭逢，生此嘉運，鑿飲耕食，自幸唐年。
entries.en: I too have met with fortune, born in this excellent age, drinking from the plow and eating from the soil, counting myself blessed to live in an age like Tang Yao's.
entries.literal: Your subject too has met with fortune, born in this excellent age, drinking from the plow and eating from the field, counting himself blessed in the years of Tang.

entries.zh: 而識用昏霾，經術疏淺，將薖且軸，豈蕨與薇。
entries.en: Yet my mind is dim and my learning shallow; I am like artemisia about to wither on its stem—how could I compare to fern and orchid?
entries.literal: Yet my knowledge and use are dim as haze, classical learning shallow and thin—I am about to wither like artemisia on its stem; how could I be fern and orchid?

entries.zh: 皇鑒燭幽，天高聽下，賞片言之或善，矜一物之失時，湔拂塵蒙，霑飾光價，拔足草廬，廁身朝序，復得拜賀歲時，瞻望日月，於臣心願，曾已畢矣。
entries.en: Your mirror illuminates the dark, heaven high yet hears below, rewarding a word if it has merit, pitying a talent mistimed, washing away dust and granting honor, lifting me from a grass hut into the court ranks, letting me again bow at the seasons and gaze on sun and moon—in my heart that wish was already fulfilled.
entries.literal: The imperial mirror illuminates the dark, heaven is high yet hears below, rewarding a fragment of speech if perhaps good, pitying a single thing's untimely loss, washing away dust and mist, touching and adorning with light and price, pulling feet from the grass hut and placing body in court order, again able to bow in congratulation at the seasons and gaze upon sun and moon—in your subject's heart the wish was already fulfilled.

entries.zh: 但千祀一逢，休明難再，思策鈆駑，樂陳涓壒。
entries.en: Yet an age like this comes once in a thousand years and cannot be repeated; I mean to spur my feeble talent and gladly offer whatever small service I can.
entries.literal: Yet a thousand years meet such brilliance but once, and this excellent clarity is hard to regain—I think to spur my leaden nag and gladly offer my tiny mound of dust.

entries.zh: 竊習戰陣攻守之術，農桑牧藝之書，申、商、韓、墨之權，伊、周、孔、孟之道。
entries.en: I have studied the arts of attack and defense, books of farming and herding, the stratagems of Shen Buhai, Shang Yang, Han Fei, and Mozi, and the Ways of Yi Yin, the Duke of Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius.
entries.literal: Secretly I have studied the arts of battle array attack and defense, books of farming, sericulture, herding, and crafts, the stratagems of Shen, Shang, Han, and Mo, the Ways of Yi, Zhou, Confucius, and Mencius.

entries.zh: 常願待詔朱闕，俯對青蒲，請閑宴之私，談當世之務。
entries.en: I have long wished to await your summons at the vermilion gate, kneel before the green rush mats, and in a private audience discuss the affairs of the age.
entries.literal: I constantly wish to await edict at the vermilion gate, bow facing the green rush mats, request the privacy of a leisurely banquet, and discuss the affairs of the age.

entries.zh: 位賤人微，徒深傾款。
entries.en: My rank is low and my person slight; I can only offer my deepest devotion.
entries.literal: My rank is low and my person slight—I can only pour out deep devotion.

entries.zh: :　　方今九服清怡，三靈和晏，木有附枝，輪無異轍，東鞮獻舞，南辮傳歌，羗、踰山，秦、屠越海，舌象翫委體之懃，輶譯厭瞻巡之數，固將開桂林於鳳山，創金城於西守。
entries.en: Today the nine domains are tranquil, heaven, earth, and man are at peace; trees flourish and wheels run true; the eastern tribes present dance, the southern tribes send song; Qiang and Di cross mountains, Qin and Yue span seas; interpreters grow weary of foreign envoys' obeisance, translators tire of imperial tours—we shall surely open Guilin at Phoenix Mountain and build Golden City in the west.
entries.literal: Now the nine domains are clear and at ease, the three numina harmonious and tranquil; trees have attached branches, wheels no differing tracks; the eastern Di present dance, the southern Man transmit song; Qiang and Di cross mountains, Qin and Yue span seas; interpreters weary of the diligence of those laying down their persons, relay-translators sated with the count of inspections—surely we shall open Guilin at Phoenix Mountain and found Golden City at the western guard.

entries.zh: 而蠢爾獯狄，敢讎大邦，假息關河，竊命函谷，淪故京之爽塏，變舊邑而荒涼，息反坫之儒衣，久伊川之被髮。
entries.en: Yet these stupid Xun and Di dare oppose the great state, clinging to life at the passes and rivers, stealing authority at Hangu, sinking the bright terraces of the old capital, turning ancient cities to desolation, silencing the scholar's robe at the ritual stand, and leaving Yi River long in disheveled hair.
entries.literal: Yet these stupid Xiongnu and Di dare make enemy of the great state, borrowing breath at the passes and rivers, stealing mandate at Hangu, sinking the old capital's bright terraces, changing old cities to desolation, ceasing the scholar's robe returned to the altar, long wearing disheveled hair at the Yi River.

entries.zh: 北地殘氓，東都遺老，莫不茹泣吞悲，傾耳戴目，翹心仁政，延首王風。
entries.en: The remnant people of the north, the old elders of the Eastern Capital—all swallow tears, strain their ears and eyes, yearn for benevolent rule, and stretch their necks for the royal transforming wind.
entries.literal: The remnant people of the northern lands, the old elders of the Eastern Capital—none fail to swallow tears and grief, incline ears and lift eyes, crane hearts toward benevolent government, stretch necks for royal wind.

entries.zh: 若試馳咫尺之書，具甄戎旅之卒，徇其墮城，納其降虜，可弗勞弦鏃，無待干戈。
entries.en: If we send a letter a few inches long and muster our troops, accept their fallen cities and their surrendering captives, we need not strain bowstrings or wait for battle.
entries.literal: If we try sending a letter of a few inches, fully selecting army troops, following their fallen cities and receiving their surrendering captives—we need not weary bowstrings and arrows, nor wait for weapons of war.

entries.zh: 真皇王之兵，征而不戰者也。
entries.en: That is the army of a true sage-king—one that campaigns without fighting.
entries.literal: This is truly the army of a sage-king—campaigning without fighting.

entries.zh: 臣乞以執殳先邁，式道中原，澄澣渚之恒流，掃狼山之積霧，係單于之頸，屈左賢之膝，習呼韓之舊儀，拜鑾輿之巡幸。
entries.en: I beg to take spear in hand and march ahead, open the way through the Central Plains, clear the constant streams, sweep the mists from Wolf Mountain, bind the Chanyu's neck, bend the Left Worthy's knee, restore the old rites of Huhanye, and bow when your imperial carriage tours the north.
entries.literal: Your subject begs to take spear in hand and advance first, open the way through the Central Plains, clarify the constant flow of the washing ford, sweep the piled mists of Wolf Mountain, bind the Chanyu's neck, bend the Left Worthy's knee, practice the old rites of Huhanye, and bow at the imperial carriage's tour of inspection.

entries.zh: 然後天移雲動，勒封岱宗，咸五登三，追蹤七十，百神肅警，萬國具僚，璯弁星離，玉帛雲聚，集三燭於蘭席，聆萬歲之禎聲，豈不盛哉！
entries.en: Then heaven will shift and clouds will move; we shall inscribe the feng on Mount Tai, complete the five rites and ascend the three, follow the seventy-two kings of old, the hundred spirits will stand in awe, the ten thousand states will attend as officials, jade caps will scatter like stars, jade and silk will gather like clouds, triple candles will burn on orchid mats, and we shall hear the auspicious cry of ten thousand years—how grand!
entries.literal: Then heaven shifts and clouds move; we inscribe feng on Mount Dai, complete the five and ascend the three, follow the trail of seventy, the hundred spirits solemnly alert, the ten thousand states all as officials, jade caps star-scattered, jade and silk cloud-gathered, gathering triple candles on orchid mats, hearing the auspicious sound of ten thousand years—how is it not grand!

entries.zh: 豈不韙哉！
entries.en: How fitting!
entries.literal: How is it not right!

entries.zh: :　　昔桓公志在伐莒，郭牙審其幽趣，魏后心存去漢，德祖究其深言。
entries.en: When Duke Huan of Qi meant to attack Ju, Guo Ya read his hidden intent; when the Wei empress meant to remove Han, Dezhi (Yang Xiu) plumbed her deeper meaning.
entries.literal: Formerly Duke Huan's will was set on attacking Ju, and Guo Ya discerned his hidden intent; the Wei empress harbored thoughts of removing Han, and Dezhi plumbed her deep words.

entries.zh: 臣愚昧，忖誠不足以知微，然伏揆聖心，規模弘遠，旣圖載其事，必克就其功。
entries.en: I am foolish and my sincerity is not enough to grasp subtleties, yet I bow to your sacred intent—its scope is vast and far; since you have set this matter down in a picture, you will surely bring it to completion.
entries.literal: Your subject is foolish and dull; sincere reckoning is insufficient to know subtleties—yet bowing to gauge the sacred heart, its scope is vast and far; since you have pictured and recorded this affair, you will surely be able to complete its achievement.

entries.zh: 臣不勝歡喜。
entries.en: I cannot contain my joy.
entries.literal: Your subject cannot overcome his joy.

entries.zh: 朝廷討雍州刺史王奐，融復上疏曰：
entries.en: When the court moved against Wang Huan, Governor of Yong Province, Rong submitted another memorial:
entries.literal: When the court campaigned against Wang Huan, Governor of Yong Province, Rong again submitted a memorial, saying:

entries.zh: :　　臣每覽史傳，見憂國忘家，捐生報德者，未曾不撫卷歎息，以爲今古共情也。
entries.en: Whenever I read the histories and see men who forgot their families for the state and gave their lives to repay kindness, I cannot help stroking the scroll and sighing, for I believe past and present share the same feeling.
entries.literal: Your subject whenever reads historical records and sees those who worry for the state and forget family, who give life to repay kindness—never fails to stroke the scroll and sigh, thinking this is feeling shared by past and present.

entries.zh: 然或以片言微感，一餐小惠，參國士之眄，同布素之遊耳。
entries.en: Yet some were moved by a single word or a meal's small favor, earning a great man's glance or sharing a commoner's friendship—that is all.
entries.literal: Yet some were moved by a fragment of speech or a slight favor at one meal, joining a national scholar's glance or sharing a plain-cloth friend's company—that is all.

entries.zh: 豈有如臣，獨拔無聞之伍，過超非分之位，名器雙假，榮祿兩升，而宴安具罷之晨，優游旰食之日。
entries.en: How could there be one like me, plucked alone from obscurity, raised beyond my deserts, given both title and regalia, both honor and salary—yet living at ease while the ruler eats late into the day?
entries.literal: How could there be one like your subject, alone plucked from the ranks of the unheard-of, surpassing a position beyond his measure, name and regalia doubly lent, honor and salary doubly raised—yet on mornings when feasting and ease are fully done, on days of leisurely ease while the ruler eats late?

entries.zh: 所以敢布丹愚，仰聞宸聽。
entries.en: That is why I dare offer my loyal counsel and beg to be heard by the throne.
entries.literal: Therefore I dare lay out my red sincerity and look up to be heard by the imperial ear.

entries.zh: :　　今議者或以西夏爲念，臣竊謂之不爾。
entries.en: Some advisers now worry about the western campaign; I do not think they should.
entries.literal: Now those who deliberate sometimes take the western Xia frontier as their concern; your subject privately thinks it is not so.

entries.zh: 其故何哉？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: What is the reason?

entries.zh: 陛下聖明，羣臣悉力，從以制逆，上而御下，指開賞黜之言，微示生死之路，方域之人，皆相爲敵。
entries.en: Your Majesty is sage and bright, your ministers give their full strength, rebellion is controlled from above, reward and punishment are made plain and the path of life and death shown—the people of the region have turned against one another.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is sage and bright, the ministers all exert their strength, following to control rebellion, governing above and mastering below, pointing to open words of reward and punishment, subtly showing the path of life and death—the people of the region all become one another's enemies.

entries.zh: 旣兵威遠臨，人不自保，雖窮鳥必啄，固等命於梁鶉，困獸斯驚，終竝懸於廚鹿。
entries.en: Once your armies press near, no one can protect himself; cornered birds must strike, beasts in a trap panic, and in the end they will all hang together like deer in the kitchen.
entries.literal: Since military might reaches from afar, men cannot preserve themselves; though a cornered bird must peck, they are alike in fate to the beam quail; a trapped beast is startled, and in the end all hang together like kitchen deer.

entries.zh: 凱師勞飲，固不待晨。
entries.en: The victory feast need not wait until morning.
entries.literal: A victorious army's labor and drinking surely need not wait for morning.

entries.zh: 臣之寸心，獨有微願。
entries.en: In my heart I have only one small wish.
entries.literal: Your subject's inch of heart has only a slight wish.

entries.zh: :　　自獫狁荐食，荒侮伊瀍，天道禍淫，危亡日至，母后內難，糧力外虛，謠言物情，屬當今會。
entries.en: Since the barbarians have repeatedly encroached and insulted the heartland, heaven punishes excess and ruin draws near daily; the empress dowager faces internal trouble, supplies abroad are exhausted, and rumor and popular feeling all point to this moment.
entries.literal: Since the Xianyun have repeatedly encroached, wildly insulting the Yi and Luo, heaven's way punishes excess and peril and ruin arrive daily; the empress dowager has internal troubles, grain and strength are empty abroad, rumors and popular feeling—all belong to the present moment.

entries.zh: 若藉巫、漢之歸師，騁士卒之餘憤，取函谷如反掌，陵關塞若摧枯。
entries.en: If we use the returning armies of Wu and Han and unleash the soldiers' remaining fury, we could take Hangu Pass as easily as turning one's hand and storm the frontier barriers as if crushing dry wood—
entries.literal: If we borrow the returning armies of Wu and Han, unleash the soldiers' remaining fury, taking Hangu as if turning the hand, storming passes and barriers as if crushing dry wood—

entries.zh: 但士非素蓄，無以卽用，不教民戰，是實棄之。
entries.en: but the troops are not long trained and cannot be used at once; not to teach the people war is truly to abandon them.
entries.literal: but the troops are not long trained and cannot be used at once; not to teach the people war is truly to abandon them.

entries.zh: 特希私集部曲，豫加習校。
entries.en: I beg only to gather my private retainers in advance and train them.
entries.literal: I especially hope to gather my private retainers in advance and add drill and training.

entries.zh: 若蒙垂許，乞隷監省拘食人身，權備石頭防衞之數。
entries.en: If you grant this, I ask to be attached to the supervisory offices for rations and temporarily to fill the Stone City defense quota.
entries.literal: If I receive gracious permission, I beg to be attached to the supervisory offices for rationed provisions, temporarily filling the Stone City defense quota.

entries.zh: 臣少重名節，早習軍旅，若試而無績，伏受面欺之誅；
entries.en: From youth I have valued honor and early studied military affairs; if tried and I fail, I accept punishment for deceiving you to your face;
entries.literal: Your subject from youth valued reputation and integrity and early studied military affairs; if tried and without achievement, I bow to accept punishment for deceiving you to your face;

entries.zh: 用且有功，仰詶知人之哲。
entries.en: if employed and I succeed, I will repay your wisdom in knowing men.
entries.literal: if employed and with achievement, I look up to repay the wisdom of knowing men.

entries.zh: 融自恃人地，三十內望爲公輔。
entries.en: Rong trusted in his birth and standing and expected to reach the highest ministerial rank before he was thirty.
entries.literal: Rong relied on his person and place, expecting within thirty years to become a minister at the highest level.

entries.zh: 直中書省，夜歎曰：「鄧禹笑人。」
entries.en: One night at the Secretariat he sighed, "Deng Yu would laugh at me."
entries.literal: While at the Secretariat he sighed at night: "Deng Yu would laugh at me."

entries.zh: 行逢大開，喧湫不得進。
entries.en: On his way he met a great throng, noisy and jammed, and could not pass.
entries.literal: Walking he met a great opening, noisy and crowded, unable to advance.

entries.zh: 又歎曰：「車前無八騶卒，何得稱爲丈夫！」
entries.en: He sighed again, "With no eight outriders before my carriage, how can I call myself a man!"
entries.literal: He sighed again: "With no eight outriders before my carriage, how can I be called a true man!"

entries.zh: 世祖答曰：「吾意不異卿。
entries.en: Emperor Wu replied, "My view is no different from yours.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu replied: "My intent does not differ from yours.

entries.zh: 今所啓，比相見更委悉。」
entries.en: What you now present is fuller than when we spoke face to face."
entries.literal: What you now present is more detailed than when we met in person."

entries.zh: 事竟不行。
entries.en: In the end nothing was done.
entries.literal: In the end the matter was not carried out.

entries.zh: 子隆在荊州，好辭賦，數集僚友，朓以文才，尤被賞愛，流連晤對，不捨日夕。
entries.en: Zilong in Jing Province loved poetry and often gathered his staff; Tiao for his literary talent was especially favored, and they lingered in conversation day and night.
entries.literal: Zilong in Jing Province loved rhapsodies and fu, often gathering staff and friends; Tiao for his literary talent was especially prized and loved, lingering in meetings day and night without parting.

entries.zh: 長史王秀之以朓年少相動，密以啓聞。
entries.en: Chief Aide Wang Xiuzhi, because Tiao was young and was exerting influence, secretly reported it to the throne.
entries.literal: Chief Aide Wang Xiuzhi, because Tiao was young, suspected improper intimacy and secretly memorialized the court.

entries.zh: 世祖敕曰：「侍讀虞雲自宜恒應侍接。
entries.en: Emperor Wu ordered, "Reader-in-Waiting Yu Yun should constantly attend the prince.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu ordered: "Reader-in-Waiting Yu Yun himself should constantly attend and receive him.

entries.zh: 朓可還都。」
entries.en: Tiao is to return to the capital."
entries.literal: Tiao may return to the capital."

entries.zh: 朓道中爲詩寄西府曰：「常恐鷹隼擊，秋菊委嚴霜。
entries.en: On the road Tiao sent a poem to the western headquarters: "I constantly fear the hawk's strike; autumn chrysanthemums bow to harsh frost.
entries.literal: On the road Tiao composed a poem sent to the western headquarters, saying: "I constantly fear the hawk and falcon's strike; autumn chrysanthemums yield to harsh frost.

entries.zh: 寄言罻羅者，寥廓已高翔。」
entries.en: Tell the fowler: in the vast sky I have already soared away."
entries.literal: I send word to the net-setter: in the vast expanse I have already soared high."

entries.zh: 遷新安王中軍記室。
entries.en: He was transferred to Recorder of the Central Army on the staff of the Prince of Xin'an.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Recorder of the Central Army under the Prince of Xin'an.

entries.zh: 朓牋辭子隆曰：「朓聞潢汙之水，思朝宗而每竭；
entries.en: Tiao wrote Zilong a farewell note: "I have heard that muddy pool water, though it longs to reach the great river, is always exhausted;
entries.literal: Tiao in a note taking leave of Zilong said: "Tiao has heard that muddy pool water, thinking to pay court to the source, is each time exhausted;

entries.zh: 駑蹇之乘，希沃若而中疲。
entries.en: a lame nag's cart, hoping for lush pasture yet failing halfway.
entries.literal: a lame nag's carriage, hoping for lush growth yet failing midway.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 皐壤搖落，對之惆悵；
entries.en: The highland soil shakes and falls; facing it one is filled with melancholy;
entries.literal: Highland soil shakes and falls; facing it one is melancholy;

entries.zh: 岐路東西，或以嗚悒。
entries.en: roads east and west—perhaps one sobs in distress.
entries.literal: crossroads east and west—perhaps one sobs in distress.

entries.zh: 況乃服義徒擁，歸志莫從，邈若墜雨，飄似秋蔕。
entries.en: How much more when duty binds me though followers crowd round, and homeward will cannot be followed—distant as falling rain, drifting like an autumn stem.
entries.literal: How much more when duty binds yet followers crowd, homeward will cannot be followed—distant as falling rain, drifting like an autumn stem.

entries.zh: 朓實庸流，行能無算，屬天地休明，山川受納，褒採一介，搜揚小善，捨耒場圃，奉筆菟園。
entries.en: I am truly a mediocrity, my conduct and ability beyond reckoning; heaven and earth were bright, mountains and rivers at peace; one man was praised and small merit sought out—I left the plow in the fields and took up the brush in the garden.
entries.literal: Tiao is truly a mediocre current, conduct and ability beyond reckoning; it happened that heaven and earth were bright and restful, mountains and rivers received and accepted—praising and selecting one man, searching and raising small goodness, leaving the plow in field and garden, taking up the brush in the rabbit garden.

entries.zh: 東亂三江，西浮七澤，契闊戎旃，從容讌語。
entries.en: East through the turmoil of the three rivers, west across the seven marshes, parting and reuniting under military banners, at ease in feast and conversation.
entries.literal: East through the turmoil of the three rivers, west floating the seven marshes, parting and reuniting under military banners, at ease in feast and talk.

entries.zh: 長裾日曳，後乘載脂，榮立府廷，恩加顏色。
entries.en: Long robes trailed day after day, rear carriages bore gifts; I stood honored in your court, and favor brightened my face.
entries.literal: Long robes trailed day by day, rear carriages bore grease; honor stood in the prince's court, favor added to his countenance.

entries.zh: 沐髮晞陽，未測涯涘；
entries.en: I bathed my hair in the sun, never guessing where the shore lay;
entries.literal: Washing hair in the drying sun, I had not measured the shore's limit;

entries.zh: 撫臆論報，早誓肌骨。
entries.en: I pressed my breast and spoke of repayment, swearing it early in flesh and bone.
entries.literal: stroking my breast I spoke of repayment, early swearing it in flesh and bone.

entries.zh: 不悟滄溟未運，波臣自蕩；
entries.en: I did not see that the great sea had not yet stirred, and I swayed like a wave-subject;
entries.literal: I did not realize the dark sea had not yet moved, and the wave-subject swayed of itself;

entries.zh: 渤澥方春，旅翮先謝。
entries.en: the Bohai was barely in spring, yet the traveler's wings already withered.
entries.literal: the Bohai was just in spring, yet the traveler's wings first withered.

entries.zh: 清切蕃房，寂寥舊蓽。
entries.en: The clear, intimate lodging abroad, the lonely old thatched hut.
entries.literal: The clear, intimate foreign lodging, the lonely old thatched hut.

entries.zh: 輕舟反泝，弔影獨留，白雲在天，龍門不見。
entries.en: A light boat turns back upstream; I mourn my shadow left alone—white clouds fill the sky, and Dragon Gate is out of sight.
entries.literal: A light boat turns back upstream; I mourn my shadow left alone—white clouds are in the sky, Dragon Gate is not seen.

entries.zh: 去德滋永，思德滋深。
entries.en: The farther I am from your grace, the longer it seems; the more I think on it, the deeper my feeling.
entries.literal: Departing from virtue grows ever longer; thinking on virtue grows ever deeper.

entries.zh: 唯待青江可望，候歸艎於春渚；
entries.en: I only wait until the green river comes in view, watching for your returning boat at the spring ford;
entries.literal: I only wait until the green river can be seen, watching for the returning boat at the spring ford;

entries.zh: 朱邸方開，效蓬心於秋實。
entries.en: your vermilion mansion newly opens—I offer my humble heart as autumn fruit.
entries.literal: the vermilion mansion newly opens—I offer my artemisia heart in autumn fruit.

entries.zh: 如其簪履或存，衽席無改，雖復身填溝壑，猶望妻子知歸。
entries.en: If your favor still remains and your seat is unchanged, though my body fill ditch and ravine, I still hope my wife and children know I would return.
entries.literal: If your cap-pins and shoes perhaps remain, your mat and seat unchanged—though my body fill gullies and ravines, I still hope my wife and children know to return.

entries.zh: 攬涕告辭，悲來橫集。」
entries.en: Wiping tears I take my leave; grief comes and gathers over me."
entries.literal: Wiping tears I take leave; grief comes and gathers across me."

entries.zh: 朓少好學，有美名，文章清麗。
entries.en: Tiao from youth loved learning, enjoyed a fine reputation, and wrote in a clear, beautiful style.
entries.literal: Tiao from youth loved learning, had a fine reputation, and his writings were clear and beautiful.

entries.zh: 解褐豫章王太尉行參軍，度隨王東中郎府，轉王儉衞軍東閤祭酒，太子舍人、隨王鎮西功曹，轉文學。
entries.en: Upon entering office he was Acting Aide to the Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Minister, moved to the staff of the Prince of Sui as Eastern Commander-in-Chief, became Eastern Pavilion Libationer on Wang Jian's staff as Guard General, then Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Western Headquarters Aide to the Prince of Sui, and finally Literary Scholar.
entries.literal: Upon leaving the cloth he was Acting Aide to the Prince of Yuzhang as Grand Minister, crossed to the Eastern Central Staff of the Prince of Sui, transferred to Wang Jian's Eastern Pavilion Libationer on the Guard General's staff, Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Western Headquarters Aide to the Prince of Sui, then transferred to Literary Scholar.

entries.zh: 尋以本官兼尚書殿中郎。
entries.en: Soon he additionally served as Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Department while keeping his original post.
entries.literal: Soon on his original post he additionally served as Attendant Gentleman of the Palace Department in the Ministry of State Affairs.

entries.zh: 隆昌初，敕朓接北使，朓自以口訥，啓讓不當，不見許。
entries.en: At the beginning of Longchang he was ordered to receive northern envoys; thinking his speech too slow, he memorialized that he was unfit, but the request was denied.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Longchang an edict ordered Tiao to receive northern envoys; Tiao himself thought his speech slow and memorialized that he was unfit—the request was not granted.

entries.zh: 高宗輔政，以朓爲驃騎諮議，領記室，掌霸府文筆。
entries.en: When Gaozong assisted in government, he made Tiao adviser to the Cavalry General, concurrently heading the Record Office and managing the princely headquarters' writings.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor assisted in government, he made Tiao Counselor to the Rapid Cavalry General, heading the Recorder's office and managing the hegemon's mansion literary brush.

entries.zh: 又掌中書詔誥，除祕書丞，未拜，仍轉中書郎。
entries.en: He also managed Secretariat edicts; was appointed Secretary Assistant but never took office, and was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.
entries.literal: He also managed Secretariat edicts and proclamations; was appointed Secretary Assistant but did not assume the post, and was transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 出爲宣城太守，以選復爲中書郎。
entries.en: He went out as Administrator of Xuancheng, then through selection returned as Secretariat Gentleman.
entries.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xuancheng; through selection he returned as Secretariat Gentleman.

entries.zh: 東昏失德，江祐欲立夏王寶玄，末更回惑，與弟祀密謂朓曰：「江夏年少輕脫，不堪負荷神器，不可復行廢立。
entries.en: When Emperor Donghun lost virtue, Jiang You wished to make the Prince of Xia, Bao Xuan, emperor, but later wavered; he and his brother Si secretly told Tiao, "The Prince of Jiangxia is young and frivolous and cannot bear the throne; we cannot depose and establish again.
entries.literal: When Emperor Donghun lost virtue, Jiang You wished to establish the Prince of Xia, Bao Xuan, but at the end wavered again; with his brother Si he secretly told Tiao: "The Prince of Jiangxia is young, frivolous, and light—he cannot bear the regalia of the divine vessel; we cannot again carry out deposition and establishment.

entries.zh: 始安年長入纂，不乖物望。
entries.en: The Prince of Shi'an is older and would succeed without going against popular expectation.
entries.literal: The Prince of Shi'an is older in entering succession and does not go against popular expectation.

entries.zh: 非以此要富貴，政是求安國家耳。」
entries.en: We do not seek wealth and honor by this—we seek only the state's peace."
entries.literal: It is not by this to seek wealth and honor—it is truly to seek the state's peace."

entries.zh: 遙光又遣親人劉渢密致意於朓，欲以爲肺腑。
entries.en: Yaoguang also sent his confidant Liu Hong to convey his intentions secretly to Tiao, wishing to make him an intimate ally.
entries.literal: Yaoguang also sent his close man Liu Hong to convey intentions secretly to Tiao, wishing to make him a heart-and-belly confidant.

entries.zh: 朓自以受恩高宗，非渢所言，不肯答。
entries.en: Tiao considered that he owed his favor to the High Ancestor and would not accept what Hong said; he refused to reply.
entries.literal: Tiao himself thought he had received favor from the High Ancestor and that Hong's words were not acceptable; he refused to reply.

entries.zh: 少日，遙光以朓兼知衞尉事，朓懼見引，卽以祏等謀告左興盛，興盛不敢發言。
entries.en: A few days later Yaoguang had Tiao additionally manage the affairs of the Commandant of Guards; fearing entanglement, Tiao reported Shi and the others' plot to Zuo Xingsheng, who did not dare speak.
entries.literal: A few days later Yaoguang had Tiao additionally manage the affairs of the Commandant of Guards; Tiao feared being drawn in and at once reported Shi and the others' plot to Zuo Xingsheng, who did not dare speak out.

entries.zh: 祏聞，以告遙光，遙光大怒，乃稱敕召朓，仍回車付廷尉，與徐孝嗣、祏、暄等連名啓誅朓曰：「謝朓資性險薄，大彰遠近。
entries.en: Si heard and told Yaoguang, who was furious; summoning Tiao in the emperor's name, he turned him over to the Minister of Justice; with Xu Xiaosi, Si, Xuan, and others he jointly memorialized for Tiao's execution: "Xie Tiao's nature is treacherous and shallow, notorious far and near.
entries.literal: Si heard and told Yaoguang; Yaoguang was greatly enraged, then in the emperor's name summoned Tiao, turned the carriage back and handed him to the Minister of Justice; with Xu Xiaosi, Si, Xuan, and others he jointly memorialized to execute Tiao, saying: "Xie Tiao's nature is dangerous and thin, greatly manifest near and far.

entries.zh: 王敬則往構凶逆，微有誠效，自爾昇擢，超越倫伍。
entries.en: Wang Jingze had plotted treason; Tiao's small service in exposing it won promotion beyond his peers.
entries.literal: Wang Jingze formerly plotted treason; he had slight sincere effect, and from then was promoted beyond his rank and peers.

entries.zh: 而谿壑無厭，著於觸事。
entries.en: Yet his greed knew no limit, shown in everything he did.
entries.literal: Yet ravines and gullies know no satiety, manifest in whatever he touches.

entries.zh: 比遂扇動內外，處處姦說，妄貶乘輿，竊論宮禁，閒謗親賢，輕議朝宰，醜言異計，非可具聞。
entries.en: Recently he has stirred court and country, spreading treacherous talk everywhere, demeaning the throne, discussing palace secrets, slandering kin and worthies, and lightly attacking ministers—ugly words and strange schemes too numerous to list.
entries.literal: Recently he has stirred inside and outside, everywhere treacherous speech, recklessly demeaning the imperial carriage, privately discussing palace prohibitions, idly slandering kin and worthies, lightly debating court ministers—ugly words and strange schemes not to be fully heard.

entries.zh: 無君之心旣著，共棄之誅宜及。
entries.en: His disloyal heart is already plain; the punishment of collective rejection should fall on him.
entries.literal: His heart without a ruler is already manifest; the punishment of collective rejection should reach him.

entries.zh: 臣等參議，宜下北里，肅正刑書。」
entries.en: We jointly recommend that he be sent to prison and the penal code solemnly applied."
entries.literal: Your subjects jointly deliberate: he should be sent to North Lane and the penal code solemnly applied."

entries.zh: 詔：「公等啓事如此，朓資性輕險，久彰物議。
entries.en: The edict read: "Your report is as stated; Tiao's nature is frivolous and dangerous and has long been notorious.
entries.literal: An edict said: "Your report is thus; Tiao's nature is light and dangerous, long manifest in public discussion.

entries.zh: 直以彫蟲薄伎，見齒衣冠。
entries.en: He was admitted to the ranks of officials only for his petty literary skill.
entries.literal: Merely because of carving-insect petty skill he was counted among caps and robes.

entries.zh: 昔在渚宮，構扇蕃邸，日夜縱諛，仰窺俯畫。
entries.en: Formerly at the Isle Palace he stirred up the prince's household, flattering day and night, spying above and plotting below.
entries.literal: Formerly at the Isle Palace he plotted and fanned the prince's mansion, day and night indulging flattery, looking up to spy and looking down to scheme.

entries.zh: 及還京師，飜自宣露，江、漢無波，以爲己功。
entries.en: When he returned to the capital he boasted of it himself, claiming credit though the Yangzi and Han were calm.
entries.literal: When he returned to the capital he turned and exposed it himself—the Yangzi and Han without waves he took as his own achievement.

entries.zh: 素論於茲而盡，縉紳所以側目。
entries.en: Public opinion ended there, which is why officials looked askance at him.
entries.literal: Plain discussion ended here; that is why the girdled and sashed turned their eyes sidelong.

entries.zh: 去夏之事，頗有微誠，賞擢曲加，踰邁倫序，感悅未聞，陵競彌著。
entries.en: Last summer's affair showed some small loyalty, and reward was bent to promote him beyond his rank—yet no gratitude was heard, and his arrogance grew only worse.
entries.literal: Last summer's affair had some slight sincerity; reward and promotion were bent to add beyond rank and order—gratitude and joy were not heard, overbearing rivalry grew all the more manifest.

entries.zh: 遂復矯構風塵，妄惑朱紫，詆貶朝政，疑閒親賢。
entries.en: Then again he stirred up trouble, confusing high and low office, slandering the government and sowing doubt among kin and worthies.
entries.literal: Then again he falsely constructed wind and dust, recklessly confusing purple and red, slandering court governance, sowing doubt and estranging kin and worthies.

entries.zh: 巧言利口，見醜前志，涓流纖孽，作戒遠圖。
entries.en: Clever words and sharp tongue are condemned in the histories; small streams of evil make warnings for far-reaching plans.
entries.literal: Clever words and sharp tongue are seen as ugly in former records; trickling streams and slender evils make warnings for far-reaching plans.

entries.zh: 宜有少正之刑，以申去害之義。
entries.en: He should receive the punishment of Shaozheng, to declare the meaning of removing harm.
entries.literal: He should receive the punishment of Shaozheng, to declare the meaning of removing harm.

entries.zh: 便可收付廷尉，肅明國典。」
entries.en: Take him at once to the Minister of Justice and solemnly apply the state code."
entries.literal: He may at once be taken and handed to the Minister of Justice, solemnly clarifying the state code."

entries.zh: 又使御史中丞范岫奏收朓，下獄死。
entries.en: He also had Censor-in-Chief Fan Xiu memorialize to arrest Tiao; he was imprisoned and executed.
entries.literal: He also had Censor-in-Chief Fan Xiu memorialize to arrest Tiao; he was imprisoned and died.

entries.zh: 時年三十六。
entries.en: He was thirty-six years old.
entries.literal: He was then thirty-six years old.

entries.zh: 贊曰：元長穎脫，拊翼將飛。
entries.en: The praise says: Yuanchang was brilliant and ready, beating his wings to fly.
entries.literal: The praise says: Yuanchang was sharp and outstanding, beating wings about to fly.

entries.zh: 時來運往，身沒志違。
entries.en: The time came and fortune passed; he died and his will was thwarted.
entries.literal: The time came and fortune passed; the body perished and the will was thwarted.

entries.zh: 高宗始業，乃顧玄暉。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor began his enterprise, he turned to Xuanhui.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor began his enterprise, he then turned to Xuanhui.

entries.zh: 逢昏屬亂，先蹈禍機。
entries.en: Meeting a benighted age and chaotic times, he was first to tread the path of disaster.
entries.literal: Meeting a benighted age belonging to chaos, he first trod the mechanism of disaster.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：晉世遷宅江表，人無北歸之計，英霸作輔，芟定中原，彌見金德之不競也。
entries.en: The historian says: In the Jin age the court moved south of the Yangzi and men abandoned any plan to return north; when heroic ministers briefly reconquered the Central Plains, it only showed how far the Jin mandate had fallen.
entries.literal: The historian says: In the Jin age they moved their residence south of the Yangzi; men had no plan to return north. When heroic hegemons served as assistants and mowed down the Central Plains, it only showed all the more that the Jin virtue could not compete.

entries.zh: 元嘉再略河南，師旅傾覆，自此以來，攻伐寢議。
entries.en: In Yuanjia they again seized Henan, but the armies were destroyed; since then offensive war has scarcely been debated.
entries.literal: In Yuanjia they again seized Henan, but armies overturned and collapsed; from then on, campaigns and attacks ceased from discussion.

entries.zh: 雖有戰爭，事存保境。
entries.en: Though war continued, the aim remained merely to hold the borders.
entries.literal: Though there was war, the affair remained preserving the borders.

entries.zh: 王融生遇永明，軍國寧息，以文敏才華，不足進取，經略心旨，殷懃表奏。
entries.en: Wang Rong was born in the Yongming era, when army and state were at peace; his literary brilliance could not win advancement by office alone, so he poured his strategic vision into earnest memorials.
entries.literal: Wang Rong was born into Yongming, when army and state were tranquil; with literary quickness and talent insufficient for advancement by office, he put his strategic intent into earnest memorials.

entries.zh: 若使宮車未晏，有事邊關，融之報效，或不易限。
entries.en: If the emperor had not died young and trouble had arisen at the frontier, Rong's service might have been hard to limit.
entries.literal: If the imperial carriage had not yet grown late and there were affairs at the frontier passes, Rong's repayment of service might not have been easy to limit.

entries.zh: 夫經國體遠，許久爲難，而立功立事，信居物右，其賈誼終軍之流亞乎！
entries.en: To govern the state with far-reaching vision is acknowledged as difficult, yet to achieve real deeds truly stands above common things—is he not of the company of Jia Yi and Zhong Jun!
entries.literal: Governing the state and embodying the far—such is acknowledged as difficult; yet establishing achievement and establishing affairs truly stand to the right among things—is he not next after the stream of Jia Yi and Zhong Jun!

entries.zh: 除安成王征虜參軍，主簿，尚書殿中郎，出爲廬陵內史，豫州治中，太祖太傅相國主簿，祕書丞。
entries.en: He was appointed military aide to the Prince of Ancheng on the Pacification campaign staff, then recorder, palace secretariat attendant, and sent out as interior governor of Luling and Yuzhou administrator; he later served as recorder to the Founding Emperor in his capacities as grand tutor and chancellor of state, and as secretary director.
entries.literal: He was appointed Military Aide to the Prince of Ancheng as Pacifier of Barbarians, Recorder, Attendant in the Palace Secretariat, then sent out as Interior Governor of Luling, Administrator of Yuzhou, Recorder to the Founding Emperor as Grand Tutor and Chancellor of State, and Secretary Director.

entries.zh: 議駮國史，檀超以《天文志》紀緯序位度，《五行志》載當時祥沴，二篇所記，事用相懸，日蝕爲災，宜居《五行》。
entries.en: In debate over the national history he objected that Tan Chao's 《Astronomical Treatise》 recorded the ordering of coordinates and degrees while his 《Treatise on the Five Phases》 recorded contemporary omens and disasters—the two chapters covered overlapping material, and since solar eclipses are calamities they ought to fall under the 《Five Phases》.
entries.literal: He debated the national history: Tan Chao in the 《Astronomical Treatise》 recorded the ordering of celestial coordinates and degrees, while in the 《Treatise on the Five Phases》 he recorded contemporary portents and disasters—the subjects recorded in the two chapters overlapped in substance; solar eclipses as calamities properly belong under the 《Five Phases》.

entries.zh: 超欲立處士傳。
entries.en: Chao also wanted to create a separate "Biographies of Recluses."
entries.literal: Chao wished to establish a "Biographies of Recluses."

entries.zh: 彖曰：「夫事關業用，方得列其名行。
entries.en: Tuan said: "Only when someone's affairs bear on public service may one set down his name and conduct at length.
entries.literal: Tuan said: "Only when affairs touch upon public service may one record a person's name and conduct in full.

entries.zh: 今栖遁之士，排斥皇王，陵轢將相，此偏介之行，不可長風移俗，故遷書未傳，班史莫編。
entries.en: The recluses of today reject the throne and trample on generals and ministers—such eccentric conduct cannot be held up to reshape custom, which is why Sima Qian's history did not pass their lives down and Ban Gu's did not compile them.
entries.literal: Those who dwell in seclusion today reject the imperial house and look down on generals and ministers—this is an eccentric course of conduct; it cannot be made a model to shift custom by, hence the Records of the Historian did not transmit such lives, and the History of Han did not compile them.

entries.zh: 一介之善，無緣頓略，宜列其姓業，附出他篇。」
entries.en: A modest virtue cannot simply be dropped; list their surname and profession and attach it as a note in some other chapter."
entries.literal: A single act of goodness has no warrant for summary omission; one should list their surname and calling and append it within some other section."

entries.zh: 遷始興王友，固辭。
entries.en: He was appointed Friend of the Prince of Shixing but firmly declined the post.
entries.literal: He was transferred to be Friend of the Prince of Shixing but firmly declined.

entries.zh: 太祖使吏部尚書何戢宣旨令就。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor dispatched Minister of Personnel He Zhan with an edict commanding him to take up the appointment.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor sent Minister of Personnel He Zhan to deliver an edict ordering him to accept.

entries.zh: 遷中書郎，兼太子中庶子。
entries.en: He was promoted to secretariat attendant and concurrently served as vice director in the heir apparent's household.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Attendant of the Secretariat and concurrently served as Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

entries.zh: 又以中書兼御史中丞。
entries.en: He also retained his secretariat post while serving concurrently as imperial censor-in-chief.
entries.literal: He also held the secretariat post while concurrently serving as Imperial Censor-in-Chief.

entries.zh: 轉黃門郎，兼中丞如故。
entries.en: He was transferred to gentleman at the yellow gates while continuing to hold the censor-in-chief post as before.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, retaining his concurrent post as censor-in-chief as before.

entries.zh: 坐彈謝超宗簡奏依違，免官。
entries.en: He was dismissed from office because his impeachment memorial against Xie Chaozong had been equivocal and inconsistent.
entries.literal: Because in impeaching Xie Chaozong his memorial was evasive and inconsistent, he was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 尋補安西諮議、南平內史。
entries.en: Before long he was reappointed adviser on the Pacification of the West staff and interior governor of Nanping.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he was reappointed Adviser of the Pacification of the West and Interior Governor of Nanping.

entries.zh: 除黃門，未拜，仍轉長史、南郡內史，行荊州事。
entries.en: He was appointed gentleman at the yellow gates but had not yet assumed the post when he was transferred to chief clerk and interior governor of Nan commandery, with charge of Jingzhou affairs.
entries.literal: He was appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gates but had not yet received the investiture when he was transferred to Chief Clerk and Interior Governor of Nan Commandery, acting on Jingzhou affairs.

entries.zh: 還爲太子中庶子，本州大中正。
entries.en: He returned to the capital as Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household and Grand Rectifier of his home province.
entries.literal: He returned to serve as Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and as Senior Rectifier of his home province.

entries.zh: 出爲冠軍將軍、監吳興郡事。
entries.en: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Might with supervisory authority over Wu commandery.
entries.literal: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Might, supervising affairs of Wu Commandery.

entries.zh: 孔稚珪字德璋，會稽山陰人也。
entries.en: Kong Zhigui, whose style name was Dezhang, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.
entries.literal: Kong Zhigui, style name Dezhang, was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji Commandery.

entries.zh: 祖道隆，位侍中。
entries.en: His grandfather Daolong had served as palace attendant.
entries.literal: His grandfather Daolong held the post of Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 父靈產，泰始中，罷晉安太守。
entries.en: His father Lingchan had retired from the post of grand administrator of Jin'an during the Taishi era.
entries.literal: His father Lingchan, during the Taishi era, left office as Grand Administrator of Jin'an.

entries.zh: 有隱遁之懷，於禹井山立館，事道精篤，吉日於靜屋四向朝拜，涕泗滂遝。
entries.en: He cherished thoughts of withdrawal from the world; on Mount Yujing he built a lodge and practiced the Way with fervent devotion, and on auspicious days in a quiet chamber he bowed toward the four directions until tears streamed down his face.
entries.literal: He harbored a wish for reclusion; on Mount Yujing he established a lodge, practiced the Way with deep devotion, and on auspicious days in a quiet chamber bowed in worship toward the four directions, his tears streaming down in profusion.

entries.zh: 東出過錢塘北郭，輙於舟中遙拜杜子恭墓，自此至都，東向坐，不敢背側。
entries.en: When he traveled east and passed the north suburb of Qiantang he would bow from his boat toward the tomb of Du Zigong; from that point until he reached the capital he always sat facing east and never turned his back or even sideways.
entries.literal: When traveling east he passed the north suburb of Qiantang and always from his boat bowed toward the tomb of Du Zigong; from that point until he reached the capital he sat facing east and dared not turn his back or side to it.

entries.zh: 元徽中，爲中散、太中大夫。
entries.en: During the Yuanhui era he held the posts of regular attendant and grand master of the palace.
entries.literal: During the Yuanhui era he served as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace.

entries.zh: 頗解星文，好術數。
entries.en: He was well versed in astronomy and fond of occult calculation.
entries.literal: He was well versed in astral lore and fond of numerology and divination.

entries.zh: 太祖輔政，沈攸之起兵，靈產密白太祖曰：「攸之兵衆雖彊，以天時冥數而觀，無能爲也。」
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor was regent, Shen Youzhi rose in arms; Lingchan secretly told him: "Though Youzhi's troops are numerous, judged by the seasons of heaven and the hidden reckonings of fate, he can accomplish nothing."
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor was assisting in government, Shen Youzhi raised troops; Lingchan secretly reported to the Founding Emperor: "Though Youzhi's forces are strong, viewed in light of heaven's seasons and the hidden numbers, he can accomplish nothing."

entries.zh: 太祖驗其言，擢遷光祿大夫。
entries.en: The Founding Emperor found his prediction borne out and promoted him to grand master for the glorious.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor verified his words and promoted him to Grand Master for the Glorious.

entries.zh: 以簏盛靈產上靈臺，令其占候。
entries.en: He had Lingchan carried in a hamper up to the Observatory and ordered him to observe the heavens and report omens.
entries.literal: He had Lingchan carried in a bamboo hamper up to the Observatory and ordered him to observe and prognosticate.

entries.zh: 餉靈產白羽扇、素隱几。
entries.en: He sent Lingchan a white-feather fan and a plain armrest for reclining.
entries.literal: He presented Lingchan with a white-feather fan and a plain reclining armrest.

entries.zh: 曰：「君性好古，故遺君古物。」
entries.en: He said: "You love antiquity, so I give you these antique things."
entries.literal: He said: "Sir, you love antiquity, so I leave you these antique objects."

entries.zh: 劉繪字士章，彭城人，太常悛弟也。
entries.en: Liu Hui, whose style name was Shizhang, came from Pengcheng and was the younger brother of Minister of Ceremonies Jun.
entries.literal: Liu Hui, style name Shizhang, was a native of Pengcheng and younger brother of the Minister of Ceremonies Jun.

entries.zh: 父勉，宋末權貴，門多人客，使繪與之共語，應接流暢。
entries.en: His father Mian, a powerful figure at the end of Song, had many guests at his door; he had Hui converse with them, and his responses were fluent.
entries.literal: His father Mian, a powerful figure at the end of Song, had many guests at his door; he had Hui converse with them, and his responses were fluent.

entries.zh: 勉喜曰：「汝後若束帶立朝，可與賔客言矣。」
entries.en: Mian said with pleasure: "If later you gird yourself and stand at court, you may speak with guests."
entries.literal: Mian said with pleasure: "If later you gird yourself and stand at court, you may speak with guests."

entries.zh: 解褐著作郎，太祖太尉行參軍。
entries.en: Upon entering office he became compiler at the historian's office and acting aide on the staff of the Founding Emperor as grand commandant.
entries.literal: Upon leaving the commoner's garb he became Compiler at the Historian's Office and Acting Aide on the staff of the Founding Emperor as Grand Commandant.

entries.zh: 太祖見而歎曰：「劉公爲不亡也。」
entries.en: The Founding Emperor saw him and sighed: "Lord Liu is not dead after all."
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor saw him and sighed: "Lord Liu is not dead after all."

entries.zh: 稚珪少學涉，有美譽。
entries.en: Zhigui was widely read from his youth and enjoyed an excellent reputation.
entries.literal: Zhigui from youth was broadly learned and enjoyed a fine reputation.

entries.zh: 太守王僧虔見而重之，引爲主簿。
entries.en: Grand Administrator Wang Sengqian took notice of him and valued him, appointing him recorder.
entries.literal: Grand Administrator Wang Sengqian saw him and valued him, taking him on as Recorder.

entries.zh: 州舉秀才。
entries.en: The province recommended him as a provincial graduate.
entries.literal: The province recommended him as a provincial graduate.

entries.zh: 解褐宋安成王車騎法曹行參軍，轉尚書殿中郎。
entries.en: Upon entering office he served as acting aide in the law section on the staff of the Prince of Ancheng as cavalry general, then was transferred to palace secretariat attendant.
entries.literal: Upon leaving the commoner's garb he became Acting Aide in the Law Section on the staff of the Prince of Ancheng as Cavalry General, then was transferred to Attendant in the Palace Secretariat.

entries.zh: 太祖爲驃騎，以稚珪有文翰，取爲記室參軍，與江淹對掌辭筆。
entries.en: When the Founding Emperor held the post of rapid cavalry general, he recruited Zhigui for his literary gifts as headquarters recorder, pairing him with Jiang Yan to share responsibility for official prose.
entries.literal: When the Founding Emperor was Rapid Cavalry General, because Zhigui had literary talent he was taken on as Recorder in the Headquarters and shared charge of drafting with Jiang Yan.

entries.zh: 遷正員郎，中書郎，尚書左丞。
entries.en: He was promoted to regular attendant, secretariat attendant, and left assistant director of the imperial secretariat.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant, Attendant of the Secretariat, and Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 父憂去官，與兄仲智還居父山舍。
entries.en: When his father died he left office and returned with his elder brother Zhongzhi to live at their father's mountain retreat.
entries.literal: Upon his father's death he left office and, with his elder brother Zhongzhi, returned to dwell at their father's mountain lodge.

entries.zh: 仲智妾李氏驕妒無禮，稚珪白太守王敬則殺之。
entries.en: Zhongzhi's concubine Lady Li was arrogant, jealous, and insolent; Zhigui reported her to Grand Administrator Wang Jingze, who had her put to death.
entries.literal: Zhongzhi's concubine Lady Li was arrogant, jealous, and without propriety; Zhigui reported her to Grand Administrator Wang Jingze, who had her executed.

entries.zh: 服闋，爲司徒從事中郎，州治中，別駕，從事史，本郡中正。
entries.en: After mourning he served as attendant of the minister over the masses, provincial administrator, vice director, aide, and senior rectifier of his home commandery.
entries.literal: When mourning ended he served as Attendant of the Minister Over the Masses, Administrator of the province, Vice Director, Aide, and Senior Rectifier of his home commandery.

entries.zh: 彖性剛，嘗以微言忤世祖，又與王晏不協。
entries.en: Tuan was by nature inflexible; he had once offended the Emperor with an oblique remark, and he was also on bad terms with Wang Yan.
entries.literal: Tuan's nature was stubborn; he once gave offense to the Emperor through a subtle remark, and he was also at odds with Wang Yan.

entries.zh: 世祖在便殿，用金柄刀子治瓜，晏在側曰：「外間有金刀之言，恐不宜用此物。」
entries.en: The Emperor was in a side hall, cutting a melon with a gold-handled knife, when Yan beside him said: "There is talk abroad of a 'golden knife'—I fear it would be unwise to use such an object."
entries.literal: The Emperor was in the side hall, using a gold-handled knife to cut a melon, when Yan at his side said: "There is talk abroad of a 'golden knife'; I fear Your Majesty ought not use this object."

entries.zh: 世祖愕然，窮問所以。
entries.en: The Emperor was taken aback and pressed to know why.
entries.literal: The Emperor was startled and pressed to know the reason.

entries.zh: 晏曰：「袁彖爲臣說之。」
entries.en: Yan said: "Yuan Tuan told me this."
entries.literal: Yan said: "Yuan Tuan told this to your servant."

entries.zh: 上銜怒良久，彖到郡，坐逆用祿錢，免官付東冶。
entries.en: The sovereign nursed his anger for a long while; when Tuan reached his commandery he was charged with misappropriating salary funds, stripped of office, and consigned to the Eastern Workshop prison.
entries.literal: The sovereign harbored anger for a long time; when Tuan reached his commandery he was charged with improper use of salary funds, dismissed from office, and sent to the Eastern Workshop prison.

entries.zh: 世祖遊孫陵，望東冶，曰：「中有一好貴囚。」
entries.en: On an excursion to Sun Mound the Emperor looked toward the Eastern Workshop and said: "There is a fine gentleman among the prisoners there."
entries.literal: The Emperor visited Sun Mound and, gazing toward the Eastern Workshop, said: "Among them is one fine and noble prisoner."

entries.zh: 數日，車駕與朝臣幸冶，履行庫藏，因宴飲，賜囚徒酒肉，敕見彖與語，明日釋之。
entries.en: A few days later the imperial procession, with the court ministers, visited the workshop, toured the storehouses, and held a feast there, bestowing wine and meat on the prisoners; he ordered Tuan brought out to speak with him, and released him the following day.
entries.literal: Several days later the imperial carriage, with court ministers, visited the workshop, inspected the storehouses, and thereupon feasted; wine and meat were bestowed on the prisoners, and he ordered Tuan brought before him to converse; the next day he was released.

entries.zh: 尋白衣行南徐州事，司徒諮議，衞軍長史，遷侍中。
entries.en: Before long he was handling South Xuzhou affairs in unofficial dress, then served as adviser to the minister over the masses and chief clerk on the guards army staff, and was promoted to palace attendant.
entries.literal: Soon afterward he served the affairs of South Xuzhou in plain dress, then Adviser to the Minister Over the Masses, Chief Clerk of the Guards Army, and was promoted to Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 永明七年，轉驍騎將軍，復領左丞。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Yongming he was transferred to valiant cavalry general and again took charge as left assistant director.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Yongming he was transferred to Valiant Cavalry General and again headed the left assistant directorship.

entries.zh: 遷黃門郎，左丞如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to gentleman at the yellow gates while continuing as left assistant director as before.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates, retaining the left assistant directorship as before.

entries.zh: 轉太子中庶子，廷尉。
entries.en: He was transferred to Junior Mentor in the heir apparent's household and Chamberlain for Law Enforcement.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and Commandant of Punishments.

entries.zh: 江左相承用晉世張杜律二十卷，世祖留心法令，數訊囚徒，詔獄官詳正舊注。
entries.en: South of the Yangtze had long followed the Jin-era Zhang-Du code in twenty scrolls; the Emperor took a close interest in law, frequently interrogated prisoners himself, and ordered the prison officials to revise the old commentaries in detail.
entries.literal: South of the Yangtze had successively used the Jin-era Zhang-Du Code in twenty scrolls; the Emperor paid close attention to statutes and frequently examined prisoners, ordering prison officials to collate and correct the old commentaries.

entries.zh: 先是七年，尚書刪定郎王植撰定律章表奏之，曰：「臣尋《晉律》，文簡辭約，旨通大綱，事之所質，取斷難釋。
entries.en: Earlier, in the seventh year, Wang Zhi, editing and fixing attendant of the imperial secretariat, drafted the statutes and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has examined the 《Jin Code》: its text is spare and its language concise, its purport grasping the great outline, yet on the matters at issue judgments are hard to extract and apply.
entries.literal: Earlier, in the seventh year, Wang Zhi, Editing and Fixing Attendant of the Imperial Secretariat, drafted the statutes and memorialized them, saying: "Your servant has examined the 《Jin Code》: its text is concise and its language spare, its purport grasping the great outline, yet on the matters at issue judgment is hard to extract and explain.

entries.zh: 張斐杜預同注一章，而生殺永殊。
entries.en: Zhang Fei and Du Yu comment on the same article, yet their rulings on life and death forever diverge.
entries.literal: Zhang Fei and Du Yu comment on the same article, yet life and death are forever at odds.

entries.zh: 自晉泰始以來，唯斟酌參用。
entries.en: Since the Jin Taishi era officials have only weighed and applied them selectively.
entries.literal: From the Jin Taishi era onward, officials have only weighed and drawn on them selectively.

entries.zh: 是則吏挾威福之勢，民懷不對之怨，所以溫舒獻辭於失政，絳侯慷慨而興歎。
entries.en: Thus clerks wield arbitrary power while the people nurse grievances of unanswered justice—hence Wen Shu offered his remonstrance against misrule, and the Marquis of Jiang sighed aloud in indignation.
entries.literal: Thus clerks wield the power of authority and favor, while the people harbor grievances of unanswered justice—hence Wen Shu offered his remonstrance against misgovernment, and the Marquis of Jiang rose up sighing in indignation.

entries.zh: 皇運革祚，道冠前王，陛下紹興，光開帝業。
entries.en: Heaven has changed the mandate; Your Majesty's Way surpasses the kings of old; Your Majesty has succeeded and revived, brilliantly opening the imperial enterprise.
entries.literal: The imperial fortune has changed its mandate; Your Majesty's Way surpasses the kings of old; Your Majesty has succeeded and revived, brilliantly opening the imperial enterprise.

entries.zh: 下車之痛，每惻上仁，滿堂之悲，有矜聖思。
entries.en: The suffering of those newly in office touches Your Majesty's benevolence at every turn; the sorrow filling the hall awakens Your Majesty's compassionate concern.
entries.literal: The pain of those just come to office moves Your Majesty's benevolence at every turn; the sorrow filling the hall stirs Your Majesty's compassionate thought.

entries.zh: 爰發德音，刪正刑律，敕臣集定張杜二注。
entries.en: Thereupon Your Majesty issued a benevolent edict to revise the penal statutes and ordered your servant to assemble and fix the Zhang and Du commentaries.
entries.literal: Thereupon Your Majesty issued a virtuous edict to revise and correct the penal statutes, ordering your servant to assemble and fix the two commentaries of Zhang and Du.

entries.zh: 謹礪愚蒙，盡思詳撰，削其煩害，錄其允衷。
entries.en: Your servant has diligently applied his dull wit, exhausting thought in detailed compilation, cutting away what is cumbersome and harmful and recording what is fair and fitting.
entries.literal: Your servant has diligently sharpened his dull wit, exhausting thought in detailed compilation, cutting away what is cumbersome and harmful and recording what is fair and fitting.

entries.zh: 取張注七百三十一條，杜注七百九十一條。
entries.en: He took seven hundred thirty-one articles from Zhang's commentary and seven hundred ninety-one from Du's.
entries.literal: From Zhang's commentary he took seven hundred thirty-one articles; from Du's, seven hundred ninety-one.

entries.zh: 或二家兩釋，於義乃備者，又取一百七條。
entries.en: Where both schools offered paired explanations that together made the meaning complete, he took another one hundred seven articles.
entries.literal: Where both schools offered paired explanations that together made the meaning complete, he took another one hundred seven articles.

entries.zh: 其注相同者，取一百三條。
entries.en: Where the commentaries agreed, he took one hundred three articles.
entries.literal: Where the commentaries agreed, he took one hundred three articles.

entries.zh: 集爲一書。
entries.en: He assembled them into a single work.
entries.literal: He assembled them into one book.

entries.zh: 凡一千五百三十二條，爲二十卷。
entries.en: In all there were one thousand five hundred thirty-two articles in twenty scrolls.
entries.literal: In all there were one thousand five hundred thirty-two articles, in twenty scrolls.

entries.zh: 請付外詳校，擿其違謬。」
entries.en: I request that it be sent out for detailed collation so that errors and inconsistencies may be identified."
entries.literal: I request that it be sent out for detailed collation and that errors and inconsistencies be picked out."

entries.zh: 從之。
entries.en: The request was approved.
entries.literal: His request was approved.

entries.zh: 於是公卿八座參議，考正舊注。
entries.en: Thereupon the ministers and the eight chief offices deliberated together to examine and correct the old commentaries.
entries.literal: Thereupon the ministers and the eight chief offices joined in deliberation to examine and correct the old commentaries.

entries.zh: 有輕重處，竟陵王子良下意，多使從輕。
entries.en: Where questions of severity arose, the Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, issued instructions that generally favored the lighter penalty.
entries.literal: Where questions of severity arose, the Prince of Jingling, Zi Liang, issued instructions that generally favored the lighter penalty.

entries.zh: 其中朝議不能斷者，制旨平決。
entries.en: Points on which court debate could not reach a decision were settled by imperial rescript.
entries.literal: Among these, points on which court debate could not decide were settled by imperial rescript.

entries.zh: 至九年，稚珪上表曰：
entries.en: By the ninth year Zhigui submitted a memorial, saying:
entries.literal: By the ninth year Zhigui submitted a memorial, saying:

entries.zh: 尋古之名流，多有法學。
entries.en: Searching among the celebrated men of antiquity, many mastered legal studies.
entries.literal: Searching among the celebrated men of antiquity, many mastered legal studies.

entries.zh: 故釋之、定國，聲光漢臺；
entries.en: Hence Shizhi and Dingguo, their fame shining on the Han terrace;
entries.literal: Hence Shizhi and Dingguo, their fame shining on the Han terrace;

entries.zh: 元常、文惠，績映魏閣。
entries.en: Yuanchang and Wenhui, their achievements reflected in the Wei pavilion.
entries.literal: Yuanchang and Wenhui, their achievements reflected in the Wei pavilion.

entries.zh: 今之士子，莫肯爲業，縱有習者，世議所輕。
entries.en: Today's scholars refuse to make it their profession; even those who study it are slighted in public opinion.
entries.literal: Today's scholars refuse to make it their profession; even those who study it are slighted in public opinion.

entries.zh: 良由空懃永歲，不逢一朝之賞，積學當年，終爲閭伍所蚩。
entries.en: Truly because they toil empty years without meeting a single morning's reward, amassing learning for years only to be mocked by their neighborhood in the end.
entries.literal: Truly because they toil empty years without meeting a single morning's reward, amassing learning for years only to be mocked by their neighborhood in the end.

entries.zh: 將恐此書永墜下走之手矣。
entries.en: I fear this book will forever fall into the hands of low runners.
entries.literal: I fear this book will forever fall into the hands of low runners.

entries.zh: 今若弘其爵賞，開其勸慕，課業宦流，班習冑子，拔其精究，使處內局，簡其才良，以居外仕，方岳咸選其能，邑長竝擢其術，則皐繇之謨，指掌可致，杜鄭之業，鬱焉何遠。
entries.en: Now if we enlarge their ranks and rewards, open paths of encouragement, set examinations for officials in service, extend instruction to imperial scions, select those of penetrating mastery to place in inner bureaus, choose the talented and good to hold outer posts, have regional governors all select for ability and district chiefs together promote for skill—then Gao Yao's counsels could be attained at a gesture, and the achievements of Du and Zheng, how distant could they be?
entries.literal: Now if we enlarge their ranks and rewards, open paths of encouragement, set examinations for officials in service, extend instruction to imperial scions, select those of penetrating mastery to place in inner bureaus, choose the talented and good to hold outer posts, have regional governors all select for ability and district chiefs together promote for skill—then Gao Yao's counsels could be attained at a gesture, and the achievements of Du and Zheng, how distant could they be?

entries.zh: 然後姦邪無所逃其刑，惡吏不能藏其詐，如身手之相驅，若絃栝之相接矣。
entries.en: Then the wicked would have nowhere to escape punishment, and evil clerks could not hide their fraud—as hand and body drive each other, as bowstring and frame join together.
entries.literal: Then the wicked would have nowhere to escape punishment, and evil clerks could not hide their fraud—as hand and body drive each other, as bowstring and frame join together.

entries.zh: 匈奴爲患，自古而然，雖三代智勇，兩漢權奇，筭略之要，二塗而已。
entries.en: The Xiongnu have been a scourge since antiquity; though the Three Dynasties had wisdom and courage and the Two Han had resourceful stratagems, the essentials of calculation and planning are only two paths.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu have been a scourge since antiquity; though the Three Dynasties had wisdom and courage and the Two Han had resourceful stratagems, the essentials of calculation and planning are only two paths.

entries.zh: 一則鐵馬風馳，奮威沙漠；
entries.en: One is iron horses racing with the wind, exerting might in the desert;
entries.literal: One is iron horses racing with the wind, exerting might in the desert;

entries.zh: 二則輕車出使，通驛虜庭。
entries.en: the other is light carriages sent on embassy, opening post roads to the barbarian court.
entries.literal: the other is light carriages sent on embassy, opening post roads to the barbarian court.

entries.zh: 搉而言之，優劣可睹。
entries.en: Weighing them together, their relative merit is plain to see.
entries.literal: Weighing them together, their relative merit is plain to see.

entries.zh: 今之議者，咸以丈夫之氣，恥居物下，況我天威，寧可先屈？
entries.en: Those who debate today all invoke manly spirit and shrink from standing beneath others; how much more under our heavenly majesty—could we yield first?
entries.literal: Those who debate today all take manly spirit and shrink from standing beneath others; how much more under our heavenly majesty—could we bow first?

entries.zh: 吳、楚勁猛，帶甲百萬，截彼鯨鯢，何往不碎？
entries.en: Wu and Chu are fierce and strong, with a million armored men—cut down those whales and krakens, where would they not be shattered?
entries.literal: Wu and Chu are fierce and strong, with a million armored men—cut down those whales and krakens, where would they not be shattered?

entries.zh: 請和示弱，非國計也。
entries.en: To sue for peace and show weakness is no state policy.
entries.literal: To sue for peace and show weakness is no state policy.

entries.zh: 臣以爲戎狄獸性，本非人倫，鴟鳴狼踞，不足喜怒，蜂目蠆尾，何關美惡。
entries.en: Your servant holds that the Rong and Di have the nature of beasts and fundamentally belong outside human relations—the owl's cry and wolf's crouch are not worth joy or anger; wasp eyes and scorpion tails have nothing to do with beauty or ugliness.
entries.literal: Your servant holds that the Rong and Di have the nature of beasts and fundamentally belong outside human relations—the owl's cry and wolf's crouch are not worth joy or anger; wasp eyes and scorpion tails have nothing to do with beauty or ugliness.

entries.zh: 唯宜勝之以深權，制之以遠，弘之以大度，處之以蟊賊。
entries.en: One should only overcome them with deep strategy, control them from afar, magnify them with great forbearance, and treat them as grain-devouring pests.
entries.literal: One should only overcome them with deep strategy, control them from afar, magnify them with great forbearance, and treat them as grain-devouring pests.

entries.zh: 豈足肆天下之忿，捐蒼生之命，發雷電之怒，爭蟲鳥之氣。
entries.en: How could one unleash the world's wrath, cast away the lives of the black-haired people, loose thunder-and-lightning anger, and contend over the spirit of insects and birds?
entries.literal: How could one unleash the world's wrath, cast away the lives of the black-haired people, loose thunder-and-lightning anger, and contend over the spirit of insects and birds?

entries.zh: 百戰百勝，不足稱雄，橫尸千里，無益上國。
entries.en: A hundred battles, a hundred victories—insufficient to be called heroic; corpses strewn for a thousand li—of no benefit to the superior state.
entries.literal: A hundred battles, a hundred victories—insufficient to be called heroic; corpses strewn for a thousand li—of no benefit to the superior state.

entries.zh: 而蟻聚蠶攢，窮誅不盡，馬足毛羣，難與競逐。
entries.en: Yet they gather like ants and swarm like silkworms; pursued to the end they cannot be exterminated—a flock at every horse's hoof, hard to race against.
entries.literal: Yet they gather like ants and swarm like silkworms; pursued to the end they cannot be exterminated—a flock at every horse's hoof, hard to race against.

entries.zh: 漢高橫威海表，窘迫長圍；
entries.en: Emperor Gaozu of Han swept might across the sea's margin yet was pressed hard in prolonged siege;
entries.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han swept might across the sea's margin yet was pressed hard in prolonged siege;

entries.zh: 孝文國富刑清，事屈陵辱；
entries.en: Emperor Xiaowen made the state rich and punishments clear, yet affairs bent to insult and humiliation;
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaowen made the state rich and punishments clear, yet affairs bent to insult and humiliation;

entries.zh: 宣帝撫納安靜，朔馬不驚；
entries.en: Emperor Xuandi soothed and accepted them into quiet, and the northern horses were not startled;
entries.literal: Emperor Xuandi soothed and accepted them into quiet, and the northern horses were not startled;

entries.zh: 光武卑辭厚禮，寒山無靄。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu used humble words and generous gifts, and the cold mountains knew no mist.
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu used humble words and generous gifts, and the cold mountains knew no mist.

entries.zh: 是兩京四主，英濟中區，輸寶貨以結和，遣宗女以通好，長轡遠馭，子孫是賴。
entries.en: These two capitals and four sovereigns brilliantly aided the central realm, sending treasure to seal peace and dispatching imperial daughters to open friendship—reins held far, descendants thereby secured.
entries.literal: These two capitals and four sovereigns brilliantly aided the central realm, sending treasure to seal peace and dispatching imperial daughters to open friendship—reins held far, descendants thereby secured.

entries.zh: 豈不欲戰，惜民命也。
entries.en: Was it that they did not wish to fight? They cherished the people's lives.
entries.literal: Was it that they did not wish to fight? They cherished the people's lives.

entries.zh: 唯漢武藉五世之資，承六合之富，驕心奢志，大事匈奴。
entries.en: Only Emperor Wu of Han, relying on five generations' accumulation and inheriting the wealth of the six directions, with proud heart and extravagant will, made the Xiongnu his great enterprise.
entries.literal: Only Emperor Wu of Han, relying on five generations' accumulation and inheriting the wealth of the six directions, with proud heart and extravagant will, made the Xiongnu his great enterprise.

entries.zh: 遂連兵積歲，轉戰千里，長驅瀚海，飲馬龍城，雖斬獲名王，屠走凶羯，而漢之卒甲十亡其九。
entries.en: Thereupon he linked armies year after year, battled across a thousand li, drove far into the Han Sea, watered horses at Dragon City—though he beheaded famous kings and slaughtered fleeing fierce Jie, nine-tenths of Han's soldiers and armor perished.
entries.literal: Thereupon he linked armies year after year, battled across a thousand li, drove far into the Han Sea, watered horses at Dragon City—though he beheaded famous kings and slaughtered fleeing fierce Jie, nine-tenths of Han's soldiers and armor perished.

entries.zh: 故衞霍出關，千隊不反，貳師入漠，百旅頓降，李廣敗於前鋒，李陵沒於後陣，其餘奔北，不可勝數。
entries.en: Thus, when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing campaigned beyond the passes, a thousand companies failed to return; when the General of Ershi entered the desert, a hundred formations surrendered at once. Li Guang was defeated in the vanguard and Li Ling was lost in the rear; the others who fled in defeat were beyond counting.
entries.literal: Hence when Wei Qing and Huo Qubing went beyond the passes, a thousand companies did not return; when the General of Ershi entered the desert, a hundred hosts collapsed in surrender; Li Guang was defeated at the vanguard, Li Ling was lost at the rear; the rest fled in defeat in numbers beyond counting.

entries.zh: 遂使國儲空懸，戶口減半，好戰之功，其利安在？
entries.en: Thus state stores hung empty and registered households were halved—where lay the profit in loving war?
entries.literal: Thus state stores hung empty and registered households were halved—where lay the profit in loving war?

entries.zh: 戰不及和，相去何若？
entries.en: How does war compare with peace—how far apart are they?
entries.literal: How does war compare with peace—how far apart are they?

entries.zh: 稚珪風韻清疏，好文詠，飲酒七八斗。
entries.en: Zhigui's bearing and charm were clear and spare; he loved literary composition and song, and could drink seven or eight dou of wine.
entries.literal: Zhigui's bearing and charm were clear and spare; he loved literary composition and song, and could drink seven or eight dou of wine.

entries.zh: 與外兄張融情趣相得，又與琅邪王思遠、廬江何點、點弟胤竝款交。
entries.en: With his cousin by marriage Zhang Rong he matched in temperament and taste; he also had warm friendships with Wang Siyuan of Langye, He Dian of Lujiang, and Dian's younger brother Yin.
entries.literal: With his cousin by marriage Zhang Rong he matched in temperament and taste; he also had warm friendships with Wang Siyuan of Langye, He Dian of Lujiang, and Dian's younger brother Yin.

entries.zh: 不樂世務，居宅盛營山水，憑机獨酌，傍無雜事。
entries.en: He took no joy in worldly affairs; his residence lavishly arranged mountains and waters—leaning on his armrest he drank alone, with nothing else beside him.
entries.literal: He took no joy in worldly affairs; his residence lavishly arranged mountains and waters—leaning on his armrest he drank alone, with nothing else beside him.

entries.zh: 門庭之內，草萊不剪，中有蛙鳴，或問之曰：「欲爲陳蕃乎？」
entries.en: Within his gates and courtyard the grass was not cut; frogs croaked within, and someone asked him: "Do you wish to be like Chen Fan?"
entries.literal: Within his gates and courtyard the grass was not cut; frogs croaked within, and someone asked him: "Do you wish to be like Chen Fan?"

entries.zh: 稚珪笑曰：「我以此當兩部鼓吹，何必期效仲舉。」
entries.en: Zhigui laughed and said: "I take this as music from both orchestras—why must I expect to emulate Zhongju?"
entries.literal: Zhigui laughed and said: "I take this as music from both orchestras—why must I expect to emulate Zhongju?"

entries.zh: 永明末，京邑人士盛爲文章談義，皆湊竟陵王西邸。
entries.en: At the end of Yongming, gentlemen of the capital flourished in literary composition and discourses on principle, all gathering at the western residence of the Prince of Jingling.
entries.literal: At the end of Yongming, capital gentlemen flourished in literary composition and discourses on principle, all gathering at the western residence of the Prince of Jingling.

entries.zh: 繪爲後進領袖，機悟多能。
entries.en: Hui stood at the head of the younger generation, quick-witted and multitalented.
entries.literal: Hui was leader among the younger generation, quick-witted and multitalented.

entries.zh: 時張融、周顒竝有言工，融音旨緩韻，顒辭致綺捷，繪之言吐，又頓挫有風氣。
entries.en: At the time Zhang Rong and Zhou Yong both excelled in speech: Rong's tones were leisurely in cadence, Yong's phrasing elegant and swift, while Hui's utterance was further marked by rhythmic pauses and spirited bearing.
entries.literal: At the time Zhang Rong and Zhou Yong both excelled in speech: Rong's tones were leisurely in cadence, Yong's phrasing elegant and swift, while Hui's utterance was further marked by rhythmic pauses and spirited bearing.

entries.zh: 時人爲之語曰：「劉繪貼宅，別開一門。」
entries.en: People of the time had a saying: "Liu Hui adjoins the house and opens a separate gate."
entries.literal: People of the time made a saying of it: "Liu Hui adjoins the house and opens a separate gate."

entries.zh: 言在二家之中也。
entries.en: Meaning he stood between the two houses.
entries.literal: Meaning he stood between the two houses.

entries.zh: 豫章王嶷爲江州，以繪爲左軍主簿。
entries.en: When the Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, took up the governorship of Jiang province, he appointed Hui recorder of the left army.
entries.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, became governor of Jiang Province and appointed Hui Recorder of the Left Army.

entries.zh: 隨鎮江陵，轉鎮西外兵曹參軍，驃騎主簿。
entries.en: He followed the garrison to Jiangling, then served as military aide in the external troops section of the Pacification of the West and as recorder on the rapid cavalry general's staff.
entries.literal: He followed the garrison to Jiangling and was transferred to Military Aide in the External Troops Section of the Pacification of the West, then Recorder on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General.

entries.zh: 繪聦警有文義，善隷書，數被賞召，進對華敏，僚吏之中，見遇莫及。
entries.en: Hui was keen-witted and literarily accomplished, skilled in clerical script; repeatedly summoned to court, he answered with brilliant quickness in audience—among the staff none was favored like him.
entries.literal: Hui was keen-witted and possessed literary discernment, skilled in clerical script; he was repeatedly summoned for reward, and in audience his responses were brilliant and quick—among the staff none was favored as he was.

entries.zh: 琅邪王詡爲功曹，以吏能自進。
entries.en: Wang Xu of Langye served as merit evaluator and advanced himself through bureaucratic competence.
entries.literal: Wang Xu of Langye served as Merit Evaluator and advanced himself through bureaucratic competence.

entries.zh: 嶷謂僚佐曰：「吾雖不能得應嗣陳蕃，然閤下自有二驥也。」
entries.en: Yan told his staff: "Though I cannot find a successor to Chen Fan, within my gate there are two fine steeds all the same."
entries.literal: Yan said to his staff: "Though I cannot obtain one to answer to Chen Fan, yet within my gate there are two fine steeds."

entries.zh: 復爲司空記室錄事，轉太子洗馬，大司馬諮議，領錄事。
entries.en: He later served as Record-Office and Registry Officer for the Minister of Works, was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent and adviser to the Grand Marshal, and headed the registry office.
entries.literal: He again served as Recorder in the Headquarters of the Minister of Works, was transferred to Groom of the Heir Apparent, Adviser to the Grand Marshal, and headed the recording office.

entries.zh: 時豫章王嶷與文惠太子以年秩不同，物論謂宮、府有疑，繪苦求外出，爲南康相。
entries.en: At the time the Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, and the Literary and Graceful Heir Apparent differed in age and rank; rumor held that palace and princely establishment were at odds, and Hui pressed hard to leave the capital, becoming chancellor of Nankang.
entries.literal: At the time the Prince of Yuzhang, Yan, and the Literary and Graceful Heir Apparent differed in age and rank; public opinion held that palace and princely establishment harbored mutual suspicion, and Hui bitterly sought to go out, becoming Chancellor of Nankang.

entries.zh: 郡事之暇，專意講說。
entries.en: Whenever commandery duties allowed, he devoted himself entirely to lecturing.
entries.literal: In the leisure of commandery affairs he devoted himself entirely to lecturing.

entries.zh: 上左右陳洪請假南還，問繪在郡何似？
entries.en: The sovereign's attendant Chen Hong requested leave to return south and was asked how Hui was faring in the commandery?
entries.literal: The sovereign's attendant Chen Hong requested leave to return south and was asked how Hui was doing in the commandery?

entries.zh: 旣而閒之曰：「南康是三州喉舌，應須治幹。
