entries.en: Afterward he remarked: "Nankang is the throat and tongue of three provinces; it requires a capable administrator.
entries.literal: Afterward he mentioned in conversation: "Nankang is the throat and tongue of three provinces; it requires a capable administrator.

entries.zh: 豈可以年少講學處之邪？」
entries.en: How can one put a young lecturer in charge there?"
entries.literal: How can one place there a young man who lectures on learning?"

entries.zh: 徵還爲安陸王護軍司馬，轉中書郎，掌詔誥。
entries.en: He was recalled and made chief of staff to the guards army of the Prince of Anlu, then transferred to secretariat attendant in charge of edicts and proclamations.
entries.literal: He was recalled and made Chief of Staff to the Guards Army of the Prince of Anlu, then transferred to Attendant of the Secretariat in charge of edicts and proclamations.

entries.zh: 敕助國子祭酒何胤撰治禮儀。
entries.en: He was ordered to assist National University rector He Yin in compiling and ordering ritual and ceremony.
entries.literal: He was ordered to assist the National University Rector He Yin in compiling and ordering ritual and ceremony.

entries.zh: 事兄悛恭謹，與人語，呼爲「使君」。
entries.en: In serving his elder brother Jun he was respectful and careful; in speaking with others he addressed him as "My Lord."
entries.literal: In serving his elder brother Jun he was respectful and careful; in speaking with others he addressed him as "My Lord."

entries.zh: 隆昌中，悛坐罪將見誅，繪伏闕請代兄死，高宗輔政，救解之。
entries.en: During Longchang, Jun was charged with a crime and about to be executed; Hui prostrated himself at the palace gate and asked to die in his brother's place; the High Ancestor, assisting in government, rescued and released him.
entries.literal: During Longchang, Jun was charged with a crime and about to be executed; Hui prostrated himself at the palace gate and asked to die in his brother's place; the High Ancestor, assisting in government, rescued and released him.

entries.zh: 引爲鎮軍長史，轉黃門郎。
entries.en: He was brought in as chief clerk of the suppression army and transferred to gentleman at the yellow gates.
entries.literal: He was brought in as Chief Clerk of the Suppression Army and transferred to Gentleman at the Yellow Gates.

entries.zh: 高宗爲驃騎，以繪爲輔國將軍，諮議，領錄事，典筆翰。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor was rapid cavalry general, he made Hui general who assists the state and adviser, head of the recording office, and in charge of brush and documents.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor was Rapid Cavalry General, he made Hui General Who Assists the State, Adviser, head of the recording office, and in charge of brush and documents.

entries.zh: 高宗卽位，遷太子中庶子，出爲寧朔將軍、撫軍長史。
entries.en: When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, Hui was transferred to vice director in the heir apparent's household and sent out as pacification general and chief clerk of the pacification army.
entries.literal: When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, Hui was transferred to Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household and sent out as Pacification General and Chief Clerk of the Pacification Army.

entries.zh: 帝不納。
entries.en: The Emperor did not accept it.
entries.literal: The Emperor did not accept it.

entries.zh: 徵侍中，不行，留本任。
entries.en: He was summoned as palace attendant but did not go, remaining in his original post.
entries.literal: He was summoned as Palace Attendant but did not go, remaining in his original post.

entries.zh: 轉御史中丞，遷驃騎長史，輔國將軍。
entries.en: He was transferred to imperial censor-in-chief, then promoted to chief clerk of the rapid cavalry general and general who assists the state.
entries.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Censor-in-Chief, then promoted to Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry General and General Who Assists the State.

entries.zh: 建武初，遷冠軍將軍、平西長史、南郡太守。
entries.en: At the beginning of Jianwu he was transferred to General Who Establishes Might, chief clerk of the Pacification of the West, and grand administrator of Nan commandery.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu he was transferred to General Who Establishes Might, Chief Clerk of the Pacification of the West, and Grand Administrator of Nan Commandery.

entries.zh: 稚珪以虜連歲南侵，征役不息，百姓死傷。
entries.en: Because the barbarians had invaded the south year after year, corvée labor never ceased, and the common people were dying and wounded, Zhigui
entries.literal: Zhigui, because the barbarians for successive years invaded southward and corvée labor never ceased, with the common people dying and wounded,

entries.zh: 乃上表曰：
entries.en: submitted a memorial, saying:
entries.literal: submitted a memorial, saying:

entries.zh: 弟瑱，字士溫。
entries.en: His younger brother Zhen, whose style name was Shiwen.
entries.literal: His younger brother Zhen, style name Shiwen.

entries.zh: 好文章，飲酒奢逸，不𠫤財物。
entries.en: He loved literature, drank lavishly, and was free-handed with his possessions.
entries.literal: He loved literature, drank wine in luxurious excess, and was not stingy with possessions.

entries.zh: 滎陽毛惠遠善畫馬，瑱善畫婦人，世竝爲第一。
entries.en: Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang excelled at painting horses; Zhen excelled at painting women—both were ranked first in their day.
entries.literal: Mao Huiyuan of Xingyang was skilled at painting horses; Zhen was skilled at painting women—both were ranked first in the age.

entries.zh: 官至吏部郎。
entries.en: He rose to the post of attendant of the ministry of personnel.
entries.literal: He reached the post of Attendant of the Ministry of Personnel.

entries.zh: 先繪卒。
entries.en: He died before Hui.
entries.literal: He died before Hui.

entries.zh: 史臣曰：刑禮相望，勸戒之道，淺識言治，莫辯後先，故宰世之堤防，御民之羈絆。
entries.en: The historiographer says: Punishment and ritual face each other—the way of admonition and warning. Those of shallow understanding speak of governance yet cannot distinguish what comes first and after; hence the dikes of one who governs the age and the halters that restrain the people.
entries.literal: The historiographer says: Punishment and ritual face each other—the way of admonition and warning. Those of shallow understanding speak of governance yet cannot distinguish what comes first and after; hence the dikes of one who governs the age and the halters that restrain the people.

entries.zh: 端簡爲政，貴在畫一，輕重屢易，手足無從。
entries.en: Upright and simple in government, what is prized is uniformity; when severity and leniency change repeatedly, hands and feet have nowhere to go.
entries.literal: Upright and simple in government, what is prized is uniformity; when severity and leniency change repeatedly, hands and feet have nowhere to go.

entries.zh: 律令之本，文約旨曠，據典行罰，各用情求。
entries.en: The root of statutes and ordinances: text spare, purport broad; according to the canon punishments are applied, each case judged by its particular circumstances.
entries.literal: The root of statutes and ordinances: text spare, purport broad; according to the canon punishments are applied, each case judged by its particular circumstances.

entries.zh: 舒慘之意旣殊，寬猛之利亦異，辭有出沒，義生增損。
entries.en: The intent behind leniency and severity already differs; the benefit of clemency and harshness also varies—phrasing has its appearances and disappearances, and meaning gives rise to additions and subtractions.
entries.literal: The intent behind leniency and severity already differs; the benefit of clemency and harshness also varies—phrasing has its appearances and disappearances, and meaning gives rise to additions and subtractions.

entries.zh: 舊尹之事，政非一途，後主所是，卽爲成用。
entries.en: Matters of former magistrates follow no single path; what a later ruler approves immediately becomes established practice.
entries.literal: Matters of former magistrates follow no single path; what a later ruler approves immediately becomes established practice.

entries.zh: 張弛代積，稍至遷訛。
entries.en: Tightening and loosening accumulate generation by generation, gradually leading to drift and error.
entries.literal: Tightening and loosening accumulate generation by generation, gradually leading to drift and error.

entries.zh: 故刑開二門，法有兩路，刀筆之態深，舞弄之風起。
entries.en: Hence punishment opens two gates and law has two paths; the manner of brush and knife runs deep, and the wind of manipulation rises.
entries.literal: Hence punishment opens two gates and law has two paths; the manner of brush and knife runs deep, and the wind of manipulation rises.

entries.zh: 承喜怒之機隙，挾千金之奸利，剪韭復生，寧失有罪，抱木牢戶，未必非冤。
entries.en: Seizing the opportune gaps of joy and anger, clutching thousand-gold bribes of wicked profit—cut leeks and they grow again; better to let the guilty go than to clasp wood at the prison gate when the accused may not be wronged.
entries.literal: Seizing the opportune gaps of joy and anger, clutching thousand-gold bribes of wicked profit—cut leeks and they grow again; better to let the guilty go than to clasp wood at the prison gate when the accused may not be wronged.

entries.zh: 下吏上司，文簿從事，辯聲察色，莫用衿府，申枉理讞，急不在躬，案法隨科，幸無咎悔。
entries.en: Lower clerks and higher superiors, documents and records in hand, judge by voice and scrutinize expression, none employing the breast of judgment; to plead injustice and reason out legal disputes is urgent yet not in one's own person—follow the statute by category and hope for no blame or regret.
entries.literal: Lower clerks and higher superiors, documents and records in hand, judge by voice and scrutinize expression, none employing the breast of judgment; to plead injustice and reason out legal disputes is urgent yet not in one's own person—follow the statute by category and hope for no blame or regret.

entries.zh: 至於郡縣親民，百務萌始，以情矜過，曾不待獄，以律定罪，無細非諐。
entries.en: As for commanderies and counties close to the people, where the hundred affairs first sprout—showing mercy for faults by feeling, sometimes without even awaiting trial; fixing guilt by statute, no detail not an offense.
entries.literal: As for commanderies and counties close to the people, where the hundred affairs first sprout—showing mercy for faults by feeling, sometimes without even awaiting trial; fixing guilt by statute, no detail not an offense.

entries.zh: 蓋由網密憲煩，文理相背。
entries.en: This is because the net is dense, the statutes burdensome, and text and principle oppose each other.
entries.literal: This is because the net is dense, the statutes burdensome, and text and principle oppose each other.

entries.zh: 夫懲恥難窮，盜賊長有，欲求猛勝，事在或然，掃墓高門，爲利孰遠。
entries.en: For shame in punishment is hard to exhaust and thieves and bandits ever exist; to seek triumph through harshness is a matter of mere chance—sweeping tombs and lofty gates, which profit is farther off.
entries.literal: For shame in punishment is hard to exhaust and thieves and bandits ever exist; to seek triumph through harshness is a matter of mere chance—sweeping tombs and lofty gates, which profit is farther off.

entries.zh: 故永明定律，多用優寬，治物不患仁心，見累於弘厚，爲令貴在必行，而惡其舛雜也。
entries.en: Therefore the statutes of Yongming largely used leniency and breadth; in governing things one need not fear a benevolent heart, though one may be encumbered by expansive generosity—what is prized in ordinances is that they must be carried out, while what is hated is their confusion and mixture.
entries.literal: Therefore the statutes of Yongming largely used leniency and breadth; in governing things one need not fear a benevolent heart, though one may be encumbered by expansive generosity—what is prized in ordinances is that they must be carried out, while what is hated is their confusion and mixture.

entries.zh: 南齊書卷卷四十八‧列傳第二十九
entries.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 48, Biographies 29
entries.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 48, Biographies 29

entries.zh: 昇明初，遷冠軍將軍、丹陽尹。
entries.en: At the opening of the Shengming era he was transferred to General Who Establishes Valor and Intendant of Danyang.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Shengming he was moved to General Who Establishes Valor and Intendant of Danyang.

entries.zh: 初，王晏父普曜爲沈攸之長史，常慮攸之舉事，不得還。
entries.en: Earlier, Wang Yan's father Puyao had served as chief administrator to Shen Youzhi and had long worried that Youzhi would rebel and that he would never get home.
entries.literal: Earlier, Wang Yan's father Puyao had been chief administrator to Shen Youzhi and had constantly feared that Youzhi would raise troops and that he would not be able to return.

entries.zh: 時奐爲吏部，轉普曜爲內職，晏深德之。
entries.en: When Huan headed the Ministry of Personnel he transferred Puyao to a capital post, for which Yan felt deep gratitude.
entries.literal: At that time Huan was in the Ministry of Personnel and transferred Puyao to an inner-office post; Yan was deeply grateful.

entries.zh: 及晏仕世祖府，奐從弟蘊反，世祖謂晏曰：「王奐宋家外戚，王蘊親同逆黨，旣其羣從，豈能無異意。
entries.en: When Yan took office in Emperor Shizu's princely household, Huan's cousin Yun rose in rebellion. Shizu said to Yan, "Wang Huan is a Song imperial in-law, and Wang Yun is close kin to the rebels. Men of the same clan—how can they not harbor divided loyalties?
entries.literal: When Yan entered service in the heir's household of Emperor Shizu, Huan's cousin Yun rebelled. Shizu said to Yan: "Wang Huan is a maternal kinsman of the Song house; Wang Yun is kin to the rebel faction. Since they are of the same clan, how could there be no divergent intent?

entries.zh: 我欲具以啓聞。」
entries.en: I intend to lay the whole matter before the throne."
entries.literal: I wish to report the whole matter fully."

entries.zh: 晏叩頭曰：「王奐脩謹，保無異志。
entries.en: Yan kowtowed and said, "Wang Huan is scrupulous and restrained; I warrant that he harbors no disloyal intent.
entries.literal: Yan kowtowed and said: "Wang Huan is cultivated and cautious; I guarantee he has no divergent intent.

entries.zh: 晏父母在都，請以爲質。」
entries.en: My parents are in the capital—let them stand as hostages for him."
entries.literal: Yan's parents are in the capital; I ask that they be held as hostages."

entries.zh: 世祖乃止。
entries.en: Shizu thereupon dropped the matter.
entries.literal: Shizu then desisted.

entries.zh: 世祖卽位，徵右僕射。
entries.en: When Shizu ascended the throne, Huan was recalled as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
entries.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Huan was summoned as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

entries.zh: 仍轉使持節監湘州軍事、前將軍、湘州刺史，
entries.en: He was soon transferred to bearer of the staff of authority supervising military affairs in Xiang Province, with the ranks of General of the Van and Governor of Xiang Province.
entries.literal: He was then transferred as bearer of the staff of authority supervising military affairs in Xiang Province, General of the Van, and Governor of Xiang Province.

entries.zh: 永明二年，徙爲散騎常侍、江州刺史。
entries.en: In the second year of Yongming, he was then transferred to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Jiang Province.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongming, he was moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Governor of Jiang Province.

entries.zh: 初省江州軍府。
entries.en: On this occasion the military headquarters of Jiang Province was abolished for the first time.
entries.literal: For the first time the military headquarters of Jiang Province was abolished.

entries.zh: 四年，遷右僕射，本州中正。
entries.en: In the fourth year he was appointed Right Vice Director and provincial rectifier for his home commandery.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to Right Vice Director and became the provincial rectifier of his native commandery.

entries.zh: 奐無學術，以事幹見處。
entries.en: Huan had no scholarly training but was advanced on account of his executive talent.
entries.literal: Huan had no scholarly learning but was placed in office because of his practical ability.

entries.zh: 遷尚書僕射，中正如故。
entries.en: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat while retaining his post as rectifier.
entries.literal: He was moved to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; his rectifier post was unchanged.

entries.zh: 校籍郎王植屬吏部郎孔琇之以校籍令史俞公喜求進署，矯稱奐意，植坐免官。
entries.en: The registrar Wang Zhi, acting under Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Kong Xiuzhi, had registrar clerk Yu Gongxi seek a promotion while falsely invoking Huan's authority; Zhi was dismissed from office.
entries.literal: The registrar Wang Zhi, subordinate to the Ministry of Personnel Gentleman Kong Xiuzhi, had the registrar clerk Yu Gongxi seek an advancement posting while falsely claiming Huan's approval; Zhi was dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 六年，遷散騎常侍，領軍將軍。
entries.en: In the sixth year he was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of the Guards.

entries.zh: 奐欲請車駕幸府。
entries.en: Huan wished to invite the emperor to visit his residence.
entries.literal: Huan wished to request that the imperial carriage visit his headquarters.

entries.zh: 上晚信佛法，御膳不宰牲。
entries.en: In his later years the emperor had come to believe in Buddhism and would not have animals slaughtered for the imperial table.
entries.literal: The emperor in his later years believed in Buddhism; the imperial meals did not slaughter animals.

entries.zh: 使王晏謂奐曰：「吾前去年爲斷殺事，不復幸詣大臣已判，無容欻爾也。」
entries.en: He sent Wang Yan to tell Huan, "These past years I have given up slaughter for my meals and no longer visit the homes of high ministers; that policy is fixed—there is no room for a sudden exception."
entries.literal: He had Wang Yan tell Huan: "I have already, these past years, ceased killing for food and no longer visit the homes of great ministers; the matter is settled—there is no room for a sudden change."

entries.zh: 王儉卒，上用奐爲尚書令，以問王晏。
entries.en: When Wang Jian died, the emperor wished to appoint Huan Director of the Imperial Secretariat and asked Wang Yan's opinion.
entries.literal: When Wang Jian died, the emperor wished to use Huan as Director of the Imperial Secretariat and consulted Wang Yan.

entries.zh: 晏位遇已重，與奐不能相推，答上曰：「柳世隆有重望，恐不宜在奐後。」
entries.en: Yan's standing was already great, and he and Huan could not readily yield to each other; he answered, "Liu Shilong commands great prestige—it would hardly be fitting to rank him below Huan."
entries.literal: Yan's position and favor were already weighty, and he and Huan could not defer to each other; he answered the emperor: "Liu Shilong enjoys great prestige—I fear it would not be fitting to place him after Huan."

entries.zh: 乃轉爲左僕射，加給事中，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡軍事、鎮北將軍、雍州刺史。
entries.en: Huan was therefore made Left Vice Director with the added post of Attendant Within the Gates, then sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Ying Province, and Sui Commandery in Si Province, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yong Province.
entries.literal: He was therefore transferred to Left Vice Director, with the added post of Attendant Within the Gates, and sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, Supernumerary Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, commander of military affairs in Yong, Liang, Northern Qin, Southern Qin, Jingling in Ying Province, and Sui Commandery in Si Province, General Who Guards the North, and Governor of Yong Province.

entries.zh: 上謂王晏曰：「奐於釋氏，實自專至。
entries.en: The emperor said to Wang Yan, "Huan's devotion to Buddhism is truly excessive.
entries.literal: The emperor said to Wang Yan: "Huan's devotion to the Buddhist teaching is in truth extreme.

entries.zh: 其在鎮或以此妨務，卿相見言次及之，勿道吾意也。」
entries.en: In his province he may let it interfere with his duties; when you see him, mention it in passing—but do not say it came from me."
entries.literal: In his province he may let this hinder affairs; when you meet, bring it up in passing—do not say it is my idea."

entries.zh: 上以行北諸戍士卒多襤縷，送褶三千具，令奐分賦之。
entries.en: Because the garrison troops on the northern marches were mostly in rags, the emperor sent three thousand pairs of trousers for Huan to distribute among them.
entries.literal: Because the garrison soldiers on the northern marches were mostly in rags, the emperor sent three thousand pairs of trousers and had Huan distribute them.

entries.zh: :　　攝興祖門生劉倪到臺辨問，列「興祖與奐共事，不能相和。
entries.en: Xingzu's student Liu Ni was brought to the capital for questioning and testified that "Xingzu and Huan served together but could not get along.
entries.literal: Liu Ni, a student of Xingzu, was brought to the capital for examination and stated: "Xingzu and Huan served together but could not get along.

entries.zh: 自去年朱公恩領軍征蠻失利，興祖啓聞，以啓呈奐，奐因此便相嫌恨。
entries.en: Last year Zhu Gong'en led a campaign against the barbarians and met defeat; Xingzu reported this and presented the report to Huan, who thereafter bore him a grudge.
entries.literal: Since last year Zhu Gong'en led troops against the barbarians and suffered defeat, Xingzu reported it and presented the report to Huan; Huan therefore came to bear hatred.

entries.zh: 若云興祖有罪，便應事在民間；
entries.en: If Xingzu were truly guilty, the matter should have been known among the people;
entries.literal: If one says Xingzu was guilty, the matter ought to have been among the people;

entries.zh: 民間恬然，都無事迹。
entries.en: yet among the people all was calm and no such facts existed.
entries.literal: among the people all was tranquil and there were no facts at all.

entries.zh: 去十年九月十八日，奐使仗身三十人來，稱敕錄興祖付獄。
entries.en: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month two years ago, Huan sent thirty armed attendants who claimed an imperial order to arrest Xingzu and commit him to prison.
entries.literal: On the eighteenth day of the ninth month of the tenth year past, Huan sent thirty armed attendants who claimed an imperial order to arrest Xingzu and hand him to prison.

entries.zh: 安定郡蠻先在郡贓私，興祖旣知其取與，卽牒啓，奐不問。
entries.en: A barbarian of Anding Commandery had earlier committed private graft in the prefecture; Xingzu, knowing the details of his bribes, at once submitted a written report, but Huan made no inquiry.
entries.literal: A barbarian of Anding Commandery had earlier committed private graft in the commandery; Xingzu, knowing his takings and payments, immediately submitted a written report, but Huan made no inquiry.
